passages.title: Rising suicide rate under COVID-19: Is Japan sounding the alarm for the world?
passages.passage: Rising suicide rate under Covid-19: Is Japan sounding the alarm for the world?  Rupert Wingfield-Hayes, BBC reporter in Tokyo.  Japan reports suicides faster and more accurately than anywhere else in the world.  Unlike most countries, the number of suicides is counted at the end of each month.  These figures reveal disturbing stories during the coronavirus pandemic.  In 2020, Japan ’ s suicide rate rose for the first time in 11 years.  Most surprisingly, while the number of male suicides declined slightly, the rate of female suicides surged by nearly 15%.  In the month of October 2020, the female suicide rate in Japan rose by more than 70% compared to the same period last year.  Why does the pandemic seem to hit women much harder than men?  Warning: The story may contain uncomfortable content.  Talking face-to-face with a young woman who has attempted suicide multiple times is a disturbing experience.  It gives me a new respect for those who work on suicide prevention.  I was sitting at a walking center in Yokohama ’ s Red Light District, run by a suicide prevention charity called the Bond Project. Across the table was a 19-year-old woman with a wave head.  She sat motionless.  The image is annotated with text, Tachibana hopes that "Bond Project" can help women.  Quietly, without any emotion, she began to tell her story.  She said it all started when she was 15, when her brother violently abused her.  Eventually she ran away from home, but that didn ’ t end the pain and loneliness.  Ending life seems to be the only way out.  “Since about this time last year, I have been in and out of the hospital many times.  She told me, “I tried to kill myself many times, but it didn ’ t work out, so now I ’ ve given up trying to kill myself. ”  The "Bond Plan" intervened to stop her.  They found a safe place for her and began to give her intensive counseling.  Jun Tachibana is the founder of the Bond Project.  She is a strong woman in her 40s with a relentless optimism.  “When girls are in real trouble and pain, they really don ’ t know what to do.  “We ’ re ready to listen to them and tell them, ‘ We ’ re with you, ’ ” she said. Tachibana said the coronavirus appears to be pushing those who are already vulnerable to the brink.  She described some distressing phone calls that employees have received in recent months.  “We hear a lot of people saying ‘ I want to die ’ and ‘ I have nowhere to go, ’ ” she said.  “They said, ‘ It ’ s too painful, I ’ m lonely, I want to disappear. ’ ”  For those who have suffered physical or sexual abuse, the COVID-19 pandemic has made things worse.  “A girl I talked to the other day said she was being sexually harassed by her father, ” Tachibana told me.“ Because of the COVID-19 pandemic, her father doesn ’ t work much, so she is often at home and she can ’ t escape him. ”  If you look at past crisis periods in Japan, such as the banking crisis in 2008, or the collapse of the Japanese stock market and real estate bubble in the early 1990s, it was mainly middle-aged men who were affected.  The rate of male suicide has risen sharply.  But COVID-19 is different. It affects young people, especially young women.  The reasons are complicated.  Japan had the highest suicide rate among developed countries.  Its huge success over the past decade has reduced the suicide rate by about a third.  The image is annotated with text, and Professor Michiko Ueda believes that the suicide trend of Japanese women during the COVID-19 pandemic is "unusual".  Professor Michiko Ueda is a leading suicide expert in Japan.  She told me that it was shocking to witness the dramatic reversals of the past few months.  “This pattern of female suicide is very, very unusual, ” she told me.  “I have never seen so much increase in my research career in this field.  The sectors most impacted by COVID-19 are those with female employees, such as travel and retail and food. ”  The number of single women living alone in Japan has increased significantly.  Many people choose to be single, rather than a marriage that then requires traditional gender roles.  Professor Michiko Ueda said that young women are also significantly more likely to take up so-called precarious jobs.  “A lot of women don ’ t get married, ” she said.  “They have to feed themselves, and they don ’ t have regular jobs.  So when the crisis happens, of course, they will be hit very, very hard.  This has been the case in the last eight months with a very large number of unemployed non-permanent workers. ”  One month was really outstanding.  Last October, 879 women committed suicide.  This is more than 70% higher than the same period in 2019.  Newspaper headlines sounded the alarm.  The total number of men and women who committed suicide in October (2,199) was compared to the total number of COVID-19 deaths in Japan up to that time (2,087).  Something particularly strange happened.  Image copyright Getty Images Image caption Yuko Takeuchi, a famous Japanese actress, was found dead in her home on September 27 last year at the age of 40.  It was later reported that she committed suicide.  Yasuyuki Shimizu, a former journalist and now runs a non-profit organization (NPO) dedicated to solving Japan ’ s suicide problem, “From the day news of celebrity suicides is reported, the number of suicides will increase, and this will continue for about 10 days. ”  "From the data, we can see that the suicide of the actress on September 27 led to 207 more female suicides in the next 10 days," he said.  If you look at the suicide data of women the same age as Takuchi, the statistical results are even more obvious.  “Of all ages, women in their 40s are most affected, ” Mr. Shimizu said.  “For this group, it has more than doubled. ”  Other experts also believe there is a very strong link between celebrity suicides and an immediate rise in suicide rates in subsequent days.  This phenomenon is not unique to Japan, which is one of the reasons why it is so difficult to report suicides.  After celebrity suicide, the more discussed in the media and social media, the greater the impact on other vulnerable people.  Mai Suganuma is one of the NPO researchers.  She was also a victim of suicide.  When she was a teenager, her father committed suicide.  Now she offers help and support to other families of suicides.  Just as COVID-19 has made it impossible for relatives to grieve for those who have died of the virus, it has also made life harder for families of suicides.  “When I talk to my family, they have a very strong feeling that they can ’ t save their loved ones, which often leads them to blame themselves. ”  Massena told me.  I also blamed myself for not being able to save my father.  Now they were told they had to stay at home.  I ’ m afraid the feeling of guilt is getting stronger.  Japanese people do not like to talk about death at the beginning of their daily conversation.  We don't talk about suicide. "  Image copyright Getty Images Image caption Japan is now in the midst of the third wave of COVID-19, with restaurants, hotels and bars closing.  Japan is now in the midst of the so-called third wave of COVID-19, and the government has ordered a second state of national emergency.  More restaurants, hotels and bars are closing, and more people are unemployed.

passages.title: The second wave of the COVID-19 epidemic increased the suicide rate in Japan by 16%
passages.passage: January 15, Minsk / Corr.  BELTA /.  The first wave of the COVID-19 epidemic reduced the number of suicides in Japan by 14%, and the second wave, which began in the fall, on the contrary, increased by 16%.  Such data scientists published in the scientific journal Nature Human Behaviour, reports TASS.  Sociologists led by Tokyo City Institute of Gerontology researcher Shohei Okamoto traced how the COVID-19 pandemic affected suicide rates in Japan.  This country ranks seventh in the world ranking of sad statistics.  The Japanese government monitors suicidal attitudes and tries to prevent them.  The researchers analyzed data from Japanese social services collected during the first and second waves of the pandemic, as well as for similar time periods between 2016 and 2019.  Particular attention was paid to the reaction of the most vulnerable segments of the population, including middle-aged men, as well as the categories that previously committed the least suicide.  "The COVID-19 epidemic has affected all aspects of Japanese society.  Within nine months of the official start of the pandemic, unemployment rose, and fear and anxiety became part of everyday life for all Japanese.  These factors may explain why there were more suicides during the second wave of the pandemic, "the researchers write.  This mainly affected residents of small settlements, women and adolescents who previously committed suicide very rarely.  The exact reasons are not yet known.  But the researchers suggest that these trends have both social and economic causes: rising unemployment, as well as school closures and social distancing.  Okamoto and his colleagues hope that they will be able to find out these reasons in the future and figure out how to prevent the number of suicides from increasing in the future.

Content: Covid and suicides in Japan.  Why among women victims more Rupert Wingfield-Hayes BBC News, Tokyo Suicides in Japan are recorded faster and more accurately than anywhere else in the world.  Unlike most countries, reporting is done on a monthly basis.  And during the Covid-19 pandemic, these statistics turned out to be more alarming than before.  In 2020, for the first time in 11 years, the number of suicides in Japan increased.  However, although the number of suicides among men decreased slightly, the increase among women was almost 15%.  In October alone, the suicide rate among women in Japan jumped more than 70% compared to the same month last year.  What's going on?  And why does the pandemic seem to affect women far more than men?  A young woman (her BBC identity unknown) met Rupert Wingfield-Hayes in Yokohama A face-to-face meeting with a young woman who repeatedly tried to commit suicide is not a pleasant experience.  I have a deep respect for people who work on suicide prevention.  I'm sitting in Yokohama's red light district in a center run by a suicide prevention charity called the Bond Project.  Anyone can enter here, no pre-registration is required.  At the table opposite, a 19-year-old woman with a short haircut is sitting motionless.  Quietly, without any emotion in her voice, she begins to tell me her story.  She said it all started when she was 15.  Her older brother began to harass her.  She eventually ran away from home, but the pain and loneliness didn ’ t go away.  Suicide seemed like the only way out.  “I ’ ve been to the hospital many times since that time last year, ” she tells me.“ I tried to kill myself many times, but I didn ’ t succeed.  It seems that attempts to die will have to be abandoned. ”  The Bond Project intervened in her life.  His staff found her a safe place to live and began intensive psychotherapy.  June Tachibana is the founder of the Bond Project, a tough woman in her 40s and a tireless optimist.  Joon Tachibana hopes the Bond Project will provide women with the help they need "When girls are in big trouble and hurt, they really don't know what to do," she says.  "We are ready to listen to them, to tell them - we are with you."  Tachibana says Covid-19 seems to be pushing vulnerable people to make a fateful decision.  She describes some of the calls her employees have received in recent months.  “We often hear ‘ I want to die ’ and ‘ I have nowhere to go, ’ ” she says.  They say, "It's so painful, I'm so lonely, I want to disappear."  The pandemic has made life much more difficult for those who are physically or sexually abused.  “The girl I spoke to the other day said her father was sexually harassing her, ” Tachibana tells me.“ But because of the covid, her father doesn ’ t work much and spends a lot of time at home, and she manages to escape from him. ”  If you look at previous crisis moments in Japan, for example, the banking crisis of 2008 or the collapse of the Japanese stock market and the real estate bubble in the early 1990s, the effect was felt mainly by middle-aged men.  During these periods, there were sharp spikes in the number of suicides among men.  A pandemic is a different story.  It affects young people, especially young women.  The reasons for this are very multifaceted.  At one time, Japan had the highest suicide rate among developed countries.  Over the past decade, it has been reduced by about a third.  Professor Michiko Ueda is one of Japan ’ s leading experts on suicide.  It tells me how alarming the growth dynamics have become over the past few months.  “This scenario leading to female suicide is very, very unusual, ” she says.  “In all the time I ’ ve been doing research on this topic, I ’ ve never seen such significant growth.  The peculiarity of the pandemic is that the industries in which many women are employed - tourism, retail trade and the food industry - have suffered the most. "  In Japan, there are more and more unmarried women living on their own.  Many of them prefer such a life to marriage, which still assumes quite traditional gender roles.  Professor Ueda says that young women are much more likely to find themselves in a state of so-called "casual employment."  Professor Michiko Ueda said: “Many women are no longer married, they have to earn a living, but they don ’ t have a regular job.  So when something happens, of course, they suffer a lot.  The number of lost jobs among non-permanent workers has increased significantly over the past eight months. ”  One month stands out.  In October last year, 879 women committed suicide.  This is more than 70% higher than in October 2019.  Newspapers are alarmed.  Some even compare the total number of suicides (both men and women) in October - 2,199 - with the total number of deaths in Japan from the coronavirus at that time - 2,087.  Something strange has happened.  On September 27 last year, a very famous and popular actress named Yuko Takeuchi was found dead in her home.  It was later reported that she had committed suicide.  Photo caption: 40-year-old Japanese actress Yuko Takeuchi was found dead in her home Yasuyuki Shimizu, a former journalist.  Today, he runs a non-profit organization dedicated to suicide in Japan.  “From the moment it becomes known about the suicide of any celebrity, the number of suicides increases and remains at this new level for about 10 days, ” he says. – For example, for the suicide of Takeuchi on September 27 in the next 10 days, 207 women committed suicide. ”  If you count the number of suicides of women about the same age as Yuko Takeuchi, the statistics become even more obvious.  "Of all age groups, Takeuchi's death has had the greatest impact on women in their 40s and 50s," says Yasuyuki Shimizu. "Suicide rates have more than doubled in this age group."  Other experts also agree that there is a link between celebrity suicides and the spike in suicides in the days that followed.  This phenomenon is not unique to Japan, and this is one of the reasons why reporting suicides is not easy.  The more celebrity suicide is discussed in the media and on social media, the more it affects other vulnerable people, especially in the early days.  Mai Suganuma works for the Shimizu organization.  Her father killed himself when she was a teenager.  Now it helps to support the families of those who have voluntarily passed away.  The pandemic makes the lives of suicide families much more difficult.  “Members of the suicide family often blame themselves for what happened, ” says Mai Suganuma. – I also blamed myself for not being able to save my father.  And now they say, "Stay at home."  I fear that this will increase the sense of guilt.  The Japanese don ’ t usually talk about death.  We don ’ t have the habit of talking about suicide. ”  Japan is now experiencing a third wave of the epidemic, and the government has declared a state of emergency for the second time.  Most likely, it will last until the end of February.  More and more restaurants, hotels and bars are being quarantined, and more people are losing their jobs.  Photo caption, The third wave of the virus led to the fact that the streets of Japan again emptied

---

**Question:**
"I need a report on suicide rates in Japan during the COVID-19 pandemic.  This would include cases in which the pandemic is identified as a causal factor, but also other factors from that period even if not clearly associated with the pandemic.  I am not looking for information on suicide rates in Japan more generally, however, unless that is used as a basis for comparison with rates during the pandemic."

Write the report in a Objective (impartial and unbiased presentation of facts and findings) tone.

passages.title: Israel, the UAE and Bahrain reach peace deals: five things that are stirring up the Middle East landscape
passages.passage: Image copyright Reuters Image caption Israel's national security adviser flew to the United Arab Emirates on September 1.  A high-level delegation from Israel and the United Arab Emirates will sign a historic peace agreement led by the United States at the White House on Tuesday, September 15, when the UAE and Israel will formally establish diplomatic relations.  U.S. President Donald Trump announced last week that Bahrain ’ s foreign minister would attend the event and sign a comprehensive normalization agreement with Israel alone.  The signing of these agreements will change the landscape in the Middle East. BBC explains why these agreements are important.  Gulf countries see more trade opportunities This agreement will help ambitious UAE.  They built up their own military forces and developed the UAE into a place of business and holiday.  The Americans used the promise of advanced weapons to help reach this agreement.  In the past, the UAE was barely able to buy weapons including the F-35 stealth fighter and the EA-18G Growler electronic fighter.  The UAE has deployed well-equipped armed forces in Libya and Yemen.  But its greatest potential enemy is Iran on the other side of the Gulf.  Israel, like the United States and the United Arab Emirates, is skeptical of Iran.  The same goes for Bahrain.  Until 1969, Iran claimed Bahrain as part of its territory.  Bahrain ’ s Sunni rulers also believe that members of its unstable Shia majority could become Iran ’ s fifth pillar.  The two Gulf states are no longer hiding ties with Israel.  They expect open trade because Israel has the most advanced high-tech industrial chain in the world.  In the non-Covid-19 era, Israelis are avid vacationers who are passionate about exploring the deserts, beaches and shopping centers around the Gulf.  There are business opportunities everywhere.  For Israel, normalization of relations with the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain is a real achievement.  In the 1920s, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu firmly believed in the strategy of building an “iron wall ” between the Jewish state and the Arab states.  The idea is that Israel ’ s strength will eventually make the Arab states realize that their only option is to acknowledge Israel ’ s existence.  Israelis don ’ t like being isolated in the Middle East.  Peace efforts with Egypt and Jordan have never been so enthusiastic.  They may be more looking forward to a better future relationship with the Gulf states far away from Jerusalem and the occupied territories.  Strengthening the anti-Iran coalition is another major advantage.  Netanyahu views Iran as Israel ’ s number one enemy, sometimes comparing its leaders to the Nazis.  He has dropped his previous complaints about the UAE arms deal.  Netanyahu is also troubled, and he is facing a possible jail term for corruption.  His handling of the COVID-19 pandemic went well in the early stages, and badly in the later stages.  Opponents gather weekly outside his Jerusalem residence.  The ceremony at the White House was appropriate.  Image copyright Reuters Image caption Trump announced the so-called Abraham Accord at the White House in August. 3.  Trump celebrated the foreign policy coup, an agreement that has implications for the president of the United States on multiple levels.  This is conducive to Trump ’ s “maximum pressure ” strategy on Iran.  In the year of the election, this helps to support his claim that he is the best trader in the world.  Anything he does that is good for Israel, or more specifically for Netanyahu ’ s government, is good for maintaining good relations with Christian evangelical voters in the United States.  These are important parts of his constituency.  If the Arab states in the Gulf can handle their relations with Israel openly, rather than secretly, then the anti-Iran “Friends of America ” coalition should work more smoothly.  Trump ’ s so-called “deal of the century ” has made peace between Israel and the Palestinians impossible.  But the Abraham Accords between Israel and the UAE are known to have led to a major shift in the Middle East landscape, which the Trump administration has called a major foreign policy coup.  Image copyright Reuters Image caption Palestinian leaders have condemned the actions of the two Gulf states to restore relations with Israel.  The Palestinians felt betrayed that they were once again the last of the tournament.  The Palestinians condemned the Abrahamic Agreement as a betrayal.  The new agreement breaks the long-standing Arab consensus that the price of establishing diplomatic relations with Israel is recognition of Palestinian independence.  But now, Israel is consolidating new public relations with the Arab states, while the Palestinians remain occupied in East Jerusalem, the West Bank, and an area the size of an open prison in Gaza.  Mohammed Al Nahyan, the de facto ruler of the UAE, said his price for the deal was Israel ’ s agreement to stop annexing large parts of the West Bank.  At least because of the current international pressure, Netanyahu seems to have abandoned the idea.  The UAE offered him a way out of the embarrassing political deadlock.  Bahrain joined the agreement and Palestinian tensions increased.  Without Saudi Arabia ’ s approval, that would never have happened.  Saudi Arabia is the leader of the Arab Peace Plan for Palestinian independence.  King Kal Salman was the administrator of two temples in Islam, which gave him great authority.  He is unlikely to suddenly recognize Israel's independence.  His son and successor, Mohammed bin Salman, may also be reluctant to do so.  Image copyright EPA Image caption An agreement between the United Arab Emirates and Israel sparked protests in Iran  Iran Has New Strategic Trouble The deal has been roundly condemned by Iran's leaders.  It ’ s not just about words, the Abrahamic Agreement puts them under even more pressure.  Trump ’ s sanctions have caused real economic pain in Iran.  Now they also have strategic problems.  Israel ’ s home air base is far from Iran, but the UAE ’ s air base is opposite the Gulf waters.  It is very important if we talk again about air strikes on Iranian nuclear bases.  Israel, the United States, Bahrain and the United Arab Emirates have a bunch of new options.  Iran has found that their room for manoeuvre has been reduced.

passages.title: NEWSru.co.il:: The Palestinian Authority is restoring relations with Israel
passages.passage: PA Civil Administration Minister Hussein al-Sheikh said the Palestinian Authority was restoring full relations with Israel.  According to the Wafa news agency, the Palestinian side will return to compliance with all the agreements that existed on May 19, 2020.  The minister said that Israel, through international mediators, had conveyed to PA President Mahmoud Abbas both written and oral commitments to abide by all agreements signed with the Palestinians.  Hamas issued a statement condemning the Palestinian Authority ’ s decision to restore relations with Israel.  The statement said that by his decision Ramallah legalizes the process of normalization of relations with Israel.  The PA chairman announced the rupture of relations with Israel after the publication of the US-prepared plan for a Palestinian-Israeli settlement - the so-called "deal of the century".  The plan provided for the extension of Israeli sovereignty to part of the territory of Judea and Samaria.  “Our rupture of agreements with the occupiers, undertaken after consultations with the leadership of the Palestinian factions, does not mean that we do not want peace.  We extend our hand and propose to hold an international conference under the auspices of the Quartet to work out a settlement mechanism, "Abbas said on June 24.  Israel has reported renouncing the annexation of Palestinian territories in normalization agreements with the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain.  The leaders of these countries declared their support for the principle of “two states ”, but noted that they do not intend to wait forever until the Palestinians agree to peace with Israel.  The Abraham Accords were perceived by the Palestinian side as a stab in the back.  Attempts to confront them have demonstrated the growing isolation of the Palestinians.  Even the Arab League refused to support them.  The rupture of relations with Israel led to the deterioration of the economic situation in the PA.  On the eve of the US presidential election, it was suggested that in the event of the victory of Democratic candidate Joe Biden, the Palestinian leadership would hurry to declare the restoration of relations, since the Palestinians themselves suffer from the rupture.

passages.title: The Russian Jewish Congress commented on the accusations of human rights defenders against Israel
passages.passage: The human rights organization Human Rights Watch released a report in which it claims that the Israeli authorities commit crimes of apartheid in order to preserve the dominance of Jewish Israelis over the Palestinians.  This position is shared by the Israeli NGO B ’ Tselem, which collects information on human rights violations in the disputed territories.  These include the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, and the Gaza Strip, calling them Israeli-occupied territories.  HRW ’ s report is based on years of human rights monitoring, government planning documents, official statements, and other sources.  The experts compared the policy and real actions in the disputed territories and in Israel itself against the Palestinians and the Jewish population.  According to the organization, in July last year, a letter was sent to the Israeli authorities in which they were invited to present their vision of the situation, but a response has not yet been received.  German Zakharyaev, vice president of the Russian Jewish Congress (RJC) and president of the STMEGI Mountain Jews Foundation, called the entire HRW report not a serious study, but a damning pamphlet aimed at stigmatizing Israel as an apartheid state.  “The report is based on the false image of Israel as the country controlling the entire West Bank and Gaza Strip, but in reality it is not, only a few dozen Jewish settlements and a number of highways leading to them are under Israeli control.  The rest of the population is under the control of Mahmoud Abbas's Palestinian Authority and the Hamas movement in the Gaza Strip, "he said.  According to Zakharyaev, on the territory of Israel proper, Arab citizens are absolutely equal.  At the same time, he recognized the persistence of a significant difference in the social status and material situation of the Jewish and Arab populations.  At the same time, the vice-president of the RJC recalled that the same difference exists within the Jewish population - between immigrants from Europe and the countries of the East.  What does the report say?  Allocation of land.  It follows from the report that the authorities, both in Israel itself and in the disputed territories, mainly seek to provide land for Jewish communities.  Most Palestinians are driven into densely populated areas.  The organization also claims the existence of a certain policy of neutralization: for example, the state plan for the development of Jerusalem proceeds from the need for “confident preservation of the Jewish majority ” and even provides for desirable demographic proportions.  German Zakharyaev explained to Gazeta.ru that the Arab population prefers to live in large families and so-called hamuls, build houses near their loved ones in the territories of their towns and cities.  Moreover, he said, these structures are often illegal, allowing Palestinians to bypass the long and costly process of buying and registering property.  Cut off from the local community.  According to HRW, Israel has laws that allow hundreds of small Jewish municipalities to effectively cut off Palestinians from the local community.  In addition, according to the document, only a small part of the budget is allocated to Palestinian schools compared to the financing of schools where Jewish Israeli children study.  The report points out that in the disputed territories, the intensity of repression against Palestinians reaches the level of “systematic oppression ” as one of the hallmarks of apartheid.  The document refers to a draconian military administration for Palestinians in these territories, while Jewish Israelis living separately there are provided with the full range of rights under Israel ’ s model civil code.  Israeli political scientist, former adviser to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu Benny Briskin, said in a comment to Gazeta.ru that Israel ’ s judicial system is built in such a way that every real violation of human rights that occurs either in the disputed territories of the Palestinian Authority, or in the territory of Israel itself in relation to the Arabs, is checked and the guilty is always punished.  “Of course, there are exaggerations, but the Israeli judicial system is recognized by the whole world as serious, independent, which deals with all cases, ” he said.  Freedom of movement.  The authors of the report cite as serious violations of the fundamental rights of the Palestinians and the “inhumane actions ” against their freedom of movement in the form of the closure of the Gaza Strip and the imposition of a permit regime, the confiscation of more than a third of land in the West Bank with the forced eviction of thousands of Palestinians, the denial of housing rights, and the suspension of basic civil rights for millions of Palestinians.  Many of the violations underlying these crimes, according to the authors of the report, cannot be justified in the interests of security, including the almost complete ban on the issuance of building permits to Palestinians and the demolition of thousands of houses on the pretext of lack of such a permit.  There are also cases, according to human rights activists, when demographic goals are covered by security interests, as in the situation with the de facto freezing by the Israeli authorities of the registration of residents in the disputed territories.  The organization noted that this almost completely blocks the reunification of families of Palestinians living there and deprives residents of the Gaza Strip of the opportunity to get to the West Bank.  According to the RJC vice-president, the Gaza Strip is an independent administrative unit, from where Israel completely withdrew its army and settlements in 2005, and where today Hamas, recognized in Israel as a terrorist organization, is in power.  “Any interaction with it should be confirmed at the state and legislative level.  To date, based on security needs, some kind of restrictions are imposed.  It seems to me that it is difficult to interact with the administration, which for any reason or for no reason fires missiles at civilians, ” he said.  In addition, HRW recalled the constitutional law adopted in 2018, according to which Israel was declared the “national state of the Jewish people ”.  The authors of the document are convinced that the growing body of legislation increasingly favors Jewish settlers in the West Bank and does not extend to Palestinians living there.  As explained by German Zakharyaev, this law is designed to strengthen the status of Israel as a Jewish state.  According to the seventh paragraph of this law, the state of Israel sees the development of Jewish settlements as a national value for the entire Jewish people, he noted.  In addition, the expert drew attention to the fact that this law does not say anything about Jewish settlers in the West Bank, but only about the nature of the State of Israel.  Benny Briskin called such reports not new to Israel.  According to him, in Israel there are two points of view on this: either it is ordinary anti-Semitism, or it is left-wing liberalism.  But in any case, the result is the same - the attitude towards Israel is based on double standards, he stated.  “The approach of human rights organizations is that everything that happens in the territories they call occupied is already a crime.  It does not matter how the Jewish population behaves.  In Israel, they are already accustomed to this, ” the political scientist said.  He argues that the facts do not fit into these allegations.  The facts that lead human rights organizations, Briskin called slanderous fabrications of one side.  “That is, they find a Palestinian who tells a story that he was told to tell by the Palestinian secret services.  This is not verified in any way and is exposed as an unquestionable fact, ” he said.  “The claims of apartheid seem particularly absurd today, when Mansour Abbas — leader of the Joint Arab List in the Knesset — holds Israel ’ s political future in the wake of the March elections.  His voice is key in determining who will form the next governing coalition in Israel: Benjamin Netanyahu and his far-right supporters or the camp of his opponents.  Both sides are courting Abbas, which is hardly a sign of apartheid, ” said German Zakharyaev, president of the STMEGI Mountain Jews Foundation.

passages.title: Zionists' actions in support of civil wars
passages.passage: A report published by the Al-Zaitouneh Research Center shows that the Zionist regime is leading the way in selling weapons to dictatorial regimes and spy equipment to Arab countries to spy on human rights activists along with money laundering.  The Al-Zaitouneh Research Center is an independent center in Beirut, founded in 2004, that conducts research on issues related to the Arab and Islamic world, particularly the Palestinian issue.  Unfortunately, some Arab countries and Arab political institutions are buying weapons from the Zionist regime.  This makes dialogue between Palestinian resistance groups and Arab political parties more necessary to counter such actions.  According to the report, Israel has been arming separatist movements in South Sudan, and the Sudanese have not reacted very seriously.  Referring to the nuclear actions of the Zionist regime, the report said that it is necessary to resume Arab studies on the dangers of the Zionist regime ’ s nuclear program against the Middle East.  These studies should be focused on the efforts of the Zionists in the production of chemical and biological weapons.  NSO Group Technologies is an Israeli spy company that uses its programs to spy on human rights activists and journalists around the world.  The company ’ s spy programs have also been used to assassinate Saudi activist Jamal Khashoggi, a critic of the Saudi regime, according to the report, the Zionist regime has not signed any of the agreements on the non-proliferation of nuclear, biological or chemical weapons.  Interestingly, these weapons end up in the hands of dictatorial regimes that violate human rights.  In addition, the Zionist regime is trying to support civil wars and power struggles by sending these weapons.  We are witnessing a process of money laundering and espionage along with the sale of these weapons in general, which is confirmed by the reports of international delegations and academic research.  Israel did not even sign the arms trade agreement, which was ratified by 82 countries in 2012, as it considers humanitarian and human rights issues an obstacle to its arms deals.  According to the report, the Zionist regime is working secretly with security companies in order to transfer weapons.  Spying-related technologies are another area of concern: NSO Group Technologies is one of the Zionist spy companies whose programs are used to spy on human rights activists and journalists around the world.  The company ’ s spy programs have also been used to assassinate Saudi activist Jamal Khashoggi, a critic of the Saudi regime.  According to the report, the Israeli company ’ s plans have been sold to the UAE, Morocco, Bahrain and Saudi Arabia.

passages.title: Human Rights Watch: Israel and Hamas May Have Committed War Crimes
passages.passage: Human Rights Watch said on Tuesday that both Israel and Hamas may have committed war crimes during the May clashes.  During the 11-day battle, Hamas and other Palestinian groups fired thousands of rockets into Israeli territory and the Israeli army bombed the Gaza Strip from the ground and air.  Human Rights Watch said it used interviews with local residents and eyewitnesses, data analysis and digital images to produce its report.  According to the human rights organization, 62 Palestinian civilians were killed in three Israeli attacks in areas where no evidence of armed personnel has been found.  The report specifically examines Israeli air strikes on May 10 on the small town of Beit Hanoun in the northeast Gaza Strip, May 15 on the al-Shati refugee camp and May 16 on the city of Gaza.  Human Rights Watch added that “other Israeli attacks during this battle were also likely in violation of international law. ”  Eight people, including six children, were killed in an attack on May 10 that destroyed several homes.  At this point, Human Rights Watch says there is no indication of the presence of the armed forces or its use for military purposes.  “Any attack that does not have specific military objectives violates international law. ”  In the May 15 attack on the al-Shati refugee camp, a three-storey residential building was targeted and 10 people were killed.  A resident told Human Rights Watch that residents were not given any warning about the attack.  Israel claims that the reason for the attack was the presence of several senior Hamas leaders in the residential complex.  Human Rights Watch said no witnesses or family members of the victims confirmed the presence of Hamas operatives in or around the building.  It added that the building was likely targeted by a bomb produced by Boeing that the United States exported to Israel.  A third attack on May 16 killed three destroyed buildings and 44 civilians, including 18 children and 14 women, in Gaza City.  Human Rights Watch said eyewitnesses interviewed said Israel gave no warning before the attack.  Israeli army videos and pieces of munitions collected by Palestinian police show that the attack was also carried out by a one-ton Boeing bomb.  At the time of the attack, Israel said it was targeting Hamas militants' tunnels, but Human Rights Watch said it found "no evidence of military targets".  Human Rights Watch also condemned “reckless ” missile attacks on Israeli civilians and said it would address the issue in a separate report.  “Israel and the Palestinians have violated international law in this battle, which could amount to war crimes. ”  The Israeli government has not yet responded to the report, but a Hamas spokesman said: "This report shows that the occupation government acts with complete impunity and beyond the law and is never punished because of the full support of the United States."  In March, a prosecutor at the International Criminal Court announced a new and comprehensive investigation into the situation in the occupied Palestinian territories.  The main focus of the study will be the 2014 war in the Gaza Strip, but it will also look at the deaths of Palestinian protesters since 2018.  On May 27, the UN Human Rights Council approved an international investigation into the recent fighting in the Gaza Strip.  According to the local government of the Gaza Strip, 260 Palestinians, including gunmen, have been killed in the recent clashes. Content: Image copyright Reuters Image caption Israel's national security adviser flew to the United Arab Emirates on September 1.  A high-level delegation from Israel and the United Arab Emirates will sign a historic peace agreement led by the United States at the White House on Tuesday, September 15, when the UAE and Israel will formally establish diplomatic relations.  U.S. President Donald Trump announced last week that Bahrain ’ s foreign minister would attend the event and sign a comprehensive normalization agreement with Israel alone.  The signing of these agreements will change the landscape in the Middle East. BBC explains why these agreements are important.  Gulf countries see more trade opportunities This agreement will help ambitious UAE.  They built up their own military forces and developed the UAE into a place of business and holiday.  The Americans used the promise of advanced weapons to help reach this agreement.  In the past, the UAE was barely able to buy weapons including the F-35 stealth fighter and the EA-18G Growler electronic fighter.  The UAE has deployed well-equipped armed forces in Libya and Yemen.  But its greatest potential enemy is Iran on the other side of the Gulf.  Israel, like the United States and the United Arab Emirates, is skeptical of Iran.  The same goes for Bahrain.  Until 1969, Iran claimed Bahrain as part of its territory.  Bahrain ’ s Sunni rulers also believe that members of its unstable Shia majority could become Iran ’ s fifth pillar.  The two Gulf states are no longer hiding ties with Israel.  They expect open trade because Israel has the most advanced high-tech industrial chain in the world.  In the non-Covid-19 era, Israelis are avid vacationers who are passionate about exploring the deserts, beaches and shopping centers around the Gulf.  There are business opportunities everywhere.  For Israel, normalization of relations with the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain is a real achievement.  In the 1920s, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu firmly believed in the strategy of building an “iron wall ” between the Jewish state and the Arab states.  The idea is that Israel ’ s strength will eventually make the Arab states realize that their only option is to acknowledge Israel ’ s existence. Title: The Russian Jewish Congress commented on the accusations of human rights defenders against Israel
Content: The human rights organization Human Rights Watch released a report in which it claims that the Israeli authorities commit crimes of apartheid in order to preserve the dominance of Jewish Israelis over the Palestinians.  This position is shared by the Israeli NGO B ’ Tselem, which collects information on human rights violations in the disputed territories.  These include the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, and the Gaza Strip, calling them Israeli-occupied territories.  HRW ’ s report is based on years of human rights monitoring, government planning documents, official statements, and other sources.  The experts compared the policy and real actions in the disputed territories and in Israel itself against the Palestinians and the Jewish population.  According to the organization, in July last year, a letter was sent to the Israeli authorities in which they were invited to present their vision of the situation, but a response has not yet been received.  German Zakharyaev, vice president of the Russian Jewish Congress (RJC) and president of the STMEGI Mountain Jews Foundation, called the entire HRW report not a serious study, but a damning pamphlet aimed at stigmatizing Israel as an apartheid state.  “The report is based on the false image of Israel as the country controlling the entire West Bank and Gaza Strip, but in reality it is not, only a few dozen Jewish settlements and a number of highways leading to them are under Israeli control.  The rest of the population is under the control of Mahmoud Abbas's Palestinian Authority and the Hamas movement in the Gaza Strip, "he said.  According to Zakharyaev, on the territory of Israel proper, Arab citizens are absolutely equal.  At the same time, he recognized the persistence of a significant difference in the social status and material situation of the Jewish and Arab populations.  At the same time, the vice-president of the RJC recalled that the same difference exists within the Jewish population - between immigrants from Europe and the countries of the East.  What does the report say?  Allocation of land.  It follows from the report that the authorities, both in Israel itself and in the disputed territories, mainly seek to provide land for Jewish communities.  Most Palestinians are driven into densely populated areas.  The organization also claims the existence of a certain policy of neutralization: for example, the state plan for the development of Jerusalem proceeds from the need for “confident preservation of the Jewish majority ” and even provides for desirable demographic proportions.  German Zakharyaev explained to Gazeta.ru that the Arab population prefers to live in large families and so-called hamuls, build houses near their loved ones in the territories of their towns and cities.  Moreover, he said, these structures are often illegal, allowing Palestinians to bypass the long and costly process of buying and registering property.  Cut off from the local community.  According to HRW, Israel has laws that allow hundreds of small Jewish municipalities to effectively cut off Palestinians from the local community.  In addition, according to the document, only a small part of the budget is allocated to Palestinian schools compared to the financing of schools where Jewish Israeli children study.  The report points out that in the disputed territories, the intensity of repression against Palestinians reaches the level of “systematic oppression ” as one of the hallmarks of apartheid.  The document refers to a draconian military administration for Palestinians in these territories, while Jewish Israelis living separately there are provided with the full range of rights under Israel ’ s model civil code.  Israeli political scientist, former adviser to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu Benny Briskin, said in a comment to Gazeta.ru that Israel ’ s judicial system is built in such a way that every real violation of human rights that occurs either in the disputed territories of the Palestinian Authority, or in the territory of Israel itself in relation to the Arabs, is checked and the guilty is always punished.  “Of course, there are exaggerations, but the Israeli judicial system is recognized by the whole world as serious, independent, which deals with all cases, ” he said.  Freedom of movement.  The authors of the report cite as serious violations of the fundamental rights of the Palestinians and the “inhumane actions ” against their freedom of movement in the form of the closure of the Gaza Strip and the imposition of a permit regime, the confiscation of more than a third of land in the West Bank with the forced eviction of thousands of Palestinians, the denial of housing rights, and the suspension of basic civil rights for millions of Palestinians.  Many of the violations underlying these crimes, according to the authors of the report, cannot be justified in the interests of security, including the almost complete ban on the issuance of building permits to Palestinians and the demolition of thousands of houses on the pretext of lack of such a permit.  There are also cases, according to human rights activists, when demographic goals are covered by security interests, as in the situation with the de facto freezing by the Israeli authorities of the registration of residents in the disputed territories.  The organization noted that this almost completely blocks the reunification of families of Palestinians living there and deprives residents of the Gaza Strip of the opportunity to get to the West Bank.  According to the RJC vice-president, the Gaza Strip is an independent administrative unit, from where Israel completely withdrew its army and settlements in 2005, and where today Hamas, recognized in Israel as a terrorist organization, is in power.  “Any interaction with it should be confirmed at the state and legislative level.  To date, based on security needs, some kind of restrictions are imposed.  It seems to me that it is difficult to interact with the administration, which for any reason or for no reason fires missiles at civilians, ” he said.  In addition, HRW recalled the constitutional law adopted in 2018, according to which Israel was declared the “national state of the Jewish people ”.  The authors of the document are convinced that the growing body of legislation increasingly favors Jewish settlers in the West Bank and does not extend to Palestinians living there.  As explained by German Zakharyaev, this law is designed to strengthen the status of Israel as a Jewish state.  According to the seventh paragraph of this law, the state of Israel sees the development of Jewish settlements as a national value for the entire Jewish people, he noted.  In addition, the expert drew attention to the fact that this law does not say anything about Jewish settlers in the West Bank, but only about the nature of the State of Israel.  Benny Briskin called such reports not new to Israel.  According to him, in Israel there are two points of view on this: either it is ordinary anti-Semitism, or it is left-wing liberalism.  But in any case, the result is the same - the attitude towards Israel is based on double standards, he stated.  “The approach of human rights organizations is that everything that happens in the territories they call occupied is already a crime.  It does not matter how the Jewish population behaves.  In Israel, they are already accustomed to this, ” the political scientist said.  He argues that the facts do not fit into these allegations.  The facts that lead human rights organizations, Briskin called slanderous fabrications of one side.  “That is, they find a Palestinian who tells a story that he was told to tell by the Palestinian secret services.  This is not verified in any way and is exposed as an unquestionable fact, ” he said.  “The claims of apartheid seem particularly absurd today, when Mansour Abbas — leader of the Joint Arab List in the Knesset — holds Israel ’ s political future in the wake of the March elections.  His voice is key in determining who will form the next governing coalition in Israel: Benjamin Netanyahu and his far-right supporters or the camp of his opponents.  Both sides are courting Abbas, which is hardly a sign of apartheid, ” said German Zakharyaev, president of the STMEGI Mountain Jews Foundation.

Title: Human Rights Watch: Israel and Hamas May Have Committed War Crimes
Content: Human Rights Watch said on Tuesday that both Israel and Hamas may have committed war crimes during the May clashes.  During the 11-day battle, Hamas and other Palestinian groups fired thousands of rockets into Israeli territory and the Israeli army bombed the Gaza Strip from the ground and air.  Human Rights Watch said it used interviews with local residents and eyewitnesses, data analysis and digital images to produce its report.  According to the human rights organization, 62 Palestinian civilians were killed in three Israeli attacks in areas where no evidence of armed personnel has been found.  The report specifically examines Israeli air strikes on May 10 on the small town of Beit Hanoun in the northeast Gaza Strip, May 15 on the al-Shati refugee camp and May 16 on the city of Gaza.  Human Rights Watch added that “other Israeli attacks during this battle were also likely in violation of international law. ”  Eight people, including six children, were killed in an attack on May 10 that destroyed several homes.  At this point, Human Rights Watch says there is no indication of the presence of the armed forces or its use for military purposes.  “Any attack that does not have specific military objectives violates international law. ”  In the May 15 attack on the al-Shati refugee camp, a three-storey residential building was targeted and 10 people were killed.  A resident told Human Rights Watch that residents were not given any warning about the attack.  Israel claims that the reason for the attack was the presence of several senior Hamas leaders in the residential complex.  Human Rights Watch said no witnesses or family members of the victims confirmed the presence of Hamas operatives in or around the building.  It added that the building was likely targeted by a bomb produced by Boeing that the United States exported to Israel.  A third attack on May 16 killed three destroyed buildings and 44 civilians, including 18 children and 14 women, in Gaza City.  Human Rights Watch said eyewitnesses interviewed said Israel gave no warning before the attack.  Israeli army videos and pieces of munitions collected by Palestinian police show that the attack was also carried out by a one-ton Boeing bomb.  At the time of the attack, Israel said it was targeting Hamas militants' tunnels, but Human Rights Watch said it found "no evidence of military targets".  Human Rights Watch also condemned “reckless ” missile attacks on Israeli civilians and said it would address the issue in a separate report.  “Israel and the Palestinians have violated international law in this battle, which could amount to war crimes. ”  The Israeli government has not yet responded to the report, but a Hamas spokesman said: "This report shows that the occupation government acts with complete impunity and beyond the law and is never punished because of the full support of the United States."  In March, a prosecutor at the International Criminal Court announced a new and comprehensive investigation into the situation in the occupied Palestinian territories.  The main focus of the study will be the 2014 war in the Gaza Strip, but it will also look at the deaths of Palestinian protesters since 2018.  On May 27, the UN Human Rights Council approved an international investigation into the recent fighting in the Gaza Strip. The PA chairman announced the rupture of relations with Israel after the publication of the US-prepared plan for a Palestinian-Israeli settlement - the so-called "deal of the century".  The plan provided for the extension of Israeli sovereignty to part of the territory of Judea and Samaria.  “Our rupture of agreements with the occupiers, undertaken after consultations with the leadership of the Palestinian factions, does not mean that we do not want peace.  We extend our hand and propose to hold an international conference under the auspices of the Quartet to work out a settlement mechanism, "Abbas said on June 24.  Israel has reported renouncing the annexation of Palestinian territories in normalization agreements with the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain.  The leaders of these countries declared their support for the principle of “two states ”, but noted that they do not intend to wait forever until the Palestinians agree to peace with Israel.  The Abraham Accords were perceived by the Palestinian side as a stab in the back.  Attempts to confront them have demonstrated the growing isolation of the Palestinians.  Even the Arab League refused to support them.  The rupture of relations with Israel led to the deterioration of the economic situation in the PA.  On the eve of the US presidential election, it was suggested that in the event of the victory of Democratic candidate Joe Biden, the Palestinian leadership would hurry to declare the restoration of relations, since the Palestinians themselves suffer from the rupture.

Title: The Russian Jewish Congress commented on the accusations of human rights defenders against Israel
Content: The human rights organization Human Rights Watch released a report in which it claims that the Israeli authorities commit crimes of apartheid in order to preserve the dominance of Jewish Israelis over the Palestinians.  This position is shared by the Israeli NGO B ’ Tselem, which collects information on human rights violations in the disputed territories.  These include the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, and the Gaza Strip, calling them Israeli-occupied territories.  HRW ’ s report is based on years of human rights monitoring, government planning documents, official statements, and other sources.  The experts compared the policy and real actions in the disputed territories and in Israel itself against the Palestinians and the Jewish population.  According to the organization, in July last year, a letter was sent to the Israeli authorities in which they were invited to present their vision of the situation, but a response has not yet been received.  German Zakharyaev, vice president of the Russian Jewish Congress (RJC) and president of the STMEGI Mountain Jews Foundation, called the entire HRW report not a serious study, but a damning pamphlet aimed at stigmatizing Israel as an apartheid state.  “The report is based on the false image of Israel as the country controlling the entire West Bank and Gaza Strip, but in reality it is not, only a few dozen Jewish settlements and a number of highways leading to them are under Israeli control.  The rest of the population is under the control of Mahmoud Abbas's Palestinian Authority and the Hamas movement in the Gaza Strip, "he said.  According to Zakharyaev, on the territory of Israel proper, Arab citizens are absolutely equal.  At the same time, he recognized the persistence of a significant difference in the social status and material situation of the Jewish and Arab populations.  At the same time, the vice-president of the RJC recalled that the same difference exists within the Jewish population - between immigrants from Europe and the countries of the East.  What does the report say?  Allocation of land.  It follows from the report that the authorities, both in Israel itself and in the disputed territories, mainly seek to provide land for Jewish communities.  Most Palestinians are driven into densely populated areas.  The organization also claims the existence of a certain policy of neutralization: for example, the state plan for the development of Jerusalem proceeds from the need for “confident preservation of the Jewish majority ” and even provides for desirable demographic proportions.  German Zakharyaev explained to Gazeta.ru that the Arab population prefers to live in large families and so-called hamuls, build houses near their loved ones in the territories of their towns and cities.  Moreover, he said, these structures are often illegal, allowing Palestinians to bypass the long and costly process of buying and registering property.  Cut off from the local community.  According to HRW, Israel has laws that allow hundreds of small Jewish municipalities to effectively cut off Palestinians from the local community.  In addition, according to the document, only a small part of the budget is allocated to Palestinian schools compared to the financing of schools where Jewish Israeli children study.  The report points out that in the disputed territories, the intensity of repression against Palestinians reaches the level of “systematic oppression ” as one of the hallmarks of apartheid.  The document refers to a draconian military administration for Palestinians in these territories, while Jewish Israelis living separately there are provided with the full range of rights under Israel ’ s model civil code.  Israeli political scientist, former adviser to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu Benny Briskin, said in a comment to Gazeta.ru that Israel ’ s judicial system is built in such a way that every real violation of human rights that occurs either in the disputed territories of the Palestinian Authority, or in the territory of Israel itself in relation to the Arabs, is checked and the guilty is always punished.  “Of course, there are exaggerations, but the Israeli judicial system is recognized by the whole world as serious, independent, which deals with all cases, ” he said.  Freedom of movement.  The authors of the report cite as serious violations of the fundamental rights of the Palestinians and the “inhumane actions ” against their freedom of movement in the form of the closure of the Gaza Strip and the imposition of a permit regime, the confiscation of more than a third of land in the West Bank with the forced eviction of thousands of Palestinians, the denial of housing rights, and the suspension of basic civil rights for millions of Palestinians.  Many of the violations underlying these crimes, according to the authors of the report, cannot be justified in the interests of security, including the almost complete ban on the issuance of building permits to Palestinians and the demolition of thousands of houses on the pretext of lack of such a permit.  There are also cases, according to human rights activists, when demographic goals are covered by security interests, as in the situation with the de facto freezing by the Israeli authorities of the registration of residents in the disputed territories.  The organization noted that this almost completely blocks the reunification of families of Palestinians living there and deprives residents of the Gaza Strip of the opportunity to get to the West Bank.  According to the RJC vice-president, the Gaza Strip is an independent administrative unit, from where Israel completely withdrew its army and settlements in 2005, and where today Hamas, recognized in Israel as a terrorist organization, is in power.  “Any interaction with it should be confirmed at the state and legislative level.  To date, based on security needs, some kind of restrictions are imposed.  It seems to me that it is difficult to interact with the administration, which for any reason or for no reason fires missiles at civilians, ” he said.  In addition, HRW recalled the constitutional law adopted in 2018, according to which Israel was declared the “national state of the Jewish people ”.  The authors of the document are convinced that the growing body of legislation increasingly favors Jewish settlers in the West Bank and does not extend to Palestinians living there.  As explained by German Zakharyaev, this law is designed to strengthen the status of Israel as a Jewish state.  According to the seventh paragraph of this law, the state of Israel sees the development of Jewish settlements as a national value for the entire Jewish people, he noted.  In addition, the expert drew attention to the fact that this law does not say anything about Jewish settlers in the West Bank, but only about the nature of the State of Israel.  Benny Briskin called such reports not new to Israel.  According to him, in Israel there are two points of view on this: either it is ordinary anti-Semitism, or it is left-wing liberalism.  But in any case, the result is the same - the attitude towards Israel is based on double standards, he stated.  “The approach of human rights organizations is that everything that happens in the territories they call occupied is already a crime.  It does not matter how the Jewish population behaves.  In Israel, they are already accustomed to this, ” the political scientist said.  He argues that the facts do not fit into these allegations.  The facts that lead human rights organizations, Briskin called slanderous fabrications of one side.  “That is, they find a Palestinian who tells a story that he was told to tell by the Palestinian secret services.  This is not verified in any way and is exposed as an unquestionable fact, ” he said.  “The claims of apartheid seem particularly absurd today, when Mansour Abbas — leader of the Joint Arab List in the Knesset — holds Israel ’ s political future in the wake of the March elections.  His voice is key in determining who will form the next governing coalition in Israel: Benjamin Netanyahu and his far-right supporters or the camp of his opponents.  Both sides are courting Abbas, which is hardly a sign of apartheid, ” said German Zakharyaev, president of the STMEGI Mountain Jews Foundation.

Title: Zionists' actions in support of civil wars
Content: A report published by the Al-Zaitouneh Research Center shows that the Zionist regime is leading the way in selling weapons to dictatorial regimes and spy equipment to Arab countries to spy on human rights activists along with money laundering.  The Al-Zaitouneh Research Center is an independent center in Beirut, founded in 2004, that conducts research on issues related to the Arab and Islamic world, particularly the Palestinian issue.  Unfortunately, some Arab countries and Arab political institutions are buying weapons from the Zionist regime.  This makes dialogue between Palestinian resistance groups and Arab political parties more necessary to counter such actions.  According to the report, Israel has been arming separatist movements in South Sudan, and the Sudanese have not reacted very seriously.  Referring to the nuclear actions of the Zionist regime, the report said that it is necessary to resume Arab studies on the dangers of the Zionist regime ’ s nuclear program against the Middle East.  These studies should be focused on the efforts of the Zionists in the production of chemical and biological weapons.  NSO Group Technologies is an Israeli spy company that uses its programs to spy on human rights activists and journalists around the world.  The company ’ s spy programs have also been used to assassinate Saudi activist Jamal Khashoggi, a critic of the Saudi regime, according to the report, the Zionist regime has not signed any of the agreements on the non-proliferation of nuclear, biological or chemical weapons.  Interestingly, these weapons end up in the hands of dictatorial regimes that violate human rights.  In addition, the Zionist regime is trying to support civil wars and power struggles by sending these weapons.  We are witnessing a process of money laundering and espionage along with the sale of these weapons in general, which is confirmed by the reports of international delegations and academic research.  Israel did not even sign the arms trade agreement, which was ratified by 82 countries in 2012, as it considers humanitarian and human rights issues an obstacle to its arms deals.  According to the report, the Zionist regime is working secretly with security companies in order to transfer weapons.  Spying-related technologies are another area of concern: NSO Group Technologies is one of the Zionist spy companies whose programs are used to spy on human rights activists and journalists around the world.  The company ’ s spy programs have also been used to assassinate Saudi activist Jamal Khashoggi, a critic of the Saudi regime.  According to the report, the Israeli company ’ s plans have been sold to the UAE, Morocco, Bahrain and Saudi Arabia.

Title: Human Rights Watch: Israel and Hamas May Have Committed War Crimes
Content: Human Rights Watch said on Tuesday that both Israel and Hamas may have committed war crimes during the May clashes.  During the 11-day battle, Hamas and other Palestinian groups fired thousands of rockets into Israeli territory and the Israeli army bombed the Gaza Strip from the ground and air.  Human Rights Watch said it used interviews with local residents and eyewitnesses, data analysis and digital images to produce its report.  According to the human rights organization, 62 Palestinian civilians were killed in three Israeli attacks in areas where no evidence of armed personnel has been found.  The report specifically examines Israeli air strikes on May 10 on the small town of Beit Hanoun in the northeast Gaza Strip, May 15 on the al-Shati refugee camp and May 16 on the city of Gaza.  Human Rights Watch added that “other Israeli attacks during this battle were also likely in violation of international law. ”  Eight people, including six children, were killed in an attack on May 10 that destroyed several homes.  At this point, Human Rights Watch says there is no indication of the presence of the armed forces or its use for military purposes.  “Any attack that does not have specific military objectives violates international law. ”  In the May 15 attack on the al-Shati refugee camp, a three-storey residential building was targeted and 10 people were killed.  A resident told Human Rights Watch that residents were not given any warning about the attack.  Israel claims that the reason for the attack was the presence of several senior Hamas leaders in the residential complex.  Human Rights Watch said no witnesses or family members of the victims confirmed the presence of Hamas operatives in or around the building.  It added that the building was likely targeted by a bomb produced by Boeing that the United States exported to Israel.  A third attack on May 16 killed three destroyed buildings and 44 civilians, including 18 children and 14 women, in Gaza City.  Human Rights Watch said eyewitnesses interviewed said Israel gave no warning before the attack.  Israeli army videos and pieces of munitions collected by Palestinian police show that the attack was also carried out by a one-ton Boeing bomb.  At the time of the attack, Israel said it was targeting Hamas militants' tunnels, but Human Rights Watch said it found "no evidence of military targets".  Human Rights Watch also condemned “reckless ” missile attacks on Israeli civilians and said it would address the issue in a separate report.  “Israel and the Palestinians have violated international law in this battle, which could amount to war crimes. ”  The Israeli government has not yet responded to the report, but a Hamas spokesman said: "This report shows that the occupation government acts with complete impunity and beyond the law and is never punished because of the full support of the United States."  In March, a prosecutor at the International Criminal Court announced a new and comprehensive investigation into the situation in the occupied Palestinian territories.  The main focus of the study will be the 2014 war in the Gaza Strip, but it will also look at the deaths of Palestinian protesters since 2018.  On May 27, the UN Human Rights Council approved an international investigation into the recent fighting in the Gaza Strip.  According to the local government of the Gaza Strip, 260 Palestinians, including gunmen, have been killed in the recent clashes.  The Israeli government says 13 people have been killed in the country, including a military man.  According to a report by the French news agency / Sr / Kr

passages.title: Chengdu medical beauty market supply and demand two strong driving consumption
passages.passage: The number of medical and aesthetic institutions has reached 381; the scale of the industry is only second to Beijing and Shanghai, and the operating income of the medical and aesthetic industry in Chengdu will reach 100 billion yuan (RMB, the same below) in 2025 and 200 billion yuan in 2030, creating a leading and world-renowned "medical and aesthetic capital" in mainland China.  China News Service reported that Wang Xidan, secretary general of Chengdu Medical and Beauty Industry Association, said that the scale of Chengdu's medical and aesthetic industry in 2018 has reached 48.7 billion yuan.  "The development of the entire industry has formed a relatively healthy cycle, and the market is showing a state of supply and demand." Wang Xidan said that concentrated medical and aesthetic resources and a higher price ratio than first-tier cities have attracted more and more consumers to Chengdu.  In 2018, the number of medical and aesthetic institutions in Chengdu soared to 407, a surge of 131 from the previous year.  The Plastic Surgery Hospital of the Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences also chose to host the first Beijing-outside branch of Chengdu ’ s eight major medical and aesthetic hospitals in Chengdu in 2018.  Tang Yong, director of eight major medical and aesthetic hospitals in Chengdu, said that with nearly 40 days of closure due to the COVID-19 epidemic, the hospital's revenue in 2020 still increased by about 30% compared to 2019.  With the rise of the “face value economy ”, medical beauty has gradually become a pressing need for some contemporary Chinese, among which light medical beauty, which has a short recovery period and low risk, is most popular.  Due to the consideration of safety, reliability and other factors, a large number of consumers have moved to cities where medical and aesthetic resources are concentrated, and "medical and aesthetic tourism" has also quietly emerged.  The total revenue of Sichuan Huamei Zixin Medical Aesthetic Hospital in 2020 is about 600 million yuan.  Xue Hong, general manager of the hospital, said that about 20% of the annual number of patients treated by the hospital are foreign consumers who come to the hospital.  "Especially in recent years, the number of these consumers has grown rapidly, from Gansu, Qinghai, Yunnan, Guizhou and other provinces."  Wang Xidan sees this phenomenon as a new inflection point for the development of Chengdu's medical and aesthetic industry.  She said that medical beauty and tourism, finance, catering and other industries are expected to achieve the continuous development, the next step of the Chengdu Medical and Beauty Industry Association will work from this aspect, strive to create a consumer ecosystem that can maximize meet the diversified needs of consumers, and enhance the competitiveness of Chengdu medical and beauty industry.  Liu Lu, a professor of economics at Southwest University of Finance and Economics, said that the medical and aesthetic industry, as a new economy that can promote regional economic development, should care for its growth, but also need to strengthen supervision, train high-quality personnel, and formulate more stringent industry norms.
