passages.title: 35% of global tourism revenue is Iran ’ s share
passages.passage: The advanced and widespread health services in Iran compared to neighboring countries and the relative superiority of these services in terms of price compared to many advanced countries has made the market of health and medical services in Iran attractive to citizens of other countries and a new branch of tourism called health tourism has emerged in the country.  The presence of many of these health tourists can not be limited to health services; these people can also travel to tourist or pilgrimage areas of Iran during and after treatment, which can also help the tourism development of those areas.  According to the Public Relations Department of the Institute of Cultural Heritage and Tourism, Saeed Amirian, discussed this issue at the specialized meeting of “Risk Management in Health Tourism ” held by the Institute of Tourism.  He described medical tourism as an economic activity that requires trade in services and participation of at least two medical and tourism sectors, adding that medical tourism in most cases includes dental services, cosmetic surgery and other types of surgeries.  Amirian, in the definition of health tourism, said: The use of services that improve or increase health and increase the morale of the person and in a place outside his residence for more than 24 hours is considered to be a health tourism.  Referring to the flow of patients from developed countries to developing countries to receive medical services, he said: “The intensifying factor in the flow of medical tourism in recent years is the third payer, employer or insurance, which encourages patients to find medical services at more affordable and faster prices. ”  In describing the dimensions of medical tourism in Iran, he said: Iran ’ s share of attracting this type of tourism during one year was only 350 million dollars; that is, only 0.35% of global health tourism revenue is Iran ’ s share, and with this amount of income, Iran ranks 10th in terms of attracting health tourists.  Referring to the importance of health tourism in Iran, Amirian stated: "The advanced and widespread health services in Iran compared to neighboring countries and the relative superiority of these services in terms of price compared to many advanced countries has made the market of health and health services of Iran attractive to citizens of other countries and a new branch of tourism called health tourism in the country emerges."  He went on to say something about the risk of tourism, saying: "It is mainly a defect in our knowledge of the future and risk is more in the future; risk and uncertainty start exactly where knowledge ends."  The expert added: "By stating that the risk of uncertainties with probabilities and possible outcomes is known, the risk classification is small and large scale, systematic and unsystematic.  Referring to the theoretical reflections of risk and uncertainty in tourism, Amirian said: "Risk is more as something to be avoided, but risk and uncertainty are considered as tourist attractions, especially adventure tourism."  He went on to describe the risks in tourism including individual risks for tourists, the responsibility of tourism service providers, destination risks and social risks, and by giving examples of risks in individual tourism, he explained the ways to cover risks for individual tourists, destination risks, social and tourism risks and governments and risk management.  Referring to the risk in tourism companies and its types, he said the four main strategies for risk management at the company level are knowledge, diversity, trust, and insurance, and said the risk management principle includes four steps; identification of small and large threats that the company may face in the future, analyzing risks and assessing the amount of costs that each risk may bring to the company, formulating a strategy for each possible risk and designing practical measures to deal with it and monitor damage. It is a risk to the company and a modification of past strategies and approaches.

passages.title: Dental tourism, looking for a beautiful smile
passages.passage: ISNA / Khorasan Razavi Dental tourism is one of the most important forms of medical tourism and as an emerging industry, it is growing at a high rate.  The criteria for choosing a dentist for medical tourists depend on factors such as cost, location and quality of service.  The researchers noted that today ’ s unhealthy lifestyles, diets and longevity are gradually increasing the demand for quality and professional dental care.  The boom in the worldwide dental tourism market is primarily due to the increase in cases of dental malformation and the second is the increase in the desire for cosmetic dentistry.  The lower cost of treatment and better services in dental treatment in foreign country and the long waiting period for dental treatment in tourist country may boost the growth of this market in the future.  The global dental tourism market can be categorized in the type of treatment and area, and in terms of the type of treatment can be divided into preventive, restorative, prosthetic and other treatments.  Worldwide demand for cosmetic dentistry and therapeutic and restorative dentures has captured a large share of the market.  The pros of dental implant tourism, like medical tourism, are low medical costs, but there are many risks along the way.  Experts predict that the global dental implant market will reach $9 billion by 2027, making dental implants popular for a number of reasons, such as durability and usually success, which can last 20 years or more.  However, they are the best tooth replacement options and, of course, the most expensive, which in turn has led to an increase in dental tourism.  Also, market experts predict that the dental tourism industry will grow to a $5.83 billion sector by 2025, with the most important factors being the cost of treatment in countries and the lack of insurance coverage for many dental treatments.  In dental tourism, people travel abroad to receive dental care.  For example, a U.S. citizen may travel to Mexico to undergo dental implant surgery or an Australian may travel to Thailand to do oral matters.  With the above in mind, most dental tourists are from countries where the cost of treatment is very high, and the destinations in turn are countries known for their cheap services.  The results showed that the success of dental implants depends on the individual ’ s gums, which should be free of disease and infection, and patients who want to have implants but have gum disease should treat the gums first.  Dental tourism makes it difficult to achieve this goal, as it means multiple trips, and sometimes it is very unpleasant.  When the dental tourist encounters the entry of bacteria into the implant at the time of the gum surgery and the infection does not immediately show symptoms and the person returns to the origin, he will face infection after a few days.  Although infections caused by implants are treatable, they are difficult to treat and can be costly, and sometimes a lack of health standards and regulations can lead to these problems.  The researchers noted that regular dental checkups and oral hygiene will be the most important factor for reducing medical tourism trips.  Dentists, in some cases, make medical tourism more charitable, not to reduce costs, but to provide services to low-income people.  Doctors travel to poor countries to put their skills at the mercy of other people and provide the key to good oral health.  Dental tourism in the corona crisis Many patients travel to areas outside their country in search of a perfect smile to fix their oral problems.  According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), travel is likely to increase the incidence of COVID-19, and the farther the trip, the greater the risk.  It should be noted, however, that before COVID-19, travelers were also at risk of developing other diseases.  The financial impact on dental tourism has been dramatic, as this type of tourism will be difficult when patients are unwilling to perform services or unable to travel to the country due to quarantine or travel ban. passages.title: The main directions of beauty tourism: plastic, weight loss, sleep
passages.passage: Hair transplants in Turkey, sleep recovery in Switzerland, liposuction in Brazil: health tourism is booming and expanding horizons.  "Kommersant Style" tells about popular destinations and beauty programs from around the world.  Medical tourism is not a new phenomenon: there have always been those who want to improve their health abroad.  Many countries have their own medical specialization - they are able to do something better than others.  For example, the United States, Brazil, Japan, Mexico and Italy account for 41.4% of all global plastic surgeries.  Patients Beyond Borders estimates that 14 million people travel abroad every year to seek health care.  The obvious reason for the popularity of such tourism for many is the difference in prices.  For example, rhinoplasty in the United States will cost an average of $4.8 thousand, and in Thailand - $1.6 thousand, in a Moscow clinic - about 200 thousand rubles, depending on the complexity.  According to the WHO, Brazil has the best healthcare system in Latin America thanks to the mass accreditation of hospitals by the Joint International Commission (JCI – the largest and oldest medical accreditation organization in the world).  This led to the phenomenon of such tourism in the country.  Surgeons here are like hairdressers.  The most popular procedures in Brazil are liposuction, abdominoplasty and buttock augmentation, called brazilian butt lift.  Of course, the cult of the body is due to the hot climate.  Interestingly, every year the government subsidizes almost half a million operations, for the locals it is the “right to beauty ”.  The same operations are being carried out in neighboring Colombia.  Almost all patients are from the United States.  About 50,000 medical tourists visit the country every year.  From 2012 to 2018, medical tourism in Colombia grew by 264%.  There are more surgeons in South Korea.  It has one of the highest rates of plastic surgery in the world - about 1 million procedures per year, as well as the largest number of plastic surgeons per capita.  The country boasts a thriving tourism industry in this area.  In Korea, they strive to make facial features more Europeanized, so first of all, they change the shape of the nose, eyes (double eyelid surgery), jaws and cheekbones.  The management of Incheon Airport in Seoul even considered the possibility of creating a plastic surgery clinic in one of the terminals so that travelers did not need to travel around the city.  Photo: Getty Images Turkey, although not one of the most popular places for plastic surgery, but the leader in the market of hair transplantation.  Often on the streets of Istanbul and other major cities of the country you can meet people with bandaged heads.  For comparison, hair transplantation costs about $25 thousand in the United States and Europe, in Turkey - from $600 to $2 thousand, in a Moscow clinic - about 100 thousand rubles. for one graft (a group of one to four follicles).  According to the Hurriyet newspaper, in 2017, among 750 thousand tourists, 60 thousand came for hair transplantation.  Most are from the Middle East. The most common procedures are the installation of implants, veneers and crowns, bleaching.  For example, Hungary has become the best place in Europe for this direction, it is visited annually by about 7 thousand patients.  This is due to favorable prices, qualified doctors and modern technologies. As a rule, resorts for the restoration of sleep are located in picturesque places: in the mountains, overlooking the water.  For example, in Portugal, Germany, Italy and Switzerland.  Services include a menu of pillows: from special anti-snoring to filled with water or memory foam, sleep masks and earplugs to choose from, a music library, meditation on demand, as well as staff who can advise on sleep issues.  For example, the hotel in Manhattan, The Benjamin, designed the Rest & Renew program with Rebecca Robbins, a professor of sleep medicine at Cornell University.  Similar programs have Six Senses Douro Valley in Portugal, Peak Health in Switzerland and Lefay on Lake Garda.  Berlin ’ s Swisstel included in its DeepSleep retreat sessions of aroma- and light therapy, as well as inhalation of mountain air.  Beauty tourism is a thriving niche in the industry.  Clinics and hotels offer complete packages, including transfers, flights, meals and even excursions.  According to a joint study by Visa and Oxford Economics, the global medical tourism industry will grow by 25% per year over the next ten years.  Daria Bogomolova

Title: Chengdu medical beauty market supply and demand two strong driving consumption
Content: The number of medical and aesthetic institutions has reached 381; the scale of the industry is only second to Beijing and Shanghai, and the operating income of the medical and aesthetic industry in Chengdu will reach 100 billion yuan (RMB, the same below) in 2025 and 200 billion yuan in 2030, creating a leading and world-renowned "medical and aesthetic capital" in mainland China.  China News Service reported that Wang Xidan, secretary general of Chengdu Medical and Beauty Industry Association, said that the scale of Chengdu's medical and aesthetic industry in 2018 has reached 48.7 billion yuan.  "The development of the entire industry has formed a relatively healthy cycle, and the market is showing a state of supply and demand." Wang Xidan said that concentrated medical and aesthetic resources and a higher price ratio than first-tier cities have attracted more and more consumers to Chengdu.  In 2018, the number of medical and aesthetic institutions in Chengdu soared to 407, a surge of 131 from the previous year.  The Plastic Surgery Hospital of the Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences also chose to host the first Beijing-outside branch of Chengdu ’ s eight major medical and aesthetic hospitals in Chengdu in 2018.  Tang Yong, director of eight major medical and aesthetic hospitals in Chengdu, said that with nearly 40 days of closure due to the COVID-19 epidemic, the hospital's revenue in 2020 still increased by about 30% compared to 2019.  With the rise of the “face value economy ”, medical beauty has gradually become a pressing need for some contemporary Chinese, among which light medical beauty, which has a short recovery period and low risk, is most popular.  Due to the consideration of safety, reliability and other factors, a large number of consumers have moved to cities where medical and aesthetic resources are concentrated, and "medical and aesthetic tourism" has also quietly emerged.  The total revenue of Sichuan Huamei Zixin Medical Aesthetic Hospital in 2020 is about 600 million yuan.  Xue Hong, general manager of the hospital, said that about 20% of the annual number of patients treated by the hospital are foreign consumers who come to the hospital.  "Especially in recent years, the number of these consumers has grown rapidly, from Gansu, Qinghai, Yunnan, Guizhou and other provinces."  Wang Xidan sees this phenomenon as a new inflection point for the development of Chengdu's medical and aesthetic industry.  She said that medical beauty and tourism, finance, catering and other industries are expected to achieve the continuous development, the next step of the Chengdu Medical and Beauty Industry Association will work from this aspect, strive to create a consumer ecosystem that can maximize meet the diversified needs of consumers, and enhance the competitiveness of Chengdu medical and beauty industry.  Liu Lu, a professor of economics at Southwest University of Finance and Economics, said that the medical and aesthetic industry, as a new economy that can promote regional economic development, should care for its growth, but also need to strengthen supervision, train high-quality personnel, and formulate more stringent industry norms.

Title: The construction of a health village is aimed at attracting foreign tourists.
Content: Director of Health, Sports and Education of the Secretariat of the Supreme Council of Free and Special Economic Zones on Wednesday, on the second day of the meeting of Cultural, Social and Tourism Managers of Free Zones Organizations hosted by Maku, said: The income from the arrival of each health tourist is 3,500 to four thousand dollars.  Hani Saghan added: Currently, health tourism in the world has a turnover of 600 billion dollars and according to forecasts, its turnover will reach 900 billion dollars by 2022.  He described beauty, dentistry, cardiovascular, cancer and infertility treatment as one of the highest paid parts of health tourism and stated: The number of tourists from developing countries to developed countries is less than the number of tourists from developed countries to Asia because the cost of health services in these countries is cheaper.  He pointed to the important factors of attracting health tourism in Iran, low cost, providing optimal health services in comparison with neighboring countries and advances in medical science, and continued: Earning foreign currency in the current economic conditions should be a priority in this sector.  He announced that the health tourism village in Anzali has been launched and foreign and domestic investors have started their work in the village, adding: “The Anzali Free Zone health village has a good economic justification and the region is fully prepared to support investors in the field of health services, health and health and issuing the necessary permits. ”  He added: Iran is in a good rank in terms of medical science and the pattern of health tourism in free zones is tested / pilot / implemented.  The chairman of the board of directors of Arya Health Tourism Company also said at the meeting: "Reasonable price, high quality, outstanding doctors and other advantages have made it possible to spend on health tourism, but Iran health tourism needs digital marketing and we must provide platforms with cooperation and consultation."  Mohammad Hadi Shajari, pointing out that the share of digital marketing of health tourism in India is about 20%, added: "In the world, health tourism is considered as an industry; we should also look to this direction." Title: 2021 Cross-Strait Reporter Sichuan Yuhang Taiwan Enterprises Leverage Sichuan Yuhang Economic Circle Advantages to Layout the Belt and Road Market Strategy

Since last year, we have worked hard to overcome the epidemic and innovated to promote interactive exchanges in various fields of Sichuan society, from the cloud to the community.  Third, the implementation of efforts, we continue to implement the central measures to benefit Taiwan people, "Sichuan 70", "support for Taiwan enterprises 12", "26" and "agricultural and forestry 22" operating guidelines landing, and constantly improve the Taiwan compatriots Taiwan enterprises enjoy the same treatment in Sichuan system guarantee.  We give full play to the role of relevant departments in the province's liaison work mechanism, and vigorously promote the implementation of policies. In 2017, the 39-year-old Lin Zhengwei made a decision that looks "very bold" to leave Taiwan's family, and only came to Sichuan Yiyang to join in the way of technology shares. En Dental Group, and is the general manager of Sichuan Hongzheng Boen Dental Technology Co., Ltd. Title: The main directions of beauty tourism: plastic, weight loss, sleep
Content: Hair transplants in Turkey, sleep recovery in Switzerland, liposuction in Brazil: health tourism is booming and expanding horizons.  "Kommersant Style" tells about popular destinations and beauty programs from around the world.  Medical tourism is not a new phenomenon: there have always been those who want to improve their health abroad.  Many countries have their own medical specialization - they are able to do something better than others.  For example, the United States, Brazil, Japan, Mexico and Italy account for 41.4% of all global plastic surgeries.  Patients Beyond Borders estimates that 14 million people travel abroad every year to seek health care.  The obvious reason for the popularity of such tourism for many is the difference in prices.  For example, rhinoplasty in the United States will cost an average of $4.8 thousand, and in Thailand - $1.6 thousand, in a Moscow clinic - about 200 thousand rubles, depending on the complexity.  According to the WHO, Brazil has the best healthcare system in Latin America thanks to the mass accreditation of hospitals by the Joint International Commission (JCI – the largest and oldest medical accreditation organization in the world).  This led to the phenomenon of such tourism in the country.  Surgeons here are like hairdressers.  The most popular procedures in Brazil are liposuction, abdominoplasty and buttock augmentation, called brazilian butt lift.  Of course, the cult of the body is due to the hot climate.  Interestingly, every year the government subsidizes almost half a million operations, for the locals it is the “right to beauty ”.  The same operations are being carried out in neighboring Colombia.  Almost all patients are from the United States.  About 50,000 medical tourists visit the country every year.  From 2012 to 2018, medical tourism in Colombia grew by 264%.  There are more surgeons in South Korea.  It has one of the highest rates of plastic surgery in the world - about 1 million procedures per year, as well as the largest number of plastic surgeons per capita.  The country boasts a thriving tourism industry in this area.  In Korea, they strive to make facial features more Europeanized, so first of all, they change the shape of the nose, eyes (double eyelid surgery), jaws and cheekbones.  The management of Incheon Airport in Seoul even considered the possibility of creating a plastic surgery clinic in one of the terminals so that travelers did not need to travel around the city.  Photo: Getty Images Turkey, although not one of the most popular places for plastic surgery, but the leader in the market of hair transplantation.  Often on the streets of Istanbul and other major cities of the country you can meet people with bandaged heads.  For comparison, hair transplantation costs about $25 thousand in the United States and Europe, in Turkey - from $600 to $2 thousand, in a Moscow clinic - about 100 thousand rubles. for one graft (a group of one to four follicles).  According to the Hurriyet newspaper, in 2017, among 750 thousand tourists, 60 thousand came for hair transplantation.  Most are from the Middle East.  Popular destinations for dental tourism are Thailand, which is called the "Land of Smiles", Vietnam, Mexico and Costa Rica, in Europe - Hungary and Poland.  The most common procedures are the installation of implants, veneers and crowns, bleaching.  For example, Hungary has become the best place in Europe for this direction, it is visited annually by about 7 thousand patients.  This is due to favorable prices, qualified doctors and modern technologies.  Another two popular areas of tourism are the restoration of sleep and weight loss, but not just on detox programs, but thanks to sports in the camps.  Fitness camps are actually recreational sports camps for adults, where in the circle of like-minded people you can surf in Sri Lanka with the Good Story Surf school, go skating on Lake Baikal with Team Trip or learn how to ski in the vicinity of Gstaad with Pro Trener, World Class or SlimFitClub trainers.  Six Senses Douro Valley The newest wellness trend is slip-retreats, which literally teach you to sleep.  As a rule, resorts for the restoration of sleep are located in picturesque places: in the mountains, overlooking the water.  For example, in Portugal, Germany, Italy and Switzerland.  Services include a menu of pillows: from special anti-snoring to filled with water or memory foam, sleep masks and earplugs to choose from, a music library, meditation on demand, as well as staff who can advise on sleep issues.  For example, the hotel in Manhattan, The Benjamin, designed the Rest & Renew program with Rebecca Robbins, a professor of sleep medicine at Cornell University.  Similar programs have Six Senses Douro Valley in Portugal, Peak Health in Switzerland and Lefay on Lake Garda.  Berlin ’ s Swisstel included in its DeepSleep retreat sessions of aroma- and light therapy, as well as inhalation of mountain air.  Beauty tourism is a thriving niche in the industry.  Clinics and hotels offer complete packages, including transfers, flights, meals and even excursions.  According to a joint study by Visa and Oxford Economics, the global medical tourism industry will grow by 25% per year over the next ten years.  Daria Bogomolova

passages.title: The gradual introduction of roof gardens to the metropolises of the country / What are the benefits of green roof structures?
passages.passage: Travelers from advanced industrial cities such as Tokyo, Toronto, Berlin, London, and Singapore are frequently confronted with buildings and towers, whether residential or commercial, with green roofs.  These green spaces, although not a new phenomenon in human history, were seen in distant times even in the influential civilizations of Iran, such as Mesopotamia, but after centuries of forgetfulness, they have now come back to the aid of human life and breathing.  According to the Tadbir and Hope Information Network, the cities mentioned are all suffering from high population and density, abundant industrial environments and high traffic and congestion, and therefore breathing space for the city is low.  As a result, the area of green space of the city has been unintentionally reduced and there is not much room for its expansion.  With these conditions, the maximum use of limited spaces to help the environment and life is a priority for urban planners.  It is not surprising that the city management system in all of these cities supports the creation of green spaces on the roof of buildings.  It is called the Garden of Eden.  There are similar examples of cities in our country.  Apart from Tehran, a number of metropolises of the country are also facing high population density and lack of green space and breathing space for the city, and no permanent solution has yet been found.  In recent years, as the problem of air pollution has become more serious, efforts have been made to use the world ’ s new solutions to address it.  Perhaps this is why the roof gardens in the metropolises of the country are slowly opening up.  Although these projects have not yet been comprehensively established among the public, it is foreseeable that in the coming years, they will become not only useful but necessary projects that will require the existence of a certain number of them in metropolitan areas.  Roofing gardens are a necessity in metropolises that grow vertically to horizontally and suffer from the problem of air pollution and lack of green space and even recreational space.  Because the advantage of roof gardens is not limited to helping the environment, it encompasses a large range of technical functions of buildings and even the social sphere of cities.  Reducing heat absorption by the building complex, reducing energy consumption, increasing urban green space per capita, improving air pollution, improving the quality of management and utilization of rainwater, social effects and creating a fun and refreshing environment, reducing travel within the city, beautifying the face and urban environment are some of the most important functions of the roof garden. passages.title: In megacities trying to recreate areas of wildlife
passages.passage: Landscape designers around the world are striving to make the urban environment in megacities more sustainable and close to nature.  To do this, in large cities, parks are planted on the site of abandoned industrial facilities, as well as gardens that can “evoke emotions ” among visitors.  This is reported by the BBC.  Part of the concept of the new garden is to give residents of cities access not only to greenery and fresher air, but also to sensations.  Visitors to the gardens will have access to all plants, walk barefoot on the paths of moss and even pick berries, but the plants will not be neatly planted on the beds.  "We're trying to get people to use all their senses by exploring the garden," said one of the project's creators, Andreas Christodoulou.  To create a sense of natural nature, designers often use bulk high beds, which are called Hugelkultur.  A feature of this type of farming is that all levels of beds are made from decomposing wood waste and other biomass.  “It ’ s the idea of creating mounds on the ground, contouring, instead of just leaving the ground flat.  We are trying to make the Hugelkultur-revolution, especially in the urban environment, ” said the representative of the organization Future Gardens London, landscape designer John Davis, who believes that gardens “do not have to be flat ”.  Another direction of greening megacities is the planting of parks and gardens on the territory of abandoned industrial facilities.  At the heart of such gardens are metal structures and concrete blocks.  However, even small plots of land are suitable for plants, which in turn will attract insects.  Park designer Martin Wilson said that for him, inspiring examples are the High Line Park on the site of the elevated railway in New York and the Duisburg-Nord landscape park on the site of the steel plant in Duisburg (Germany), as well as places that have been abandoned and which have not yet begun to be used for other purposes - for example, the former MG Rover plant in Birmingham (UK).  "The concept may be to restore abandoned objects in the form in which they are known," - said the designer.  The material was provided by the project "+ 1".

passages.title: "Rubinstein Street Effect". Yuri Berestov about how the union under the roof of the technopark helps business (photo)
passages.passage: Photo: Yury Berestov, CEO of Aira Technopark Yury Berestov, President of the Association of Smart Cities and CEO of Aira Technopark, told Fontanka why the creation of bicycle paths is especially important in the era of coronavirus, how the urban environment is being transformed and why the effect of Rubinstein Street works for companies uniting in technoparks. – You have been building bicycle paths in different cities of Russia since 2014.  Is the interest of cities in the development of cycling growing? — In St. Petersburg, cyclists are more and more, but they ride mainly on sidewalks.  Surprisingly, even pedestrians consider this normal.  And cyclists are different: now, especially during the coronavirus epidemic, there are many couriers - they ride like kamikaze, so it can even be dangerous for pedestrians.  Driving on the road is dangerous for cyclists.  That ’ s because we don ’ t have a normal infrastructure.  What is done on Fontanka, for example, it is difficult to call a real bike path - cars are parked there, there is no single traffic scheme and still have to go to the sidewalk or road.  Safety is not thought out, there is no lighting, so they are simply not visible in the evening.  Meanwhile, we see that after the epidemic in European cities, where cycling is already developed, even more money is allocated to transfer as many people as possible from public transport to bicycles.  To get into the global trend, it is necessary that the Ministry of Construction make cycle paths part of the program for the development of a comfortable urban environment.  And we intend to apply to departments of different levels with such an initiative. – What should be a modern bike path? – It should be a comprehensive infrastructure facility that includes not only the lane itself, but also bathrooms for cyclists, repair stations, bike rental, recreation areas.  We have developed a controlled backlight system, it is inexpensive, but allows you to program a light wave, show the direction of movement.  Components for "smart" bike paths (Smart Track) are produced in Grozny on the basis of the rehabilitation center of the society of the blind, the parts are made by employees - disabled I and II groups of vision.  The rest of the products are produced at the enterprise in the Leningrad region.  Photo: press service of the company "Aira" - Where has the new technology already been used? - A landmark for us was the work in the city of Almetyevsk in the Republic of Tatarstan.  There we built and smart bike paths, and traffic lights under the feet, and swing balancers with game mechanics, and children's video playgrounds.  Thus, a new image of the city was formed, and at the Moscow International Forum Almetyevsk was recognized as the most comfortable urban settlement of Russia-2017 and the startup capital of Russia.  And in 2019, within the framework of the IV International Cycling Congress, he received a special prize "Leadership" for the bicycle project implemented by our company.  It was thanks to this project that Natalia Fishman (a member of the reconstruction team at the Gorky Central Park of Culture and Culture in Moscow) noticed us in 2017 and invited us to participate together with ArchDesant in the reconstruction of 60 parks in Tatarstan.  A bench made of light-diffusing fiberglass Photo: the press service of the company "Aira" Another cycling project we implemented in 2017 in the city of Grozny.  In turn, the mayor of Grozny, Ibrahim Zakriev, who now holds the post of head of the administration of the head and government of the Chechen Republic, presented an innovative bicycle infrastructure to St. Petersburg - now you can see it on the updated pedestrian zone on Karpovka.  In this project, we were supported by the administration of the Petrogradsky District and the deputy chairman of the landscaping committee Larisa Kanunnikova.  In general, we still 3-4 years ago came up with the idea of ​ ​ building bicycle paths in St. Petersburg.  Moreover, in the proposed option, you do not need to spend money from the budget - the city allocates a route, and along it you could place cafes and pop-up stores, banks, chain sports stores, points for the sale of healthy food.  So the track will pay for itself, it turns out the option of a reliable public-private partnership. — If in Almetyevsk it was easier to implement ideas than in Moscow or St. Petersburg, then maybe you need to pay attention to small cities?  For example, in the Leningrad region? - In a big city, of course, it is more difficult to allocate space, because everything is already built up, there are not enough roads.  It is much easier to design when laying new streets, and some developers in their residential complexes create such infrastructure.  But it is necessary that there be a connection between these islands of civilization.  A progressive solution would be the construction of the world ’ s first circular cycle path around the city, in parallel with the creation of a circular railway route, which was agreed by the city authorities with Russian Railways last year at the St. Petersburg Economic Forum.  The bicycle ring will unite the sleeping areas, and the lines will go from it to the interior of the city, including parks, and to the Leningrad region.  This will relieve the traffic jams, and it is useful for health, and you do not have to push in public transport.  Another project we would like to take part in is a bike path from Svetogorsk to the border with Finland.  In general, we learned about it from the publication on "Fontanka" and appealed to both the Finns and the administration of the Leningrad region to consider our proposal. - At what stage of negotiations with the government of St. Petersburg, districts or city services? - We are actively working with "Lensvet" - our technology of marker illumination is new, it has not been used before, so it needs to be agreed, submit all the technical characteristics and documentation, so that city specialists can service it.  Another option for its use is recumbent traffic lights, the first we installed in 2015 in Moscow on Mira Avenue, in St. Petersburg, the pilot sample was on Malaya Morskaya Street.  Such traffic lights are also installed in Grozny and Almetyevsk, and their peculiarity lies in the use of the optical shock-resistant polymer developed by us.  If the road is wide, then under the feet the color of the signal can be seen much better than a little man on the other side of the street.  In addition, people most of the time look at smartphones, their attention is scattered, and the edge of the eye under the feet is more convenient to look than to raise your head.  According to experts, such a traffic light reduces the likelihood of an accident by up to 90%.  Potentially everyone is for the introduction of this technology, but you still need to go the way of approvals. – Is there a demand for innovative improvement now? – Previously, people often spoke negatively about the improvement, holidays and New Year ’ s decoration of cities.  Modern MAFs (small architectural forms) and art objects that have long become familiar in the West and are already considered an indispensable element of improvement, our residents seemed an unnecessary waste of budget money.  Even despite the fact that some of the elements in terms of cost did not differ from the dull, bored for decades of objects.  Gradually, there is an understanding that this is another item of expenditure, and a comfortable urban environment is needed first of all by the citizens themselves.  The turning point occurred in 2013, when the Gorky Central Park opened in Moscow after reconstruction.  It became the first world-class park in Russia, a space for recreation, sports, dancing and outdoor games.  His concept has revolutionized the thinking of many.  The members of the creative team that worked on the project later became the ideologists of creating such modern spaces in Russia.  The steady growth of the market began after the opening of the Zaryadye Park in the capital and the reconstruction of VDNH.  This trend was noticed in the regions, where we saw what modern public spaces can be.  There was a priority federal project “Formation of a comfortable urban environment ”.  Thanks to him, world-class projects are being implemented today.  Now young architects are actively attracted to it, centers of competence are created in the regions. – How fully do ideas come to life? – We notice that often the quality of execution of what looked beautiful in the project turns out to be low in practice.  Young architects often simply do not understand what small architectural forms should be made of, how to process the material so that the object stands for more than one season, but 5-10 years, does not rot, does not rust, does not break.  In particular, that ’ s why we decided to gather professional participants of the landscaping market under one roof.  So there was a technopark "Aira" with free rent for residents.  In September, together with our partners, we will begin to hold seminars, lectures for architects and all those who are engaged in projects “comfortable environment ” and“ smart city ” in the regions.  When they return home, they will be able to put their knowledge into practice.  If the Ministry of Construction supports us, we can open such technoparks in other regions. –

passages.title: Pocket park, this year new renovation of 50 - citizens out of the house there is a park, you can walk, chat, fitness, enjoy the green -- News Morning Post official website
passages.passage: Morning Post reporter Yu Wenyan at the corner of Fuxing East Road and Zhonghua Road, there is a small green space of only 500 square meters, which has installed three leisure seats and some small outdoor fitness equipment, which has become a "Cao Jia Street small garden" in the eyes of nearby residents. A number of pocket parks, which are often referred to as street gardens in the past, their presence not only allows nearby residents to walk, chat, fitness, and enjoy the green, but also lights up the environmental face of the block.  It is reported that the city built 47 pocket parks last year, and this year will build or upgrade 50.  Last year, 47 pocket parks were built at the corner of Fuxing East Road and Zhonghua Road, with a small green space of only 500 square meters.  Once, it was a green space, and now, it has become a "small garden in Cao Jia Street" in the eyes of nearby residents.  In Hongkou District, after a number of illegal buildings were demolished, a pocket park was built.  For example, the Huishan Garden at 207 Lintong Road, do not look at it with an area of only 408 square meters, but "five dirty", not only has exquisite and small green products, but also fitness trails.  In order to coordinate with the surrounding architectural style, the entrance to the park has also been designed in the style of Shikumen.  More than 2,300 square meters of public green space has been built in the area of 1501 North Xinshi Road, Jiangwan Town.  If there are no pavilions and seats for rest, it is also a little larger than the green space of Cao Jia Street.  But with activities and rest facilities, it becomes a simple little park.  According to incomplete statistics, 47 pocket parks were built in the city last year.  Pocket Park is not clearly defined Pocket Park, which originated from the proposal of the New York Parks Association in 1963, originally refers to small parks scattered in high-density urban centers and distributed in plaques.  Since the beginning of just over half a century, the United States, Britain, Japan and China and other countries have begun to have their own unique "pocket park plan".  Today's pocket parks refer to small green open spaces scattered in plaques in the city.  At present, there is no clear definition of pocket parks, and various small green spaces, small parks, street gardens, and small community sports venues in the city are common pocket parks.  Liu Yuelai, a scholar at Tongji University's School of Architecture and Urban Planning, said that there is currently no clear definition of the size of the pocket park.  In terms of area, he personally feels that it can be counted as small as tens of square meters and as large as thousands of square meters.  Unlike the comprehensive park, it offers simple and short breaks, such as a walk after a meal, a small sitting or children's play.  The city's greening department said that at present, their definition of the street garden from the area generally refers to the area of 300-3000 square meters of green space.  The municipal greening and cityscape administration bureau recently introduced that this year Shencheng plans to build or upgrade 50 pocket parks.  The actual number may be more than that.  Among the 79 colorful community projects recently released in Pudong, nearly 40 projects are defined as pocket parks. The pocket park in Hongkou District is planning to build the second phase of Yongnian Li, so that the pocket park function is becoming more and more perfect.  This year, Putuo plans to build a new 10,000 li community green space with a total area of 14,930 square meters, consisting of forests, wetlands and pocket parks.  The first part covers an area of about 10,970 square meters, and is designed to be an accessible urban forest and wetland.  The second part is located at the northwest corner of Wanquan Road and Fu Ping Road, covering an area of about 3960 square meters, and is designed to be positioned as a pocket park.  Fang Yan, deputy director of the municipal greening and cityscape administration bureau, said that the greening department is trying to make more parks around the citizens, even some street gardens and pocket parks, so that people can walk in parks not far from their homes.  According to the relevant person in charge of the municipal greening and cityscape administration bureau, the goal of allowing citizens to go out 500 meters to see a 3,000 square meter park green space has been basically achieved.  However, some residents feel that the greening of Shanghai is not enough.  Shanghai is still far behind Beijing, Hangzhou, Guangzhou and other cities, as well as New York, London and Paris.  For example, according to the area of public green space in the city and the base ratio of the resident population of more than 24 million, the per capita public green space is only about 8%, while some cities in China are generally more than 10%.  Therefore, in the case of limited land resources, Shanghai can only build more "pocket parks" and make dojo in snail shells.  It is understood that there are 243 urban parks in Shanghai, and by 2020, the number of urban parks will reach 300, forming a three-level system of "pocket parks - community parks - regional parks", and basically realizing that citizens go out 500 meters to have parks.

**Report on the Benefits of Small "Pocket Parks" in High-Density Urban Settings**

Pocket parks are small-scale urban open spaces that provide a refuge against city crowds and a place for rest and relaxation [ee368122-879d-43ed-98ca-293ce65ddf38]. 
They are a solution to offset part of the lack of green spaces in urban centers, residential complexes, and other areas of the city [ee368122-879d-43ed-98ca-293ce65ddf38].

The benefits of pocket parks in high-density urban settings include reducing air pollution [2f31b682-dd36-426c-aee5-509e5172844e]. 
They also improve the quality of management and utilization of rainwater [2f31b682-dd36-426c-aee5-509e5172844e]. 
Additionally, pocket parks increase urban green space per capita [2f31b682-dd36-426c-aee5-509e5172844e]. 
Furthermore, they provide a space for recreation, sports, dancing, and outdoor games [93e05d05-4e27-428b-ad4d-dbe50339cb48].

Pocket parks can be designed to evoke emotions among visitors, providing a sense of natural nature [ec96c7db-2829-4874-9fc2-55f35770f271]. 
They can include features such as bulk high beds, which are called Hugelkultur, made from decomposing wood waste and other biomass [ec96c7db-2829-4874-9fc2-55f35770f271]. 
These beds are designed to create a sense of natural nature, allowing visitors to explore the garden using all their senses [ec96c7db-2829-4874-9fc2-55f35770f271].

The design of pocket parks is closely related to the greening and sustainability of the city [19ed0e93-9c89-41e1-9312-86d1ef81346b]. 
Emerging towns and new communities are more capable of implementing greening policy declarations and integrating physical elements of nature [19ed0e93-9c89-41e1-9312-86d1ef81346b]. 
Cities close to the valley and mountains are easier to introduce walkers and bike-friendly infrastructure [19ed0e93-9c89-41e1-9312-86d1ef81346b].

Pocket parks can be used to create a natural play space for children, allowing them to engage in free play with no standard gameplay and regulations [19ed0e93-9c89-41e1-9312-86d1ef81346b]. 
This type of play space can include features such as game elements, basic climbing tree trunks, running into the passage, crossing the net bridge over the pool, and using imagination to create a place [19ed0e93-9c89-41e1-9312-86d1ef81346b].

The construction of pocket parks can be done in partnership with local authorities, such as the Deputy of Infrastructure, Transport and Traffic Affairs [ee368122-879d-43ed-98ca-293ce65ddf38]. 
The goal of creating pocket parks is to increase urban green space per capita and balance the distribution of amenities throughout the city [ee368122-879d-43ed-98ca-293ce65ddf38].

In summary, pocket parks are a valuable resource for high-density urban settings, providing a range of benefits for both residents and the environment. 
They offer a space for recreation, sports, and outdoor games, as well as a refuge against city crowds and a place for rest and relaxation. 
By incorporating features such as Hugelkultur and natural play spaces, pocket parks can be designed to evoke emotions and promote a sense of natural nature.

Title: The gradual introduction of roof gardens to the metropolises of the country / What are the benefits of green roof structures?
Content: Travelers from advanced industrial cities such as Tokyo, Toronto, Berlin, London, and Singapore are frequently confronted with buildings and towers, whether residential or commercial, with green roofs.  These green spaces, although not a new phenomenon in human history, were seen in distant times even in the influential civilizations of Iran, such as Mesopotamia, but after centuries of forgetfulness, they have now come back to the aid of human life and breathing.  According to the Tadbir and Hope Information Network, the cities mentioned are all suffering from high population and density, abundant industrial environments and high traffic and congestion, and therefore breathing space for the city is low.  As a result, the area of green space of the city has been unintentionally reduced and there is not much room for its expansion.  With these conditions, the maximum use of limited spaces to help the environment and life is a priority for urban planners.  It is not surprising that the city management system in all of these cities supports the creation of green spaces on the roof of buildings.  It is called the Garden of Eden.  There are similar examples of cities in our country.  Apart from Tehran, a number of metropolises of the country are also facing high population density and lack of green space and breathing space for the city, and no permanent solution has yet been found.  In recent years, as the problem of air pollution has become more serious, efforts have been made to use the world ’ s new solutions to address it.  Perhaps this is why the roof gardens in the metropolises of the country are slowly opening up.  Although these projects have not yet been comprehensively established among the public, it is foreseeable that in the coming years, they will become not only useful but necessary projects that will require the existence of a certain number of them in metropolitan areas.  Roofing gardens are a necessity in metropolises that grow vertically to horizontally and suffer from the problem of air pollution and lack of green space and even recreational space.  Because the advantage of roof gardens is not limited to helping the environment, it encompasses a large range of technical functions of buildings and even the social sphere of cities.  Reducing heat absorption by the building complex, reducing energy consumption, increasing urban green space per capita, improving air pollution, improving the quality of management and utilization of rainwater, social effects and creating a fun and refreshing environment, reducing travel within the city, beautifying the face and urban environment are some of the most important functions of the roof garden.  Currently, the authorities of some metropolises have officially announced their support for the implementation and expansion of the roof garden.  This is especially seen in the cities of Mashhad, Qom, Tabriz, Isfahan and Kerman and a few other cities.  The municipalities have announced their readiness to support the roof gardens.  Several major projects have been implemented in each of them.  In Isfahan, these projects started a few years ago, in Qom, structures that have a roof garden are discounted in receiving a license.  In Mashhad, this issue has been taken seriously by both the authorities and the executives of the projects, and for example, in the project of the 5-star Arman Hotel of Mashhad, due to its size and technical and structural specifications, a combination of the extensive roof garden system and the centralized roof garden system has been selected.  In Tabriz and Kerman, several projects have been started in this field.  With this trend, it can be predicted that with the implementation of this project and similar projects, the roof gardens will open their place in the major cities; an event that is a necessity and hope that this issue will cause other cities of the country to gradually enter this area and even set criteria to support such structures. Title: In megacities trying to recreate areas of wildlife
Content: Landscape designers around the world are striving to make the urban environment in megacities more sustainable and close to nature.  To do this, in large cities, parks are planted on the site of abandoned industrial facilities, as well as gardens that can “evoke emotions ” among visitors.  This is reported by the BBC.  Part of the concept of the new garden is to give residents of cities access not only to greenery and fresher air, but also to sensations.  Visitors to the gardens will have access to all plants, walk barefoot on the paths of moss and even pick berries, but the plants will not be neatly planted on the beds.  "We're trying to get people to use all their senses by exploring the garden," said one of the project's creators, Andreas Christodoulou.  To create a sense of natural nature, designers often use bulk high beds, which are called Hugelkultur.  A feature of this type of farming is that all levels of beds are made from decomposing wood waste and other biomass.  “It ’ s the idea of creating mounds on the ground, contouring, instead of just leaving the ground flat.  We are trying to make the Hugelkultur-revolution, especially in the urban environment, ” said the representative of the organization Future Gardens London, landscape designer John Davis, who believes that gardens “do not have to be flat ”.  Another direction of greening megacities is the planting of parks and gardens on the territory of abandoned industrial facilities.  At the heart of such gardens are metal structures and concrete blocks.  However, even small plots of land are suitable for plants, which in turn will attract insects.  Park designer Martin Wilson said that for him, inspiring examples are the High Line Park on the site of the elevated railway in New York and the Duisburg-Nord landscape park on the site of the steel plant in Duisburg (Germany), as well as places that have been abandoned and which have not yet begun to be used for other purposes - for example, the former MG Rover plant in Birmingham (UK).  "The concept may be to restore abandoned objects in the form in which they are known," - said the designer.  The material was provided by the project "+ 1".

Title: "Rubinstein Street Effect". Yuri Berestov about how the union under the roof of the technopark helps business (photo)
Content: Photo: Yury Berestov, CEO of Aira Technopark Yury Berestov, President of the Association of Smart Cities and CEO of Aira Technopark, told Fontanka why the creation of bicycle paths is especially important in the era of coronavirus, how the urban environment is being transformed and why the effect of Rubinstein Street works for companies uniting in technoparks. – You have been building bicycle paths in different cities of Russia since 2014.  Is the interest of cities in the development of cycling growing? — In St. Petersburg, cyclists are more and more, but they ride mainly on sidewalks.  Surprisingly, even pedestrians consider this normal.  And cyclists are different: now, especially during the coronavirus epidemic, there are many couriers - they ride like kamikaze, so it can even be dangerous for pedestrians.  Driving on the road is dangerous for cyclists.  That ’ s because we don ’ t have a normal infrastructure.  What is done on Fontanka, for example, it is difficult to call a real bike path - cars are parked there, there is no single traffic scheme and still have to go to the sidewalk or road.  Safety is not thought out, there is no lighting, so they are simply not visible in the evening.  Meanwhile, we see that after the epidemic in European cities, where cycling is already developed, even more money is allocated to transfer as many people as possible from public transport to bicycles.  To get into the global trend, it is necessary that the Ministry of Construction make cycle paths part of the program for the development of a comfortable urban environment.  And we intend to apply to departments of different levels with such an initiative. – What should be a modern bike path? – It should be a comprehensive infrastructure facility that includes not only the lane itself, but also bathrooms for cyclists, repair stations, bike rental, recreation areas.  We have developed a controlled backlight system, it is inexpensive, but allows you to program a light wave, show the direction of movement.  Components for "smart" bike paths (Smart Track) are produced in Grozny on the basis of the rehabilitation center of the society of the blind, the parts are made by employees - disabled I and II groups of vision.  The rest of the products are produced at the enterprise in the Leningrad region.  Photo: press service of the company "Aira" - Where has the new technology already been used? - A landmark for us was the work in the city of Almetyevsk in the Republic of Tatarstan.  There we built and smart bike paths, and traffic lights under the feet, and swing balancers with game mechanics, and children's video playgrounds.  Thus, a new image of the city was formed, and at the Moscow International Forum Almetyevsk was recognized as the most comfortable urban settlement of Russia-2017 and the startup capital of Russia.  And in 2019, within the framework of the IV International Cycling Congress, he received a special prize "Leadership" for the bicycle project implemented by our company.  It was thanks to this project that Natalia Fishman (a member of the reconstruction team at the Gorky Central Park of Culture and Culture in Moscow) noticed us in 2017 and invited us to participate together with ArchDesant in the reconstruction of 60 parks in Tatarstan.  A bench made of light-diffusing fiberglass Photo: the press service of the company "Aira" Another cycling project we implemented in 2017 in the city of Grozny.  In turn, the mayor of Grozny, Ibrahim Zakriev, who now holds the post of head of the administration of the head and government of the Chechen Republic, presented an innovative bicycle infrastructure to St. Petersburg - now you can see it on the updated pedestrian zone on Karpovka.  In this project, we were supported by the administration of the Petrogradsky District and the deputy chairman of the landscaping committee Larisa Kanunnikova.  In general, we still 3-4 years ago came up with the idea of ​ ​ building bicycle paths in St. Petersburg.  Moreover, in the proposed option, you do not need to spend money from the budget - the city allocates a route, and along it you could place cafes and pop-up stores, banks, chain sports stores, points for the sale of healthy food.  So the track will pay for itself, it turns out the option of a reliable public-private partnership. — If in Almetyevsk it was easier to implement ideas than in Moscow or St. Petersburg, then maybe you need to pay attention to small cities?  For example, in the Leningrad region? - In a big city, of course, it is more difficult to allocate space, because everything is already built up, there are not enough roads.  It is much easier to design when laying new streets, and some developers in their residential complexes create such infrastructure.  But it is necessary that there be a connection between these islands of civilization.  A progressive solution would be the construction of the world ’ s first circular cycle path around the city, in parallel with the creation of a circular railway route, which was agreed by the city authorities with Russian Railways last year at the St. Petersburg Economic Forum.  The bicycle ring will unite the sleeping areas, and the lines will go from it to the interior of the city, including parks, and to the Leningrad region.  This will relieve the traffic jams, and it is useful for health, and you do not have to push in public transport.  Another project we would like to take part in is a bike path from Svetogorsk to the border with Finland.  In general, we learned about it from the publication on "Fontanka" and appealed to both the Finns and the administration of the Leningrad region to consider our proposal. - At what stage of negotiations with the government of St. Petersburg, districts or city services? - We are actively working with "Lensvet" - our technology of marker illumination is new, it has not been used before, so it needs to be agreed, submit all the technical characteristics and documentation, so that city specialists can service it.  Another option for its use is recumbent traffic lights, the first we installed in 2015 in Moscow on Mira Avenue, in St. Petersburg, the pilot sample was on Malaya Morskaya Street.  Such traffic lights are also installed in Grozny and Almetyevsk, and their peculiarity lies in the use of the optical shock-resistant polymer developed by us.  If the road is wide, then under the feet the color of the signal can be seen much better than a little man on the other side of the street.  In addition, people most of the time look at smartphones, their attention is scattered, and the edge of the eye under the feet is more convenient to look than to raise your head.  According to experts, such a traffic light reduces the likelihood of an accident by up to 90%.  Potentially everyone is for the introduction of this technology, but you still need to go the way of approvals. – Is there a demand for innovative improvement now? – Previously, people often spoke negatively about the improvement, holidays and New Year ’ s decoration of cities.  Modern MAFs (small architectural forms) and art objects that have long become familiar in the West and are already considered an indispensable element of improvement, our residents seemed an unnecessary waste of budget money.  Even despite the fact that some of the elements in terms of cost did not differ from the dull, bored for decades of objects.  Gradually, there is an understanding that this is another item of expenditure, and a comfortable urban environment is needed first of all by the citizens themselves.  The turning point occurred in 2013, when the Gorky Central Park opened in Moscow after reconstruction.  It became the first world-class park in Russia, a space for recreation, sports, dancing and outdoor games.  His concept has revolutionized the thinking of many.  The members of the creative team that worked on the project later became the ideologists of creating such modern spaces in Russia.  The steady growth of the market began after the opening of the Zaryadye Park in the capital and the reconstruction of VDNH.  This trend was noticed in the regions, where we saw what modern public spaces can be.  There was a priority federal project “Formation of a comfortable urban environment ”.  Thanks to him, world-class projects are being implemented today.  Now young architects are actively attracted to it, centers of competence are created in the regions. – How fully do ideas come to life? – We notice that often the quality of execution of what looked beautiful in the project turns out to be low in practice.  Young architects often simply do not understand what small architectural forms should be made of, how to process the material so that the object stands for more than one season, but 5-10 years, does not rot, does not rust, does not break. Title: Pocket park, this year new renovation of 50 - citizens out of the house there is a park, you can walk, chat, fitness, enjoy the green -- News Morning Post official website
Content: Morning Post reporter Yu Wenyan at the corner of Fuxing East Road and Zhonghua Road, there is a small green space of only 500 square meters, which has installed three leisure seats and some small outdoor fitness equipment, which has become a "Cao Jia Street small garden" in the eyes of nearby residents. A number of pocket parks, which are often referred to as street gardens in the past, their presence not only allows nearby residents to walk, chat, fitness, and enjoy the green, but also lights up the environmental face of the block.  It is reported that the city built 47 pocket parks last year, and this year will build or upgrade 50.  Last year, 47 pocket parks were built at the corner of Fuxing East Road and Zhonghua Road, with a small green space of only 500 square meters.  Once, it was a green space, and now, it has become a "small garden in Cao Jia Street" in the eyes of nearby residents.  In Hongkou District, after a number of illegal buildings were demolished, a pocket park was built.  For example, the Huishan Garden at 207 Lintong Road, do not look at it with an area of only 408 square meters, but "five dirty", not only has exquisite and small green products, but also fitness trails.  In order to coordinate with the surrounding architectural style, the entrance to the park has also been designed in the style of Shikumen.  More than 2,300 square meters of public green space has been built in the area of 1501 North Xinshi Road, Jiangwan Town.  If there are no pavilions and seats for rest, it is also a little larger than the green space of Cao Jia Street.  But with activities and rest facilities, it becomes a simple little park.  According to incomplete statistics, 47 pocket parks were built in the city last year.  Pocket Park is not clearly defined Pocket Park, which originated from the proposal of the New York Parks Association in 1963, originally refers to small parks scattered in high-density urban centers and distributed in plaques.  Since the beginning of just over half a century, the United States, Britain, Japan and China and other countries have begun to have their own unique "pocket park plan".  Today's pocket parks refer to small green open spaces scattered in plaques in the city.  At present, there is no clear definition of pocket parks, and various small green spaces, small parks, street gardens, and small community sports venues in the city are common pocket parks.  Liu Yuelai, a scholar at Tongji University's School of Architecture and Urban Planning, said that there is currently no clear definition of the size of the pocket park.  In terms of area, he personally feels that it can be counted as small as tens of square meters and as large as thousands of square meters.  Unlike the comprehensive park, it offers simple and short breaks, such as a walk after a meal, a small sitting or children's play.  The city's greening department said that at present, their definition of the street garden from the area generally refers to the area of 300-3000 square meters of green space.  The municipal greening and cityscape administration bureau recently introduced that this year Shencheng plans to build or upgrade 50 pocket parks.  The actual number may be more than that.  Among the 79 colorful community projects recently released in Pudong, nearly 40 projects are defined as pocket parks. The pocket park in Hongkou District is planning to build the second phase of Yongnian Li, so that the pocket park function is becoming more and more perfect.  This year, Putuo plans to build a new 10,000 li community green space with a total area of 14,930 square meters, consisting of forests, wetlands and pocket parks.  The first part covers an area of about 10,970 square meters, and is designed to be an accessible urban forest and wetland.  The second part is located at the northwest corner of Wanquan Road and Fu Ping Road, covering an area of about 3960 square meters, and is designed to be positioned as a pocket park.  Fang Yan, deputy director of the municipal greening and cityscape administration bureau, said that the greening department is trying to make more parks around the citizens, even some street gardens and pocket parks, so that people can walk in parks not far from their homes.  According to the relevant person in charge of the municipal greening and cityscape administration bureau, the goal of allowing citizens to go out 500 meters to see a 3,000 square meter park green space has been basically achieved.  However, some residents feel that the greening of Shanghai is not enough.  Shanghai is still far behind Beijing, Hangzhou, Guangzhou and other cities, as well as New York, London and Paris.  For example, according to the area of public green space in the city and the base ratio of the resident population of more than 24 million, the per capita public green space is only about 8%, while some cities in China are generally more than 10%.  Therefore, in the case of limited land resources, Shanghai can only build more "pocket parks" and make dojo in snail shells.  It is understood that there are 243 urban parks in Shanghai, and by 2020, the number of urban parks will reach 300, forming a three-level system of "pocket parks - community parks - regional parks", and basically realizing that citizens go out 500 meters to have parks.

Title: The gradual introduction of roof gardens to the metropolises of the country / What are the benefits of green roof structures?
Content: Travelers from advanced industrial cities such as Tokyo, Toronto, Berlin, London, and Singapore are frequently confronted with buildings and towers, whether residential or commercial, with green roofs.  These green spaces, although not a new phenomenon in human history, were seen in distant times even in the influential civilizations of Iran, such as Mesopotamia, but after centuries of forgetfulness, they have now come back to the aid of human life and breathing.  According to the Tadbir and Hope Information Network, the cities mentioned are all suffering from high population and density, abundant industrial environments and high traffic and congestion, and therefore breathing space for the city is low.  As a result, the area of green space of the city has been unintentionally reduced and there is not much room for its expansion.  With these conditions, the maximum use of limited spaces to help the environment and life is a priority for urban planners.  It is not surprising that the city management system in all of these cities supports the creation of green spaces on the roof of buildings.  It is called the Garden of Eden.  There are similar examples of cities in our country.  Apart from Tehran, a number of metropolises of the country are also facing high population density and lack of green space and breathing space for the city, and no permanent solution has yet been found.  In recent years, as the problem of air pollution has become more serious, efforts have been made to use the world ’ s new solutions to address it.  Perhaps this is why the roof gardens in the metropolises of the country are slowly opening up.  Although these projects have not yet been comprehensively established among the public, it is foreseeable that in the coming years, they will become not only useful but necessary projects that will require the existence of a certain number of them in metropolitan areas.  Roofing gardens are a necessity in metropolises that grow vertically to horizontally and suffer from the problem of air pollution and lack of green space and even recreational space.  Because the advantage of roof gardens is not limited to helping the environment, it encompasses a large range of technical functions of buildings and even the social sphere of cities.  Reducing heat absorption by the building complex, reducing energy consumption, increasing urban green space per capita, improving air pollution, improving the quality of management and utilization of rainwater, social effects and creating a fun and refreshing environment, reducing travel within the city, beautifying the face and urban environment are some of the most important functions of the roof garden.  Currently, the authorities of some metropolises have officially announced their support for the implementation and expansion of the roof garden.  This is especially seen in the cities of Mashhad, Qom, Tabriz, Isfahan and Kerman and a few other cities.  The municipalities have announced their readiness to support the roof gardens.  Several major projects have been implemented in each of them.  In Isfahan, these projects started a few years ago, in Qom, structures that have a roof garden are discounted in receiving a license.  In Mashhad, this issue has been taken seriously by both the authorities and the executives of the projects, and for example, in the project of the 5-star Arman Hotel of Mashhad, due to its size and technical and structural specifications, a combination of the extensive roof garden system and the centralized roof garden system has been selected.  In Tabriz and Kerman, several projects have been started in this field.  With this trend, it can be predicted that with the implementation of this project and similar projects, the roof gardens will open their place in the major cities; an event that is a necessity and hope that this issue will cause other cities of the country to gradually enter this area and even set criteria to support such structures. Title: In megacities trying to recreate areas of wildlife
Content: Landscape designers around the world are striving to make the urban environment in megacities more sustainable and close to nature.  To do this, in large cities, parks are planted on the site of abandoned industrial facilities, as well as gardens that can “evoke emotions ” among visitors.  This is reported by the BBC.  Part of the concept of the new garden is to give residents of cities access not only to greenery and fresher air, but also to sensations.  Visitors to the gardens will have access to all plants, walk barefoot on the paths of moss and even pick berries, but the plants will not be neatly planted on the beds.  "We're trying to get people to use all their senses by exploring the garden," said one of the project's creators, Andreas Christodoulou.  To create a sense of natural nature, designers often use bulk high beds, which are called Hugelkultur.  A feature of this type of farming is that all levels of beds are made from decomposing wood waste and other biomass.  “It ’ s the idea of creating mounds on the ground, contouring, instead of just leaving the ground flat.  We are trying to make the Hugelkultur-revolution, especially in the urban environment, ” said the representative of the organization Future Gardens London, landscape designer John Davis, who believes that gardens “do not have to be flat ”.  Another direction of greening megacities is the planting of parks and gardens on the territory of abandoned industrial facilities.  At the heart of such gardens are metal structures and concrete blocks.  However, even small plots of land are suitable for plants, which in turn will attract insects.  Park designer Martin Wilson said that for him, inspiring examples are the High Line Park on the site of the elevated railway in New York and the Duisburg-Nord landscape park on the site of the steel plant in Duisburg (Germany), as well as places that have been abandoned and which have not yet begun to be used for other purposes - for example, the former MG Rover plant in Birmingham (UK).  "The concept may be to restore abandoned objects in the form in which they are known," - said the designer.  The material was provided by the project "+ 1".
