Title: "Rubinstein Street Effect". Yuri Berestov about how the union under the roof of the technopark helps business (photo)
Content: Photo: Yury Berestov, CEO of Aira Technopark Yury Berestov, President of the Association of Smart Cities and CEO of Aira Technopark, told Fontanka why the creation of bicycle paths is especially important in the era of coronavirus, how the urban environment is being transformed and why the effect of Rubinstein Street works for companies uniting in technoparks. – You have been building bicycle paths in different cities of Russia since 2014.  Is the interest of cities in the development of cycling growing? — In St. Petersburg, cyclists are more and more, but they ride mainly on sidewalks.  Surprisingly, even pedestrians consider this normal.  And cyclists are different: now, especially during the coronavirus epidemic, there are many couriers - they ride like kamikaze, so it can even be dangerous for pedestrians.  Driving on the road is dangerous for cyclists.  That ’ s because we don ’ t have a normal infrastructure.  What is done on Fontanka, for example, it is difficult to call a real bike path - cars are parked there, there is no single traffic scheme and still have to go to the sidewalk or road.  Safety is not thought out, there is no lighting, so they are simply not visible in the evening.  Meanwhile, we see that after the epidemic in European cities, where cycling is already developed, even more money is allocated to transfer as many people as possible from public transport to bicycles.  To get into the global trend, it is necessary that the Ministry of Construction make cycle paths part of the program for the development of a comfortable urban environment.  And we intend to apply to departments of different levels with such an initiative. – What should be a modern bike path? – It should be a comprehensive infrastructure facility that includes not only the lane itself, but also bathrooms for cyclists, repair stations, bike rental, recreation areas.  We have developed a controlled backlight system, it is inexpensive, but allows you to program a light wave, show the direction of movement.  Components for "smart" bike paths (Smart Track) are produced in Grozny on the basis of the rehabilitation center of the society of the blind, the parts are made by employees - disabled I and II groups of vision.  The rest of the products are produced at the enterprise in the Leningrad region.  Photo: press service of the company "Aira" - Where has the new technology already been used? - A landmark for us was the work in the city of Almetyevsk in the Republic of Tatarstan.  There we built and smart bike paths, and traffic lights under the feet, and swing balancers with game mechanics, and children's video playgrounds.  Thus, a new image of the city was formed, and at the Moscow International Forum Almetyevsk was recognized as the most comfortable urban settlement of Russia-2017 and the startup capital of Russia.  And in 2019, within the framework of the IV International Cycling Congress, he received a special prize "Leadership" for the bicycle project implemented by our company.  It was thanks to this project that Natalia Fishman (a member of the reconstruction team at the Gorky Central Park of Culture and Culture in Moscow) noticed us in 2017 and invited us to participate together with ArchDesant in the reconstruction of 60 parks in Tatarstan.  A bench made of light-diffusing fiberglass Photo: the press service of the company "Aira" Another cycling project we implemented in 2017 in the city of Grozny.  In turn, the mayor of Grozny, Ibrahim Zakriev, who now holds the post of head of the administration of the head and government of the Chechen Republic, presented an innovative bicycle infrastructure to St. Petersburg - now you can see it on the updated pedestrian zone on Karpovka.  In this project, we were supported by the administration of the Petrogradsky District and the deputy chairman of the landscaping committee Larisa Kanunnikova.  In general, we still 3-4 years ago came up with the idea of ​ ​ building bicycle paths in St. Petersburg.  Moreover, in the proposed option, you do not need to spend money from the budget - the city allocates a route, and along it you could place cafes and pop-up stores, banks, chain sports stores, points for the sale of healthy food.  So the track will pay for itself, it turns out the option of a reliable public-private partnership. — If in Almetyevsk it was easier to implement ideas than in Moscow or St. Petersburg, then maybe you need to pay attention to small cities?  For example, in the Leningrad region? - In a big city, of course, it is more difficult to allocate space, because everything is already built up, there are not enough roads.  It is much easier to design when laying new streets, and some developers in their residential complexes create such infrastructure.  But it is necessary that there be a connection between these islands of civilization.  A progressive solution would be the construction of the world ’ s first circular cycle path around the city, in parallel with the creation of a circular railway route, which was agreed by the city authorities with Russian Railways last year at the St. Petersburg Economic Forum.  The bicycle ring will unite the sleeping areas, and the lines will go from it to the interior of the city, including parks, and to the Leningrad region.  This will relieve the traffic jams, and it is useful for health, and you do not have to push in public transport.  Another project we would like to take part in is a bike path from Svetogorsk to the border with Finland.  In general, we learned about it from the publication on "Fontanka" and appealed to both the Finns and the administration of the Leningrad region to consider our proposal. - At what stage of negotiations with the government of St. Petersburg, districts or city services? - We are actively working with "Lensvet" - our technology of marker illumination is new, it has not been used before, so it needs to be agreed, submit all the technical characteristics and documentation, so that city specialists can service it.  Another option for its use is recumbent traffic lights, the first we installed in 2015 in Moscow on Mira Avenue, in St. Petersburg, the pilot sample was on Malaya Morskaya Street.  Such traffic lights are also installed in Grozny and Almetyevsk, and their peculiarity lies in the use of the optical shock-resistant polymer developed by us.  If the road is wide, then under the feet the color of the signal can be seen much better than a little man on the other side of the street.  In addition, people most of the time look at smartphones, their attention is scattered, and the edge of the eye under the feet is more convenient to look than to raise your head.  According to experts, such a traffic light reduces the likelihood of an accident by up to 90%.  Potentially everyone is for the introduction of this technology, but you still need to go the way of approvals. – Is there a demand for innovative improvement now? – Previously, people often spoke negatively about the improvement, holidays and New Year ’ s decoration of cities.  Modern MAFs (small architectural forms) and art objects that have long become familiar in the West and are already considered an indispensable element of improvement, our residents seemed an unnecessary waste of budget money.  Even despite the fact that some of the elements in terms of cost did not differ from the dull, bored for decades of objects.  Gradually, there is an understanding that this is another item of expenditure, and a comfortable urban environment is needed first of all by the citizens themselves.  The turning point occurred in 2013, when the Gorky Central Park opened in Moscow after reconstruction.  It became the first world-class park in Russia, a space for recreation, sports, dancing and outdoor games.  His concept has revolutionized the thinking of many.  The members of the creative team that worked on the project later became the ideologists of creating such modern spaces in Russia.  The steady growth of the market began after the opening of the Zaryadye Park in the capital and the reconstruction of VDNH.  This trend was noticed in the regions, where we saw what modern public spaces can be.  There was a priority federal project “Formation of a comfortable urban environment ”. Title: Pocket park, this year new renovation of 50 - citizens out of the house there is a park, you can walk, chat, fitness, enjoy the green -- News Morning Post official website
Content: Morning Post reporter Yu Wenyan at the corner of Fuxing East Road and Zhonghua Road, there is a small green space of only 500 square meters, which has installed three leisure seats and some small outdoor fitness equipment, which has become a "Cao Jia Street small garden" in the eyes of nearby residents. A number of pocket parks, which are often referred to as street gardens in the past, their presence not only allows nearby residents to walk, chat, fitness, and enjoy the green, but also lights up the environmental face of the block.  It is reported that the city built 47 pocket parks last year, and this year will build or upgrade 50.  Last year, 47 pocket parks were built at the corner of Fuxing East Road and Zhonghua Road, with a small green space of only 500 square meters.  Once, it was a green space, and now, it has become a "small garden in Cao Jia Street" in the eyes of nearby residents.  In Hongkou District, after a number of illegal buildings were demolished, a pocket park was built.  For example, the Huishan Garden at 207 Lintong Road, do not look at it with an area of only 408 square meters, but "five dirty", not only has exquisite and small green products, but also fitness trails.  In order to coordinate with the surrounding architectural style, the entrance to the park has also been designed in the style of Shikumen.  More than 2,300 square meters of public green space has been built in the area of 1501 North Xinshi Road, Jiangwan Town.  If there are no pavilions and seats for rest, it is also a little larger than the green space of Cao Jia Street.  But with activities and rest facilities, it becomes a simple little park.  According to incomplete statistics, 47 pocket parks were built in the city last year.  Pocket Park is not clearly defined Pocket Park, which originated from the proposal of the New York Parks Association in 1963, originally refers to small parks scattered in high-density urban centers and distributed in plaques.  Since the beginning of just over half a century, the United States, Britain, Japan and China and other countries have begun to have their own unique "pocket park plan".  Today's pocket parks refer to small green open spaces scattered in plaques in the city.  At present, there is no clear definition of pocket parks, and various small green spaces, small parks, street gardens, and small community sports venues in the city are common pocket parks.  Liu Yuelai, a scholar at Tongji University's School of Architecture and Urban Planning, said that there is currently no clear definition of the size of the pocket park.  In terms of area, he personally feels that it can be counted as small as tens of square meters and as large as thousands of square meters.  Unlike the comprehensive park, it offers simple and short breaks, such as a walk after a meal, a small sitting or children's play.  The city's greening department said that at present, their definition of the street garden from the area generally refers to the area of 300-3000 square meters of green space.  The municipal greening and cityscape administration bureau recently introduced that this year Shencheng plans to build or upgrade 50 pocket parks.  The actual number may be more than that.  Among the 79 colorful community projects recently released in Pudong, nearly 40 projects are defined as pocket parks. The pocket park in Hongkou District is planning to build the second phase of Yongnian Li, so that the pocket park function is becoming more and more perfect.  This year, Putuo plans to build a new 10,000 li community green space with a total area of 14,930 square meters, consisting of forests, wetlands and pocket parks.  The first part covers an area of about 10,970 square meters, and is designed to be an accessible urban forest and wetland.  The second part is located at the northwest corner of Wanquan Road and Fu Ping Road, covering an area of about 3960 square meters, and is designed to be positioned as a pocket park.  Fang Yan, deputy director of the municipal greening and cityscape administration bureau, said that the greening department is trying to make more parks around the citizens, even some street gardens and pocket parks, so that people can walk in parks not far from their homes.  According to the relevant person in charge of the municipal greening and cityscape administration bureau, the goal of allowing citizens to go out 500 meters to see a 3,000 square meter park green space has been basically achieved.  However, some residents feel that the greening of Shanghai is not enough.  Shanghai is still far behind Beijing, Hangzhou, Guangzhou and other cities, as well as New York, London and Paris.  For example, according to the area of public green space in the city and the base ratio of the resident population of more than 24 million, the per capita public green space is only about 8%, while some cities in China are generally more than 10%.  Therefore, in the case of limited land resources, Shanghai can only build more "pocket parks" and make dojo in snail shells.  It is understood that there are 243 urban parks in Shanghai, and by 2020, the number of urban parks will reach 300, forming a three-level system of "pocket parks - community parks - regional parks", and basically realizing that citizens go out 500 meters to have parks.

Sotoudeh Nia said the work will be carried out in partnership with the Deputy of Infrastructure, Transport and Traffic Affairs, adding: Given Gorgan Municipality ’ s approach to increasing urban green space per capita and the balanced distribution of amenities throughout the city, as well as taking steps towards creating a child-friendly city, Gorgan Municipality will continue its efforts to build and operate 12 pocket parks, with the highest emphasis on creating space for children and installing playgrounds in them until the end of the year. The series reportedly shows pictures of the new headquarters and has received positive feedback among the public.  However, critics say the series has an "informational" function. This spirit of “victory ” quickly pervaded all social networks.  One Twitter user wrote: “France, know us.  You condemn us, but we salute you on your soil.  Long live Turkey, we are making history.  In addition, many people have used the hashtag # ConquestofEurope.  Another social media user wrote: “A small reminder to Western and UEFA media that the salute is a political or racist message: it is not a political message but a way of expressing respect for the soldiers of a country made with the blood of its soldiers. ”  AFP Image caption Many Turks see Turkey's operation in northern Syria as a broader form of its fight against Kurdish militants on their soil, and why the Turks are defending their army in the Turkish border town of Agça Qala.  A resident of the city, waving the country's flag, told the BBC: "We are ready to go to the front line and fight.  We are waiting for Erdogan ’ s order. ”  Turkey has been at war with the PKK on its territory for more than three decades.  That ’ s why supporters of Turkey ’ s military intervention in northern Syria see the move as a broader struggle.  The popular support for the Turkish military shows a sense of nationalism in the country, which is louder than the wave of criticism, mostly because those who dare to oppose the national discourse of military operations face criminal charges.  Nearly 80 social media users who criticized the operation were prosecuted for "inciting hatred and engaging in propaganda to intimidate" and a large number of Twitter accounts belonging to Kurdish activists and journalists in Turkey have been closed.  The main tool of Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan to use his power to shape public opinion has been the media, which has always been criticized for misusing them as propaganda machines.  The bulk of Turkey ’ s mainstream media belong to Erdogan ’ s corporate conglomerates.  So it ’ s no surprise that the voices of the opposition are not being heard.  Media that mainly reflect the thinking of the government.  Turkey ’ s prominent TV anchors who have gone to the border, dressed in military uniforms, portray Turkey ’ s military intervention in northern Syria in an epic and passionate way.  Playback of this file on your device is not supported.  Why is Turkey now fighting the Kurds in northern Syria?  The nationalist narrative is also very popular in the Turkish press.  They don ’ t give much space to criticism, and if they do, they will attack it.  David Lamy, Labour MP in the UK, was no exception.  LeMay posted a video of a child who died, writing: “The human face of Trump ’ s decision to give free tickets to Turkey to attack Kurdish allies in northeastern Syria.  CNN Turk, the pro-government network on Twitter, along with an image of Mr. Lami, in which his skin was darkened by manipulation, accused him of "black propaganda" about Turkey's military intervention.  It was a reaction that was accepted by many racially minded people.  @ DavidLammy Why have @ cnnturk darkened my image in this picture to accuse me of spreading propaganda?  I am raising important issues about Trump's decision to abandon the Kurds to Erdogan's forces in north eastern Syria.  pic.twitter.com / k2907GqCck — David Lammy (@ DavidLammy) October 12, 2019 What do Turkish Kurds think is the official policy of Turkey in this operation to clear its borders from the SDF, which consists mainly of Syrian Kurdish militias as well as Arab and Christian fighters?  Kurds make up nearly 20 percent of Turkey ’ s population, but their voices are barely heard.  Most residents of the Kurdish city of Diyarbakir have decided to remain silent because of fear of legal action against them.  Among them is the owner of a spice shop in the city ’ s busiest market, who told the BBC: “We are all hurt but we suppress our emotions.  When you ’ re surrounded by cops in civilian clothes, no one will talk to you.  “The political parties in Turkey largely follow the line of the ruling Justice and Development Party: the secular Republican People ’ s Party, the Good Nationalist Party, and the Nationalist National Action Party all support this military operation.  With regard to opposition parties, there is only one exception: the Peoples ’ Democratic Party (HDP), which is pro-Kurdish.  Its leaders are in prison and its members face ongoing prosecution, threats and online violence.  A large number of HDP members who protested in the southeastern region of Turkey against the country ’ s military intervention were either arrested or forced to leave by police.  Police have raided several municipal buildings in the predominantly Kurdish cities of Hakkari, Mardin and Van, arresting a number of Kurdish executives.  When voices opposing military intervention are silenced or suppressed, a sense of nationalism is all that remains, a sense that pro-government media plays a central role in creating.

passages.title: No Iranian government!
passages.passage: Is it possible to dream of a day when fair debate and debate become a phenomenon every day or every night, the national media, and assume a serialized and continuous state?  In this case, what comes out of free dialogue and discussion about the urgent and breathtaking issues of the society will be compatible with the public interest and certainly different from the issues that they intend to display to the society by relying on huge financial resources.  Report by ISNA Rabiei in a note titled “Iranian stateless!  “Our people are not passive consumers and receptionists of domestic and foreign television programs and series.  Right from the moment a series ends, another series begins in the form of endless discussions on the social and social networks about the “main theme ” of the show, and the film is enslaved to“ film criticism. ”  Is it possible to witness a series of free debates in the same media as a series of serial ideas to instill a certain idea?  Otherwise, in the absence of free debate in the review of films and series, the debate will not stop under the city ’ s skin, but will find out what the series did not want to show due to their inherent limitations and yet unconsciously and unwittingly “showed. ”  Think of it as a sign of the presence of two people in the kingdom.  In this neighboring country of Turkey, the series “Wadi of the Wolves ” (Turkish Kortelar Wadi Si), which began in 2003 and lasted about 100 episodes in three years, depicts the phenomenon of“ two-state ” and even “two-nation ” in Turkey in a special way.  If you remove all the theatrical costumes, the show is based on a simple story: Turkey is run by an American-Israeli council called the Council of Wolves.  The invisible hands of that council control all of Turkey ’ s affairs.  A hero named "Polat Alamdar", who has risen from the lower ranks of the Mafia, eventually finds his way to the central council of that Mafia organization, and gradually, with the knowledge of the anti-national nature of the council, destroys it.  At the same time, the money is inflicting heavy blows on the branch of that multinational council in Iraq.  The American spy, Aaron Feller, is the head of a Center for Strategic Studies and holds the Turkish government and institutions in his hands.  The money also leaves the right of the spy / researcher in the palm of his hand.  The name “wolf ” in the series is symbolic and evokes a kind of social Darwinism: where the foreign wolves have taken control of the country ’ s affairs, the heroes of the nation, although they are not wolf-like, bury their wolf paws in the bodies of the influential wolves who have taken control of the state and institutions.  In that series, as well as the “bad mafia good mafia ”, the wolf is divided into good and bad and symbolizes the war of the heroes of“ Valley of the Wolves ” against the “Wolf Council ”.  The good wolf can be called, on credit, by borrowing an interpretation of an Iranian novel, “The Killing Wolf. ”  Movies and TV shows have the same characteristics as any work of art: what is unconsciously and unwittingly in the film is more meaningful than what is openly “shouting. ”  Have we not unwittingly fallen into the trap of simulated enemies who try to portray our country and our sovereignty as an “unusual ” government that is incompatible with the demands of modern times?  In Turkey, during the time of the series “Kurtelar Wadi Si ” on the stage, the phenomenon of“ two states ” was a common phenomenon.  The series and films that try to instill “dual sovereignty ” and“ two-state ” system in our country unconsciously fall into the trap of simulations that overshadow the incomparable and original nature of an Islamic system and the people ’ s base under the shadow of a series of police and security operations.  The enemies of Iran want to say that in Iran there is no conventional and normal system that works according to the legitimate and popular norms of “one nation state. ”  They are not only trying to “talk ” about the two states ruling Iran, but they are also trying to“ show ” their claim in some way.  The first attempt to attack the principle of “one nation-state ” was manifested in Trump ’ s UN speech in September 2017.  To instill “Iranian statelessness ”, Trump pointed the sharp edge of his attacks on the democratic legitimacy of the Iranian regime, claiming that every single manifestation of statecraft and democracy that is observed in Iran is in fact a“ mask ” and a false appearance that has nothing to do with the nature of the system.  Trump ’ s claim was that Iran ’ s regime is dictatorial in nature and a mask of democracy is encrusted upon it.  In fact, Trump repeated the Zionist burning of Netanyahu against Rouhani in a more refined way.  The analogy of “the wolf in the sheep ’ s clothing of democracy ” this time, and indeed for the first time, became the dominant speech of the president of the United States against Iran and the Iranian government.  The main goal of the Zionists and the US warmongering lobby in the White House and Congress is clear from the claim: The Zionists want to say that Iran is not a “normal ” government whose popular and electoral side is reflected in its foreign and domestic policy, on the contrary, behind the facade of the government and the republic that erupts from the ballot boxes, there is another government deep inside that is a“ true government. ”  That is, although the people of Iran choose this visible and apparent government, there is something else called the “deep state ”, which is in his hands and which should be considered the“ real government ” of Iran.  In fact, by this means, the Zionists are trying to project an image of a different background and of a different country on the political face of our country: “deep state ” is a well-known term in the years of the coup d ’ état in Turkey.  In those years, behind the “ostensible state ” that was the showcase of Turkey ’ s half-baked democracy, there was another government called the“ deep state. ”  The distinctive position of the military in Turkey and the separation between the visible state and the deep state was, of course, rooted in the specific history of Turkey, which represented the military as the core and central element in the establishment of the Turkish nation-state.  It is this particular and different history that breaks the foundation of the simulation between the political structure and the structure of the two countries: the Islamic Republic system in our country has emerged from a revolution whose architect considered the Shah ’ s regime to be an “illegal state ” and said that a government that does not rely on the nation and on elected institutions such as the parliament and the presidency and has been established by force of a coup is an“ illegal state ”.  The new system in Turkey, however, has come from a different context, that is, from the absolute supremacy of the military at the point of its establishment, and that model cannot be projected on Iran.  At the point of establishment of the Islamic Republic, there is no trace of the fact that this system has emerged from a completely mysterious secret, security, police and military environment.  In the visual semiotics of Turkish films and series, we see the highlighting of the security police of the “better of us ” community, which by definition is the only incorruptible and uncompromising group and organization that can withstand the most gruesome tests.  Those films have their own function in that society and in those particular circumstances, and they respond to the sense of powerlessness and lack of confidence in society in some way.  The adaptation of that history and that particular circumstance to our society is an unforgivable error even inadvertently.  Instead of films and show programs that instill “two-state ” and“ dual sovereignty ”, one should use a little more creativity and return to the context of society and respect its choice.  Especially when the media sanctifying war and sanctions abroad have used all their imaginations to instill disappointment and futility of elections in Iran, it should clear its borders with those distorted imaginations, and should not throw the wealth and resources of the nation into cheap simulations and destroy the borders of a people-based system with Donald Trump ’ s imaginations and representations of the nature of the revolution and the state and the system of choice. mingled.  End of message.

passages.title: Turkey's hot markets in South America
passages.passage: Turkish television series now reached South America after capturing the film market of the Indian subcontinent, the Middle East, the Caucasus, Central Asia and the Balkans.  In South America, Chile, Argentina and Mexico are among the biggest customers of Turkish TV series.  The popularity of Turkish series in the Middle East or the Caucasus may be due to cultural and historical commonalities, but what could be the reason for the booming Turkish series market on the other side of the Atlantic in South America?  Tuggs Shaw, a German broadcaster, has been trying to answer this question in a report on the popularity of Turkish shows in South America.  Yamaj Okur, producer of the Çukur story series, which has been translated into Persian as “Gut ”, says that a 140-minute episode will be produced every week, which will be broadcast on Turkish television five days later.  The Trench series is currently one of Turkey ’ s most successful series.  It tells the story of a family who controls one of Istanbul ’ s most dangerous neighborhoods, the Pit.  The neighborhood has long been in the hands of small families, whose most important rule is to be strict about the distribution of drugs in the neighborhood.  If someone spreads drugs, they have to leave the neighborhood.  The first episode of the series premiered on October 23, 2017 on TV and is still ongoing.  Correspondents from Istanbul and Rio de Janeiro say the demand for Turkish TV shows has increased.  Diazis, or series, forms a separate genre on Turkish television that is more comparable to the well-known South American telenovelas.  Araya Kisternas, a Chilean couple who have been married for almost 50 years, has just discovered their love for Turkish TV shows.  They say they show love with respect in this series.  The looks are romantic and traditional families are portrayed as important and valuable.  The Chilean couple have a herd that "in modern South American nostalgia traps shows a lot of bare limbs, men kiss men, and violence is part of the film."  Juan Vicente, director of the Chilean TV channel Mega, brought the first Turkish series to South America seven years ago.  He recalls that when the show “Binbir gece ” was broadcast on the mega network, he enthralled people and saved the mega network from bankruptcy at the time.  Juwan goes on to say that since many South Americans are conservative and dream of an ideal world, Turkish TV shows are in their best interest.  Family structures in Turkey are comparable to those in South America.  The patriarchal structures with a strong grandfather or father who determines and leads everything in the family are similar to the Chilean family structure.  The traditional family structure is also popular in Turkey, thanks to Erdoğan ’ s conservative and Islamist government.  Thousands took to the streets in recent days to protest Turkey ’ s withdrawal from the Convention against Violence against Women, but the protests have not been successful so far.  Yamaj Okor, producer of The Pit, says sex, swearing, alcohol in movies and TV shows are as taboo as they were in the '90s.  Okor added, “We have to tell our stories more gently, otherwise the TV won ’ t play it. ”  The series as Turkey ’ s “soft power ” is different from most Turkish series that depict the glamorous life of the middle and upper classes.  In this series, usually luxury cars, expensive clothes are displayed.  But the hole has a different atmosphere.  The series is filmed in the Balat district of Istanbul.  In the Balat district of Istanbul, which used to be home to Jewish, Armenian and Greek communities, it is now a simple working-class area, but thanks to the series, the neighborhood has now flourished and many cafes have opened in its corners over the past few years.  Tagus Shaw reports that at any given time during filming, about 200 fans of the Pit series gather at the scene.  On the other hand, vendors are trying to sell their goods, and in the future, visitors to South America are likely to be seen in the narrow alleys of Balat.  The series was recently sold to Chile.  The Chilean couple who are fascinated by the film are also planning a trip to Turkey.  Hector said: “A trip to Turkey would be a dream for us. ”  His wife, Patricia, interrupts him: “In the past, we never had any idea of Turkey.  We knew a Turkey full of violence with terrorist attacks.  But now it seems to be getting better. ”  Turkey ’ s $1 billion in revenue has become the world ’ s second-largest TV series exporter after Hollywood.  Recent research by Turkish state television shows that Turkish dramas are a “soft power, ” often trying to convey a specific image in the form of a romantic historical drama from the Ottoman period, which is usually reflected in the politics of the current Turkish government.  Follow Deutsche Welle on Instagram: “We are exporting Turkish culture, language and products.  Many of them just became popular abroad through our series.  Take, for example, Turkish music, which is now popular in South America. ”  According to estimates by the Turkish film industry, the revenue of the series could reach $1 billion by 2023.  At the end of his report on the Turkish series, Tagus Shaw has written that the next goal of the Turkish series is to capture the film market in Spain and Italy.

passages.title: The first round of turkeys didn ’ t stop.
passages.passage: While the coronavirus outbreak stopped imaging Turkish series, some of these series continued to work in a new way.  According to ISNA, the Al Jazeera website has reported on how to continue shooting Turkish series that broadcast with a short distance.  The report said that some production groups of Turkish series used a new method to continue shooting their series.  In this way, some parts were filmed in the home of the actors and with the camera of their mobile phones, and without violating the rules of the home quarantine, the desired parts were prepared for broadcast.  The series “Eighties ” and“ Let ’ s Go ” continue to air, reaching audiences both inside and outside Turkey.  In the new episodes, these series also deal with the coronavirus.  In the final episode of the series "Forbidden Apple", before its broadcast temporarily stops, one of the actors of the series, while sitting in a taxi, has used a disinfectant and is worried about the coronavirus.  This is the first scene of the Turkish series that deals with the issue of Corona.  In an episode of the “Miracle Doctor ” series, there is mention of a dangerous virus that has entered Turkey through an East Asian traveler, but the name of the coronavirus is not mentioned.  Turkish actors these days have shared pictures of themselves on social media and in various places have been wearing masks and gloves to warn against the spread of the coronavirus.  The comedy series "Tranquility Neighborhood" has dedicated parts to the coronavirus and the importance of prevention in order to reduce the spread of the virus and how to spend free time during the quarantine.  The series, which explores various social issues with humor, now continues through shooting on mobile phones and in the actors ’ own homes.  Gülce Biersel, author of the series, said: “Shooting on mobile phones and in the actors ’ homes was a new exercise that taught us a lot, but some of the things that are necessary for a comedy show, such as walking, running, and certain body movements, can ’ t be done.  It had to be filmed in a consistent manner.  He added that turning each actor ’ s home into a suitable location for filming was difficult.  We asked them to send us a picture of their house.  The show has 11 actors, all of whom it was difficult to coordinate, but with the effort of the actors, we overcame the technical hurdles and got the job done.  Turkish actor Genghis Buzghorud said on Twitter: “The idea of having mobile phones in our homes was Jali ’ s idea.  I welcomed it as an initiative and set up a tent in my backyard for photography.  Mohammad Oymak, president of the Association for Culture and Literature, also welcomed the idea and expressed hope that the scenes filmed in the actors ’ homes would convey happiness and hope to the viewers.  In particular, this idea has been realized through extensive efforts and cooperation between actors and their technical staff and their Internet communication.  End of message.

passages.title: Home show, competitor or second branch of Turkish networks?
passages.passage: According to the Cinema Zone, the cultural group of the Young Journalists Club, with the increasing influence of satellite networks among Iranian families, one of the most significant damage that was mentioned for these networks was the cultural impact of the works broadcast by these networks, especially the Turkish series dubbed.  The series, based on the family as the central subject, provided sexist, pornographic, aristocratic and corrupt narratives of Turkish families, which due to the visual and sexual attractions, these series were able to tell stories of love triangles, betrayal, class divisions, anti-family, mere pleasure and corruption in the context of melodrama to many audiences with their own.  The increase in the activity of satellite networks and the distribution of Turkish works in Iranian satellite networks coincided with the increase of activities in Iran ’ s home theater network; at that time, some cultural analysts considered the home theater network as a reasonable response to satellite networks and an opportunity to overcome their works, a network that had less audits on its works and could attract the audience of Turkish TV series.  But that ’ s where the mistake started.  Many of the programmers and artists who were born and raised by the IRIB moved from television to the home theater network in order to gain more profit and freedom.  This, more than ever, left the hands of the cultural authorities of the IRIB empty to produce attractive and popular works and caused the TV audience to collapse.  On the other hand, less monitoring of the home screen network caused the creators active in this network, instead of presenting a new form and production of a cultural product, to resort to repetitive and sexual formulas of Turkish series and, with a glance from the rival, produced works that even in some cases, had lower quality and content than their Turkish rivals, and even caused some Iranian families to protest against some of these works.  Works that were only economical and did not spare any effort to sell more, from unnecessarily stretching the story, music-based video clips and creating triangular and square love nodes to the inclusion of erotic sequences.  Content works that, as a cultural commodity, had a countercultural function and only filled the pockets of its creators.  This is something that even the creators of these works are aware of.  From Manouchehr Hadi, the director of the love and romance series, who himself has confessed to modeling the Turkish series, to the writer of the series Dell, who says that the reason for the increase in the series' episodes is more money.  Now, some time after increasing the activity of VOD and attracting the audience through free subscription services and attractive plans to sell the works of the home theater network at a lower price than physical broadcasters and strengthening their position among the families as a multimedia and video broadcaster, in their latest action, they have dubbed and broadcast exclusive Turkish series.  The home theater network and VOD, which were supposed to rival Turkish satellite and TV channels, have now become their second branch.  Their cultural and content performance shows that the lack of proper supervision of the production of cultural works and the transfer of the field to individuals who are concerned only with financial interests, not cultural ones, provides the way for cultural influence and the destruction of the cultural foundations of the country and Iranian families.  Now that we are living in the era of the soft cultural war, the abandonment and lack of supervision in the field of cultural production can cause irreparable damage to our country; therefore, it is recommended that we not leave the field of culture to the enemy, by increasing the controls on the production of cultural works in the home theater network, and by producing great cultural works, such as Mokhtarnameh, the lost innocence, Hazrat Yusuf, English Kiev, Imam Ali, zero degree Hats off and...  We ourselves become the issuer of TV series, not the importer of Turkish serials, which can leave Iranian families with many cultural problems.  Author: The End of the Message

📝 Report written for 'I'd like a report on how Turkish soap operas, dramas, and other television series are used by the Turkish government to exert influence on other countries in which they are viewed. Specifically, I want to understand how these shows are used to alter the views of people in other countries about Turkey, its people, and its culture.'

report:
Turkish soap operas, dramas, and other television series have been used by the Turkish government to exert influence on other countries in which they are viewed. 


These shows are often referred to as "soft power" tools, which are used to promote Turkish culture, language, and values abroad [dc1d43cf-ebab-47c9-9901-bb4e58178865]. 


The Turkish government has established various institutions and organizations to produce and promote these shows, including the Yunus Emre Institute, the Anadolu Agency, and Turkish Airlines [dc1d43cf-ebab-47c9-9901-bb4e58178865]. 


These institutions have been instrumental in promoting Turkish culture and values abroad, and have been successful in attracting international attention and audiences [a6548811-e0ef-420b-b5dd-9cac6edc1dd9].

Turkish series have been particularly popular in the Middle East, the Balkans, and the Indian subcontinent, where they are often broadcast on local television channels [e7c5f2a3-a5a2-49f4-b977-506cf29d6990]. 


In Saudi Arabia, for example, Turkish series were previously broadcast on the MBC TV group, but were stopped due to deteriorating relations between Turkey and Saudi Arabia [e7c5f2a3-a5a2-49f4-b977-506cf29d6990]. 


However, MBC will soon be showcasing a new series called "Kingdoms of Fire," which depicts the end of the Mamlukan country and portrays the Ottoman Empire as a bloodthirsty state [e7c5f2a3-a5a2-49f4-b977-506cf29d6990].

This move has been seen as a hostile act by the Turkish government, which views it as an attempt to undermine Turkish history and culture [e7c5f2a3-a5a2-49f4-b977-506cf29d6990].

Turkish series have also been used to promote Turkish culture and values in South America, where they have become extremely popular [260f6b4b-4f1d-48cb-9dad-b0fc3eaa8798]. 


In Chile, Argentina, and Mexico, Turkish series are among the most-watched television programs, and have been credited with promoting Turkish culture and language in these countries [260f6b4b-4f1d-48cb-9dad-b0fc3eaa8798].

The Turkish government has also used its series to promote its foreign policy goals, such as its military intervention in northern Syria [74e89d0d-5812-4124-9b60-550f69c48f15]. 


The series "The Establishment" has been particularly notable for its portrayal of Turkish intelligence and security agency operations, and has been seen as a tool for promoting Turkish nationalism and patriotism [a6548811-e0ef-420b-b5dd-9cac6edc1dd9].

However, not all Turkish series have been successful in promoting Turkish culture and values abroad. 


In Iran, for example, Turkish series have been criticized for their portrayal of Turkish families and culture, which are seen as being too similar to those in the West [98d6062b-88d2-4069-bef3-521f9b4e60ed].

As a result, the Iranian government has established its own home theater network, which produces and broadcasts its own television series, in an effort to promote Iranian culture and values [98d6062b-88d2-4069-bef3-521f9b4e60ed].

Despite these efforts, Turkish series remain extremely popular in many countries, and continue to be used by the Turkish government as a tool for promoting Turkish culture and values abroad [e27b651d-e5b4-46b5-abee-8396c2a25bc9].

In fact, Turkish television series have become the second-largest exporter of TV series in the world, after Hollywood, with a revenue of over $1 billion [e27b651d-e5b4-46b5-abee-8396c2a25bc9].

The Turkish government has also used its series to promote its conservative and Islamist values, particularly in countries where these values are not well-represented [260f6b4b-4f1d-48cb-9dad-b0fc3eaa8798].

For example, the series "The Pit" has been praised for its portrayal of traditional family values and its promotion of Turkish culture and language [260f6b4b-4f1d-48cb-9dad-b0fc3eaa8798].

Overall, Turkish soap operas, dramas, and other television series have been used by the Turkish government to exert influence on other countries in which they are viewed, promoting Turkish culture, language, and values abroad [dc1d43cf-ebab-47c9-9901-bb4e58178865].

These shows have been successful in attracting international attention and audiences, and have become an important tool for promoting Turkish soft power [a6548811-e0ef-420b-b5dd-9cac6edc1dd9].

Content: What is Turkey looking for with the ‘ establishment ’ security series?  Turkish affairs expert Beryl Akmal, BBC monitoring 57 minutes ago image source, TRT Description of the picture, the organization is broadcast from the Turkish state television network Tarti, a television series that aired in Turkey in March and praised the Turkish intelligence and security agency, has become a popular program.  The series has attracted attention due to its many parallels with Turkey ’ s sharp foreign policy and nationalist rhetoric.  The series "The Establishment", broadcast on the state television network TRT, focuses on the missions of the National Intelligence and Security Agency (MITT) forces who want to return the security documents related to the stolen drone program to the country.  The series reportedly shows pictures of the new headquarters and has received positive feedback among the public.  However, critics say the series has an "informational" function.  The establishment is the latest in a popular series that opens a window into the world within Turkey ’ s ruling circles, as Ankara tries to strengthen its international power.  What is the story?  The series revolves around the operation to protect Turkey from a shadowy global network that tries to turn the world against Turkey ’ s ambitions.  A group of agents is responsible for returning documents related to the drone program to the country.  Image source, TRT1 Image Description, is the villainous Fadi in the series, whose plan is to curb Turkey ’ s ambitions; Zayed Fadi is the villainous and villainous character who is a member of the “Company ” group.  The pro-government Yeni Shafagh newspaper wrote that Fadi was an allusion to Mohammed Dahlan, the ouster and former leader of the Palestinian Fatah movement.  Fadi ’ s background is reminiscent of Dahlan, both Palestinians who grew up in refugee camps.  It is said that Dahlan was known as Abu Fadi.  Dahlan has long been on the Turkish government ’ s hate list.  The Turkish government has placed him on the "Most Wanted Terrorist List", which includes those accused of involvement in the July 2016 coup.  Images of Turkish drones appear throughout the series.  Turkey-made drones have attracted global attention in recent years and have been used in Libya, Iraq and Nagorno-Karabakh. He said, “Don ’ t hesitate for a moment, we ’ ll do it. ”  The “terrorism ” of Turkey ’ s overseas operations is a central theme in the series, with“ terrorists ” among the evil forces working with Fadi. Title: Turkish operation in Syria; sense of nationalism rises in Turks
Content: Getty Images Image caption The military salute of the Turkish national team was greeted by fans, as Turkish national football players cheered for their goals in their match against Albania, which was repeated in front of the French national team.  They were warned not to make political moves in the stadium, but they have already done so twice.  Following this move, the fans of the team, who were present at the Stade de France in Paris, began waving their country ’ s flags with great excitement.  These actions were a tribute to Turkey ’ s military operation in northern Syria and a “symbol of indifference ” to the international condemnation of Turkey ’ s operation in Syria.  In Turkey, when it comes to international competitions, football has succeeded in evoking a sense of nationalism, and when it is mixed with anti-West, it has become even more intense.  This spirit of “victory ” quickly pervaded all social networks.  One Twitter user wrote: “France, know us.  You condemn us, but we salute you on your soil.  Long live Turkey, we are making history.  In addition, many people have used the hashtag # ConquestofEurope.  Another social media user wrote: “A small reminder to Western and UEFA media that the salute is a political or racist message: it is not a political message but a way of expressing respect for the soldiers of a country made with the blood of its soldiers. ”  AFP Image caption Many Turks see Turkey's operation in northern Syria as a broader form of its fight against Kurdish militants on their soil, and why the Turks are defending their army in the Turkish border town of Agça Qala.  A resident of the city, waving the country's flag, told the BBC: "We are ready to go to the front line and fight.  We are waiting for Erdogan ’ s order. ”  Turkey has been at war with the PKK on its territory for more than three decades.  That ’ s why supporters of Turkey ’ s military intervention in northern Syria see the move as a broader struggle.  The popular support for the Turkish military shows a sense of nationalism in the country, which is louder than the wave of criticism, mostly because those who dare to oppose the national discourse of military operations face criminal charges.  Nearly 80 social media users who criticized the operation were prosecuted for "inciting hatred and engaging in propaganda to intimidate" and a large number of Twitter accounts belonging to Kurdish activists and journalists in Turkey have been closed.  The main tool of Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan to use his power to shape public opinion has been the media, which has always been criticized for misusing them as propaganda machines.  The bulk of Turkey ’ s mainstream media belong to Erdogan ’ s corporate conglomerates.  So it ’ s no surprise that the voices of the opposition are not being heard.  Media that mainly reflect the thinking of the government.  Turkey ’ s prominent TV anchors who have gone to the border, dressed in military uniforms, portray Turkey ’ s military intervention in northern Syria in an epic and passionate way.  Playback of this file on your device is not supported.  Why is Turkey now fighting the Kurds in northern Syria?  The nationalist narrative is also very popular in the Turkish press.  They don ’ t give much space to criticism, and if they do, they will attack it.  David Lamy, Labour MP in the UK, was no exception.  LeMay posted a video of a child who died, writing: “The human face of Trump ’ s decision to give free tickets to Turkey to attack Kurdish allies in northeastern Syria.  CNN Turk, the pro-government network on Twitter, along with an image of Mr. Lami, in which his skin was darkened by manipulation, accused him of "black propaganda" about Turkey's military intervention.  It was a reaction that was accepted by many racially minded people.  @ DavidLammy Why have @ cnnturk darkened my image in this picture to accuse me of spreading propaganda?  I am raising important issues about Trump's decision to abandon the Kurds to Erdogan's forces in north eastern Syria.  pic.twitter.com / k2907GqCck — David Lammy (@ DavidLammy) October 12, 2019 What do Turkish Kurds think is the official policy of Turkey in this operation to clear its borders from the SDF, which consists mainly of Syrian Kurdish militias as well as Arab and Christian fighters?  Kurds make up nearly 20 percent of Turkey ’ s population, but their voices are barely heard.  Most residents of the Kurdish city of Diyarbakir have decided to remain silent because of fear of legal action against them.  Among them is the owner of a spice shop in the city ’ s busiest market, who told the BBC: “We are all hurt but we suppress our emotions.  When you ’ re surrounded by cops in civilian clothes, no one will talk to you.  “The political parties in Turkey largely follow the line of the ruling Justice and Development Party: the secular Republican People ’ s Party, the Good Nationalist Party, and the Nationalist National Action Party all support this military operation.  With regard to opposition parties, there is only one exception: the Peoples ’ Democratic Party (HDP), which is pro-Kurdish.  Its leaders are in prison and its members face ongoing prosecution, threats and online violence.  A large number of HDP members who protested in the southeastern region of Turkey against the country ’ s military intervention were either arrested or forced to leave by police.  Police have raided several municipal buildings in the predominantly Kurdish cities of Hakkari, Mardin and Van, arresting a number of Kurdish executives.  When voices opposing military intervention are silenced or suppressed, a sense of nationalism is all that remains, a sense that pro-government media plays a central role in creating.

Title: No Iranian government!
Content: Is it possible to dream of a day when fair debate and debate become a phenomenon every day or every night, the national media, and assume a serialized and continuous state?  In this case, what comes out of free dialogue and discussion about the urgent and breathtaking issues of the society will be compatible with the public interest and certainly different from the issues that they intend to display to the society by relying on huge financial resources.  Report by ISNA Rabiei in a note titled “Iranian stateless!  “Our people are not passive consumers and receptionists of domestic and foreign television programs and series.  Right from the moment a series ends, another series begins in the form of endless discussions on the social and social networks about the “main theme ” of the show, and the film is enslaved to“ film criticism. ”  Is it possible to witness a series of free debates in the same media as a series of serial ideas to instill a certain idea?  Otherwise, in the absence of free debate in the review of films and series, the debate will not stop under the city ’ s skin, but will find out what the series did not want to show due to their inherent limitations and yet unconsciously and unwittingly “showed. ”  Think of it as a sign of the presence of two people in the kingdom.  In this neighboring country of Turkey, the series “Wadi of the Wolves ” (Turkish Kortelar Wadi Si), which began in 2003 and lasted about 100 episodes in three years, depicts the phenomenon of“ two-state ” and even “two-nation ” in Turkey in a special way.  If you remove all the theatrical costumes, the show is based on a simple story: Turkey is run by an American-Israeli council called the Council of Wolves.  The invisible hands of that council control all of Turkey ’ s affairs.  A hero named "Polat Alamdar", who has risen from the lower ranks of the Mafia, eventually finds his way to the central council of that Mafia organization, and gradually, with the knowledge of the anti-national nature of the council, destroys it.  At the same time, the money is inflicting heavy blows on the branch of that multinational council in Iraq.  The American spy, Aaron Feller, is the head of a Center for Strategic Studies and holds the Turkish government and institutions in his hands.  The money also leaves the right of the spy / researcher in the palm of his hand.  The name “wolf ” in the series is symbolic and evokes a kind of social Darwinism: where the foreign wolves have taken control of the country ’ s affairs, the heroes of the nation, although they are not wolf-like, bury their wolf paws in the bodies of the influential wolves who have taken control of the state and institutions.  In that series, as well as the “bad mafia good mafia ”, the wolf is divided into good and bad and symbolizes the war of the heroes of“ Valley of the Wolves ” against the “Wolf Council ”.  The good wolf can be called, on credit, by borrowing an interpretation of an Iranian novel, “The Killing Wolf. ”  Movies and TV shows have the same characteristics as any work of art: what is unconsciously and unwittingly in the film is more meaningful than what is openly “shouting. ”  Have we not unwittingly fallen into the trap of simulated enemies who try to portray our country and our sovereignty as an “unusual ” government that is incompatible with the demands of modern times?  In Turkey, during the time of the series “Kurtelar Wadi Si ” on the stage, the phenomenon of“ two states ” was a common phenomenon.  The series and films that try to instill “dual sovereignty ” and“ two-state ” system in our country unconsciously fall into the trap of simulations that overshadow the incomparable and original nature of an Islamic system and the people ’ s base under the shadow of a series of police and security operations.  The enemies of Iran want to say that in Iran there is no conventional and normal system that works according to the legitimate and popular norms of “one nation state. ”  They are not only trying to “talk ” about the two states ruling Iran, but they are also trying to“ show ” their claim in some way.  The first attempt to attack the principle of “one nation-state ” was manifested in Trump ’ s UN speech in September 2017.  To instill “Iranian statelessness ”, Trump pointed the sharp edge of his attacks on the democratic legitimacy of the Iranian regime, claiming that every single manifestation of statecraft and democracy that is observed in Iran is in fact a“ mask ” and a false appearance that has nothing to do with the nature of the system.  Trump ’ s claim was that Iran ’ s regime is dictatorial in nature and a mask of democracy is encrusted upon it.  In fact, Trump repeated the Zionist burning of Netanyahu against Rouhani in a more refined way.  The analogy of “the wolf in the sheep ’ s clothing of democracy ” this time, and indeed for the first time, became the dominant speech of the president of the United States against Iran and the Iranian government.  The main goal of the Zionists and the US warmongering lobby in the White House and Congress is clear from the claim: The Zionists want to say that Iran is not a “normal ” government whose popular and electoral side is reflected in its foreign and domestic policy, on the contrary, behind the facade of the government and the republic that erupts from the ballot boxes, there is another government deep inside that is a“ true government. ”  That is, although the people of Iran choose this visible and apparent government, there is something else called the “deep state ”, which is in his hands and which should be considered the“ real government ” of Iran.  In fact, by this means, the Zionists are trying to project an image of a different background and of a different country on the political face of our country: “deep state ” is a well-known term in the years of the coup d ’ état in Turkey.  In those years, behind the “ostensible state ” that was the showcase of Turkey ’ s half-baked democracy, there was another government called the“ deep state. ”  The distinctive position of the military in Turkey and the separation between the visible state and the deep state was, of course, rooted in the specific history of Turkey, which represented the military as the core and central element in the establishment of the Turkish nation-state.  It is this particular and different history that breaks the foundation of the simulation between the political structure and the structure of the two countries: the Islamic Republic system in our country has emerged from a revolution whose architect considered the Shah ’ s regime to be an “illegal state ” and said that a government that does not rely on the nation and on elected institutions such as the parliament and the presidency and has been established by force of a coup is an“ illegal state ”.  The new system in Turkey, however, has come from a different context, that is, from the absolute supremacy of the military at the point of its establishment, and that model cannot be projected on Iran.  At the point of establishment of the Islamic Republic, there is no trace of the fact that this system has emerged from a completely mysterious secret, security, police and military environment.  In the visual semiotics of Turkish films and series, we see the highlighting of the security police of the “better of us ” community, which by definition is the only incorruptible and uncompromising group and organization that can withstand the most gruesome tests.  Those films have their own function in that society and in those particular circumstances, and they respond to the sense of powerlessness and lack of confidence in society in some way.  The adaptation of that history and that particular circumstance to our society is an unforgivable error even inadvertently.  Instead of films and show programs that instill “two-state ” and“ dual sovereignty ”, one should use a little more creativity and return to the context of society and respect its choice.  Especially when the media sanctifying war and sanctions abroad have used all their imaginations to instill disappointment and futility of elections in Iran, it should clear its borders with those distorted imaginations, and should not throw the wealth and resources of the nation into cheap simulations and destroy the borders of a people-based system with Donald Trump ’ s imaginations and representations of the nature of the revolution and the state and the system of choice. mingled.  End of message.

Title: Turkey's hot markets in South America
Content: Turkish television series now reached South America after capturing the film market of the Indian subcontinent, the Middle East, the Caucasus, Central Asia and the Balkans.  In South America, Chile, Argentina and Mexico are among the biggest customers of Turkish TV series.  The popularity of Turkish series in the Middle East or the Caucasus may be due to cultural and historical commonalities, but what could be the reason for the booming Turkish series market on the other side of the Atlantic in South America?  Tuggs Shaw, a German broadcaster, has been trying to answer this question in a report on the popularity of Turkish shows in South America.  Yamaj Okur, producer of the Çukur story series, which has been translated into Persian as “Gut ”, says that a 140-minute episode will be produced every week, which will be broadcast on Turkish television five days later.  The Trench series is currently one of Turkey ’ s most successful series.  It tells the story of a family who controls one of Istanbul ’ s most dangerous neighborhoods, the Pit.  The neighborhood has long been in the hands of small families, whose most important rule is to be strict about the distribution of drugs in the neighborhood. The name “wolf ” in the series is symbolic and evokes a kind of social Darwinism: where the foreign wolves have taken control of the country ’ s affairs, the heroes of the nation, although they are not wolf-like, bury their wolf paws in the bodies of the influential wolves who have taken control of the state and institutions.  In that series, as well as the “bad mafia good mafia ”, the wolf is divided into good and bad and symbolizes the war of the heroes of“ Valley of the Wolves ” against the “Wolf Council ”.  The good wolf can be called, on credit, by borrowing an interpretation of an Iranian novel, “The Killing Wolf. ”  Movies and TV shows have the same characteristics as any work of art: what is unconsciously and unwittingly in the film is more meaningful than what is openly “shouting. ”  Have we not unwittingly fallen into the trap of simulated enemies who try to portray our country and our sovereignty as an “unusual ” government that is incompatible with the demands of modern times?  In Turkey, during the time of the series “Kurtelar Wadi Si ” on the stage, the phenomenon of“ two states ” was a common phenomenon.  The series and films that try to instill “dual sovereignty ” and“ two-state ” system in our country unconsciously fall into the trap of simulations that overshadow the incomparable and original nature of an Islamic system and the people ’ s base under the shadow of a series of police and security operations.  The enemies of Iran want to say that in Iran there is no conventional and normal system that works according to the legitimate and popular norms of “one nation state. ”  They are not only trying to “talk ” about the two states ruling Iran, but they are also trying to“ show ” their claim in some way.  The first attempt to attack the principle of “one nation-state ” was manifested in Trump ’ s UN speech in September 2017.  To instill “Iranian statelessness ”, Trump pointed the sharp edge of his attacks on the democratic legitimacy of the Iranian regime, claiming that every single manifestation of statecraft and democracy that is observed in Iran is in fact a“ mask ” and a false appearance that has nothing to do with the nature of the system.  Trump ’ s claim was that Iran ’ s regime is dictatorial in nature and a mask of democracy is encrusted upon it.  In fact, Trump repeated the Zionist burning of Netanyahu against Rouhani in a more refined way.  The analogy of “the wolf in the sheep ’ s clothing of democracy ” this time, and indeed for the first time, became the dominant speech of the president of the United States against Iran and the Iranian government.  The main goal of the Zionists and the US warmongering lobby in the White House and Congress is clear from the claim: The Zionists want to say that Iran is not a “normal ” government whose popular and electoral side is reflected in its foreign and domestic policy, on the contrary, behind the facade of the government and the republic that erupts from the ballot boxes, there is another government deep inside that is a“ true government. ”  That is, although the people of Iran choose this visible and apparent government, there is something else called the “deep state ”, which is in his hands and which should be considered the“ real government ” of Iran.  In fact, by this means, the Zionists are trying to project an image of a different background and of a different country on the political face of our country: “deep state ” is a well-known term in the years of the coup d ’ état in Turkey.  In those years, behind the “ostensible state ” that was the showcase of Turkey ’ s half-baked democracy, there was another government called the“ deep state. ”  The distinctive position of the military in Turkey and the separation between the visible state and the deep state was, of course, rooted in the specific history of Turkey, which represented the military as the core and central element in the establishment of the Turkish nation-state.  It is this particular and different history that breaks the foundation of the simulation between the political structure and the structure of the two countries: the Islamic Republic system in our country has emerged from a revolution whose architect considered the Shah ’ s regime to be an “illegal state ” and said that a government that does not rely on the nation and on elected institutions such as the parliament and the presidency and has been established by force of a coup is an“ illegal state ”.  The new system in Turkey, however, has come from a different context, that is, from the absolute supremacy of the military at the point of its establishment, and that model cannot be projected on Iran.  At the point of establishment of the Islamic Republic, there is no trace of the fact that this system has emerged from a completely mysterious secret, security, police and military environment.  In the visual semiotics of Turkish films and series, we see the highlighting of the security police of the “better of us ” community, which by definition is the only incorruptible and uncompromising group and organization that can withstand the most gruesome tests.  Those films have their own function in that society and in those particular circumstances, and they respond to the sense of powerlessness and lack of confidence in society in some way.  The adaptation of that history and that particular circumstance to our society is an unforgivable error even inadvertently.  Instead of films and show programs that instill “two-state ” and“ dual sovereignty ”, one should use a little more creativity and return to the context of society and respect its choice.  Especially when the media sanctifying war and sanctions abroad have used all their imaginations to instill disappointment and futility of elections in Iran, it should clear its borders with those distorted imaginations, and should not throw the wealth and resources of the nation into cheap simulations and destroy the borders of a people-based system with Donald Trump ’ s imaginations and representations of the nature of the revolution and the state and the system of choice. mingled.  End of message.

Title: Turkey's hot markets in South America
Content: Turkish television series now reached South America after capturing the film market of the Indian subcontinent, the Middle East, the Caucasus, Central Asia and the Balkans.  In South America, Chile, Argentina and Mexico are among the biggest customers of Turkish TV series.  The popularity of Turkish series in the Middle East or the Caucasus may be due to cultural and historical commonalities, but what could be the reason for the booming Turkish series market on the other side of the Atlantic in South America?  Tuggs Shaw, a German broadcaster, has been trying to answer this question in a report on the popularity of Turkish shows in South America.  Yamaj Okur, producer of the Çukur story series, which has been translated into Persian as “Gut ”, says that a 140-minute episode will be produced every week, which will be broadcast on Turkish television five days later.  The Trench series is currently one of Turkey ’ s most successful series.  It tells the story of a family who controls one of Istanbul ’ s most dangerous neighborhoods, the Pit.  The neighborhood has long been in the hands of small families, whose most important rule is to be strict about the distribution of drugs in the neighborhood.  If someone spreads drugs, they have to leave the neighborhood.  The first episode of the series premiered on October 23, 2017 on TV and is still ongoing.  Correspondents from Istanbul and Rio de Janeiro say the demand for Turkish TV shows has increased.  Diazis, or series, forms a separate genre on Turkish television that is more comparable to the well-known South American telenovelas.  Araya Kisternas, a Chilean couple who have been married for almost 50 years, has just discovered their love for Turkish TV shows.  They say they show love with respect in this series.  The looks are romantic and traditional families are portrayed as important and valuable.  The Chilean couple have a herd that "in modern South American nostalgia traps shows a lot of bare limbs, men kiss men, and violence is part of the film."  Juan Vicente, director of the Chilean TV channel Mega, brought the first Turkish series to South America seven years ago.  He recalls that when the show “Binbir gece ” was broadcast on the mega network, he enthralled people and saved the mega network from bankruptcy at the time.  Juwan goes on to say that since many South Americans are conservative and dream of an ideal world, Turkish TV shows are in their best interest.  Family structures in Turkey are comparable to those in South America.  The patriarchal structures with a strong grandfather or father who determines and leads everything in the family are similar to the Chilean family structure.  The traditional family structure is also popular in Turkey, thanks to Erdoğan ’ s conservative and Islamist government.  Thousands took to the streets in recent days to protest Turkey ’ s withdrawal from the Convention against Violence against Women, but the protests have not been successful so far.  Yamaj Okor, producer of The Pit, says sex, swearing, alcohol in movies and TV shows are as taboo as they were in the '90s.  Okor added, “We have to tell our stories more gently, otherwise the TV won ’ t play it. ”  The series as Turkey ’ s “soft power ” is different from most Turkish series that depict the glamorous life of the middle and upper classes.  In this series, usually luxury cars, expensive clothes are displayed.  But the hole has a different atmosphere.  The series is filmed in the Balat district of Istanbul.  In the Balat district of Istanbul, which used to be home to Jewish, Armenian and Greek communities, it is now a simple working-class area, but thanks to the series, the neighborhood has now flourished and many cafes have opened in its corners over the past few years.  Tagus Shaw reports that at any given time during filming, about 200 fans of the Pit series gather at the scene.  On the other hand, vendors are trying to sell their goods, and in the future, visitors to South America are likely to be seen in the narrow alleys of Balat.  The series was recently sold to Chile.  The Chilean couple who are fascinated by the film are also planning a trip to Turkey.  Hector said: “A trip to Turkey would be a dream for us. ”  His wife, Patricia, interrupts him: “In the past, we never had any idea of Turkey.  We knew a Turkey full of violence with terrorist attacks.  But now it seems to be getting better. ”  Turkey ’ s $1 billion in revenue has become the world ’ s second-largest TV series exporter after Hollywood.  Recent research by Turkish state television shows that Turkish dramas are a “soft power, ” often trying to convey a specific image in the form of a romantic historical drama from the Ottoman period, which is usually reflected in the politics of the current Turkish government.  Follow Deutsche Welle on Instagram: “We are exporting Turkish culture, language and products.  Many of them just became popular abroad through our series.  Take, for example, Turkish music, which is now popular in South America. ”  According to estimates by the Turkish film industry, the revenue of the series could reach $1 billion by 2023.  At the end of his report on the Turkish series, Tagus Shaw has written that the next goal of the Turkish series is to capture the film market in Spain and Italy.

Title: The first round of turkeys didn ’ t stop.
Content: While the coronavirus outbreak stopped imaging Turkish series, some of these series continued to work in a new way.  According to ISNA, the Al Jazeera website has reported on how to continue shooting Turkish series that broadcast with a short distance.  The report said that some production groups of Turkish series used a new method to continue shooting their series.  In this way, some parts were filmed in the home of the actors and with the camera of their mobile phones, and without violating the rules of the home quarantine, the desired parts were prepared for broadcast.  The series “Eighties ” and“ Let ’ s Go ” continue to air, reaching audiences both inside and outside Turkey.  In the new episodes, these series also deal with the coronavirus.  In the final episode of the series "Forbidden Apple", before its broadcast temporarily stops, one of the actors of the series, while sitting in a taxi, has used a disinfectant and is worried about the coronavirus.  This is the first scene of the Turkish series that deals with the issue of Corona.  In an episode of the “Miracle Doctor ” series, there is mention of a dangerous virus that has entered Turkey through an East Asian traveler, but the name of the coronavirus is not mentioned.  Turkish actors these days have shared pictures of themselves on social media and in various places have been wearing masks and gloves to warn against the spread of the coronavirus.  The comedy series "Tranquility Neighborhood" has dedicated parts to the coronavirus and the importance of prevention in order to reduce the spread of the virus and how to spend free time during the quarantine.  The series, which explores various social issues with humor, now continues through shooting on mobile phones and in the actors ’ own homes.  Gülce Biersel, author of the series, said: “Shooting on mobile phones and in the actors ’ homes was a new exercise that taught us a lot, but some of the things that are necessary for a comedy show, such as walking, running, and certain body movements, can ’ t be done.  It had to be filmed in a consistent manner.  He added that turning each actor ’ s home into a suitable location for filming was difficult.  We asked them to send us a picture of their house.  The show has 11 actors, all of whom it was difficult to coordinate, but with the effort of the actors, we overcame the technical hurdles and got the job done.  Turkish actor Genghis Buzghorud said on Twitter: “The idea of having mobile phones in our homes was Jali ’ s idea.  I welcomed it as an initiative and set up a tent in my backyard for photography.  Mohammad Oymak, president of the Association for Culture and Literature, also welcomed the idea and expressed hope that the scenes filmed in the actors ’ homes would convey happiness and hope to the viewers.  In particular, this idea has been realized through extensive efforts and cooperation between actors and their technical staff and their Internet communication.  End of message.
