Title: Home show, competitor or second branch of Turkish networks?
Content: According to the Cinema Zone, the cultural group of the Young Journalists Club, with the increasing influence of satellite networks among Iranian families, one of the most significant damage that was mentioned for these networks was the cultural impact of the works broadcast by these networks, especially the Turkish series dubbed.  The series, based on the family as the central subject, provided sexist, pornographic, aristocratic and corrupt narratives of Turkish families, which due to the visual and sexual attractions, these series were able to tell stories of love triangles, betrayal, class divisions, anti-family, mere pleasure and corruption in the context of melodrama to many audiences with their own.  The increase in the activity of satellite networks and the distribution of Turkish works in Iranian satellite networks coincided with the increase of activities in Iran ’ s home theater network; at that time, some cultural analysts considered the home theater network as a reasonable response to satellite networks and an opportunity to overcome their works, a network that had less audits on its works and could attract the audience of Turkish TV series.  But that ’ s where the mistake started.  Many of the programmers and artists who were born and raised by the IRIB moved from television to the home theater network in order to gain more profit and freedom.  This, more than ever, left the hands of the cultural authorities of the IRIB empty to produce attractive and popular works and caused the TV audience to collapse.  On the other hand, less monitoring of the home screen network caused the creators active in this network, instead of presenting a new form and production of a cultural product, to resort to repetitive and sexual formulas of Turkish series and, with a glance from the rival, produced works that even in some cases, had lower quality and content than their Turkish rivals, and even caused some Iranian families to protest against some of these works.  Works that were only economical and did not spare any effort to sell more, from unnecessarily stretching the story, music-based video clips and creating triangular and square love nodes to the inclusion of erotic sequences.  Content works that, as a cultural commodity, had a countercultural function and only filled the pockets of its creators.  This is something that even the creators of these works are aware of.  From Manouchehr Hadi, the director of the love and romance series, who himself has confessed to modeling the Turkish series, to the writer of the series Dell, who says that the reason for the increase in the series' episodes is more money.  Now, some time after increasing the activity of VOD and attracting the audience through free subscription services and attractive plans to sell the works of the home theater network at a lower price than physical broadcasters and strengthening their position among the families as a multimedia and video broadcaster, in their latest action, they have dubbed and broadcast exclusive Turkish series.  The home theater network and VOD, which were supposed to rival Turkish satellite and TV channels, have now become their second branch.  Their cultural and content performance shows that the lack of proper supervision of the production of cultural works and the transfer of the field to individuals who are concerned only with financial interests, not cultural ones, provides the way for cultural influence and the destruction of the cultural foundations of the country and Iranian families.  Now that we are living in the era of the soft cultural war, the abandonment and lack of supervision in the field of cultural production can cause irreparable damage to our country; therefore, it is recommended that we not leave the field of culture to the enemy, by increasing the controls on the production of cultural works in the home theater network, and by producing great cultural works, such as Mokhtarnameh, the lost innocence, Hazrat Yusuf, English Kiev, Imam Ali, zero degree Hats off and...  We ourselves become the issuer of TV series, not the importer of Turkish serials, which can leave Iranian families with many cultural problems.  Author: The End of the Message

passages.title: Mars Rover Perseverance for the first time was able to get oxygen from the atmosphere of Mars
passages.passage: The Perseverance rover, which landed on Mars in February, was able to get oxygen from the planet ’ s atmosphere for the first time.  This was reported by the NASA website.  It is reported that on board the Rover Perseverance is an experimental instrument MOXIE (Mars Oxygen In-situ Resource Utilization Experiment) the size of a toaster, which extracted oxygen.  "The test took place on April 20, the 60th Martian day since the mission landed on February 18," NASA said.  The National Aerospace Agency said it was an important first step in converting carbon dioxide into oxygen on Mars.  "MOXIE has a lot to work on, but the results of this technology demonstration are promising as we approach our goal of one day seeing humans on Mars.  Oxygen is not just what we breathe.  Rocket fuel depends on oxygen, and future explorers will depend on the production of fuel on Mars to make the journey home, ” said Jim Reuters, assistant administrator of STMD.  The atmosphere of Mars is 96% carbon dioxide.  MOXIE works by separating oxygen atoms from carbon dioxide molecules.  A residual product, carbon monoxide, is emitted into the Martian atmosphere, the scientists explained.  As reported by Ukrainian News, NASA launched the first unmanned helicopter on Mars.  Earlier, Elon Musk announced the need to build a self-sufficient colony on Mars before the start of World War III or another large-scale cataclysm on Earth.

This was reported by the National Aerospace Agency of the United States (NASA).  As specified in NASA, the experiment was conducted on April 20 with the help of the experimental installation MOXIE, which was placed on board the Rover Perseverance.  The device made it possible to produce about five grams of oxygen - this amount would be enough to ensure human breathing for ten minutes Scientists believe that in the future this technology will allow to receive and store oxygen on Mars. passages.passage: South Korea ’ s Samsung Group Vice President Lee Jae-yong was sentenced to two and a half years in prison in January for bribing former President Park Geun-hye ’ s confidants.  As the government and business sectors recently asked the government to pardon Li, he appeared in court again on Thursday (22) on charges of fraud and stock price manipulation, the first appearance of the company after about three months.  According to South Korean media reports, 52-year-old Li Jae-rong dressed in a black suit and white shirt to appear in court.  Lee Jae-yong appeared in court 10 minutes before the start of the trial. In addition to answering that the judge did not want a jury, Lee Jae-yong remained silent.  Prosecutors alleged that in the process of promoting the merger of Samsung C & T and Cheil Industries in 2015, Samsung executives deliberately published false information to raise the share price of First Woven and depress the share price of Samsung Property in order to boost Li Zaihong ’ s acquisition of shares after First Woven was acquired by Samsung Property to become the largest shareholder and strengthen his influence on the Samsung Group.  If Li is convicted of fraud and stock price manipulation, his sentence may be increased.  Lee has so far served half of his sentence, which is 15 months.  South Korea ’ s government faces growing pressure from business and opposition parties to pardon Lee.  Utilizing Lee Jae-yong ’ s global network will help safeguard South Korea ’ s vaccine supply, according to the Federation of South Korean Industries.  Park Jen, a conservative lawmaker, also said that South Korea ’ s investment in U.S. semiconductor production will ensure that South Korea receives vaccines from the United States.  Russia plans to withdraw from the International Space Station from 2025, space agency chief Dmitry Rogozin said on Wednesday, with President Vladimir Putin's approval, Russia will build its own space station and hopes to put it into orbit by 2030, a plan that reportedly costs $6 billion (about HK $46.6 billion).  If successful, it will open a new chapter in Russia ’ s space exploration and end more than two decades of U.S.-Russian cooperation on the International Space Station.  Russian Deputy Prime Minister Yuri Borisov told Russian television last weekend that Moscow would notify its partners to leave the International Space Station from 2025.  Russia ’ s Interfax news agency reported that Rogozin said it plans to put the space station into orbit by 2030, and unlike the International Space Station, it is likely that there will not be permanent members of the Russian space station, because the space station ’ s orbit will expose the astronauts to high radiation, but Russian astronauts can go, and the space station will also use artificial intelligence and robots.  He added that Russia is ready to consider allowing foreign space visitors, “but the space station must be national … If you want to do things well, you have to do it yourself. ”  Since 1998, Russian cosmonauts have cooperated with astronauts from the United States and 16 other countries on missions to the International Space Station, one of the areas in which Moscow has worked closely with Washington.  However, the US-Russian relationship is in crisis due to issues such as human rights and hacking.  NASA ’ s Perseverance successfully extracted oxygen from the Martian atmosphere The recent mission of the Mars rover Perseverance successfully converted carbon dioxide from the Martian atmosphere into breathable pure oxygen, NASA said on Wednesday.  NASA said that the device, called MOXIE (Mars Oxygen In-Situ Resource Utilization Experiment), is the size of a toaster, and uses extreme heat to separate oxygen atoms from carbon dioxide molecules through electrolysis work. MOXIE successfully generated about 5 grams of oxygen, which can allow an astronaut to breathe for 10 minutes.  This feat marks the first time humans have extracted natural resources available for human use from the environment of another planet.  Oxygen content in the Martian atmosphere is extremely low, carbon dioxide accounts for 95% of the Martian atmosphere, and the rest is mainly composed of molecular nitrogen and argon.  Adequate oxygen supply is key to human exploration of Mars, experts believe that astronauts living and working on Mars may need 1 ton of oxygen to maintain their needs for a year, and believe that it is more practical to convert oxygen on Mars than to transport 25 tons of oxygen from Earth.  MOXIE ’ s operating concept is to produce 10 grams of oxygen per hour.  NASA says scientists plan to run the MOXIE device at least nine more times over the next two years, under different conditions and at different speeds. passages.title: Oxygen and hydrogen on Mars proposed to get from brine
passages.passage: Scientists have developed a method for producing oxygen and hydrogen from a liquid saline solution in Martian lakes using electrolysis.  A feature of the experiment was the use of lead-ruthenium oxide as an electrocatalyst for oxygen production.  The production of oxygen using such an installation was 25 times more energy efficient than in the case of MOXIE, launched to the Red Planet as part of the Mars 2020 mission, and the size and weight of the device for life support based on the described technology will be less than that of analogues.  The article was published in the journal PNAS.  Conditions on Mars are far from favorable for humans: the atmosphere is rarefied and 95 percent consists of carbon dioxide, and temperature changes exceed 100 degrees Celsius with an average temperature of minus 63 degrees.  Therefore, colonization of the Red Planet is impossible without the creation of a life support system that would be able to provide people with oxygen for breathing and fuel (for example, hydrogen) for energy supply and, ideally, return flight.  To solve the first problem, NASA created MOXIE (Mars Oxygen ISRU Experiment) - an experimental installation for obtaining oxygen from atmospheric carbon dioxide by electrolysis.  To test the effectiveness of such a method in the field, the installation became part of the Mars Rover Perseverance, which was launched on July 30, 2020 as part of the Mars 2020 mission.  An alternative source of not only oxygen, but also hydrogen on Mars can be water, the first direct evidence of the existence of which on the red planet was obtained in 1971.  Particularly attractive for use in applications, however, would be the reserves of salt water, impurities in which would allow it to remain in a liquid state even at low temperature and pressure.  The first traces of such brine (liquid salt solution) with magnesium perchlorate as the main component were found on Mars in 2015, and in 2018, a reservoir with a diameter of about 20 kilometers was found under the polar ice of the planet, which could have been formed due to volcanic activity.  Later, planetary scientists confirmed that such lakes on Mars really exist and can be numerous.  Now Pralay Gayen (Pralay Gayen) from the University of Washington in St. Louis together with colleagues created an installation for obtaining oxygen and hydrogen from a saline solution close in composition and temperature to that in Martian lakes.  As a brine in the experiment, a solution of magnesium perchlorate in water with a concentration of 2.8 mol per liter was used, cooled to minus 36 degrees Celsius and blown by carbon dioxide (the latter played the role of the Martian atmosphere).  As an electrocatalyst for the production of oxygen, the scientists used lead-ruthenium oxide Pb2Ru2O7-δ, the effectiveness of which they previously showed for alkaline solutions.  The electrocatalyst for hydrogen production was platinum on activated carbon - the standard catalyst in this case, and a commercially produced anion-exchange membrane was used as a separator.  Installation diagram.  In the red region, oxygen is produced, in the blue - hydrogen.  Image source: Pralay Gayen et al. / PNAS In the course of the study, scientists showed that lead-ruthenium oxide as an electrocatalyst is indeed several times more effective than the ruthenium oxide commonly used in such installations.  After the behavior of the created installation was studied in a wide range of temperatures from − 36 to 21 degrees Celsius and saw no radical fluctuations in the efficiency and rate of production.  The current output of the experimental installation was 70 percent, and the energy efficiency was in the range between 36 and 70 percent (depending on the voltage applied to the plates).  In addition, the installation was resistant to degradation of the catalyst: scientists were not able to find traces of ruthenium in the solution after 300-minute operation of the device.  The rate of production of oxygen (blue dots) and hydrogen (red dots), depending on the density of the cathode current.  Image source: Pralay Gayen et al. / PNAS Also, the researchers compared the achieved rate of oxygen production with MOXIE values of 10-22 grams per hour: it turned out that with the same energy supply, the created installation produces 25 times more oxygen than the experiment on the Mars Rover “Perseverance ”.  To have the same rate of oxygen production as MOXIE, the device would have to have electrodes with an area of ​ ​ 28-62 square centimeters, and to ensure the vital activity of a sleeping and actively moving person, this parameter would have to be 375 and 1235 square centimeters, respectively.  At the same time, the mass and volume of the installation will be less than if you use the technology inherent in MOXIE.  Moreover, the developed method of obtaining oxygen does not require its subsequent purification, while during electrolysis in MOXIE, carbon monoxide is also produced, which must be filtered.  Dependence on the power consumption of the rate of oxygen production of the installation (blue line), as well as its capes and volume to ensure various modes of human life (black lines).  The blue dot is the power and rate of oxygen production at MOXIE.  Image source: Pralay Gayen et al. / PNAS Previously, we talked about another method of obtaining oxygen from carbon dioxide in the Martian atmosphere (like MOXIE): scientists proposed to do this using low-temperature plasma.  And what is the role of the Mars Rover “Perseverance ” in addition to checking the method of oxygen production, you can read in our material“ Mars, there and back ”.  Nikita Kozyrev

passages.title: Elon Musk said when will finish the rocket for a flight to Mars
passages.passage: The main task of his “Martian ” project, which Musk has been talking about for more than a decade, the entrepreneur considers the creation of an autonomous colony on the Red Planet with a population of up to a million people.  The founder of Tesla and SpaceX, Elon Musk, told when to expect the first flight of the new interplanetary spacecraft being developed by his company.  Fresh details about the planned program for the development of Mars entrepreneur shared at the conference SXSW in Austin, where unexpectedly for all appeared at one of the events, reports vesti.ru.  Recall that in September 2017, Musk announced his project for the development of the red planet and announced that he was going to organize the first delivery of cargo to Mars in 2022.  To perform the flight should not yet ready super-heavy rocket codenamed BFR.  Speaking on Sunday evening at SXSW, the billionaire suggested that the first short test flights of the new missile could take place in the first half of 2019.  “Although sometimes with deadlines I have a little … well, you know, ” Musk joked, hinting that he did not always fulfill his promises to release this or that Tesla product or launch a new SpaceX rocket in the promised time.  The main task of his “Martian ” project, which Musk has been talking about for more than a decade, the entrepreneur considers the creation of an autonomous colony on the Red Planet with a population of up to a million people.  In his opinion, such a settlement is a guarantee of the survival of civilization in the event of a nuclear war or other global cataclysm on Earth.  In the short term, the Martian colony will need glass domes in which it will be possible to maintain an Earth-like composition of air, a propulsion system and a set of other basic things to support life.  Once the infrastructure is ready, “there will really be an explosion of business opportunities, because Mars will need everything from steel mills to pizzerias. ”  But the main threat to humanity, the founder of Tesla and SpacX still considers not weapons of mass destruction or catastrophic climate change, but artificial intelligence.  “Remember my words, ” he told the audience at SXSW,“ AI is far more dangerous than nuclear missiles.  So why isn ’ t it regulated yet? ”  More important news in the Telegram channel “zakon.kz ”.  Sign up!

passages.title: People are preparing for the pollution of Mars - our review
passages.passage: The experiment was conducted on Earth, more precisely, in the stratosphere of our planet.  There, scientists from two space agencies sent a probe with various microorganisms to check how they would behave in the atmosphere of the red planet.  "We successfully tested a new method of placing bacteria and fungi in Martian conditions using a probe sent into the stratosphere," says Marta Filipa Cortezao of DLR.  "Some microbes, especially black mold embryos, were able to survive the journey even after exposure to very high levels of ultraviolet radiation."  Understanding how microorganisms react to space travel and the Martian environment is key to future missions.  One of the motives is that in the search for extraterrestrial life, scientists should be sure that there are no microorganisms brought from Earth.  But there are other threats.  “On long missions to Mars, we need to know that the microorganisms associated with humans would survive on the Red Planet, because some of them can threaten the lives of astronauts, ” says Katarina Zins, one of the main authors of the publication, which appeared in the publication Frontiers in Microbiology.  But such resistant to harsh conditions earthly life forms still harbor additional opportunities.  "Some microbes may be underestimated by us in the exploration of Mars.  But they are able to help us in the production of food and other materials, regardless of the Earth.  This is a key opportunity to survive away from home, ” the expert adds.  According to experts, it is very difficult to reproduce Martian conditions on Earth. passages.title: Found organisms that can survive on Mars
passages.passage: Scientists at the University of Bremen in Germany have found microorganisms that can grow and develop in the Martian atmosphere.  According to the researchers, based on cyanobacteria or blue-green algae, it is possible to create life support systems for people who will live on the surface of Mars.  This is reported in an article published in the journal Frontiers in Microbiology.  Scientists have shown that cyanobacteria can support life by using the gases of the Martian atmosphere as a source of carbon and oxygen, despite the low pressure.  Blue-green algae multiplied in water with a suspension of Martian dust, which makes it possible to use them to feed other living organisms.  In addition, cyanobacteria produce oxygen as a byproduct of photosynthesis.  Researchers have developed an Atmos bioreactor that maintains atmospheric pressure at 10 percent of Earth ’ s and nitrogen and carbon dioxide concentrations of 96 percent and 4 percent, respectively.  These conditions are close to Martian, but differ from them: atmospheric pressure is a percentage of Earth's, and the proportion of carbon dioxide is 95 percent.  Water and a mixture of minerals mimicking Martian regolith were also added to the bioreactor.  For the experiment, the team chose a species of nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria Anabaena sp.  PCC 7938, which preliminary tests have shown is most likely to thrive in these conditions.  Although the bacteria grew better on a nutrient medium, the researchers also observed growth on Martian regolith.  Then the scientists dried the culture of microorganisms and used it as a substrate for growing E. coli.  This proves that cyanobacteria on Mars can be used to feed crops that, in turn, are suitable for the synthesis of nutrients, including drugs.  Leonid Nemov

The creation of a sustainable atmosphere on Mars is a crucial aspect of making the planet habitable for humans. 
To achieve this, NASA has been conducting experiments to generate oxygen from the Martian atmosphere. 
The Mars Oxygen In-Situ Resource Utilization Experiment (MOXIE) is an experimental instrument on board the Perseverance rover, which was able to extract oxygen from the Martian atmosphere for the first time on April 20 [0fcd78b3-e830-4156-aad4-b8b1e06855f3].

MOXIE works by separating oxygen atoms from carbon dioxide molecules using electrolysis [9b8bc268-c55b-4127-8bcb-7db17237c8e9]. 
The device generated about 5 grams of oxygen, which is enough to sustain an astronaut for 10 minutes [0fcd78b3-e830-4156-aad4-b8b1e06855f3]. 
This feat marks the first time humans have extracted natural resources available for human use from the environment of another planet [9b8bc268-c55b-4127-8bcb-7db17237c8e9].

The MOXIE device is the size of a toaster and uses extreme heat to separate oxygen atoms from carbon dioxide molecules [9b8bc268-c55b-4127-8bcb-7db17237c8e9]. 
The operating concept of MOXIE is to produce 10 grams of oxygen per hour [9b8bc268-c55b-4127-8bcb-7db17237c8e9]. 
Scientists plan to run the MOXIE device at least nine more times over the next two years, under different conditions and at different speeds [9b8bc268-c55b-4127-8bcb-7db17237c8e9].

Another method for producing oxygen on Mars involves using electrolysis of a liquid saline solution in Martian lakes [94be6797-91aa-4e53-9c26-4731a3b49188]. 
This method is more energy-efficient than MOXIE, producing 25 times more oxygen with the same amount of energy [94be6797-91aa-4e53-9c26-4731a3b49188]. 
The installation used in this experiment was able to produce oxygen at a rate of 70% and had an energy efficiency of 36-70% [94be6797-91aa-4e53-9c26-4731a3b49188].

The device made it possible to produce about five grams of oxygen, which can allow an astronaut to breathe for 10 minutes [0fcd78b3-e830-4156-aad4-b8b1e06855f3].

To create a sustainable atmosphere on Mars, it is essential to consider the worst-case scenarios that could affect the planet's habitability. 
One such scenario is the presence of microorganisms that could threaten the lives of astronauts [308024fb-6072-410f-99fe-f8f17636eaf7]. 
However, some microorganisms may be underestimated in the exploration of Mars but could help us in the production of food and other materials [308024fb-6072-410f-99fe-f8f17636eaf7].

Title: Mars Rover Perseverance for the first time was able to get oxygen from the atmosphere of Mars
Content: The Perseverance rover, which landed on Mars in February, was able to get oxygen from the planet ’ s atmosphere for the first time.  This was reported by the NASA website.  It is reported that on board the Rover Perseverance is an experimental instrument MOXIE (Mars Oxygen In-situ Resource Utilization Experiment) the size of a toaster, which extracted oxygen.  "The test took place on April 20, the 60th Martian day since the mission landed on February 18," NASA said.  The National Aerospace Agency said it was an important first step in converting carbon dioxide into oxygen on Mars.  "MOXIE has a lot to work on, but the results of this technology demonstration are promising as we approach our goal of one day seeing humans on Mars.  Oxygen is not just what we breathe.  Rocket fuel depends on oxygen, and future explorers will depend on the production of fuel on Mars to make the journey home, ” said Jim Reuters, assistant administrator of STMD.  The atmosphere of Mars is 96% carbon dioxide.  MOXIE works by separating oxygen atoms from carbon dioxide molecules.  A residual product, carbon monoxide, is emitted into the Martian atmosphere, the scientists explained.  As reported by Ukrainian News, NASA launched the first unmanned helicopter on Mars. Title: Oxygen and hydrogen on Mars proposed to get from brine
Content: Scientists have developed a method for producing oxygen and hydrogen from a liquid saline solution in Martian lakes using electrolysis.  A feature of the experiment was the use of lead-ruthenium oxide as an electrocatalyst for oxygen production.  The production of oxygen using such an installation was 25 times more energy efficient than in the case of MOXIE, launched to the Red Planet as part of the Mars 2020 mission, and the size and weight of the device for life support based on the described technology will be less than that of analogues.  The article was published in the journal PNAS.  Conditions on Mars are far from favorable for humans: the atmosphere is rarefied and 95 percent consists of carbon dioxide, and temperature changes exceed 100 degrees Celsius with an average temperature of minus 63 degrees.  Therefore, colonization of the Red Planet is impossible without the creation of a life support system that would be able to provide people with oxygen for breathing and fuel (for example, hydrogen) for energy supply and, ideally, return flight.  To solve the first problem, NASA created MOXIE (Mars Oxygen ISRU Experiment) - an experimental installation for obtaining oxygen from atmospheric carbon dioxide by electrolysis.  To test the effectiveness of such a method in the field, the installation became part of the Mars Rover Perseverance, which was launched on July 30, 2020 as part of the Mars 2020 mission.  An alternative source of not only oxygen, but also hydrogen on Mars can be water, the first direct evidence of the existence of which on the red planet was obtained in 1971.  Particularly attractive for use in applications, however, would be the reserves of salt water, impurities in which would allow it to remain in a liquid state even at low temperature and pressure.  The first traces of such brine (liquid salt solution) with magnesium perchlorate as the main component were found on Mars in 2015, and in 2018, a reservoir with a diameter of about 20 kilometers was found under the polar ice of the planet, which could have been formed due to volcanic activity.  Later, planetary scientists confirmed that such lakes on Mars really exist and can be numerous.  Now Pralay Gayen (Pralay Gayen) from the University of Washington in St. Louis together with colleagues created an installation for obtaining oxygen and hydrogen from a saline solution close in composition and temperature to that in Martian lakes.  As a brine in the experiment, a solution of magnesium perchlorate in water with a concentration of 2.8 mol per liter was used, cooled to minus 36 degrees Celsius and blown by carbon dioxide (the latter played the role of the Martian atmosphere).  As an electrocatalyst for the production of oxygen, the scientists used lead-ruthenium oxide Pb2Ru2O7-δ, the effectiveness of which they previously showed for alkaline solutions.  The electrocatalyst for hydrogen production was platinum on activated carbon - the standard catalyst in this case, and a commercially produced anion-exchange membrane was used as a separator.  Installation diagram.  In the red region, oxygen is produced, in the blue - hydrogen.  Image source: Pralay Gayen et al. / PNAS In the course of the study, scientists showed that lead-ruthenium oxide as an electrocatalyst is indeed several times more effective than the ruthenium oxide commonly used in such installations.  After the behavior of the created installation was studied in a wide range of temperatures from − 36 to 21 degrees Celsius and saw no radical fluctuations in the efficiency and rate of production.  The current output of the experimental installation was 70 percent, and the energy efficiency was in the range between 36 and 70 percent (depending on the voltage applied to the plates).  In addition, the installation was resistant to degradation of the catalyst: scientists were not able to find traces of ruthenium in the solution after 300-minute operation of the device.  The rate of production of oxygen (blue dots) and hydrogen (red dots), depending on the density of the cathode current.  Image source: Pralay Gayen et al. / PNAS Also, the researchers compared the achieved rate of oxygen production with MOXIE values of 10-22 grams per hour: it turned out that with the same energy supply, the created installation produces 25 times more oxygen than the experiment on the Mars Rover “Perseverance ”.  To have the same rate of oxygen production as MOXIE, the device would have to have electrodes with an area of ​ ​ 28-62 square centimeters, and to ensure the vital activity of a sleeping and actively moving person, this parameter would have to be 375 and 1235 square centimeters, respectively.  At the same time, the mass and volume of the installation will be less than if you use the technology inherent in MOXIE.  Moreover, the developed method of obtaining oxygen does not require its subsequent purification, while during electrolysis in MOXIE, carbon monoxide is also produced, which must be filtered. Title: Oxygen and hydrogen on Mars proposed to get from brine
Content: Scientists have developed a method for producing oxygen and hydrogen from a liquid saline solution in Martian lakes using electrolysis.  A feature of the experiment was the use of lead-ruthenium oxide as an electrocatalyst for oxygen production.  The production of oxygen using such an installation was 25 times more energy efficient than in the case of MOXIE, launched to the Red Planet as part of the Mars 2020 mission, and the size and weight of the device for life support based on the described technology will be less than that of analogues.  The article was published in the journal PNAS.  Conditions on Mars are far from favorable for humans: the atmosphere is rarefied and 95 percent consists of carbon dioxide, and temperature changes exceed 100 degrees Celsius with an average temperature of minus 63 degrees.  Therefore, colonization of the Red Planet is impossible without the creation of a life support system that would be able to provide people with oxygen for breathing and fuel (for example, hydrogen) for energy supply and, ideally, return flight.  To solve the first problem, NASA created MOXIE (Mars Oxygen ISRU Experiment) - an experimental installation for obtaining oxygen from atmospheric carbon dioxide by electrolysis.  To test the effectiveness of such a method in the field, the installation became part of the Mars Rover Perseverance, which was launched on July 30, 2020 as part of the Mars 2020 mission.  An alternative source of not only oxygen, but also hydrogen on Mars can be water, the first direct evidence of the existence of which on the red planet was obtained in 1971.  Particularly attractive for use in applications, however, would be the reserves of salt water, impurities in which would allow it to remain in a liquid state even at low temperature and pressure.  The first traces of such brine (liquid salt solution) with magnesium perchlorate as the main component were found on Mars in 2015, and in 2018, a reservoir with a diameter of about 20 kilometers was found under the polar ice of the planet, which could have been formed due to volcanic activity.  Later, planetary scientists confirmed that such lakes on Mars really exist and can be numerous.  Now Pralay Gayen (Pralay Gayen) from the University of Washington in St. Louis together with colleagues created an installation for obtaining oxygen and hydrogen from a saline solution close in composition and temperature to that in Martian lakes.  As a brine in the experiment, a solution of magnesium perchlorate in water with a concentration of 2.8 mol per liter was used, cooled to minus 36 degrees Celsius and blown by carbon dioxide (the latter played the role of the Martian atmosphere).  As an electrocatalyst for the production of oxygen, the scientists used lead-ruthenium oxide Pb2Ru2O7-δ, the effectiveness of which they previously showed for alkaline solutions.  The electrocatalyst for hydrogen production was platinum on activated carbon - the standard catalyst in this case, and a commercially produced anion-exchange membrane was used as a separator.  Installation diagram.  In the red region, oxygen is produced, in the blue - hydrogen.  Image source: Pralay Gayen et al. / PNAS In the course of the study, scientists showed that lead-ruthenium oxide as an electrocatalyst is indeed several times more effective than the ruthenium oxide commonly used in such installations.  After the behavior of the created installation was studied in a wide range of temperatures from − 36 to 21 degrees Celsius and saw no radical fluctuations in the efficiency and rate of production.  The current output of the experimental installation was 70 percent, and the energy efficiency was in the range between 36 and 70 percent (depending on the voltage applied to the plates).  In addition, the installation was resistant to degradation of the catalyst: scientists were not able to find traces of ruthenium in the solution after 300-minute operation of the device.  The rate of production of oxygen (blue dots) and hydrogen (red dots), depending on the density of the cathode current.  Image source: Pralay Gayen et al. / PNAS Also, the researchers compared the achieved rate of oxygen production with MOXIE values of 10-22 grams per hour: it turned out that with the same energy supply, the created installation produces 25 times more oxygen than the experiment on the Mars Rover “Perseverance ”.  To have the same rate of oxygen production as MOXIE, the device would have to have electrodes with an area of ​ ​ 28-62 square centimeters, and to ensure the vital activity of a sleeping and actively moving person, this parameter would have to be 375 and 1235 square centimeters, respectively.  At the same time, the mass and volume of the installation will be less than if you use the technology inherent in MOXIE.  Moreover, the developed method of obtaining oxygen does not require its subsequent purification, while during electrolysis in MOXIE, carbon monoxide is also produced, which must be filtered. The blue dot is the power and rate of oxygen production at MOXIE. Roundup was a novelty: Monsanto employee John Franz synthesized the active ingredient of the herbicide, glyphosate, only in 1970.  The couple bought Roundup for four decades, until in 2011 Alva heard a diagnosis of non-Hodgkin lymphoma, a cancer of the lymphatic system with lesions of the bones, including the spine.  Four years later, non-Hodgkin lymphoma was found in his wife Alberta, but with brain damage.  In 2017, the couple filed a lawsuit against Monsanto, based on the fact that two years earlier, the International Agency for Research on Cancer at the WHO announced the probable carcinogenicity of glyphosate.  In addition, their claim was not the first: at that time, the courts had already considered several similar complaints.  The case was accelerated due to the poor health of the plaintiffs, who at that time were already in their 70s, and on May 14, 2019, the jury decided after five weeks of consideration that Monsanto violated the law by not warning buyers about the likely risks, in connection with which it must pay a fine of $2 billion and $55 million in damages in favor of the plaintiffs.  This is the eighth highest fine in the history of the United States.  Monsanto Roundup sprayers in a garden shop Photo: REUTERS / Yves Herman Representatives of the owner of Monsanto - the German concern Bayer - said that they do not agree with the decision and will appeal because "all the world's leading health organizations agree on the safety of glyphosate and its non-carcinogenicity" It seems that justice has been served, greedy industries the nics got what they deserved, and the ordinary people who suffered from their actions left as winners.  If not for a few “but ”: first, victory in court will not save the lives of cancer patients.  And, secondly, the compensation awarded to them to the Pilliod spouses will not receive soon and in the wrong volumes.  The fact is that, according to a 2016 ruling of the US Supreme Court, the amount of the fine cannot exceed the amount of compensation for damage by more than nine times.  Thus, even if the appellate court reduces the amount of punitive payments to the maximum possible, the Pilliod spouses will receive, in addition to their compensatory $55 million, only $495 million.  This is the most favorable outcome for the plaintiffs.  Throughout the process, Monsanto ’ s lawyers argued that their products were harmless, as confirmed by research from the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), a federal agency that develops and monitors compliance with environmental and human health standards.  Moreover, in April, the EPA confirmed its initial findings, saying that while glyphosate use does entail some environmental risks, the agency ’ s findings on its impact on human health are consistent with those of other federal agencies.  “If we are going to feed 10 billion people by 2050, we will need all the tools at our disposal, including glyphosate, ” U.S. Secretary of Agriculture Sonny Purdue said in a statement.  Monsanto ’ s defense was largely based on the findings of an EPA study, and Bayer said after the verdict that the decision would not have been so harsh if the scientists ’ findings had been taken into account.  According to the defendant, Alva and Alberta Pilliod suffered from various diseases for a long time, which became the main factor in the development of cancer.  The concern also noted that if it were not for glyphosate, which is poured into fields to destroy weeds, the soil would have to be plowed regularly, which is expensive and harmful to the environment, since a large amount of carbon dioxide is emitted due to the overturning of the earth.  During the judicial investigation, it turned out that those conclusions of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), which the company refers to more than once as a justification for the safety of Roundup, can be questioned.  Demonstrators protest against Bayer Monsanto on the Place de la République in Paris Photo: REUTERS / Philippe Wojazer At the disposal of CNN was the correspondence of a Monsanto employee with one of the Agency officials Jess Rowland.  In it, a federal employee notes that if he can “kill ” glyphosate research at the Agency for the Registration of Toxic Substances and Diseases, he will“ deserve a medal. ”  Monsanto employees in internal correspondence note a low probability that Rowland and the EPA will be able to stop the study of another agency, but note that there is hope.  Judging by the fact that the Agency for the Registration of Toxic Substances never released a study on glyphosate, Rowland, already happily retired, coped with the task.  The Pilliod case is the third trial Bayer has faced over Monsanto products, particularly glyphosate-containing Roundup.  In all three cases, the jury ruled in favor of the plaintiffs with oncology, which developed due to prolonged contact with herbicides.  The first lawsuit against Monsanto was considered by the court last year.  In August, a San Francisco jury awarded $289 million to a former school gardener who was diagnosed with late-stage cancer.  However, a few months later, the judge reduced this amount to $78 million.  The case did not end there, as Bayer filed an appeal.  As a result, after almost a year, the cancer claimant still did not receive the compensation awarded to him.  In March this year, a California resident was awarded $80 million after he sued Monsanto for developing non-Hodgkin lymphoma.  The result is predictable: Bayer appealed, far from the outcome.  Thus, the concern is currently awaiting a decision on three appeals due to Monsanto products.  In addition, there are about 130,000 such claims under consideration in the United States.  And even for a giant like Bayer, it ’ s a pretty sensitive punch.  Bayer acquired 100% of Monsanto in 2018 for $63.5 billion, becoming the largest agricultural concern.  Since the first Roundup carcinogenicity conviction, the conglomerate has lost nearly 46% of its market value and its share price has fallen to 2012 levels.  According to The Fortune, Bayer shareholders told the company ’ s CEO Werner Baumann, who made the merger deal with Monsanto, of no confidence.  He was given nine months to prove that he deserved his place.  Glyphosate is currently the most popular herbicide in the world, despite the fact that after the report of the Agency for Research on Cancer, first France and then other European countries raised the issue of using this substance to combat weeds, and then began to remove it from store shelves.  Despite this, in 2017, EU countries extended the license for the use of glyphosate in agriculture for five years.  Photo: Global Look Press / Christian Charisius / dpa In Russia, Monsanto is present as a supplier of seeds of traditional breeding of corn, vegetable crops, offers farmers various plant protection products, while some of the products are produced in Russia since 2015.  Also in the country you can freely buy the herbicide Roundup, both wholesale and retail.  In addition, Russian companies produce about a hundred drugs based on glyphosate (the Monsanto patent for the molecule of the substance expired in 2000).  The volume of sales of the substance offered under the trademarks "Hurricane", "Typhoon", "Tornado" and others, is estimated at 15-20 thousand tons per year.  Monsanto is no stranger to scandals with seven-mile-long steps: since the 1980s, the company has been a defendant in cases involving harm to health with dioxin, polychlorinated biphenyls, the EU-banned Alachlor herbicide and Agent Orange defoliant used during the Vietnam War.  In addition, several senior employees of the corporation were found guilty of corruption in 2005; the company admitted that it paid bribes to Indonesian officials between 1997 and 2002.  So why are the US, EU and other countries stubbornly renewing the license to use glyphosate-containing herbicides?  Thanks to the more than $4 million that, according to OpenSecrets, Monsanto spends annually on lobbying?  Or because otherwise you will have to use more expensive ways to control weeds, which will reduce the effectiveness of soil use? bed Red-brown grass after treatment with a herbicide Photo: Depositphotos Probably, each of the reasons can be called correct.  World agriculture is dependent on chemical fertilizers, the former methods of tillage already seem ineffective.  Governments and world leaders are thinking about how to feed millions of people, forgetting that they may be losing their health.  In addition, the harm of glyphosate has not been proven, and this makes it possible to sleep peacefully.

passages.title: Russia: Environmental issues turn into political issues
passages.passage: For the second month in Russia, the scandal continues around the Yadrovo test site near Moscow in the city of Volokolamsk, where mass poisoning of children occurred due to emissions from the test site, after which rallies began.  Protests continue in mid-April, and the city authorities, meanwhile, intend to introduce a state of emergency and solve the problem with the landfill.  The situation in Volokolamsk is a sign of a deeper problem, which is associated with the annual growth of industrial and consumer waste in the country, which has nowhere to go.  The state to solve the problem announced garbage reform, which for various reasons has stalled.  The environmental crisis, meanwhile, has begun a transition into a political channel, which does not bode well for the authorities, experts say.  According to Rosstat, from 2006 to 2016, the formation of production and consumption waste in the country increased by 55% to 5.4 billion tons per year, and in comparison with 2003 - by 108%.  Data for 2017 are not available.  The special representative of the President of the Russian Federation on environmental protection, ecology and transport Sergey Ivanov at the end of 2016 estimated at 100 billion tons the volume of accumulated in the country for all time undisposed waste.  The accumulation of waste appears to be related to the underdeveloped recycling market.  Secondary use, according to the Ministry of Natural Resources, is limited to the processing of 50% of industrial waste and 10% of municipal waste.  Everything else is sent to landfills and buried in landfills.  In turn, representatives of Rosprirodnadzor said in 2016 that the existing capacities of the landfills will be enough to receive new waste for another 3-4 years.  The most acute situation with the loading of landfills is in the Central, North-Western, Volga, Siberian and North Caucasian districts.  The lack of space not only at landfills, but also at landfills, is stated in the “Final report of the ONF for the Year of Ecology 2017 ”.  “There are almost no free and suitable places for waste disposal, ” the authors write.  The situation is aggravated by the spread of illegal garbage dumps, which usually appear in forests.  At the end of 2017, Sergei Ivanov estimated the number of illegal dumps in the country at 60 thousand (it is assumed that the number of legal dumps is 4 thousand).  The cost of eliminating environmental damage from their work, he estimated at “trillions of rubles. ”  Political scientist Georgy Bovt is convinced that the work of illegal dumps is carried out with the tacit permission of the regional authorities.  “There are very specific people here.  Municipal authorities simply cannot fail to be a part of it.  For the sake of curiosity, ask in the search engine “garbage collection ”.  You will receive dozens of proposals, most of which will be related to illegal business, ” he writes in his column.  “The profitability of the shadow business associated with waste, only slightly lost [until 2016] revenues from drug trafficking, ” said Deputy Minister of Natural Resources Artem Sidorov.  Hazards to nature and health Landfills and landfills contain a considerable amount of waste that is hazardous to nature and health.  According to the latest report of Rosprirodnadzor, published in February 2018, at the beginning of 2016 in Russia there were 743 objects with a particularly harmful impact on the environment.  And these are only those that were at that time on the account of the department.  Due to the lack of separate garbage collection, extremely toxic materials fall into the garbage dumps, including mercury (from lamps and thermometer), nickel, cadmium and lead (from batteries and accumulators), etc.  The country has no capacity to accommodate or dispose of such waste, follows from the data of the meeting of the board of the Ministry of Natural Resources on plans for 2018.  Every year, the volume of waste of the second and first hazard classes (highly hazardous and extremely hazardous) increases by 300 thousand and 30 thousand tons, respectively.  In addition to waste officially recognized as dangerous, landfills, according to the ONF report, get cheap types of packaging, which “can have a strong negative impact on nature and health. ”  “For example, foamed polystyrene, which is almost not processed and when heated emits carcinogens.  In addition, manufacturers of goods often use multicomponent packaging, that is, consisting of and assembled from various materials, which, due to the need for additional separation into components, are usually ignored by processors as unprofitable and as a result they are sent to landfill, ” the report says.  According to the analytical department of the Federation Council, the contribution of environmental problems to public health is estimated by different specialists in the range of 10-50%, and in the near future “due to the progressive environmental crisis and the low level of material provision of medical institutions ” this contribution will grow to 60% or more.  However, according to the requirements of the World Health Organization, this contribution should not exceed 25%.  To solve the problem in 2015, Russia launched a reform in the field of waste management, which involves the gradual abandonment of burial in favor of recycling.  According to the idea of the government, manufacturers and importers of certain goods must either process the waste themselves or pay an environmental fee to the budget, with the money of which the state is going to build processing plants and organize a system of separate reception of garbage.  However, on the one hand, the collection rate was below the expectations of the state, and, on the other hand, state bodies for more than two years of reform, according to the ONF, could not combine their efforts and distribute powers among themselves.  In this regard, according to the authors of the report, the situation in this area has practically not changed.  Against this background, the authorities continue to develop plans for the construction of incinerators, which contradicts the ideas of reform.  In particular, four such enterprises are planned to be built in the Moscow region, another in Tatarstan.  However, according to ONF, the new plants in the Moscow region will not cope with the influx of garbage from the capital.  Their total capacity is 2.8 million tons per year, while the actual formation of only municipal waste in Moscow, subject to export to other subjects, is 6 million tons, the report says.  Moreover, three of the four plots allocated for the plants are located in a densely populated recreational area, which causes discontent among the local population, according to the report of the Council for the Development of Civil Society and Human Rights under the President of the Russian Federation.  “To date, neither Rosprirodnadzor nor the population has the necessary information about the detailed characteristics of the incinerators planned for construction and convincing evidence of their safety for the environment and the health of citizens, ” the report says.  As a result of the operation of these plants, ash and slag will be formed in the amount of 30% of the initial volume of waste, which have a higher hazard class and require placement on special landfills.  According to Nikolai Kichigin, associate professor at the Higher School of Urban Studies, there is nothing wrong with burning garbage (in some European countries, according to him, up to 50% of garbage is burned), but provided that the garbage is carefully sorted before this.  But in Russia, this condition has not yet been met.  In addition to the environmental crisis, problems with garbage, according to some experts, caused political difficulties.  According to political scientist Lilia Shevtsova, the events in Volokolamsk, caused by the mass poisoning of children, became one of the reasons for the “blow to the new presidency [of Vladimir Putin]. ”  Rallies in Volokolamsk are a sign of “changes in public consciousness and a serious challenge to the authorities, ” said Maxim Artemyev, an associate professor at the Russian State Humanitarian Institute.  “Environmental issues are at the forefront of the agenda of political and public life.  A few years ago in Italy, the garbage collection crisis in Naples was one of the reasons for the fall of the government of Roman Prodi, ” he said.

passages.title: Detecting plastic particles in water bottles
passages.passage: Tests on large company water bottles show that almost all of them contain tiny plastic particles.  In the largest study of its kind, 250 bottles purchased in nine different countries were tested.  The study, led by the press organization Orb Media, found that on average, there are 10 plastic particles per liter of water, each wider than a human hair (more than 100 microns) in diameter.  Manufacturers whose products were tested told the BBC that their factories operate to the highest standard.  The experiments were conducted at New York State University in Fredonia.  Sherry Mason, a chemistry professor at the university who conducted the analysis, told the BBC: “Bottle after bottle, Mark after Mark had plastic particles. ”  “The goal is not to make certain brands conspicuous; this experiment shows that the problem is universal, and plastic has become such a pervasive material in our society that it has found its way into all of the products we consume. ”  There is currently no evidence that microplastics are harmful, but understanding the potential consequences is a matter of scientific investigation.  Commenting on the results, Professor Mason said: “The numbers we see are not catastrophic, but they are a cause for concern.  Experts told the BBC that people in countries where tap water is likely to be contaminated should continue to use bottled water.  Playback of this file on your device is not supported.  Thousands of plastic particles in drinking water bottles from manufacturers have responded to the BBC by insisting that their products meet the highest standards of safety and quality.  They also noted the lack of regulations regulating microplastics and their standard testing practices.  Professor Mason found plastic particles in samples of tap water last year, and other researchers have found them in seafood, beer, sea salt and even air.  The new study comes amid further attention to the increasing penetration of plastic materials into nature following the BBC's second series "Blue Planet", in which Sir David Attenborough highlighted the threat of plastic waste in the oceans.  Aquaphina, Dasani, Evian, Nesli Pure Life and San Pellegrino as internationally recognized products, and Aqua (Indonesia), Bisleri (India), Opura (Mexico), Gerolsteiner (Germany), Minalba (Brazil) and Vahaha (China) as national products were reviewed in this study.  The number of particles smaller than 100 microns (one thousandth of a millimeter per micron) was much higher than the number of particles larger than 100 microns, which averaged 314 particles per liter.  The chemical composition of this group of smaller particles was not confirmed, but Professor Mason said they could also be expected to be plastic.  One obvious question was how the plastic got into the water.  One theory is that due to the amount of polypropylin used in production in the bottle, the process of opening the bottle may cause it to leak into the water.

**Report: Scale of Potential Harms and Cost for Producers in Roundup Cases**

The Roundup herbicide, a product of Bayer, has been at the center of numerous lawsuits and claims from individuals and organizations worldwide [2e190a2b-468a-400a-a1b7-7c137ccfeed9].

In the United States, over 130,000 claims have been filed against Bayer due to alleged health issues caused by the use of Roundup [428b6b50-45d6-4307-b3f3-d3bee5532856].

Bayer acquired 100% of Monsanto in 2018 for $63.5 billion, becoming the largest agricultural concern [2e190a2b-468a-400a-a1b7-7c137ccfeed9].

Since the first Roundup carcinogenicity conviction, the conglomerate has lost nearly 46% of its market value, and its share price has fallen to 2012 levels [2e190a2b-468a-400a-a1b7-7c137ccfeed9].

Bayer shareholders have expressed no confidence in the company's CEO, Werner Baumann, who made the merger deal with Monsanto [2e190a2b-468a-400a-a1b7-7c137ccfeed9].

In 2018, a San Francisco jury awarded $289 million to a former school gardener who was diagnosed with late-stage cancer, allegedly caused by Roundup use [428b6b50-45d6-4307-b3f3-d3bee5532856].

However, the judge later reduced the amount to $78 million [428b6b50-45d6-4307-b3f3-d3bee5532856].

Bayer appealed the decision, and the cancer claimant still did not receive the compensation awarded [428b6b50-45d6-4307-b3f3-d3bee5532856].

Title: Bayer lost the first stage of the court in the United States in the case of a potentially carcinogenic herbicide Roundup
Content: This content was published on March 20, 2019.  9: 26 in San Francisco.  March 20.  German chemical company Bayer AG lost the first stage of the trial in the United States in the case of a potentially carcinogenic herbicide Roundup, developed by the American company Monsanto, which since June last year came under the control of Bayer.  According to The Wall Street Journal, a jury in San Francisco ruled that plaintiff Edwin Hardeman contracted cancer as a result of the use of the herbicide Roundup.  During the first stage, only evidence of the potential harm of Roundup and its active substance, glyphosate, was considered.  In the second phase of the trial, which begins on March 20, six jurors must determine whether Monsanto should be held accountable.  Their decision could mean significant financial losses for Monsanto and Bayer, as their turn is waiting for about 11.2 thousand related to Roundup claims.  According to Bloomberg Intelligence analyst Holly Froome, the aggregate payments for all claims could exceed $5 billion.  Another six hearings are already scheduled for 2019.  Shares of Bayer fell more than 10% at the opening of trading in Frankfurt on Wednesday, then the fall slowed to 9.9%.  In August last year, a court in the United States ruled that Bayer should pay $289.2 million to school gardener Diwayne Johnson, who contracted cancer as a result of the use of the herbicide Roundup.  A few months later, the amount was reduced to $78.5 million as a result of Bayer ’ s appeal.  During the second stage, as in the case of D. Johnson, the jury will have to consider the role of Monsanto in concealing data on the dangers of glyphosate.  According to the plaintiffs, the company did not warn buyers of its products that herbicides can lead to cancer.  There is no consensus on the effects of glyphosate, the most common element in herbicides.  The International Agency for Research on Cancer considers this substance "probably carcinogenic", while the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) of the United States claims that glyphosate is safe when used cautiously. Title: Death in the garden: an American corporation found guilty of selling a carcinogenic herbicide
Content: When the elderly Pilliod of California heard the fatal diagnosis of non-Hodgkin lymphoma, they did not know that a few years later they would win a lawsuit against Monsanto, the world ’ s largest producer of chemicals for the agro-industrial complex.  However, this trial was only the tip of the iceberg, because thousands of Americans with cancer caused by Monsanto products are ready to file similar lawsuits.  Izvestia found out what transnational corporations are ready to do for billions of dollars in profits.  The manufacturer does not warn Alberta and Alva Pilliod began using Monsanto's Roundup herbicide to kill weeds in 1975.  Roundup was a novelty: Monsanto employee John Franz synthesized the active ingredient of the herbicide, glyphosate, only in 1970.  The couple bought Roundup for four decades, until in 2011 Alva heard a diagnosis of non-Hodgkin lymphoma, a cancer of the lymphatic system with lesions of the bones, including the spine.  Four years later, non-Hodgkin lymphoma was found in his wife Alberta, but with brain damage.  In 2017, the couple filed a lawsuit against Monsanto, based on the fact that two years earlier, the International Agency for Research on Cancer at the WHO announced the probable carcinogenicity of glyphosate.  In addition, their claim was not the first: at that time, the courts had already considered several similar complaints.  The case was accelerated due to the poor health of the plaintiffs, who at that time were already in their 70s, and on May 14, 2019, the jury decided after five weeks of consideration that Monsanto violated the law by not warning buyers about the likely risks, in connection with which it must pay a fine of $2 billion and $55 million in damages in favor of the plaintiffs.  This is the eighth highest fine in the history of the United States.  Monsanto Roundup sprayers in a garden shop Photo: REUTERS / Yves Herman Representatives of the owner of Monsanto - the German concern Bayer - said that they do not agree with the decision and will appeal because "all the world's leading health organizations agree on the safety of glyphosate and its non-carcinogenicity" It seems that justice has been served, greedy industries the nics got what they deserved, and the ordinary people who suffered from their actions left as winners.  If not for a few “but ”: first, victory in court will not save the lives of cancer patients.  And, secondly, the compensation awarded to them to the Pilliod spouses will not receive soon and in the wrong volumes.  The fact is that, according to a 2016 ruling of the US Supreme Court, the amount of the fine cannot exceed the amount of compensation for damage by more than nine times.  Thus, even if the appellate court reduces the amount of punitive payments to the maximum possible, the Pilliod spouses will receive, in addition to their compensatory $55 million, only $495 million.  This is the most favorable outcome for the plaintiffs.  Throughout the process, Monsanto ’ s lawyers argued that their products were harmless, as confirmed by research from the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), a federal agency that develops and monitors compliance with environmental and human health standards.  Moreover, in April, the EPA confirmed its initial findings, saying that while glyphosate use does entail some environmental risks, the agency ’ s findings on its impact on human health are consistent with those of other federal agencies.  “If we are going to feed 10 billion people by 2050, we will need all the tools at our disposal, including glyphosate, ” U.S. Secretary of Agriculture Sonny Purdue said in a statement.  Monsanto ’ s defense was largely based on the findings of an EPA study, and Bayer said after the verdict that the decision would not have been so harsh if the scientists ’ findings had been taken into account.  According to the defendant, Alva and Alberta Pilliod suffered from various diseases for a long time, which became the main factor in the development of cancer.  The concern also noted that if it were not for glyphosate, which is poured into fields to destroy weeds, the soil would have to be plowed regularly, which is expensive and harmful to the environment, since a large amount of carbon dioxide is emitted due to the overturning of the earth.  During the judicial investigation, it turned out that those conclusions of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), which the company refers to more than once as a justification for the safety of Roundup, can be questioned.  Demonstrators protest against Bayer Monsanto on the Place de la République in Paris Photo: REUTERS / Philippe Wojazer At the disposal of CNN was the correspondence of a Monsanto employee with one of the Agency officials Jess Rowland.  In it, a federal employee notes that if he can “kill ” glyphosate research at the Agency for the Registration of Toxic Substances and Diseases, he will“ deserve a medal. ”  Monsanto employees in internal correspondence note a low probability that Rowland and the EPA will be able to stop the study of another agency, but note that there is hope.  Judging by the fact that the Agency for the Registration of Toxic Substances never released a study on glyphosate, Rowland, already happily retired, coped with the task.  The Pilliod case is the third trial Bayer has faced over Monsanto products, particularly glyphosate-containing Roundup.  In all three cases, the jury ruled in favor of the plaintiffs with oncology, which developed due to prolonged contact with herbicides.  The first lawsuit against Monsanto was considered by the court last year.  In August, a San Francisco jury awarded $289 million to a former school gardener who was diagnosed with late-stage cancer.  However, a few months later, the judge reduced this amount to $78 million.  The case did not end there, as Bayer filed an appeal.  As a result, after almost a year, the cancer claimant still did not receive the compensation awarded to him.  In March this year, a California resident was awarded $80 million after he sued Monsanto for developing non-Hodgkin lymphoma.  The result is predictable: Bayer appealed, far from the outcome.  Thus, the concern is currently awaiting a decision on three appeals due to Monsanto products.  In addition, there are about 130,000 such claims under consideration in the United States.  And even for a giant like Bayer, it ’ s a pretty sensitive punch.  Bayer acquired 100% of Monsanto in 2018 for $63.5 billion, becoming the largest agricultural concern.  Since the first Roundup carcinogenicity conviction, the conglomerate has lost nearly 46% of its market value and its share price has fallen to 2012 levels.  According to The Fortune, Bayer shareholders told the company ’ s CEO Werner Baumann, who made the merger deal with Monsanto, of no confidence.  He was given nine months to prove that he deserved his place.  Glyphosate is currently the most popular herbicide in the world, despite the fact that after the report of the Agency for Research on Cancer, first France and then other European countries raised the issue of using this substance to combat weeds, and then began to remove it from store shelves.  Despite this, in 2017, EU countries extended the license for the use of glyphosate in agriculture for five years.  Photo: Global Look Press / Christian Charisius / dpa In Russia, Monsanto is present as a supplier of seeds of traditional breeding of corn, vegetable crops, offers farmers various plant protection products, while some of the products are produced in Russia since 2015.  Also in the country you can freely buy the herbicide Roundup, both wholesale and retail.  In addition, Russian companies produce about a hundred drugs based on glyphosate (the Monsanto patent for the molecule of the substance expired in 2000).  The volume of sales of the substance offered under the trademarks "Hurricane", "Typhoon", "Tornado" and others, is estimated at 15-20 thousand tons per year.  Monsanto is no stranger to scandals with seven-mile-long steps: since the 1980s, the company has been a defendant in cases involving harm to health with dioxin, polychlorinated biphenyls, the EU-banned Alachlor herbicide and Agent Orange defoliant used during the Vietnam War.  In addition, several senior employees of the corporation were found guilty of corruption in 2005; the company admitted that it paid bribes to Indonesian officials between 1997 and 2002.  So why are the US, EU and other countries stubbornly renewing the license to use glyphosate-containing herbicides?  Thanks to the more than $4 million that, according to OpenSecrets, Monsanto spends annually on lobbying?  Or because otherwise you will have to use more expensive ways to control weeds, which will reduce the effectiveness of soil use? bed Red-brown grass after treatment with a herbicide Photo: Depositphotos Probably, each of the reasons can be called correct.  World agriculture is dependent on chemical fertilizers, the former methods of tillage already seem ineffective.  Governments and world leaders are thinking about how to feed millions of people, forgetting that they may be losing their health.  In addition, the harm of glyphosate has not been proven, and this makes it possible to sleep peacefully.

Title: Russia: Environmental issues turn into political issues
Content: For the second month in Russia, the scandal continues around the Yadrovo test site near Moscow in the city of Volokolamsk, where mass poisoning of children occurred due to emissions from the test site, after which rallies began.  Protests continue in mid-April, and the city authorities, meanwhile, intend to introduce a state of emergency and solve the problem with the landfill.  The situation in Volokolamsk is a sign of a deeper problem, which is associated with the annual growth of industrial and consumer waste in the country, which has nowhere to go.  The state to solve the problem announced garbage reform, which for various reasons has stalled.  The environmental crisis, meanwhile, has begun a transition into a political channel, which does not bode well for the authorities, experts say.  According to Rosstat, from 2006 to 2016, the formation of production and consumption waste in the country increased by 55% to 5.4 billion tons per year, and in comparison with 2003 - by 108%.  Data for 2017 are not available.  The special representative of the President of the Russian Federation on environmental protection, ecology and transport Sergey Ivanov at the end of 2016 estimated at 100 billion tons the volume of accumulated in the country for all time undisposed waste.  The accumulation of waste appears to be related to the underdeveloped recycling market.  Secondary use, according to the Ministry of Natural Resources, is limited to the processing of 50% of industrial waste and 10% of municipal waste.  Everything else is sent to landfills and buried in landfills.  In turn, representatives of Rosprirodnadzor said in 2016 that the existing capacities of the landfills will be enough to receive new waste for another 3-4 years.  The most acute situation with the loading of landfills is in the Central, North-Western, Volga, Siberian and North Caucasian districts.  The lack of space not only at landfills, but also at landfills, is stated in the “Final report of the ONF for the Year of Ecology 2017 ”.  “There are almost no free and suitable places for waste disposal, ” the authors write.  The situation is aggravated by the spread of illegal garbage dumps, which usually appear in forests.  At the end of 2017, Sergei Ivanov estimated the number of illegal dumps in the country at 60 thousand (it is assumed that the number of legal dumps is 4 thousand).  The cost of eliminating environmental damage from their work, he estimated at “trillions of rubles. ”  Political scientist Georgy Bovt is convinced that the work of illegal dumps is carried out with the tacit permission of the regional authorities.  “There are very specific people here.  Municipal authorities simply cannot fail to be a part of it.  For the sake of curiosity, ask in the search engine “garbage collection ”.  You will receive dozens of proposals, most of which will be related to illegal business, ” he writes in his column.  “The profitability of the shadow business associated with waste, only slightly lost [until 2016] revenues from drug trafficking, ” said Deputy Minister of Natural Resources Artem Sidorov.  Hazards to nature and health Landfills and landfills contain a considerable amount of waste that is hazardous to nature and health.  According to the latest report of Rosprirodnadzor, published in February 2018, at the beginning of 2016 in Russia there were 743 objects with a particularly harmful impact on the environment.  And these are only those that were at that time on the account of the department.  Due to the lack of separate garbage collection, extremely toxic materials fall into the garbage dumps, including mercury (from lamps and thermometer), nickel, cadmium and lead (from batteries and accumulators), etc.  The country has no capacity to accommodate or dispose of such waste, follows from the data of the meeting of the board of the Ministry of Natural Resources on plans for 2018.  Every year, the volume of waste of the second and first hazard classes (highly hazardous and extremely hazardous) increases by 300 thousand and 30 thousand tons, respectively.  In addition to waste officially recognized as dangerous, landfills, according to the ONF report, get cheap types of packaging, which “can have a strong negative impact on nature and health. ”  “For example, foamed polystyrene, which is almost not processed and when heated emits carcinogens.  In addition, manufacturers of goods often use multicomponent packaging, that is, consisting of and assembled from various materials, which, due to the need for additional separation into components, are usually ignored by processors as unprofitable and as a result they are sent to landfill, ” the report says.  According to the analytical department of the Federation Council, the contribution of environmental problems to public health is estimated by different specialists in the range of 10-50%, and in the near future “due to the progressive environmental crisis and the low level of material provision of medical institutions ” this contribution will grow to 60% or more.  However, according to the requirements of the World Health Organization, this contribution should not exceed 25%.  To solve the problem in 2015, Russia launched a reform in the field of waste management, which involves the gradual abandonment of burial in favor of recycling.  According to the idea of the government, manufacturers and importers of certain goods must either process the waste themselves or pay an environmental fee to the budget, with the money of which the state is going to build processing plants and organize a system of separate reception of garbage.  However, on the one hand, the collection rate was below the expectations of the state, and, on the other hand, state bodies for more than two years of reform, according to the ONF, could not combine their efforts and distribute powers among themselves.  In this regard, according to the authors of the report, the situation in this area has practically not changed.  Against this background, the authorities continue to develop plans for the construction of incinerators, which contradicts the ideas of reform.  In particular, four such enterprises are planned to be built in the Moscow region, another in Tatarstan.  However, according to ONF, the new plants in the Moscow region will not cope with the influx of garbage from the capital.  Their total capacity is 2.8 million tons per year, while the actual formation of only municipal waste in Moscow, subject to export to other subjects, is 6 million tons, the report says.  Moreover, three of the four plots allocated for the plants are located in a densely populated recreational area, which causes discontent among the local population, according to the report of the Council for the Development of Civil Society and Human Rights under the President of the Russian Federation.  “To date, neither Rosprirodnadzor nor the population has the necessary information about the detailed characteristics of the incinerators planned for construction and convincing evidence of their safety for the environment and the health of citizens, ” the report says.  As a result of the operation of these plants, ash and slag will be formed in the amount of 30% of the initial volume of waste, which have a higher hazard class and require placement on special landfills.  According to Nikolai Kichigin, associate professor at the Higher School of Urban Studies, there is nothing wrong with burning garbage (in some European countries, according to him, up to 50% of garbage is burned), but provided that the garbage is carefully sorted before this.  But in Russia, this condition has not yet been met.  In addition to the environmental crisis, problems with garbage, according to some experts, caused political difficulties.  According to political scientist Lilia Shevtsova, the events in Volokolamsk, caused by the mass poisoning of children, became one of the reasons for the “blow to the new presidency [of Vladimir Putin]. ”  Rallies in Volokolamsk are a sign of “changes in public consciousness and a serious challenge to the authorities, ” said Maxim Artemyev, an associate professor at the Russian State Humanitarian Institute.  “Environmental issues are at the forefront of the agenda of political and public life.  A few years ago in Italy, the garbage collection crisis in Naples was one of the reasons for the fall of the government of Roman Prodi, ” he said.
