Title: Detecting plastic particles in water bottles
Content: Tests on large company water bottles show that almost all of them contain tiny plastic particles.  In the largest study of its kind, 250 bottles purchased in nine different countries were tested.  The study, led by the press organization Orb Media, found that on average, there are 10 plastic particles per liter of water, each wider than a human hair (more than 100 microns) in diameter.  Manufacturers whose products were tested told the BBC that their factories operate to the highest standard.  The experiments were conducted at New York State University in Fredonia.  Sherry Mason, a chemistry professor at the university who conducted the analysis, told the BBC: “Bottle after bottle, Mark after Mark had plastic particles. ”  “The goal is not to make certain brands conspicuous; this experiment shows that the problem is universal, and plastic has become such a pervasive material in our society that it has found its way into all of the products we consume. ”  There is currently no evidence that microplastics are harmful, but understanding the potential consequences is a matter of scientific investigation.  Commenting on the results, Professor Mason said: “The numbers we see are not catastrophic, but they are a cause for concern.  Experts told the BBC that people in countries where tap water is likely to be contaminated should continue to use bottled water.  Playback of this file on your device is not supported.  Thousands of plastic particles in drinking water bottles from manufacturers have responded to the BBC by insisting that their products meet the highest standards of safety and quality.  They also noted the lack of regulations regulating microplastics and their standard testing practices.  Professor Mason found plastic particles in samples of tap water last year, and other researchers have found them in seafood, beer, sea salt and even air.  The new study comes amid further attention to the increasing penetration of plastic materials into nature following the BBC's second series "Blue Planet", in which Sir David Attenborough highlighted the threat of plastic waste in the oceans.  Aquaphina, Dasani, Evian, Nesli Pure Life and San Pellegrino as internationally recognized products, and Aqua (Indonesia), Bisleri (India), Opura (Mexico), Gerolsteiner (Germany), Minalba (Brazil) and Vahaha (China) as national products were reviewed in this study.  The number of particles smaller than 100 microns (one thousandth of a millimeter per micron) was much higher than the number of particles larger than 100 microns, which averaged 314 particles per liter.  The chemical composition of this group of smaller particles was not confirmed, but Professor Mason said they could also be expected to be plastic.  One obvious question was how the plastic got into the water.  One theory is that due to the amount of polypropylin used in production in the bottle, the process of opening the bottle may cause it to leak into the water.

Content: Bayer offered to pay $8 billion for the settlement of claims over the herbicide Round On this information, the company ’ s quotes went up sharply Photo: Reuters Moscow.  9 August. Title: Bayer reported a bad quarter due to the pandemic and lawsuits « Russian Pharmaceuticals
Content: Bayer reported an unsuccessful quarter due to the pandemic and lawsuits Bayer published a report for the third quarter, according to which revenue and sales of the company decreased.  The pharmaceutical industry of the corporation tried as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic and legal proceedings. Title: Bayer lost the first stage of the court in the United States in the case of a potentially carcinogenic herbicide Roundup
Content: This content was published on March 20, 2019.  9: 26 in San Francisco.  March 20.  German chemical company Bayer AG lost the first stage of the trial in the United States in the case of a potentially carcinogenic herbicide Roundup, developed by the American company Monsanto, which since June last year came under the control of Bayer.  According to The Wall Street Journal, a jury in San Francisco ruled that plaintiff Edwin Hardeman contracted cancer as a result of the use of the herbicide Roundup.  During the first stage, only evidence of the potential harm of Roundup and its active substance, glyphosate, was considered.  In the second phase of the trial, which begins on March 20, six jurors must determine whether Monsanto should be held accountable.  Their decision could mean significant financial losses for Monsanto and Bayer, as their turn is waiting for about 11.2 thousand related to Roundup claims.  According to Bloomberg Intelligence analyst Holly Froome, the aggregate payments for all claims could exceed $5 billion.  Another six hearings are already scheduled for 2019.  Shares of Bayer fell more than 10% at the opening of trading in Frankfurt on Wednesday, then the fall slowed to 9.9%.  In August last year, a court in the United States ruled that Bayer should pay $289.2 million to school gardener Diwayne Johnson, who contracted cancer as a result of the use of the herbicide Roundup.  A few months later, the amount was reduced to $78.5 million as a result of Bayer ’ s appeal.  During the second stage, as in the case of D. Johnson, the jury will have to consider the role of Monsanto in concealing data on the dangers of glyphosate.  According to the plaintiffs, the company did not warn buyers of its products that herbicides can lead to cancer.  There is no consensus on the effects of glyphosate, the most common element in herbicides.  The International Agency for Research on Cancer considers this substance "probably carcinogenic", while the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) of the United States claims that glyphosate is safe when used cautiously. Title: Death in the garden: an American corporation found guilty of selling a carcinogenic herbicide
Content: When the elderly Pilliod of California heard the fatal diagnosis of non-Hodgkin lymphoma, they did not know that a few years later they would win a lawsuit against Monsanto, the world ’ s largest producer of chemicals for the agro-industrial complex.  However, this trial was only the tip of the iceberg, because thousands of Americans with cancer caused by Monsanto products are ready to file similar lawsuits.  Izvestia found out what transnational corporations are ready to do for billions of dollars in profits.  The manufacturer does not warn Alberta and Alva Pilliod began using Monsanto's Roundup herbicide to kill weeds in 1975.  Roundup was a novelty: Monsanto employee John Franz synthesized the active ingredient of the herbicide, glyphosate, only in 1970.  The couple bought Roundup for four decades, until in 2011 Alva heard a diagnosis of non-Hodgkin lymphoma, a cancer of the lymphatic system with lesions of the bones, including the spine.  Four years later, non-Hodgkin lymphoma was found in his wife Alberta, but with brain damage.  In 2017, the couple filed a lawsuit against Monsanto, based on the fact that two years earlier, the International Agency for Research on Cancer at the WHO announced the probable carcinogenicity of glyphosate.  In addition, their claim was not the first: at that time, the courts had already considered several similar complaints.  The case was accelerated due to the poor health of the plaintiffs, who at that time were already in their 70s, and on May 14, 2019, the jury decided after five weeks of consideration that Monsanto violated the law by not warning buyers about the likely risks, in connection with which it must pay a fine of $2 billion and $55 million in damages in favor of the plaintiffs.  This is the eighth highest fine in the history of the United States.  Monsanto Roundup sprayers in a garden shop Photo: REUTERS / Yves Herman Representatives of the owner of Monsanto - the German concern Bayer - said that they do not agree with the decision and will appeal because "all the world's leading health organizations agree on the safety of glyphosate and its non-carcinogenicity" It seems that justice has been served, greedy industries the nics got what they deserved, and the ordinary people who suffered from their actions left as winners.  If not for a few “but ”: first, victory in court will not save the lives of cancer patients.  And, secondly, the compensation awarded to them to the Pilliod spouses will not receive soon and in the wrong volumes.  The fact is that, according to a 2016 ruling of the US Supreme Court, the amount of the fine cannot exceed the amount of compensation for damage by more than nine times.  Thus, even if the appellate court reduces the amount of punitive payments to the maximum possible, the Pilliod spouses will receive, in addition to their compensatory $55 million, only $495 million.  This is the most favorable outcome for the plaintiffs.  Throughout the process, Monsanto ’ s lawyers argued that their products were harmless, as confirmed by research from the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), a federal agency that develops and monitors compliance with environmental and human health standards.  Moreover, in April, the EPA confirmed its initial findings, saying that while glyphosate use does entail some environmental risks, the agency ’ s findings on its impact on human health are consistent with those of other federal agencies.  “If we are going to feed 10 billion people by 2050, we will need all the tools at our disposal, including glyphosate, ” U.S. Secretary of Agriculture Sonny Purdue said in a statement.  Monsanto ’ s defense was largely based on the findings of an EPA study, and Bayer said after the verdict that the decision would not have been so harsh if the scientists ’ findings had been taken into account.  According to the defendant, Alva and Alberta Pilliod suffered from various diseases for a long time, which became the main factor in the development of cancer.  The concern also noted that if it were not for glyphosate, which is poured into fields to destroy weeds, the soil would have to be plowed regularly, which is expensive and harmful to the environment, since a large amount of carbon dioxide is emitted due to the overturning of the earth.  During the judicial investigation, it turned out that those conclusions of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), which the company refers to more than once as a justification for the safety of Roundup, can be questioned.  Demonstrators protest against Bayer Monsanto on the Place de la République in Paris Photo: REUTERS / Philippe Wojazer At the disposal of CNN was the correspondence of a Monsanto employee with one of the Agency officials Jess Rowland.  In it, a federal employee notes that if he can “kill ” glyphosate research at the Agency for the Registration of Toxic Substances and Diseases, he will“ deserve a medal. ”  Monsanto employees in internal correspondence note a low probability that Rowland and the EPA will be able to stop the study of another agency, but note that there is hope.  Judging by the fact that the Agency for the Registration of Toxic Substances never released a study on glyphosate, Rowland, already happily retired, coped with the task.  The Pilliod case is the third trial Bayer has faced over Monsanto products, particularly glyphosate-containing Roundup.  In all three cases, the jury ruled in favor of the plaintiffs with oncology, which developed due to prolonged contact with herbicides.  The first lawsuit against Monsanto was considered by the court last year.  In August, a San Francisco jury awarded $289 million to a former school gardener who was diagnosed with late-stage cancer.  However, a few months later, the judge reduced this amount to $78 million.  The case did not end there, as Bayer filed an appeal.  As a result, after almost a year, the cancer claimant still did not receive the compensation awarded to him.  In March this year, a California resident was awarded $80 million after he sued Monsanto for developing non-Hodgkin lymphoma.  The result is predictable: Bayer appealed, far from the outcome.  Thus, the concern is currently awaiting a decision on three appeals due to Monsanto products.  In addition, there are about 130,000 such claims under consideration in the United States.  And even for a giant like Bayer, it ’ s a pretty sensitive punch.  Bayer acquired 100% of Monsanto in 2018 for $63.5 billion, becoming the largest agricultural concern.  Since the first Roundup carcinogenicity conviction, the conglomerate has lost nearly 46% of its market value and its share price has fallen to 2012 levels.  According to The Fortune, Bayer shareholders told the company ’ s CEO Werner Baumann, who made the merger deal with Monsanto, of no confidence.  He was given nine months to prove that he deserved his place.  Glyphosate is currently the most popular herbicide in the world, despite the fact that after the report of the Agency for Research on Cancer, first France and then other European countries raised the issue of using this substance to combat weeds, and then began to remove it from store shelves.  Despite this, in 2017, EU countries extended the license for the use of glyphosate in agriculture for five years.  Photo: Global Look Press / Christian Charisius / dpa In Russia, Monsanto is present as a supplier of seeds of traditional breeding of corn, vegetable crops, offers farmers various plant protection products, while some of the products are produced in Russia since 2015.  Also in the country you can freely buy the herbicide Roundup, both wholesale and retail.  In addition, Russian companies produce about a hundred drugs based on glyphosate (the Monsanto patent for the molecule of the substance expired in 2000).  The volume of sales of the substance offered under the trademarks "Hurricane", "Typhoon", "Tornado" and others, is estimated at 15-20 thousand tons per year.  Monsanto is no stranger to scandals with seven-mile-long steps: since the 1980s, the company has been a defendant in cases involving harm to health with dioxin, polychlorinated biphenyls, the EU-banned Alachlor herbicide and Agent Orange defoliant used during the Vietnam War.  In addition, several senior employees of the corporation were found guilty of corruption in 2005; the company admitted that it paid bribes to Indonesian officials between 1997 and 2002.  So why are the US, EU and other countries stubbornly renewing the license to use glyphosate-containing herbicides?  Thanks to the more than $4 million that, according to OpenSecrets, Monsanto spends annually on lobbying?  Or because otherwise you will have to use more expensive ways to control weeds, which will reduce the effectiveness of soil use? bed Red-brown grass after treatment with a herbicide Photo: Depositphotos Probably, each of the reasons can be called correct.  World agriculture is dependent on chemical fertilizers, the former methods of tillage already seem ineffective.  Governments and world leaders are thinking about how to feed millions of people, forgetting that they may be losing their health.  In addition, the harm of glyphosate has not been proven, and this makes it possible to sleep peacefully.

Title: Russia: Environmental issues turn into political issues
Content: For the second month in Russia, the scandal continues around the Yadrovo test site near Moscow in the city of Volokolamsk, where mass poisoning of children occurred due to emissions from the test site, after which rallies began.  Protests continue in mid-April, and the city authorities, meanwhile, intend to introduce a state of emergency and solve the problem with the landfill.  The situation in Volokolamsk is a sign of a deeper problem, which is associated with the annual growth of industrial and consumer waste in the country, which has nowhere to go.  The state to solve the problem announced garbage reform, which for various reasons has stalled.  The environmental crisis, meanwhile, has begun a transition into a political channel, which does not bode well for the authorities, experts say.  According to Rosstat, from 2006 to 2016, the formation of production and consumption waste in the country increased by 55% to 5.4 billion tons per year, and in comparison with 2003 - by 108%.  Data for 2017 are not available.  The special representative of the President of the Russian Federation on environmental protection, ecology and transport Sergey Ivanov at the end of 2016 estimated at 100 billion tons the volume of accumulated in the country for all time undisposed waste.  The accumulation of waste appears to be related to the underdeveloped recycling market.  Secondary use, according to the Ministry of Natural Resources, is limited to the processing of 50% of industrial waste and 10% of municipal waste.  Everything else is sent to landfills and buried in landfills.  In turn, representatives of Rosprirodnadzor said in 2016 that the existing capacities of the landfills will be enough to receive new waste for another 3-4 years.  The most acute situation with the loading of landfills is in the Central, North-Western, Volga, Siberian and North Caucasian districts.  The lack of space not only at landfills, but also at landfills, is stated in the “Final report of the ONF for the Year of Ecology 2017 ”.  “There are almost no free and suitable places for waste disposal, ” the authors write.  The situation is aggravated by the spread of illegal garbage dumps, which usually appear in forests.  At the end of 2017, Sergei Ivanov estimated the number of illegal dumps in the country at 60 thousand (it is assumed that the number of legal dumps is 4 thousand).  The cost of eliminating environmental damage from their work, he estimated at “trillions of rubles. ”  Political scientist Georgy Bovt is convinced that the work of illegal dumps is carried out with the tacit permission of the regional authorities.  “There are very specific people here.  Municipal authorities simply cannot fail to be a part of it.  For the sake of curiosity, ask in the search engine “garbage collection ”.  You will receive dozens of proposals, most of which will be related to illegal business, ” he writes in his column.  “The profitability of the shadow business associated with waste, only slightly lost [until 2016] revenues from drug trafficking, ” said Deputy Minister of Natural Resources Artem Sidorov.  Hazards to nature and health Landfills and landfills contain a considerable amount of waste that is hazardous to nature and health.  According to the latest report of Rosprirodnadzor, published in February 2018, at the beginning of 2016 in Russia there were 743 objects with a particularly harmful impact on the environment.  And these are only those that were at that time on the account of the department.  Due to the lack of separate garbage collection, extremely toxic materials fall into the garbage dumps, including mercury (from lamps and thermometer), nickel, cadmium and lead (from batteries and accumulators), etc.  The country has no capacity to accommodate or dispose of such waste, follows from the data of the meeting of the board of the Ministry of Natural Resources on plans for 2018.  Every year, the volume of waste of the second and first hazard classes (highly hazardous and extremely hazardous) increases by 300 thousand and 30 thousand tons, respectively.  In addition to waste officially recognized as dangerous, landfills, according to the ONF report, get cheap types of packaging, which “can have a strong negative impact on nature and health. ”  “For example, foamed polystyrene, which is almost not processed and when heated emits carcinogens.  In addition, manufacturers of goods often use multicomponent packaging, that is, consisting of and assembled from various materials, which, due to the need for additional separation into components, are usually ignored by processors as unprofitable and as a result they are sent to landfill, ” the report says.  According to the analytical department of the Federation Council, the contribution of environmental problems to public health is estimated by different specialists in the range of 10-50%, and in the near future “due to the progressive environmental crisis and the low level of material provision of medical institutions ” this contribution will grow to 60% or more.  However, according to the requirements of the World Health Organization, this contribution should not exceed 25%.  To solve the problem in 2015, Russia launched a reform in the field of waste management, which involves the gradual abandonment of burial in favor of recycling.  According to the idea of the government, manufacturers and importers of certain goods must either process the waste themselves or pay an environmental fee to the budget, with the money of which the state is going to build processing plants and organize a system of separate reception of garbage.  However, on the one hand, the collection rate was below the expectations of the state, and, on the other hand, state bodies for more than two years of reform, according to the ONF, could not combine their efforts and distribute powers among themselves.  In this regard, according to the authors of the report, the situation in this area has practically not changed.  Against this background, the authorities continue to develop plans for the construction of incinerators, which contradicts the ideas of reform.  In particular, four such enterprises are planned to be built in the Moscow region, another in Tatarstan.  However, according to ONF, the new plants in the Moscow region will not cope with the influx of garbage from the capital.  Their total capacity is 2.8 million tons per year, while the actual formation of only municipal waste in Moscow, subject to export to other subjects, is 6 million tons, the report says.  Moreover, three of the four plots allocated for the plants are located in a densely populated recreational area, which causes discontent among the local population, according to the report of the Council for the Development of Civil Society and Human Rights under the President of the Russian Federation.  “To date, neither Rosprirodnadzor nor the population has the necessary information about the detailed characteristics of the incinerators planned for construction and convincing evidence of their safety for the environment and the health of citizens, ” the report says.  As a result of the operation of these plants, ash and slag will be formed in the amount of 30% of the initial volume of waste, which have a higher hazard class and require placement on special landfills.  According to Nikolai Kichigin, associate professor at the Higher School of Urban Studies, there is nothing wrong with burning garbage (in some European countries, according to him, up to 50% of garbage is burned), but provided that the garbage is carefully sorted before this.  But in Russia, this condition has not yet been met.  In addition to the environmental crisis, problems with garbage, according to some experts, caused political difficulties.  According to political scientist Lilia Shevtsova, the events in Volokolamsk, caused by the mass poisoning of children, became one of the reasons for the “blow to the new presidency [of Vladimir Putin]. ”  Rallies in Volokolamsk are a sign of “changes in public consciousness and a serious challenge to the authorities, ” said Maxim Artemyev, an associate professor at the Russian State Humanitarian Institute.  “Environmental issues are at the forefront of the agenda of political and public life.  A few years ago in Italy, the garbage collection crisis in Naples was one of the reasons for the fall of the government of Roman Prodi, ” he said.

Title: Detecting plastic particles in water bottles
Content: Tests on large company water bottles show that almost all of them contain tiny plastic particles.  In the largest study of its kind, 250 bottles purchased in nine different countries were tested.  The study, led by the press organization Orb Media, found that on average, there are 10 plastic particles per liter of water, each wider than a human hair (more than 100 microns) in diameter.  Manufacturers whose products were tested told the BBC that their factories operate to the highest standard.  The experiments were conducted at New York State University in Fredonia.  Sherry Mason, a chemistry professor at the university who conducted the analysis, told the BBC: “Bottle after bottle, Mark after Mark had plastic particles. ”  “The goal is not to make certain brands conspicuous; this experiment shows that the problem is universal, and plastic has become such a pervasive material in our society that it has found its way into all of the products we consume. ”  There is currently no evidence that microplastics are harmful, but understanding the potential consequences is a matter of scientific investigation.  Commenting on the results, Professor Mason said: “The numbers we see are not catastrophic, but they are a cause for concern.  Experts told the BBC that people in countries where tap water is likely to be contaminated should continue to use bottled water.  Playback of this file on your device is not supported.  Thousands of plastic particles in drinking water bottles from manufacturers have responded to the BBC by insisting that their products meet the highest standards of safety and quality.  They also noted the lack of regulations regulating microplastics and their standard testing practices.  Professor Mason found plastic particles in samples of tap water last year, and other researchers have found them in seafood, beer, sea salt and even air.  The new study comes amid further attention to the increasing penetration of plastic materials into nature following the BBC's second series "Blue Planet", in which Sir David Attenborough highlighted the threat of plastic waste in the oceans.  Aquaphina, Dasani, Evian, Nesli Pure Life and San Pellegrino as internationally recognized products, and Aqua (Indonesia), Bisleri (India), Opura (Mexico), Gerolsteiner (Germany), Minalba (Brazil) and Vahaha (China) as national products were reviewed in this study.  The number of particles smaller than 100 microns (one thousandth of a millimeter per micron) was much higher than the number of particles larger than 100 microns, which averaged 314 particles per liter.  The chemical composition of this group of smaller particles was not confirmed, but Professor Mason said they could also be expected to be plastic.  One obvious question was how the plastic got into the water.  One theory is that due to the amount of polypropylin used in production in the bottle, the process of opening the bottle may cause it to leak into the water.

background: I am a private detective based in Italy who is interested in Gustav Klimt's painting "Portrait of a Lady."
title: "Portrait of a Lady" found

passages.title: Found in the wall of the gallery picture Klimt recognized as the original
passages.passage: ROME, 17 Jan – RIA Novosti, Alexander Logunov.  Experts confirmed the authenticity of the found picture of the Austrian artist Gustav Klimt “Portrait of a woman ”, which was stolen in 1997 from a gallery in the Italian Piacenza, told RIA Novosti the head of the staff of the police department of the city Filippo Sordi.  The "Portrait of a Woman", believed to have been stolen from the Ricci Oddy Gallery since 1997, was discovered in mid-December by gardeners who were cleaning the walls from ivy.  The picture lay in a niche behind a partition in a black bag, which was hidden by thick vegetation.  Doubts art critics in the authenticity of the find was caused by the fact that the picture remained in excellent condition, being, presumably, abandoned by robbers 22 years ago.  “The research lasted a month from the discovery, experts appointed by the prosecutor ’ s office confirmed the authenticity of the painting, ” Sordi said.  According to him, now there are new examinations of the canvas for the left fingerprints and other evidence that can shed light on the mystery of the abduction of the portrait.  According to one of the most common versions, the kidnappers left the picture in a secluded place immediately after the crime, but were unable to return for it because of the uproar.  "As long as the painting is kept in a guarded safe by the Italian Central Bank, it remains at the disposal of the judiciary," Sordi said.  Despite the fact that the authenticity of the work has been established, investigators do not yet give an answer to another question of this detective story: whether the picture could all this time be in the chamber or was secretly planted there shortly before the discovery.  As told RIA Novosti, the president of the gallery of contemporary art Massimo Ferrari, on the day of discovery of the picture, the museum staff managed to get acquainted with the state of the picture.  “It ’ s too well preserved, especially when it comes to small scratches and a back with traces of wax.  If it was a fake, it would have to be made by a skilled craftsman, ” said the head of the gallery.  According to him, the traces that could be seen on the surface of the painting were quite comparable with other paintings of the museum.  In the conversation, Ferrari, however, does not hide the disappointment that the timing of the return of the portrait of Klimt to Piacenza remains unknown.  A small gallery has already planned for this year a series of events with the participation of the acquired canvas.  "Portrait of a Woman" was included in the list of the most wanted works of world art.  A small picture in green colors hit the front pages of newspapers a year before it disappeared.  In 1996, an 18-year-old student, flipping through a catalog of Klimat ’ s works in the gallery, drew attention to another female portrait that no one had seen since 1912.  As shown by x-rays conducted at the local hospital and subsequent studies, Klimt rewrote an earlier picture, which presumably depicted his deceased muse Maria Munch.  A new version of the painting, painted between 1916-1918, was soon acquired by the Italian collector Ricci Oddi.  However, to appear before the public with a newly acquired history of the picture was not destined.  In February 1997, shortly before the opening of the exhibition dedicated to Klimt, the painting was stolen.  In the conditions of the beginning of repair and turmoil around the organization of the show, the disappearance of the canvas was noticed a few days later.  The main version of the theft was built around the frame found on the roof, which gave reason to believe that the picture was pulled up with a fishing rod, but it is possible that the thieves entered the gallery from the front entrance - it is still unclear whether the outdated alarm system worked.  In 2016, new details emerged in the form of DNA samples found on the frame, but nothing has been reported since.

passages.title: The stolen painting returned home.
passages.passage: A painting by Gustav Klimt, a famous Austrian artist, discovered after decades at the site of the robbery, is on display again in its former location.  In February 1997, a painting by Gustav Klimt was stolen from the Ricci Odi art gallery in Piacenza.  The painting, known as “Portrait of a Young Woman, ” was the gallery ’ s most valuable work.  The painting was discovered at the scene of the robbery.  Workers at the Ricci Odi Gallery in Piacenza, after cleaning the outer wall of the gallery, came upon a secret door containing a portrait of a young woman.  Workers discovered the artwork while it was placed in a plastic bag.  Upon the discovery of the painting, the thieves admitted that they had returned the artwork to the scene of the theft.  After one of Caravaggio ’ s paintings stolen from a church in Sicily in 1969, it is considered the second most valuable art stolen in Italy.  The portrait of a young woman doubled in value when, shortly before it disappeared, an art student noticed that the portrait of the young woman had been painted on the portrait of another young woman.  It became the only painting by Gustav Klimt in the art world that has been painted twice.  Due to the closure of galleries and museums in Italy due to the spread of the coronavirus, it has not been possible for the public to visit the work in person, and officials of the Ricci Odi Gallery have provided the opportunity to visit the painting in its former exhibition.  Upon the return of the painting, the gallery ’ s director, Massimo Ferrari, referred to it as part of his gallery identity.  This painting is one of the works that Klimt created in the last years of his life.  End of message.

passages.title: Krimut painting worth 79.3 billion won found in garbage bag
passages.passage: A Klimt painting worth 79.3 billion won was found in a garbage bag.  13, 2019 07: 35. by Ren Bo-mei bom @ donga.com.  Gustav Klimt ’ s supposedly stolen work reappeared in the museum ’ s walls 22 years later.  Italy's Ansa news agency reported on the 10th (local time) that in Piacenza, the Ricky Ordi Museum of Modern Art has found a work suspected to have been lost in 1997, which is believed to be Klimt's Portrait of a Woman (photo).  According to the "Daily Telegraph" reported that on the same day, the museum's gardener found a metal plate attached to the wall while cleaning the climbing tiger on the outer wall of the building.  After opening, you see a gap connecting the inner and outer walls of the building with a black bag inside.  The gardener said, “At first I thought it was rubbish. ” Laura Bonpanti, the museum ’ s deputy curator, said:“ From the privy seal or seal on the back of the work, it seems to be the real thing. ”  It seems to be the best Christmas gift. ” If it is authentic, its value is estimated to reach 60 million euros (about 79,306.92 billion won).  The head of the Cultural Advisory Committee of Piacenza did not rule out the possibility of the theft of the works and their return.  "Immediately after the theft, we conducted a thorough search of all parts of the museum and the courtyard at the time," the person in charge said in the square.  The strangest thing is that the work is in very good condition.  I can't see it staying there for 22 years. '  In 1996, about 10 months before her disappearance, Portrait of a Woman was revealed to be the only work Klimt had ever painted on any of his other works.  At the time, X-ray analysis showed that Portrait of a Woman was supposedly painted on another of Klimt's paintings, Portrait of a Young Woman, which had been stolen in 1912.  한국어

passages.passage: The Belverede.Wien Museum Image caption A critic of the Kiss has called the "Image of Humanity" all great artists have a handwriting that is more or less recognizable, but if there is one whose works can be truly considered unique and imitable, Gustav Klimt is an Austrian artist of the early 20th century.  Klimt is hard to imitate in the days of “mechanical reproduction, ” as Walter Benjamin put it, but no one has ever been able to replicate the artist ’ s work with that stunning focus, balance, and harmonic balance.  Klimt ’ s art has a twofold and sometimes contradictory aspect: he was on the one hand a pioneer and avant-garde artist of his time who influenced a generation of modernist artists with impressive innovations and bold experiences, but on the other hand he based his art on simple and familiar themes that are beautiful and caressing to every eye.  Klimt ’ s paintings are easily adapted to any look and “eat ” the wall of any bedroom, living room or office.  It should not be forgotten that this perfection has been achieved with a lifetime of effort and struggle.  The revolution in the decorative art of Vienna at the beginning of the 20th century and the period known as the "end of the century" or "degeneration" stage was one of the main bases of modern art.  Gustav Klimt, with his revolt against academic painting, is one of the main representatives of the Art Nouveau style, which together with a group of modernist artists affiliated with the Céción exhibition created the Yogendale Steele (Young Style).  Classical and “scholastic ” painters considered Klimt ’ s work to be more of an arrangement and decor that moves away from“ the higher purposes of art. ”  In contrast to Klimt and his friends, they believed that the artist should have complete freedom in creativity and taste testing, and that no authority had the right to set a course for him.  Unlike many of his fellow artists, Klimt studied not at the Vienna School of Art, but at the Academy of Industrial and Applied Arts.  In the first phase of Klimt ’ s career, which he co-operated with his younger brother in a workshop, the combination of artistic creation and craftsmanship forms an intense combination that is both beautiful and “beneficial. ”  In the "Gesst" school, these compositional works, which could be a mixture of painting, sculpture and architecture, were called "art collections".  The aim of these "artisan artists" was to create harmonic forms and eye-catching compositions that can be used both in functional industries such as consumer appliances and furniture, as well as in the decoration of halls, interior decoration and architectural style of facades.  It was a poem of fine writing and color.  He has more than three thousand designs left, revealing his precise look and powerful hand. These works usually have a dramatic background or reference, in ancient mythology or tragic heroes, such as Salome, Judith, Danae and Athena.  He was very close to the stage of his career.  In many of these works he has a tendency to symbolism, which was one of the main trends in the art of the day.  As a passionate poet, he tries to embody general and abstract concepts such as life, death, philosophy, music, lust and jealousy with subtle and symbolic lines and forms.  In a series of colorful designs and paintings, "Hope" is a pregnant woman who is staring at her bulging stomach.  Despite Klimt ’ s mastery of design, he shuns accurate representations of the real world in colorful paintings.  His human figures change shape, along with the wave of lines and the dance of forms.  Klimt always fills the place of the "natural" motif with small and compact designs, so that the main texture of the figures and their surroundings is full of spirit and movement.  The Klimt gives the viewer the freedom to see the work in his own way and to evaluate and interpret it with his own mood.  In his art, he finds something hidden with a profound meaning that cannot be expressed; or he simply looks and moves the eye around the angles of lines, designs, and colors, and enjoys their harmony.  Klimt has something for every view and taste, and approaching his art does not require an expert.  Klimt's paintings are best known for their works known as the "Golden Age" and were created more or less during his artistic maturity, around the age of 40.  His father was an avid engraver and worked with gold.  It can be said that he inherited his love of gold from his father, but his familiarity with Byzantine tiles and paintings undoubtedly contributed to his interest in gold motifs. You have made your beanstalk with earthworms.  In his works, there are usually beautiful, naked and charming women in place of saints.  He may follow the Father ’ s tradition, showing each figure as a “piece of jewelry. ”  Perhaps the most famous of these is "The Kiss".  It all revolves around a love kiss.  Men and women kneel before each other in an ethereal space.  The man is strong, and the woman is strong, and he is strong.  The man ’ s coat is of angular and “hard ” roles, while the woman ’ s coat is covered with round and“ soft ” roles.  He is naked and alone, and does not reveal anything about the position of man or woman.  They are just two ordinary people who are intertwined with two different organs and can belong to any age and culture.  A critic has dubbed this position “the image of humanity. ”  By the end of Klimt ’ s life, the cold and grim charm of Expressionism had filled the air, but Klimt was more inclined to praise the joy of life, the joy of love, and the drink.  Her lively and beautiful nature is best seen in her natural landscapes and female portraits, which she brought to the canvas in the last decade of her life, from 1908 to 1918, with stunning perfection. Title: Found in the wall of the gallery picture Klimt recognized as the original
Content: ROME, 17 Jan – RIA Novosti, Alexander Logunov.  Experts confirmed the authenticity of the found picture of the Austrian artist Gustav Klimt “Portrait of a woman ”, which was stolen in 1997 from a gallery in the Italian Piacenza, told RIA Novosti the head of the staff of the police department of the city Filippo Sordi.  The "Portrait of a Woman", believed to have been stolen from the Ricci Oddy Gallery since 1997, was discovered in mid-December by gardeners who were cleaning the walls from ivy.  The picture lay in a niche behind a partition in a black bag, which was hidden by thick vegetation.  Doubts art critics in the authenticity of the find was caused by the fact that the picture remained in excellent condition, being, presumably, abandoned by robbers 22 years ago.  “The research lasted a month from the discovery, experts appointed by the prosecutor ’ s office confirmed the authenticity of the painting, ” Sordi said.  According to him, now there are new examinations of the canvas for the left fingerprints and other evidence that can shed light on the mystery of the abduction of the portrait.  According to one of the most common versions, the kidnappers left the picture in a secluded place immediately after the crime, but were unable to return for it because of the uproar.  "As long as the painting is kept in a guarded safe by the Italian Central Bank, it remains at the disposal of the judiciary," Sordi said.  Despite the fact that the authenticity of the work has been established, investigators do not yet give an answer to another question of this detective story: whether the picture could all this time be in the chamber or was secretly planted there shortly before the discovery.  As told RIA Novosti, the president of the gallery of contemporary art Massimo Ferrari, on the day of discovery of the picture, the museum staff managed to get acquainted with the state of the picture.  “It ’ s too well preserved, especially when it comes to small scratches and a back with traces of wax.  If it was a fake, it would have to be made by a skilled craftsman, ” said the head of the gallery.  According to him, the traces that could be seen on the surface of the painting were quite comparable with other paintings of the museum.  In the conversation, Ferrari, however, does not hide the disappointment that the timing of the return of the portrait of Klimt to Piacenza remains unknown.  A small gallery has already planned for this year a series of events with the participation of the acquired canvas. passages.title: Infographic Understanding Climate Change: Warmer weather not only harms human health, but agriculture and the economy have also paid the price
passages.passage: David Nelles and Christian Serrer: Climate change has now directly or indirectly affected the lives of 7.5 billion people on the planet.  However, the impact of global warming varies from place to place, which means that people and people living together in different regions will also be affected to varying degrees.  In any case, one thing is certain: the continued warming of the climate will continue to bring all kinds of adverse effects to mankind.  Climate change can have many effects on human health, such as heat stress caused by high temperature, operating environment factors (including air temperature, humidity, wind speed and radiation heat) and clothing, and high temperature events, which can worsen heart, blood circulation and respiratory related diseases. Increase the mortality rate of these diseases.  On the other hand, high temperatures are conducive to the formation of ozone close to the ground, which has adverse effects on human health, such as may lead to decreased lung function.  Extreme weather events such as floods or storms are more frequent and can also bring more hidden risks to human health, such as injuries and even death in serious cases.  In addition, already polluted waters may increase the risk of infectious disease outbreaks due to heavy rainfall and flooding.  Another effect of climate change in Germany is the lengthening of the pollen season, which exacerbates the symptoms of respiratory diseases such as asthma or allergic rhinitis.  And such climatic conditions are more conducive to the growth and reproduction of allergenic plants, such as Ambrosia is a good example.  Photo Credit: Businessweek / Lisa Schwegler, Stefan Kraiss, and Janna Geisse Produced The 2010 increase in global deaths due to climate change A spreading vector of disease caused by climate change refers to organisms that can transmit pathogens from infected animals or humans to other animals or humans, such as ticks commonly known as ticks, or mosquitoes.  Climate change is changing the current environmental conditions in which pathogens are spread by vectors.  In recent decades, due to globalization and favorable climatic conditions, the Asian-native Aedes albopictus (also known as the Asian tiger mosquito) has reached parts of southern Europe.  In the near future, other areas of higher latitudes in Europe should also become suitable for mosquito activity due to climate change.  It is important to note that the white line mosquito spreads dengue fever and Chikungunya virus.  On the other hand, the high temperature must be maintained for a period of time before the virus can be spread through the infected mosquitoes, because the warm temperature allows the virus to successfully reproduce in the mosquitoes and then transmit the virus to humans when the mosquitoes bite.  Rising temperatures create favorable conditions for the spread of Aedes albopictus and shorten the propagation time of the virus in Aedes albopictus.  Combining globalization with the risks that come with it, such as the importation of foreign goods that could trap Aedes albopictus, or returning travelers infected with the virus, increases the risk of disease transmission.  Photo Credit: Businessweek / Lisa Schwegler, Stefan Kraiss, and Janna Geisse produce Climate change impacts on agriculture High temperatures, high levels of carbon dioxide in the air, changes in rainfall patterns, and associated changing weather parameters can affect plant growth.  When the temperature rises to the most appropriate growth temperature, the yield of a particular crop can be increased, but once the temperature exceeds this optimum value, the crop yield begins to decrease.  In the case of corn and soybeans, as long as the growth period is more than 30 ° C, it is not conducive to the development of these crops.  In addition, extreme weather, especially drought and high temperatures, as well as heavy rain, can negatively affect yields. Between 2000 and 2007 alone, droughts and high temperatures have reduced global cereal crops by about 6.2%.  When the concentration of carbon dioxide in the air increases, many plants respond quickly by reducing the amount of water released from the leaves and increasing photosynthesis.  In this way, there is enough water and nutrients to promote plant growth, which is known as the "CO2 fertilization effect" (CO2-Düngungseffekt).  There is debate as to how much this fertilization effect can offset the reduction in production in some areas due to changes in temperature and rainfall patterns.  In addition, increased carbon dioxide concentration in the air can promote plant growth, but it also means that the nutrient concentration in the plant will be relatively reduced.  If higher average temperatures lead to longer tillage periods, less cold damage and higher crop yields, then climate change has positive implications for higher latitudes, such as northern Europe.  In contrast, climate change is not necessarily a good thing for crop yields in tropical and subtropical regions.  Climate change comes with three different types of costs: First, the cost of damage, such as direct damage to real estate or public infrastructure caused by extreme weather events.  This is followed by adaptation costs, such as levees or ponds for flood control.  The third is the so-called avoidance costs, such as the costs of switching from fossil to renewable energy to limit future global warming.  Because it is not possible to have a clear and comprehensive picture of all the costs incurred, it is actually very difficult to calculate precise figures for the economic costs of climate change.  Therefore, the calculated cost can only depend on the assumptions made, and it is very difficult to accurately grasp the costs of such things, such as melted permafrost, so it is extremely difficult to analyze the chart below.  Photo Credit: Business Week Publishing / Produced by Lisa Schwegler, Stefan Kraiss, and Janna Geisse Because of these high levels of uncertainty, it is very difficult to know exactly what climate protection measures should be taken and how much it should be interfered with from a purely economic point of view.  If people want to limit warming to 1.5 ° C, they will have to pay a very high investment cost.  Compared to setting the temperature rise range at a maximum of 3.5 ° C, the investment cost, although significantly reduced, will result in higher damage costs.  Overall, the cost of limiting global warming should be much less than the cost of damage caused by an unrestricted rise in global temperatures.  It is worth noting that as the temperature rises, the risk of irreversible damage is also increased.  Photo Credit: Businessweek / Lisa Schwegler, Stefan Kraiss, and Janna Geisse conclude that climate change is not a distant vision of the future, and that it represents more than just melting icebergs and rising sea levels, which are already threatening many people and their livelihoods.  In addition, it also shows that the temperature rise observed since the beginning of the industrial era is mainly due to man-made greenhouse gas emissions.  Fortunately, there ’ s also some ironic good news: we have the opportunity to influence the future of the climate, and we ’ re not completely powerless against climate change!  Climate model simulations show that as long as humans reduce greenhouse gas emissions, it is expected to limit the development of global warming.  Photo Credit: Businessweek / Lisa Schwegler, Stefan Kraiss, and Janna Geisse produced a global average temperature forecast for greenhouse gas emissions, but since the United Nations Climate Conference (UN-Klimakonferenz) was first held in Berlin in 1995, global greenhouse gas emissions have risen by 50%, reaching a record high.  If human beings continue to produce large quantities of greenhouse gases, it is not impossible to imagine that global temperatures will rise by another 5 ° C by the end of the century.  Therefore, we must all be aware of our responsibility: how the future of the climate, and the extent to which the impact of global warming will worsen, is entirely in our hands! passages.title: Climate Change Impact Assessment on Taiwan ’ s Human Resources (Part I)
passages.passage: Rising temperatures, intense heat, drought, orchard burning and heavy rain are expected to increasingly undermine agricultural productivity.  Challenges to livestock health, expected increases, declining crop yields and quality, and changes in extreme weather threaten rural livelihoods, food security, and price stability.  Pixabay economic growth is engulfed if we do not make substantial and sustained global mitigation of climate change, and regional adaptation efforts, it is expected to cost us infrastructure and property, increasingly, and hinder economic growth.  In the absence of major global mitigation actions and regional adaptation efforts, rising temperatures, rising sea levels and changes in extreme weather will continue to destroy infrastructure and property, labor productivity, and community vitality, especially as regional economies and industries that rely on natural resources and climate-friendly conditions, such as agriculture, tourism, and fisheries, are increasingly vulnerable to climate change.  Rising temperatures are expected to reduce the efficiency of power generation and increase energy demand, which in turn increases the cost of electricity.  Climate change is also expected to increasingly affect trade and the economy, including import and export prices, as well as businesses with overseas operations and supply chains.  In a moderately warm world, some aspects of the economy may improve slightly in the short term.  However, if the world does not reduce greenhouse gas emissions significantly and continuously, the planet is expected to continue to warm, causing significant net damage to the economy this century, especially as adaptation efforts are thwarted.  It is expected that the annual losses in some sectors of the economy will reach hundreds of billions of dollars by the end of the century, continuing to grow at the rate of past emissions.  Agriculture is highly challenged and threatened by rising temperatures, heat, drought, orchard burning and heavy rains, which are expected to increasingly undermine agricultural productivity.  Challenges to livestock health, expected increases, declining crop yields and quality, and changes in extreme weather threaten rural livelihoods, food security, and price stability.  Climate change poses many challenges to maintaining and improving crop productivity, livestock health and the economic viability of rural communities.  While some regions may see gains in productivity favoring expanded or alternative crops in the coming decades, overall, production of major crops is expected to decline due to higher temperatures, potentially altering water availability, soil erosion, and outbreaks of disease and pests.  Rising temperatures during the growing season are expected to be the biggest factor in the decline in agricultural productivity.  If the temperature at night exceeds 35 ° C, it will cause rice to be unable to pollinate; it will also aggravate the impact of diseases and pests, affecting the harvest of crops; high temperature and rain will make the soil unable to maintain nutrients, reduce crop yields and increase production costs.  The expected increase in extreme hot weather is expected to result in further heat stress for livestock, resulting in significant economic losses for producers.  Climate change is also likely to cause large-scale changes in the supply and prices of many agricultural products around the world, and the global supply and prices of agricultural products will also change dramatically.  These changes threaten future gains in commodity crop production and endanger rural livelihoods.  Agricultural production is an industry that is highly dependent on natural resources such as water, soil and biodiversity.  Climate change causes global temperature increases and uneven rainfall, disrupting crop growth, affecting the original habitats of ecosystems, and affecting the yield and quality of agricultural products, endangering food security and productivity, and causing loss of biodiversity.  There are many adaptation strategies to cope with climate variability, while reversing the adverse effects of change on agricultural production.  These include changes in production content, production inputs, the adoption of new technologies, and changes in management principles.  However, these strategies have limitations under severe climate change impacts and require both long-term and short-term investments.  High risk to health Climate change Air quality and health risks from extreme weather, air quality, and insects and pests, diseases transmitted through food and water supplies, are increasingly threatening the health and well-being of already vulnerable people; changes in temperature and precipitation increase air quality and health risks from wildfires (or incineration) and ground ozone pollution; rising air and water temperatures and more intense extreme weather are expected to increase exposure to waterborne diseases and foodborne diseases (food Sexual diseases), affecting the safety of food and water supplies.  Due to climate change, the frequency and severity of allergic diseases, including asthma and pollen fever, are expected to increase.  It also changes and expands the geographical distribution of disease-carrying insects and pests, exposing more people to the lice that bring Lyme disease and the mosquitoes that transmit Zika virus (such as dengue, yellow fever, Japanese encephalitis and Nile virus), which affect different transregions.  For example, communities in southwestern Taiwan are particularly vulnerable to the combined health effects of vector-borne diseases and high temperatures and floods.  Extreme and climate-related weather can have lasting mental health effects on communities, with adverse consequences, in particular resulting in degradation of livelihoods or relocation of communities.  Including the elderly, children, people in low-income communities and some indigenous and new communities, they tend to be disproportionately affected by the health impacts of climate change and are less resilient.  This helps individuals, communities, and counties to prepare for climate change risks with policies and programs to adapt and mitigate to reduce the number of injuries, illnesses, and deaths from adverse health outcomes.  According to the study, if the average temperature in Taiwan increases by 1 ° C in the future, the high risk of dengue fever will increase to 86, affecting more than 7 million people. In addition, the number of medium-risk areas has also increased to 203, and the future warming status will significantly increase the prevalence of dengue fever in Taiwan.  In addition, the increase in temperature in Taiwan will also increase the risk of related infectious diseases, and the impact of rainfall changes on infectious diseases will be more significant when the "daily extreme rainfall" is greater than 200mm.  In the face of the impact of climate change on public health, the adaptation that must be considered and prepared can be classified as at least three major aspects of infectious diseases, chronic non-communicable diseases and emergency medical care.  The main adjustment policies can basically be considered from the angle of strengthening and prevention.

passages.title: Climate change and 21% reduction in agricultural productivity
passages.passage: In a new study led by Cornell University in the US, experts have found that farms have averaged 21 percent less yields over the past six decades as a result of climate change.  According to the researchers, this equates to a total loss of seven years of agricultural productivity growth.  Global agriculture is increasingly exposed to the effects of climate change, with warmer places such as Africa and Latin America suffering the most, and agricultural productivity growth is currently down by 34%.  To quantify the impact of human-induced climate change on what economists call “total factor productivity or a measure of overall agricultural sector productivity, ” experts developed a comprehensive econometric model.  Professor Robert Chambers, from the University of Maryland, said the results show that climate-related factors have already had a major impact on agricultural productivity.  In this paper, we used a model to estimate how the total factor productivity patterns would be if climate change were not present.  Professor Ariel Ortiz Boba, principal investigator of the study and assistant professor at Cornell University ’ s School of Applied Economics and Management, said: “We found that climate change has wiped out about seven years of progress in agricultural productivity over the past 60 years, equating to pressing the stop button for productivity growth in 2013, after which no progress has been made, and now human climate change is slowing down.  According to Professor Ortiz Boba, the group considered more than 200 systematic changes from the econometric model, and the results were largely consistent.  When we focus on different regions of the world, we find that the historical impacts of climate change have been greatest in areas that have become warmer, including areas of Africa, Latin America and Asia.  Most people see climate change as a distant problem, but it ’ s one that ’ s already having an impact.  We need to address climate change now so that we can prevent future generations from being harmed.  The study was published in the journal Nature Climate Change.  End of message.

passages.title: Warming continues to warm India's rainy season will expand
passages.passage: Warming will make India ’ s summer rainy season more visible.  European studies have found that as Earth ’ s temperature gets warmer, every 1 degree Celsius increase in temperature is expected to lead to a 5% increase in summer rainfall in India, with consequences that will not only affect local crop yields in India, but also increase the chance of major flooding.  According to The Independent, India, which accounts for one fifth of the world ’ s population, relies on seasonal rains from June to September each year as a source of drinking water and farming.  However, the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research in Germany found that global warming will make the rainy season stronger and more unstable.  Using 31 new climate models, the researchers analyzed possible changes in India ’ s rainy season in four future climate scenarios, including successful efforts to limit warming to 2 degrees Celsius and ineffective efforts to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.  It was found that if we managed to keep the temperature within 2 degrees, the seasonal rainfall would increase by 10% between 1985 and 2015 by the end of the century, but if humans did nothing, the rainfall would increase by 24%.  In addition, for every 1 degree increase in global temperature, rainfall increases by 5%, compared to 3% in previous studies using earlier models.  In response to this, researcher Anders Leverman said, “As the difference becomes more pronounced from year to year, it will make the annual rainy season more unpredictable. ”  We also found that the increase in rainfall during the rainy season was more pronounced than in past climate models. ”  He also pointed out that climate change makes the rainy season more intense for many reasons, one of which is that warmer air will carry more water.  Andrew Turner, a scientist at the University of Reading in the United Kingdom, also believes that “the results also support the conclusion of earlier studies that rainfall will increase in India during the rainy season when greenhouse gases increase. ” According to CNN, India ’ s agricultural production accounts for nearly 20% of GDP, which plays an important role in the smooth development of the country.  Crops need rainfall, but too much or too little can harm plants.  In this regard, agricultural policy expert Devender Sharma pointed out that agricultural practices must adapt to climate change, but the specific way is still unknown.  “We don ’ t know how climate change will develop, and there is a possibility that a period of heavy rain will be followed by droughts or hurricanes, with no consistency, ” he said.  This will create a lot of problems for the agricultural sector and the economy, "he said.  The results of the study are published in the journal Earth Dynamics Systems.  [More details, see here]

passages.title: In the North Caucasus and southern Russia will increase snowfall and droughts
passages.passage: Climatologists predict that in the 21st century, the amount and intensity of snowfall will increase throughout Russia, and in some regions, arid conditions are expected to worsen.  This is reported by RIA Novosti with reference to the national report “Global climate and soil cover of Russia: assessment of risks and environmental and economic consequences of land degradation ”.  The study was conducted with the aim of developing measures for adapting agricultural and forest management systems and technologies to climate change.  Discussion of the report, analyzing the forecast scenarios of climate change and their impact on agriculture and forestry, was held at the Vasily Dokuchaev Soil Institute.  According to scientists, if at the beginning of the XXI century in Russia there was a small increase in precipitation, then by the middle of the century it will increase, especially in the eastern and northern regions of the country.  “The increase in summer precipitation is most significant, mainly in the north and east of Russia.  In the south of the European part of Russia - in the Southern and North Caucasus Federal Districts - the worsening of arid (on average per year) conditions is expected, "the study says.  At the same time, more "sharp" precipitation will probably occur in the form of separate showers or snowfalls.  There will also be more floods and floods.  Note that recently, scientists said that in 30 years the climate of the Rostov region in 30 years may change to subtropical, and the weather on the coast of the Sea of Azov will be close to the climate of Abkhazia and Sochi.  So far, we are lagging behind in temperatures: in the subtropics, the annual is + 11, we have + 9.95, - said Lyudmila Bespalova, Doctor of Geographical Sciences.  In her opinion, the summer shallowing of the Don in 2017, when the water left the coast by ten meters, is one of the brightest examples of climate change.  Changes in climatic conditions can lead not only to a change in flora and fauna, but also to a change in the economy of the region.  For example, Don farmers will have to breed new varieties of wheat and shift the timing of crops.

passages.title: Climate change and water scarcity are top priorities.
passages.passage: Assistant Professor of Water Engineering at the Faculty of Agriculture of Shahrekord University said: “The main priority of the authorities should be water shortage and climate change, so that water factories are moved to the seaside and agriculture in areas that are facing water shortage is limited. ”  He said: “It ’ s been a long time, it ’ s been a long time, it ’ s been a long time, it ’ s been a long time.  “When we talk about climate change, we mean meteorological parameters that have been measured over long periods of time, and these changes manifest themselves in either natural or artificial forms, which are caused by humans.  Nasr Esfahani said: “Various factors such as sunspots, changes in the earth ’ s crust, changes in vegetation or the movement of continents, or changes in ocean temperature naturally cause climate change.  “What has happened in the past year is that humans have caused an imbalance in meteorological parameters due to excessive consumption of natural resources, including oil, gas and fossil fuels, and by destroying natural resources such as forests and expanding factories and cities.  The university professor pointed out that the country is climatally located in a dry region, saying: "We should not expect the climate to change from dry to wet, because this is a very wrong expectation that some in the society suggest this."  He said: "Climate change has become very clear in the last 40 years, so we have to adapt to this situation that has been fluctuating and know that drought or drought fluctuations are part of the nature of the region's climate."  Nasr Isfahani said: "In this situation, climate change is occurring and extreme phenomena such as severe droughts, drought, heat and cold are increasing, there is no alternative but to adapt to them, for example, agricultural products can be used to prevent frostbite, to use resistant products.  Regarding water resources, he said: “At the same time as the climate change, the consumption of water resources has greatly expanded, especially in the last 50 years, when agriculture has been the center of development in the country. ”  The university professor said: "If we examine the rainfall parameter in more detail, we see that the average rainfall has not changed, but the extremes have changed a lot and these changes are significant, on the other hand, the effective rainfall has not changed and the ineffective rainfall has increased, which means that there is a shortage of water resources."  He said: "What has been observed is that, contrary to the rainfall parameter, changes in the temperature parameter, especially the minimum temperature, are highly effective and the trend of increasing the minimum temperature is observed in many stations in the country."  Nasr Esfahani pointed out that in mountainous areas the precipitation has changed from solid to liquid state, adding: "When there is snow in the region, because the snow is slowly melting and sinking into underground sources, it feeds them, on the other hand, the occurrence of rain brings water runoff, which feeds surface water instead of feeding groundwater resources."  He added that excessive consumption of water resources, expansion of the area under cultivation, non-observance of the cultivation pattern and the use of traditional methods for irrigation have led to the reduction of groundwater.  Assistant Professor of Water Engineering at Shahrekord University emphasized: "The authorities were aware of the current situation, but they did not think that the effects of climate change would be egregious and misrepresented, and today we face a fundamental problem, for example, if there was a shortage of water, it was solved by harvesting from underground water resources and we assigned this problem to the future."  He continued: “We have reached a point where groundwater resources are not the answer to the shortage of water, and this problem has become such that measures must be taken.  Nasr Esfahani said that for short-term purposes, water resources have not been considered because steel and water mills have been built in the country, which if this decision process continues, despite the lack of water resources, will still be built in the future.  “We should not expect that one day our country will be as abundant as Europe, because the lack of rainfall in our region has been caused by the rotation of the earth and the circulation of the atmosphere, so in addition to adapting to climate change, if there is to be a cost to this, it should be done today and we should not postpone those costs to the future, because we may face more limitations in the future. ”  The university professor noted that the main priority of the authorities should be water scarcity and climate change, so that water factories are moved to the seaside and agriculture is limited in areas with water scarcity.  End of message.

passages.title: Land abuse contributes to climate change
passages.passage: The land is often abused and contributes to the harm of climate change 2019-08-06 16: 42 Taiwan Awakening News reporter Zhuang Ruimeng / Taipei reported that the land has been used by humans to cultivate and lose its original function of absorbing carbon.  (Photo by M. Prinke on Flicker under Creative Commons license) Share Facebook Treating land better helps humanity fight climate change.  The UN Intergovernmental Panel of Experts on Climate Change, which is currently meeting, will present an updated report on the current state of human land use.  Experts pointed out that due to human behavior, land has changed from carbon capture to carbon release, threatening to exacerbate the power of climate change, and highlighting the importance of land use.  According to The Independent, global soils can currently absorb 1% of carbon, down from 7% in the past.  If the land is cultivated in a more sustainable way, carbon will be absorbed by the soil to become a carbon reservoir.  Currently, 1 / 3 of all pollution emissions come from land.  “If we take the severity of the climate problem seriously now, it will be worse if we don ’ t have land as a carbon reservoir, ” said Li Wen, a representative of the World Resources Institute. The scientists also pointed out that continued pressure on land, including the provision of food, wood and plant raw materials to meet increasing population needs, will make carbon reduction targets more difficult to achieve.  In addition, 33% of arable land has been used to grow crops that provide animal feed.  Professor Lixon of the University of Clanfield in the UK also believes that the latest IPCC report will provide more evidence that land degradation will also exacerbate climate change and lead to an increase in the crisis.  Addressing land abuse can focus on intensive agriculture, which involves farming on as small a land as possible, allowing more natural land to absorb carbon dioxide, according to the BBC.  Another option is to farm in a less dense and friendly climate.  Either way, however, the IPCC report will point out that poor farmers will be the group most affected by global warming.  Professor Berman, of the University of Oxford ’ s Institute of Environmental Change, said climate change had led to soil erosion in the south of the UK through more intense rainfall.  “Warmer temperatures and heavier rainfall will worsen soil erosion, soil compaction, loss of organic matter and biodiversity, and soil and rock flows, ” said Li Huicheng, chairman of the IPCC.“ I hope this report will serve to remind the world more about the threat that climate change poses to land. ”  [More details, see here]

report:
Climate change is affecting agriculture in various ways, including shifts in temperature, rainfall patterns, and carbon dioxide levels.

The rising temperature is expected to increase the frequency and severity of extreme weather events, such as droughts and heavy rain, which can negatively affect crop yields [a9485530-47ec-4015-8f1f-55d0e9b989ec].

High temperatures can also lead to a decrease in crop yields, as seen in the case of corn and soybeans, which are not conducive to growth when the temperature exceeds 30°C [19cf5a8f-d23b-4960-83dd-f4bc93f025fa].

Changes in rainfall patterns can also impact crop growth, with droughts and heavy rain being particularly detrimental to agricultural productivity [a9485530-47ec-4015-8f1f-55d0e9b989ec].

The increasing concentration of carbon dioxide in the air can lead to a "CO2 fertilization effect," where plants respond by increasing photosynthesis and growth, but this effect is debated and may not offset the reduction in production due to changes in temperature and rainfall patterns [19cf5a8f-d23b-4960-83dd-f4bc93f025fa].

Higher average temperatures can lead to longer growing seasons, less cold damage, and higher crop yields in higher latitudes, such as northern Europe [19cf5a8f-d23b-4960-83dd-f4bc93f025fa].

However, climate change is not necessarily beneficial for crop yields in tropical and subtropical regions [19cf5a8f-d23b-4960-83dd-f4bc93f025fa].

Agricultural productivity growth is currently down by 34% globally, with warmer regions such as Africa and Latin America suffering the most [1d5c736b-083a-42c0-a27c-6f57ca775bd2].

The total factor productivity of the agricultural sector has been affected by climate-related factors, with a comprehensive econometric model estimating that climate change has wiped out about seven years of progress in agricultural productivity over the past 60 years [1d5c736b-083a-42c0-a27c-6f57ca775bd2].

Rising temperatures during the growing season are expected to be the biggest factor in the decline in agricultural productivity [a9485530-47ec-4015-8f1f-55d0e9b989ec].

Extreme hot weather can cause heat stress for livestock, resulting in significant economic losses for producers [a9485530-47ec-4015-8f1f-55d0e9b989ec].

Climate change is also likely to cause large-scale changes in the supply and prices of many agricultural products around the world [a9485530-47ec-4015-8f1f-55d0e9b989ec].

The global supply and prices of agricultural products will also change dramatically, threatening future gains in commodity crop production and endangering rural livelihoods [a9485530-47ec-4015-8f1f-55d0e9b989ec].

Agricultural production is highly dependent on natural resources such as water, soil, and biodiversity, and climate change is disrupting crop growth, affecting ecosystems, and reducing the yield and quality of agricultural products [a9485530-47ec-4015-8f1f-55d0e9b989ec].

To adapt to climate change, farmers may need to change their cultivation patterns, such as planting crops that are more resistant to drought or extreme weather [38af1d5c-63ed-432d-b1e0-d57a347f6173].

In regions with brackish soils, such as the east of Mazandaran province, it is recommended to use plants that are resistant to salinity, such as soybeans and sesame, which have low water consumption [38af1d5c-63ed-432d-b1e0-d57a347f6173].

In areas with water scarcity, it is suggested to use direct planting and dryness in rice cultivation to reduce water consumption [38af1d5c-63ed-432d-b1e0-d57a347f6173].

The cultivation pattern and determination of suitable plants for each region should be based on geographical and meteorological information, water and soil studies, and zoning data [38af1d5c-63ed-432d-b1e0-d57a347f6173].

A suitable cultivation pattern should be implemented with a 10- or 20-year plan, subject to different scenarios, and should take into account geographical information, soil data, natural facilities, labor, ancillary industries, and product market prediction [38af1d5c-63ed-432d-b1e0-d57a347f6173].

Climate change is also expected to lead to an increase in snowfall and droughts in some regions, such as the North Caucasus and southern Russia [f1192a10-d9b4-4683-8e27-f8374d3cabf8].

The amount and intensity of snowfall are expected to increase throughout Russia, with arid conditions worsening in some regions [f1192a10-d9b4-4683-8e27-f8374d3cabf8].

The consumption of water resources has greatly expanded, especially in the last 50 years, with agriculture being the center of development in the country [b9d4a151-8bc6-4f35-99d9-b5d6ddca7ca2].

The average rainfall has not changed, but the extremes have changed a lot, and the ineffective rainfall has increased, leading to a shortage of water resources [b9d4a151-8bc6-4f35-99d9-b5d6ddca7ca2].

The effective rainfall has not changed, and the ineffective rainfall has increased, which means that there is a shortage of water resources [b9d4a151-8bc6-4f35-99d9-b5d6ddca7ca2].

The land is often abused and contributes to the harm of climate change, with 1/3 of all pollution emissions coming from land [8973d6cd-8e11-4ba7-8096-34dcc0e122d6].

Global soils can currently absorb 1% of carbon, down from 7% in the past, and if the land is cultivated in a more sustainable way, carbon will be absorbed by the soil to become a carbon reservoir [8973d6cd-8e11-4ba7-8096-34dcc0e122d6].

Addressing land abuse can focus on intensive agriculture, which involves farming on as small a land as possible, allowing more natural land to absorb carbon dioxide [8973d6cd-8e11-4ba7-8096-34dcc0e122d6].

Farming in a less dense and friendly climate is another option, but either way, the IPCC report will point out that poor farmers will be the group most affected by global warming [8973d6cd-8e11-4ba7-8096-34dcc0e122d6].
