passages.title: Britain's border controls are being tested by a surge in migrant arrivals at sea
passages.passage: Image copyright Susan Pilcher Image caption On New Year's Eve 2019, 12 stowaways arrived in the UK in a small rubber dinghy, including a 10-year-old child.  British Border Service agents are checking what they throw away.  With Brexit imminent, a large number of stowaways in small rubber dinghies flocked to England from mainland Europe.  At the request of the Home Secretary, the Royal Navy and Air Force sent aircraft and warships to help resolve the crisis.  Once the EU leaves the EU, both the UK and the EU will no longer be bound by the Dublin Agreement, which defined the return of refugees, but it may be difficult for the UK to repatriate any influx of migrants to the EU.  The 2019 New Year holiday has been a rough ride for Home Secretary David Javid: he ended his holiday in South Africa early and rushed back to London to discuss the crisis of stowaways arriving on the British coast by boat from the sea.  Britain is planning to leave the European Union by the end of March 2019. A BBC investigation found that human smugglers tricked refugees who had arrived in the Calais region of France into "selling tickets for the last chance to sneak into the UK before the UK closes its border gates".  They were in small rubber boats, not visible from the radar of the British border defense.  The shortest distance from Calais, France to the British coast is only 33.3 kilometers, so how many people come by boat from mainland Europe?  No one may know the exact number.  However, on New Year ’ s Eve 2019, the number of illegal immigrants suddenly increased significantly.  Why in the coldest, English Channel wind high waves when risking life and death to smuggle? The reason is still related to Brexit!  Image copyright @ premarmanche Image caption Britain and France have stepped up efforts to crack down on smuggling across the Channel.  A small boat was stopped off the coast of France.  According to the EU Dublin Agreement, refugees arriving in the EU must register in the country where they first arrive. Although all are based on the EU agreement, the treatment and even development prospects of refugees vary from country to country.  The British have begun to worry that once Britain leaves the EU, there will be no reason for the UK to repatriate refugees from mainland Europe to their original EU countries, whether France, Spain, the Netherlands or any other EU country, based on the principle of first arrival.  After urgent consultations, the Home Secretary ordered the return of two ships that had been part of a search and rescue project in the Mediterranean Sea to the English Channel to intercept smugglers along with border ships already patrolling the Channel.  However, the Ministry of the Interior does not feel comfortable.  Home Secretary David Javid said the deployment of the Royal Navy and Air Force was the only way to avoid the tragedy of the sudden arrival of so many refugees at sea.  The Secretary of State for Defence immediately dispatched the Mersey coastal patrol ship and Royal Air Force aircraft to help solve the problem of smuggling of refugees.  Mr Javid said Britain would continue to honour its promise to give asylum to those in genuine need, but would not allow criminals to use the system to exploit the most vulnerable.  Who are the stowaways?  According to the BBC, in a single month from November to December 2018, more than 239 people successfully reached the UK by rubber boat from coastal locations such as Calais, France, where refugees are concentrated.  This includes women and children.  Most of those arriving in Britain on rubber boats came from the Middle East, such as Iran.  Minister Javid said the reasons for the sudden increase in the number of people trying to sneak into the UK by dinghy were complex, including the turmoil in the Middle East, organized crime operations and Britain's increased protection against stowaways travelling to the UK by trucks, trains and ferries in Calais.  Many of these people will come to the police and ask the British government for asylum when they arrive in the UK. Although these people will be detained by the police, the British side will always need to provide these refugees, especially the children, with basic humanitarian safeguards.  Although the French side has pledged to help strengthen the fight against illegal illegal immigration to the English Channel, objectively, the departure of illegal immigrants from France does not appear to have caused pressure on French society.  How many people are currently applying for asylum in the UK?  The United Kingdom grants "refugee status" to people who are unable to live in their home country due to various reasons such as race, religion, nationality, political opinion or sexual orientation.  Successful applications usually allow applicants to stay legally in the UK for 5 years, after which they can apply for permanent residence in the UK as long as they meet conditions such as no criminal record.  Applicants include those arriving in the UK by rubber boats as described above, as well as stowaways arriving in the UK by ferries, trucks and other means.  According to the Home Office, the Home Office received more than 26,000 asylum applications in 2017.  This is a small number compared to the number of asylum applications received by other major Western European countries in the same period: 198,000 in Germany, 126,000 in Italy and 91,000 in France.  On the issue of the number of refugees, the European Union has been criticized and dissatisfied with the United Kingdom.  In the same period, the Home Office approved more than 21,000 applications and granted asylum to 31.8% of them.  At the end of 2018, more than 24,500 people in the UK were waiting for the Home Office to approve their asylum applications, of which 42% had been waiting for more than six months.  Most asylum seekers rejected by the Ministry of the Interior go back to court. In 2017, more than 5,000 of the more than 14,000 asylum applications rejected by the Ministry of the Interior were approved by court decisions, meaning that the Ministry ’ s initial refusal was overturned.  Image copyright Lewis Morris Image caption A large number of migrants, many of them Iranians, have recently arrived in Britain by boat from France.  It is worth noting that the number of illegal immigrants from China to the United Kingdom, which attracted attention more than a decade ago, has been drastically reduced in today ’ s refugee flows.  More than a decade ago, many Chinese people smuggled into Britain through Russia and mainland Europe. The deaths of 58 stowaways in Dover in 2000 and 23 shell-pickers in Merkham Bay in 2004 reflect the problem of a large number of illegal immigrants from China sneaking into Britain more than a decade ago.  The British government has also stepped up efforts to crack down on illegal immigration and illegal labor in the wake of the Merkham Bay tragedy, but illegal immigration remains a serious problem in other countries due to the high appeal of Britain ’ s welfare social and humanitarian policies to war-torn and economically backward regions.  The top 10 countries of origin with the largest number of asylum seekers are Syria, Eritrea, Sudan, Iran, Afghanistan, Iraq, Pakistan, Nigeria, Bangladesh and India.  Most of the stowaways who enter the UK find it difficult to repatriate if their asylum claims are rejected. In 2016, the British government spent a huge amount of money repatriating 6,000 foreign criminals.  The UK has a population of 70 million, but there are huge numbers of illegal immigrants, including stowaways and people who have expired their visas to stay in the UK illegally.  On the one hand, these people's work income, welfare and even human rights are difficult to be protected, such as being exploited by human smugglers, and on the other hand, they live in the society to the British free medical, education and other systems to increase the invisible pressure, which a few people breed crime problems to the society caused serious losses.  How many illegal immigrants are there in the UK?  There are no official figures available, and no one seems to be able to tell.  In 2001, the Home Office estimated the number of illegal immigrants in the UK at around 430,000.  A 2017 report in the Guardian quoted a senior Home Office official as saying that 150,000 to 250,000 foreigners do not leave the UK on time every year, including 26,000 who were refused asylum in 2016, and more than 1.2 million may be living in the UK illegally.

passages.title: Macron calls for resettlement of migrants in the Mediterranean
passages.passage: According to French newspaper Le Figaro, Guillaume Larrivé, deputy secretary general of the Republican Party of the French parliament, on Tuesday called on Emmanuel Macron to take the initiative of the Euro-Mediterranean summit on the issue of migrants to regulate the flow.  While humanitarian ships have rescued hundreds of migrants in international waters off the coast of Libya in recent days, Larivet told AFP that this is in fact a collective predicament that has brought us into conflict because of the plight of migrants, so I call on the president to take the initiative of the Euro-Mediterranean summit to stop this.  He called for organizing the flow of migrants in particular by creating “international cities for the temporary reception of migrants on the southern shores of the Mediterranean. ”  The humanitarian aid ship Ocean Viking, which on Monday rescued 105 additional migrants in international waters off the Libyan coast, has so far transported 356 people onshore to find a safe harbor.  During this time, more than 150 other migrants have been stranded on the Italian island of Lampedusa on the Spanish Open Arms for more than 10 days.  The governments of France, Italy, Spain, Malta and Portugal from Europe and Algeria, Libya, Morocco, Mauritania and Tunisia from the southern margin of the Mediterranean Sea in North Africa form members of the Euro-Mediterranean Group (5 + 5).  Earlier, Spain, Malta and France hosted the Euro-Mediterranean Group summit.  The most recent summit was held on 23 – 26 June 2019 in Marseille, France.  Following tough measures to block illegal migration routes through the Mediterranean and Libya, France ’ s Mayotte has become a safe gateway for African migrants to enter Europe in recent years.  In a report entitled "The Hidden Gate of Migrants to Europe", the newspaper said that to prevent the terrible crossings of Libya and the Mediterranean, African migrants are increasingly flocking to the shores of the 11st part of France (the island of Mayotte).  Last year, more than a million migrants arrived in Europe, with 3,800 drowning in the Mediterranean Sea, followed by strict security measures to prevent refugees from entering Europe.  The situation in Libya has been tense since April 4, 2019, when the army commander Haftar ordered his forces to attack Tripoli.  According to the United Nations, more than 220 civilians were killed and 1,066 others wounded, and many Libyans were forced to flee.  Libya has been divided into two parallel governments in the east and west since the overthrow of former dictator Muammar Gaddafi in 2011.  According to the United Nations, irregular arrivals from the Middle East and North Africa have fallen from more than one million in 2015 to around 141,000 last year.  Since the beginning of the year, less than 23,000 people have crossed the Mediterranean Sea and entered Europe as refugees or migrants.  The figures also show that nearly 15,000 people have been killed or missing on their way to Europe from the Mediterranean since 2015, a figure of around 500 this year.  France and the United Kingdom have pledged to control their water borders under the TUKE Treaty, which was signed in 2003 and entered into force in 2004.  France did not allow asylum seekers who were trying to cross the country to Britain.  This created makeshift refugee camps in the port of Calais, and thousands of refugees and migrants waited for the opportunity to reach the UK via the sea or the Channel Tunnel and the trucks that pass through it.  On June 5, 2019, Amnesty International issued a statement accusing France not only of threatening and detaining migrants, but also of detaining people who want to help migrants in camps.  The 14 member states of the European Union (EU) in Paris on July 23 agreed to a proposed German and French immigration plan aimed at expanding immigration on the green continent.  Under the proposal, asylum seekers arriving in Europe through the Mediterranean will be divided among the countries of the continent.  French President Emmanuel Macron said at the time that 14 EU member states had in principle agreed to a solidarity mechanism for the distribution of migrants led by Paris and Berlin in Paris with the “active ” participation of eight countries.  The French president did not elaborate on the plan, but said the "solidarity mechanism" of a new initiative to tackle Europe's migrant crisis would be "swift" and "automatic."  Establishing proper security conditions for asylum seekers and avoiding holding them in detention centers are among the other points emphasized in this plan.  A source close to the office said that in addition to France and Germany, countries such as Finland, Luxembourg, Portugal, Lithuania, Croatia and Ireland have also called for a new immigration system within their borders.

passages.title: Four People Drowned Down Boat of Iranian Refugees in Channel; French and British Authorities Emphasize on Tackling Illegal Migration
passages.passage: A British sailor who witnessed the capsizing of a fishing boat carrying asylum seekers in poor conditions told local authorities about the incident at around 9: 30 a.m., followed by a massive rescue operation involving six ships and three helicopters.  On Tuesday, October 27, four people, including two children, drowned in the English Channel between France and Britain.  French authorities have announced the rescue and transfer of the survivors to a hospital, while the search for the other passengers on board is ongoing.  On Tuesday, October 27, local authorities in northern France announced that a boat carrying refugees bound for Britain had capsized in the English Channel and a woman and a man, along with two children aged 5 and 8, drowned and died.  Although the exact number of people on board the boat is not known, nearly 20 refugees, most of them Iranian nationals, were on the boat.  According to local authorities in the northern French city of Dunkirk, near the scene of the incident, rescue operations began on Tuesday morning to transport the survivors to a hospital, but a man drowned and died before the rescue, followed by a woman and two children who died of cardiac arrest.  According to AFP, 15 of the rescued refugees are Iranian and have been placed in medical facilities in the port of Calais and the city of Dunkirk, among them a seriously ill man.  While the search for the other passengers was halted by nightfall, the Dunkirk city prosecutor and border police are still investigating the cause of the boat's sinking.  A British sailor who saw a fishing boat carrying asylum seekers capsize told local authorities about the incident at 9: 30 a.m., followed by a massive rescue operation with six ships and three helicopters.  The first investigation by local authorities found that the boat was carrying between 19 and 20 people and that the weather at the waterway was bad.  Marlene Schiapa, the French Interior Minister ’ s representative for citizenship, tweeted on Tuesday afternoon that she was “deeply saddened by the news of a boat carrying 19 refugees bound for the UK, and will work with the UK authorities to prevent such incidents. ”  Nous avons appris avec une grande tristesse le naufrage d'une embarcation qui transportait 19 migrants en direction de l'Angleterre.  @ MarleneSchiappa (@ MarleneSchiappa) October 27, 2020 "Refugees are risking their lives by crossing the Channel; I will do everything in my power to prevent unscrupulous criminals from exploiting vulnerable people."  British Prime Minister Boris Johnson also expressed sympathy for the families of the victims on his Twitter account, stressing that “the British government, along with the French authorities, will fight the smuggling gangs that prepare the dangerous journey of these vulnerable people. ”  My statement on those who tragically lost their lives in the Channel today. pic.twitter.com / W7zT5NKINr — Boris Johnson (@ BorisJohnson) October 27, 2020  Thousands of people from the Middle East and African countries attempt to cross the Channel each year, leaving 2358 people rescued by boat to the coast of France or the United Kingdom in 2019 alone, up from 2,586 in 2018.  One of the first asylum seekers to drown in the English Channel in 2019 was Mitra, a 31-year-old Iranian girl with a master ’ s degree in psychology who, along with 19 Iranian and Iraqi refugees, including seven children, boarded a boat for the UK on August 9.  The Channel between France and Britain has seen a surge in small boats carrying refugees to Britain since 1918, in which a number of refugees have been involved in accidents and some have lost their lives. passages.passage: A woman and a man who died with their three children while trying to reach Britain are from the village of Glynne.  The website also published the names and photos of the deceased.  French authorities on Tuesday confirmed the capsizing of a small boat carrying asylum seekers and the death of four people on board in the English Channel.  The third child of the Kurdish family is missing.  A total of 27 people were on the way.  A number of survivors are being treated in the hospital.  The rescue operation involved several coast guard boats and a Belgian army helicopter.  British Prime Minister Boris Johnson offered his condolences to the survivors.  British Home Secretary Priti Patel expressed sympathy for the victims and said she was very sorry to hear the news.  Patel said the incident once again highlighted the dangers of crossing the canal.  He promised to do everything in his power to stop traffickers from exploiting refugees in need.  The English Channel (English Channel) is a canal in northern France and southern Britain that connects the Atlantic Ocean to the North Sea.  According to data from PA Media, more than 7,400 people reached the UK via the English Channel in small boats this year, nearly four times more than in 2019.  This year ’ s “record ” was set with the arrival of 416 refugees on September 2.  Official statistics show that from June 2019 to June 2020, more than 3,400 people who applied for asylum are under the age of 17.  Of these, nearly 2,800 were unaccompanied children.  The British government can return refugees arriving from France under the Dublin Accords.  According to the treaty, asylum seekers who have entered Europe are only allowed to apply for asylum at their place of entry on European soil.

passages.title: 50 asylum seekers, including several Iranians, arrested in UK
passages.passage: British authorities have detained nearly 50 migrants trying to cross the English Channel.  British border guards have seized four boats with 49 migrants trying to reach England's shores on the English Channel.  According to the newspaper, the British Border Service received reports of an illegal attempt to cross the strait at around 01.30 local time and rushed to the scene of the incident.  All of the detainees, including several citizens of Iran, Iraq and Afghanistan, were transferred to the British Immigration Service.  In addition, the newspaper reported that French authorities rescued 14 others who had been sent to Britain along with the 49-strong group, who had difficulty crossing the strait.  Illegal migrants often seek every opportunity to cross the English Channel, where they are granted asylum and financial benefits by the UK ’ s special social programme.  According to the Daily Mail, about 1.7 thousand asylum seekers arrived in the UK in January, a significant number of whom risked their lives to reach the UK.  On the other hand, the Home Office is spending millions of pounds to tackle illegal immigration.

passages.title: Britain's new anti-immigration policy
passages.passage: Under the plan, which will soon be presented by Home Secretary Priti Patel, migrants who arrive on UK shores illegally by paying smugglers will not be allowed to enter the country.  On the other hand, the government will welcome refugees who use safe and legal means.  In other words, the UK wants to deal with migrants coming illegally from the Middle East and North Africa from now on.  In comments made at the party ’ s annual conference, which began online yesterday, officials from the ruling Conservative Party called the plan the most important policy review of the country ’ s asylum system in decades.  The move comes as a large number of asylum seekers tried to cross the English Channel to the south coast in September.  The British interior minister told a British newspaper: “Now everyone who enters our country and asks for asylum is treated the same way, regardless of the route they took to get there.  This is wrong and needs to be changed.  Patel has been trying to tighten immigration laws in the UK since taking over the Home Office.  He said he was seeking a law that would force police to return illegal migrants in the Channel to France.  British border officers now have no such authority and only intervene when the boat is sinking.  However, the Home Secretary has found existing laws ineffective and is considering new restrictions for the post-Brexit period.  In general, the number of arrivals has been increasing since a year before the UK officially left the EU.  Migrants from the coast near the French port of Calais try to reach the southern ports of England by crossing the English Channel.  Britain and France have taken special measures to tackle illegal crossings, but Paris has refused to accept migrants who have crossed the border illegally.  This challenge is one of the issues that UK and EU representatives are negotiating in post-Brexit negotiations.  Last year, the British government unveiled a new plan to welcome immigrants, which would drastically reduce the chances of applicants lacking the skills and expertise to immigrate to the UK in the post-Brexit period.

passages.title: No Asylum for Illegal Arrivals - 20201005 - International
passages.passage: The relevant provisions will be part of the “Fair Border Act ” to be published next year, which will stipulate that the treatment will be different according to conditions such as the mode of immigration to the UK.  Asylum is generally not granted to persons who enter through the Channel by boat or other illegal means, but it will be considered on a case-by-case basis.  Legal channels will be opened for those who are genuinely facing persecution to come to the UK, but if their asylum application is rejected, they will be sent back to a safe country they passed through before arriving in the UK, and there will be no “endless ” appeal.  Offenders and asylum seekers will also be deported if they are not at risk.  In an interview with the newspaper, Ms Pang said that all asylum seekers are being treated in the same way, without considering their way to the UK. For example, paying smugglers to smugglers is “morally indefensible ” for those who really need asylum.  The British media recently reported that the government intends to deal with the influx of illegal immigrants with an iron fist, including studying their placement on abandoned oil platforms or building a floating wall at sea to prevent illegal entry.  (Sunday Times)

passages.title: UK proposes new bill to establish special humanitarian channels for Hong Kong residents to apply for asylum ｜ Hong Kong 01 ｜ Real-time International
passages.passage: British media said on October 4 that the British government will routinely deny asylum to migrants boarding ships across the English Channel or arriving in the UK through illegal routes.  Separately, Home Secretary Priti Patel said the British government would establish “special humanitarian access ” for Hong Kong people.  The Sunday Times reported on the 4th that Home Secretary Theresa May will announce the Fair Borders Bill.  The government plans to adopt two systems for migrants. For the most vulnerable, the government will establish a new system to help them more easily obtain refugee status, but there will be different treatment for migrants who come to the UK to pay for criminal gangs.  "At present, everyone who comes to our country and applies for asylum is treated the same, regardless of the route they take into our country, which is wrong," Peng Daizhen said in an interview with the media.  The report said that the new legal route will be for those migrants who are really at risk. Pang said the government will work with the United Nations and refugee organizations to identify the most vulnerable people in refugee camps in the Middle East, and will set up a "special humanitarian route" for Hong Kong people applying for asylum in the UK.  Foreign criminals and those seeking asylum who are not at risk will be deported.

passages.title: France, France Sign Agreement to Stop Illegal Migrants from Crossing the English Channel – Radio France Internationale
passages.passage: LONDON (AFP) Britain and France have signed a new deal to stop illegal migrants from venturing across the English Channel by stepping up patrols and deploying technology on French beaches.  In recent months, a growing number of migrants have attempted to cross the dangerous and busy transport route from southern France to the south of Britain, killing four people last year and seven so far this year.  Home Secretary Priti Patel said today that under the agreement, French patrols will double from December 1 and use drones and radar to detect any attempts across the sea.  Bartel said the two countries share a "common mission to make the crossing completely unworkable" and that the new agreement would be useful in fulfilling that mission.  The problem of migrants crossing the English Channel has always been the crux of tensions between Britain and France, and London has condemned the Paris authorities for not doing enough to stop the smuggling of migrants.  From January 1 to the end of August this year, some 6,200 people attempted to cross the Channel by using inflatable boats, paddle boards, canoes and even life jackets to stay on the water. © 2020 AFP

passages.title: Britain and France agree to tackle illegal immigration
passages.passage: Britain and France have signed an agreement to further tackle illegal immigration through the English Channel.  Britain and France have signed a new agreement aimed at strengthening the fight against illegal immigration through communication channels with measures such as increasing the number of officers on the French coastline and better equipping them.  The agreement was signed by British Interior Minister Priti Patel and French Interior Minister Gerald Darmin.  As a result of a new agreement between the two ministers to tackle migrant activity, the number of patrols on the French coast is expected to double.  The two countries reaffirmed their commitment to block the route.  According to the press release, the number of French patrols will increase from December 1.  According to the press release, the cooperation will continue as more police patrols on the French coast and increased information sharing between the security and law enforcement agencies of the two countries have helped prevent illegal immigration from 41% in 2019 to 60% in recent weeks.  In addition to increasing the number of French officers, the new agreement also uses an “advanced edge surveillance technology package ” that includes drones, radar equipment, hunting cameras and fixed cameras to ensure migrants stop arriving in the country and leave the French coast, Patel added:“ In addition to these new action plans, we will introduce a new robust and fair asylum system and next year we will introduce a new law to enforce this commitment. ” We offer.  He said London and Paris were determined to provide safe and legal means to migrants in need of asylum, and that they wanted to fix their failed immigration system.  End of message.

passages.title: France to implement action plan to prevent migrants crossing the English Channel
passages.passage: Paris, January 5, 2019 (AFP) The French government announced today that it will use a "plan of action" to counter migrants attempting to cross the English Channel to the UK, pledging to end the phenomenon, which the British Conservative government fears.  The increase in asylum seekers across the sea, mostly Iranians, has put pressure on the British government to respond, with Home Secretary Sajid Javid declaring it a “major event ”.  French Interior Minister Christophe Castaner said in a statement today: "This project should allow us to put an end to the sea crossing," adding that these actions are not only illegal but also extremely dangerous.  "It is in our interest and that of the United Kingdom to do everything possible to prevent the development of new networks that would again attract irregular migrants to our shores," the statement added.  The plan will increase police patrols near ports where some migrants try to steal boats and monitor beaches where rubber boats have been deployed.  In addition to four British coastal patrol vessels, a British naval vessel was also patrolling the English Channel today.  A spokesman for French maritime operations in the region told AFP this week that France had doubled the number of coast guard vessels in the Channel depending on the weather. passages.title: France and Britain strengthen security measures to prevent illegal crossings of asylum seekers from the Channel Sea
passages.passage: France ’ s Interior Minister Christophe Castaner and his British counterpart Sajid Javid met on Sunday to discuss the expansion of cooperation between the two countries to deal with the illegal passage of asylum seekers across the Channel Sea, and several measures will be implemented soon.  Measures taken by both France and the United Kingdom to prevent asylum seekers from moving from northern France to the United Kingdom will include an increase in the number of surveillance patrols, serious measures to combat trafficking groups, as well as alerting refugees to the dangers of unsafe passage through the Channel Sea.  Interior Minister Sajid Javid said more border protection would also protect refugees and prevent humanitarian disasters.  According to the House of Commons MP Kent, more than 200 illegal asylum seekers have arrived in the UK from France in the past two months using unsafe boats and equipment.  On Sunday, December 30, an Iranian asylum seeker who had crossed the Channel using a motorboat to reach the UK were arrested.

passages.title: Why do Iranians go to Britain by boat?
passages.passage: PREMAR MANCHE Image caption Over the past three weeks, a boat group of asylum seekers, more than 100 migrants and asylum seekers who say they are Iranian, have tried to cross the dangerous route to Britain in small boats.  Why do they take such a perilous journey and where do they come from?  On November 23, shortly before sunrise, eight asylum seekers were found in a small boat in stormy waters off the coast of Kent in southeastern England.  They told rescuers they had been on the water for 12 hours.  A similar thing happened the day before.  Seven others were found in a boat off the coast of Dover.  A few hours earlier, the same number had been found in the same area in a windy boat.  Since November 3, 101 asylum-seekers, including children, have attempted a 34-kilometre route across the English Channel to reach Britain from France.  The Home Office has not released official figures on the number, but the BBC has found that at least some of them have been able to enter British waters since the beginning of the month.  All of them, without exception, have told the authorities that they are Iranian.  Image caption The BBC's Simon Jones posted a picture of one of the rescued boats around Dover, from the Balkans to Britain, why did so many boats sail to the coast of Kent in such a short time?  How are the authorities going to stop them?  Why are they all Muslims, as they say?  The answer to the last question lies about 2,000 kilometers away in Belgrade, the capital of Serbia.  Miudrag Chakic, the managing director of Serbia ’ s refugee relief agency, which monitors the movement of migrants in the Balkans, said refugees arriving in the UK were among the thousands who flocked to Serbia after Serbia decided to revoke visas for Iranian citizens last summer.  The Serbian government ’ s decision to cancel the visa was originally intended to boost the country ’ s tourism industry and trade with Iran.  The plan, which was said to have “exploited ” migrants and asylum seekers to reach Western Europe, was scrapped on 17 October 2018.  By then, it is estimated that about 40,000 Iranians had traveled to Serbia.  It is not known how many of the passengers had returned to Iran, but according to Serbian media, many of the flights were filled and returned empty.  According to Info Park, a refugee support group in Belgrade, Serbian police estimate that about 12,000 Iranians have not returned home.  Photo copyright MIODRAG?? REFUGEE AID Image caption Most asylum-seekers in Serbia sleep in abandoned buildings, but some Iranians who went there to seek asylum or emigrate to Western Europe are said to stay in hotels, asylum seekers or tourists?  Mr Chakic said he heard in a circle of people and groups dealing with refugees that Iranians were using "fake passports and very sophisticated methods" to reach Western Europe.  Unlike many asylum-seekers, they start their journey with more preparation and stay in a hotel or hostel.  Refugees from countries such as Syria, Afghanistan, Iraq and Pakistan sometimes walk thousands of kilometers and then sleep through the streets and abandoned buildings of Belgrade at night.  Gordon Panovic, of Infopark Group, says Iranians “look more like tourists than the rest of the migrants. ”  There were kids, all in jeans and jackets and backpacks. ”  “Many [Iranians] travel with fake passports that cost between 3,000 and 6,000 euros in Istanbul, ” Panović said.  Their situation is not the same as other refugees and migrants who have very difficult conditions in the Balkans.  They don ’ t have to sleep like everyone else or go to refugee camps. ”  “They were here for a month, staying in a hotel and making arrangements with the smugglers for their journey. ”  Iranians may be different from other immigrants in terms of economic conditions, but for many of them, life is not so easy with an “oppressive ” government.  Photo copyright MIODRAG, AKIAGE / REFUGEE AID Image caption The situation of Iranians is generally said to be different from other asylum seekers in the Balkat region, where Kaveh Kalantari, of the Iranian Association that supports asylum seekers in the United Kingdom, says the lack of freedom and human rights violations are driving these citizens to emigrate from Iran.  “People are arrested at the risk of having liberal or left-wing views, or because they are from religious minorities, ” he says.  Many people see violence on a daily basis. ”  It is estimated that since the Islamic Revolution about four decades ago, between 15,000 and 200,000 Iranians have left their country each year to emigrate.  According to the British Home Office, over the past two years Iranian citizens have applied for asylum more than any other country in the UK.  In 2017, about 9% of all 26,350 asylum applications were submitted by Iranians.  Image copyright NICOLAS ECONOMOU / NURPHOTO / GETTY IMAGES Image caption Tens of thousands of Iranians are believed to have emigrated to Belgrade, Mr Kalantari said: "It is not unusual for Iranians to come to Britain, but the way they are coming is unusual."  One theory about why Iranians risk their lives on boats, despite a better economic situation than other migrants, is that they have enough money to pay smugglers.  Maya Conforti, of the Migrant Hotel group that supports Calais refugees in France, describes this type of canal crossing as unique to Iranians.  "Crossing the Channel by boat (from France to the UK) is only possible for those with money," she said.  Africans have no money when they arrive in Calais. ”  "A new flood of Iranians has reached the port of Calais.  They seem to be the only ones who have the courage to do so and find a way. ”  Mr Chakic says Iranians moving to Kent in Britain have entered the European Union through Serbia.  “I don ’ t see any other explanation.  Serbia is the only country on the Balkan route that has a large number of Iranians. ”  Ingrid Parrot, who works for border forces in Cherbourg, France, has blamed "organized criminal and mafia networks" for the increased efforts to cross the canal.  Ms Parrot said there were 30 attempts to cross the canal in 2018, and the number was 12 and 23 in 2017 and 2016, respectively.  Photo copyright JEREMIAS GONZALEZ / IP3 Image caption The Calais Forest was dismantled in 2016, but refugees from different parts of Africa and the Middle East continue to live in refugee camps.  British border agents say it has become easier and cheaper to access smaller vessels, providing more opportunities for smugglers.  Charlie Alfik, MP for Dover and Dale in Britain's parliament, who described the increase in the number of attempts to cross the Channel as "unprecedented", said border forces needed more resources, including funding, to increase patrol boats as a deterrent force.  The number of refugees identified in Dover trucks has fallen by a third since the destruction of the Calais forest, the representative said.  But Bridget Chapman, of the Kent Immigrant Action Network, says the increase in channel crossings is "a natural consequence of becoming more violent and tightening conditions at borders."  “People are being forced to find ways that are becoming more dangerous day by day. ”  Damien Green, Ashford MP and former immigration minister, said there must be an emphasis on "where the refugees are coming from and the international criminal gangs behind it".  The Home Office says authorities are working "to identify criminal groups that facilitate illegal immigration".  According to Parrot, France has stepped up its measures to prevent attempts to cross the Channel, not just rescue operations.  "Our greatest concern is an incident that may result in loss of life or an incident at sea that requires our assistance.  "The fear that we will see wounded people on the water or the bodies that the water will bring to the shore."

passages.title: Interview with Zeng Yucheng: Why should we reflect on the immigration tide and urge the central government to try to win back the hearts of Hong Kong people _ Hong Kong 01 _ Political situation
passages.passage: By: Lin Jian Last updated: 2021-02-08 07: 00 "As a government, whether it is the central government or the SAR, it should also be realistic and analytical, why will more people leave during this period?"  Britain ’ s latest BNO expansion plan has triggered renewed debate between China and the UK.  Chairman of the Democratic Alliance for the Betterment of Hong Kong (DAB) and former President of the Legislative Council, Jasper Tsang, was interviewed by "Hong Kong 01" and talked about the political situation, immigration and other issues.  Jasper Tsang believes that in order for one country, two systems to be stable and far-reaching, at least two issues must be resolved first, including deep-seated social and economic issues, and the controversy over political reform.  No matter how much they dislike the opposition and cannot deny that they represent a considerable part of the voice of Hong Kong people, it is necessary for the government to create a good communication environment and jointly resolve disputes, no matter how difficult it is.  He also believes that not all opposition parties are “not patriots ” and that there are still some who can come together to discuss Hong Kong ’ s way out.  As for immigration, Jasper Tsang believes that the UK only wants to deal with China on the issue of the Hong Kong National Security Law through the BNO expansion plan, and attract Hong Kong talent and capital, and the so-called "historical responsibility" has nothing to do with it.  But he said he would look at the flow of migrants with a sense of normalcy and reflect deeply on where these Hong Kong people want to leave.  He called on the SAR and the central government to win back the confidence of the majority of Hong Kong people in one country, two systems as soon as possible.  Focus on the practice of one country, two systems: When will there be a "soft hand" when the "hard hand" has been done?  Throughout the interview, Mr Tsang talked about the political future of Hong Kong in a rather heavy tone.  Tsang said that in the 23 and a half years since the reunification, there are some phenomena that everyone has seen that the practice of one country, two systems, whether it is the role of the central government, or the relationship between the central government and the SAR, has undergone great changes in the past.  So the first question he asked was: "All those who care about the future of Hong Kong, and the Central Government, and those who care about the practice of one country, two systems, have to explore, if today we have entered a new mode of practice of one country, two systems, is this a normal situation that makes the practice of one country, two systems far away?"  Is the situation in Hong Kong, as we have seen since the implementation of the National Security Law, that most Hong Kong people will feel confident in one country, two systems if it continues? ”  He mentioned that after the implementation of the National Security Law in Hong Kong, some street violence and acts that hit the bottom line of one country have indeed converged, but if one country, two systems are to be stable, it must also win the support of the majority of Hong Kong people, and this "remains to be studied": "I believe that most Hong Kong people have a negative attitude towards acts of social order and Hong Kong independence. But then everyone will see whether the situation in Hong Kong will continue to be like this." Zeng Yucheng pointed out that recently, when talking with many friends about the political situation in Hong Kong, they will ask a question: The central government has done a good job in Hong Kong's "hard hand" and has been effective, when will there be a "soft hand" to win back the hearts of Hong Kong people and heartfelt support for one country, two systems?  In principle, I agree with the "01" advocate for social and economic structural reform, and believe that there are at least two deep-seated contradictions that must be dealt with in the way out of Hong Kong's political and social situation.  First, the serious inequity of society.  He pointed out that the gap between the rich and the poor has widened rather than narrowed in the more than 20 years since the reunification, so he agreed in principle that Hong Kong must usher in a major reform, and the government's governance thinking needs to change: "Simply put, it is to 'turn to the left' and change the set of 'positive non-intervention', 'big market small government' and 'far-right capitalism' left by the British people."  Second, Jasper Tsang believes that reconciling the contradictions in Hong Kong society has never been able to evade the political controversy.  Articles 45 and 68 of the Basic Law stipulate that the ultimate goal is to elect the Chief Executive and the legislature by universal suffrage.  The final goal of universal suffrage is still to be achieved unless an authoritative person says that "it was written wrong in the drafting of the year" and raises the issue of political system, the topic will inevitably fall to political reform and universal suffrage disputes.  Former Chief Executive Leung Chun-ying, Vice Chairman of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC) and former Chief Executive of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC), raised the "Chief Executive's Discussion" during an interview with "Hong Kong 01" earlier, which caused political debate.  Mr Tsang, who seems to have shown little interest in these debates, reiterated only one key point: Article 45 of the Basic Law stipulates that the method for selecting the Chief Executive shall be based on the "actual situation and the principle of gradual and orderly progress" with the ultimate goal of "electing the Chief Executive by universal suffrage after nomination by a broadly representative nominating committee in accordance with democratic procedures".  If someone really believes that the “actual situation ” in Hong Kong has changed and it is not worth pursuing this goal, or even going back, the government needs to come out and make it clear.  "Unless I hear authoritative people and central leaders come out and say that we were wrong when we wrote the Basic Law, universal suffrage is not a good system.  One day no one denies this, it is the ultimate goal of the Basic Law, that is to accept, the drafter tells us that he thinks universal suffrage is a good thing.  Recently, some articles came out and said, “It ’ s outdated, and I still think the election is good, how is the United States now? ” If so, please ask the authoritative person in the central government to tell us,“ Sorry, we made a mistake at that time. ”  Mr Leung's earlier suggestion of "consultation" caused political controversy.  (Photo) Call on the Central Authorities, the SAR Government to take the initiative to re-open the door of communication with the democrats. Tsang admitted that with the political energy of the current SAR Government, it is more difficult to push forward the political reform plan, but believes that as a government, it is responsible for dialogue with people from different camps as far as possible to find where there is room for discussion.  "Of course you can say that it is the opposition itself that does not accept the 8.31 framework, but it is your responsibility to re-establish the dialogue channel."  Have you tried it? "  He mentioned that there have been private exchanges with some pan-democrats, and the other side also admitted that if the political reality is to restart the political reform, it must also be based on the 8.31 decision, but it was only during the 2014 Umbrella Movement and the 2015 voting political reform, and it was impossible to support the political reform under the 8.31 framework at that time.  However, today, after the enactment of the National Security Law, political reform is still a potential starting point for political contradictions, and both the SAR and the central government have the responsibility to actively establish communication channels with the unorganized camps and unite all those who can be united.  “You can ’ t deny the fact that a significant number of Hong Kong people still support these unformed factions, even if they fully accept the National Security Law and all the decisions of the Standing Committee of the National People ’ s Congress, and believe that some pan-democrats are not patriotic and cannot be given the opportunity to enter politics, does it mean that they (the citizens) all support the establishment? ”  Therefore, Jasper Zeng believes that the central government and the SAR government must first establish a sense of communication with the democrats, before it is expected to resolve political differences: "Restarting political reform is not like a door, saying that it is very windy outside, sitting here and waiting, to open the door to restart political reform without wind, not so, now we must start doing things."  Maybe the first time, the second time, the other side will "bang" shut the door and kick you out, don't talk to you, but still have to continue knocking on the door? "」  He also believes that even if some extreme radicals are "not saved", but they believe that among the democrats, there are many people who hope that one country, two systems can be successfully implemented, and that the country is good for Hong Kong, and they can unite, and they do not think that all the democrats are "anti-China and Hong Kong".  The controversy over political reform is one of the underlying causes of political contradictions in Hong Kong. (Photo by Andrew Law) “Patriotism ” is another core issue in the political controversy over

passages.title: Exclusive _ Home Office Report Reveals $30 Billion in Economic Benefits for Millions of Hong Kong Residents to Move to the UK in 5 Years _ Apple Daily
passages.passage: According to the Ministry of Home Affairs, it is estimated that between 2021 and 2025, the number of Hong Kong people moving to the UK can reach a maximum of 1,048,100, while the BNO policy will bring a maximum of 2.939 billion pounds (about 31 billion Hong Kong dollars) to the British government in five years.  Since Wuhan pneumonia has not been taken into account by the authorities, based on the current LOTR and new BNO applications, the authorities conservatively estimate that about 290,000 people have moved to the UK, of which about 138,000 will apply for visas this year.  Billy, head of Hong Kong at Goodbye HK, Hello UK, believes that the number of people moving to the UK is reasonable, but does not believe that up to 1 million people will leave.  If 1 million people emigrate, the school dropout in Hong Kong could be “even more violent ”.  Regarding the loss of hundreds of thousands of talents due to the BNO policy, it is reported that China ’ s countermeasures will include consideration of re-opening the talent scheme and importing more “mainland elites ” to fill the gap.  George, a Hong Kong resident who has lived in the UK for more than 10 years and is engaged in the financial industry in London, believes that if there are really more than a million people to the UK, it is not a bad thing. "Before Brexit, millions of people come from Europe every year, many of them are Eastern Europeans, especially London and Birmingham.  He believes that the British cities themselves are multicultural, Hong Kong people are not refugees, but really can bring some quality talent and capital to come, "London's Chinese circle is actually very small, more people are good, sometimes I will Homesick, in the future, the United Kingdom may have a" small Hong Kong "like Canada." $80 billion in capital outflows.  The Home Office has released an assessment report on the impact assessment of the BNO visa policy for Hong Kong residents. It is estimated that Hong Kong residents will bring 2.939 billion pounds of income to the UK. Billy believes that these figures are not exaggerated, because Hong Kong immigrant families generally have higher asset values, plus consumption and work, together with income tax, will definitely bring substantial long-term economic benefits to the UK.  The report also said that only 167,000 people originally held BNO before July 2019, but in August 2020, it has increased to 612,000, reflecting a sharp increase in the number of BNO applications after the anti-extradition campaign, which is estimated to have increased to 733,000 by the end of 2020.  After the Hong Kong government implemented the National Security Law in Hong Kong in July last year, the British government immediately announced the BNO resettlement policy, which is eligible for 2.9 million Hong Kong residents, 2.3 million relatives, and 187,000 BNO dependants aged between 18 and 23.  Based on figures from the Hong Kong Immigration Department, David Webb, an independent stock reviewer, concluded that between 1 July 2020 and 8 January 2021, there were 115,000 net outbound Hong Kong residents, accounting for about 1.5% of Hong Kong ’ s 7.5 million population.  Between 15 July and 14 October last year, 2,116 BNO eligible individuals and their relatives entered the country early with Leave Outside The Rules (LOTR).  As for the number of LOTR failure cases, the UK Ministry of Home Affairs replied that after careful consideration by the authorities, it is believed that the disclosure of the information will affect public affairs and interests, so the relevant data will not be disclosed for the time being.  Based on the increase in BNO applications from July 2019 to October 2020, it is estimated that the maximum number of people moving to the UK between 2021 and 2025 will be about 833,000. Based on the increase from July 2019 to the end of 2020, the maximum number of people moving to the UK will reach 1.05 million.  In terms of economic benefits, the first five years of BNO immigration will bring 6.671 billion pounds (about HK $70.6 billion) of tax revenue to the UK, 792 million pounds (about HK $8.4 billion) of health care costs and 86 million pounds (about HK $900 million) of visa application costs.).  As it is difficult to measure all cases, the report divides BNO eligible applicants into two categories. The first category is BNO applicants after the social movement in 2019, which are reported to be more likely to immigrate. The second category is applicants before the social movement in 2019.  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

passages.title: Iranian migrant boat sinking in English Channel; UK and France
passages.passage: The sinking of boats of Iranian migrants in the English Channel; the support of refugees from Britain and France has been criticized by several refugee organizations, Reuters, who have said that the deaths of two children and two adults in the sinking of a boat carrying migrants in the English Channel should be a "wake-up call" for those in power.  Save the Children said the English Channel should not be a graveyard for children.  On Monday, a boat carrying refugees sank across the English Channel in waters between France and Britain, killing at least four people.  The victims may have been Iranian.  A man drowned, and a woman and two children aged five and eight died of cardiac arrest, but their resuscitation was not successful.  Another 15 people believed to be Iranian were taken to the hospital, and two others are believed to be missing at sea.  Arsalan Yarahmadi, editor-in-chief of the website of the Hengaw Human Rights Organization, told BBC Persian that our sources have confirmed that "the drowned were five members of a cold-blooded family".  The Hengaw human rights organization said: "The bodies of four members of the family have been discovered by search teams.  “There is no news of the 15-month-old baby. ”  The search for the missing passengers is expected to resume today, after a nighttime stop.  The BBC's Simon Jones said: "If someone is still on the channel, it's probably not a 'rescue operation' anymore and it's a search operation."  The prosecutor of the French city of Dunkirk has opened an investigation into the cause of the sinking of the ship.  Image source, Reuters explaining the image, the survivors were taken to hospital by the group "Calais Care", calling on the British government to find a legal way for refugees to arrive in the country.  “The loss of life should be a wake-up call for those in power in France and Britain. ”  The organisation said the creation of a new system that would allow asylum seekers to enter the UK from outside its borders would "put an end to the dreaded and dangerous sea crossing and prevent such catastrophes".  British Prime Minister Boris Johnson expressed his condolences to the families of the victims, saying: “We have told France that we will not spare any support to investigate this terrible incident and at the same time we will do all we can to crack down on ruthless criminal groups who are sending vulnerable people on such dangerous journeys. ”  At the same time, Save the Children called for a “joint action plan ” between France and Britain to ensure the safety of families affected.  The English Channel should not be turned into a children ’ s cemetery.  The boat, about two kilometres off the coast of France, was accidentally spotted by a passing sailboat at 9: 30 am local time and the matter was immediately reported to French authorities.  Four French vessels, a Belgian helicopter and a French fishing boat were involved in the search, but when rescue teams arrived, the boat had sunk.

passages.title: 40 refugees, including several Iranians, rescued from the English Channel
passages.passage: British and French officials said they had rescued a total of 40 asylum-seekers, including several children, in separate operations in the English Channel on Tuesday morning.  The migrants were on five boats and, according to British officials, came from three countries: Iraq, Iran and Afghanistan.  Eight of them, including two children, were rescued by the French navy after their boat ’ s engine failed 20 kilometers from Calais.  France has extradited these refugees to Britain.  All of the rescued refugees were handed over to immigration authorities after initial medical treatment.  Children have also been handed over to youth support institutions.  Join Deutsche Welle ’ s Telegram channel. Thousands of refugees have been trying to reach Britain through France in recent years.  Two years ago, French authorities closed a refugee camp in the port of Calais, known as the Jungle.  There were 6,000 refugees in the camp.  Since then, France has been trying to prevent the formation of small refugee camps.  In the past few months, several asylum seekers believed to be Iranian nationals have been rescued by British forces in the English Channel.  In November, about 100 asylum-seekers, most of them Iranian nationals, made their way to Britain ’ s shores via the English Channel.  The English Channel is located in the north of France and the south of England and is one of the busiest British shipping routes.

passages.title: Joint Water Patrol with France: Six More Iranian Refugees Off British Coast
passages.passage: Photo copyright PA Image caption UK water patrols have taken many refugees from the water in recent days amid increasing numbers of migrants trying to reach Britain by water, and the country has agreed with France to further protect the border between the two countries.  A large number of these refugees are Iranian.  Sajid Javid, the British Home Secretary, returned to London in the middle of a family holiday and planned a joint Blue Patrol force with his French counterpart.  It was reported that on Sunday, at the same time as the minister ’ s efforts, six other Iranian men reached the beach near Dover.  The French say they stopped the influx of more refugees on Saturday.  Mr Javid has been accused by his rival party and even his own party of failing to act properly and should have dealt with the matter more harshly.  Javid eventually reached an agreement with French Interior Minister Christophe Castaner to become more active in the coming weeks.  LEWIS MORRIS Image caption Six Iranian men were taken from the water on Sunday The group was found in a boat where the two ministers agreed to deal with human traffickers, and another part involved informing refugees about the dangers of crossing the Channel in small boats.  The British Interior Ministry has given no further explanation in this regard.  More than 220 people have tried to reach the UK by boat in the past two months.  In addition to the Iranians, citizens of Afghanistan and Syria are also among the refugees.  Britain has five lifeboats, only one currently operating.  The other four are in the Mediterranean Sea and are helping with rescue operations there.  It is not known whether the other four boats will return to Britain.  Since 2017, about 2,200 people have taken refuge in the UK every month.  The increase in the number of Iranian refugees, according to the Financial Times, is the result of the worsening economic situation in the country.

passages.title: Hong Kong version of national security law in southern China: Hong Kong people seeking foreign asylum hit a new high in recent years, Australia has risen to 136 cases, and Canada has nearly doubled.
passages.passage: The number of Hong Kong people seeking asylum abroad has reached a new high in recent years, with Australia leading the destination.  According to the South China Morning Post, 136 Hong Kong people sought asylum in Australia in 2020 alone, up nearly 20% from 116 in 2019. The number of Hong Kong people seeking asylum in Canada also rose by nearly 178%.  Emily Lau, chairman of the Democratic Party ’ s International Affairs Committee, said Hong Kong people had to flee to other places to take refuge in fear.  Australia is the most popular place for Hong Kong people to seek asylum, according to South Morning, which asked five countries about the number of Hong Kong people seeking asylum there.  In 2018, the number of asylum applications from Hong Kong people to Australia was only 50, and in 2019, when the anti-amendment movement broke out, the number soared more than 1.3 times to 116. 2020 is still two months away, but this year there have been 136 asylum applications.  Another country with a high number of asylum applications is Canada, where 25 people applied for asylum in 2020, nearly double the nine in 2019 and only two in 2018.  As for the UK, which has just offered a BNO immigration scheme to Hong Kong residents, a total of 14 people applied for asylum in the UK in 2020, up slightly from 13 in 2019.  New Zealand and Germany received three and two applications respectively this year.  Australian and Hong Kong Federation spokesman Dennis Chan said the number of asylum applications had risen sharply at the beginning of the year, but he pointed out that due to the closure of the border in Australia due to Wuhan pneumonia, Australia currently only accepts asylum applications from people who are already there.  Emily Lau: Canada ’ s parliament is considering relaxing visas for Hong Kong residents Emily Lau, chairman of the Democratic Party ’ s International Affairs Committee, said in an inquiry that the increase in the number of Hong Kong people seeking asylum overseas reflected “the social troubles in Hong Kong and the fear of the people ”, which caused people to flee Hong Kong.  She pointed out that Australia had earlier relaxed the work and student visas for Hong Kong people to help Hong Kong people apply for immigration, and the Canadian Parliament is also actively considering the relevant policy.  She revealed that the Democratic Party ’ s International Affairs Committee met with British consular staff this morning, and the other side said that the relevant British immigration program for BNO holders will be accepted at the end of January next year. As long as one person in a family holds a BNO passport, his immediate family is also eligible to participate in the program.  She also reflected to the other party that she hoped that the British side would give the arrested or prosecuted person the opportunity to make a statement, "It is not usually seen today", and quoted the British Consulate's position on the case, "peaceful expression (demonstrators) will be careful to see (applications), not peaceful ones."  She said that seeking political asylum is a different matter, but the British side also said that the Home Office approval is very strict.  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Support Apple in-depth reporting, deep into the community, kick the power, that is, like Apple Special Topics and Investigation Group FB Page!

passages.title: Two minors arrive in Britain alone to seek protection ｜ Apple Daily
passages.passage: With the implementation of the National Security Law in Hong Kong last July, the number of Hong Kong people seeking political asylum in the United Kingdom has soared.  A total of 21 Hong Kong people sought political asylum in the UK from October to December last year, down nearly half from 41 in the previous quarter, but including two “Unaccompanied Asylum Seekers ” (UASC), children or young people who are separated from their parents or caregivers and who come to the UK for asylum on their own.  According to statistics from the Ministry of Home Affairs, in the fourth quarter of 2020, a total of 21 people sought political asylum in the UK, 19 were main applicants, and 2 were family members of the applicants; 8 people applied after arriving at British airports and 13 applied after entering the country.  The applicants are 13 men and 8 women, 3 under the age of 18, 16 between the ages of 18 and 29, and 2 between the ages of 50 and 69.  In the fourth quarter of last year, since 2007, UASC cases have re-emerged for the first time, that is, children or young people who are separated from their parents or caregivers and come to the UK to seek shelter on their own.  The two cases, one man and one woman, were made upon arrival at the British Airport Control Point.  A total of 76 Hong Kong people sought political asylum in the UK in 2020, including 45 men and 31 women, of whom 63 were major applicants.  Asylum seekers were the highest number aged 18 to 29, with 41, followed by 14 aged 30 to 49 and 12 aged under 18.

passages.title: Canada ’ s refugee application backlog is growing, waiting times will double
passages.passage: According to a new report by the federal government ’ s spending watchdog, the number of refugee applications received in Canada is on the rise, and the processing system suffers from long delays and lack of criminal review.  The report, published by The Auditor General of Canada, criticizes Canada ’ s inefficient and outdated refugee claims processing system and predicts a further increase in waiting times for asylum seekers.  In a report released on Tuesday (May 7), Canada ’ s acting Auditor-General Sylvain Ricard wrote that we expect the number of new asylum applications to stabilize at about 50,000 per year. Their waiting time for application results will reach five years in 2024, more than double the current waiting time.  The radio-canada report found a surge in the number of people entering Canada from the United States through informal entry points, but the federal government ’ s processing process has not kept pace.  Radio-canada People who cross the border from the United States, mainly through Roxham Road in Quebec, have crossed into Canada illegally over the past two years.  As of the end of 2018, there were a total of 71,380 refugee applications in Canada "lining up", with the current waiting time of about two years.  Copyright www.rcinet.ca Wechat: radio-canada Security Risks Copyright www.rcinet.ca Wechat: radio-canada Acting Auditor-General also pointed out the security risks during the trial reception process.  Radio-canada reports that the Canadian Border Services Agency (CBSA), Immigration Refugees and Citizenship (IRCC) do not have a quality assurance program to ensure the accuracy and completeness of information.  In a sample check, the Auditor-General found that 0.5% of the applications were processed without completing a biometric check of crime or identity.  The radio-canada report reads that neither CBSA nor IRCC have systems to track whether these applications have completed criminal record checks.  The report concluded that low efficiency, delays in hearings, and the continued use of paper documents by relevant departments to process refugee applications are the reasons for the large backlog of applications. ada CBSA, IRCC and the Canadian Immigration and Refugee Board agreed with the findings and responded that new approaches are being explored to respond to the growing number of refugee applications.  Canada ’ s federal government has announced in this year ’ s budget an additional $1.2 billion over the next five years to strengthen border controls, speed up processing of refugee claims and fast-track deportations of those whose applications have been rejected.  At the same time, the Acting Auditor-General of Canada also criticized the RCMP / GRC ’ s lack of master planning in his report.  Radio-canada reports that not all RCMP officers have equipment to protect themselves in the event of a shooting.  The radio-canada audit report found that the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) received an increase in firearms and hardware protection equipment since 2014, but that the equipment was unevenly distributed, leaving some subdistricts with a lack of equipment and inadequate long-term training for police officers. passages.title: Refugee crisis: France and Britain strengthen border surveillance to stop migrants crossing the Channel
passages.passage: France and the United Kingdom have signed a new agreement to end illegal immigration through the English Channel.  In recent months, with an increasing number of migrants trying to reach the British coast illegally, the English Channel has become one of the most dangerous crossings for asylum seekers.  Since the beginning of the year, seven people, including a family of five, have drowned while crossing the English Channel.  Britain ’ s interior minister, Priti Patel, announced on Saturday that the French and British governments had reached an agreement to combat migrant smuggling and stop illegal immigration through the Channel.  Britain ’ s interior minister and his French counterpart, Gerald Darmann, have signed the agreement, stressing that they intend to make it impossible for asylum seekers to cross the English Channel, which has reached more than 8,000 this year.  Priti Patel said that as part of the agreement, the French government has committed to doubling the number of its coast guard patrols in the area by December 1 to stop migrant boats in the Channel, and to use new equipment such as drones and radar to identify people trying to cross the Channel to reach the British coast.  Britain ’ s interior minister expressed his satisfaction with the signing of the agreement, saying: “This agreement will make it possible for both France and Britain to make it impossible for migrants to cross the Channel. ”  Signing a new 😍 😍 😍 😍 covenant to tackle small boat crossings.  There will be an increase in surveillance with cuttingedge tech introduce greater security at ports Ensure accommodation for migrants in France https: / / t.co / vjG1KiTkep pic.twitter.com / COJ1jncjcjitC — i Patel (@ pritipatel) November 28, 2020 According to AFP, the two countries have agreed to spend 31.4 million euros on the joint project.  In recent months, the number of migrants attempting to cross the English Channel illegally has increased dramatically.  News of the sinking of boats carrying refugees, which killed four people last year and killed seven this year, including a family of five, has made the Channel a dangerous crossroads for migrants and has severely affected public opinion.  Following the incident, the British government accused France of not doing enough to stop refugees from crossing the Channel.  In September, French authorities said they had blocked 1,300 migrants trying to cross the English Channel.  Between January 1 and August 31, some 6,200 asylum seekers, wearing life jackets and using a variety of inflatable boats, paddles and kayaks provided by smugglers, tried to reach the British coast by illegally crossing the English Channel.  On October 27, following the capsizing of the boat carrying refugees, the majority of whom were Iranian nationals, the 35-year-old Rasoul Irannejad, his wife Shiva Mohammad Panahi, two children aged 6 and 9, and their 15-month-old baby, who were from Sardasht and were trying to cross the Channel from France to Britain, drowned and died.  One of the first asylum seekers to drown in the English Channel in 2019 was Mitra, a 31-year-old Iranian girl with a master ’ s degree in psychology who, along with 19 Iranian and Iraqi refugees, including seven children, boarded a boat for the UK on August 9.  Every year, thousands of people from the Middle East and African countries try to reach Britain through the English Channel.  The Channel, which lies between France and Britain, has seen a dramatic increase in small boats carrying refugees to Britain since 1918, in which a number of refugees have been involved in accidents and some have died. passages.title: And how many of them are in the kingdom?
passages.passage: Photo copyright Lewis Morris Image caption In recent weeks, groups of asylum seekers have taken small boats off the coast of the UK, according to BBC News, 230 people have tried to reach the UK in small boats crossing the English Channel since the beginning of November.  British Interior Minister Sajid Javid called the incident a "serious incident."  He says that while the UK has commitments to help and support genuine refugees, it is not willing or willing to allow reckless criminals to reap the benefits that belong to the most vulnerable people in the international community.  But how many people have actually applied for asylum by sea in recent weeks?  The British Interior Ministry declined to provide detailed information.  But if all of them have applied for asylum, they would still be equal to the number of people who apply for asylum in the UK every three days on average.  How many asylum seekers are there?  In 2017, 26,350 asylum applications were filed in the UK.  In comparison to other European countries in the same period, 198,255 asylum applications were filed in Germany, 126,550 in Italy and 91,70 in France.  Of these, 21,290 cases have been decided, with 31.8% receiving some form of support.  The UK offers asylum to people who fear being prosecuted in their home country because of their race, religion, nationality, political opinions and factors such as sexual orientation and are unable to live in their home country.  If the asylum application is accepted, people will be allowed to live and work in the UK for five years, after which they will be able to apply for permanent residence.  Not much is known about how the asylum seekers made their way to the UK, but a report from the Home Office ’ s Migration Advisory Committee released in May 2018 estimated that they were “sneaking in ”.  This includes people arriving either by boat to the British coast or being smuggled onto ships or trucks.  Between 2016-2017, the number of these people was 2,366, with the number reduced to 1,832 in 2017-2018.  The Ministry of Interior ’ s report did not say the proportion of these people who applied for asylum.  Which countries are asylum seekers from?  Last year, Iranians were the largest group of asylum seekers in Britain.  In recent days, it has been reported that most of the people who crossed the Channel are Iranians.  Of the 2,690 Iranian asylum seekers, 47 percent received asylum in the first stage of the decision.  These statistics show that the success of Iranian asylum applications is higher than the average number of asylum seekers, or that Iranian asylum seekers have a higher chance of being accepted than other nationalities.  These statistics relate to cases in which a final decision has been made.  Others are in a “wait or wait ” situation.  At the end of last year, 24,557 people were waiting for the outcome of their asylum application, 42 percent of whom had been waiting more than six months.  Rejected asylum applications are usually admissible in court, and people who are rejected often appeal.  Of the 14,149 appeals filed in 2017, 5,222, a third of the appeals court cases, resulted in a breach of the Migration and Asylum Service ’ s initial decision.
