Title: SpaceX successfully sent two astronauts into space as part of the Demo-2 mission » DailyTechInfo
Content: On May 30, 2020, at 19: 22 GMT, the famous American space company SpaceX successfully launched a manned mission Demo-2.  The Crew Dragon spacecraft, which now holds two astronauts, Robert Behnken and Douglas Hurley, was launched into space by a Falcon 9 rocket launched from Launch Complex 39A at NASA ’ s Kennedy Space Center in Florida.  The spacecraft is currently in space, performing maneuvers that will lead it to the International Space Station (ISS), docking with which will be made during today, May 31, 2020.Yesterday's launch was made after the first attempt, scheduled for Wednesday last week, was postponed due to the approach of the storm front, carrying strong wind, rain and an increased risk of lightning strike. passages.title: Ontario court: Iran ’ s shooting down of Ukrainian plane was ‘ intentional ’ and ‘ terrorist ’
passages.passage: One year and four months after the Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) shot down Ukraine International Airlines Flight 752, Ontario ’ s Supreme Court on Thursday, May 20, called the shooting down of Ukrainian aircraft by Iran an “intentional ” and a“ terrorist ” act.  Ontario Supreme Court Justice Edward Billubaba announced in a ruling Thursday, May 20, that the downing of the Ukrainian plane PS752 over Tehran was "deliberate" and "terrorist".  The Ontario Supreme Court ruled that “the plaintiffs in this case have proved that the downing of Flight 752 by Iran was a deliberate act of terrorism. ”  In his ruling, he also condemned the Iranian government to pay compensation to the families of the victims of the Ukrainian plane that was shot down by the Islamic Republic ’ s Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) defense over Tehran.  The Supreme Court of Ontario of Canada has issued a ruling in the case of four relatives of the passengers of the Ukrainian plane who are officials of the Islamic Republic of Iran.  Shahin Moghadam, Shakiba Faghaati ’ s wife and Rustin Moghadam ’ s father, Mehrzad Zarei, Arad Zarei ’ s father, Ali Gorji ’ s uncle, and another member of the families of the victims, who did not want to be named, are four plaintiffs in the case.  In their complaint to the Ontario Supreme Court, they named Ali Khamenei, the Supreme Leader of the Islamic Republic of Iran, and several top Revolutionary Guard commanders.  In a statement, the four lawyers, Mark and Jonah Arnold, described the Supreme Court ruling as “unprecedented. ”  They stressed that the sentence would have "a significant impact on the relatives of the victims who seek justice."  According to the two lawyers, four plaintiffs in the case have asked Iran for 1 million euros in compensation.  Ukraine International Airlines Flight PS752 was shot down on January 8, 2021 after two IRGC missiles were fired over Tehran.  All 176 people on board, dual Iranian-Canadian citizens as well as citizens of Afghanistan, Britain, Germany, Sweden and Ukraine, were killed in the crash.  The crash of Ukraine Airlines Flight 752 occurred just four hours before Iran attacked U.S. military bases in response to the killing of former Quds commander Qasem Soleimani in Iraq.  Canadian broadcaster CBC reported on Saturday, July 4, that it had obtained a 90-minute audio file.  According to the network, Tehran ’ s sky was open at the time of the shooting down of the Ukrainian plane so that the plan of the IRGC ’ s attack on US military bases in Iraq would not be revealed.  The Iranian authorities, after publishing evidence and documents by Canada, the United States, Australia and the United Kingdom, finally declared "human error" after three days of concealment.  One year and four months after the downing of Ukraine International Airlines Flight PS752 by the Islamic Republic of Iran ’ s Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), the families of the victims refuse to accept the claims of the Iranian authorities and call for the identification and prosecution of the perpetrators. passages.title: Iran does not recognize the decisions of the Canadian court in the case of the downed Ukrainian plane
passages.passage: Iran said on Friday, May 21 that a Canadian court has no jurisdiction to hear a claim for damages in the crash of a Ukrainian passenger plane shot down by Islamic Revolutionary Guards last year.  The Supreme Court of the Canadian province of Ontario ruled on Thursday that Iran should compensate families who sued for the plane crash that killed 176 people, 138 of whom were Canadian citizens. The Iranian government said the plane crash in January 2020, shortly after its take-off in Tehran, was a "catastrophic mistake" by forces that were on high alert during a tense confrontation with the United States.  Foreign states usually do not fall under the jurisdiction of Canadian courts, but Canadian law since 2012 has changed this for countries classified as "foreign states supporting terrorism." passages.passage: Ontario Court: The shooting of Ukrainian aircraft by Iran was' intentional and terrorist 'May 30, 1400 - May 20, 2021, 20: 18 GMT Updated 4 minutes ago Picture description, memorial to the victims - 176 Sereneges were killed Flight 752 The Ontario Supreme Court in Canada has concluded that the shooting of Ukrainian flight PS752 by Iran was a deliberate act and based on criminal law of terrorist act.  Ukraine International Airlines Flight 752 was hit by two Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps missiles in January 2020, killing 176 people.  Judge Edward Blubaba wrote in a decision issued Thursday: "By weighing the possibilities, I found that the missile attacks on Flight 752 were deliberate and directly responsible for the deaths of all those on board."  "I also realized, weighing the possibilities, that there was no armed conflict in the region at the time."  The judge said the plaintiffs had proven that the downing of the plane was based on state immunity laws, justice for victims of terrorist acts and criminal law as "terrorist activity."  Former Canadian Foreign Minister Francois Philippe Champagne said in December that he did not believe the flight was caused by human error.  The plaintiffs' lawyer said in a statement that another hearing would be held in the court to determine compensation.  Mark Arnold has previously said that the best way to get compensation for the families of the victims is to accuse the Iranian government of “committing a terrorist act. ”  He is the legal representative of the plaintiffs who lost their relatives on that flight.  Despite being informed of the charge, the Iranian government has refused to defend itself in this court.  Mark and Jonah Arnold, lawyers for the case, wrote: “The decision of the Supreme Court of Justice in Canada is unprecedented.  "This is a significant ruling in terms of the immediate impact on the families of victims seeking justice."  Habib Haghjoo, whose daughter Shahnaz Haghjoo and eight-year-old grandson Elsa lost a new one on flight 752, said it was a success for the families making the complaint.  He said: “I ’ m very happy and I think it ’ s a big step.  Canadian Foreign Minister Mark Garneau told parliament last week that Canada would soon negotiate compensation for the families of the victims.  The association representing the families of the victims has repeatedly said it wants answers and justice for the overthrow before any talks about reparations.  More than a year after the shooting down of the plane, there are still serious uncertainties about the causes of the shooting down and those involved in the “unconscionable, ” Mr. Garno told a parliamentary committee on Thursday:“ I must honestly say that the behavior of the Iranian government over the past 15 months has been unconscionable and we will not let them go to ensure accountability. ”  After months of pressure, Tehran has just agreed to hand over flight data recorders for independent analysis, he said, adding that Iran has not yet explained why it did not close its skies on the night of the incident.  Flight 752 was hit by two IRGC missiles on January 8, 2020.  Ukraine and four other countries where citizens or residents were killed - including Canada, Britain, Afghanistan and Sweden - have called on Iran to provide a full and comprehensive explanation of the downing of the plane.  The Iranian armed forces denied any responsibility within three days of the overthrow.  Authorities also allowed the occupants ’ assets scattered at the crash site to be looted and then bulldozed.  But accumulating evidence from the IRGC Aerospace Force, he said that an anti-aircraft unit mistook the Boeing 737-800 for a missile.  On that day, Iran ’ s air defenses were on high alert because of the IRGC ’ s action in firing missiles at two Iraqi bases where U.S. forces were stationed. The Civil Aviation Organization recently reported in March 2021 that an anti-aircraft defense operator of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) had “mistakenly ” identified the aircraft as hostile and fired the missiles without the permission of the commanders.  According to Iran ’ s Civil Aviation Organization, the downing of the plane was due to a “chain of human errors ” that occurred on the day of the disaster.  Ukraine and Canada rejected the report. Our statement notes that our states, their citizens and residents on board flight PS752 suffered substantial and irreparable damage as a result of the tragedy, and Iran must fulfill its obligations to ensure full reparation to the group of states. At the same time, Tokyo said that the country intends to remain in the ranks of the commission as an observer.  Japan stopped commercial whaling in accordance with an international moratorium in 1982.  Subsequently, the fishery was partially resumed; in Tokyo, the decision was motivated by the need to study migration routes, diet and other factors related to marine mammals.  At the same time, the meat of the killed animals is sold to Japanese restaurants and supermarkets, which gives grounds for opponents of the fishery to doubt the nature of this activity. passages.title: Animal Husbandry in the World + Pictures
passages.passage: They send a boat to find whales and dolphins in front of them.  After finding a flock of animals, other boats make terrible noises and sound walls as they move.  Frightened whales and dolphins swim to the bay, after the animals are exhausted, spears are thrust into their bodies, and the entire sea turns red.  Images of the sea of blood and the slaughter of animals have been repeatedly published in the media.  Japan is one of the countries that, as a tradition, kill large numbers of whales and dolphins.  Although environmental groups have repeatedly protested the move, the country withdrew from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) last year and resumed whaling.  Japan has been whaling for centuries, and its meat has been used as a key source of protein in the post-World War II years when the country was in extreme poverty.  Japanese fishermen also killed more than 300 large finned whales in the Antarctic Ocean last year, including 122 pregnant whales.  The country says it hunts for scientific research, while critics argue that killing whales is for commercial use and Japan sells and uses them for food.  In 2014, the International Court of Justice ruled that Japan ’ s Antarctic whaling program was not for scientific and research purposes and therefore had to be stopped.  However, Japanese authorities claim that the scale of whaling off beaches for commercial purposes is very small compared to whaling in the northern ocean for scientific purposes.  Apart from Japan, many other countries offer different animal sacrifices each year.  The killing of cows after bullfights in Spain, animal sacrifices in Haiti, the killing of whales in Denmark, and the killing of cows and sheep in Nepal and Africa are still held around the world, and in some cases, people are injured or killed.  Photographs published by Alistair Ward, a 22-year-old student at the University of Cambridge, of whaling in Sandavago Bay have received a lot of media attention.  People from the Faroe Islands in Denmark kill whales every year, and this tradition has been going on for centuries.  The Faroe Islands lie in northern Europe between the Norwegian Sea and the North Atlantic Ocean and are made up of 18 small islands.  Whale meat and tallow are a source of food for the nearly 59,000 islanders who are said to be spending the winter there.  The hunters at this ceremony guide the whales to the bay with their oars, and when they get close enough, the killing begins.  Even children participate in the ceremony.  Residents of the area consider whaling a collective activity that everyone can participate in.  They say this is done under national regulations and laws, so that the whales suffer the least amount of pain and suffering.  Many Faroe Islanders believe whaling is not incompatible with the ecosystem, and they hunt 800 pilot whales each year out of the 100,000 whales that surround the island.  Images of this massacre on social media caused a lot of reactions, and some of them, in response to the reaction of European animal rights defenders to the slaughter of animals in East Asia and Africa, wrote sarcastically: “Because Europeans are blond and white, the name of this work is not barbarism and the supply of meat, but the religious slaughter of Muslims is barbaric! ”  The Gadhimai Festival is another event in which thousands of cows and sheep are sacrificed.  The ceremony takes place every five years over two days in Nepal and is inspired by a Hindu religion in the village of Baryapur, which believes that sacrificing to the goddess Gadhimai will capture the devil and bring them happiness.  What animal rights advocates have been protesting at the festival is an unusual form of victimization.  In this place, the cattle are gathered in a field, and they are slashed from the back of the neck.  Animal rights advocates call it the largest animal slaughterhouse in the world because of its remarkable violence.  In addition to the whaling, the Gadhimai festival in Japan has another 3,500-year-old ceremony that takes place in Taiji.  This event is known for the hunt of dolphins by the people of the world.  The people of this city have long been engaged in fishing and whale or dolphin hunting.  Despite opposition, Taijis continue to do so for their food, claiming it has long been a source of livelihood and a part of their cultural identity.  Taiji ’ s history shows the existence of 400-year-old whaling weapons.  The World Health Organization (WHO) studied dolphin meat and declared the amount of toxins and mercury in the meat to be very high, warning people that high levels of mercury in dolphin meat cause diseases such as cancer, infertility and suppression of the immune system.  However, traditional Taiji fishermen continue to slaughter the animal, and its products can be seen in the city ’ s stores.  The people of Taiji send a boat out to hunt for the dolphins in the first place.  After finding a flock of dolphins, the other boats are arranged in the shape of an English letter V, making terrifying sounds and sound walls as they move.  Scared dolphins swim to the bay.  Then other boats chase them to throw their frightened dolphins ashore and crash into the rocks.  After the dolphins are exhausted, the spears are thrust into the bodies of these animals and the entire sea turns red.  Among the wounded dolphins, the more beautiful ones are hunted for aquariums and circuses.  In Taiji, Haiti, there is also a ceremony in which animals are killed.  Voodoo believers gather in the country in April and declare their obedience to their gods by sacrificing animals, dancing and playing music.  After the sacrifice, they pour the warm blood of the animal into a container and drink it.  Those present in the ceremony, dressed in white, shed some of this blood on themselves, and while believing that they are under the control of the spirits, they jump into the water and continue to worship.  Wearing white clothes with blood symbolizes adherence to voodoo.  Followers of the cult have combined drum dancing as an African tradition with traditional elements of the Catholic religion.  Millions of Haitians believe in voodoo, and the government adopted it as an official religion in 1960.  But in 2012, the Haitian Senate and House of Representatives decried Voodoo as the official religion with a constitutional amendment approved by their president, a move that caused widespread discontent among Haitian followers.  In Spain, bullfighting is also one of the most popular entertainment in the world.  San Fermin in Spain attracts many tourists every year.  The celebration of the release and running of angry cows among the crowd through the narrow alleys lasts a few minutes, but the celebration lasts for hours.  Cows enter the stadium after passing through the city center to witness the matador battle with the bulls.  In the past, due to the narrow streets and the lack of possibility of passing the cart, ranchers had to drive the cows on a short path to the stadium.  Over time, young people started running in front of the cows to show their courage.  Those who run in front of cows traditionally wear white shirts and trousers and a red necktie around their necks.  Every year, the ceremony leaves a number of injured and even killed.  At the end of the festivities in Spain, bullfighters circle the animals and kill them with decorated spears and knives.  Due to opposition to the ceremony, bullfighting festivals were banned in some Spanish cities, including the Canary Islands.  It is not only in rituals that animals are abused and slaughtered, but also in pictures and videos of the slaughter of pregnant cows in France, sheep in Australian slaughterhouses, the killing of goats in Thailand, the slaughter of camels in Mauritania, and the cooking of live pigs in Europe. Japan has started hunting whales again due to several reasons. 


The Japanese government has stated that eating whale meat is Japan's traditional food culture [ca4ad247-415d-4236-ab9e-cd141b7aecfe]. 

This cultural tradition has been passed down for generations, and many Japanese people consider whale meat a delicacy [56413e55-0f89-45e1-94f9-7626dd17cbe2]. 

In fact, whale meat has been a part of Japan's cuisine since the post-World War II era when the country was in extreme poverty, and whale meat became a key source of protein [14366427-1989-44bf-b090-2a60f2e838fa]. 

Today, whale meat is still consumed in Japan, and its price is relatively affordable, with a kilogram of whale meat costing around 1,600 yen (about HK $110) per kilogram [56413e55-0f89-45e1-94f9-7626dd17cbe2]. 


Another reason for Japan's decision to resume commercial whaling is the potential economic benefits [5d5792ec-8053-43ad-948c-2ca1de7d4ea8]. 

The whaling industry has the potential to revitalize the local economy, particularly in areas that were once dependent on whaling [56413e55-0f89-45e1-94f9-7626dd17cbe2]. 

For example, the Amikawa area in Miyagi Prefecture, which was once a major whaling port, hopes to revive its economy by restarting whale hunting [56413e55-0f89-45e1-94f9-7626dd17cbe2]. 

Additionally, the Japanese government believes that the resumption of commercial whaling can lead to a revival of the local economy [ca4ad247-415d-4236-ab9e-cd141b7aecfe]. 


Japan has also stated that the global whale population has recovered, and some commercial whaling can be resumed [0e44f38c-fffb-4550-b294-3de9d5e310f8]. 

This decision was made after the Japanese government announced that the population of some whale species has recovered, allowing for the resumption of commercial whaling [527be2e4-188c-4b13-8679-3e24183d08a8]. 

However, environmental groups have criticized this decision, arguing that it is a "chicken and egg" circular argument [0e44f38c-fffb-4550-b294-3de9d5e310f8]. 


Furthermore, Japan's decision to resume commercial whaling is also driven by domestic political considerations [5d5792ec-8053-43ad-948c-2ca1de7d4ea8]. 

Prime Minister Shinzo Abe, who was born in Yamaguchi Prefecture, a whaling prefecture, has been accused of promoting the resumption of whale hunting to gain the support of local residents [5d5792ec-8053-43ad-948c-2ca1de7d4ea8]. 

In fact, many politicians in Japan have close ties to the whaling industry, and some have even been accused of prioritizing the interests of the whaling industry over conservation efforts [5d5792ec-8053-43ad-948c-2ca1de7d4ea8]. 


Additionally, Japan's decision to withdraw from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) and resume commercial whaling is also seen as a response to the "retreat" wave set off by the United States [5d5792ec-8053-43ad-948c-2ca1de7d4ea8]. 

Japan believes that this is the best time to withdraw from the IWC, given the current international environment, which is characterized by anti-globalization and a rise in protectionism [5d5792ec-8053-43ad-948c-2ca1de7d4ea8]. 


It is worth noting that Japan's decision to resume commercial whaling has been met with international criticism and condemnation [ca4ad247-415d-4236-ab9e-cd141b7aecfe]. 

Many countries, including Australia and Brazil, have strongly opposed Japan's decision to resume commercial whaling [527be2e4-188c-4b13-8679-3e24183d08a8]. 

However, Japan has stated that it will only hunt whales in its territorial waters and exclusive economic zone [55f03ae7-157e-4e63-a0df-4d6d9cb8de74].

Title: Japan's' dolphin killing festival 'in long-running dispute over resumption of commercial whaling
Content: Image copyright AFP Image caption For half a year starting on September 1, a large-scale dolphin killing event is held in Taiji, a fishing village in Wakayama, southern Japan, and is internationally criticized.  Japan has started its controversial annual dolphin hunt in the coastal town of Taiji.  Japan recently resumed commercial whaling in defiance of international criticism.  In 2010, a documentary, Dolphin Bay, won the Oscar for Best Documentary, drawing global attention to the mass killing of dolphins in Japan.  After the bloody documentary, the decades-old tradition in Taiji, Japan, sparked criticism from nature and animal conservationists around the world.  Dolphins are not fish, they are aquatic mammals, and they are cetaceans.  Dolphins are one of the most intelligent animals, with a friendly appearance and a playful personality, has always been very popular in human culture.  But Japan's dolphin festival is their nightmare.  Dolphin killing festival and Dolphin Bay The dolphin festival is held every six months from September 1 in the fishing village of Taiji in Wakayama, southern Japan.  Hunters drove the animals into a bay and then slaughtered most of the trapped dolphins with knives and harpoons in shallow waters.  The slain dolphin meat was used for consumption.  The remaining dolphins were sold to aquariums and marine parks.  In the past, the media reported that in the next six months, more than 20,000 dolphins and thousands of whales will be slaughtered in Taiji Bay, and the blood of the dolphins will almost dye the sea water in the Bay.  In 2009, European and American marine conservationists broke through the Japanese blockade and secretly filmed a documentary "Dolphin Bay", which won the Oscar for Best Documentary the following year.  The film, which shows fishermen brutally killing dolphins and selling dolphin meat in Taiji Town, has caused international public pressure and controversy in the area.  Image copyright AFP Image caption There has been much international opposition and condemnation of Japan's commercial whaling.  Environmentalists: Hunting is very cruel as the annual Dolphin Festival in 2019 begins, and it has become a focus of media and animal protection organizations. The official total quota for the season allows for the killing or capture of more than 1,700 dolphins or whales.  Conservationists say the chase is so brutal that it can take up to 30 minutes for dolphins to die from asphyxiation or drowning. With the encouragement of General MacArthur of the United States, Japan converted two huge U.S. Navy ships into whaling processing ships to go to the Southern Ocean, playing an important role in solving Japan's acute food shortage. Title: Animal Husbandry in the World + Pictures
Content: They send a boat to find whales and dolphins in front of them.  After finding a flock of animals, other boats make terrible noises and sound walls as they move.  Frightened whales and dolphins swim to the bay, after the animals are exhausted, spears are thrust into their bodies, and the entire sea turns red.  Images of the sea of blood and the slaughter of animals have been repeatedly published in the media.  Japan is one of the countries that, as a tradition, kill large numbers of whales and dolphins.  Although environmental groups have repeatedly protested the move, the country withdrew from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) last year and resumed whaling.  Japan has been whaling for centuries, and its meat has been used as a key source of protein in the post-World War II years when the country was in extreme poverty.  Japanese fishermen also killed more than 300 large finned whales in the Antarctic Ocean last year, including 122 pregnant whales.  The country says it hunts for scientific research, while critics argue that killing whales is for commercial use and Japan sells and uses them for food.  In 2014, the International Court of Justice ruled that Japan ’ s Antarctic whaling program was not for scientific and research purposes and therefore had to be stopped.  However, Japanese authorities claim that the scale of whaling off beaches for commercial purposes is very small compared to whaling in the northern ocean for scientific purposes.  Apart from Japan, many other countries offer different animal sacrifices each year.  The killing of cows after bullfights in Spain, animal sacrifices in Haiti, the killing of whales in Denmark, and the killing of cows and sheep in Nepal and Africa are still held around the world, and in some cases, people are injured or killed.  Photographs published by Alistair Ward, a 22-year-old student at the University of Cambridge, of whaling in Sandavago Bay have received a lot of media attention.  People from the Faroe Islands in Denmark kill whales every year, and this tradition has been going on for centuries.  The Faroe Islands lie in northern Europe between the Norwegian Sea and the North Atlantic Ocean and are made up of 18 small islands.  Whale meat and tallow are a source of food for the nearly 59,000 islanders who are said to be spending the winter there.  The hunters at this ceremony guide the whales to the bay with their oars, and when they get close enough, the killing begins.  Even children participate in the ceremony.  Residents of the area consider whaling a collective activity that everyone can participate in.  They say this is done under national regulations and laws, so that the whales suffer the least amount of pain and suffering.  Many Faroe Islanders believe whaling is not incompatible with the ecosystem, and they hunt 800 pilot whales each year out of the 100,000 whales that surround the island.  Images of this massacre on social media caused a lot of reactions, and some of them, in response to the reaction of European animal rights defenders to the slaughter of animals in East Asia and Africa, wrote sarcastically: “Because Europeans are blond and white, the name of this work is not barbarism and the supply of meat, but the religious slaughter of Muslims is barbaric! ”  The Gadhimai Festival is another event in which thousands of cows and sheep are sacrificed.  The ceremony takes place every five years over two days in Nepal and is inspired by a Hindu religion in the village of Baryapur, which believes that sacrificing to the goddess Gadhimai will capture the devil and bring them happiness.  What animal rights advocates have been protesting at the festival is an unusual form of victimization.  In this place, the cattle are gathered in a field, and they are slashed from the back of the neck.  Animal rights advocates call it the largest animal slaughterhouse in the world because of its remarkable violence.  In addition to the whaling, the Gadhimai festival in Japan has another 3,500-year-old ceremony that takes place in Taiji.  This event is known for the hunt of dolphins by the people of the world.  The people of this city have long been engaged in fishing and whale or dolphin hunting.  Despite opposition, Taijis continue to do so for their food, claiming it has long been a source of livelihood and a part of their cultural identity.  Taiji ’ s history shows the existence of 400-year-old whaling weapons.  The World Health Organization (WHO) studied dolphin meat and declared the amount of toxins and mercury in the meat to be very high, warning people that high levels of mercury in dolphin meat cause diseases such as cancer, infertility and suppression of the immune system.  However, traditional Taiji fishermen continue to slaughter the animal, and its products can be seen in the city ’ s stores.  The people of Taiji send a boat out to hunt for the dolphins in the first place.  After finding a flock of dolphins, the other boats are arranged in the shape of an English letter V, making terrifying sounds and sound walls as they move.  Scared dolphins swim to the bay.  Then other boats chase them to throw their frightened dolphins ashore and crash into the rocks.  After the dolphins are exhausted, the spears are thrust into the bodies of these animals and the entire sea turns red.  Among the wounded dolphins, the more beautiful ones are hunted for aquariums and circuses.  In Taiji, Haiti, there is also a ceremony in which animals are killed.  Voodoo believers gather in the country in April and declare their obedience to their gods by sacrificing animals, dancing and playing music.  After the sacrifice, they pour the warm blood of the animal into a container and drink it.  Those present in the ceremony, dressed in white, shed some of this blood on themselves, and while believing that they are under the control of the spirits, they jump into the water and continue to worship.  Wearing white clothes with blood symbolizes adherence to voodoo.  Followers of the cult have combined drum dancing as an African tradition with traditional elements of the Catholic religion.  Millions of Haitians believe in voodoo, and the government adopted it as an official religion in 1960.  But in 2012, the Haitian Senate and House of Representatives decried Voodoo as the official religion with a constitutional amendment approved by their president, a move that caused widespread discontent among Haitian followers.  In Spain, bullfighting is also one of the most popular entertainment in the world.  San Fermin in Spain attracts many tourists every year.  The celebration of the release and running of angry cows among the crowd through the narrow alleys lasts a few minutes, but the celebration lasts for hours.  Cows enter the stadium after passing through the city center to witness the matador battle with the bulls.  In the past, due to the narrow streets and the lack of possibility of passing the cart, ranchers had to drive the cows on a short path to the stadium.  Over time, young people started running in front of the cows to show their courage.  Those who run in front of cows traditionally wear white shirts and trousers and a red necktie around their necks.  Every year, the ceremony leaves a number of injured and even killed.  At the end of the festivities in Spain, bullfighters circle the animals and kill them with decorated spears and knives. After World War II, Japan ’ s whaling industry soared due to food shortages and foreign exchange earnings. In 1982, the IWC passed the Convention on the Prohibition of Commercial Whaling. However, commercial whaling does not mean that whaling will no longer be done. After extensive damage during the Great East Japan Earthquake, residents hope to revive the local economy by reviving the whaling industry. Whale meat sashimi, but in fact, the price of whale meat is not particularly expensive due to the low supply and demand. (Reuters) Possible political reasons behind this.  Including Prime Minister Shinzo Abe, the constituency of the former president of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party ’ s faction, the “Chi Shih Association ”, is a land of whaling. However, whether it is for cultural, industrial or political reasons, the low supply and demand of whale meat and the low price of whale meat can not be ignored, and Japan will face condemnation from international environmental groups.

At the same time, Tokyo said that the country intends to remain in the ranks of the commission as an observer. Title: Animal Husbandry in the World + Pictures
Content: They send a boat to find whales and dolphins in front of them.  After finding a flock of animals, other boats make terrible noises and sound walls as they move.  Frightened whales and dolphins swim to the bay, after the animals are exhausted, spears are thrust into their bodies, and the entire sea turns red.  Images of the sea of blood and the slaughter of animals have been repeatedly published in the media.  Japan is one of the countries that, as a tradition, kill large numbers of whales and dolphins.  Although environmental groups have repeatedly protested the move, the country withdrew from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) last year and resumed whaling.  Japan has been whaling for centuries, and its meat has been used as a key source of protein in the post-World War II years when the country was in extreme poverty.  Japanese fishermen also killed more than 300 large finned whales in the Antarctic Ocean last year, including 122 pregnant whales.  The country says it hunts for scientific research, while critics argue that killing whales is for commercial use and Japan sells and uses them for food.  In 2014, the International Court of Justice ruled that Japan ’ s Antarctic whaling program was not for scientific and research purposes and therefore had to be stopped.  However, Japanese authorities claim that the scale of whaling off beaches for commercial purposes is very small compared to whaling in the northern ocean for scientific purposes.  Apart from Japan, many other countries offer different animal sacrifices each year.  The killing of cows after bullfights in Spain, animal sacrifices in Haiti, the killing of whales in Denmark, and the killing of cows and sheep in Nepal and Africa are still held around the world, and in some cases, people are injured or killed.  Photographs published by Alistair Ward, a 22-year-old student at the University of Cambridge, of whaling in Sandavago Bay have received a lot of media attention.  People from the Faroe Islands in Denmark kill whales every year, and this tradition has been going on for centuries.  The Faroe Islands lie in northern Europe between the Norwegian Sea and the North Atlantic Ocean and are made up of 18 small islands.  Whale meat and tallow are a source of food for the nearly 59,000 islanders who are said to be spending the winter there.  The hunters at this ceremony guide the whales to the bay with their oars, and when they get close enough, the killing begins.  Even children participate in the ceremony.  Residents of the area consider whaling a collective activity that everyone can participate in.  They say this is done under national regulations and laws, so that the whales suffer the least amount of pain and suffering.  Many Faroe Islanders believe whaling is not incompatible with the ecosystem, and they hunt 800 pilot whales each year out of the 100,000 whales that surround the island.  Images of this massacre on social media caused a lot of reactions, and some of them, in response to the reaction of European animal rights defenders to the slaughter of animals in East Asia and Africa, wrote sarcastically: “Because Europeans are blond and white, the name of this work is not barbarism and the supply of meat, but the religious slaughter of Muslims is barbaric! ”  The Gadhimai Festival is another event in which thousands of cows and sheep are sacrificed.  The ceremony takes place every five years over two days in Nepal and is inspired by a Hindu religion in the village of Baryapur, which believes that sacrificing to the goddess Gadhimai will capture the devil and bring them happiness.  What animal rights advocates have been protesting at the festival is an unusual form of victimization.  In this place, the cattle are gathered in a field, and they are slashed from the back of the neck.  Animal rights advocates call it the largest animal slaughterhouse in the world because of its remarkable violence.  In addition to the whaling, the Gadhimai festival in Japan has another 3,500-year-old ceremony that takes place in Taiji.  This event is known for the hunt of dolphins by the people of the world.  The people of this city have long been engaged in fishing and whale or dolphin hunting.  Despite opposition, Taijis continue to do so for their food, claiming it has long been a source of livelihood and a part of their cultural identity.  Taiji ’ s history shows the existence of 400-year-old whaling weapons.  The World Health Organization (WHO) studied dolphin meat and declared the amount of toxins and mercury in the meat to be very high, warning people that high levels of mercury in dolphin meat cause diseases such as cancer, infertility and suppression of the immune system.  However, traditional Taiji fishermen continue to slaughter the animal, and its products can be seen in the city ’ s stores.  The people of Taiji send a boat out to hunt for the dolphins in the first place.  After finding a flock of dolphins, the other boats are arranged in the shape of an English letter V, making terrifying sounds and sound walls as they move.  Scared dolphins swim to the bay.  Then other boats chase them to throw their frightened dolphins ashore and crash into the rocks.  After the dolphins are exhausted, the spears are thrust into the bodies of these animals and the entire sea turns red.  Among the wounded dolphins, the more beautiful ones are hunted for aquariums and circuses.  In Taiji, Haiti, there is also a ceremony in which animals are killed.  Voodoo believers gather in the country in April and declare their obedience to their gods by sacrificing animals, dancing and playing music.  After the sacrifice, they pour the warm blood of the animal into a container and drink it.  Those present in the ceremony, dressed in white, shed some of this blood on themselves, and while believing that they are under the control of the spirits, they jump into the water and continue to worship.  Wearing white clothes with blood symbolizes adherence to voodoo.  Followers of the cult have combined drum dancing as an African tradition with traditional elements of the Catholic religion.  Millions of Haitians believe in voodoo, and the government adopted it as an official religion in 1960.  But in 2012, the Haitian Senate and House of Representatives decried Voodoo as the official religion with a constitutional amendment approved by their president, a move that caused widespread discontent among Haitian followers.  In Spain, bullfighting is also one of the most popular entertainment in the world.  San Fermin in Spain attracts many tourists every year.  The celebration of the release and running of angry cows among the crowd through the narrow alleys lasts a few minutes, but the celebration lasts for hours.  Cows enter the stadium after passing through the city center to witness the matador battle with the bulls.  In the past, due to the narrow streets and the lack of possibility of passing the cart, ranchers had to drive the cows on a short path to the stadium.  Over time, young people started running in front of the cows to show their courage.  Those who run in front of cows traditionally wear white shirts and trousers and a red necktie around their necks.  Every year, the ceremony leaves a number of injured and even killed.  At the end of the festivities in Spain, bullfighters circle the animals and kill them with decorated spears and knives.  Due to opposition to the ceremony, bullfighting festivals were banned in some Spanish cities, including the Canary Islands.  It is not only in rituals that animals are abused and slaughtered, but also in pictures and videos of the slaughter of pregnant cows in France, sheep in Australian slaughterhouses, the killing of goats in Thailand, the slaughter of camels in Mauritania, and the cooking of live pigs in Europe. passages.passage: Rose Aitmatova is destined to always remain the younger sister of the famous writer with a world name.  But she ’ s not just proud of her family name.  Roza Torekulovna, despite her solid age (March 8, she turned 80 years old), continues to work hard to preserve the literary heritage of Chingiz Aitmatov.  She is also active in protecting the rights of Kyrgyz women.  Today, Roza Aitmatova is a guest of our traditional top-5 category and presents her favorite books.  The story "White steamer" Chingiz Aitmatov.  In the story Chingiz Torekulovich raised the eternal theme of good and evil.  It is a message to humanity: do good in this world.  In addition, I think the work forms in a person a sense of humane and careful attitude to nature.  Another important aspect that Chingiz Torekulovich reveals to us is the preservation of the value of the family.  Children should not be left orphans with living parents.  Rose Aitmatova is wise, isn't it?  “Grandfather says that if people don ’ t remember their fathers, they will go bad.  Grandfather says that then no one will be ashamed of bad deeds, because children and children of children will not remember them.  And no one will do good things, because the children will not know about it anyway, ” the book says.  I think that this story and now, in the age of globalization, more than ever should be in demand for the younger generation.  We must not forget our roots and national traditions.  This, as you know, leads to the decline of culture.  Turning to metaphors through the legend of the horned Mother of the Deer, Chingiz Torekulovich reminds us of how important the spiritual connection of generations is for our people.  Rose Aitmatova The problem of good and evil is the basis of fairy tales and legends.  But if in fairy tales good almost always triumphs, and evil is punished, then in reality this is not always the case.  I think the story "White steamer" is also interesting because it simultaneously coexists modern life and ancient legend, and the problem of good and evil is solved differently from the usual outcome. It was difficult for the Kyrgyz historical path to independence.  “Broken Sword ”, telling us about the turbulent and complex historical events during the period of Kyrgyzstan ’ s accession to Russia, reminds us that we must take care of our history more than ever. Ernest Hemingway ’ s “The Old Man and the Sea ”.“ Oh, I wish there was a boy with me! ” But there is no boy with you, ” he thought. “You can only count on yourself, and even though it is dark now, it would be better if you tried to get that last forest, cut it off and tie two spare skeins... A person should always be able to win, no matter what difficulties in life.  In 1954, Ernest Hemingway was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature “for the storytelling skills demonstrated in The Old Man and the Sea, as well as for the influence on modern prose. ”  You can read the story online here.  4 thoughts on “1916.  Diaries.  A letter to Stalin by Zhusup Abdrakhmanov.  “By the will of fate, I have witnessed the events of the greatest historical epoch. True, I do it with a great delay, but better late than never, ” wrote Zhusup Abdrakhmanov.  "My diary...  From now on, you are my only, faithful and silent friend.  Faithful for time and time.  You are loyal to me as long as you are in my hands, or you can become a traitor when you pass into the wrong hands.  The last possibility is not excluded, but still I will not hide anything from you.  I will tell you the thoughts and experiences not only of a political figure, but also of a mortal person, ” Reading Abdrakhmanov ’ s diaries, you imagine what life was like in our society in the thirties of the last century.  Immerse yourself in that difficult time for our people, the history of which for many years was distorted and in every possible way concealed from society.  Between these very personal lines you can feel the scale of Abdrakhmanov as a statesman who faithfully served the country for its prosperity.  Reflections of Zhusup Abdrakhmanov, his feelings for the future of the country, active work on the creation and strengthening of our statehood should serve as a vivid example for the current generation.  After all, they are a reminder to everyone that in those terrible 1930s, part of the generation sacrificed themselves for our future, putting their young heads on this terribly cruel altar.  We all need to remember that.  You can read some of the letters here.  5 The story "Kyly uzulgon komuzum" ("My Komuz with torn strings") Tenti Adysheva.  The life of the famous poetess Tenti Adysheva in our history occupies a special place.  Describing her life, she captured the period of the rise of Kyrgyz literature from the times of Zhoomart Bokonbaev, Mukay Elebaev, Aala Tokombaev, Zhusup Turusbekov, Temirkul Umotaliev, Kubanychbek Malikov, Alykul Osmonov, Tugelbai Sydykbekov.  As a poet, she managed to describe her memories in a poetic way, which causes great reader interest.  Kyrgyz women have always played a special role.  Tenti Adysheva is one of such bright personalities that left an indelible mark on our memory.  Given that the formation of her personality took place in the difficult circumstances of the totalitarian regime of Soviet power, her life positions and fate can serve as a vivid example for the younger generation.  Rose Aitmatova The story “My Komuz with torn strings ” was reprinted twice, instantly diverged and became a bibliographic rarity.  In it, in the magnificent literary Kyrgyz language, live portraits of the "Mighty Bunch" of great personalities - the founders of Kyrgyz literature, culture, art and science are given.  Zhoomart Bokonbaev was called the Kyrgyz Pushkin, and Tenti Adysheva is called the Kyrgyz Anna Akhmatova.  Unfortunately, there is no free access to Tenti Adysheva ’ s books.

passages.title: Hemingway: A typewriter in the trenches
passages.passage: Hemingway was the spokesperson for “Lost Generation, ” Ernest Hemingway liked to be a war reporter, professional athlete, hunter or adventurer.  He considered writing to be little, but eventually became one of the greatest writers of the 20th century.  He won the Nobel Prize for Literature and influenced many writers after World War II.  Today, Hemingway is one of the emblems of the modern world.  He ended his life 50 years ago.  Ernest Hemingway was born in Oak Park, Illinois, North America in 1899.  Her father was a doctor and gave a good life to the family.  Ernest was playful in school and hated homework, but he was smart enough to get good grades.  Hemingway was drawn into journalism at the age of 18.  With a rebellious nature that never calmed down, his heart yearned for distant lands and found this “opportunity ” in war.  As an ambulance driver for the International Red Cross, he traveled to Europe in the last year of the Great War with American troops.  During the war, he felt the horror of death with flesh and skin.  Under Austrian bombardment, he suffered severe injuries and was hospitalized for several months.  At the hospital in Milan, more than 200 pieces of shrapnel were removed from his body, and he used to pull metal from his leg with the tip of a knife.  Hemingway was also a lover and was impatient with beautiful women.  He was married four times in his life, amidst dozens of love stories.  At the hospital, she fell madly in love with her nurse.  But a few months later, after the war ended, he returned to the United States and married another woman.  He was 22 years old and his first wife was 29.  A decent and kind woman, who "accidentally" had a good financial situation.  A spokesman for Hemingway ’ s Lost Generation went to Europe in 1921 with his young wife, and in Paris joined the ranks of modernist writers who had gathered in the “capital of modern art ”: Scott Fitzgerald, John dos Passos, Ezra Pound, and others.  Gertrude Stein called it the “Lost Generation. ”  The children of this generation lost all hope and faith in the muddy fields of war and they no longer believed and trusted in anything.  The moral lessons and moral values and the bragging of “bourgeois civilization ” were seen as a bunch of deceptive lies.  Hemingway, who had begun to write real reports and his first short stories, brought this anger and frustration to paper in a new tone.  His stories, full of vitality, infused the deep anger and frustration of this generation with vivid and effective expression.  “The Sun Still Rises ” was a vivid account of the story of this generation, seeking consolation that could not be found in foreign cities.  The novel A Farewell to Arms, published in 1928, clearly expressed this disillusionment.  This wasn ’ t an ordinary princeling.  Someone was talking about the war, who had been wounded by it and still had its shrapnel in his body.  “I had seen nothing sacred, and the things that were glorious had no honor, and the victims were like cattle and sheep in the Chicago slaughterhouse — if they had nothing to do with the carcasses but to bury them. ”  (Farewell to Arms, translation of Najaf Daryabandari) This was the look of the masses of those who lost the war anyway, and this was of course different from the look and expression of the elites and commanders, for whom the war was a "field of honor" and full of "blessings".  Ernest Hemingway was married four times — his second wife, Pauline Pfeiffer, can be seen in this photo, some critics point out that Hemingway ’ s participation in the war was not just an individual experience that influenced his literary work, but, more than that, the war took over his whole being and his mentality, gave him a “war-torn ” temperament and shaped his worldview.  Hemingway was constantly ready to fight and saw in everything a challenge to fight: on the battlefield, in the boxing ring, or in the bullfight.  The novel The Sun Still Rises, published in 1927, illustrates this view in a variety of colorful depictions and images.  In Death in the Afternoon, published in the form of a true memoir or travelogue in 1932, the bullfight is a metaphor for confronting death: standing face to face with death, gazing into its eyes, shivering with this horror / pleasure, mingling with it, and finally sinking into its black palate.  It has been said that Hemingway ’ s hobbies, fishing, from hunting wild animals to hunting women, were manifestations of this constant temptation of war and bullying.  Even writing was a big challenge for him, with special preparation and discipline to “fight ” it.  Some critics have said that he saw killing and being killed as the only natural form of human history, so much so that he believed that a "healthy and natural" man should die on the field, not in bed.  There has always been a man of struggle and action in Hemingway ’ s “Square. ”  not from the works of others, as he has said with pride, but from blood and sweat.  Will Durant has said that in few writers life experiences are so closely intertwined with literary endeavors.  Hemingway hated intellectual habits and debate.  He despised the intellectuals who, steeped in abstract discussions, had forgotten the principle of life; he called them cowards and cowards.  He was not a theorist and did not even consider himself a literary and literary writer, in the classical sense.  He once said, “I ’ m not going to compete with Tolstoy. ”  In his Nobel Prize speech (1954), Hemingway's style and language explained his style with the metaphor of an "iceberg": "I try to be like an iceberg, seven eighths of which are hidden under water and only one eighth of which is visible.  The more we remove from the body of the story, the stronger the iceberg becomes.  The power of the story lies in what the author knows but doesn ’ t reveal.  If he omits something because he doesn ’ t know, there ’ s a hole in the story. ”  The author knows all about his space and characters but only gives the reader the least necessary information.  In this precise, measured and compact style, most of the notes and explanations are eliminated, but they do not go away; the reader senses them and is affected with far greater intensity.  With the technique of "elimination" in both story structure and language, a pure and clear text is provided that has a direct and lightning effect.  The plot or plot is missing.  The tongue is compact, concise, dry, and without sentimental frills.  Short sentences convey only a thin surface and leave the rest to the reader ’ s intelligence.  This is how the joy of reading the story is multiplied by the joy of discovery.  Hemingway wrote from real, live experiences.  (He even boasted that he had killed dozens of people in the war!)  It was the only objective language, unadorned and transparent, that could convey vivid experiences directly and directly, away from the repetitive pronouncements and fluttering sentimental adjectives.  Hemingway ’ s best work comes from personal tensions and struggles.  From a man ’ s quarrel with a giant fish, he presented one of the most fascinating stories of the 20th century.  It ’ s a true story with ancient myths.  All kinds of interpretations and interpretations have been published about "The Old Man and the Sea".  Hemingway ’ s own explanation is probably the best: “I have shown a true old man against a true fish in a true sea! ”  That too, true or false, had its origin in life.  Hemingway boasted that he once caught a 355-kilogram fish.  In the world of politics, Hemingway cannot be considered a “committed ” writer, even though he was“ engaged ” with political adventures all his life.  (His file on the FBI is thousands of pages!)  He was more or less present in all the important events of his time, a correspondent in the two world wars, and a little more active in the Spanish Civil War.  After all, he was a terrible writer.  The painful experience of war and the constant presence of death had engulfed his soul, infecting it with bitterness and deadly pessimism.  For the rest of his life, he looked at every struggle with ridicule and “cynicism ”.  Politics required a minimum of optimism and idealism, whereas Hemingway only “believed ” in himself and held the highest value in being“ loyal ” to himself.  Perhaps, following Nietzsche, without engaging himself with philosophical deliberations, he believed in individual power and “the will to power. ”  He had an iron fist, and he held his hand.  He had no weakness, no weakness, no weakness.  (He said, “Man can be destroyed, but he cannot be defeated. ”)  He knew the people and the people of both worlds.  In extreme individualism, Hemingway's goodness is equal to joy.  He liked prosperity and pleasure, but with a more or less Bohemian tendency he avoided “bourgeois ” life and culture.

passages.title: 【 Green Bird Residence 】 Event Feature ： Chen Jung-bin / Impression of Paris in Hemingway 's Text
passages.passage: In the 1920s, the Treaty of Versailles proclaimed the end of World War I, Hitler in Europe joined the Nazi Party, and the Communist Party of China rose in the East.  And the United States introduced a national prohibition of alcohol, so a group of American "expats" came to Paris, free and exile in various cafes and bars. Hemingway also moved to the old city as a reporter in 1921, beginning his penniless, but indulgent days.  A hundred years later, Chen Jung-bin and the audience of the Blue Bird House look back at the impression of Paris that was reflected in Hemingway ’ s words.  The Old Man and the Sea was born on an alcohol-soaked beach in Cuba; The War Bell is an interview from the Spanish Civil War; The Dawn of Truth records the memories of a trip to Africa with his fourth wife, Mary, and Hemingway, born in Oak Park, Illinois, USA.  At the age of 21, he worked as a reporter for the Toronto Star in Canada, became a special correspondent in Europe the next year, and moved to Paris to spend his 20 generations, nearly a decade of his golden years.  Ernest Hemingway in World War I. When he first arrived in Paris, he stayed in a small hotel and wrote in the Toronto Star: “PARIS — Paris in the winter is rainy, cold, beautiful and cheap. ”  It is also noisy, jostling, crowded and cheap.  It is anything you want — and cheap. ” — Living on $1,000 a Year in Paris Describes the bankruptcy of Europe at the end of World War I, the relative advantage of the dollar, and the ability to spend a thousand dollars in Paris for a year.  Although this article is published in the newspaper, the writing and rhyme are poetic.  “We ate well and cheaply and drank well and cheaply and slept well and warm together and love each other. ”  After graduating from high school, Hemingway worked as a reporter for the Kansas City Star, and his entire writing career was inextricably linked to journalistic writing.  “From Hemingway ’ s early writings, the Kansas Star newspaper ’ s“ style sheet ” for the rookie reporter shaped his unique style of writing, and the rules in the guide were as many as 110, and the first paragraph was indeed Hemingway ’ s rule: write short sentences.  The first paragraph is shorter.  Write articles in vivid English.  The influence of the rookie reporter period on his career also corresponds to the iceberg theory he proposed in 1932: "Prose is like architecture, not interior decoration, and the Baroque era is over... If you have enough understanding of what you are describing and write well enough, even if you write only one-eighth of the text, you can let the reader fully grasp the scene, plot and character description that he wants to express." Hemingway often uses a concise style to bury clues in the details or background, so that it is connected with emotional intimacy.  Paris was not only the place where Hemingway worked as a journalist, but also the beginning of his literary career.  The first two books, Three Stories & Ten Poems, and a collection of short stories, in our time, were published here.  Ernest Hemingway wrote many notes about his life and literary work in the 1920s. Two boxes were left in the basement of the Ritz Hotel in Paris, and when he returned to Paris in 1957, he opened these dusty old memories, namely, "The Feast on the Move".  This prose memoir of Paris also later became a guide for people on their pilgrimage journey, following Hemingway for a drink, order a cup of coffee at the Lilac Café, borrow a book at Shakespeare ’ s Bookstore on the Rue d ’ Odeon, and then take a walk in Luxembourg Park.  “If you are lucky enough to have lived in Paris as a young man, then wherever you go for the rest of your life it stays with you, for Paris is a movable feast. ” — Ernest Hemingway A moving feast.  Shakespeare Bookstore (Photo / Courtesy of Blue Bird) Mr. Chen then pointed out on the map several places where Hemingway often stopped in Paris. First came to the Shakespeare Bookstore, which is also like a library, which can rent books at affordable prices, and also provides mail collection services, which is suitable for young and poor boy Hemingway.  The owner of the bookstore, Shelville Beach, is also an American, and in her autobiography, Shakespeare's Bookstore, there is a chapter entitled "The Best Customer Hemingway".  In his translation of the book, Mr. Chen found hundreds of references to Hemingway, and the description of his affinity showed their deep and warm friendship at the time.  At the end of World War II, Hemingway returns to Paris with the Americans and meets Chevelle again.  There are still a lot of gun battles in the theater street, and we ’ ve had enough.  One day a jeep pulled into the street and stopped at the door of my bookstore.  I heard a low voice shouting, “Chevy! ” and it spread all over the street.  Edhiena cried, "It's Hemingway! It's Hemingway!" I rushed downstairs and hit the oncoming Hemingway.  He picked me up in circles and kissed me, and the people at the window of the street cheered … He asked if there was anything else I could do, and I said if I could get rid of the Nazi snipers on the roof of the street, especially those on Edsieena ’ s roof.  He called his buddies out of their jeeps, took them all to the roof, and then came the last gunfight on Theater Street.  Hemingway got down with his men and drove off in the jeep — next, Hemingway said, to the wine cellar at the Ritz.  The Lilac Garden Cafe (Photo / Courtesy of the Blue Bird House) The Lilac Garden on the Boulevard Montparnasse is the place where the artistic and cultural trends of Paris in the 1920s met and collided, and where Fitzgerald, Zola, Cezanne and Picasso all stopped.  “I sat in the corner writing with my notebook, and the afternoon sun was on my shoulders.  The waiter took me a cup of hot cream coffee (café crème), and I drank half of it after cooling, and the other half was on the table while I was writing.  When I stopped writing, I really didn ’ t want to leave the river where the trout could be seen in the pool. ” — Chen Jung-bin, author of “Feast on the Move, ” mentioned this text, poetically describing the process of creating the novel“ Our Time ” in Lilac Garden, and the river where the trout can be seen is the title of the book, “The Big Twin Heart River. ”  A Good Café on the Place St.-Michel "A girl walks into a cafe and sits alone at a table by the window.  She was beautiful, and her face was as fresh as a new coin — if only coins could be minted with silky muscles and rain-washed skin.  Her hair was as dark as the wings of a raven, cut into a blade, and covered her face obliquely.  I stared at her, and she disturbed my thoughts and made me very excited.  I wanted to put her in my novel or something, but she was sitting where she could see the street and the entrance to the cafe, so I knew she was waiting for someone.  So I continued to write.  The story seemed to unfold automatically, and my pen managed to keep up with it.  I ordered another glass of St. James ’ s brandy.  Whenever I raised my head or sharpened the pencil with a sharpener, I would look at the girl and let the curly scraps fall into the saucer under the glass. "  "I see you, my beauty, now you belong to me, no matter who you are waiting for, and no matter whether I can see you again in the future," I thought.  You belong to me, and all Paris belongs to me, and I belong to this notebook and this pencil.  From this Paris memoir, Teacher Chen Jung-bin led us to read this famous article. Reading this text, we followed Hemingway ’ s eyes, met the girl who distracted him in a cafe next to the square, took control between the mind and the pen, and then sat in the whole Paris.  Hemingway and Fitzgerald Fitzgerald (Photo / Courtesy of Blue Bird) Hemingway and artists from all walks of life in Paris, and Fitzgerald also met here, they first met at Dingo American Bar, and each other's affirmation is extremely sincere.  Hemingway left such a comment on Fitzgerald in "The Moving Feast": After reading "The Tycoon", he felt that no matter what outrageous things Fitzgerald did, he had to treat it as if Fitzgerald was sick, and he had to try to help him from the standpoint of a friend, "because, if he could write such a book, he could write a better book." This is probably the biggest compliment Hemingway has ever given to any of his peers.  Fitzgerald also gave Hemingway "He's the real thing." ("He's the real thing."), he introduced the editor and publisher to Hemingway, which greatly helped his writing career.  In "The Floating Feast",

passages.title: Hemingway's Myth
passages.passage: In 1953, Hemingway was sitting at a dinner table at his camp in Kenya, writing. (NARA, Photographer, Look Magazine) Anyone familiar with American literature and literary criticism should know the iceberg talk about literary creation.  The author of this statement is the famous American writer and Nobel Prize winner Ernest Hemingway.  The main point is that if a writer has a mind about what he wants to write, he can omit something he knows when he creates, and the reader will feel those omissions because the author is writing true.  It is like an iceberg that looks magnificent as it moves in the sea, but in fact only one-eighth of it is out of the water, and the invisible part is more and more real.  In the theory of ancient Chinese poetry creation, there is a saying of "artistic conception", emphasizing the scenes and emotions depicted through the works, stimulating the imagination of the readers, and leaving them a space for full reflection and play.  This is synonymous with the "iceberg theory", but Hemingway emphasized the authenticity of the work, aiming to criticize some writers who seemed to him to be quite incompetent, who simply "omitted something because they did not understand".  Hemingway ’ s “iceberg talk ” actually interprets his own creative style, which is to omit everything he thinks is optional in his writing, and to be as simple and implicit as possible.  This creative style of Hemingway is indeed unique and has had a profound impact, some even said: Hemingway with no one has the courage, "English attached to the literature of the hair cut clean." But what interests me is that he uses the "iceberg" as a metaphor.  This analogy is really good.  What people usually use as metaphors are some common things, such as peach blossoms in "face like peach blossoms" and torches in "eyes like torches". How many people have seen an iceberg?  Three years ago, I went to Alaska to visit, and all I saw was a large piece of ice floe on the sea surface, real sea icebergs, probably only in the South Pole and Arctic areas where ordinary people are difficult to set foot.  However, this parable is also very relevant and can make people understand God.  What you can read in a good work is certainly brilliant, like the magnificence of an iceberg above the surface of the water, but what it contains can be much wider and deeper than the literal meaning, like a much larger body of mountain undersea support.  Without the presence of seven eighths below, there is no beauty at the top.  In the book of Revelation, there is a great deal to be said about the use of metaphors.  He said that the metaphor contains two aspects that are opposite and complementary, and the things that are compared must be the same, otherwise they cannot be joined together; but at the same time, they must be different, otherwise they cannot be distinguished.  As for the interaction between the two, the greater the difference, the more the same thing will be baked; the more open it will be, the more unexpected it will be, the more novel the metaphor will be, and the better the effect will be.  According to the theory of Qian Zhongshu, Hemingway uses the iceberg as a metaphor, and the things that belong to it are "very divided", and it has indeed produced a surprising winning effect, so it is unforgettable.  There are many other examples of this in the metaphor Hemingway has used.  After Hemingway became famous, he often compared himself with other writers, and was quite conceited, many writers he could not see, and only Shakespeare and Tolstoy were really admired.  He did not know this, but used boxing as a metaphor.  He said that he did not want to play Dostoyevsky in the first game, because he knew that Dostoyevsky was almost as good as he was, so he chose to play with Turgenev first because he felt he could play with him.  Then try Maupassant again, although it is difficult, but also can beat him; as for Henry James, he said, "As soon as I catch me, I press him, and immediately give him a blow where he has no meat, so tell the referee to stop the game." Hemingway's words, you can see his confidence.  About him and Cervantes who is stronger, he has a different saying, he believes that 20 rounds of war, you can beat the other side of the fart, but also admitted that Mr. Cervantes is very shrewd, while playing and learning, maybe the second game he will lose to the other side.  In Hemingway ’ s eyes, Shakespeare is the champion who can ’ t beat.  And speaking of Tolstoy, whom he equally admired, he said something different.  He said that if he played six rounds with Tolstoy, the opponent would not want to hit him, but he would be beaten enough, but if he played 20 rounds with Tolstoy, he would be knocked off the ear.  He also said that if he could live to sixty, he might defeat Tolstoy.  I guess Hemingway is probably trying to say that some of his works can win Tolstoy, but in general, they can ’ t talk about each other, unless he can create more good works in the future (need to live longer).  What kind of metaphor is used is often related to the personality and creation style of the user.  Pushkin is an emotional romantic poet, in his short life, wrote many beautiful people's poems.  I noticed that Pushkin often compared his beloved poetry to a harp.  So I thought, it must be because this ancient instrument can play a very moving tune, like a poem to move the heart.  Then because of the occasional experience, I have a new feeling about it.  That time was a trip to the Rocky Mountains, staying at the Castle Hotel by Lake Louise.  In the afternoon, a woman dressed like a classical beauty in a long skirt played the harp in the hotel's glittering lobby. Some of the hotel's guests sat, some stood, and listened.  It was at this moment that I suddenly understood why Pushkin used the harp as a metaphor for poetry, because the scenes and atmosphere in the lobby were so romantic.  Unlike Hemingway, his work has created many images of tough men, and he himself loves tough and exciting activities such as bullfighting, horse racing, boxing and hunting, so it is not surprising that he uses boxing as a metaphor.  However, not all people can use the analogy of the things that are "very divided" as Mr. Qian Zhongshu said.  In other words, the winning or losing of a boxing match and the level of a writer were originally two things that could not be fought with eight poles, but Hemingway "closed" them.  The Nobel laureate often had this idea.  His son once copied Turgenev's work and wrote a novel, which Hemingway did not notice at first, and praised his son after reading it.  Of course, he found out later.  However, when someone asked if his son would write a novel, his father ’ s face smiled and replied, “Gregory (his son ’ s name) sometimes does a little lame proofreading. ” Hemingway said this, and the people on the side laughed heartily.  To call plagiarism “lame proofreading ” is not a metaphor, it is hard to say, but I really admire Hemingway ’ s mental flexibility and language wisdom.  Aristotle said, "Parables are the sign of genius." Hemingway was indeed a genius. (From India)

passages.title: Ernest Hemingway: As long as one of us lives, the other lives forever in his heart.
passages.passage: The novel is like an iceberg, only one eighth of which is on the surface of the water, and the rest is underwater.  Deleting more sentences and leaving more sentences underwater is enough to strengthen your novel.  This is Ernest Hemingway ’ s “theory of the iceberg ”, which he implemented in his novels. Today, 1940, For Whom the Bell Tolls is published.  Before publication, Hemingway revised the manuscript every day after finishing it, and did not leave the room for 96 consecutive hours.  He used iceberg theory to remove unnecessary sentences, and used symbols, pictures and ideas to navigate the story, resulting in this monumental work that was later adapted into a film and used by the college to teach literature.  Ernest Hemingway (Getty Images) The bell-ringing story in the field focuses on an attack by a guerrilla group during the Spanish Civil War in the summer of 1937.  The story is only four days long, focusing on the tension of the war and the appearance of human nature.  The protagonist, Robert Jordan, is an American professor who teaches Spanish. At the outbreak of the war, he joined the volunteer army and was ordered to go deep into the mountains to break through enemy lines, and the story begins when the protagonist enters the mountains, he tries to contact the guerrillas and cooperate with them to blow up the bridge.  For Whom the Bell Tolls: The Hemingway Library Edition (Scribner) Guerrilla Captain Pablo opposes the bridge, losing his fighting spirit and even stealing the detonator.  Robert manages to gain support from the rest of the team, isolating the captain and planning to blow up the bridge.  Robert takes in Maria, a girl who has been abused and enslaved by the enemy, and falls in love with her.  After stealing the horses from the enemy line, the two walked hand in hand, and he imagined that after the war was over, he would return to the United States to teach, and the two would end up together.  But after a while, he shot and killed one of the other soldiers, and while he did not get any information from the enemy, he read a home letter, which made him feel the cruelty of the war.  In the early hours of the last day, the few remaining teams set out for the bridge, and due to the small number of people and the behavior of the captain, several people had to risk their lives.  In the final scene, Robert and his companions blow the bridge in mid-air with explosives, but when he runs away on horseback in the direction of Maria, he is unfortunately shot and fell, his left leg is broken, and he can no longer escape from the enemy's attack.  At the end of his life, he said to Mary, “As long as one of us lives, the other will live in his heart forever. ”  In 1943, Battlefield Bell was transformed into a film (file picture) The tragic color of "tough man" Hemingway's novels often appear as "tough man", meaning that he has a very strong will and a strong and unyielding spirit.  When the Nobel Prize for Literature was awarded to him, he said that he "has a kind of man who likes to take risks" and vowed not to bow down and fight to the end when faced with the pressure of fate.  The old fisherman in The Old Man and the Sea said, “Man can be destroyed, but he cannot be defeated. ”  But when we talk about fate and rebellion, we often talk about tragedy, and the end of Battlefield Bell is clearly tragic.  [The Old Man and the Sea] Hemingway's many novels have been exposed hundreds of wrong scholars: The fault is not in the spirit of his ancient Greek tragedy, it is that when people face the choice of fate, they know that they have to bear a heavy price and still struggle to insist on their own choices, and finally they really want to meet the tragic consequences.  It may be against fate, it may be against power, and it ends tragically.  In The Birth of Tragedy, Nietzsche pointed out that the ancient Greek tragedy was the manifestation of the god of wine, freed from the "self", disordered and led to a carnival, chanting that people "believe in eternal life".
