passages.title: How to read Hemingway?
passages.passage: Ernest Hemingway, a Nobel laureate and one of the most important of the 20th century, was born on July 21, 1899 in Illinois and wrote seven novels, six collections of short stories and two nonfiction books during his lifetime.  On the occasion of the birth of this author, which coincided with the thirteenth of July, we have suggestions for better reading of the works of this author.  Hemingway ’ s work is fluid, simple, and clear, but for many readers of literature, it may be difficult to begin reading Hemingway ’ s books.  Why read Hemingway?  Ernest Hemingway is an influential writer in the history of literature and fiction, his works have repeatedly won the most prestigious international literary awards such as Nobel and Pulitzer, this author employed a different kind of narrative description and caused many writers after him to borrow his own literary style.  Hemingway has named his literary style the Iceberg Theory, in this way of writing, fictional events are narrated like an iceberg floating in water, only one-eighth of which is visible, and the author includes only the information that is essential in the process and omits the rest of the information.  This technique created a tremendous change in storytelling, especially the writing of short stories, and it was a development that freed the stories from conventional chatter.  Hemingway ’ s works are included in the list of books of the century, books to read before death, and the best fiction books in history, highlighting the importance of this author.  What do we need to know?  One of the topics that helps to better understand Ernest Hemingway ’ s work is getting to know his personal life.  Much of what we read in his books is what he has turned from his personal life into a story.  At the age of 19, he volunteered for the First World War but was not allowed to fight because of poor eyesight, but Hemingway insisted on serving as an ambulance driver for the Red Cross.  He was wounded several times during the Chang, but his most significant injury is when he was wounded by mortar shell fragments and spent a long time in the hospital, a novel about this part of Hemingway ’ s life and the war.  Even the character of Catherine Barkley in this book is based on the nurse Hemingway fell in love with.  Hemingway also participated in World War II as a war correspondent, and several short stories are the result of this era.  The sun continues to blow, the Great River or along the river to the trees, each of which is somehow tied to the World War, and their heroes are survivors of the war and have many memories of these days.  But Hemingway ’ s most important masterpiece is a relic of his childhood, Hemingway ’ s father had a great interest in fishing, and this hobby was passed on to Ernest, a point that can be clearly seen in the famous and widely read story of The Old Man and the Sea.  But before the Old Man and the Sea, Hemingway had written about having and not having a fishing boat captain.  Another important point to know before reading Hemingway ’ s works is his political approach, he has written a lot in opposition to fascism and against dictatorship, both as a journalist and as a writer, sometimes even changing from a journalist to a social-political activist, who is this point in The Bell for, or who is this death knell?  It is a story of an American soldier in the Spanish Civil War fighting alongside groups against General Franco, which Hemingway did.  Perhaps the other thing that matters is that during the World War, Hemingway led a French group against the Nazis that was tried after the war for armed acts but was never proven guilty.  The political and social history of the world in the years of Hemingway's life, his personal life, as well as the knowledge of his contemporaries, such as Scott Fitzgerald, with whom he has written, are points that contribute to the understanding of his works.  Getting to know Hemingway ’ s contemporary writers helps to better understand the difference between him and his contemporaries.  Is it a classic?  To read Hemingway ’ s work, we must note that he is not a classic writer in his different style, he did not deal with the long margins and descriptions of classical literature, and his long novels are not immune.  He was interested in shorthand and engaging the audience with fiction, which is a feature of modern literature.  In general, Hemingway ’ s works are innovative and even among modern works have their own creativity, but the value of this author ’ s work has always been compared to classical works, and even classical enthusiasts have not been able to be indifferent to it.  In these works we have a happy and well-spoken writer, a writer who was in middle age with young people and was even close friends with a group of hippies.  Hemingway is a realistic writer, but he has always tried to maintain his sense of humor.  Where do we start?  To read Hemingway ’ s works, the first and most important suggestion is The Old Man and the Sea.  The book, translated by Najaf Daryabandari, was published in 222 pages by Kharazmi Publications.  The next book, Farewell to Arms, is again translated by Najaf Daryabendari, published by Amir Kabir Publications in 343 pages.  These two books are always on the list of works to be read or masterpieces of the 20th century.  If you are interested in short stories, you can also read Men Without Women, a collection of stories that have been published in various magazines by the author.  This book has been translated by Asadollah Amraei for publication of Horizon in 222 pages.  Even if you are interested in writing, Hemingway can be a good teacher and read his series of talks and learn very precise points.  The book The Last Interview and Other Conversations of Ernest Hemingway with a translation by Houshang Jirani has been published in 88 pages by Cheshmeh Publishing.  The final chapter of many critics considered Ernest Hemingway to be the greatest writer of the 20th century.  His stories are an exploration of real human life, suffering and the meaning of life.  The portrayal of human inner feelings is the most important characteristic of this author, which makes his works a read for every reader.  Who was Ernest Hemingway?  Ernest Hemingway was born on July 21, 1899 in Oak Park, Illinois.  His father, Clarence, was a doctor and his mother, Grace, was a piano and singing teacher.  Ernest spent the summers with his family in northern Michigan, where he discovered his passion for fishing.  After finishing high school, he worked for a while in Kansas City as a reporter for the Star Chronicle in 1917.  During World War I, he volunteered to serve in the army, but poor eyesight prevented him from doing so, instead serving as an ambulance driver for the Red Cross near the Italian front.  On July 8, 1918, he was injured and spent months in the hospital.  In 1925, his first collection of short stories, in our time, was published, which spoke well of his particular style.  His memoirs from that period were published after his death in 1964 as The Variable Eid.  Ernest Hemingway was an adventurer for most of his life.  From being wounded in Italy by 200 pieces of Austrian shrapnel during World War I, to taking part in the frontlines of the Spanish Civil War or touring the African wilderness, to fishing and hunting wildlife and living in Cuba.  He finally said goodbye to life with his hunting rifle.

Title: Top 5 books from the sister of the national writer of Kyrgyzstan Roza Aitmatova
Content: Rose Aitmatova is destined to always remain the younger sister of the famous writer with a world name.  But she ’ s not just proud of her family name.  Roza Torekulovna, despite her solid age (March 8, she turned 80 years old), continues to work hard to preserve the literary heritage of Chingiz Aitmatov.  She is also active in protecting the rights of Kyrgyz women.  Today, Roza Aitmatova is a guest of our traditional top-5 category and presents her favorite books.  The story "White steamer" Chingiz Aitmatov.  In the story Chingiz Torekulovich raised the eternal theme of good and evil.  It is a message to humanity: do good in this world.  In addition, I think the work forms in a person a sense of humane and careful attitude to nature.  Another important aspect that Chingiz Torekulovich reveals to us is the preservation of the value of the family.  Children should not be left orphans with living parents.  Rose Aitmatova is wise, isn't it?  “Grandfather says that if people don ’ t remember their fathers, they will go bad.  Grandfather says that then no one will be ashamed of bad deeds, because children and children of children will not remember them.  And no one will do good things, because the children will not know about it anyway, ” the book says.  I think that this story and now, in the age of globalization, more than ever should be in demand for the younger generation.  We must not forget our roots and national traditions.  This, as you know, leads to the decline of culture.  Turning to metaphors through the legend of the horned Mother of the Deer, Chingiz Torekulovich reminds us of how important the spiritual connection of generations is for our people.  Rose Aitmatova The problem of good and evil is the basis of fairy tales and legends.  But if in fairy tales good almost always triumphs, and evil is punished, then in reality this is not always the case.  I think the story "White steamer" is also interesting because it simultaneously coexists modern life and ancient legend, and the problem of good and evil is solved differently from the usual outcome.  You can read the story online here.  2 The novel “Syngan kylych ” (“ Broken sword ”) by Tologon Kasymbekov.  It was difficult for the Kyrgyz historical path to independence.  “Broken Sword ”, telling us about the turbulent and complex historical events during the period of Kyrgyzstan ’ s accession to Russia, reminds us that we must take care of our history more than ever.  This level of historical works in Kyrgyz literature is not enough.  Knowing your history is the key to the future.  You can read the novel here.  Ernest Hemingway ’ s “The Old Man and the Sea ”.“ Oh, I wish there was a boy with me! ” But there is no boy with you, ” he thought. “You can only count on yourself, and even though it is dark now, it would be better if you tried to get that last forest, cut it off and tie two spare skeins...  What simple words.  "Fish," he called quietly, "I will not part with you until I die."  For many people, including me, this is a very powerful work.  One that needs to be read between the lines.  The artistic power of the story is to show the inner strength of a person and his ability to realize not only the beauty and grandeur of the surrounding world, but also his place in it.  A person should always be able to win, no matter what difficulties in life.  In 1954, Ernest Hemingway was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature “for the storytelling skills demonstrated in The Old Man and the Sea, as well as for the influence on modern prose. ”  You can read the story online here.  4 thoughts on “1916.  Diaries.  A letter to Stalin by Zhusup Abdrakhmanov.  “By the will of fate, I have witnessed the events of the greatest historical epoch.  Therefore, historically interesting fixation of what you saw, experienced, felt for each day.  This can be done with the help of a diary, and I will try to do it.  True, I do it with a great delay, but better late than never, ” wrote Zhusup Abdrakhmanov.  "My diary...  From now on, you are my only, faithful and silent friend.  Faithful for time and time.  You are loyal to me as long as you are in my hands, or you can become a traitor when you pass into the wrong hands.  The last possibility is not excluded, but still I will not hide anything from you.  I will tell you the thoughts and experiences not only of a political figure, but also of a mortal person, ” Reading Abdrakhmanov ’ s diaries, you imagine what life was like in our society in the thirties of the last century.  Immerse yourself in that difficult time for our people, the history of which for many years was distorted and in every possible way concealed from society.  Between these very personal lines you can feel the scale of Abdrakhmanov as a statesman who faithfully served the country for its prosperity.  Reflections of Zhusup Abdrakhmanov, his feelings for the future of the country, active work on the creation and strengthening of our statehood should serve as a vivid example for the current generation.  After all, they are a reminder to everyone that in those terrible 1930s, part of the generation sacrificed themselves for our future, putting their young heads on this terribly cruel altar.  We all need to remember that.  You can read some of the letters here.  5 The story "Kyly uzulgon komuzum" ("My Komuz with torn strings") Tenti Adysheva.  The life of the famous poetess Tenti Adysheva in our history occupies a special place.  Describing her life, she captured the period of the rise of Kyrgyz literature from the times of Zhoomart Bokonbaev, Mukay Elebaev, Aala Tokombaev, Zhusup Turusbekov, Temirkul Umotaliev, Kubanychbek Malikov, Alykul Osmonov, Tugelbai Sydykbekov.  As a poet, she managed to describe her memories in a poetic way, which causes great reader interest.  Kyrgyz women have always played a special role.  Tenti Adysheva is one of such bright personalities that left an indelible mark on our memory.  Given that the formation of her personality took place in the difficult circumstances of the totalitarian regime of Soviet power, her life positions and fate can serve as a vivid example for the younger generation.  Rose Aitmatova The story “My Komuz with torn strings ” was reprinted twice, instantly diverged and became a bibliographic rarity.  In it, in the magnificent literary Kyrgyz language, live portraits of the "Mighty Bunch" of great personalities - the founders of Kyrgyz literature, culture, art and science are given.  Zhoomart Bokonbaev was called the Kyrgyz Pushkin, and Tenti Adysheva is called the Kyrgyz Anna Akhmatova.  Unfortunately, there is no free access to Tenti Adysheva ’ s books.

Title: Hemingway: A typewriter in the trenches
Content: Hemingway was the spokesperson for “Lost Generation, ” Ernest Hemingway liked to be a war reporter, professional athlete, hunter or adventurer.  He considered writing to be little, but eventually became one of the greatest writers of the 20th century.  He won the Nobel Prize for Literature and influenced many writers after World War II.  Today, Hemingway is one of the emblems of the modern world.  He ended his life 50 years ago.  Ernest Hemingway was born in Oak Park, Illinois, North America in 1899.  Her father was a doctor and gave a good life to the family.  Ernest was playful in school and hated homework, but he was smart enough to get good grades.  Hemingway was drawn into journalism at the age of 18.  With a rebellious nature that never calmed down, his heart yearned for distant lands and found this “opportunity ” in war.  As an ambulance driver for the International Red Cross, he traveled to Europe in the last year of the Great War with American troops.  During the war, he felt the horror of death with flesh and skin.  Under Austrian bombardment, he suffered severe injuries and was hospitalized for several months.  At the hospital in Milan, more than 200 pieces of shrapnel were removed from his body, and he used to pull metal from his leg with the tip of a knife.  Hemingway was also a lover and was impatient with beautiful women.  He was married four times in his life, amidst dozens of love stories.  At the hospital, she fell madly in love with her nurse.  But a few months later, after the war ended, he returned to the United States and married another woman.  He was 22 years old and his first wife was 29.  A decent and kind woman, who "accidentally" had a good financial situation.  A spokesman for Hemingway ’ s Lost Generation went to Europe in 1921 with his young wife, and in Paris joined the ranks of modernist writers who had gathered in the “capital of modern art ”: Scott Fitzgerald, John dos Passos, Ezra Pound, and others.  Gertrude Stein called it the “Lost Generation. ”  The children of this generation lost all hope and faith in the muddy fields of war and they no longer believed and trusted in anything.  The moral lessons and moral values and the bragging of “bourgeois civilization ” were seen as a bunch of deceptive lies.  Hemingway, who had begun to write real reports and his first short stories, brought this anger and frustration to paper in a new tone.  His stories, full of vitality, infused the deep anger and frustration of this generation with vivid and effective expression.  “The Sun Still Rises ” was a vivid account of the story of this generation, seeking consolation that could not be found in foreign cities.  The novel A Farewell to Arms, published in 1928, clearly expressed this disillusionment.  This wasn ’ t an ordinary princeling.  Someone was talking about the war, who had been wounded by it and still had its shrapnel in his body.  “I had seen nothing sacred, and the things that were glorious had no honor, and the victims were like cattle and sheep in the Chicago slaughterhouse — if they had nothing to do with the carcasses but to bury them. ”  (Farewell to Arms, translation of Najaf Daryabandari) This was the look of the masses of those who lost the war anyway, and this was of course different from the look and expression of the elites and commanders, for whom the war was a "field of honor" and full of "blessings".  Ernest Hemingway was married four times — his second wife, Pauline Pfeiffer, can be seen in this photo, some critics point out that Hemingway ’ s participation in the war was not just an individual experience that influenced his literary work, but, more than that, the war took over his whole being and his mentality, gave him a “war-torn ” temperament and shaped his worldview.  Hemingway was constantly ready to fight and saw in everything a challenge to fight: on the battlefield, in the boxing ring, or in the bullfight.  The novel The Sun Still Rises, published in 1927, illustrates this view in a variety of colorful depictions and images.  In Death in the Afternoon, published in the form of a true memoir or travelogue in 1932, the bullfight is a metaphor for confronting death: standing face to face with death, gazing into its eyes, shivering with this horror / pleasure, mingling with it, and finally sinking into its black palate.  It has been said that Hemingway ’ s hobbies, fishing, from hunting wild animals to hunting women, were manifestations of this constant temptation of war and bullying.  Even writing was a big challenge for him, with special preparation and discipline to “fight ” it.  Some critics have said that he saw killing and being killed as the only natural form of human history, so much so that he believed that a "healthy and natural" man should die on the field, not in bed.  There has always been a man of struggle and action in Hemingway ’ s “Square. ”  not from the works of others, as he has said with pride, but from blood and sweat.  Will Durant has said that in few writers life experiences are so closely intertwined with literary endeavors.  Hemingway hated intellectual habits and debate.  He despised the intellectuals who, steeped in abstract discussions, had forgotten the principle of life; he called them cowards and cowards.  He was not a theorist and did not even consider himself a literary and literary writer, in the classical sense.  He once said, “I ’ m not going to compete with Tolstoy. ”  In his Nobel Prize speech (1954), Hemingway's style and language explained his style with the metaphor of an "iceberg": "I try to be like an iceberg, seven eighths of which are hidden under water and only one eighth of which is visible.  The more we remove from the body of the story, the stronger the iceberg becomes.  The power of the story lies in what the author knows but doesn ’ t reveal.  If he omits something because he doesn ’ t know, there ’ s a hole in the story. ”  The author knows all about his space and characters but only gives the reader the least necessary information.  In this precise, measured and compact style, most of the notes and explanations are eliminated, but they do not go away; the reader senses them and is affected with far greater intensity.  With the technique of "elimination" in both story structure and language, a pure and clear text is provided that has a direct and lightning effect.  The plot or plot is missing.  The tongue is compact, concise, dry, and without sentimental frills.  Short sentences convey only a thin surface and leave the rest to the reader ’ s intelligence.  This is how the joy of reading the story is multiplied by the joy of discovery.  Hemingway wrote from real, live experiences.  (He even boasted that he had killed dozens of people in the war!)  It was the only objective language, unadorned and transparent, that could convey vivid experiences directly and directly, away from the repetitive pronouncements and fluttering sentimental adjectives.  Hemingway ’ s best work comes from personal tensions and struggles.  From a man ’ s quarrel with a giant fish, he presented one of the most fascinating stories of the 20th century.  It ’ s a true story with ancient myths.  All kinds of interpretations and interpretations have been published about "The Old Man and the Sea".  Hemingway ’ s own explanation is probably the best: “I have shown a true old man against a true fish in a true sea! ”  That too, true or false, had its origin in life.  Hemingway boasted that he once caught a 355-kilogram fish.  In the world of politics, Hemingway cannot be considered a “committed ” writer, even though he was“ engaged ” with political adventures all his life.  (His file on the FBI is thousands of pages!)  He was more or less present in all the important events of his time, a correspondent in the two world wars, and a little more active in the Spanish Civil War.  After all, he was a terrible writer.  The painful experience of war and the constant presence of death had engulfed his soul, infecting it with bitterness and deadly pessimism.  For the rest of his life, he looked at every struggle with ridicule and “cynicism ”.  Politics required a minimum of optimism and idealism, whereas Hemingway only “believed ” in himself and held the highest value in being“ loyal ” to himself.  Perhaps, following Nietzsche, without engaging himself with philosophical deliberations, he believed in individual power and “the will to power. ”  He had an iron fist, and he held his hand.  He had no weakness, no weakness, no weakness.  (He said, “Man can be destroyed, but he cannot be defeated. ”)  He knew the people and the people of both worlds.  In extreme individualism, Hemingway's goodness is equal to joy.  He liked prosperity and pleasure, but with a more or less Bohemian tendency he avoided “bourgeois ” life and culture.

Title: 【 Green Bird Residence 】 Event Feature ： Chen Jung-bin / Impression of Paris in Hemingway 's Text
Content: In the 1920s, the Treaty of Versailles proclaimed the end of World War I, Hitler in Europe joined the Nazi Party, and the Communist Party of China rose in the East.  And the United States introduced a national prohibition of alcohol, so a group of American "expats" came to Paris, free and exile in various cafes and bars. Hemingway also moved to the old city as a reporter in 1921, beginning his penniless, but indulgent days.  A hundred years later, Chen Jung-bin and the audience of the Blue Bird House look back at the impression of Paris that was reflected in Hemingway ’ s words.  The Old Man and the Sea was born on an alcohol-soaked beach in Cuba; The War Bell is an interview from the Spanish Civil War; The Dawn of Truth records the memories of a trip to Africa with his fourth wife, Mary, and Hemingway, born in Oak Park, Illinois, USA.  At the age of 21, he worked as a reporter for the Toronto Star in Canada, became a special correspondent in Europe the next year, and moved to Paris to spend his 20 generations, nearly a decade of his golden years.  Ernest Hemingway in World War I. When he first arrived in Paris, he stayed in a small hotel and wrote in the Toronto Star: “PARIS — Paris in the winter is rainy, cold, beautiful and cheap. ”  It is also noisy, jostling, crowded and cheap.  It is anything you want — and cheap. ” — Living on $1,000 a Year in Paris Describes the bankruptcy of Europe at the end of World War I, the relative advantage of the dollar, and the ability to spend a thousand dollars in Paris for a year.  Although this article is published in the newspaper, the writing and rhyme are poetic.  “We ate well and cheaply and drank well and cheaply and slept well and warm together and love each other. ”  After graduating from high school, Hemingway worked as a reporter for the Kansas City Star, and his entire writing career was inextricably linked to journalistic writing.  “From Hemingway ’ s early writings, the Kansas Star newspaper ’ s“ style sheet ” for the rookie reporter shaped his unique style of writing, and the rules in the guide were as many as 110, and the first paragraph was indeed Hemingway ’ s rule: write short sentences.  The first paragraph is shorter.  Write articles in vivid English.  The influence of the rookie reporter period on his career also corresponds to the iceberg theory he proposed in 1932: "Prose is like architecture, not interior decoration, and the Baroque era is over... If you have enough understanding of what you are describing and write well enough, even if you write only one-eighth of the text, you can let the reader fully grasp the scene, plot and character description that he wants to express." Hemingway often uses a concise style to bury clues in the details or background, so that it is connected with emotional intimacy.  Paris was not only the place where Hemingway worked as a journalist, but also the beginning of his literary career.  The first two books, Three Stories & Ten Poems, and a collection of short stories, in our time, were published here.  Ernest Hemingway wrote many notes about his life and literary work in the 1920s. Two boxes were left in the basement of the Ritz Hotel in Paris, and when he returned to Paris in 1957, he opened these dusty old memories, namely, "The Feast on the Move".  This prose memoir of Paris also later became a guide for people on their pilgrimage journey, following Hemingway for a drink, order a cup of coffee at the Lilac Café, borrow a book at Shakespeare ’ s Bookstore on the Rue d ’ Odeon, and then take a walk in Luxembourg Park.  “If you are lucky enough to have lived in Paris as a young man, then wherever you go for the rest of your life it stays with you, for Paris is a movable feast. ” — Ernest Hemingway A moving feast.  Shakespeare Bookstore (Photo / Courtesy of Blue Bird) Mr. Chen then pointed out on the map several places where Hemingway often stopped in Paris. First came to the Shakespeare Bookstore, which is also like a library, which can rent books at affordable prices, and also provides mail collection services, which is suitable for young and poor boy Hemingway.  The owner of the bookstore, Shelville Beach, is also an American, and in her autobiography, Shakespeare's Bookstore, there is a chapter entitled "The Best Customer Hemingway".  In his translation of the book, Mr. Chen found hundreds of references to Hemingway, and the description of his affinity showed their deep and warm friendship at the time.  At the end of World War II, Hemingway returns to Paris with the Americans and meets Chevelle again.  There are still a lot of gun battles in the theater street, and we ’ ve had enough.  One day a jeep pulled into the street and stopped at the door of my bookstore.  I heard a low voice shouting, “Chevy! ” and it spread all over the street.  Edhiena cried, "It's Hemingway! It's Hemingway!" I rushed downstairs and hit the oncoming Hemingway.  He picked me up in circles and kissed me, and the people at the window of the street cheered … He asked if there was anything else I could do, and I said if I could get rid of the Nazi snipers on the roof of the street, especially those on Edsieena ’ s roof.  He called his buddies out of their jeeps, took them all to the roof, and then came the last gunfight on Theater Street.  Hemingway got down with his men and drove off in the jeep — next, Hemingway said, to the wine cellar at the Ritz.  The Lilac Garden Cafe (Photo / Courtesy of the Blue Bird House) The Lilac Garden on the Boulevard Montparnasse is the place where the artistic and cultural trends of Paris in the 1920s met and collided, and where Fitzgerald, Zola, Cezanne and Picasso all stopped.  “I sat in the corner writing with my notebook, and the afternoon sun was on my shoulders.  The waiter took me a cup of hot cream coffee (café crème), and I drank half of it after cooling, and the other half was on the table while I was writing.  When I stopped writing, I really didn ’ t want to leave the river where the trout could be seen in the pool. ” — Chen Jung-bin, author of “Feast on the Move, ” mentioned this text, poetically describing the process of creating the novel“ Our Time ” in Lilac Garden, and the river where the trout can be seen is the title of the book, “The Big Twin Heart River. ”  A Good Café on the Place St.-Michel "A girl walks into a cafe and sits alone at a table by the window.  She was beautiful, and her face was as fresh as a new coin — if only coins could be minted with silky muscles and rain-washed skin.  Her hair was as dark as the wings of a raven, cut into a blade, and covered her face obliquely.  I stared at her, and she disturbed my thoughts and made me very excited.  I wanted to put her in my novel or something, but she was sitting where she could see the street and the entrance to the cafe, so I knew she was waiting for someone.  So I continued to write.  The story seemed to unfold automatically, and my pen managed to keep up with it.  I ordered another glass of St. James ’ s brandy.  Whenever I raised my head or sharpened the pencil with a sharpener, I would look at the girl and let the curly scraps fall into the saucer under the glass. "  "I see you, my beauty, now you belong to me, no matter who you are waiting for, and no matter whether I can see you again in the future," I thought.  You belong to me, and all Paris belongs to me, and I belong to this notebook and this pencil.  From this Paris memoir, Teacher Chen Jung-bin led us to read this famous article. Reading this text, we followed Hemingway ’ s eyes, met the girl who distracted him in a cafe next to the square, took control between the mind and the pen, and then sat in the whole Paris.  Hemingway and Fitzgerald Fitzgerald (Photo / Courtesy of Blue Bird) Hemingway and artists from all walks of life in Paris, and Fitzgerald also met here, they first met at Dingo American Bar, and each other's affirmation is extremely sincere.  Hemingway left such a comment on Fitzgerald in "The Moving Feast": After reading "The Tycoon", he felt that no matter what outrageous things Fitzgerald did, he had to treat it as if Fitzgerald was sick, and he had to try to help him from the standpoint of a friend, "because, if he could write such a book, he could write a better book." This is probably the biggest compliment Hemingway has ever given to any of his peers.  Fitzgerald also gave Hemingway "He's the real thing." Title: Hemingway's Myth
Content: In 1953, Hemingway was sitting at a dinner table at his camp in Kenya, writing. (NARA, Photographer, Look Magazine) Anyone familiar with American literature and literary criticism should know the iceberg talk about literary creation.  The author of this statement is the famous American writer and Nobel Prize winner Ernest Hemingway.  The main point is that if a writer has a mind about what he wants to write, he can omit something he knows when he creates, and the reader will feel those omissions because the author is writing true.  It is like an iceberg that looks magnificent as it moves in the sea, but in fact only one-eighth of it is out of the water, and the invisible part is more and more real.  In the theory of ancient Chinese poetry creation, there is a saying of "artistic conception", emphasizing the scenes and emotions depicted through the works, stimulating the imagination of the readers, and leaving them a space for full reflection and play.  This is synonymous with the "iceberg theory", but Hemingway emphasized the authenticity of the work, aiming to criticize some writers who seemed to him to be quite incompetent, who simply "omitted something because they did not understand".  Hemingway ’ s “iceberg talk ” actually interprets his own creative style, which is to omit everything he thinks is optional in his writing, and to be as simple and implicit as possible.  This creative style of Hemingway is indeed unique and has had a profound impact, some even said: Hemingway with no one has the courage, "English attached to the literature of the hair cut clean." But what interests me is that he uses the "iceberg" as a metaphor.  This analogy is really good.  What people usually use as metaphors are some common things, such as peach blossoms in "face like peach blossoms" and torches in "eyes like torches". How many people have seen an iceberg?  Three years ago, I went to Alaska to visit, and all I saw was a large piece of ice floe on the sea surface, real sea icebergs, probably only in the South Pole and Arctic areas where ordinary people are difficult to set foot.  However, this parable is also very relevant and can make people understand God.  What you can read in a good work is certainly brilliant, like the magnificence of an iceberg above the surface of the water, but what it contains can be much wider and deeper than the literal meaning, like a much larger body of mountain undersea support.  Without the presence of seven eighths below, there is no beauty at the top.  In the book of Revelation, there is a great deal to be said about the use of metaphors.  He said that the metaphor contains two aspects that are opposite and complementary, and the things that are compared must be the same, otherwise they cannot be joined together; but at the same time, they must be different, otherwise they cannot be distinguished.  As for the interaction between the two, the greater the difference, the more the same thing will be baked; the more open it will be, the more unexpected it will be, the more novel the metaphor will be, and the better the effect will be.  According to the theory of Qian Zhongshu, Hemingway uses the iceberg as a metaphor, and the things that belong to it are "very divided", and it has indeed produced a surprising winning effect, so it is unforgettable.  There are many other examples of this in the metaphor Hemingway has used.  After Hemingway became famous, he often compared himself with other writers, and was quite conceited, many writers he could not see, and only Shakespeare and Tolstoy were really admired.  He did not know this, but used boxing as a metaphor.  He said that he did not want to play Dostoyevsky in the first game, because he knew that Dostoyevsky was almost as good as he was, so he chose to play with Turgenev first because he felt he could play with him.  Then try Maupassant again, although it is difficult, but also can beat him; as for Henry James, he said, "As soon as I catch me, I press him, and immediately give him a blow where he has no meat, so tell the referee to stop the game." Hemingway's words, you can see his confidence.  About him and Cervantes who is stronger, he has a different saying, he believes that 20 rounds of war, you can beat the other side of the fart, but also admitted that Mr. Cervantes is very shrewd, while playing and learning, maybe the second game he will lose to the other side.  In Hemingway ’ s eyes, Shakespeare is the champion who can ’ t beat.  And speaking of Tolstoy, whom he equally admired, he said something different.  He said that if he played six rounds with Tolstoy, the opponent would not want to hit him, but he would be beaten enough, but if he played 20 rounds with Tolstoy, he would be knocked off the ear.  He also said that if he could live to sixty, he might defeat Tolstoy.  I guess Hemingway is probably trying to say that some of his works can win Tolstoy, but in general, they can ’ t talk about each other, unless he can create more good works in the future (need to live longer).  What kind of metaphor is used is often related to the personality and creation style of the user.  Pushkin is an emotional romantic poet, in his short life, wrote many beautiful people's poems.  I noticed that Pushkin often compared his beloved poetry to a harp.  So I thought, it must be because this ancient instrument can play a very moving tune, like a poem to move the heart.  Then because of the occasional experience, I have a new feeling about it.  That time was a trip to the Rocky Mountains, staying at the Castle Hotel by Lake Louise.  In the afternoon, a woman dressed like a classical beauty in a long skirt played the harp in the hotel's glittering lobby. Some of the hotel's guests sat, some stood, and listened.  It was at this moment that I suddenly understood why Pushkin used the harp as a metaphor for poetry, because the scenes and atmosphere in the lobby were so romantic.  Unlike Hemingway, his work has created many images of tough men, and he himself loves tough and exciting activities such as bullfighting, horse racing, boxing and hunting, so it is not surprising that he uses boxing as a metaphor.  However, not all people can use the analogy of the things that are "very divided" as Mr. Qian Zhongshu said.  In other words, the winning or losing of a boxing match and the level of a writer were originally two things that could not be fought with eight poles, but Hemingway "closed" them.  The Nobel laureate often had this idea.  His son once copied Turgenev's work and wrote a novel, which Hemingway did not notice at first, and praised his son after reading it.  Of course, he found out later.  However, when someone asked if his son would write a novel, his father ’ s face smiled and replied, “Gregory (his son ’ s name) sometimes does a little lame proofreading. ” Hemingway said this, and the people on the side laughed heartily.  To call plagiarism “lame proofreading ” is not a metaphor, it is hard to say, but I really admire Hemingway ’ s mental flexibility and language wisdom.  Aristotle said, "Parables are the sign of genius." Hemingway was indeed a genius. (From India)

Title: Ernest Hemingway: As long as one of us lives, the other lives forever in his heart.
Content: The novel is like an iceberg, only one eighth of which is on the surface of the water, and the rest is underwater.  Deleting more sentences and leaving more sentences underwater is enough to strengthen your novel.  This is Ernest Hemingway ’ s “theory of the iceberg ”, which he implemented in his novels. Today, 1940, For Whom the Bell Tolls is published.  Before publication, Hemingway revised the manuscript every day after finishing it, and did not leave the room for 96 consecutive hours.  He used iceberg theory to remove unnecessary sentences, and used symbols, pictures and ideas to navigate the story, resulting in this monumental work that was later adapted into a film and used by the college to teach literature.  Ernest Hemingway (Getty Images) The bell-ringing story in the field focuses on an attack by a guerrilla group during the Spanish Civil War in the summer of 1937.  The story is only four days long, focusing on the tension of the war and the appearance of human nature.  The protagonist, Robert Jordan, is an American professor who teaches Spanish. At the outbreak of the war, he joined the volunteer army and was ordered to go deep into the mountains to break through enemy lines, and the story begins when the protagonist enters the mountains, he tries to contact the guerrillas and cooperate with them to blow up the bridge.  For Whom the Bell Tolls: The Hemingway Library Edition (Scribner) Guerrilla Captain Pablo opposes the bridge, losing his fighting spirit and even stealing the detonator. Title: How to read Hemingway?
Content: Ernest Hemingway, a Nobel laureate and one of the most important of the 20th century, was born on July 21, 1899 in Illinois and wrote seven novels, six collections of short stories and two nonfiction books during his lifetime.  On the occasion of the birth of this author, which coincided with the thirteenth of July, we have suggestions for better reading of the works of this author.  Hemingway ’ s work is fluid, simple, and clear, but for many readers of literature, it may be difficult to begin reading Hemingway ’ s books.  Why read Hemingway?  Ernest Hemingway is an influential writer in the history of literature and fiction, his works have repeatedly won the most prestigious international literary awards such as Nobel and Pulitzer, this author employed a different kind of narrative description and caused many writers after him to borrow his own literary style.  Hemingway has named his literary style the Iceberg Theory, in this way of writing, fictional events are narrated like an iceberg floating in water, only one-eighth of which is visible, and the author includes only the information that is essential in the process and omits the rest of the information.  This technique created a tremendous change in storytelling, especially the writing of short stories, and it was a development that freed the stories from conventional chatter.  Hemingway ’ s works are included in the list of books of the century, books to read before death, and the best fiction books in history, highlighting the importance of this author.  What do we need to know?  One of the topics that helps to better understand Ernest Hemingway ’ s work is getting to know his personal life.  Much of what we read in his books is what he has turned from his personal life into a story.  At the age of 19, he volunteered for the First World War but was not allowed to fight because of poor eyesight, but Hemingway insisted on serving as an ambulance driver for the Red Cross.  He was wounded several times during the Chang, but his most significant injury is when he was wounded by mortar shell fragments and spent a long time in the hospital, a novel about this part of Hemingway ’ s life and the war.  Even the character of Catherine Barkley in this book is based on the nurse Hemingway fell in love with.  Hemingway also participated in World War II as a war correspondent, and several short stories are the result of this era.  The sun continues to blow, the Great River or along the river to the trees, each of which is somehow tied to the World War, and their heroes are survivors of the war and have many memories of these days.  But Hemingway ’ s most important masterpiece is a relic of his childhood, Hemingway ’ s father had a great interest in fishing, and this hobby was passed on to Ernest, a point that can be clearly seen in the famous and widely read story of The Old Man and the Sea.  But before the Old Man and the Sea, Hemingway had written about having and not having a fishing boat captain.  Another important point to know before reading Hemingway ’ s works is his political approach, he has written a lot in opposition to fascism and against dictatorship, both as a journalist and as a writer, sometimes even changing from a journalist to a social-political activist, who is this point in The Bell for, or who is this death knell?  It is a story of an American soldier in the Spanish Civil War fighting alongside groups against General Franco, which Hemingway did.  Perhaps the other thing that matters is that during the World War, Hemingway led a French group against the Nazis that was tried after the war for armed acts but was never proven guilty.  The political and social history of the world in the years of Hemingway's life, his personal life, as well as the knowledge of his contemporaries, such as Scott Fitzgerald, with whom he has written, are points that contribute to the understanding of his works.  Getting to know Hemingway ’ s contemporary writers helps to better understand the difference between him and his contemporaries.  Is it a classic?  To read Hemingway ’ s work, we must note that he is not a classic writer in his different style, he did not deal with the long margins and descriptions of classical literature, and his long novels are not immune.  He was interested in shorthand and engaging the audience with fiction, which is a feature of modern literature.  In general, Hemingway ’ s works are innovative and even among modern works have their own creativity, but the value of this author ’ s work has always been compared to classical works, and even classical enthusiasts have not been able to be indifferent to it.  In these works we have a happy and well-spoken writer, a writer who was in middle age with young people and was even close friends with a group of hippies.  Hemingway is a realistic writer, but he has always tried to maintain his sense of humor.  Where do we start?  To read Hemingway ’ s works, the first and most important suggestion is The Old Man and the Sea.  The book, translated by Najaf Daryabandari, was published in 222 pages by Kharazmi Publications.  The next book, Farewell to Arms, is again translated by Najaf Daryabendari, published by Amir Kabir Publications in 343 pages.  These two books are always on the list of works to be read or masterpieces of the 20th century.  If you are interested in short stories, you can also read Men Without Women, a collection of stories that have been published in various magazines by the author.  This book has been translated by Asadollah Amraei for publication of Horizon in 222 pages.  Even if you are interested in writing, Hemingway can be a good teacher and read his series of talks and learn very precise points.  The book The Last Interview and Other Conversations of Ernest Hemingway with a translation by Houshang Jirani has been published in 88 pages by Cheshmeh Publishing.  The final chapter of many critics considered Ernest Hemingway to be the greatest writer of the 20th century.  His stories are an exploration of real human life, suffering and the meaning of life.  The portrayal of human inner feelings is the most important characteristic of this author, which makes his works a read for every reader.  Who was Ernest Hemingway?  Ernest Hemingway was born on July 21, 1899 in Oak Park, Illinois.  His father, Clarence, was a doctor and his mother, Grace, was a piano and singing teacher.  Ernest spent the summers with his family in northern Michigan, where he discovered his passion for fishing.  After finishing high school, he worked for a while in Kansas City as a reporter for the Star Chronicle in 1917.  During World War I, he volunteered to serve in the army, but poor eyesight prevented him from doing so, instead serving as an ambulance driver for the Red Cross near the Italian front.  On July 8, 1918, he was injured and spent months in the hospital.  In 1925, his first collection of short stories, in our time, was published, which spoke well of his particular style.  His memoirs from that period were published after his death in 1964 as The Variable Eid.  Ernest Hemingway was an adventurer for most of his life.  From being wounded in Italy by 200 pieces of Austrian shrapnel during World War I, to taking part in the frontlines of the Spanish Civil War or touring the African wilderness, to fishing and hunting wildlife and living in Cuba.  He finally said goodbye to life with his hunting rifle.

Title: Hemingway: A typewriter in the trenches
Content: Hemingway was the spokesperson for “Lost Generation, ” Ernest Hemingway liked to be a war reporter, professional athlete, hunter or adventurer.  He considered writing to be little, but eventually became one of the greatest writers of the 20th century.  He won the Nobel Prize for Literature and influenced many writers after World War II.  Today, Hemingway is one of the emblems of the modern world.  He ended his life 50 years ago.  Ernest Hemingway was born in Oak Park, Illinois, North America in 1899.  Her father was a doctor and gave a good life to the family.  Ernest was playful in school and hated homework, but he was smart enough to get good grades.  Hemingway was drawn into journalism at the age of 18.  With a rebellious nature that never calmed down, his heart yearned for distant lands and found this “opportunity ” in war.  As an ambulance driver for the International Red Cross, he traveled to Europe in the last year of the Great War with American troops.  During the war, he felt the horror of death with flesh and skin.  Under Austrian bombardment, he suffered severe injuries and was hospitalized for several months.  At the hospital in Milan, more than 200 pieces of shrapnel were removed from his body, and he used to pull metal from his leg with the tip of a knife.  Hemingway was also a lover and was impatient with beautiful women.  He was married four times in his life, amidst dozens of love stories.  At the hospital, she fell madly in love with her nurse.  But a few months later, after the war ended, he returned to the United States and married another woman.  He was 22 years old and his first wife was 29.  A decent and kind woman, who "accidentally" had a good financial situation.  A spokesman for Hemingway ’ s Lost Generation went to Europe in 1921 with his young wife, and in Paris joined the ranks of modernist writers who had gathered in the “capital of modern art ”: Scott Fitzgerald, John dos Passos, Ezra Pound, and others.  Gertrude Stein called it the “Lost Generation. ”  The children of this generation lost all hope and faith in the muddy fields of war and they no longer believed and trusted in anything.  The moral lessons and moral values and the bragging of “bourgeois civilization ” were seen as a bunch of deceptive lies.  Hemingway, who had begun to write real reports and his first short stories, brought this anger and frustration to paper in a new tone.  His stories, full of vitality, infused the deep anger and frustration of this generation with vivid and effective expression.  “The Sun Still Rises ” was a vivid account of the story of this generation, seeking consolation that could not be found in foreign cities.  The novel A Farewell to Arms, published in 1928, clearly expressed this disillusionment.  This wasn ’ t an ordinary princeling.  Someone was talking about the war, who had been wounded by it and still had its shrapnel in his body.  “I had seen nothing sacred, and the things that were glorious had no honor, and the victims were like cattle and sheep in the Chicago slaughterhouse — if they had nothing to do with the carcasses but to bury them. ”  (Farewell to Arms, translation of Najaf Daryabandari) This was the look of the masses of those who lost the war anyway, and this was of course different from the look and expression of the elites and commanders, for whom the war was a "field of honor" and full of "blessings".  Ernest Hemingway was married four times — his second wife, Pauline Pfeiffer, can be seen in this photo, some critics point out that Hemingway ’ s participation in the war was not just an individual experience that influenced his literary work, but, more than that, the war took over his whole being and his mentality, gave him a “war-torn ” temperament and shaped his worldview.  Hemingway was constantly ready to fight and saw in everything a challenge to fight: on the battlefield, in the boxing ring, or in the bullfight.  The novel The Sun Still Rises, published in 1927, illustrates this view in a variety of colorful depictions and images.  In Death in the Afternoon, published in the form of a true memoir or travelogue in 1932, the bullfight is a metaphor for confronting death: standing face to face with death, gazing into its eyes, shivering with this horror / pleasure, mingling with it, and finally sinking into its black palate.  It has been said that Hemingway ’ s hobbies, fishing, from hunting wild animals to hunting women, were manifestations of this constant temptation of war and bullying.  Even writing was a big challenge for him, with special preparation and discipline to “fight ” it.  Some critics have said that he saw killing and being killed as the only natural form of human history, so much so that he believed that a "healthy and natural" man should die on the field, not in bed.  There has always been a man of struggle and action in Hemingway ’ s “Square. ”  not from the works of others, as he has said with pride, but from blood and sweat.  Will Durant has said that in few writers life experiences are so closely intertwined with literary endeavors.  Hemingway hated intellectual habits and debate.  He despised the intellectuals who, steeped in abstract discussions, had forgotten the principle of life; he called them cowards and cowards.  He was not a theorist and did not even consider himself a literary and literary writer, in the classical sense.  He once said, “I ’ m not going to compete with Tolstoy. ”  In his Nobel Prize speech (1954), Hemingway's style and language explained his style with the metaphor of an "iceberg": "I try to be like an iceberg, seven eighths of which are hidden under water and only one eighth of which is visible.  The more we remove from the body of the story, the stronger the iceberg becomes.  The power of the story lies in what the author knows but doesn ’ t reveal.  If he omits something because he doesn ’ t know, there ’ s a hole in the story. ”  The author knows all about his space and characters but only gives the reader the least necessary information.  In this precise, measured and compact style, most of the notes and explanations are eliminated, but they do not go away; the reader senses them and is affected with far greater intensity.  With the technique of "elimination" in both story structure and language, a pure and clear text is provided that has a direct and lightning effect.  The plot or plot is missing.  The tongue is compact, concise, dry, and without sentimental frills.  Short sentences convey only a thin surface and leave the rest to the reader ’ s intelligence.  This is how the joy of reading the story is multiplied by the joy of discovery.  Hemingway wrote from real, live experiences.  (He even boasted that he had killed dozens of people in the war!)  It was the only objective language, unadorned and transparent, that could convey vivid experiences directly and directly, away from the repetitive pronouncements and fluttering sentimental adjectives.  Hemingway ’ s best work comes from personal tensions and struggles.  From a man ’ s quarrel with a giant fish, he presented one of the most fascinating stories of the 20th century.  It ’ s a true story with ancient myths.  All kinds of interpretations and interpretations have been published about "The Old Man and the Sea".  Hemingway ’ s own explanation is probably the best: “I have shown a true old man against a true fish in a true sea! ”  That too, true or false, had its origin in life.  Hemingway boasted that he once caught a 355-kilogram fish.  In the world of politics, Hemingway cannot be considered a “committed ” writer, even though he was“ engaged ” with political adventures all his life.  (His file on the FBI is thousands of pages!)  He was more or less present in all the important events of his time, a correspondent in the two world wars, and a little more active in the Spanish Civil War.  After all, he was a terrible writer.  The painful experience of war and the constant presence of death had engulfed his soul, infecting it with bitterness and deadly pessimism.  For the rest of his life, he looked at every struggle with ridicule and “cynicism ”.  Politics required a minimum of optimism and idealism, whereas Hemingway only “believed ” in himself and held the highest value in being“ loyal ” to himself.  Perhaps, following Nietzsche, without engaging himself with philosophical deliberations, he believed in individual power and “the will to power. ”  He had an iron fist, and he held his hand.  He had no weakness, no weakness, no weakness.  (He said, “Man can be destroyed, but he cannot be defeated. ”)  He knew the people and the people of both worlds. Content: In the 1920s, the Treaty of Versailles proclaimed the end of World War I, Hitler in Europe joined the Nazi Party, and the Communist Party of China rose in the East.  And the United States introduced a national prohibition of alcohol, so a group of American "expats" came to Paris, free and exile in various cafes and bars. Hemingway also moved to the old city as a reporter in 1921, beginning his penniless, but indulgent days.  A hundred years later, Chen Jung-bin and the audience of the Blue Bird House look back at the impression of Paris that was reflected in Hemingway ’ s words.  The Old Man and the Sea was born on an alcohol-soaked beach in Cuba; The War Bell is an interview from the Spanish Civil War; The Dawn of Truth records the memories of a trip to Africa with his fourth wife, Mary, and Hemingway, born in Oak Park, Illinois, USA.  At the age of 21, he worked as a reporter for the Toronto Star in Canada, became a special correspondent in Europe the next year, and moved to Paris to spend his 20 generations, nearly a decade of his golden years.  Ernest Hemingway in World War I. When he first arrived in Paris, he stayed in a small hotel and wrote in the Toronto Star: “PARIS — Paris in the winter is rainy, cold, beautiful and cheap. ”  It is also noisy, jostling, crowded and cheap.  It is anything you want — and cheap. ” — Living on $1,000 a Year in Paris Describes the bankruptcy of Europe at the end of World War I, the relative advantage of the dollar, and the ability to spend a thousand dollars in Paris for a year.  Although this article is published in the newspaper, the writing and rhyme are poetic.  “We ate well and cheaply and drank well and cheaply and slept well and warm together and love each other. ”  After graduating from high school, Hemingway worked as a reporter for the Kansas City Star, and his entire writing career was inextricably linked to journalistic writing.  “From Hemingway ’ s early writings, the Kansas Star newspaper ’ s“ style sheet ” for the rookie reporter shaped his unique style of writing, and the rules in the guide were as many as 110, and the first paragraph was indeed Hemingway ’ s rule: write short sentences.  The first paragraph is shorter.  Write articles in vivid English.  The influence of the rookie reporter period on his career also corresponds to the iceberg theory he proposed in 1932: "Prose is like architecture, not interior decoration, and the Baroque era is over... If you have enough understanding of what you are describing and write well enough, even if you write only one-eighth of the text, you can let the reader fully grasp the scene, plot and character description that he wants to express." Hemingway often uses a concise style to bury clues in the details or background, so that it is connected with emotional intimacy.  Paris was not only the place where Hemingway worked as a journalist, but also the beginning of his literary career.  The first two books, Three Stories & Ten Poems, and a collection of short stories, in our time, were published here.  Ernest Hemingway wrote many notes about his life and literary work in the 1920s. Two boxes were left in the basement of the Ritz Hotel in Paris, and when he returned to Paris in 1957, he opened these dusty old memories, namely, "The Feast on the Move".  This prose memoir of Paris also later became a guide for people on their pilgrimage journey, following Hemingway for a drink, order a cup of coffee at the Lilac Café, borrow a book at Shakespeare ’ s Bookstore on the Rue d ’ Odeon, and then take a walk in Luxembourg Park.  “If you are lucky enough to have lived in Paris as a young man, then wherever you go for the rest of your life it stays with you, for Paris is a movable feast. ” — Ernest Hemingway A moving feast.  Shakespeare Bookstore (Photo / Courtesy of Blue Bird) Mr. Chen then pointed out on the map several places where Hemingway often stopped in Paris. First came to the Shakespeare Bookstore, which is also like a library, which can rent books at affordable prices, and also provides mail collection services, which is suitable for young and poor boy Hemingway.  The owner of the bookstore, Shelville Beach, is also an American, and in her autobiography, Shakespeare's Bookstore, there is a chapter entitled "The Best Customer Hemingway".  In his translation of the book, Mr. Chen found hundreds of references to Hemingway, and the description of his affinity showed their deep and warm friendship at the time.  At the end of World War II, Hemingway returns to Paris with the Americans and meets Chevelle again.  There are still a lot of gun battles in the theater street, and we ’ ve had enough.  One day a jeep pulled into the street and stopped at the door of my bookstore.  I heard a low voice shouting, “Chevy! ” and it spread all over the street.  Edhiena cried, "It's Hemingway! It's Hemingway!" I rushed downstairs and hit the oncoming Hemingway.  He picked me up in circles and kissed me, and the people at the window of the street cheered … He asked if there was anything else I could do, and I said if I could get rid of the Nazi snipers on the roof of the street, especially those on Edsieena ’ s roof.  He called his buddies out of their jeeps, took them all to the roof, and then came the last gunfight on Theater Street.  Hemingway got down with his men and drove off in the jeep — next, Hemingway said, to the wine cellar at the Ritz.  The Lilac Garden Cafe (Photo / Courtesy of the Blue Bird House) The Lilac Garden on the Boulevard Montparnasse is the place where the artistic and cultural trends of Paris in the 1920s met and collided, and where Fitzgerald, Zola, Cezanne and Picasso all stopped.  “I sat in the corner writing with my notebook, and the afternoon sun was on my shoulders.  The waiter took me a cup of hot cream coffee (café crème), and I drank half of it after cooling, and the other half was on the table while I was writing.  When I stopped writing, I really didn ’ t want to leave the river where the trout could be seen in the pool. ” — Chen Jung-bin, author of “Feast on the Move, ” mentioned this text, poetically describing the process of creating the novel“ Our Time ” in Lilac Garden, and the river where the trout can be seen is the title of the book, “The Big Twin Heart River. ”  A Good Café on the Place St.-Michel "A girl walks into a cafe and sits alone at a table by the window.  She was beautiful, and her face was as fresh as a new coin — if only coins could be minted with silky muscles and rain-washed skin.  Her hair was as dark as the wings of a raven, cut into a blade, and covered her face obliquely.  I stared at her, and she disturbed my thoughts and made me very excited.  I wanted to put her in my novel or something, but she was sitting where she could see the street and the entrance to the cafe, so I knew she was waiting for someone.  So I continued to write.  The story seemed to unfold automatically, and my pen managed to keep up with it.  I ordered another glass of St. James ’ s brandy.  Whenever I raised my head or sharpened the pencil with a sharpener, I would look at the girl and let the curly scraps fall into the saucer under the glass. "  "I see you, my beauty, now you belong to me, no matter who you are waiting for, and no matter whether I can see you again in the future," I thought.  You belong to me, and all Paris belongs to me, and I belong to this notebook and this pencil.  From this Paris memoir, Teacher Chen Jung-bin led us to read this famous article. Reading this text, we followed Hemingway ’ s eyes, met the girl who distracted him in a cafe next to the square, took control between the mind and the pen, and then sat in the whole Paris.  Hemingway and Fitzgerald Fitzgerald (Photo / Courtesy of Blue Bird) Hemingway and artists from all walks of life in Paris, and Fitzgerald also met here, they first met at Dingo American Bar, and each other's affirmation is extremely sincere.  Hemingway left such a comment on Fitzgerald in "The Moving Feast": After reading "The Tycoon", he felt that no matter what outrageous things Fitzgerald did, he had to treat it as if Fitzgerald was sick, and he had to try to help him from the standpoint of a friend, "because, if he could write such a book, he could write a better book." This is probably the biggest compliment Hemingway has ever given to any of his peers.  Fitzgerald also gave Hemingway "He's the real thing." Title: Hemingway's Myth
Content: In 1953, Hemingway was sitting at a dinner table at his camp in Kenya, writing. (NARA, Photographer, Look Magazine) Anyone familiar with American literature and literary criticism should know the iceberg talk about literary creation.  The author of this statement is the famous American writer and Nobel Prize winner Ernest Hemingway.  The main point is that if a writer has a mind about what he wants to write, he can omit something he knows when he creates, and the reader will feel those omissions because the author is writing true.  It is like an iceberg that looks magnificent as it moves in the sea, but in fact only one-eighth of it is out of the water, and the invisible part is more and more real.  In the theory of ancient Chinese poetry creation, there is a saying of "artistic conception", emphasizing the scenes and emotions depicted through the works, stimulating the imagination of the readers, and leaving them a space for full reflection and play.  This is synonymous with the "iceberg theory", but Hemingway emphasized the authenticity of the work, aiming to criticize some writers who seemed to him to be quite incompetent, who simply "omitted something because they did not understand".  Hemingway ’ s “iceberg talk ” actually interprets his own creative style, which is to omit everything he thinks is optional in his writing, and to be as simple and implicit as possible.  This creative style of Hemingway is indeed unique and has had a profound impact, some even said: Hemingway with no one has the courage, "English attached to the literature of the hair cut clean." But what interests me is that he uses the "iceberg" as a metaphor.  This analogy is really good.  What people usually use as metaphors are some common things, such as peach blossoms in "face like peach blossoms" and torches in "eyes like torches". How many people have seen an iceberg?  Three years ago, I went to Alaska to visit, and all I saw was a large piece of ice floe on the sea surface, real sea icebergs, probably only in the South Pole and Arctic areas where ordinary people are difficult to set foot.  However, this parable is also very relevant and can make people understand God.  What you can read in a good work is certainly brilliant, like the magnificence of an iceberg above the surface of the water, but what it contains can be much wider and deeper than the literal meaning, like a much larger body of mountain undersea support.  Without the presence of seven eighths below, there is no beauty at the top.  In the book of Revelation, there is a great deal to be said about the use of metaphors.  He said that the metaphor contains two aspects that are opposite and complementary, and the things that are compared must be the same, otherwise they cannot be joined together; but at the same time, they must be different, otherwise they cannot be distinguished.  As for the interaction between the two, the greater the difference, the more the same thing will be baked; the more open it will be, the more unexpected it will be, the more novel the metaphor will be, and the better the effect will be.  According to the theory of Qian Zhongshu, Hemingway uses the iceberg as a metaphor, and the things that belong to it are "very divided", and it has indeed produced a surprising winning effect, so it is unforgettable.  There are many other examples of this in the metaphor Hemingway has used.  After Hemingway became famous, he often compared himself with other writers, and was quite conceited, many writers he could not see, and only Shakespeare and Tolstoy were really admired.  He did not know this, but used boxing as a metaphor.  He said that he did not want to play Dostoyevsky in the first game, because he knew that Dostoyevsky was almost as good as he was, so he chose to play with Turgenev first because he felt he could play with him.  Then try Maupassant again, although it is difficult, but also can beat him; as for Henry James, he said, "As soon as I catch me, I press him, and immediately give him a blow where he has no meat, so tell the referee to stop the game." Hemingway's words, you can see his confidence.  About him and Cervantes who is stronger, he has a different saying, he believes that 20 rounds of war, you can beat the other side of the fart, but also admitted that Mr. Cervantes is very shrewd, while playing and learning, maybe the second game he will lose to the other side.  In Hemingway ’ s eyes, Shakespeare is the champion who can ’ t beat.  And speaking of Tolstoy, whom he equally admired, he said something different.  He said that if he played six rounds with Tolstoy, the opponent would not want to hit him, but he would be beaten enough, but if he played 20 rounds with Tolstoy, he would be knocked off the ear.  He also said that if he could live to sixty, he might defeat Tolstoy.  I guess Hemingway is probably trying to say that some of his works can win Tolstoy, but in general, they can ’ t talk about each other, unless he can create more good works in the future (need to live longer).  What kind of metaphor is used is often related to the personality and creation style of the user.  Pushkin is an emotional romantic poet, in his short life, wrote many beautiful people's poems.  I noticed that Pushkin often compared his beloved poetry to a harp.  So I thought, it must be because this ancient instrument can play a very moving tune, like a poem to move the heart.  Then because of the occasional experience, I have a new feeling about it.  That time was a trip to the Rocky Mountains, staying at the Castle Hotel by Lake Louise.  In the afternoon, a woman dressed like a classical beauty in a long skirt played the harp in the hotel's glittering lobby. Some of the hotel's guests sat, some stood, and listened.  It was at this moment that I suddenly understood why Pushkin used the harp as a metaphor for poetry, because the scenes and atmosphere in the lobby were so romantic.  Unlike Hemingway, his work has created many images of tough men, and he himself loves tough and exciting activities such as bullfighting, horse racing, boxing and hunting, so it is not surprising that he uses boxing as a metaphor.  However, not all people can use the analogy of the things that are "very divided" as Mr. Qian Zhongshu said.  In other words, the winning or losing of a boxing match and the level of a writer were originally two things that could not be fought with eight poles, but Hemingway "closed" them.  The Nobel laureate often had this idea.  His son once copied Turgenev's work and wrote a novel, which Hemingway did not notice at first, and praised his son after reading it.  Of course, he found out later.  However, when someone asked if his son would write a novel, his father ’ s face smiled and replied, “Gregory (his son ’ s name) sometimes does a little lame proofreading. ” Hemingway said this, and the people on the side laughed heartily.  To call plagiarism “lame proofreading ” is not a metaphor, it is hard to say, but I really admire Hemingway ’ s mental flexibility and language wisdom.  Aristotle said, "Parables are the sign of genius." Hemingway was indeed a genius. (From India)

Title: Ernest Hemingway: As long as one of us lives, the other lives forever in his heart.
Content: The novel is like an iceberg, only one eighth of which is on the surface of the water, and the rest is underwater.  Deleting more sentences and leaving more sentences underwater is enough to strengthen your novel.  This is Ernest Hemingway ’ s “theory of the iceberg ”, which he implemented in his novels. Today, 1940, For Whom the Bell Tolls is published.  Before publication, Hemingway revised the manuscript every day after finishing it, and did not leave the room for 96 consecutive hours.  He used iceberg theory to remove unnecessary sentences, and used symbols, pictures and ideas to navigate the story, resulting in this monumental work that was later adapted into a film and used by the college to teach literature.  Ernest Hemingway (Getty Images) The bell-ringing story in the field focuses on an attack by a guerrilla group during the Spanish Civil War in the summer of 1937.  The story is only four days long, focusing on the tension of the war and the appearance of human nature.  The protagonist, Robert Jordan, is an American professor who teaches Spanish. At the outbreak of the war, he joined the volunteer army and was ordered to go deep into the mountains to break through enemy lines, and the story begins when the protagonist enters the mountains, he tries to contact the guerrillas and cooperate with them to blow up the bridge.  For Whom the Bell Tolls: The Hemingway Library Edition (Scribner) Guerrilla Captain Pablo opposes the bridge, losing his fighting spirit and even stealing the detonator.  Robert manages to gain support from the rest of the team, isolating the captain and planning to blow up the bridge.  Robert takes in Maria, a girl who has been abused and enslaved by the enemy, and falls in love with her.  After stealing the horses from the enemy line, the two walked hand in hand, and he imagined that after the war was over, he would return to the United States to teach, and the two would end up together.  But after a while, he shot and killed one of the other soldiers, and while he did not get any information from the enemy, he read a home letter, which made him feel the cruelty of the war.  In the early hours of the last day, the few remaining teams set out for the bridge, and due to the small number of people and the behavior of the captain, several people had to risk their lives.  In the final scene, Robert and his companions blow the bridge in mid-air with explosives, but when he runs away on horseback in the direction of Maria, he is unfortunately shot and fell, his left leg is broken, and he can no longer escape from the enemy's attack.  At the end of his life, he said to Mary, “As long as one of us lives, the other will live in his heart forever. ”  In 1943, Battlefield Bell was transformed into a film (file picture) The tragic color of "tough man" Hemingway's novels often appear as "tough man", meaning that he has a very strong will and a strong and unyielding spirit.  When the Nobel Prize for Literature was awarded to him, he said that he "has a kind of man who likes to take risks" and vowed not to bow down and fight to the end when faced with the pressure of fate.  The old fisherman in The Old Man and the Sea said, “Man can be destroyed, but he cannot be defeated. ”  But when we talk about fate and rebellion, we often talk about tragedy, and the end of Battlefield Bell is clearly tragic.  [The Old Man and the Sea] Hemingway's many novels have been exposed hundreds of wrong scholars: The fault is not in the spirit of his ancient Greek tragedy, it is that when people face the choice of fate, they know that they have to bear a heavy price and still struggle to insist on their own choices, and finally they really want to meet the tragic consequences.  It may be against fate, it may be against power, and it ends tragically.  In The Birth of Tragedy, Nietzsche pointed out that the ancient Greek tragedy was the manifestation of the god of wine, freed from the "self", disordered and led to a carnival, chanting that people "believe in eternal life".
