Title: How to read Hemingway?
Content: Ernest Hemingway, a Nobel laureate and one of the most important of the 20th century, was born on July 21, 1899 in Illinois and wrote seven novels, six collections of short stories and two nonfiction books during his lifetime.  On the occasion of the birth of this author, which coincided with the thirteenth of July, we have suggestions for better reading of the works of this author.  Hemingway ’ s work is fluid, simple, and clear, but for many readers of literature, it may be difficult to begin reading Hemingway ’ s books.  Why read Hemingway?  Ernest Hemingway is an influential writer in the history of literature and fiction, his works have repeatedly won the most prestigious international literary awards such as Nobel and Pulitzer, this author employed a different kind of narrative description and caused many writers after him to borrow his own literary style.  Hemingway has named his literary style the Iceberg Theory, in this way of writing, fictional events are narrated like an iceberg floating in water, only one-eighth of which is visible, and the author includes only the information that is essential in the process and omits the rest of the information.  This technique created a tremendous change in storytelling, especially the writing of short stories, and it was a development that freed the stories from conventional chatter.  Hemingway ’ s works are included in the list of books of the century, books to read before death, and the best fiction books in history, highlighting the importance of this author.  What do we need to know?  One of the topics that helps to better understand Ernest Hemingway ’ s work is getting to know his personal life.  Much of what we read in his books is what he has turned from his personal life into a story.  At the age of 19, he volunteered for the First World War but was not allowed to fight because of poor eyesight, but Hemingway insisted on serving as an ambulance driver for the Red Cross.  He was wounded several times during the Chang, but his most significant injury is when he was wounded by mortar shell fragments and spent a long time in the hospital, a novel about this part of Hemingway ’ s life and the war.  Even the character of Catherine Barkley in this book is based on the nurse Hemingway fell in love with.  Hemingway also participated in World War II as a war correspondent, and several short stories are the result of this era.  The sun continues to blow, the Great River or along the river to the trees, each of which is somehow tied to the World War, and their heroes are survivors of the war and have many memories of these days.  But Hemingway ’ s most important masterpiece is a relic of his childhood, Hemingway ’ s father had a great interest in fishing, and this hobby was passed on to Ernest, a point that can be clearly seen in the famous and widely read story of The Old Man and the Sea.  But before the Old Man and the Sea, Hemingway had written about having and not having a fishing boat captain.  Another important point to know before reading Hemingway ’ s works is his political approach, he has written a lot in opposition to fascism and against dictatorship, both as a journalist and as a writer, sometimes even changing from a journalist to a social-political activist, who is this point in The Bell for, or who is this death knell?  It is a story of an American soldier in the Spanish Civil War fighting alongside groups against General Franco, which Hemingway did.  Perhaps the other thing that matters is that during the World War, Hemingway led a French group against the Nazis that was tried after the war for armed acts but was never proven guilty.  The political and social history of the world in the years of Hemingway's life, his personal life, as well as the knowledge of his contemporaries, such as Scott Fitzgerald, with whom he has written, are points that contribute to the understanding of his works.  Getting to know Hemingway ’ s contemporary writers helps to better understand the difference between him and his contemporaries.  Is it a classic?  To read Hemingway ’ s work, we must note that he is not a classic writer in his different style, he did not deal with the long margins and descriptions of classical literature, and his long novels are not immune.  He was interested in shorthand and engaging the audience with fiction, which is a feature of modern literature.  In general, Hemingway ’ s works are innovative and even among modern works have their own creativity, but the value of this author ’ s work has always been compared to classical works, and even classical enthusiasts have not been able to be indifferent to it.  In these works we have a happy and well-spoken writer, a writer who was in middle age with young people and was even close friends with a group of hippies.  Hemingway is a realistic writer, but he has always tried to maintain his sense of humor.  Where do we start?  To read Hemingway ’ s works, the first and most important suggestion is The Old Man and the Sea.  The book, translated by Najaf Daryabandari, was published in 222 pages by Kharazmi Publications.  The next book, Farewell to Arms, is again translated by Najaf Daryabendari, published by Amir Kabir Publications in 343 pages.  These two books are always on the list of works to be read or masterpieces of the 20th century.  If you are interested in short stories, you can also read Men Without Women, a collection of stories that have been published in various magazines by the author.  This book has been translated by Asadollah Amraei for publication of Horizon in 222 pages.  Even if you are interested in writing, Hemingway can be a good teacher and read his series of talks and learn very precise points.  The book The Last Interview and Other Conversations of Ernest Hemingway with a translation by Houshang Jirani has been published in 88 pages by Cheshmeh Publishing.  The final chapter of many critics considered Ernest Hemingway to be the greatest writer of the 20th century.  His stories are an exploration of real human life, suffering and the meaning of life.  The portrayal of human inner feelings is the most important characteristic of this author, which makes his works a read for every reader.  Who was Ernest Hemingway?  Ernest Hemingway was born on July 21, 1899 in Oak Park, Illinois.  His father, Clarence, was a doctor and his mother, Grace, was a piano and singing teacher.  Ernest spent the summers with his family in northern Michigan, where he discovered his passion for fishing.  After finishing high school, he worked for a while in Kansas City as a reporter for the Star Chronicle in 1917.  During World War I, he volunteered to serve in the army, but poor eyesight prevented him from doing so, instead serving as an ambulance driver for the Red Cross near the Italian front.  On July 8, 1918, he was injured and spent months in the hospital.  In 1925, his first collection of short stories, in our time, was published, which spoke well of his particular style.  His memoirs from that period were published after his death in 1964 as The Variable Eid.  Ernest Hemingway was an adventurer for most of his life.  From being wounded in Italy by 200 pieces of Austrian shrapnel during World War I, to taking part in the frontlines of the Spanish Civil War or touring the African wilderness, to fishing and hunting wildlife and living in Cuba.  He finally said goodbye to life with his hunting rifle.

Unlike some great storytellers, who only a specific audience of fiction is willing to read their stories, Hemingway ’ s works are pleasant for a specific and general audience. passages.title: China's "artificial sun" record
passages.passage: China's artificial sun has set a new record in its quest for fusion energy.  While similar efforts are underway in the United States, Europe, Russia and South Korea, the artificial sun improved its previous record by five times.  According to state media, China has reached another milestone in its quest to realize a fusion reactor, and one of its artificial suns has managed to maintain extreme temperatures several times higher than its previous record.  State news agency Xinhua reported that the Tokamak Advanced Experimental Superconductor (EAST) at a facility in the eastern city of Hefei maintained a plasma temperature of 120 million degrees Celsius for 101 seconds.  The report said the artificial sun also managed to maintain a temperature of 160 million degrees Celsius for 20 seconds.  Last year, EAST achieved a record 100 million degrees Celsius of plasma temperature for 20 seconds.  The experiment means that Chinese scientists have managed to maintain extremely high temperatures up to five times higher than previous experiments.  Another Chinese artificial sun project in Chengdu, the Tokamak HL-2m device, maintained temperatures of 150 million degrees Celsius for up to 10 seconds in a test late last year.  The construction and development of these artificial suns is part of China ’ s effort to reach fusion reactors that will revive hopes for clean and unlimited energy.  But there are many challenges that need to be overcome in the decades-long effort of the world ’ s scientists.  Similar efforts are underway in the United States, Europe, Russia and South Korea.  China is also one of the 35 countries involved in the International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER) project in France.  It is difficult to directly compare these types of experiments in different countries, because the devices are designed differently.  These facilities are called “artificial suns ” because they aim to replicate nuclear fusion reactions that power the sun at 15 million degrees Celsius.  When two atoms reach the fusion point, they release a large amount of energy.  To do this on Earth, scientists need to be able to maintain high temperatures for long periods of time.  Despite the advances made, fusion reactors are still a long way from being operational.  Song Yuntao, director of the Institute of Plasma Physics of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, said the latest results are a major breakthrough for physics and engineering in China.  The success of the test is the foundation for the construction of a nuclear fusion energy station in China.  China joined the ITER project in 2003 and at that time it was reported as an opportunity for its scientists to expand their expertise and gain an opportunity to emerge in the international scientific community.  The project in southern France has been repeatedly delayed, with the country ’ s latest plasma production target set for 2025.  The European Union has pledged $6.8 billion in new funding to the project in February.  Also, China National Nuclear Corporation will install the main equipment "ITER".  End of message.

passages.title: MEPhI told about the prospects of the artificial sun of China
passages.passage: In 2020, Chinese scientists will launch a new experimental fusion reactor HL-2M as part of the EAST project.  Such installations are sometimes called "artificial Sun" - they undergo the same processes as in the core of our star.  About the prospects of the Chinese project and in general about the technology of thermonuclear fusion "360" talked with Professor George Tikhomirov - Deputy Director of the Institute of Nuclear Physics and Technology of NRNU MEPhI.  The head of the Southwest Institute of Physics, Duan Xuzhu, previously said that the HL-2M reactor will be able to heat the plasma to a temperature above 200 million degrees Celsius.  The previous record was also set in China: a year ago in another experimental tokamak EAST - HT-7U - the peak temperature was 100 million degrees.  Tokamak HT-7U project EAST Tokamak is an abbreviation of "toroidal chamber with magnetic coils".  The name was invented by Soviet physicists in the 1950s, at the same time the first experiments were carried out to retain heated plasma with the help of powerful magnets.  Thermonuclear reactions are constantly on the Sun.  In the core, whose temperature reaches 15 million degrees Celsius, hydrogen is converted into helium.  A huge amount of energy is released.  To recreate the process on Earth, it is necessary to heat the hydrogen isotopes deuterium and tritium to a temperature above 100 million degrees Celsius.  At this point, the gas becomes plasma.  Such temperatures are needed to achieve a higher density of energy release than on the Sun, Tikhomirov explained.  The sun is very large, and therefore the energy it gives is enough for everyone.  And on Earth, we create conditions to a lesser extent.  If the conditions are close to solar, it does not allow us to use them for practical needs.  Georgy Tikhomirov Deputy Director of the Institute of Nuclear Physics and Technology of the National Research Nuclear University MEPhI In addition, for a functional thermonuclear reactor (which would give more energy than spent) it is necessary to hold the plasma inside the tokamak for a long time and obtain high-density plasma.  According to Tikhomirov, the Chinese installation HL-2M “in some respects will surpass the existing ones, ” but“ there is no breakthrough in this. ”  The deputy director of the Institute of Nuclear Physics and Technology recalled that the largest thermonuclear reactor in the world, ITER, is being built at the Cadarache Research Center in France.  This international project involves the EU, Japan, Russia, the United States, China, India and South Korea.  The reactor, which is planned to be completed by 2025, the Chinese “can not surpass ”, the professor is sure.  Most likely, they will create some compact small installation, where they will achieve good plasma parameters.  But there will be no breakthrough in energy.  Georgy Tikhomirov, deputy director of the Institute of Nuclear Physics and Technology of the National Research Nuclear University MEPhI, added that in Russia thermonuclear research "is developing in various directions."  “We will soon launch the T-15, our tokamak, there are other installations.  We are also part of the ITER program.  This topic is known, and we are not inferior to the Chinese here, ” Tikhomirov said.  The professor noted that the launch of a thermonuclear power plant has great prospects, because the fuel that can be used is deuterium "very much in the oceans."

passages.title: Atomic energy
passages.passage: Over the past 20 years, the amount of clean energy has doubled.  This energy is obtained from environmentally friendly sources - hydroelectric, nuclear, solar, wind, geothermal, tidal, biomass energy.  However, its share in the total amount of energy produced remained the same and even decreased slightly.  The fossil fuel industry is growing faster than the clean energy industry.  Many poor countries still use wood, manure and coal as their primary fuel.  The share of alternative renewable sources over the past 20 years has increased to almost 10% in 2018, and nuclear power plants, on the contrary, were closed.  And this despite the fact that solar and wind energy is unstable, it can be received only 10-30% of the time, when the sun is shining enough and the wind blows.  And hospitals, homes, cities and factories need energy all the time.  The United Nations Intergovernmental Committee on Climate Change (IPCC) has studied the CO2 content of all fuels.  Nuclear energy is one of the most environmentally friendly.  At the same time, the nuclear power plant can be used 92% of the time.  So why are we so afraid of nuclear power plants?  Nuclear energy seems like a good solution in the fight against climate change.  But there is one big problem – people don ’ t like it.  According to a 2014 Ipsos survey, nuclear power is one of the least popular.  Only 28% of respondents preferred nuclear power.  Even people are better at oil (30%).  Most people trust solar (85%) and wind energy (78%).  The fear of nuclear power is linked to three factors – the possibility of leakage, the disposal of waste and the association with nuclear weapons.  But it is difficult to make nuclear energy even safer than it is now.  According to a study conducted by one of the largest medical journals Lancet, nuclear energy is the safest among all other sources of energy.  It is safer than wind turbines and solar panels.  After reviewing data on the Fukushima and Chernobyl accidents, the WHO found that a large proportion of the damage was caused by panic.  The UN has also conducted comprehensive studies of the Chernobyl disaster.  The explosion at the Chernobyl nuclear power plant is the worst nuclear accident of all that happened.  As a result, 28 people died from acute radiation syndrome and another 15 people died over the next 25 years from thyroid cancer.  16,000 people became ill with thyroid cancer after Chernobyl, and it is estimated that 160 of them will die from this type of cancer.  The Fukushima nuclear disaster ranks second in severity.  The radiation emission was much smaller than that of Chernobyl.  There are no deaths from radiation after Fukushima.  Fifteen thousand people were killed, who were dragged out of nursing homes and hospitals.  They received a large dose of radiation just because they were moved a long distance.  In many ways, this was the result of a general panic.  For a person living in a big city, such as London, Berlin or New York, the risk of mortality increases by 2.8% from air pollution alone.  For those who live near smokers – by 1.7%.  For the liquidators of the Chernobyl accident, who received a dose of radiation of 250 millisieverts, it increased by only 1%.  By comparison, fuel energy creates uncontrolled waste in the form of greenhouse gas emissions, which kills 7 million people a year.  Therefore, the reduction of fuel energy in favor of nuclear energy has already saved the lives of 1.8 million people.  What about the waste?  Nuclear waste, as it turned out, is not so much.  If you take nuclear waste from the entire history of the United States and fill a football stadium with it, their height will be only 6 m. The waste is stored in special isolated containers, and they are constantly monitored.  In addition, development is underway to use nuclear waste as fuel.  It is the same with nuclear weapons.  There are no examples of countries with nuclear industry suddenly starting to develop nuclear weapons.  In fact, the opposite is happening.  It turns out that the only known way to get rid of a large number of nuclear weapons is to use plutonium from warheads as fuel for nuclear power plants.  Over the next 50 years, humanity will consume more energy than has been consumed in all previous history.  Earlier forecasts about the growth rate of energy consumption and the development of new energy technologies did not materialize: the level of consumption is growing much faster, and new energy sources will work on an industrial scale and at competitive prices not earlier than 2030.  The problem of the shortage of fossil energy resources is becoming more acute.  The capacity to build new hydropower plants is also very limited.  Do not forget about the fight against the “greenhouse effect ”, which imposes restrictions on the burning of oil, gas and coal in thermal power plants.  The solution to the problem can be the active development of nuclear energy, one of the youngest and fastest growing sectors of the global economy.  An increasing number of countries today come to the need to start the development of a peaceful atom.  The use of nuclear power may prove to be one of the solutions to these pressing problems, however unlikely it may seem.  But for this, the methods of its application need to be reviewed.  At the heart of the production of atomic energy is the force that holds the parts of the atom together.  If an atom is unstable, it will tend to move to a more stable state by splitting.  The instability of the atom can be natural or caused by the addition of additional neutrons to the nucleus.  When the atom becomes more stable and ejects particles, a huge amount of energy is released, which in a closed system can be used to generate enough heat to propel the turbine.  Radiation, which is often misrepresented, occurs for the most part due to natural causes.  Let ’ s see what the advantages of nuclear power are: 1 kg of uranium can produce 90,000 times more energy than 1 kg of coal.  Modern technologies make it possible to switch to a closed fuel cycle, which involves the repeated use of fuel products and the minimization of waste.  Every year, nuclear power plants in Europe avoid the emission of 700 million tons of CO2.  One job in the construction of nuclear power plants creates more than 10 jobs in related industries.  The development of nuclear energy contributes to the growth of scientific research and intellectual potential of the country.  According to the IAEA directory published in 2019, 98 nuclear reactors operated in the United States in 2018, 58 in France, 46 in China, 39 in Japan, 38 in Russia, 24 in the Republic of Korea, 22 in India, 19 in Canada, and 15 in the United Kingdom and Ukraine.  The total generating capacity of the nuclear power plant is over 380 GW.  A nuclear power plant is a complex of necessary systems, devices, equipment and structures designed to generate electricity by using the heat released in a nuclear reactor as a result of a controlled fission chain reaction of the nuclei of heavy elements (mainly uranium-233, uranium-235, plutonium-239).  The heat generated in the core of the nuclear reactor is transferred (directly or through an intermediate coolant) to the working medium (mainly water vapor), which drives steam turbines with turbogenerators, where the mechanical energy of the steam is converted into electrical energy.  Then the electricity through the wires goes to consumers.  As heat carriers, ordinary and heavy water, water vapor, liquid metals, organic liquids, some gases, for example, helium or carbon dioxide, are used.  The coolant circulates through sealed pipelines, which, in combination with circulation pumps, form a so-called reactor circuit or loop.  The circuits through which the coolant circulates are always closed to avoid leakage of radioactivity, their number is determined mainly by the type of nuclear reactor, as well as the properties of the working fluid and coolant.  Nuclear power plants can have single-circuit, double-circuit and three-circuit circuit of heat carrier operation.  Single-circuit circuit is used at nuclear power plants with channel-type reactors.  In such nuclear power plants, the coolant is also a working fluid.  In them, the boiling reactor itself is a steam generator, so the entire circuit is radioactive.  It's surrounded by biological defenses.  Two-circuit circuit circuit is used at nuclear power plants with water-water reactors.  In such nuclear power plants, water is supplied under pressure to the reactor core, which is heated.  Heat carrier energy is used in steam generator to form saturated steam.  The first circuit is radioactive and is surrounded by biological protection, except when inert gas is used as heat carrier.  The second circuit is usually radiation-safe, since the working fluid and coolant of the first circuit do not touch.  Three-circuit circuit circuit is used at nuclear power plants with fast neutron reactors with sodium coolant.  To exclude contact of radioactive sodium with water, a second circuit with non-radioactive sodium is constructed.  Thus, the scheme turns out to be three-circuit.  The peculiarity of nuclear power plants with a fast neutron reactor is that simultaneously with the generation of electrical and thermal energy, they reproduce fissile isotopes suitable for use in thermal nuclear reactors.  One of the advantages of nuclear power plants compared to conventional thermal power plants is their high environmental friendliness, which remains with

passages.title: China Science and Technology 2020 ｜ How far is the ultimate energy for mankind?
passages.passage: At the economic work conference of the CPC Central Committee at the end of 2020, the government deployed eight major tasks for the development of 2021.  This working meeting of top officials of the Communist Party of China not only listed "strengthening the national strategic scientific and technological strength" as the top priority for economic development next year, but also admitted to developing high technology through the advantages of the national system, "as soon as possible to solve a number of" neck jam "problems.  Looking back at 2020, China has a bright performance or national strategic deployment in the fields of lunar exploration, Mars exploration, satellite navigation, manned deep diving, quantum research, database technology replacement, international participation in nuclear fusion technology, and neutrino experiments and chip manufacturing.  What is the practical significance of scientific and technological research in these fields? What is China ’ s competitive advantage and realistic challenge?  Where is the next step?  The sun is the source of human energy, and the ultimate energy for human beings is still to be found inside the sun, which simulates the internal fusion reaction of the sun on the earth, that is, controlled nuclear fusion, and has also become the "artificial sun".  This is an incredible image of a solar “explosion ” released by NASA in 2018.  The Sun, the closest star to humans, is actually a supernuclear fusion reactor, with 600 million tons of hydrogen being converted into helium by fusion reactions every second. In the process, about 4.2 million tons of net energy is released into the universe, equivalent to 3.78 × 10 ^ 26 joules of energy.  The Earth obtained only 1.72 × 10 ^ 17 joules from it, equivalent to a net energy release of about 19 kilograms per second, creating a livable Earth ecosystem, which shows the power of nuclear fusion energy.  Compared with fossil fuels such as coal, oil and natural gas, clean energy such as solar energy, and even cracking energy as nuclear energy, nuclear fusion energy has obvious advantages in energy density and environmental protection.  Take a power plant with 1 million kilowatts as an example, using coal, 2.5 million tons per year, requiring 250 trains of 100 sections to transport; using fuel, 110,000 barrels of oil per year, requiring 11 supertankers to transport; using a fission reactor, consuming 28 tons of uranium dioxide per year; using solar energy, requiring 5,000 acres of land and energy storage space; using a nuclear fusion reactor, requiring only 400 pounds of deuterium and 600 pounds. A ton of tritium, 1,300 pounds of lithium-6 can meet the need, and a small car can be transported.  At the same time, with coal, fuel oil as fuel, will produce tens of millions of tons of waste every year, human air pollution, greenhouse effect has long been intolerable; nuclear fission will produce 28 tons of highly radioactive waste, the current global nuclear waste treatment landfill as the main, the processing capacity has been saturated, these nuclear waste landfill tens of thousands of years after the human is still harmful; and nuclear fusion only produces 900 pounds of helium, zero environmental pollution.  More importantly, compared to coal, oil, natural gas and other fossil energy reserves are limited, solar energy, wind energy and other clean energy energy density is low, nuclear fusion energy has a very high energy density at the same time also has almost unlimited storage.  One liter of deuterium in seawater is equivalent to 300 liters of gasoline released by nuclear fusion, and there are more than 45 trillion tons of deuterium in seawater alone, releasing enough energy for humans to use for hundreds of millions of years.  Because of this, nuclear fusion energy is regarded as the "ultimate energy" of mankind. The so-called controlled nuclear fusion is actually simulating the nuclear fusion reaction inside the sun on Earth, so it is called the "artificial sun".  China's habitual confinement nuclear fusion experimental device "Shenguang" has so far developed to "Shenguang III", its ultimate goal is to achieve laser controlled nuclear fusion ignition.  (Shanghai Institute of Optics and Precision Machinery, Chinese Academy of Sciences) The US national ignition device and China's Shenguang controlled nuclear fusion technology are two major difficulties, one is how to trigger nuclear fusion, hydrogen bomb is formed by atomic bomb explosion high temperature and high pressure triggered fusion reaction, obviously can not be applied to controlled nuclear fusion; the first is how to control nuclear fusion under human control. Provide energy instead of releasing the power of destruction like a hydrogen bomb.  In addition, no material on Earth can withstand the high temperature and pressure required for nuclear fusion.  After several decades of development, there are currently two main branches of technology in the world controlled nuclear fusion research, one is the route of inertial confinement fusion (ICF), one is the route of magnetic confinement fusion (MCF).  The core of the device is that, through inertial or magnetic constraints, nuclear fusion occurs inside the device, while the entire device operates at a tolerable temperature and even ultra-low temperature.  For China, whether it is inertial restraint or magnetic restraint, there are research institutions that continue to exert efforts and walk on two legs.  The so-called inertial confinement, that is, the use of laser shock waves to make the fuel ball, which usually contains deuterium and tritium, reach extremely high temperature and pressure, and then "ignite" the nuclear fusion reaction inside the fuel ball.  Based on the way that the laser directly triggers the fusion reaction, the results of inertial confinement research can be used to produce pure fusion nuclear weapons, so most of the nuclear weapons research institutions in various countries are responsible for inertial confinement research, such as the United States Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL), China Institute of Engineering Physics, and there is very little exchange and cooperation between countries.  The National Ignition Facility (NIF), built by Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory in the United States, is the world ’ s highest energy inertial confinement fusion experimental device. The building that houses the NIF device is 215 meters long and 120 meters wide, equivalent to three football fields, and can focus 2 million joules of energy through 192 laser beams to one point.  At present, NIF has successfully achieved "energy gain", that is, the energy generated by the fusion reaction exceeds the energy absorbed by the fuel for the first time, and also proves the feasibility of using a powerful pulse laser to "ignite" artificial thermonuclear fusion.  The "Shenguang-III" device, built in 2015 by the China Institute of Engineering Physics and the Shanghai Institute of Optics and Precision Machinery of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, is the world's second largest laser driver after the NIF in the United States.  In addition, Russia, France and others are building similar high-energy laser devices.  US National Ignition Facility Detailed explanation (click to view high-definition big picture): + 6 + 6 At present, the ICF technology route is still a long way ahead, compared with the magnetic confinement fusion route, the road ahead is much brighter, which can be called the field of modern nuclear fusion research.  Magnetic confinement fusion is currently focused on the Tokamak technology route, the Tokamak device was first developed by Igor of the Kurchatov Institute in the Soviet Union.  Igor Tamm, Andrei Sakharov, Lev Artsimovich and others invented it in the 1950s. In 1968, at the Third International Conference on Plasma Physics and Controlled Nuclear Fusion Research, the research results were first presented – plasma up to 1KeV was confined for a few milliseconds to shock the world, opening up magnetic confinement. The New World of Nuclear Fusion Research.  The center of the Tokamak device is an annular vacuum chamber, wrapped around a wire, and the inside of the Tokamak will generate a huge helical magnetic field when powered on, heating the plasma to a very high temperature to achieve the purpose of nuclear fusion.  After decades of research, the current Tokamak device has developed to the stage of superconducting Tokamak, and different from the ICF technical route, there has been continuous international cooperation and exchanges since the 1950s.  In the 1980s, the United States, the Soviet Union, the European Union, and Japan launched the International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER) construction plan, which was later stopped due to budget and other problems.  In 2006, China, the United States, Russia, India, Japan, South Korea and the European Union signed the ITER plan to build a superconducting Kamake-type fusion reactor in Cadarache, southern France, to explore the scientific and engineering feasibility of using fusion energy for peaceful purposes.  It is understood that ITER will become the world's first power station level fusion experimental reactor, which is an indispensable step to finally realize the commercialization of magnetic confinement fusion, which is also the largest international cooperation project that China has participated in as an equal partner for the first time.  According to the plan, China, the United States, Russia, India, Japan and South Korea each shoulder about 9% of the budget for a total of 65%, and the European Union as the equipment organizer provides the remaining 45% of the budget.  For example, India is responsible for the manufacture of low temperature constant, the United States is responsible for the central spiral tube, South Korea and the European Union are responsible for the vacuum container

Title: China's "artificial sun" record
Content: China's artificial sun has set a new record in its quest for fusion energy.  While similar efforts are underway in the United States, Europe, Russia and South Korea, the artificial sun improved its previous record by five times.  According to state media, China has reached another milestone in its quest to realize a fusion reactor, and one of its artificial suns has managed to maintain extreme temperatures several times higher than its previous record.  State news agency Xinhua reported that the Tokamak Advanced Experimental Superconductor (EAST) at a facility in the eastern city of Hefei maintained a plasma temperature of 120 million degrees Celsius for 101 seconds.  The report said the artificial sun also managed to maintain a temperature of 160 million degrees Celsius for 20 seconds.  Last year, EAST achieved a record 100 million degrees Celsius of plasma temperature for 20 seconds.  The experiment means that Chinese scientists have managed to maintain extremely high temperatures up to five times higher than previous experiments.  Another Chinese artificial sun project in Chengdu, the Tokamak HL-2m device, maintained temperatures of 150 million degrees Celsius for up to 10 seconds in a test late last year.  The construction and development of these artificial suns is part of China ’ s effort to reach fusion reactors that will revive hopes for clean and unlimited energy.  But there are many challenges that need to be overcome in the decades-long effort of the world ’ s scientists.  Similar efforts are underway in the United States, Europe, Russia and South Korea.  China is also one of the 35 countries involved in the International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER) project in France.  It is difficult to directly compare these types of experiments in different countries, because the devices are designed differently.  These facilities are called “artificial suns ” because they aim to replicate nuclear fusion reactions that power the sun at 15 million degrees Celsius.  When two atoms reach the fusion point, they release a large amount of energy.  To do this on Earth, scientists need to be able to maintain high temperatures for long periods of time.  Despite the advances made, fusion reactors are still a long way from being operational.  Song Yuntao, director of the Institute of Plasma Physics of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, said the latest results are a major breakthrough for physics and engineering in China.  The success of the test is the foundation for the construction of a nuclear fusion energy station in China.  China joined the ITER project in 2003 and at that time it was reported as an opportunity for its scientists to expand their expertise and gain an opportunity to emerge in the international scientific community.  The project in southern France has been repeatedly delayed, with the country ’ s latest plasma production target set for 2025.  The European Union has pledged $6.8 billion in new funding to the project in February.  Also, China National Nuclear Corporation will install the main equipment "ITER".  End of message.

Title: MEPhI told about the prospects of the artificial sun of China
Content: In 2020, Chinese scientists will launch a new experimental fusion reactor HL-2M as part of the EAST project.  Such installations are sometimes called "artificial Sun" - they undergo the same processes as in the core of our star.  About the prospects of the Chinese project and in general about the technology of thermonuclear fusion "360" talked with Professor George Tikhomirov - Deputy Director of the Institute of Nuclear Physics and Technology of NRNU MEPhI.  The head of the Southwest Institute of Physics, Duan Xuzhu, previously said that the HL-2M reactor will be able to heat the plasma to a temperature above 200 million degrees Celsius.  The previous record was also set in China: a year ago in another experimental tokamak EAST - HT-7U - the peak temperature was 100 million degrees.  Tokamak HT-7U project EAST Tokamak is an abbreviation of "toroidal chamber with magnetic coils".  The name was invented by Soviet physicists in the 1950s, at the same time the first experiments were carried out to retain heated plasma with the help of powerful magnets.  Thermonuclear reactions are constantly on the Sun.  In the core, whose temperature reaches 15 million degrees Celsius, hydrogen is converted into helium.  A huge amount of energy is released.  To recreate the process on Earth, it is necessary to heat the hydrogen isotopes deuterium and tritium to a temperature above 100 million degrees Celsius.  At this point, the gas becomes plasma.  Such temperatures are needed to achieve a higher density of energy release than on the Sun, Tikhomirov explained.  The sun is very large, and therefore the energy it gives is enough for everyone.  And on Earth, we create conditions to a lesser extent.  If the conditions are close to solar, it does not allow us to use them for practical needs.  Georgy Tikhomirov Deputy Director of the Institute of Nuclear Physics and Technology of the National Research Nuclear University MEPhI In addition, for a functional thermonuclear reactor (which would give more energy than spent) it is necessary to hold the plasma inside the tokamak for a long time and obtain high-density plasma.  According to Tikhomirov, the Chinese installation HL-2M “in some respects will surpass the existing ones, ” but“ there is no breakthrough in this. ”  The deputy director of the Institute of Nuclear Physics and Technology recalled that the largest thermonuclear reactor in the world, ITER, is being built at the Cadarache Research Center in France.  This international project involves the EU, Japan, Russia, the United States, China, India and South Korea.  The reactor, which is planned to be completed by 2025, the Chinese “can not surpass ”, the professor is sure.  Most likely, they will create some compact small installation, where they will achieve good plasma parameters.  But there will be no breakthrough in energy.  Georgy Tikhomirov, deputy director of the Institute of Nuclear Physics and Technology of the National Research Nuclear University MEPhI, added that in Russia thermonuclear research "is developing in various directions."  “We will soon launch the T-15, our tokamak, there are other installations.  We are also part of the ITER program.  This topic is known, and we are not inferior to the Chinese here, ” Tikhomirov said.  The professor noted that the launch of a thermonuclear power plant has great prospects, because the fuel that can be used is deuterium "very much in the oceans."

Title: Atomic energy
Content: Over the past 20 years, the amount of clean energy has doubled.  This energy is obtained from environmentally friendly sources - hydroelectric, nuclear, solar, wind, geothermal, tidal, biomass energy.  However, its share in the total amount of energy produced remained the same and even decreased slightly.  The fossil fuel industry is growing faster than the clean energy industry.  Many poor countries still use wood, manure and coal as their primary fuel.  The share of alternative renewable sources over the past 20 years has increased to almost 10% in 2018, and nuclear power plants, on the contrary, were closed.  And this despite the fact that solar and wind energy is unstable, it can be received only 10-30% of the time, when the sun is shining enough and the wind blows.  And hospitals, homes, cities and factories need energy all the time.  The United Nations Intergovernmental Committee on Climate Change (IPCC) has studied the CO2 content of all fuels.  Nuclear energy is one of the most environmentally friendly.  At the same time, the nuclear power plant can be used 92% of the time.  So why are we so afraid of nuclear power plants?  Nuclear energy seems like a good solution in the fight against climate change.  But there is one big problem – people don ’ t like it.  According to a 2014 Ipsos survey, nuclear power is one of the least popular.  Only 28% of respondents preferred nuclear power.  Even people are better at oil (30%).  Most people trust solar (85%) and wind energy (78%).  The fear of nuclear power is linked to three factors – the possibility of leakage, the disposal of waste and the association with nuclear weapons.  But it is difficult to make nuclear energy even safer than it is now.  According to a study conducted by one of the largest medical journals Lancet, nuclear energy is the safest among all other sources of energy.  It is safer than wind turbines and solar panels.  After reviewing data on the Fukushima and Chernobyl accidents, the WHO found that a large proportion of the damage was caused by panic.  The UN has also conducted comprehensive studies of the Chernobyl disaster.  The explosion at the Chernobyl nuclear power plant is the worst nuclear accident of all that happened.  As a result, 28 people died from acute radiation syndrome and another 15 people died over the next 25 years from thyroid cancer.  16,000 people became ill with thyroid cancer after Chernobyl, and it is estimated that 160 of them will die from this type of cancer.  The Fukushima nuclear disaster ranks second in severity.  The radiation emission was much smaller than that of Chernobyl.  There are no deaths from radiation after Fukushima.  Fifteen thousand people were killed, who were dragged out of nursing homes and hospitals.  They received a large dose of radiation just because they were moved a long distance.  In many ways, this was the result of a general panic.  For a person living in a big city, such as London, Berlin or New York, the risk of mortality increases by 2.8% from air pollution alone.  For those who live near smokers – by 1.7%.  For the liquidators of the Chernobyl accident, who received a dose of radiation of 250 millisieverts, it increased by only 1%.  By comparison, fuel energy creates uncontrolled waste in the form of greenhouse gas emissions, which kills 7 million people a year.  Therefore, the reduction of fuel energy in favor of nuclear energy has already saved the lives of 1.8 million people.  What about the waste?  Nuclear waste, as it turned out, is not so much.  If you take nuclear waste from the entire history of the United States and fill a football stadium with it, their height will be only 6 m. The waste is stored in special isolated containers, and they are constantly monitored.  In addition, development is underway to use nuclear waste as fuel.  It is the same with nuclear weapons.  There are no examples of countries with nuclear industry suddenly starting to develop nuclear weapons.  In fact, the opposite is happening.  It turns out that the only known way to get rid of a large number of nuclear weapons is to use plutonium from warheads as fuel for nuclear power plants.  Over the next 50 years, humanity will consume more energy than has been consumed in all previous history.  Earlier forecasts about the growth rate of energy consumption and the development of new energy technologies did not materialize: the level of consumption is growing much faster, and new energy sources will work on an industrial scale and at competitive prices not earlier than 2030.  The problem of the shortage of fossil energy resources is becoming more acute.  The capacity to build new hydropower plants is also very limited.  Do not forget about the fight against the “greenhouse effect ”, which imposes restrictions on the burning of oil, gas and coal in thermal power plants.  The solution to the problem can be the active development of nuclear energy, one of the youngest and fastest growing sectors of the global economy.  An increasing number of countries today come to the need to start the development of a peaceful atom.  The use of nuclear power may prove to be one of the solutions to these pressing problems, however unlikely it may seem.  But for this, the methods of its application need to be reviewed.  At the heart of the production of atomic energy is the force that holds the parts of the atom together.  If an atom is unstable, it will tend to move to a more stable state by splitting.  The instability of the atom can be natural or caused by the addition of additional neutrons to the nucleus.  When the atom becomes more stable and ejects particles, a huge amount of energy is released, which in a closed system can be used to generate enough heat to propel the turbine.  Radiation, which is often misrepresented, occurs for the most part due to natural causes.  Let ’ s see what the advantages of nuclear power are: 1 kg of uranium can produce 90,000 times more energy than 1 kg of coal.  Modern technologies make it possible to switch to a closed fuel cycle, which involves the repeated use of fuel products and the minimization of waste.  Every year, nuclear power plants in Europe avoid the emission of 700 million tons of CO2.  One job in the construction of nuclear power plants creates more than 10 jobs in related industries.  The development of nuclear energy contributes to the growth of scientific research and intellectual potential of the country.  According to the IAEA directory published in 2019, 98 nuclear reactors operated in the United States in 2018, 58 in France, 46 in China, 39 in Japan, 38 in Russia, 24 in the Republic of Korea, 22 in India, 19 in Canada, and 15 in the United Kingdom and Ukraine.  The total generating capacity of the nuclear power plant is over 380 GW.  A nuclear power plant is a complex of necessary systems, devices, equipment and structures designed to generate electricity by using the heat released in a nuclear reactor as a result of a controlled fission chain reaction of the nuclei of heavy elements (mainly uranium-233, uranium-235, plutonium-239).  The heat generated in the core of the nuclear reactor is transferred (directly or through an intermediate coolant) to the working medium (mainly water vapor), which drives steam turbines with turbogenerators, where the mechanical energy of the steam is converted into electrical energy.  Then the electricity through the wires goes to consumers.  As heat carriers, ordinary and heavy water, water vapor, liquid metals, organic liquids, some gases, for example, helium or carbon dioxide, are used.  The coolant circulates through sealed pipelines, which, in combination with circulation pumps, form a so-called reactor circuit or loop.  The circuits through which the coolant circulates are always closed to avoid leakage of radioactivity, their number is determined mainly by the type of nuclear reactor, as well as the properties of the working fluid and coolant.  Nuclear power plants can have single-circuit, double-circuit and three-circuit circuit of heat carrier operation.  Single-circuit circuit is used at nuclear power plants with channel-type reactors.  In such nuclear power plants, the coolant is also a working fluid.  In them, the boiling reactor itself is a steam generator, so the entire circuit is radioactive.  It's surrounded by biological defenses.  Two-circuit circuit circuit is used at nuclear power plants with water-water reactors.  In such nuclear power plants, water is supplied under pressure to the reactor core, which is heated.  Heat carrier energy is used in steam generator to form saturated steam.  The first circuit is radioactive and is surrounded by biological protection, except when inert gas is used as heat carrier.  The second circuit is usually radiation-safe, since the working fluid and coolant of the first circuit do not touch.  Three-circuit circuit circuit is used at nuclear power plants with fast neutron reactors with sodium coolant.  To exclude contact of radioactive sodium with water, a second circuit with non-radioactive sodium is constructed.  Thus, the scheme turns out to be three-circuit.  The peculiarity of nuclear power plants with a fast neutron reactor is that simultaneously with the generation of electrical and thermal energy, they reproduce fissile isotopes suitable for use in thermal nuclear reactors. Title: China Science and Technology 2020 ｜ How far is the ultimate energy for mankind?
Content: At the economic work conference of the CPC Central Committee at the end of 2020, the government deployed eight major tasks for the development of 2021.  This working meeting of top officials of the Communist Party of China not only listed "strengthening the national strategic scientific and technological strength" as the top priority for economic development next year, but also admitted to developing high technology through the advantages of the national system, "as soon as possible to solve a number of" neck jam "problems.  Looking back at 2020, China has a bright performance or national strategic deployment in the fields of lunar exploration, Mars exploration, satellite navigation, manned deep diving, quantum research, database technology replacement, international participation in nuclear fusion technology, and neutrino experiments and chip manufacturing.  What is the practical significance of scientific and technological research in these fields? What is China ’ s competitive advantage and realistic challenge?  Where is the next step?  The sun is the source of human energy, and the ultimate energy for human beings is still to be found inside the sun, which simulates the internal fusion reaction of the sun on the earth, that is, controlled nuclear fusion, and has also become the "artificial sun".  This is an incredible image of a solar “explosion ” released by NASA in 2018.  The Sun, the closest star to humans, is actually a supernuclear fusion reactor, with 600 million tons of hydrogen being converted into helium by fusion reactions every second. In the process, about 4.2 million tons of net energy is released into the universe, equivalent to 3.78 × 10 ^ 26 joules of energy.  The Earth obtained only 1.72 × 10 ^ 17 joules from it, equivalent to a net energy release of about 19 kilograms per second, creating a livable Earth ecosystem, which shows the power of nuclear fusion energy.  Compared with fossil fuels such as coal, oil and natural gas, clean energy such as solar energy, and even cracking energy as nuclear energy, nuclear fusion energy has obvious advantages in energy density and environmental protection.  Take a power plant with 1 million kilowatts as an example, using coal, 2.5 million tons per year, requiring 250 trains of 100 sections to transport; using fuel, 110,000 barrels of oil per year, requiring 11 supertankers to transport; using a fission reactor, consuming 28 tons of uranium dioxide per year; using solar energy, requiring 5,000 acres of land and energy storage space; using a nuclear fusion reactor, requiring only 400 pounds of deuterium and 600 pounds. A ton of tritium, 1,300 pounds of lithium-6 can meet the need, and a small car can be transported.  At the same time, with coal, fuel oil as fuel, will produce tens of millions of tons of waste every year, human air pollution, greenhouse effect has long been intolerable; nuclear fission will produce 28 tons of highly radioactive waste, the current global nuclear waste treatment landfill as the main, the processing capacity has been saturated, these nuclear waste landfill tens of thousands of years after the human is still harmful; and nuclear fusion only produces 900 pounds of helium, zero environmental pollution.  More importantly, compared to coal, oil, natural gas and other fossil energy reserves are limited, solar energy, wind energy and other clean energy energy density is low, nuclear fusion energy has a very high energy density at the same time also has almost unlimited storage.  One liter of deuterium in seawater is equivalent to 300 liters of gasoline released by nuclear fusion, and there are more than 45 trillion tons of deuterium in seawater alone, releasing enough energy for humans to use for hundreds of millions of years.  Because of this, nuclear fusion energy is regarded as the "ultimate energy" of mankind. The so-called controlled nuclear fusion is actually simulating the nuclear fusion reaction inside the sun on Earth, so it is called the "artificial sun".  China's habitual confinement nuclear fusion experimental device "Shenguang" has so far developed to "Shenguang III", its ultimate goal is to achieve laser controlled nuclear fusion ignition.  (Shanghai Institute of Optics and Precision Machinery, Chinese Academy of Sciences) The US national ignition device and China's Shenguang controlled nuclear fusion technology are two major difficulties, one is how to trigger nuclear fusion, hydrogen bomb is formed by atomic bomb explosion high temperature and high pressure triggered fusion reaction, obviously can not be applied to controlled nuclear fusion; the first is how to control nuclear fusion under human control. Provide energy instead of releasing the power of destruction like a hydrogen bomb.  In addition, no material on Earth can withstand the high temperature and pressure required for nuclear fusion.  After several decades of development, there are currently two main branches of technology in the world controlled nuclear fusion research, one is the route of inertial confinement fusion (ICF), one is the route of magnetic confinement fusion (MCF).  The core of the device is that, through inertial or magnetic constraints, nuclear fusion occurs inside the device, while the entire device operates at a tolerable temperature and even ultra-low temperature.  For China, whether it is inertial restraint or magnetic restraint, there are research institutions that continue to exert efforts and walk on two legs.  The so-called inertial confinement, that is, the use of laser shock waves to make the fuel ball, which usually contains deuterium and tritium, reach extremely high temperature and pressure, and then "ignite" the nuclear fusion reaction inside the fuel ball.  Based on the way that the laser directly triggers the fusion reaction, the results of inertial confinement research can be used to produce pure fusion nuclear weapons, so most of the nuclear weapons research institutions in various countries are responsible for inertial confinement research, such as the United States Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL), China Institute of Engineering Physics, and there is very little exchange and cooperation between countries.  The National Ignition Facility (NIF), built by Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory in the United States, is the world ’ s highest energy inertial confinement fusion experimental device. The building that houses the NIF device is 215 meters long and 120 meters wide, equivalent to three football fields, and can focus 2 million joules of energy through 192 laser beams to one point.  At present, NIF has successfully achieved "energy gain", that is, the energy generated by the fusion reaction exceeds the energy absorbed by the fuel for the first time, and also proves the feasibility of using a powerful pulse laser to "ignite" artificial thermonuclear fusion.  The "Shenguang-III" device, built in 2015 by the China Institute of Engineering Physics and the Shanghai Institute of Optics and Precision Machinery of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, is the world's second largest laser driver after the NIF in the United States.  In addition, Russia, France and others are building similar high-energy laser devices.  US National Ignition Facility Detailed explanation (click to view high-definition big picture): + 6 + 6 At present, the ICF technology route is still a long way ahead, compared with the magnetic confinement fusion route, the road ahead is much brighter, which can be called the field of modern nuclear fusion research.  Magnetic confinement fusion is currently focused on the Tokamak technology route, the Tokamak device was first developed by Igor of the Kurchatov Institute in the Soviet Union.  Igor Tamm, Andrei Sakharov, Lev Artsimovich and others invented it in the 1950s. In 1968, at the Third International Conference on Plasma Physics and Controlled Nuclear Fusion Research, the research results were first presented – plasma up to 1KeV was confined for a few milliseconds to shock the world, opening up magnetic confinement. The New World of Nuclear Fusion Research.  The center of the Tokamak device is an annular vacuum chamber, wrapped around a wire, and the inside of the Tokamak will generate a huge helical magnetic field when powered on, heating the plasma to a very high temperature to achieve the purpose of nuclear fusion.  After decades of research, the current Tokamak device has developed to the stage of superconducting Tokamak, and different from the ICF technical route, there has been continuous international cooperation and exchanges since the 1950s.  In the 1980s, the United States, the Soviet Union, the European Union, and Japan launched the International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER) construction plan, which was later stopped due to budget and other problems.  In 2006, China, the United States, Russia, India, Japan, South Korea and the European Union signed the ITER plan to build a superconducting Kamake-type fusion reactor in Cadarache, southern France, to explore the scientific and engineering feasibility of using fusion energy for peaceful purposes.  It is understood that ITER will become the world's first power station level fusion experimental reactor, which is an indispensable step to finally realize the commercialization of magnetic confinement fusion, which is also the largest international cooperation project that China has participated in as an equal partner for the first time.  According to the plan, China, the United States, Russia, India, Japan and South Korea each shoulder about 9% of the budget for a total of 65%, and the European Union as the equipment organizer provides the remaining 45% of the budget. The head of the Southwest Institute of Physics, Duan Xuzhu, previously said that the HL-2M reactor will be able to heat the plasma to a temperature above 200 million degrees Celsius.  The previous record was also set in China: a year ago in another experimental tokamak EAST - HT-7U - the peak temperature was 100 million degrees.  Tokamak HT-7U project EAST Tokamak is an abbreviation of "toroidal chamber with magnetic coils".  The name was invented by Soviet physicists in the 1950s, at the same time the first experiments were carried out to retain heated plasma with the help of powerful magnets.  Thermonuclear reactions are constantly on the Sun.  In the core, whose temperature reaches 15 million degrees Celsius, hydrogen is converted into helium.  A huge amount of energy is released.  To recreate the process on Earth, it is necessary to heat the hydrogen isotopes deuterium and tritium to a temperature above 100 million degrees Celsius.  At this point, the gas becomes plasma.  Such temperatures are needed to achieve a higher density of energy release than on the Sun, Tikhomirov explained.  The sun is very large, and therefore the energy it gives is enough for everyone.  And on Earth, we create conditions to a lesser extent.  If the conditions are close to solar, it does not allow us to use them for practical needs.  Georgy Tikhomirov Deputy Director of the Institute of Nuclear Physics and Technology of the National Research Nuclear University MEPhI In addition, for a functional thermonuclear reactor (which would give more energy than spent) it is necessary to hold the plasma inside the tokamak for a long time and obtain high-density plasma. The reactor, which is planned to be completed by 2025, the Chinese “can not surpass ”, the professor is sure. Title: Atomic energy
Content: Over the past 20 years, the amount of clean energy has doubled.  This energy is obtained from environmentally friendly sources - hydroelectric, nuclear, solar, wind, geothermal, tidal, biomass energy.  However, its share in the total amount of energy produced remained the same and even decreased slightly.  The fossil fuel industry is growing faster than the clean energy industry.  Many poor countries still use wood, manure and coal as their primary fuel.  The share of alternative renewable sources over the past 20 years has increased to almost 10% in 2018, and nuclear power plants, on the contrary, were closed.  And this despite the fact that solar and wind energy is unstable, it can be received only 10-30% of the time, when the sun is shining enough and the wind blows.  And hospitals, homes, cities and factories need energy all the time.  The United Nations Intergovernmental Committee on Climate Change (IPCC) has studied the CO2 content of all fuels.  Nuclear energy is one of the most environmentally friendly.  At the same time, the nuclear power plant can be used 92% of the time.  So why are we so afraid of nuclear power plants?  Nuclear energy seems like a good solution in the fight against climate change.  But there is one big problem – people don ’ t like it.  According to a 2014 Ipsos survey, nuclear power is one of the least popular.  Only 28% of respondents preferred nuclear power.  Even people are better at oil (30%).  Most people trust solar (85%) and wind energy (78%).  The fear of nuclear power is linked to three factors – the possibility of leakage, the disposal of waste and the association with nuclear weapons.  But it is difficult to make nuclear energy even safer than it is now.  According to a study conducted by one of the largest medical journals Lancet, nuclear energy is the safest among all other sources of energy.  It is safer than wind turbines and solar panels.  After reviewing data on the Fukushima and Chernobyl accidents, the WHO found that a large proportion of the damage was caused by panic.  The UN has also conducted comprehensive studies of the Chernobyl disaster.  The explosion at the Chernobyl nuclear power plant is the worst nuclear accident of all that happened.  As a result, 28 people died from acute radiation syndrome and another 15 people died over the next 25 years from thyroid cancer.  16,000 people became ill with thyroid cancer after Chernobyl, and it is estimated that 160 of them will die from this type of cancer.  The Fukushima nuclear disaster ranks second in severity.  The radiation emission was much smaller than that of Chernobyl.  There are no deaths from radiation after Fukushima.  Fifteen thousand people were killed, who were dragged out of nursing homes and hospitals.  They received a large dose of radiation just because they were moved a long distance.  In many ways, this was the result of a general panic.  For a person living in a big city, such as London, Berlin or New York, the risk of mortality increases by 2.8% from air pollution alone.  For those who live near smokers – by 1.7%.  For the liquidators of the Chernobyl accident, who received a dose of radiation of 250 millisieverts, it increased by only 1%.  By comparison, fuel energy creates uncontrolled waste in the form of greenhouse gas emissions, which kills 7 million people a year.  Therefore, the reduction of fuel energy in favor of nuclear energy has already saved the lives of 1.8 million people.  What about the waste?  Nuclear waste, as it turned out, is not so much.  If you take nuclear waste from the entire history of the United States and fill a football stadium with it, their height will be only 6 m. The waste is stored in special isolated containers, and they are constantly monitored.  In addition, development is underway to use nuclear waste as fuel.  It is the same with nuclear weapons.  There are no examples of countries with nuclear industry suddenly starting to develop nuclear weapons.  In fact, the opposite is happening.  It turns out that the only known way to get rid of a large number of nuclear weapons is to use plutonium from warheads as fuel for nuclear power plants.  Over the next 50 years, humanity will consume more energy than has been consumed in all previous history.  Earlier forecasts about the growth rate of energy consumption and the development of new energy technologies did not materialize: the level of consumption is growing much faster, and new energy sources will work on an industrial scale and at competitive prices not earlier than 2030.  The problem of the shortage of fossil energy resources is becoming more acute.  The capacity to build new hydropower plants is also very limited.  Do not forget about the fight against the “greenhouse effect ”, which imposes restrictions on the burning of oil, gas and coal in thermal power plants.  The solution to the problem can be the active development of nuclear energy, one of the youngest and fastest growing sectors of the global economy.  An increasing number of countries today come to the need to start the development of a peaceful atom.  The use of nuclear power may prove to be one of the solutions to these pressing problems, however unlikely it may seem.  But for this, the methods of its application need to be reviewed.  At the heart of the production of atomic energy is the force that holds the parts of the atom together.  If an atom is unstable, it will tend to move to a more stable state by splitting.  The instability of the atom can be natural or caused by the addition of additional neutrons to the nucleus.  When the atom becomes more stable and ejects particles, a huge amount of energy is released, which in a closed system can be used to generate enough heat to propel the turbine.  Radiation, which is often misrepresented, occurs for the most part due to natural causes.  Let ’ s see what the advantages of nuclear power are: 1 kg of uranium can produce 90,000 times more energy than 1 kg of coal.  Modern technologies make it possible to switch to a closed fuel cycle, which involves the repeated use of fuel products and the minimization of waste.  Every year, nuclear power plants in Europe avoid the emission of 700 million tons of CO2.  One job in the construction of nuclear power plants creates more than 10 jobs in related industries.  The development of nuclear energy contributes to the growth of scientific research and intellectual potential of the country.  According to the IAEA directory published in 2019, 98 nuclear reactors operated in the United States in 2018, 58 in France, 46 in China, 39 in Japan, 38 in Russia, 24 in the Republic of Korea, 22 in India, 19 in Canada, and 15 in the United Kingdom and Ukraine.  The total generating capacity of the nuclear power plant is over 380 GW.  A nuclear power plant is a complex of necessary systems, devices, equipment and structures designed to generate electricity by using the heat released in a nuclear reactor as a result of a controlled fission chain reaction of the nuclei of heavy elements (mainly uranium-233, uranium-235, plutonium-239).  The heat generated in the core of the nuclear reactor is transferred (directly or through an intermediate coolant) to the working medium (mainly water vapor), which drives steam turbines with turbogenerators, where the mechanical energy of the steam is converted into electrical energy.  Then the electricity through the wires goes to consumers.  As heat carriers, ordinary and heavy water, water vapor, liquid metals, organic liquids, some gases, for example, helium or carbon dioxide, are used.  The coolant circulates through sealed pipelines, which, in combination with circulation pumps, form a so-called reactor circuit or loop.  The circuits through which the coolant circulates are always closed to avoid leakage of radioactivity, their number is determined mainly by the type of nuclear reactor, as well as the properties of the working fluid and coolant.  Nuclear power plants can have single-circuit, double-circuit and three-circuit circuit of heat carrier operation.  Single-circuit circuit is used at nuclear power plants with channel-type reactors.  In such nuclear power plants, the coolant is also a working fluid.  In them, the boiling reactor itself is a steam generator, so the entire circuit is radioactive.  It's surrounded by biological defenses.  Two-circuit circuit circuit is used at nuclear power plants with water-water reactors.  In such nuclear power plants, water is supplied under pressure to the reactor core, which is heated.  Heat carrier energy is used in steam generator to form saturated steam.  The first circuit is radioactive and is surrounded by biological protection, except when inert gas is used as heat carrier.  The second circuit is usually radiation-safe, since the working fluid and coolant of the first circuit do not touch.  Three-circuit circuit circuit is used at nuclear power plants with fast neutron reactors with sodium coolant.  To exclude contact of radioactive sodium with water, a second circuit with non-radioactive sodium is constructed.  Thus, the scheme turns out to be three-circuit.  The peculiarity of nuclear power plants with a fast neutron reactor is that simultaneously with the generation of electrical and thermal energy, they reproduce fissile isotopes suitable for use in thermal nuclear reactors.
