Title: China Science and Technology 2020 ｜ How far is the ultimate energy for mankind?
Content: At the economic work conference of the CPC Central Committee at the end of 2020, the government deployed eight major tasks for the development of 2021.  This working meeting of top officials of the Communist Party of China not only listed "strengthening the national strategic scientific and technological strength" as the top priority for economic development next year, but also admitted to developing high technology through the advantages of the national system, "as soon as possible to solve a number of" neck jam "problems.  Looking back at 2020, China has a bright performance or national strategic deployment in the fields of lunar exploration, Mars exploration, satellite navigation, manned deep diving, quantum research, database technology replacement, international participation in nuclear fusion technology, and neutrino experiments and chip manufacturing.  What is the practical significance of scientific and technological research in these fields? What is China ’ s competitive advantage and realistic challenge?  Where is the next step?  The sun is the source of human energy, and the ultimate energy for human beings is still to be found inside the sun, which simulates the internal fusion reaction of the sun on the earth, that is, controlled nuclear fusion, and has also become the "artificial sun".  This is an incredible image of a solar “explosion ” released by NASA in 2018.  The Sun, the closest star to humans, is actually a supernuclear fusion reactor, with 600 million tons of hydrogen being converted into helium by fusion reactions every second. In the process, about 4.2 million tons of net energy is released into the universe, equivalent to 3.78 × 10 ^ 26 joules of energy.  The Earth obtained only 1.72 × 10 ^ 17 joules from it, equivalent to a net energy release of about 19 kilograms per second, creating a livable Earth ecosystem, which shows the power of nuclear fusion energy.  Compared with fossil fuels such as coal, oil and natural gas, clean energy such as solar energy, and even cracking energy as nuclear energy, nuclear fusion energy has obvious advantages in energy density and environmental protection.  Take a power plant with 1 million kilowatts as an example, using coal, 2.5 million tons per year, requiring 250 trains of 100 sections to transport; using fuel, 110,000 barrels of oil per year, requiring 11 supertankers to transport; using a fission reactor, consuming 28 tons of uranium dioxide per year; using solar energy, requiring 5,000 acres of land and energy storage space; using a nuclear fusion reactor, requiring only 400 pounds of deuterium and 600 pounds. A ton of tritium, 1,300 pounds of lithium-6 can meet the need, and a small car can be transported.  At the same time, with coal, fuel oil as fuel, will produce tens of millions of tons of waste every year, human air pollution, greenhouse effect has long been intolerable; nuclear fission will produce 28 tons of highly radioactive waste, the current global nuclear waste treatment landfill as the main, the processing capacity has been saturated, these nuclear waste landfill tens of thousands of years after the human is still harmful; and nuclear fusion only produces 900 pounds of helium, zero environmental pollution.  More importantly, compared to coal, oil, natural gas and other fossil energy reserves are limited, solar energy, wind energy and other clean energy energy density is low, nuclear fusion energy has a very high energy density at the same time also has almost unlimited storage.  One liter of deuterium in seawater is equivalent to 300 liters of gasoline released by nuclear fusion, and there are more than 45 trillion tons of deuterium in seawater alone, releasing enough energy for humans to use for hundreds of millions of years.  Because of this, nuclear fusion energy is regarded as the "ultimate energy" of mankind. The so-called controlled nuclear fusion is actually simulating the nuclear fusion reaction inside the sun on Earth, so it is called the "artificial sun".  China's habitual confinement nuclear fusion experimental device "Shenguang" has so far developed to "Shenguang III", its ultimate goal is to achieve laser controlled nuclear fusion ignition.  (Shanghai Institute of Optics and Precision Machinery, Chinese Academy of Sciences) The US national ignition device and China's Shenguang controlled nuclear fusion technology are two major difficulties, one is how to trigger nuclear fusion, hydrogen bomb is formed by atomic bomb explosion high temperature and high pressure triggered fusion reaction, obviously can not be applied to controlled nuclear fusion; the first is how to control nuclear fusion under human control. Provide energy instead of releasing the power of destruction like a hydrogen bomb.  In addition, no material on Earth can withstand the high temperature and pressure required for nuclear fusion.  After several decades of development, there are currently two main branches of technology in the world controlled nuclear fusion research, one is the route of inertial confinement fusion (ICF), one is the route of magnetic confinement fusion (MCF).  The core of the device is that, through inertial or magnetic constraints, nuclear fusion occurs inside the device, while the entire device operates at a tolerable temperature and even ultra-low temperature.  For China, whether it is inertial restraint or magnetic restraint, there are research institutions that continue to exert efforts and walk on two legs.  The so-called inertial confinement, that is, the use of laser shock waves to make the fuel ball, which usually contains deuterium and tritium, reach extremely high temperature and pressure, and then "ignite" the nuclear fusion reaction inside the fuel ball.  Based on the way that the laser directly triggers the fusion reaction, the results of inertial confinement research can be used to produce pure fusion nuclear weapons, so most of the nuclear weapons research institutions in various countries are responsible for inertial confinement research, such as the United States Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL), China Institute of Engineering Physics, and there is very little exchange and cooperation between countries.  The National Ignition Facility (NIF), built by Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory in the United States, is the world ’ s highest energy inertial confinement fusion experimental device. The building that houses the NIF device is 215 meters long and 120 meters wide, equivalent to three football fields, and can focus 2 million joules of energy through 192 laser beams to one point.  At present, NIF has successfully achieved "energy gain", that is, the energy generated by the fusion reaction exceeds the energy absorbed by the fuel for the first time, and also proves the feasibility of using a powerful pulse laser to "ignite" artificial thermonuclear fusion.  The "Shenguang-III" device, built in 2015 by the China Institute of Engineering Physics and the Shanghai Institute of Optics and Precision Machinery of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, is the world's second largest laser driver after the NIF in the United States.  In addition, Russia, France and others are building similar high-energy laser devices.  US National Ignition Facility Detailed explanation (click to view high-definition big picture): + 6 + 6 At present, the ICF technology route is still a long way ahead, compared with the magnetic confinement fusion route, the road ahead is much brighter, which can be called the field of modern nuclear fusion research.  Magnetic confinement fusion is currently focused on the Tokamak technology route, the Tokamak device was first developed by Igor of the Kurchatov Institute in the Soviet Union.  Igor Tamm, Andrei Sakharov, Lev Artsimovich and others invented it in the 1950s. In 1968, at the Third International Conference on Plasma Physics and Controlled Nuclear Fusion Research, the research results were first presented – plasma up to 1KeV was confined for a few milliseconds to shock the world, opening up magnetic confinement. The New World of Nuclear Fusion Research.  The center of the Tokamak device is an annular vacuum chamber, wrapped around a wire, and the inside of the Tokamak will generate a huge helical magnetic field when powered on, heating the plasma to a very high temperature to achieve the purpose of nuclear fusion.  After decades of research, the current Tokamak device has developed to the stage of superconducting Tokamak, and different from the ICF technical route, there has been continuous international cooperation and exchanges since the 1950s.  In the 1980s, the United States, the Soviet Union, the European Union, and Japan launched the International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER) construction plan, which was later stopped due to budget and other problems.  In 2006, China, the United States, Russia, India, Japan, South Korea and the European Union signed the ITER plan to build a superconducting Kamake-type fusion reactor in Cadarache, southern France, to explore the scientific and engineering feasibility of using fusion energy for peaceful purposes.  It is understood that ITER will become the world's first power station level fusion experimental reactor, which is an indispensable step to finally realize the commercialization of magnetic confinement fusion, which is also the largest international cooperation project that China has participated in as an equal partner for the first time.  According to the plan, China, the United States, Russia, India, Japan and South Korea each shoulder about 9% of the budget for a total of 65%, and the European Union as the equipment organizer provides the remaining 45% of the budget. On July 28, the International Thermonuclear Fusion Experimental Reactor (ITER), humanity ’ s largest nuclear fusion project, began a five-year assembly project in southern France, marking a new phase for the largest nuclear fusion project in human history.  + 4 + 3 + 2 The Guardian reported on July 28 that representatives of the participating countries of the project participated in the installation and launch ceremony of ITER on the same day.  The project was jointly built by the European Union, China, the United States, Russia, the United Kingdom, India, Japan and South Korea at a total cost of 20 billion euros.  Speaking at the launch ceremony, ITER Director General Bernard Bigot said that the clean energy generated by the ITER project would be a “miracle for the planet ” and that the energy provided by nuclear fusion and other renewable energy sources would transform energy use in industries such as transport, construction and industry.  The Guardian notes that the ITER project aims to provide conceptual proof for large-scale nuclear fusion, not for future commercial use.  Consisting of millions of components, the nuclear fusion device will be the first self-heating plasma, which is expected to generate 10 times more heat than the input, far more than any previous related test, and the process itself will not produce carbon dioxide that can cause climate warming, and will produce less radioactive waste, which is expected to power magnets and scientific instruments.  The main purpose of the ITER project is to simulate the process of nuclear fusion in which the sun generates energy, so its core device, the tokamak, which controls fusion reactions, is also known as the "artificial sun".  A technician watches the circular shield at the construction site of the International Thermonuclear Fusion Experimental Reactor (ITER) in France on November 7, 2019. passages.title: The second wave of the COVID-19 epidemic increased the suicide rate in Japan by 16%
passages.passage: January 15, Minsk / Corr.  BELTA /.  The first wave of the COVID-19 epidemic reduced the number of suicides in Japan by 14%, and the second wave, which began in the fall, on the contrary, increased by 16%.  Such data scientists published in the scientific journal Nature Human Behaviour, reports TASS.  Sociologists led by Tokyo City Institute of Gerontology researcher Shohei Okamoto traced how the COVID-19 pandemic affected suicide rates in Japan.  This country ranks seventh in the world ranking of sad statistics.  The Japanese government monitors suicidal attitudes and tries to prevent them.  The researchers analyzed data from Japanese social services collected during the first and second waves of the pandemic, as well as for similar time periods between 2016 and 2019.  Particular attention was paid to the reaction of the most vulnerable segments of the population, including middle-aged men, as well as the categories that previously committed the least suicide.  "The COVID-19 epidemic has affected all aspects of Japanese society.  Within nine months of the official start of the pandemic, unemployment rose, and fear and anxiety became part of everyday life for all Japanese.  These factors may explain why there were more suicides during the second wave of the pandemic, "the researchers write.  This mainly affected residents of small settlements, women and adolescents who previously committed suicide very rarely.  The exact reasons are not yet known.  But the researchers suggest that these trends have both social and economic causes: rising unemployment, as well as school closures and social distancing.  Okamoto and his colleagues hope that they will be able to find out these reasons in the future and figure out how to prevent the number of suicides from increasing in the future.

passages.title: Rising suicide rate under COVID-19: Is Japan sounding the alarm for the world?
passages.passage: Rising suicide rate under Covid-19: Is Japan sounding the alarm for the world?  Rupert Wingfield-Hayes, BBC reporter in Tokyo.  Japan reports suicides faster and more accurately than anywhere else in the world.  Unlike most countries, the number of suicides is counted at the end of each month.  These figures reveal disturbing stories during the coronavirus pandemic.  In 2020, Japan ’ s suicide rate rose for the first time in 11 years.  Most surprisingly, while the number of male suicides declined slightly, the rate of female suicides surged by nearly 15%.  In the month of October 2020, the female suicide rate in Japan rose by more than 70% compared to the same period last year.  Why does the pandemic seem to hit women much harder than men?  Warning: The story may contain uncomfortable content.  Talking face-to-face with a young woman who has attempted suicide multiple times is a disturbing experience.  It gives me a new respect for those who work on suicide prevention.  I was sitting at a walking center in Yokohama ’ s Red Light District, run by a suicide prevention charity called the Bond Project. Across the table was a 19-year-old woman with a wave head.  She sat motionless.  The image is annotated with text, Tachibana hopes that "Bond Project" can help women.  Quietly, without any emotion, she began to tell her story.  She said it all started when she was 15, when her brother violently abused her.  Eventually she ran away from home, but that didn ’ t end the pain and loneliness.  Ending life seems to be the only way out.  “Since about this time last year, I have been in and out of the hospital many times.  She told me, “I tried to kill myself many times, but it didn ’ t work out, so now I ’ ve given up trying to kill myself. ”  The "Bond Plan" intervened to stop her.  They found a safe place for her and began to give her intensive counseling.  Jun Tachibana is the founder of the Bond Project.  She is a strong woman in her 40s with a relentless optimism.  “When girls are in real trouble and pain, they really don ’ t know what to do.  “We ’ re ready to listen to them and tell them, ‘ We ’ re with you, ’ ” she said. Tachibana said the coronavirus appears to be pushing those who are already vulnerable to the brink.  She described some distressing phone calls that employees have received in recent months.  “We hear a lot of people saying ‘ I want to die ’ and ‘ I have nowhere to go, ’ ” she said.  “They said, ‘ It ’ s too painful, I ’ m lonely, I want to disappear. ’ ”  For those who have suffered physical or sexual abuse, the COVID-19 pandemic has made things worse.  “A girl I talked to the other day said she was being sexually harassed by her father, ” Tachibana told me.“ Because of the COVID-19 pandemic, her father doesn ’ t work much, so she is often at home and she can ’ t escape him. ”  If you look at past crisis periods in Japan, such as the banking crisis in 2008, or the collapse of the Japanese stock market and real estate bubble in the early 1990s, it was mainly middle-aged men who were affected.  The rate of male suicide has risen sharply.  But COVID-19 is different. It affects young people, especially young women.  The reasons are complicated.  Japan had the highest suicide rate among developed countries.  Its huge success over the past decade has reduced the suicide rate by about a third.  The image is annotated with text, and Professor Michiko Ueda believes that the suicide trend of Japanese women during the COVID-19 pandemic is "unusual".  Professor Michiko Ueda is a leading suicide expert in Japan.  She told me that it was shocking to witness the dramatic reversals of the past few months.  “This pattern of female suicide is very, very unusual, ” she told me.  “I have never seen so much increase in my research career in this field.  The sectors most impacted by COVID-19 are those with female employees, such as travel and retail and food. ”  The number of single women living alone in Japan has increased significantly.  Many people choose to be single, rather than a marriage that then requires traditional gender roles.  Professor Michiko Ueda said that young women are also significantly more likely to take up so-called precarious jobs.  “A lot of women don ’ t get married, ” she said.  “They have to feed themselves, and they don ’ t have regular jobs.  So when the crisis happens, of course, they will be hit very, very hard.  This has been the case in the last eight months with a very large number of unemployed non-permanent workers. ”  One month was really outstanding.  Last October, 879 women committed suicide.  This is more than 70% higher than the same period in 2019.  Newspaper headlines sounded the alarm.  The total number of men and women who committed suicide in October (2,199) was compared to the total number of COVID-19 deaths in Japan up to that time (2,087).  Something particularly strange happened.  Image copyright Getty Images Image caption Yuko Takeuchi, a famous Japanese actress, was found dead in her home on September 27 last year at the age of 40.  It was later reported that she committed suicide.  Yasuyuki Shimizu, a former journalist and now runs a non-profit organization (NPO) dedicated to solving Japan ’ s suicide problem, “From the day news of celebrity suicides is reported, the number of suicides will increase, and this will continue for about 10 days. ”  "From the data, we can see that the suicide of the actress on September 27 led to 207 more female suicides in the next 10 days," he said.  If you look at the suicide data of women the same age as Takuchi, the statistical results are even more obvious.  “Of all ages, women in their 40s are most affected, ” Mr. Shimizu said.  “For this group, it has more than doubled. ”  Other experts also believe there is a very strong link between celebrity suicides and an immediate rise in suicide rates in subsequent days.  This phenomenon is not unique to Japan, which is one of the reasons why it is so difficult to report suicides.  After celebrity suicide, the more discussed in the media and social media, the greater the impact on other vulnerable people.  Mai Suganuma is one of the NPO researchers.  She was also a victim of suicide.  When she was a teenager, her father committed suicide.  Now she offers help and support to other families of suicides.  Just as COVID-19 has made it impossible for relatives to grieve for those who have died of the virus, it has also made life harder for families of suicides.  “When I talk to my family, they have a very strong feeling that they can ’ t save their loved ones, which often leads them to blame themselves. ”  Massena told me.  I also blamed myself for not being able to save my father.  Now they were told they had to stay at home.  I ’ m afraid the feeling of guilt is getting stronger.  Japanese people do not like to talk about death at the beginning of their daily conversation.  We don't talk about suicide. "  Image copyright Getty Images Image caption Japan is now in the midst of the third wave of COVID-19, with restaurants, hotels and bars closing.  Japan is now in the midst of the so-called third wave of COVID-19, and the government has ordered a second state of national emergency. Why among women victims more Rupert Wingfield-Hayes BBC News, Tokyo Suicides in Japan are recorded faster and more accurately than anywhere else in the world.  Unlike most countries, reporting is done on a monthly basis.  And during the Covid-19 pandemic, these statistics turned out to be more alarming than before.  In 2020, for the first time in 11 years, the number of suicides in Japan increased.  However, although the number of suicides among men decreased slightly, the increase among women was almost 15%.  In October alone, the suicide rate among women in Japan jumped more than 70% compared to the same month last year.  What's going on?  And why does the pandemic seem to affect women far more than men?  A young woman (her BBC identity unknown) met Rupert Wingfield-Hayes in Yokohama A face-to-face meeting with a young woman who repeatedly tried to commit suicide is not a pleasant experience.  I have a deep respect for people who work on suicide prevention.  I'm sitting in Yokohama's red light district in a center run by a suicide prevention charity called the Bond Project.  Anyone can enter here, no pre-registration is required.  At the table opposite, a 19-year-old woman with a short haircut is sitting motionless.  Quietly, without any emotion in her voice, she begins to tell me her story.  She said it all started when she was 15.  Her older brother began to harass her.  She eventually ran away from home, but the pain and loneliness didn ’ t go away.  Suicide seemed like the only way out.  “I ’ ve been to the hospital many times since that time last year, ” she tells me.“ I tried to kill myself many times, but I didn ’ t succeed.  It seems that attempts to die will have to be abandoned. ”  The Bond Project intervened in her life.  His staff found her a safe place to live and began intensive psychotherapy.  June Tachibana is the founder of the Bond Project, a tough woman in her 40s and a tireless optimist.  Joon Tachibana hopes the Bond Project will provide women with the help they need "When girls are in big trouble and hurt, they really don't know what to do," she says.  "We are ready to listen to them, to tell them - we are with you."  Tachibana says Covid-19 seems to be pushing vulnerable people to make a fateful decision.  She describes some of the calls her employees have received in recent months.  “We often hear ‘ I want to die ’ and ‘ I have nowhere to go, ’ ” she says.  They say, "It's so painful, I'm so lonely, I want to disappear."  The pandemic has made life much more difficult for those who are physically or sexually abused.  “The girl I spoke to the other day said her father was sexually harassing her, ” Tachibana tells me.“ But because of the covid, her father doesn ’ t work much and spends a lot of time at home, and she manages to escape from him. ”  If you look at previous crisis moments in Japan, for example, the banking crisis of 2008 or the collapse of the Japanese stock market and the real estate bubble in the early 1990s, the effect was felt mainly by middle-aged men.  During these periods, there were sharp spikes in the number of suicides among men.  A pandemic is a different story.  It affects young people, especially young women.  The reasons for this are very multifaceted.  At one time, Japan had the highest suicide rate among developed countries.  Over the past decade, it has been reduced by about a third.  Professor Michiko Ueda is one of Japan ’ s leading experts on suicide.  It tells me how alarming the growth dynamics have become over the past few months.  “This scenario leading to female suicide is very, very unusual, ” she says.  “In all the time I ’ ve been doing research on this topic, I ’ ve never seen such significant growth.  The peculiarity of the pandemic is that the industries in which many women are employed - tourism, retail trade and the food industry - have suffered the most. "  In Japan, there are more and more unmarried women living on their own.  Many of them prefer such a life to marriage, which still assumes quite traditional gender roles.  Professor Ueda says that young women are much more likely to find themselves in a state of so-called "casual employment."  Professor Michiko Ueda said: “Many women are no longer married, they have to earn a living, but they don ’ t have a regular job.  So when something happens, of course, they suffer a lot.  The number of lost jobs among non-permanent workers has increased significantly over the past eight months. ”  One month stands out.  In October last year, 879 women committed suicide.  This is more than 70% higher than in October 2019.  Newspapers are alarmed.  Some even compare the total number of suicides (both men and women) in October - 2,199 - with the total number of deaths in Japan from the coronavirus at that time - 2,087.  Something strange has happened.  On September 27 last year, a very famous and popular actress named Yuko Takeuchi was found dead in her home.  It was later reported that she had committed suicide.  Photo caption: 40-year-old Japanese actress Yuko Takeuchi was found dead in her home Yasuyuki Shimizu, a former journalist.  Today, he runs a non-profit organization dedicated to suicide in Japan.  “From the moment it becomes known about the suicide of any celebrity, the number of suicides increases and remains at this new level for about 10 days, ” he says. – For example, for the suicide of Takeuchi on September 27 in the next 10 days, 207 women committed suicide. ”  If you count the number of suicides of women about the same age as Yuko Takeuchi, the statistics become even more obvious.  "Of all age groups, Takeuchi's death has had the greatest impact on women in their 40s and 50s," says Yasuyuki Shimizu. "Suicide rates have more than doubled in this age group."  Other experts also agree that there is a link between celebrity suicides and the spike in suicides in the days that followed.  This phenomenon is not unique to Japan, and this is one of the reasons why reporting suicides is not easy.  The more celebrity suicide is discussed in the media and on social media, the more it affects other vulnerable people, especially in the early days.  Mai Suganuma works for the Shimizu organization.  Her father killed himself when she was a teenager.  Now it helps to support the families of those who have voluntarily passed away.  The pandemic makes the lives of suicide families much more difficult.  “Members of the suicide family often blame themselves for what happened, ” says Mai Suganuma. – I also blamed myself for not being able to save my father.  And now they say, "Stay at home."  I fear that this will increase the sense of guilt.  The Japanese don ’ t usually talk about death.  We don ’ t have the habit of talking about suicide. ”  Japan is now experiencing a third wave of the epidemic, and the government has declared a state of emergency for the second time.  Most likely, it will last until the end of February.  More and more restaurants, hotels and bars are being quarantined, and more people are losing their jobs. passages.passage: Image copyright Reuters Image caption Israel's national security adviser flew to the United Arab Emirates on September 1.  A high-level delegation from Israel and the United Arab Emirates will sign a historic peace agreement led by the United States at the White House on Tuesday, September 15, when the UAE and Israel will formally establish diplomatic relations.  U.S. President Donald Trump announced last week that Bahrain ’ s foreign minister would attend the event and sign a comprehensive normalization agreement with Israel alone.  The signing of these agreements will change the landscape in the Middle East. BBC explains why these agreements are important.  Gulf countries see more trade opportunities This agreement will help ambitious UAE.  They built up their own military forces and developed the UAE into a place of business and holiday.  The Americans used the promise of advanced weapons to help reach this agreement.  In the past, the UAE was barely able to buy weapons including the F-35 stealth fighter and the EA-18G Growler electronic fighter.  The UAE has deployed well-equipped armed forces in Libya and Yemen.  But its greatest potential enemy is Iran on the other side of the Gulf.  Israel, like the United States and the United Arab Emirates, is skeptical of Iran.  The same goes for Bahrain.  Until 1969, Iran claimed Bahrain as part of its territory.  Bahrain ’ s Sunni rulers also believe that members of its unstable Shia majority could become Iran ’ s fifth pillar.  The two Gulf states are no longer hiding ties with Israel.  They expect open trade because Israel has the most advanced high-tech industrial chain in the world.  In the non-Covid-19 era, Israelis are avid vacationers who are passionate about exploring the deserts, beaches and shopping centers around the Gulf.  There are business opportunities everywhere.  For Israel, normalization of relations with the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain is a real achievement.  In the 1920s, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu firmly believed in the strategy of building an “iron wall ” between the Jewish state and the Arab states.  The idea is that Israel ’ s strength will eventually make the Arab states realize that their only option is to acknowledge Israel ’ s existence.  Israelis don ’ t like being isolated in the Middle East.  Peace efforts with Egypt and Jordan have never been so enthusiastic.  They may be more looking forward to a better future relationship with the Gulf states far away from Jerusalem and the occupied territories.  Strengthening the anti-Iran coalition is another major advantage.  Netanyahu views Iran as Israel ’ s number one enemy, sometimes comparing its leaders to the Nazis.  He has dropped his previous complaints about the UAE arms deal.  Netanyahu is also troubled, and he is facing a possible jail term for corruption.  His handling of the COVID-19 pandemic went well in the early stages, and badly in the later stages.  Opponents gather weekly outside his Jerusalem residence.  The ceremony at the White House was appropriate.  Image copyright Reuters Image caption Trump announced the so-called Abraham Accord at the White House in August. 3.  Trump celebrated the foreign policy coup, an agreement that has implications for the president of the United States on multiple levels.  This is conducive to Trump ’ s “maximum pressure ” strategy on Iran.  In the year of the election, this helps to support his claim that he is the best trader in the world.  Anything he does that is good for Israel, or more specifically for Netanyahu ’ s government, is good for maintaining good relations with Christian evangelical voters in the United States.  These are important parts of his constituency.  If the Arab states in the Gulf can handle their relations with Israel openly, rather than secretly, then the anti-Iran “Friends of America ” coalition should work more smoothly.  Trump ’ s so-called “deal of the century ” has made peace between Israel and the Palestinians impossible.  But the Abraham Accords between Israel and the UAE are known to have led to a major shift in the Middle East landscape, which the Trump administration has called a major foreign policy coup.  Image copyright Reuters Image caption Palestinian leaders have condemned the actions of the two Gulf states to restore relations with Israel.  The Palestinians felt betrayed that they were once again the last of the tournament.  The Palestinians condemned the Abrahamic Agreement as a betrayal.  The new agreement breaks the long-standing Arab consensus that the price of establishing diplomatic relations with Israel is recognition of Palestinian independence.  But now, Israel is consolidating new public relations with the Arab states, while the Palestinians remain occupied in East Jerusalem, the West Bank, and an area the size of an open prison in Gaza.  Mohammed Al Nahyan, the de facto ruler of the UAE, said his price for the deal was Israel ’ s agreement to stop annexing large parts of the West Bank.  At least because of the current international pressure, Netanyahu seems to have abandoned the idea.  The UAE offered him a way out of the embarrassing political deadlock.  Bahrain joined the agreement and Palestinian tensions increased.  Without Saudi Arabia ’ s approval, that would never have happened.  Saudi Arabia is the leader of the Arab Peace Plan for Palestinian independence.  King Kal Salman was the administrator of two temples in Islam, which gave him great authority.  He is unlikely to suddenly recognize Israel's independence.  His son and successor, Mohammed bin Salman, may also be reluctant to do so. Thus, Sudan became another country to join the “Abrahamic Agreements ”.  “By the way, the Palestinians, if you ask about the Palestinians, want to do something about it.  They've never seen anything like it.  They want to do something.  I am sure that this will also be done, "TASS quoted the head of the White House as saying.  According to the American leader, now “at least five ” Muslim countries want to sign agreements on the normalization of relations with Israel.  And as Trump added, there will soon be many more.  Earlier in October, the Knesset of Israel approved an agreement on the normalization of relations between the Jewish state and the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain.  The agreements on normalization of relations were signed on September 15 at the White House by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, UAE Foreign Minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan and Bahraini Foreign Minister Abdel Latif al-Zayani.  The event was held at the White House in the presence of US President Donald Trump, his wife Melania and invited guests.  One of the points of the “Abraham accords ” implies a suspension by Israel of the extension of its sovereignty to Jewish settlements in the West Bank.  This condition is spelled out in Washington ’ s plan to resolve the Palestinian-Israeli conflict.  The signing of the agreements was condemned in Palestine.  They recalled their ambassador to the UAE and called Abu Dhabi ’ s actions an aggression against its people and a disregard for their rights and shrines.  The Arab Peace Initiative adopted in 2002, on which Palestine is based, provides for the possibility of concluding peace agreements and establishing good-neighbourly relations between the Arabs and Israel, but only if the Jewish State withdraws from the territories it occupied in 1967, including the Golan Heights and the Shab'a farms, and recognizes the State of Palestine in the West Bank and Gaza Strip, with East Jerusalem as its capital.

passages.title: Abu Dhabi and Manama betrayed Palestinian ideals
passages.passage: According to the Al-Ahad news agency, Sami Abu Zuhri, a senior member of the Hamas movement, reacted to the signing of a compromise agreement by Al-Khalifa and Al-Nahyan with the Zionist regime.  According to the report, he said that the officials of Abu Dhabi and Manama betrayed the Palestinian ideals through compromise with the Zionists.  Abu Zuhri said that a compromise agreement with the Zionist regime cannot bring peace to Abu Dhabi and Manama.  The struggle of the nations of the region against the Zionist enemy will continue.  The officials of Bahrain, the United Arab Emirates, Israel and the United States last night at a ceremony at the White House signed a compromise agreement called the “Abraham Peace Agreement. ”  The goal of the agreement is to normalize relations with Tel Aviv.  The ceremony was attended by US President Donald Trump along with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and the foreign ministers of the UAE and Bahrain.

passages.title: Trump mediates with UAE, Israel to agree to establish diplomatic relations
passages.passage: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu (left) and Prince Mohammed of Abu Dhabi, the United Arab Emirates, announced that the two countries have reached a peace agreement and relations will be fully normalized. (AFP) 2020-08-15 05: 30: 00 Palestine denounces the betrayal of Turkey's severance of diplomatic relations. On the third day, it was announced that a peace agreement had been reached, diplomatic relations would be fully normalized, and Israel agreed to suspend the annexation of Jewish settlements in the West Bank in exchange for the Arab League agreeing to become the third Arab country to recognize Israel after Egypt and Jordan, and the first Persian Gulf country to establish diplomatic relations with Israel.  The Palestinian self-rule government has been reviled by the Arab League for betrayal, Israel ’ s arch-enemy Iran has denounced it as a stupid strategy, and Turkey has threatened to sever ties with the Arab League.  In a joint statement, Trump, the first Gulf state to recognize Israel, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, and Saudi Arabia ’ s Prince Mohammed bin Zayed Al-Nahyan announced that they had agreed to normalize full Israeli-Arab relations and “chart a new path that opens up great potential in the Middle East. ”  The Israeli-Arab peace agreement, known as the "Abraham Accords" and described as a "historic" and "breakthrough for peace," will be signed at the White House. It will include strengthening bilateral economic relations, scientific and technological cooperation, the opening of direct flights, and the exchange of ambassadors and the establishment of embassies in the Arab capital Abu Dhabi and the Israeli city of Tel Aviv. Israel's new capital, Jerusalem, has established an embassy.  Please continue reading...  Suspension of the annexation of the West Bank?  However, the key to the agreement is whether Israel ’ s annexation of the West Bank will be suspended or suspended. The joint statement said that Israel will “suspend ” its declaration of sovereignty over the West Bank, but the Arab League ’ s Mohammed then said on Twitter that the agreement is a“ cessation ” of the annexation of Palestinian territory, but the hawk Netanyahu later insisted in a televised speech that the annexation plan was only "We will never renounce our rights to our territory."  The Israeli-Palestinian conflict has continued since Israel took the West Bank from the Palestinians in 1967 in the Six-Day War.  In his Middle East peace plan in January this year, Trump agreed to Israel's annexation of the West Bank of the Jordan River, with the government setting July 1 as the start date of the annexation plan.  The Palestinian Authority expressed "strong opposition and condemnation" to the establishment of diplomatic relations between Israel and Arab countries, viewing the Arab League's move as a betrayal and demanding an urgent meeting of the Arab League. Iran's Foreign Ministry criticized the establishment of diplomatic relations between the Arab League and Israel as a "strategic folly".  Israel has been boycotted by the Arab world and Muslim countries for historical and religious reasons, and isolated by its neighbors because of its geographical location.  But the United Kingdom, Germany, Bahrain, and Egypt, which has established diplomatic relations with Israel, are happy to see normalization.  U.S. President Donald Trump receives applause from the Middle East Policy team at the White House Oval Office after Israel and the United Arab Emirates reached a peace agreement.  From left, there are US Special Envoy to Iran, US Special Representative to the President and Special Representative for International Negotiations, US Ambassador to Israel Freeman, Trump son-in-law and Mideast peace plan planner Kushner, and US Treasury Secretary John Nuqin.

The agreement, brokered by the United States and signed by the United States, Israel, the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain, normalizes relations between these countries and further isolates Tehran.  The agreement also excludes Palestinians, who have not had contact with the Trump administration or its peace efforts since Washington recognized Jerusalem as Israel ’ s capital.  The deal upended nearly a century of regional politics and business and united America ’ s key allies in the volatile Middle East.  It's...

passages.passage: A Palestinian official said the Palestinian Authority would once again send its ambassadors to the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain.  This is while the Palestinian Authority has previously recalled its ambassadors from the two Arab Gulf states in protest of the agreement to normalize diplomatic relations between the UAE and Bahrain.  It should be noted that on September 15, Bahrain, following the United Arab Emirates, began its formal relations with the Zionist regime by signing an agreement called the “Abraham Agreement ”.  Subsequently, in October, a group of senior Israeli and American officials visited Bahrain and signed several memorandums of cooperation with Manama officials in the fields of economics, energy, aviation, and so on.  In the latest developments, Bahraini Foreign Minister Abdul Latif bin Rashid al-Ziyani, who traveled to occupied Palestine on Wednesday (November 18), called for the opening of the Bahraini embassy in the Zionist regime.  He claimed that “Bahrain is committed to peace and peaceful coexistence and acceptance of the other. ”  During a joint press conference with Israeli Foreign Minister Gabi Ashkenazi, Al Khalifa ’ s foreign minister spoke about the role of the United States in the realization of peace and invited his Zionist counterpart to travel to Manama.

passages.title: Zionists' actions in support of civil wars
passages.passage: A report published by the Al-Zaitouneh Research Center shows that the Zionist regime is leading the way in selling weapons to dictatorial regimes and spy equipment to Arab countries to spy on human rights activists along with money laundering.  The Al-Zaitouneh Research Center is an independent center in Beirut, founded in 2004, that conducts research on issues related to the Arab and Islamic world, particularly the Palestinian issue.  Unfortunately, some Arab countries and Arab political institutions are buying weapons from the Zionist regime.  This makes dialogue between Palestinian resistance groups and Arab political parties more necessary to counter such actions.  According to the report, Israel has been arming separatist movements in South Sudan, and the Sudanese have not reacted very seriously.  Referring to the nuclear actions of the Zionist regime, the report said that it is necessary to resume Arab studies on the dangers of the Zionist regime ’ s nuclear program against the Middle East.  These studies should be focused on the efforts of the Zionists in the production of chemical and biological weapons.  NSO Group Technologies is an Israeli spy company that uses its programs to spy on human rights activists and journalists around the world.  The company ’ s spy programs have also been used to assassinate Saudi activist Jamal Khashoggi, a critic of the Saudi regime, according to the report, the Zionist regime has not signed any of the agreements on the non-proliferation of nuclear, biological or chemical weapons.  Interestingly, these weapons end up in the hands of dictatorial regimes that violate human rights.  In addition, the Zionist regime is trying to support civil wars and power struggles by sending these weapons.  We are witnessing a process of money laundering and espionage along with the sale of these weapons in general, which is confirmed by the reports of international delegations and academic research.  Israel did not even sign the arms trade agreement, which was ratified by 82 countries in 2012, as it considers humanitarian and human rights issues an obstacle to its arms deals.  According to the report, the Zionist regime is working secretly with security companies in order to transfer weapons.  Spying-related technologies are another area of concern: NSO Group Technologies is one of the Zionist spy companies whose programs are used to spy on human rights activists and journalists around the world.  The company ’ s spy programs have also been used to assassinate Saudi activist Jamal Khashoggi, a critic of the Saudi regime.  According to the report, the Israeli company ’ s plans have been sold to the UAE, Morocco, Bahrain and Saudi Arabia.

passages.title: The Russian Jewish Congress commented on the accusations of human rights defenders against Israel
passages.passage: The human rights organization Human Rights Watch released a report in which it claims that the Israeli authorities commit crimes of apartheid in order to preserve the dominance of Jewish Israelis over the Palestinians.  This position is shared by the Israeli NGO B ’ Tselem, which collects information on human rights violations in the disputed territories.  These include the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, and the Gaza Strip, calling them Israeli-occupied territories.  HRW ’ s report is based on years of human rights monitoring, government planning documents, official statements, and other sources.  The experts compared the policy and real actions in the disputed territories and in Israel itself against the Palestinians and the Jewish population.  According to the organization, in July last year, a letter was sent to the Israeli authorities in which they were invited to present their vision of the situation, but a response has not yet been received.  German Zakharyaev, vice president of the Russian Jewish Congress (RJC) and president of the STMEGI Mountain Jews Foundation, called the entire HRW report not a serious study, but a damning pamphlet aimed at stigmatizing Israel as an apartheid state.  “The report is based on the false image of Israel as the country controlling the entire West Bank and Gaza Strip, but in reality it is not, only a few dozen Jewish settlements and a number of highways leading to them are under Israeli control.  The rest of the population is under the control of Mahmoud Abbas's Palestinian Authority and the Hamas movement in the Gaza Strip, "he said.  According to Zakharyaev, on the territory of Israel proper, Arab citizens are absolutely equal.  At the same time, he recognized the persistence of a significant difference in the social status and material situation of the Jewish and Arab populations.  At the same time, the vice-president of the RJC recalled that the same difference exists within the Jewish population - between immigrants from Europe and the countries of the East.  What does the report say?  Allocation of land.  It follows from the report that the authorities, both in Israel itself and in the disputed territories, mainly seek to provide land for Jewish communities.  Most Palestinians are driven into densely populated areas.  The organization also claims the existence of a certain policy of neutralization: for example, the state plan for the development of Jerusalem proceeds from the need for “confident preservation of the Jewish majority ” and even provides for desirable demographic proportions.  German Zakharyaev explained to Gazeta.ru that the Arab population prefers to live in large families and so-called hamuls, build houses near their loved ones in the territories of their towns and cities.  Moreover, he said, these structures are often illegal, allowing Palestinians to bypass the long and costly process of buying and registering property.  Cut off from the local community.  According to HRW, Israel has laws that allow hundreds of small Jewish municipalities to effectively cut off Palestinians from the local community.  In addition, according to the document, only a small part of the budget is allocated to Palestinian schools compared to the financing of schools where Jewish Israeli children study.  The report points out that in the disputed territories, the intensity of repression against Palestinians reaches the level of “systematic oppression ” as one of the hallmarks of apartheid.  The document refers to a draconian military administration for Palestinians in these territories, while Jewish Israelis living separately there are provided with the full range of rights under Israel ’ s model civil code.  Israeli political scientist, former adviser to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu Benny Briskin, said in a comment to Gazeta.ru that Israel ’ s judicial system is built in such a way that every real violation of human rights that occurs either in the disputed territories of the Palestinian Authority, or in the territory of Israel itself in relation to the Arabs, is checked and the guilty is always punished.  “Of course, there are exaggerations, but the Israeli judicial system is recognized by the whole world as serious, independent, which deals with all cases, ” he said.  Freedom of movement.  The authors of the report cite as serious violations of the fundamental rights of the Palestinians and the “inhumane actions ” against their freedom of movement in the form of the closure of the Gaza Strip and the imposition of a permit regime, the confiscation of more than a third of land in the West Bank with the forced eviction of thousands of Palestinians, the denial of housing rights, and the suspension of basic civil rights for millions of Palestinians.  Many of the violations underlying these crimes, according to the authors of the report, cannot be justified in the interests of security, including the almost complete ban on the issuance of building permits to Palestinians and the demolition of thousands of houses on the pretext of lack of such a permit.  There are also cases, according to human rights activists, when demographic goals are covered by security interests, as in the situation with the de facto freezing by the Israeli authorities of the registration of residents in the disputed territories.  The organization noted that this almost completely blocks the reunification of families of Palestinians living there and deprives residents of the Gaza Strip of the opportunity to get to the West Bank.  According to the RJC vice-president, the Gaza Strip is an independent administrative unit, from where Israel completely withdrew its army and settlements in 2005, and where today Hamas, recognized in Israel as a terrorist organization, is in power.  “Any interaction with it should be confirmed at the state and legislative level.  To date, based on security needs, some kind of restrictions are imposed.  It seems to me that it is difficult to interact with the administration, which for any reason or for no reason fires missiles at civilians, ” he said.  In addition, HRW recalled the constitutional law adopted in 2018, according to which Israel was declared the “national state of the Jewish people ”.  The authors of the document are convinced that the growing body of legislation increasingly favors Jewish settlers in the West Bank and does not extend to Palestinians living there.  As explained by German Zakharyaev, this law is designed to strengthen the status of Israel as a Jewish state.  According to the seventh paragraph of this law, the state of Israel sees the development of Jewish settlements as a national value for the entire Jewish people, he noted.  In addition, the expert drew attention to the fact that this law does not say anything about Jewish settlers in the West Bank, but only about the nature of the State of Israel.  Benny Briskin called such reports not new to Israel.  According to him, in Israel there are two points of view on this: either it is ordinary anti-Semitism, or it is left-wing liberalism.  But in any case, the result is the same - the attitude towards Israel is based on double standards, he stated.  “The approach of human rights organizations is that everything that happens in the territories they call occupied is already a crime.  It does not matter how the Jewish population behaves.  In Israel, they are already accustomed to this, ” the political scientist said.  He argues that the facts do not fit into these allegations.  The facts that lead human rights organizations, Briskin called slanderous fabrications of one side.  “That is, they find a Palestinian who tells a story that he was told to tell by the Palestinian secret services.  This is not verified in any way and is exposed as an unquestionable fact, ” he said.  “The claims of apartheid seem particularly absurd today, when Mansour Abbas — leader of the Joint Arab List in the Knesset — holds Israel ’ s political future in the wake of the March elections.  His voice is key in determining who will form the next governing coalition in Israel: Benjamin Netanyahu and his far-right supporters or the camp of his opponents.  Both sides are courting Abbas, which is hardly a sign of apartheid, ” said German Zakharyaev, president of the STMEGI Mountain Jews Foundation.

passages.title: Human Rights Watch: Israel and Hamas May Have Committed War Crimes
passages.passage: Human Rights Watch said on Tuesday that both Israel and Hamas may have committed war crimes during the May clashes.  During the 11-day battle, Hamas and other Palestinian groups fired thousands of rockets into Israeli territory and the Israeli army bombed the Gaza Strip from the ground and air.  Human Rights Watch said it used interviews with local residents and eyewitnesses, data analysis and digital images to produce its report.  According to the human rights organization, 62 Palestinian civilians were killed in three Israeli attacks in areas where no evidence of armed personnel has been found.  The report specifically examines Israeli air strikes on May 10 on the small town of Beit Hanoun in the northeast Gaza Strip, May 15 on the al-Shati refugee camp and May 16 on the city of Gaza.  Human Rights Watch added that “other Israeli attacks during this battle were also likely in violation of international law. ”  Eight people, including six children, were killed in an attack on May 10 that destroyed several homes.  At this point, Human Rights Watch says there is no indication of the presence of the armed forces or its use for military purposes.  “Any attack that does not have specific military objectives violates international law. ”  In the May 15 attack on the al-Shati refugee camp, a three-storey residential building was targeted and 10 people were killed.  A resident told Human Rights Watch that residents were not given any warning about the attack.  Israel claims that the reason for the attack was the presence of several senior Hamas leaders in the residential complex.  Human Rights Watch said no witnesses or family members of the victims confirmed the presence of Hamas operatives in or around the building.  It added that the building was likely targeted by a bomb produced by Boeing that the United States exported to Israel.  A third attack on May 16 killed three destroyed buildings and 44 civilians, including 18 children and 14 women, in Gaza City.  Human Rights Watch said eyewitnesses interviewed said Israel gave no warning before the attack.  Israeli army videos and pieces of munitions collected by Palestinian police show that the attack was also carried out by a one-ton Boeing bomb.  At the time of the attack, Israel said it was targeting Hamas militants' tunnels, but Human Rights Watch said it found "no evidence of military targets".  Human Rights Watch also condemned “reckless ” missile attacks on Israeli civilians and said it would address the issue in a separate report.  “Israel and the Palestinians have violated international law in this battle, which could amount to war crimes. ”  The Israeli government has not yet responded to the report, but a Hamas spokesman said: "This report shows that the occupation government acts with complete impunity and beyond the law and is never punished because of the full support of the United States."  In March, a prosecutor at the International Criminal Court announced a new and comprehensive investigation into the situation in the occupied Palestinian territories.  The main focus of the study will be the 2014 war in the Gaza Strip, but it will also look at the deaths of Palestinian protesters since 2018.  On May 27, the UN Human Rights Council approved an international investigation into the recent fighting in the Gaza Strip.  According to the local government of the Gaza Strip, 260 Palestinians, including gunmen, have been killed in the recent clashes.  The Israeli government says 13 people have been killed in the country, including a military man.  According to a report by the French news agency / Sr / Kr

Title: The Russian Jewish Congress commented on the accusations of human rights defenders against Israel
Content: The human rights organization Human Rights Watch released a report in which it claims that the Israeli authorities commit crimes of apartheid in order to preserve the dominance of Jewish Israelis over the Palestinians.  This position is shared by the Israeli NGO B ’ Tselem, which collects information on human rights violations in the disputed territories.  These include the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, and the Gaza Strip, calling them Israeli-occupied territories.  HRW ’ s report is based on years of human rights monitoring, government planning documents, official statements, and other sources.  The experts compared the policy and real actions in the disputed territories and in Israel itself against the Palestinians and the Jewish population.  According to the organization, in July last year, a letter was sent to the Israeli authorities in which they were invited to present their vision of the situation, but a response has not yet been received.  German Zakharyaev, vice president of the Russian Jewish Congress (RJC) and president of the STMEGI Mountain Jews Foundation, called the entire HRW report not a serious study, but a damning pamphlet aimed at stigmatizing Israel as an apartheid state.  “The report is based on the false image of Israel as the country controlling the entire West Bank and Gaza Strip, but in reality it is not, only a few dozen Jewish settlements and a number of highways leading to them are under Israeli control.  The rest of the population is under the control of Mahmoud Abbas's Palestinian Authority and the Hamas movement in the Gaza Strip, "he said.  According to Zakharyaev, on the territory of Israel proper, Arab citizens are absolutely equal.  At the same time, he recognized the persistence of a significant difference in the social status and material situation of the Jewish and Arab populations.  At the same time, the vice-president of the RJC recalled that the same difference exists within the Jewish population - between immigrants from Europe and the countries of the East.  What does the report say?  Allocation of land.  It follows from the report that the authorities, both in Israel itself and in the disputed territories, mainly seek to provide land for Jewish communities.  Most Palestinians are driven into densely populated areas.  The organization also claims the existence of a certain policy of neutralization: for example, the state plan for the development of Jerusalem proceeds from the need for “confident preservation of the Jewish majority ” and even provides for desirable demographic proportions.  German Zakharyaev explained to Gazeta.ru that the Arab population prefers to live in large families and so-called hamuls, build houses near their loved ones in the territories of their towns and cities.  Moreover, he said, these structures are often illegal, allowing Palestinians to bypass the long and costly process of buying and registering property.  Cut off from the local community.  According to HRW, Israel has laws that allow hundreds of small Jewish municipalities to effectively cut off Palestinians from the local community.  In addition, according to the document, only a small part of the budget is allocated to Palestinian schools compared to the financing of schools where Jewish Israeli children study.  The report points out that in the disputed territories, the intensity of repression against Palestinians reaches the level of “systematic oppression ” as one of the hallmarks of apartheid.  The document refers to a draconian military administration for Palestinians in these territories, while Jewish Israelis living separately there are provided with the full range of rights under Israel ’ s model civil code.  Israeli political scientist, former adviser to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu Benny Briskin, said in a comment to Gazeta.ru that Israel ’ s judicial system is built in such a way that every real violation of human rights that occurs either in the disputed territories of the Palestinian Authority, or in the territory of Israel itself in relation to the Arabs, is checked and the guilty is always punished.  “Of course, there are exaggerations, but the Israeli judicial system is recognized by the whole world as serious, independent, which deals with all cases, ” he said.  Freedom of movement.  The authors of the report cite as serious violations of the fundamental rights of the Palestinians and the “inhumane actions ” against their freedom of movement in the form of the closure of the Gaza Strip and the imposition of a permit regime, the confiscation of more than a third of land in the West Bank with the forced eviction of thousands of Palestinians, the denial of housing rights, and the suspension of basic civil rights for millions of Palestinians.  Many of the violations underlying these crimes, according to the authors of the report, cannot be justified in the interests of security, including the almost complete ban on the issuance of building permits to Palestinians and the demolition of thousands of houses on the pretext of lack of such a permit.  There are also cases, according to human rights activists, when demographic goals are covered by security interests, as in the situation with the de facto freezing by the Israeli authorities of the registration of residents in the disputed territories.  The organization noted that this almost completely blocks the reunification of families of Palestinians living there and deprives residents of the Gaza Strip of the opportunity to get to the West Bank.  According to the RJC vice-president, the Gaza Strip is an independent administrative unit, from where Israel completely withdrew its army and settlements in 2005, and where today Hamas, recognized in Israel as a terrorist organization, is in power.  “Any interaction with it should be confirmed at the state and legislative level.  To date, based on security needs, some kind of restrictions are imposed.  It seems to me that it is difficult to interact with the administration, which for any reason or for no reason fires missiles at civilians, ” he said.  In addition, HRW recalled the constitutional law adopted in 2018, according to which Israel was declared the “national state of the Jewish people ”.  The authors of the document are convinced that the growing body of legislation increasingly favors Jewish settlers in the West Bank and does not extend to Palestinians living there.  As explained by German Zakharyaev, this law is designed to strengthen the status of Israel as a Jewish state.  According to the seventh paragraph of this law, the state of Israel sees the development of Jewish settlements as a national value for the entire Jewish people, he noted.  In addition, the expert drew attention to the fact that this law does not say anything about Jewish settlers in the West Bank, but only about the nature of the State of Israel.  Benny Briskin called such reports not new to Israel.  According to him, in Israel there are two points of view on this: either it is ordinary anti-Semitism, or it is left-wing liberalism.  But in any case, the result is the same - the attitude towards Israel is based on double standards, he stated.  “The approach of human rights organizations is that everything that happens in the territories they call occupied is already a crime.  It does not matter how the Jewish population behaves.  In Israel, they are already accustomed to this, ” the political scientist said.  He argues that the facts do not fit into these allegations.  The facts that lead human rights organizations, Briskin called slanderous fabrications of one side.  “That is, they find a Palestinian who tells a story that he was told to tell by the Palestinian secret services.  This is not verified in any way and is exposed as an unquestionable fact, ” he said.  “The claims of apartheid seem particularly absurd today, when Mansour Abbas — leader of the Joint Arab List in the Knesset — holds Israel ’ s political future in the wake of the March elections.  His voice is key in determining who will form the next governing coalition in Israel: Benjamin Netanyahu and his far-right supporters or the camp of his opponents.  Both sides are courting Abbas, which is hardly a sign of apartheid, ” said German Zakharyaev, president of the STMEGI Mountain Jews Foundation.

Title: Human Rights Watch: Israel and Hamas May Have Committed War Crimes
Content: Human Rights Watch said on Tuesday that both Israel and Hamas may have committed war crimes during the May clashes.  During the 11-day battle, Hamas and other Palestinian groups fired thousands of rockets into Israeli territory and the Israeli army bombed the Gaza Strip from the ground and air.  Human Rights Watch said it used interviews with local residents and eyewitnesses, data analysis and digital images to produce its report.  According to the human rights organization, 62 Palestinian civilians were killed in three Israeli attacks in areas where no evidence of armed personnel has been found.  The report specifically examines Israeli air strikes on May 10 on the small town of Beit Hanoun in the northeast Gaza Strip, May 15 on the al-Shati refugee camp and May 16 on the city of Gaza.  Human Rights Watch added that “other Israeli attacks during this battle were also likely in violation of international law. ”  Eight people, including six children, were killed in an attack on May 10 that destroyed several homes.  At this point, Human Rights Watch says there is no indication of the presence of the armed forces or its use for military purposes.  “Any attack that does not have specific military objectives violates international law. ”  In the May 15 attack on the al-Shati refugee camp, a three-storey residential building was targeted and 10 people were killed.  A resident told Human Rights Watch that residents were not given any warning about the attack.  Israel claims that the reason for the attack was the presence of several senior Hamas leaders in the residential complex.  Human Rights Watch said no witnesses or family members of the victims confirmed the presence of Hamas operatives in or around the building.  It added that the building was likely targeted by a bomb produced by Boeing that the United States exported to Israel.  A third attack on May 16 killed three destroyed buildings and 44 civilians, including 18 children and 14 women, in Gaza City.  Human Rights Watch said eyewitnesses interviewed said Israel gave no warning before the attack.  Israeli army videos and pieces of munitions collected by Palestinian police show that the attack was also carried out by a one-ton Boeing bomb.  At the time of the attack, Israel said it was targeting Hamas militants' tunnels, but Human Rights Watch said it found "no evidence of military targets".  Human Rights Watch also condemned “reckless ” missile attacks on Israeli civilians and said it would address the issue in a separate report.  “Israel and the Palestinians have violated international law in this battle, which could amount to war crimes. ”  The Israeli government has not yet responded to the report, but a Hamas spokesman said: "This report shows that the occupation government acts with complete impunity and beyond the law and is never punished because of the full support of the United States." Title: Trump said about the possible desire of Palestine to normalize ties with Israel
Content: US President Donald Trump believes that the state of Palestine would also like to take some steps to normalize relations with Israel.  He said this on Friday, October 23, in the presence of journalists during a telephone conversation with the leaders of Israel and Sudan.  Earlier, it was officially announced that the two countries had reached an agreement on normalizing ties through the mediation of the United States.  Thus, Sudan became another country to join the “Abrahamic Agreements ”.  “By the way, the Palestinians, if you ask about the Palestinians, want to do something about it.  They've never seen anything like it.  They want to do something.  I am sure that this will also be done, "TASS quoted the head of the White House as saying. Earlier in October, the Knesset of Israel approved an agreement on the normalization of relations between the Jewish state and the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain.  The agreements on normalization of relations were signed on September 15 at the White House by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, UAE Foreign Minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan and Bahraini Foreign Minister Abdel Latif al-Zayani.  The event was held at the White House in the presence of US President Donald Trump, his wife Melania and invited guests.  One of the points of the “Abraham accords ” implies a suspension by Israel of the extension of its sovereignty to Jewish settlements in the West Bank.  This condition is spelled out in Washington ’ s plan to resolve the Palestinian-Israeli conflict.  The signing of the agreements was condemned in Palestine.  They recalled their ambassador to the UAE and called Abu Dhabi ’ s actions an aggression against its people and a disregard for their rights and shrines.  The Arab Peace Initiative adopted in 2002, on which Palestine is based, provides for the possibility of concluding peace agreements and establishing good-neighbourly relations between the Arabs and Israel, but only if the Jewish State withdraws from the territories it occupied in 1967, including the Golan Heights and the Shab'a farms, and recognizes the State of Palestine in the West Bank and Gaza Strip, with East Jerusalem as its capital.

Title: The Russian Jewish Congress commented on the accusations of human rights defenders against Israel
Content: The human rights organization Human Rights Watch released a report in which it claims that the Israeli authorities commit crimes of apartheid in order to preserve the dominance of Jewish Israelis over the Palestinians.  This position is shared by the Israeli NGO B ’ Tselem, which collects information on human rights violations in the disputed territories.  These include the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, and the Gaza Strip, calling them Israeli-occupied territories.  HRW ’ s report is based on years of human rights monitoring, government planning documents, official statements, and other sources.  The experts compared the policy and real actions in the disputed territories and in Israel itself against the Palestinians and the Jewish population.  According to the organization, in July last year, a letter was sent to the Israeli authorities in which they were invited to present their vision of the situation, but a response has not yet been received.  German Zakharyaev, vice president of the Russian Jewish Congress (RJC) and president of the STMEGI Mountain Jews Foundation, called the entire HRW report not a serious study, but a damning pamphlet aimed at stigmatizing Israel as an apartheid state.  “The report is based on the false image of Israel as the country controlling the entire West Bank and Gaza Strip, but in reality it is not, only a few dozen Jewish settlements and a number of highways leading to them are under Israeli control.  The rest of the population is under the control of Mahmoud Abbas's Palestinian Authority and the Hamas movement in the Gaza Strip, "he said.  According to Zakharyaev, on the territory of Israel proper, Arab citizens are absolutely equal.  At the same time, he recognized the persistence of a significant difference in the social status and material situation of the Jewish and Arab populations.  At the same time, the vice-president of the RJC recalled that the same difference exists within the Jewish population - between immigrants from Europe and the countries of the East.  What does the report say?  Allocation of land.  It follows from the report that the authorities, both in Israel itself and in the disputed territories, mainly seek to provide land for Jewish communities.  Most Palestinians are driven into densely populated areas.  The organization also claims the existence of a certain policy of neutralization: for example, the state plan for the development of Jerusalem proceeds from the need for “confident preservation of the Jewish majority ” and even provides for desirable demographic proportions.  German Zakharyaev explained to Gazeta.ru that the Arab population prefers to live in large families and so-called hamuls, build houses near their loved ones in the territories of their towns and cities.  Moreover, he said, these structures are often illegal, allowing Palestinians to bypass the long and costly process of buying and registering property.  Cut off from the local community.  According to HRW, Israel has laws that allow hundreds of small Jewish municipalities to effectively cut off Palestinians from the local community.  In addition, according to the document, only a small part of the budget is allocated to Palestinian schools compared to the financing of schools where Jewish Israeli children study.  The report points out that in the disputed territories, the intensity of repression against Palestinians reaches the level of “systematic oppression ” as one of the hallmarks of apartheid.  The document refers to a draconian military administration for Palestinians in these territories, while Jewish Israelis living separately there are provided with the full range of rights under Israel ’ s model civil code.  Israeli political scientist, former adviser to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu Benny Briskin, said in a comment to Gazeta.ru that Israel ’ s judicial system is built in such a way that every real violation of human rights that occurs either in the disputed territories of the Palestinian Authority, or in the territory of Israel itself in relation to the Arabs, is checked and the guilty is always punished.  “Of course, there are exaggerations, but the Israeli judicial system is recognized by the whole world as serious, independent, which deals with all cases, ” he said.  Freedom of movement.  The authors of the report cite as serious violations of the fundamental rights of the Palestinians and the “inhumane actions ” against their freedom of movement in the form of the closure of the Gaza Strip and the imposition of a permit regime, the confiscation of more than a third of land in the West Bank with the forced eviction of thousands of Palestinians, the denial of housing rights, and the suspension of basic civil rights for millions of Palestinians.  Many of the violations underlying these crimes, according to the authors of the report, cannot be justified in the interests of security, including the almost complete ban on the issuance of building permits to Palestinians and the demolition of thousands of houses on the pretext of lack of such a permit.  There are also cases, according to human rights activists, when demographic goals are covered by security interests, as in the situation with the de facto freezing by the Israeli authorities of the registration of residents in the disputed territories.  The organization noted that this almost completely blocks the reunification of families of Palestinians living there and deprives residents of the Gaza Strip of the opportunity to get to the West Bank.  According to the RJC vice-president, the Gaza Strip is an independent administrative unit, from where Israel completely withdrew its army and settlements in 2005, and where today Hamas, recognized in Israel as a terrorist organization, is in power.  “Any interaction with it should be confirmed at the state and legislative level.  To date, based on security needs, some kind of restrictions are imposed.  It seems to me that it is difficult to interact with the administration, which for any reason or for no reason fires missiles at civilians, ” he said.  In addition, HRW recalled the constitutional law adopted in 2018, according to which Israel was declared the “national state of the Jewish people ”.  The authors of the document are convinced that the growing body of legislation increasingly favors Jewish settlers in the West Bank and does not extend to Palestinians living there.  As explained by German Zakharyaev, this law is designed to strengthen the status of Israel as a Jewish state.  According to the seventh paragraph of this law, the state of Israel sees the development of Jewish settlements as a national value for the entire Jewish people, he noted.  In addition, the expert drew attention to the fact that this law does not say anything about Jewish settlers in the West Bank, but only about the nature of the State of Israel.  Benny Briskin called such reports not new to Israel.  According to him, in Israel there are two points of view on this: either it is ordinary anti-Semitism, or it is left-wing liberalism.  But in any case, the result is the same - the attitude towards Israel is based on double standards, he stated.  “The approach of human rights organizations is that everything that happens in the territories they call occupied is already a crime.  It does not matter how the Jewish population behaves.  In Israel, they are already accustomed to this, ” the political scientist said.  He argues that the facts do not fit into these allegations.  The facts that lead human rights organizations, Briskin called slanderous fabrications of one side.  “That is, they find a Palestinian who tells a story that he was told to tell by the Palestinian secret services.  This is not verified in any way and is exposed as an unquestionable fact, ” he said.  “The claims of apartheid seem particularly absurd today, when Mansour Abbas — leader of the Joint Arab List in the Knesset — holds Israel ’ s political future in the wake of the March elections.  His voice is key in determining who will form the next governing coalition in Israel: Benjamin Netanyahu and his far-right supporters or the camp of his opponents.  Both sides are courting Abbas, which is hardly a sign of apartheid, ” said German Zakharyaev, president of the STMEGI Mountain Jews Foundation.
