Title: Human Rights Watch: Israel and Hamas May Have Committed War Crimes
Content: Human Rights Watch said on Tuesday that both Israel and Hamas may have committed war crimes during the May clashes.  During the 11-day battle, Hamas and other Palestinian groups fired thousands of rockets into Israeli territory and the Israeli army bombed the Gaza Strip from the ground and air.  Human Rights Watch said it used interviews with local residents and eyewitnesses, data analysis and digital images to produce its report.  According to the human rights organization, 62 Palestinian civilians were killed in three Israeli attacks in areas where no evidence of armed personnel has been found.  The report specifically examines Israeli air strikes on May 10 on the small town of Beit Hanoun in the northeast Gaza Strip, May 15 on the al-Shati refugee camp and May 16 on the city of Gaza.  Human Rights Watch added that “other Israeli attacks during this battle were also likely in violation of international law. ”  Eight people, including six children, were killed in an attack on May 10 that destroyed several homes.  At this point, Human Rights Watch says there is no indication of the presence of the armed forces or its use for military purposes.  “Any attack that does not have specific military objectives violates international law. ”  In the May 15 attack on the al-Shati refugee camp, a three-storey residential building was targeted and 10 people were killed.  A resident told Human Rights Watch that residents were not given any warning about the attack.  Israel claims that the reason for the attack was the presence of several senior Hamas leaders in the residential complex.  Human Rights Watch said no witnesses or family members of the victims confirmed the presence of Hamas operatives in or around the building.  It added that the building was likely targeted by a bomb produced by Boeing that the United States exported to Israel.  A third attack on May 16 killed three destroyed buildings and 44 civilians, including 18 children and 14 women, in Gaza City.  Human Rights Watch said eyewitnesses interviewed said Israel gave no warning before the attack.  Israeli army videos and pieces of munitions collected by Palestinian police show that the attack was also carried out by a one-ton Boeing bomb.  At the time of the attack, Israel said it was targeting Hamas militants' tunnels, but Human Rights Watch said it found "no evidence of military targets".  Human Rights Watch also condemned “reckless ” missile attacks on Israeli civilians and said it would address the issue in a separate report.  “Israel and the Palestinians have violated international law in this battle, which could amount to war crimes. ”  The Israeli government has not yet responded to the report, but a Hamas spokesman said: "This report shows that the occupation government acts with complete impunity and beyond the law and is never punished because of the full support of the United States."  In March, a prosecutor at the International Criminal Court announced a new and comprehensive investigation into the situation in the occupied Palestinian territories.  The main focus of the study will be the 2014 war in the Gaza Strip, but it will also look at the deaths of Palestinian protesters since 2018.  On May 27, the UN Human Rights Council approved an international investigation into the recent fighting in the Gaza Strip.  According to the local government of the Gaza Strip, 260 Palestinians, including gunmen, have been killed in the recent clashes. passages.title: Health tourism: a concept beyond treatment
passages.passage: ISNA / Khorasan Razavi Treatment is one of the motivations through which people travel to different places and travel to improve their physical and mental condition.  Health tourism is not limited to medical services and includes naturopathic services as well.  Director of the Research Department of Tourism Management and Planning at the Institute of Tourism, ACECR, in an interview with ISNA, regarding the introduction of "health tourism" as one of the types of tourism, said: "Health tourism" in recent years has created advantages including job creation and poverty reduction and has promoted the economic situation of countries.  Masoumeh Tavangar stated: The World Tourism Organization (WTO) has provided a definition of health tourism, according to this definition, services that improve and increase health and morale of people, and in a place outside of their residence for more than 24 hours, is considered health tourism.  He added that the use of the health properties of mineral waters, healthy weather in one place and the use of medical services of a country are among the services that have been mentioned in health tourism, so health tourism has a concept beyond medical tourism.  Nature therapy is one of the types of health tourism, this faculty member of the Institute of Tourism, ACECR said: Those who work in the field of health tourism believe that the provision of services in this area should be in the level of the first world countries and in contrast, prices and costs should be in the level of developing countries and the third world to encourage people to travel to use these services.  Tavangar pointed out: According to the history of health tourism, topics such as nature therapy, such as the use of hot springs, began from the past and from Greece and Rome, and with the development of this type of tourism in European and American countries, health tourism has also become more prevalent, but recently in this type of tourism, medical issues have become more prevalent than nature therapy.  He continued: In the past, only in Western countries, advanced medical services, superior doctors and up-to-date medical equipment were used; but recently, in developing countries such as Singapore, Thailand, India and Turkey, health tourism has become popular and tourists choose these countries to use their medical services.  Director of the Research Department of Tourism Management and Planning at the Institute of Tourism, ACECR stated: Usually, countries create their competitive advantage in certain fields and try to attract tourists in a specific field, for example, some countries specialize in cancer treatment, organ donation and treatment of neurological diseases, but some other countries promote their services in the field of plastic and cosmetic surgery.  Iran has low statistics in the field of health tourism, Tavangar explained: Today Mashhad is more active in the field of beauty, heart and eye surgery and has received more patients in these areas, but in general, Iran has not opened its position in the field of health tourism among neighboring countries and has a low rate of tourism in the field of health tourism, while Iran has skilled manpower and costs are very affordable for health tourists.  He added that medical issues in Iran have come from the past when Avicenna expresses his medical opinions and writes books, and it can be related to health tourism, but officially, this type of tourism was recognized by the Ministry of Health in 2003, and in 2004, this issue was raised in the Cultural Heritage Organization and the description of the duties in this organization for the management of health tourism, and since then it was introduced as an independent industry. And he is known.  We can plan for new forms of health tourism in Khorasan Razavi. This faculty member of the Institute of Tourism, ACECR stated: Since health tourism is effective in the economic development of countries, it has been considered in the country 's laws and policies, and in our country, for this type of tourism, the Health Tourism Policy Council and the International Health Services Committee have been formed in the Ministry of Health and Medical Education.  Tavangar said that improving infrastructures such as international relations of the country, transportation, excellent medical services, the appropriate cost of treatment, health facilities and facilities, the feeling of security, the provision of treatment visas, the presence of skilled professionals and the provision of medical services to foreign tourists in various languages and several languages of the world can help expand this type of tourism.  He continued: Mashhad is one of the most important economic hubs of the country, and along with medical issues, it can also work in health fields due to its diverse nature, and now it is possible to plan for new forms of health tourism in Khorasan Razavi province, as well as to increase health villages in the province, which is currently low in number.  What Threatens Health Tourism?  Director of the Research Department of Tourism Management and Planning at the Institute of Tourism, ACECR said: In general, development is a category that, if its aspects are not measured, will be harmful.  For example, in the field of health tourism, the rights of indigenous people should be considered and they should be provided with medical and health services at an affordable cost, otherwise the development of health tourism is a threat, on the other hand, tourists who travel to a country to receive health services should have clear rules to protect them against possible medical errors that protect their rights.  Tavangar said: One of the challenges that the industry now faces is the mismanagement of those who help to attract health tourists, in fact, they can be referred to as informal marketers.  At present, there is not yet a coherent structure for the management of these people, and for better management of health tourism, a full and comprehensive statistics must be obtained from the University of Medical Sciences in order to plan carefully through the policy making organizations in this area to improve it.  End of message.

Speech, in particular, about transplantation, pediatric neurosurgery, a number of other areas where Chelyabinsk doctors work at the level of European standards.  Alexey Larin lists: private clinics of the region are able to provide high-tech assistance in the field of oncology, ophthalmology, traumatology and orthopedics, obstetrics and gynecology...  What attracts foreign patients?  In some countries, Dmitry Dovbnya notes, due to traditional specifics or policies aimed at limiting the birth rate, a number of medical services have been banned.  In China, it is in vitro fertilization, in Arab countries - laser treatment.  Residents of China are also interested in dental services - here they are cheaper than in their homeland.  Among the clients of private medicine, there are many former compatriots who left for Germany, Israel, scattered around the world.  They often visit relatives, and the price and quality of medical services encourage them to seek help in Chelyabinsk clinics: in developed countries, similar treatment for the family budget is much more burdensome.  Frequent guests in medical institutions of the region and residents of Kazakhstan.  Moreover, it is they who form the main flow from the near abroad.  Director and chief physician of the private medical center Elena Kolyada said that 95 percent of all international appeals to her institution are accounted for by residents of the neighboring republic.  Among the most popular services are IVF, surgical treatment, polyclinic examination, pediatrician consultations.  Many, as, indeed, all over the world, are concerned about prevention - comprehensive examination programs have been developed for such tourists.  Unfortunately, there are no statistics in the field of medical tourism in the region yet.  Each institution counts its own figures, for example, for the clinic Elena Kolyada this market annually grows by 10-15 percent.  Coordinator of international internships of the Ural Society of Aesthetic Medicine Specialists Irina Kuznetsova says that everything depends on the profile of the medical institution - for some, the growth reaches 25-32 percent.  To spur the development of exports can create a unique product that does not exist in other territories.  For the firm headed by Irina, this was an international project involving Italian surgeons invited to Russia: they provide high-tech care to patients, including those with severe post-traumatic consequences.  It is clear that the goal of the development of medical tourism, as well as any other services, is additional financial revenues to the budgets of clinics, the city, the region.  After all, Russians from other regions "bring" with them funding through compulsory health insurance, foreigners - "live" money.  At the same time, even in state medical institutions, the receipt of extra-budgetary funds can increase many times.  However, representatives of Opora Rossii believe that private clinics should be the basis for the development of the export direction, since the main function of public health is social.  But public-private partnership will clearly benefit the industry, especially when it comes to creating infrastructure, acquiring expensive equipment. - The modern world is generally moving towards car sharing: when you use, but do not own.  This principle can open a second wind to medical entrepreneurship, which remains the marketing of the product, its promotion, - says Dmitry Dovbnya. - We would like business to complement the system that already exists, - develops the idea of Irina Gekht, - maybe offering assistance that the state does not provide so professionally, as a socially oriented non-profit organization does, engaged, for example, in the rehabilitation of children with autism.  Officials are ready to include entrepreneurs providing such services in state support programs: to reduce taxes for them, to provide subsidies, to open access to the compulsory medical insurance system.  And similar examples in the region already exist, one of them is a Magnitogorsk company that carries out early diagnosis of oncological diseases.  But before spreading the experience, the authorities want to understand how many social entrepreneurs there are in the region, in what areas they work, and how effective they are.  The next stage is the creation of a self-regulatory organization uniting social business, or a state structure under the auspices of the regional government.  The Russian capitals have already reached this level of development: in St. Petersburg, the medical tourism agency was created under the regional Ministry of Health, in Moscow it exists as a private initiative, but also works effectively.  Expanding the export of health services will require other interactions.  On the one hand, you will need new hotels, hostels where patients can stay, new tourist products, and this is an uncultivated field for business.  On the other hand, logistics and infrastructure development will have to be addressed.  So it is impossible to do without cooperation with the authorities.  According to the Medical Tourism Index (MTI), by 2025, the turnover of this market in the world will exceed three trillion dollars.  The annual increase is estimated at a minimum of 25 percent.  Among the most popular countries among tourists going for medical care are Canada, Great Britain, Israel, Italy, Germany, France, South Korea, Singapore, India.  Russia is not yet among the leaders of such ratings, but experts believe that it has great potential.

passages.title: Save a lot, good quality Americans like to go overseas for medical tourism
passages.passage: The Mexican border city of Tijuana has become famous for its medical tourism, showing Meriel taking a ride to the U.S.-Mexico border crossing after undergoing gastric surgery in Tijuana. (Getty Images) Share Facebook When Rael decided to have gastric reduction surgery to lose weight, she faced two choices: spend $12,000 to operate in the United States, or spend $4,000 to do the same in Mexico.  Agence France-Presse said her insurance covers the procedure only for people who are morbidly obese and have diabetes and high blood pressure, but 50-year-old Meryl is not eligible.  She wants to lose 210 pounds to 160 pounds to avoid these ailments.  After doing some research, Merrell contacted the Medical Tourism Corporation and went to the Mexican border town of Tijuana for surgery.  Tijuana has long been famous for its medical tourism, where people come to do weight loss surgery, dental visits, plastic surgery, treatment of cardiovascular diseases, cancer, pregnancy assistance, and drug purchases.  Each year, an estimated 20 million “medical tourists ” travel to other countries to seek medical care, including about 1.9 million Americans.  Mexico, Colombia, Costa Rica, and the Dominican Republic are America ’ s favorite places to visit for medical tourism, with low prices and good quality of medical care.  Founded 13 years ago, the medical tourism company helps Meryl arrange everything, including a flight from Phoenix to San Diego and a driver driving her across the U.S.-Mexico border to a luxury hotel.  The airfare, hotel and hospital surgeries all together cost a total of $3,800.  The company sends 60 to 70 people a month to various countries around the world for medical treatment, mostly to Mexico.  Merrill ’ s surgeons operate on at least two foreigners a day, the busiest tax refund season in the United States after April each year.  Obamacare, introduced in 2010, requires all adults to have health insurance provided by their employer or the government, but medical tourism in the United States has increased.  Some employers almost doubled their health insurance costs after the introduction of Oak Health Insurance and encouraged employees to travel abroad for treatment.  One company sent its employees abroad for plastic surgery and weight loss surgery, saving 20 million yuan over five years.  Experts say that even with universal health coverage, the United States may not be able to stop medical tourism, becoming like Canada and Europe, where non-emergency procedures such as gastric contractions may have to wait in line for years to get their turn, forcing people to seek medical treatment abroad.  In fact, Tijuana, who operated on Merrill, wanted Oasis Hospital to have many foreign patients from Canada.  Americans also enjoy visiting Europe for medical treatment, although European countries are not as active in promoting medical tourism as Singapore, Thailand and the Philippines.  America ’ s highly advanced medical system has also attracted wealthy Arabs and Asians to treat their diseases.  It's just that Meryl doesn't deserve it.

passages.title: It's the doctors who are multiplying Barbie.
passages.passage: Zahra Chizari The rapid barbeque fever and thirst for the resemblance of Hollywood stars in the face, smile and body has led to the black market in the field of all kinds of beauty surgeries and many underground specialized centers for skin and hair beauty and barbeque shaving to form, but with the formation of these marketing centers and finding customers is one of the important concerns of their operators and here is the channel Telegram and Instagram pages are coming to the fore to make this market hotter.  A striking point is the display of pornographic and nude images of men and women who have undergone liposuction to make their faces look like Hollywood faces.  The pictures that some of them are placed on the operating table and in the operating room, while others are like the cooking of the people themselves.  Pornographic advertising is displayed on these channels and pages, while for a long time, it is forbidden by the law to advertise doctors, and the display of images of patients on a hospital bed is the most objectionable example of immorality and breaking the boundaries of privacy of individuals.  On the other hand, the billion-dollar turnover of this field has led doctors to multiply barby instead of treating patients!  Lipomatic, Body Contouring, Body Contouring, or any other name, is a type of plastic and cosmetic surgery in which fat points such as abdomen and flank are removed from under the skin by injection of anesthetic drugs and then injected into other areas such as buttocks or breasts to make people look like Hollywood actors. Unmatched!  This surgery also includes treatment, for example, men who have gynecomastia and bulging breasts, but naturally, the main part of the patients to doctors who have unlimited surgery centers and a high percentage of them are doctors and general surgeons and their surgery center is also home or office, at least they are not physically facing a problem.  These people, who are part of the delusion of ugly self, and some others are obsessed with themselves in the advertising storm, for having an ideal body, instead of passing through reasonable and logical ways such as diet and sports, go to such irrational shortcuts; shortcuts that may kill them due to fat embolism, but worst of all, the immoral and illegal activities of these people. Doakes in pornographic advertising and depicting naked figures of their clients in cyberspace to hunt more patients.  Medical advertising is a violation, Dr. Jahangiri, Deputy of Monitoring and Planning of the Medical Organization in relation to the advertisements of physicians, especially on Instagram pages, says: In general, in the field of health services, we do not have a word called advertising and if it is intended to inform that according to the approval of the Medical Council, it is responsible for monitoring this information and advertising.  According to him, in this regard, a bylaw has been approved by the Supreme Council of the Medical System and has been communicated to the relevant areas, according to which anyone who wants to advertise or inform in the field of health services, equipment, food and beverage, must receive a license from the Medical Council.  The Deputy of Supervision and Planning of the Medical Organization emphasizes: It is not morally right that some physicians show before and after their surgery and we do not allow this.  Of course, in the field of monitoring advertising on Instagram, it should be noted that this issue has recently spread and we have been working with the Supreme Council of Cyberspace and the Ministry of Guidance to increase the supervision in this regard.  Jahangiri adds that the parliament has a law in the field of monitoring Instagram advertising: We also pursue violations on the same basis.  At the same time, he believes: We should accept that monitoring this issue in cyberspace such as Instagram pages is difficult, but in general, advertising and information, if it is seductive and other than the workplace and type of work, other information is done, the violation has taken place and the medical system in this regard will take the necessary action.  Arj Harirchi, a spokesman for the Ministry of Health, said: "Some of the images released are fake, while some of them are published without the patient's permission."  Emphasizing that we do not have advertising in most health services, he considers this type of advertising illegal and adds: We ask the medical system to take serious and necessary action in this regard.  Billions of underground violations continue to circulate due to the lack of oversight that should be in place.  One of the knowledgeable doctors in this field, in an interview with Javan about the activities of these centers, says: Many of these centers are underground and are carried out by general physicians and general surgeons in residential buildings.  Referring to the astronomical revenues of physicians working in this field, he adds: One of the general surgeons active in these centers earned one billion and 100 million tomans in one year.  As the informed source says: Apparently, these channels and Instagram pages have been able to provide customers to these centers even from European countries, in a situation where they do not observe any of the rules of health tourism and this may cause problems for our country.  Apparently, these dealers take as much money as they can from their domestic and foreign customers and cost from about one, two million tomans to 30, 40 million.  Doctors who multiply instead of cure!  This doctor emphasizes: The propaganda is not the same as the scientific centers, and we do not have any such thing as no return in sculpting surgeries, but general physicians often market for this work and then refer applicants to private hospitals or limited surgical centers to general or plastic surgeons.  He also presents impressive figures and says that up to 600 general surgeons are working in this area, which if this energy and time is put on the necessary surgeries, the number of tumor surgeries and such problems will be reduced, but the high turnover in this area and the lack of serious determination to deal with offenders has led these people to continue their violations.  It also has the risk of fat embolism and death.

passages.title: We need to relax restrictions on medical advertising.
passages.passage: Medical tourism and medical promotion to relax restrictions on medical advertising 2019-03-24 17: 39 United Daily News reporter Deng Guifen / Instant report Taiwan's medical standards are internationally recognized, but the value of international medical services is the last place in the Asia-Pacific region.  The Taiwan Association of Aesthetic Surgeons pointed out that the main factor is that there are many restrictions on medical advertising in China, and there are many chaos in the medical and aesthetic industry, which makes it difficult to set foot internationally.  It is recommended that the government amend medical treatment, focusing on the three principles of dealing with exaggerated advertising, non-disclosure of specialist information and illegal solicitation. The rest should be given full play by the medical profession in order to achieve the purpose of economic promotion.  Cai Fengzhou, executive director of the Taiwan Society of Aesthetic Surgeons, said at a media dinner that the Ministry of Health and Welfare used to promote international medical treatment based on "medical treatment", but its economic benefits are far from the "medical tourism" promoted by Asian countries, and medical advertising restrictions, when it comes to disease treatment or medical aesthetics, most foreigners will not think of Taiwan.  But the quickest way to get foreign people to know Taiwan ’ s medical care and beauty is through advertising and online promotion.  Cai Fengzhou believes that the medical law for the medical advertising part has been necessary to amend the law, the past time and space background is to prevent underground radio stations from illegally buying drugs, but the era is far away, should focus on profit rather than doctors as thieves.  For example, Article 84 of medical treatment stipulates that "non-medical institutions shall not be allowed to advertise for medical purposes", but it has been interpreted as saying that only the responsible person of the hospital can write medical articles.  When it comes to medical aesthetics, Yang Kuo-hui, president of the Taiwan Society of Aesthetic Surgeons, laments that "plastic surgery" is a specialty term of the Ministry of Health and Welfare, but the outside world often refers to "medical aesthetics doctors" as plastic surgeons, resulting in the chaos of "cosmetic doctors".  In addition, there are many medical and aesthetic clinics that use beautiful words such as "experts" and "famous doctors" to attract people to visit, but some clinics introduce only the doctor's lecturers and training experience, but do not mention the personal specialty of the doctor, seemingly professional, but easy to confuse the public.

passages.title: Medical Suitcase in the Hands of Providers!
passages.passage: "One of the important concerns and challenges in the field of medical tourism is the proper and proper guidance of foreign patients to Iranian medical centers, that medical tourists from the moment of arrival in the country will not be caught by the dealers, non-medical interventions by physicians for applicants for cosmetic surgeries will not be done, and finally, medical tourists will be able to advertise Iranian medical services by receiving standard medical services in reputable centers."  According to ISNA, Iran's newspaper wrote: "Medical tourists can be described as the phenomenon of traveling to different countries to access medical services.  On this basis, in the description of medical tourism, patients from developed countries travel to undeveloped countries in search of medical treatment.  The reason is clear.  The cost of treatment in underdeveloped countries is three times lower than in developed countries.  Medical tourism in India is growing rapidly.  In 2004, 1.2 million patients visited India for health care and 1.1 million medical tourists visited Thailand.  While increasing GDP, economic development, job opportunities are among the advantages of this industry, and Iran can also be referred to as a combination of medical and recreational tourism and the existence of historical and ancient monuments, pilgrimage centers and natural beauty and natural remedies (traditional medicine) at the top of the patients of the Persian Gulf countries, Afghanistan, Pakistan, Europe, Turkey, Azerbaijan and...  But the lack of advertising and branding of overseas medical tourism, as well as the presence of unauthorized intermediaries and institutions of health tourism, has put the industry in serious harm ’ s way.  The issue that has recently become a significant point for top managers of the country, following the increase in exchange rates, and even the officials of the Ministry of Health have been thinking about the development of the medical tourism industry.  As activists in this field say, one of the important concerns and challenges in this regard is the proper guidance of foreign patients to Iranian medical centers, that medical tourists from the moment of arrival in the country will not be caught by dealers, non-medical interventions by physicians for cosmetic surgery applicants, and finally, medical tourists will be able to advertise Iranian medical services by receiving standard medical services in reputable medical centers.  About the role and general policies of the Ministry of Health in the development of medical tourism, challenges and opportunities to attract and follow patients from the country of origin to Iran, we spoke with Dr. Saeed Hashemzadeh, the head of the health tourism department of the Ministry of Health, which you can read below.  How are medical tourists attracted to Iranian treatment centers?  I mean, because of the presence of intermediaries, foreign patients are not properly directed to medical centers and do not reach the hands of specialists, and sometimes we hear that they fall into the hands of dealers and unauthorized institutions, and they also direct applicants for these types of surgeries to people who are not qualified.  Is there a specific model for guiding the patient to the medical centers that the medical tourist does not receive non-standard medical services and does not lead to invalid medical centers?  We at the Ministry of Health believe that dealers are not causes, but effects.  Therefore, if we want to deal with the phenomenon of brokerage in the field of health tourism, we will simply ask the police to stop the work of dealers, but we believe that this approach will not eliminate the work of dealers.  So we tried to identify the problems that exist in the supply chain in health tourism, and then, based on that, brokers out of the industry.  Of course, I should say that the country ’ s medical centers have capabilities and capabilities, but they have not been able to properly introduce and present these capabilities abroad, where our customers are present.  Who gives the foreign patient the information at which medical center and under what conditions and at what cost?  The answer to this question is clear: an element found in the name of the dealer.  Because of this gap or lack of information between health centers and patients applying abroad, an element called a broker plays this role.  In order to reduce the activity of brokers in principle, we need to see who is acting in successful models of the world and who is going to give this information to the patient to reduce the activity of brokers.  When you look at successful models in West Asia, including India, Turkey and Jordan, there is an actor here called “Facilitator Company. ”  The main task of facilitating companies is to provide the necessary medical information from health centers and physicians and to inform about transparent prices to foreign patients. With this knowledge, we designed a regulation to form companies based on this bylaw that work in this area, that is, these companies play a role in making decisions for patients who enter the country, then facilitate the entry of the patient to the country and after receiving medical services from the patient. Outside, follow up after treatment.  Of course, follow-up after treatment is an important part of the work that has been forgotten in our country, that is, we did not have a regular and structured follow-up, so we started to do the same.  The companies facilitating the recruitment of medical tourism have a specific channel for attracting foreign patients, how do these companies cut the hands of brokers and intermediaries in this field?  These companies, with the permission of the Ministry of Health, attract different types of foreign patients to Iranian medical centers.  They start their activities in cyberspace, including websites and social networks, and inform the people of foreign countries about the capabilities of their contractual health centers in cyberspace.  The second solution is to attend national and international exhibitions and events of health tourism.  The third option is to join similar companies in the target markets.  That is, Iranian companies connect with similar companies in Iraq and Afghanistan and refer the patient to our country.  A very important solution is to join the facilitators with insurance companies on the other side of the border, which, of course, has not been paid attention to in our country.  That is, there is a lack of actors here, and that is the connection of foreign insurance companies to Iranian facilitators in order to attract patients in an organized manner in international markets.  This is a model that is used in all countries.  In our country, which of the channels you mentioned provides the way to attract foreign patients?  Other than the type of brokerage, the type that is very emphasized is the attraction of the patient through cyberspace.  Does it seem like there ’ s more to attract foreign patients?  Do you have any statistics about how many medical tourists enter Iran ’ s treatment centers through dealers?  It is not more than 5 months since the notification of the regulations of the Facilitating Companies should take some time to make a proper comparison.  The vast majority of patients entering treatment centers are owned by these dealers, but the balance shifts in favor of companies.  Between 80% and 90% of patients are brought by brokers and the share of direct patient visits is less than 10%.  At the moment, the weight is shifting towards companies.  Medical centers have reported the same to us, that is, the centers that previously said that 90 percent of foreign patients come to Iran through dealers now say that 70 percent of them enter the country through dealers.  The trend of change, although small, has begun, that is, 10% of the market is owned by companies, while we only allowed 15% of these companies to operate.  If insurance is added to the supply chain, this will happen quickly.  You mentioned the connection of Iranian facilitators to foreign insurance companies to attract medical tourism.  Since the arrival of medical tourists in Iran, what is the process of receiving their services?  Please let me know if medical visas are issued for patients.  Do you offer unpaid and VIP services to them?  On the basis of what process the patient enters the medical center of a foreign country, let me first say the model of the world.  It is usually the case that the patient travels to another country to receive a special service that is not covered by his or her insurance.  For example, in Europe, if a person with a doctor ’ s diagnosis needs a knee replacement and this service is not covered by insurance, the insurance office suggests that the patient use the services of a consultant facilitator and go to India or Turkey for knee surgery, in which case the knee replacement service is covered by the insurance of the country of origin, that is, this person does not have insurance coverage for joint replacement in Europe, but in India and Turkey. The insurance mode not only covers the costs of the patient, but also the airline ticket and accommodation costs.  In the United States, for example, a knee replacement costs $220,000, but if the patient goes to India with the best hotel, plane and service, it costs $15,000 for his insurance company.  In our country, almost the same cycle must be carried out.  We will be successful in medical tourism when we can implement the same general cycle, for now, the process is like this: a patient who has been recommended to do medical work in Iraq will enter Iran.  If it is in a healthy cycle, with the advertisements that the facilitator companies have in cyberspace, the patient chooses which city and hospital to enter, then the patient contracts with the facilitator company, and the company coordinates the visa, ticket, accommodation and transportation of the patient, and the patient enters Iran and returns to his home country after receiving the service, of course his treatment is followed by the facilitator company.  What we need to do is for the patient to decide in his or her place of residence which Iranian medical center he or she should go to.  It is interesting to know that since

passages.title: 【 TAIWAN HEALTH INSPECTION 】 How does Kaohsiung win after Asia 's leading medical tourism? ｜ Hong Kong 01 ｜ The World Says
passages.passage: Kaohsiung has designated 2019 as the “first year of medical tourism ” and is aggressively marketing local medical products.  However, looking at other advanced cities in Asia, it is certainly not a pioneer in the development of medical tourism.  Bangkok in Thailand, Seoul in Korea, Kuala Lumpur in Malaysia and other places have been implementing medical tourism for many years, each with its own characteristics.  Can Kaohsiung, a rising star, develop a unique chain of medical tourism industry to compete with other Asian cities?  (This is the sixth feature of the "Taiwan Health Insurance" series) Can hospitals in Kaohsiung capture a share of the medical tourism industry among the best in Asia? (photo by Yang Yalin) Chang Hung-tai, director of Kaohsiung Municipal Union Hospital, believes that the advantages of Kaohsiung and the whole of Taiwan are its internationally recognized medical standards and low medical service prices.  "Taiwan medical care because of the relationship of health insurance, the cost is very low, almost one-tenth of that of other countries, cheaper than the mainland, our drug prices are also low, many mainlanders are willing to come to Taiwan."  First, the price is low, and the second is high quality credibility.  Taiwan ’ s Ministry of Health and Welfare has strict management, and health insurance audits are conducted from time to time. ”  Zhang Hongtai believes that the surrounding potential competitors have their own advantages. For example, Thailand has a lot of experience in tourism medicine, and even several hospitals are specialized in tourism medicine, so the service personnel of the entire hospital have been carefully trained and tailored according to the principles of tourism medicine.  Medical tourism in the capital Bangkok is mature enough to be a "package tour" and receive thousands of medical tourists.  “Many hospitals have even scheduled their annual schedules … Taiwan can make this kind of money. ” Thailand is the world ’ s largest medical tourism destination, with more than 2 million foreign tourists coming to Thailand each year to receive medical services, and the related industries make an average annual profit of 120 billion baht (about HK $29.6 billion).  Thailand is famous for its rich tourism resources, coupled with the maturity of medical technology in health examination, plastic surgery, dentistry and other aspects, the average price of related services is only about half of that of European and American countries, so medical tourism has been one of the alternative tourism projects in Thailand.  The famous CBS news program “60 Minutes Magazine ” reported on Bangkok ’ s famous“ Bumrungrad Hospital ” in a feature way back in 2005.  The hospital receives more than 500,000 foreign patients from more than 190 countries around the world every year. It has the largest health screening center in Bangkok, serving more than 60,000 people every year, which shows that its medical tourism resources are very sufficient.  Bangkok ’ s famous “Regal Hospital ” (Bumrungrad Hospital). (online picture) When it comes to medical tourism, it has to mention Seoul, South Korea. Its advanced medical minimally invasive technology has always led Asia, and it has a mature operating system and supporting medical aesthetic technology such as microplastic surgery, which has become the Asian plastic surgery center.  Since 2009, the annual growth rate of medical tourists visiting Korea has exceeded 34%, and they come from China, the United States, Russia, Japan and other countries.  In December last year, the Korean Medical Tourism Service Center at Incheon International Airport was officially opened, allowing foreign travelers to book local consultation services, nearby dining and accommodation facilities, transportation to the hospital, and more.  The service center also has a resident nurse who is fluent in multiple languages, providing tourists with professional consulting services for medical tourism.  The government has partnered with the industry to make it the number one driver of medical tourism.  The medical tourism industry in Seoul is mainly engaged in microsurgery and cosmetic surgery.  (Online photo) Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia has always been the best destination for medical tourism. In 2016, Kuala Lumpur was named the Best Medical Tourism Destination of the Year by International Medical Tourism Magazine.  Kuala Lumpur also has a language advantage. Due to its multi-ethnic society, there is no shortage of health care workers fluent in Chinese and English. In addition to this, it has been favored by medical tourists from Europe and the United States, and it has also helped it to seize the huge Chinese market and become a rival to Kaohsiung.  (Hong Kong 01 map) Kaohsiung needs to "decorate" first to enter the market. Zhang Hongtai admitted that Kaohsiung still needs to prepare a lot of things in medical tourism and do a good job of supporting the work.  He cited the United Hospital, where he worked, as an example, because it belongs to the regional hospital level, it has the conditions to build medical aesthetics equipment.  He pointed out that the first thing to do is to redecorate the internal facilities and renovate them into a new type of ward.  "Medical beauty is not the same as general medical treatment, can not be treated as a general patient."  They want to have a private, safe and beautiful ward, "he said.  Another problem is professionalism.  Zhang Hongtai believes that at present, Taiwan does not restrict what doctors can do medical aesthetics, as long as they have a doctor's license, so there are many people doing it, and the quality is difficult to control.  He does not mean that doctors have problems with their medical skills, but that the medical community should have a unique professional process and code for medical aesthetics in order to enhance the attractiveness of medical tourism in Kaohsiung and compete with neighboring regions.  For example, laser, if used inappropriately, may cause burns.  Therefore, even if you do medical aesthetics, you still need a professional evaluation by a specialist.  If Kaohsiung is to do a good job in medical tourism, it must pay attention to the professionalism of medical aesthetics.  "What we do is a medical beauty with a certain standard, and it can't be seen as a night market selling things."  "The Big Thing".  With professionalism, we can have the quality and safety that the international medical industry has always emphasized. There are already large medical and aesthetic teams in nearby cities, who value the quality of their services and treat their customers as valued guests rather than simply patients.  The above section is from the 166th issue of Hong Kong 01 (June 10, 2019).  More Weekly Articles..  Hong Kong 01 is available at major newsstands, Circle K and Vango stores.  You can also subscribe to the weekly newsletter here to read more in-depth reports.

passages.title: Tracing prostheses used in plastic surgery
passages.passage: According to Mehr News Agency, Hamed Bateni, in connection with the issue of medical tourism, said: "The medical conditions of the country have scientifically caused patients from other countries to travel to Iran from the region and even from remote parts of the world and benefit from the medical field in Iran."  Pointing out that some people think that patients from other parts of the world come to Iran only because of the cheapness of medical services, he said: "This is a mistake because many countries offer cheaper services in the field of medicine, but patients do not trust and do not want to travel to their country for treatment because their medicine is not strong or the facilities of surgical centers are weak and sometimes unsterile."  The head of the Iranian Society of Plastic and Aesthetic Surgeons continued: In recent years, measures have been started to organize medical tourists through the Ministry of Health and gradually the programs are going to be written and comprehensive so that we hope that soon the field of medical tourism will be completely out of control and operated by translators or non-standard institutions and only under the supervision of the Ministry of Health.  In response to the question of what effect the sanctions of the enemies have had on the field of plastic and cosmetic surgery and whether you are facing a shortage of drugs in this field, he noted: The field of plastic and cosmetic surgery is not very dependent on the aspect of drugs with shortages, but equipment and devices such as implants, prosthetics and beauty products with changing currency fluctuations have increased prices and sometimes products are scarce and imports are not easy.  He said: "The equipment required by plastic surgeons is provided by different brands, depending on the company's production and distribution and their price varies, but all of these equipment and equipment are of good quality and there is no problem in this regard."  The head of the Iranian Society of Plastic and Aesthetic Surgeons noted that most of the equipment and equipment needed for plastic and cosmetic surgery such as implants and prostheses do not have passenger or luggage entry because the reference of these devices is known and all of them have serial numbers that can be traced on the website of the manufacturer and distributor, so there is no concern in this regard.  Bateni said that patients can use this serial number and specifications to track the prosthesis and device used in their body and make sure of its quality, because the prostheses used in plastic and cosmetic surgeries are different from some other surgeries and the patient has a direct role in its preparation.

passages.title: A separate type of tourism in Moldova: people from all over the world come for this
passages.passage: Why dental tourism is popular in Moldova, what is the main problem of patients, as well as what unusual requests some of them turn to - this and not only told Dr. Valery Fala.  CHISINAU, 9 Feb – Sputnik.  Dentistry in Moldova is developing at a rapid pace, specialists can boast not only modern technologies, but also earn the trust of foreigners who specially come to the country for treatment.  About it in comments radio studio Sputnik Moldova said doctor of medical Sciences, teacher and head of the Department of continuing education of the Faculty of Dentistry of the Medical University Valery Fala.  According to him, in recent years, dental tourism has become quite popular in our country.  As the interlocutor noted, foreigners come to us for various reasons - we have good specialists and technologies that meet all modern requirements, and all this is much more affordable than abroad.  As for Moldovan patients, according to the specialist, some are afraid to go to the dentist and undergo an examination.  This is due to the fact that many go to the doctor only when there is a serious dental problem, which manifests itself in the form of acute pain that is difficult to tolerate.  The dentist called the cause of caries and how to deal with it > > > "This is the biggest problem of our patients, because they are treated at the last moment - sometimes even there is nothing to help.  And then you need to remove this tooth.  Therefore, we recommend that you periodically visit the dentist - at least twice a year, "Fala said in a comment to Sputnik Moldova radio studio.  However, some patients come to doctors not only for treatment, but also make very unusual requests - for example, inlay of teeth with precious stones.  “Personally, I do not approve of this and do not strongly recommend our patients to install these precious stones on their teeth.  But this is a patient's request...  I think that they, having seen a lot of pictures on the Internet and consulted with Google, want this for themselves.  We try to convince that it is not very good to install stones on your teeth.  But if they want to, ” Falah said. passages.title: Foreign Trade Association and Dentist Association build a platform for international marketing and friendship
passages.passage: The Association of Foreign Trade and the Association of Dentists took the platform to expand international marketing and friendship 2019-06-28 11: 39 United Daily News reporter Jiao Haozheng / Immediate report on Taiwan's dental care, and strive to enter the international stage.  The Ministry of Health and Welfare and the Bureau of International Trade of the Ministry of Economic Affairs have joined hands to support the establishment of a dental international marketing platform by the Foreign Trade Association, the Federation of Dentists and the Metal Center.  The quality of dental services in Taiwan is internationally renowned, and international medical care has become popular in recent years.  Wang Tung-yuan, president of the All Association of Dentists, said that according to the analysis of the American Medical Association and George Washington University, international patients go overseas for medical projects, and dental treatment accounts for the second place in service demand, second only to medical aesthetics.  Wang Dongyuan said that in recent years, the Association has actively participated in international volunteer clinic activities and provided home medical treatment to protect the health of patients.  In order to share Taiwan ’ s high-quality and caring dental services with patients in international demand, the Association of Dentists invites domestic dentists to participate in the promotion of international medical care, and strive to establish Taiwan ’ s international dental brand and develop international patients.  Among the marketing methods of international medical care, international assistance is the best way to build international friendship, and medical care can build very good friendships.  And the development of international medical care, not only to Taiwan's dental and other medical industries to help, but also medical diplomacy, humanitarian assistance, Taiwan's popularity also has a great help, but also to promote Taiwan's medical materials, wisdom of medical care can be more overseas.  Chen Shizhong, Minister of Health and Welfare, said that the dental industry should be promoted to the international stage, including the government is promoting the new southward, one country, one center and other policies, as well as the foundation laid by the Foreign Trade Association for many years, and it has been easier to expand than before.

passages.title: Overseas medical treatment is on the rise, and the medical tourism industry in Asia is booming.
passages.passage: SEOUL, Oct. 4 (Reuters) - This is one of the fastest growing industries in Asia, and it is not showing signs of weakness even as the global economy falters.  Today, medical tourism has become a billion-dollar industry.  From cosmetic surgery to heart bypass, hospitals in India, Singapore and South Korea receive more than 1 million foreign patients a year for no less than the following reasons: cost-effective surgery, no waiting in line for treatment, advanced technology and well-trained doctors.  Industry experts predict that as the number of new affluent people in the region increases, the medical tourism industry in the region will grow at a rate of 15-20% per year.  “As Asia has become richer and more mobile, medical tourism in Asia … seems to be growing, ” said David Vequist, director of the Center for Medical Tourism Research at the University of the Incarnate Word in Texas.  “Consumer choice is now a powerful force in the healthcare industry, with Asia ’ s aging population, growing obesity, sicker populations and more in need all having an impact on the healthcare industry. ”  Medscape News predicts that Asia ’ s medical tourism industry could generate $4.4 billion in value by 2012.  Among them, the largest number of patients came from the United States.  To avoid the high cost of private treatment at home, many Americans seek medical treatment overseas.  In general, this can save Americans 40% -50% of the cost of treatment.  Now, a new patient has been added to the operating table - the Chinese.  Many Chinese people try to solve their problems at any cost.  "No matter how expensive it is, I will do it," said Liu Xiaoyang, a 34-year-old Shanghainese who has just undergone double eyelid surgery, plastic surgery and jaw correction in Seoul, South Korea.  The rise of China's affluent class and the fascination with the "Korean Wave", to the popularity of pop music and Korean dramas, has led to a huge increase in the medical tourism industry in South Korea, especially the plastic surgery industry.  "Every time I watch Korean dramas and TV programs, I think the characters on TV are beautiful, and I hope I can be like them," Liu said.  Kim Byung-gun, a plastic surgeon at BK Dongyang Plastic Surgery Clinic in Seoul, says his patients are as young as six and as old as 70.  On average, their surgery costs about $5,000-10,000.  "The medical tourism industry will become one of the engines of the Korean economy," Kim said, adding that the "Korean Wave" is a key factor in promoting the development of the medical tourism industry in the country.

passages.title: Chengdu medical beauty market supply and demand two strong driving consumption
passages.passage: The number of medical and aesthetic institutions has reached 381; the scale of the industry is only second to Beijing and Shanghai, and the operating income of the medical and aesthetic industry in Chengdu will reach 100 billion yuan (RMB, the same below) in 2025 and 200 billion yuan in 2030, creating a leading and world-renowned "medical and aesthetic capital" in mainland China.  China News Service reported that Wang Xidan, secretary general of Chengdu Medical and Beauty Industry Association, said that the scale of Chengdu's medical and aesthetic industry in 2018 has reached 48.7 billion yuan.  "The development of the entire industry has formed a relatively healthy cycle, and the market is showing a state of supply and demand." Wang Xidan said that concentrated medical and aesthetic resources and a higher price ratio than first-tier cities have attracted more and more consumers to Chengdu.  In 2018, the number of medical and aesthetic institutions in Chengdu soared to 407, a surge of 131 from the previous year.  The Plastic Surgery Hospital of the Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences also chose to host the first Beijing-outside branch of Chengdu ’ s eight major medical and aesthetic hospitals in Chengdu in 2018.  Tang Yong, director of eight major medical and aesthetic hospitals in Chengdu, said that with nearly 40 days of closure due to the COVID-19 epidemic, the hospital's revenue in 2020 still increased by about 30% compared to 2019.  With the rise of the “face value economy ”, medical beauty has gradually become a pressing need for some contemporary Chinese, among which light medical beauty, which has a short recovery period and low risk, is most popular.  Due to the consideration of safety, reliability and other factors, a large number of consumers have moved to cities where medical and aesthetic resources are concentrated, and "medical and aesthetic tourism" has also quietly emerged.  The total revenue of Sichuan Huamei Zixin Medical Aesthetic Hospital in 2020 is about 600 million yuan.  Xue Hong, general manager of the hospital, said that about 20% of the annual number of patients treated by the hospital are foreign consumers who come to the hospital.  "Especially in recent years, the number of these consumers has grown rapidly, from Gansu, Qinghai, Yunnan, Guizhou and other provinces."  Wang Xidan sees this phenomenon as a new inflection point for the development of Chengdu's medical and aesthetic industry.  She said that medical beauty and tourism, finance, catering and other industries are expected to achieve the continuous development, the next step of the Chengdu Medical and Beauty Industry Association will work from this aspect, strive to create a consumer ecosystem that can maximize meet the diversified needs of consumers, and enhance the competitiveness of Chengdu medical and beauty industry.  Liu Lu, a professor of economics at Southwest University of Finance and Economics, said that the medical and aesthetic industry, as a new economy that can promote regional economic development, should care for its growth, but also need to strengthen supervision, train high-quality personnel, and formulate more stringent industry norms.

passages.title: Asians go to Russia to treat their teeth
passages.passage: TODAY 14: 39 2018-03-30T14: 39: 01 + 03: 00 Resize text: A A In 2017, medical institutions in Russia were visited by 110 thousand foreign tourists, 44% of them used dental services.  To treat teeth in Russia came mainly citizens of Vietnam, South Korea, China and Japan.  In just a year, the external tourist flow amounted to 24.5 million foreigners.  Other popular medical services for foreign tourists were gynecology and urology - 25%, as well as plastic surgery - 10%.  The most popular routes, as they say in Rosturizm, are Moscow, Novosibirsk, St. Petersburg, Kazan, Krasnodar and other large cities.  In addition to Asians, Europeans, especially citizens of Finland and Germany, also use medical services in Russia.  Treatment in Russia is cheaper, write “Izvestia ”, on dentistry foreigners can save up to 80% in dollar terms.  The state supports the development of medical tourism, at the end of 2017 adopted the corresponding state program.  According to it, until 2025, the medical tourist flow should be 500 thousand people annually, which can affect the country's economy by an additional 13 billion rubles.  Earlier, the website kp.ru reported that in 2017 the total tourist flow to Russia reached a record high, in Moscow it grew by 65% over seven years.

passages.passage: White collar men in mainland China pay more and more attention to medical beauty consumption and personal care.  (Photo / Reporter Wei Youde) Reporter Wei Youde / A comprehensive report on the consumption behavior of new white collar workers in China in 2020 shows that nearly 20% of male white collar workers spend 1131 yuan (about 4863 NT dollars) per month on skin care, which is basically the same as women's 1197 yuan (about 5147 NT dollars).  In addition, there are e-commerce platforms in the double 11 period in 2020 to obtain a nearly seven-fold increase in the number of medical and aesthetic medical orders, of which nearly 30% of the orders came from male consumers.  ▲ Dongsen Natural Beauty 's eyelash service. Even younger, the proportion of men who have tried medical beauty since the age of 19-22 has exceeded that of women, and "after 00" men have become the main growth point of medical beauty consumption. Hangzhou white-collar Chen Shanshan went back to her hometown in rural Henan for Chinese New Year during the Spring Festival this year, and she found that her cousin, who had not seen her for two years, had a little change in appearance. "I felt much younger than when I saw her two years ago, the skin became better, and the eyes seemed to be more divine." The price is much better than the city's. Among them, the plastic and cosmetic department of the Second People ’ s Hospital of Gansu Province has carried out more than 40 cosmetic and plastic surgeries every month. Perform all kinds of surgery.  Since the medical and aesthetic industry is one of the important components of the "beautiful economy", with high added value and strong driving force, the beauty consumption demand represented by medical beauty has become the fourth largest consumer hot spot after housing, automobiles and tourism in addition to basic living consumption.  Some cities have even taken medical beauty as a regional economic weighting point, such as Chengdu, Sichuan, which plans to build a "medical beauty capital", according to local government planning, the business income of the medical and beauty industry will reach 100 billion yuan in 2025 (units, Renminbi, the same below), and 200 billion yuan in 2030.

passages.title: 35% of global tourism revenue is Iran ’ s share
passages.passage: The advanced and widespread health services in Iran compared to neighboring countries and the relative superiority of these services in terms of price compared to many advanced countries has made the market of health and medical services in Iran attractive to citizens of other countries and a new branch of tourism called health tourism has emerged in the country.  The presence of many of these health tourists can not be limited to health services; these people can also travel to tourist or pilgrimage areas of Iran during and after treatment, which can also help the tourism development of those areas.  According to the Public Relations Department of the Institute of Cultural Heritage and Tourism, Saeed Amirian, discussed this issue at the specialized meeting of “Risk Management in Health Tourism ” held by the Institute of Tourism.  He described medical tourism as an economic activity that requires trade in services and participation of at least two medical and tourism sectors, adding that medical tourism in most cases includes dental services, cosmetic surgery and other types of surgeries.  Amirian, in the definition of health tourism, said: The use of services that improve or increase health and increase the morale of the person and in a place outside his residence for more than 24 hours is considered to be a health tourism.  Referring to the flow of patients from developed countries to developing countries to receive medical services, he said: “The intensifying factor in the flow of medical tourism in recent years is the third payer, employer or insurance, which encourages patients to find medical services at more affordable and faster prices. ”  In describing the dimensions of medical tourism in Iran, he said: Iran ’ s share of attracting this type of tourism during one year was only 350 million dollars; that is, only 0.35% of global health tourism revenue is Iran ’ s share, and with this amount of income, Iran ranks 10th in terms of attracting health tourists.  Referring to the importance of health tourism in Iran, Amirian stated: "The advanced and widespread health services in Iran compared to neighboring countries and the relative superiority of these services in terms of price compared to many advanced countries has made the market of health and health services of Iran attractive to citizens of other countries and a new branch of tourism called health tourism in the country emerges."  He went on to say something about the risk of tourism, saying: "It is mainly a defect in our knowledge of the future and risk is more in the future; risk and uncertainty start exactly where knowledge ends."  The expert added: "By stating that the risk of uncertainties with probabilities and possible outcomes is known, the risk classification is small and large scale, systematic and unsystematic.  Referring to the theoretical reflections of risk and uncertainty in tourism, Amirian said: "Risk is more as something to be avoided, but risk and uncertainty are considered as tourist attractions, especially adventure tourism."  He went on to describe the risks in tourism including individual risks for tourists, the responsibility of tourism service providers, destination risks and social risks, and by giving examples of risks in individual tourism, he explained the ways to cover risks for individual tourists, destination risks, social and tourism risks and governments and risk management.  Referring to the risk in tourism companies and its types, he said the four main strategies for risk management at the company level are knowledge, diversity, trust, and insurance, and said the risk management principle includes four steps; identification of small and large threats that the company may face in the future, analyzing risks and assessing the amount of costs that each risk may bring to the company, formulating a strategy for each possible risk and designing practical measures to deal with it and monitor damage. It is a risk to the company and a modification of past strategies and approaches.

passages.title: The main directions of beauty tourism: plastic, weight loss, sleep
passages.passage: Hair transplants in Turkey, sleep recovery in Switzerland, liposuction in Brazil: health tourism is booming and expanding horizons.  "Kommersant Style" tells about popular destinations and beauty programs from around the world.  Medical tourism is not a new phenomenon: there have always been those who want to improve their health abroad.  Many countries have their own medical specialization - they are able to do something better than others.  For example, the United States, Brazil, Japan, Mexico and Italy account for 41.4% of all global plastic surgeries.  Patients Beyond Borders estimates that 14 million people travel abroad every year to seek health care.  The obvious reason for the popularity of such tourism for many is the difference in prices.  For example, rhinoplasty in the United States will cost an average of $4.8 thousand, and in Thailand - $1.6 thousand, in a Moscow clinic - about 200 thousand rubles, depending on the complexity.  According to the WHO, Brazil has the best healthcare system in Latin America thanks to the mass accreditation of hospitals by the Joint International Commission (JCI – the largest and oldest medical accreditation organization in the world).  This led to the phenomenon of such tourism in the country.  Surgeons here are like hairdressers.  The most popular procedures in Brazil are liposuction, abdominoplasty and buttock augmentation, called brazilian butt lift.  Of course, the cult of the body is due to the hot climate.  Interestingly, every year the government subsidizes almost half a million operations, for the locals it is the “right to beauty ”.  The same operations are being carried out in neighboring Colombia.  Almost all patients are from the United States.  About 50,000 medical tourists visit the country every year.  From 2012 to 2018, medical tourism in Colombia grew by 264%.  There are more surgeons in South Korea.  It has one of the highest rates of plastic surgery in the world - about 1 million procedures per year, as well as the largest number of plastic surgeons per capita.  The country boasts a thriving tourism industry in this area.  In Korea, they strive to make facial features more Europeanized, so first of all, they change the shape of the nose, eyes (double eyelid surgery), jaws and cheekbones.  The management of Incheon Airport in Seoul even considered the possibility of creating a plastic surgery clinic in one of the terminals so that travelers did not need to travel around the city.  Photo: Getty Images Turkey, although not one of the most popular places for plastic surgery, but the leader in the market of hair transplantation.  Often on the streets of Istanbul and other major cities of the country you can meet people with bandaged heads.  For comparison, hair transplantation costs about $25 thousand in the United States and Europe, in Turkey - from $600 to $2 thousand, in a Moscow clinic - about 100 thousand rubles. for one graft (a group of one to four follicles).  According to the Hurriyet newspaper, in 2017, among 750 thousand tourists, 60 thousand came for hair transplantation.  Most are from the Middle East.  Popular destinations for dental tourism are Thailand, which is called the "Land of Smiles", Vietnam, Mexico and Costa Rica, in Europe - Hungary and Poland.  The most common procedures are the installation of implants, veneers and crowns, bleaching.  For example, Hungary has become the best place in Europe for this direction, it is visited annually by about 7 thousand patients.  This is due to favorable prices, qualified doctors and modern technologies.  Another two popular areas of tourism are the restoration of sleep and weight loss, but not just on detox programs, but thanks to sports in the camps.  Fitness camps are actually recreational sports camps for adults, where in the circle of like-minded people you can surf in Sri Lanka with the Good Story Surf school, go skating on Lake Baikal with Team Trip or learn how to ski in the vicinity of Gstaad with Pro Trener, World Class or SlimFitClub trainers.  Six Senses Douro Valley The newest wellness trend is slip-retreats, which literally teach you to sleep.  As a rule, resorts for the restoration of sleep are located in picturesque places: in the mountains, overlooking the water.  For example, in Portugal, Germany, Italy and Switzerland.  Services include a menu of pillows: from special anti-snoring to filled with water or memory foam, sleep masks and earplugs to choose from, a music library, meditation on demand, as well as staff who can advise on sleep issues.  For example, the hotel in Manhattan, The Benjamin, designed the Rest & Renew program with Rebecca Robbins, a professor of sleep medicine at Cornell University.  Similar programs have Six Senses Douro Valley in Portugal, Peak Health in Switzerland and Lefay on Lake Garda.  Berlin ’ s Swisstel included in its DeepSleep retreat sessions of aroma- and light therapy, as well as inhalation of mountain air.  Beauty tourism is a thriving niche in the industry.  Clinics and hotels offer complete packages, including transfers, flights, meals and even excursions.  According to a joint study by Visa and Oxford Economics, the global medical tourism industry will grow by 25% per year over the next ten years.  Daria Bogomolova

passages.title: Dental tourism, looking for a beautiful smile
passages.passage: ISNA / Khorasan Razavi Dental tourism is one of the most important forms of medical tourism and as an emerging industry, it is growing at a high rate.  The criteria for choosing a dentist for medical tourists depend on factors such as cost, location and quality of service.  The researchers noted that today ’ s unhealthy lifestyles, diets and longevity are gradually increasing the demand for quality and professional dental care.  The boom in the worldwide dental tourism market is primarily due to the increase in cases of dental malformation and the second is the increase in the desire for cosmetic dentistry.  The lower cost of treatment and better services in dental treatment in foreign country and the long waiting period for dental treatment in tourist country may boost the growth of this market in the future.  The global dental tourism market can be categorized in the type of treatment and area, and in terms of the type of treatment can be divided into preventive, restorative, prosthetic and other treatments.  Worldwide demand for cosmetic dentistry and therapeutic and restorative dentures has captured a large share of the market.  The pros of dental implant tourism, like medical tourism, are low medical costs, but there are many risks along the way.  Experts predict that the global dental implant market will reach $9 billion by 2027, making dental implants popular for a number of reasons, such as durability and usually success, which can last 20 years or more.  However, they are the best tooth replacement options and, of course, the most expensive, which in turn has led to an increase in dental tourism.  Also, market experts predict that the dental tourism industry will grow to a $5.83 billion sector by 2025, with the most important factors being the cost of treatment in countries and the lack of insurance coverage for many dental treatments.  In dental tourism, people travel abroad to receive dental care.  For example, a U.S. citizen may travel to Mexico to undergo dental implant surgery or an Australian may travel to Thailand to do oral matters.  With the above in mind, most dental tourists are from countries where the cost of treatment is very high, and the destinations in turn are countries known for their cheap services.  The results showed that the success of dental implants depends on the individual ’ s gums, which should be free of disease and infection, and patients who want to have implants but have gum disease should treat the gums first.  Dental tourism makes it difficult to achieve this goal, as it means multiple trips, and sometimes it is very unpleasant.  When the dental tourist encounters the entry of bacteria into the implant at the time of the gum surgery and the infection does not immediately show symptoms and the person returns to the origin, he will face infection after a few days.  Although infections caused by implants are treatable, they are difficult to treat and can be costly, and sometimes a lack of health standards and regulations can lead to these problems.  The researchers noted that regular dental checkups and oral hygiene will be the most important factor for reducing medical tourism trips.  Dentists, in some cases, make medical tourism more charitable, not to reduce costs, but to provide services to low-income people.  Doctors travel to poor countries to put their skills at the mercy of other people and provide the key to good oral health.  Dental tourism in the corona crisis Many patients travel to areas outside their country in search of a perfect smile to fix their oral problems.  According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), travel is likely to increase the incidence of COVID-19, and the farther the trip, the greater the risk.  It should be noted, however, that before COVID-19, travelers were also at risk of developing other diseases.  The financial impact on dental tourism has been dramatic, as this type of tourism will be difficult when patients are unwilling to perform services or unable to travel to the country due to quarantine or travel ban.
