Title: Medical Suitcase in the Hands of Providers!
Content: "One of the important concerns and challenges in the field of medical tourism is the proper and proper guidance of foreign patients to Iranian medical centers, that medical tourists from the moment of arrival in the country will not be caught by the dealers, non-medical interventions by physicians for applicants for cosmetic surgeries will not be done, and finally, medical tourists will be able to advertise Iranian medical services by receiving standard medical services in reputable centers."  According to ISNA, Iran's newspaper wrote: "Medical tourists can be described as the phenomenon of traveling to different countries to access medical services.  On this basis, in the description of medical tourism, patients from developed countries travel to undeveloped countries in search of medical treatment.  The reason is clear.  The cost of treatment in underdeveloped countries is three times lower than in developed countries.  Medical tourism in India is growing rapidly.  In 2004, 1.2 million patients visited India for health care and 1.1 million medical tourists visited Thailand.  While increasing GDP, economic development, job opportunities are among the advantages of this industry, and Iran can also be referred to as a combination of medical and recreational tourism and the existence of historical and ancient monuments, pilgrimage centers and natural beauty and natural remedies (traditional medicine) at the top of the patients of the Persian Gulf countries, Afghanistan, Pakistan, Europe, Turkey, Azerbaijan and...  But the lack of advertising and branding of overseas medical tourism, as well as the presence of unauthorized intermediaries and institutions of health tourism, has put the industry in serious harm ’ s way.  The issue that has recently become a significant point for top managers of the country, following the increase in exchange rates, and even the officials of the Ministry of Health have been thinking about the development of the medical tourism industry.  As activists in this field say, one of the important concerns and challenges in this regard is the proper guidance of foreign patients to Iranian medical centers, that medical tourists from the moment of arrival in the country will not be caught by dealers, non-medical interventions by physicians for cosmetic surgery applicants, and finally, medical tourists will be able to advertise Iranian medical services by receiving standard medical services in reputable medical centers.  About the role and general policies of the Ministry of Health in the development of medical tourism, challenges and opportunities to attract and follow patients from the country of origin to Iran, we spoke with Dr. Saeed Hashemzadeh, the head of the health tourism department of the Ministry of Health, which you can read below.  How are medical tourists attracted to Iranian treatment centers?  I mean, because of the presence of intermediaries, foreign patients are not properly directed to medical centers and do not reach the hands of specialists, and sometimes we hear that they fall into the hands of dealers and unauthorized institutions, and they also direct applicants for these types of surgeries to people who are not qualified.  Is there a specific model for guiding the patient to the medical centers that the medical tourist does not receive non-standard medical services and does not lead to invalid medical centers?  We at the Ministry of Health believe that dealers are not causes, but effects.  Therefore, if we want to deal with the phenomenon of brokerage in the field of health tourism, we will simply ask the police to stop the work of dealers, but we believe that this approach will not eliminate the work of dealers.  So we tried to identify the problems that exist in the supply chain in health tourism, and then, based on that, brokers out of the industry.  Of course, I should say that the country ’ s medical centers have capabilities and capabilities, but they have not been able to properly introduce and present these capabilities abroad, where our customers are present.  Who gives the foreign patient the information at which medical center and under what conditions and at what cost?  The answer to this question is clear: an element found in the name of the dealer.  Because of this gap or lack of information between health centers and patients applying abroad, an element called a broker plays this role.  In order to reduce the activity of brokers in principle, we need to see who is acting in successful models of the world and who is going to give this information to the patient to reduce the activity of brokers.  When you look at successful models in West Asia, including India, Turkey and Jordan, there is an actor here called “Facilitator Company. ”  The main task of facilitating companies is to provide the necessary medical information from health centers and physicians and to inform about transparent prices to foreign patients. With this knowledge, we designed a regulation to form companies based on this bylaw that work in this area, that is, these companies play a role in making decisions for patients who enter the country, then facilitate the entry of the patient to the country and after receiving medical services from the patient. Outside, follow up after treatment.  Of course, follow-up after treatment is an important part of the work that has been forgotten in our country, that is, we did not have a regular and structured follow-up, so we started to do the same.  The companies facilitating the recruitment of medical tourism have a specific channel for attracting foreign patients, how do these companies cut the hands of brokers and intermediaries in this field?  These companies, with the permission of the Ministry of Health, attract different types of foreign patients to Iranian medical centers.  They start their activities in cyberspace, including websites and social networks, and inform the people of foreign countries about the capabilities of their contractual health centers in cyberspace.  The second solution is to attend national and international exhibitions and events of health tourism.  The third option is to join similar companies in the target markets.  That is, Iranian companies connect with similar companies in Iraq and Afghanistan and refer the patient to our country.  A very important solution is to join the facilitators with insurance companies on the other side of the border, which, of course, has not been paid attention to in our country.  That is, there is a lack of actors here, and that is the connection of foreign insurance companies to Iranian facilitators in order to attract patients in an organized manner in international markets.  This is a model that is used in all countries.  In our country, which of the channels you mentioned provides the way to attract foreign patients?  Other than the type of brokerage, the type that is very emphasized is the attraction of the patient through cyberspace.  Does it seem like there ’ s more to attract foreign patients?  Do you have any statistics about how many medical tourists enter Iran ’ s treatment centers through dealers?  It is not more than 5 months since the notification of the regulations of the Facilitating Companies should take some time to make a proper comparison.  The vast majority of patients entering treatment centers are owned by these dealers, but the balance shifts in favor of companies.  Between 80% and 90% of patients are brought by brokers and the share of direct patient visits is less than 10%.  At the moment, the weight is shifting towards companies.  Medical centers have reported the same to us, that is, the centers that previously said that 90 percent of foreign patients come to Iran through dealers now say that 70 percent of them enter the country through dealers.  The trend of change, although small, has begun, that is, 10% of the market is owned by companies, while we only allowed 15% of these companies to operate.  If insurance is added to the supply chain, this will happen quickly.  You mentioned the connection of Iranian facilitators to foreign insurance companies to attract medical tourism.  Since the arrival of medical tourists in Iran, what is the process of receiving their services?  Please let me know if medical visas are issued for patients.  Do you offer unpaid and VIP services to them?  On the basis of what process the patient enters the medical center of a foreign country, let me first say the model of the world.  It is usually the case that the patient travels to another country to receive a special service that is not covered by his or her insurance.  For example, in Europe, if a person with a doctor ’ s diagnosis needs a knee replacement and this service is not covered by insurance, the insurance office suggests that the patient use the services of a consultant facilitator and go to India or Turkey for knee surgery, in which case the knee replacement service is covered by the insurance of the country of origin, that is, this person does not have insurance coverage for joint replacement in Europe, but in India and Turkey. The insurance mode not only covers the costs of the patient, but also the airline ticket and accommodation costs.  In the United States, for example, a knee replacement costs $220,000, but if the patient goes to India with the best hotel, plane and service, it costs $15,000 for his insurance company.  In our country, almost the same cycle must be carried out.  We will be successful in medical tourism when we can implement the same general cycle, for now, the process is like this: a patient who has been recommended to do medical work in Iraq will enter Iran.  If it is in a healthy cycle, with the advertisements that the facilitator companies have in cyberspace, the patient chooses which city and hospital to enter, then the patient contracts with the facilitator company, and the company coordinates the visa, ticket, accommodation and transportation of the patient, and the patient enters Iran and returns to his home country after receiving the service, of course his treatment is followed by the facilitator company. Title: 【 TAIWAN HEALTH INSPECTION 】 How does Kaohsiung win after Asia 's leading medical tourism? ｜ Hong Kong 01 ｜ The World Says
Content: Kaohsiung has designated 2019 as the “first year of medical tourism ” and is aggressively marketing local medical products.  However, looking at other advanced cities in Asia, it is certainly not a pioneer in the development of medical tourism.  Bangkok in Thailand, Seoul in Korea, Kuala Lumpur in Malaysia and other places have been implementing medical tourism for many years, each with its own characteristics.  Can Kaohsiung, a rising star, develop a unique chain of medical tourism industry to compete with other Asian cities?  (This is the sixth feature of the "Taiwan Health Insurance" series) Can hospitals in Kaohsiung capture a share of the medical tourism industry among the best in Asia? (photo by Yang Yalin) Chang Hung-tai, director of Kaohsiung Municipal Union Hospital, believes that the advantages of Kaohsiung and the whole of Taiwan are its internationally recognized medical standards and low medical service prices.  "Taiwan medical care because of the relationship of health insurance, the cost is very low, almost one-tenth of that of other countries, cheaper than the mainland, our drug prices are also low, many mainlanders are willing to come to Taiwan."  First, the price is low, and the second is high quality credibility.  Taiwan ’ s Ministry of Health and Welfare has strict management, and health insurance audits are conducted from time to time. ”  Zhang Hongtai believes that the surrounding potential competitors have their own advantages. For example, Thailand has a lot of experience in tourism medicine, and even several hospitals are specialized in tourism medicine, so the service personnel of the entire hospital have been carefully trained and tailored according to the principles of tourism medicine.  Medical tourism in the capital Bangkok is mature enough to be a "package tour" and receive thousands of medical tourists.  “Many hospitals have even scheduled their annual schedules … Taiwan can make this kind of money. ” Thailand is the world ’ s largest medical tourism destination, with more than 2 million foreign tourists coming to Thailand each year to receive medical services, and the related industries make an average annual profit of 120 billion baht (about HK $29.6 billion).  Thailand is famous for its rich tourism resources, coupled with the maturity of medical technology in health examination, plastic surgery, dentistry and other aspects, the average price of related services is only about half of that of European and American countries, so medical tourism has been one of the alternative tourism projects in Thailand.  The famous CBS news program “60 Minutes Magazine ” reported on Bangkok ’ s famous“ Bumrungrad Hospital ” in a feature way back in 2005.  The hospital receives more than 500,000 foreign patients from more than 190 countries around the world every year. It has the largest health screening center in Bangkok, serving more than 60,000 people every year, which shows that its medical tourism resources are very sufficient.  Bangkok ’ s famous “Regal Hospital ” (Bumrungrad Hospital). (online picture) When it comes to medical tourism, it has to mention Seoul, South Korea. Its advanced medical minimally invasive technology has always led Asia, and it has a mature operating system and supporting medical aesthetic technology such as microplastic surgery, which has become the Asian plastic surgery center.  Since 2009, the annual growth rate of medical tourists visiting Korea has exceeded 34%, and they come from China, the United States, Russia, Japan and other countries.  In December last year, the Korean Medical Tourism Service Center at Incheon International Airport was officially opened, allowing foreign travelers to book local consultation services, nearby dining and accommodation facilities, transportation to the hospital, and more.  The service center also has a resident nurse who is fluent in multiple languages, providing tourists with professional consulting services for medical tourism.  The government has partnered with the industry to make it the number one driver of medical tourism.  The medical tourism industry in Seoul is mainly engaged in microsurgery and cosmetic surgery.  (Online photo) Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia has always been the best destination for medical tourism. In 2016, Kuala Lumpur was named the Best Medical Tourism Destination of the Year by International Medical Tourism Magazine.  Kuala Lumpur also has a language advantage. Due to its multi-ethnic society, there is no shortage of health care workers fluent in Chinese and English. In addition to this, it has been favored by medical tourists from Europe and the United States, and it has also helped it to seize the huge Chinese market and become a rival to Kaohsiung.  (Hong Kong 01 map) Kaohsiung needs to "decorate" first to enter the market. Zhang Hongtai admitted that Kaohsiung still needs to prepare a lot of things in medical tourism and do a good job of supporting the work.  He cited the United Hospital, where he worked, as an example, because it belongs to the regional hospital level, it has the conditions to build medical aesthetics equipment.  He pointed out that the first thing to do is to redecorate the internal facilities and renovate them into a new type of ward.  "Medical beauty is not the same as general medical treatment, can not be treated as a general patient."  They want to have a private, safe and beautiful ward, "he said.  Another problem is professionalism.  Zhang Hongtai believes that at present, Taiwan does not restrict what doctors can do medical aesthetics, as long as they have a doctor's license, so there are many people doing it, and the quality is difficult to control.  He does not mean that doctors have problems with their medical skills, but that the medical community should have a unique professional process and code for medical aesthetics in order to enhance the attractiveness of medical tourism in Kaohsiung and compete with neighboring regions.  For example, laser, if used inappropriately, may cause burns.  Therefore, even if you do medical aesthetics, you still need a professional evaluation by a specialist.  If Kaohsiung is to do a good job in medical tourism, it must pay attention to the professionalism of medical aesthetics.  "What we do is a medical beauty with a certain standard, and it can't be seen as a night market selling things."  "The Big Thing".  With professionalism, we can have the quality and safety that the international medical industry has always emphasized. There are already large medical and aesthetic teams in nearby cities, who value the quality of their services and treat their customers as valued guests rather than simply patients. Title: Tracing prostheses used in plastic surgery
Content: According to Mehr News Agency, Hamed Bateni, in connection with the issue of medical tourism, said: "The medical conditions of the country have scientifically caused patients from other countries to travel to Iran from the region and even from remote parts of the world and benefit from the medical field in Iran."  Pointing out that some people think that patients from other parts of the world come to Iran only because of the cheapness of medical services, he said: "This is a mistake because many countries offer cheaper services in the field of medicine, but patients do not trust and do not want to travel to their country for treatment because their medicine is not strong or the facilities of surgical centers are weak and sometimes unsterile."  The head of the Iranian Society of Plastic and Aesthetic Surgeons continued: In recent years, measures have been started to organize medical tourists through the Ministry of Health and gradually the programs are going to be written and comprehensive so that we hope that soon the field of medical tourism will be completely out of control and operated by translators or non-standard institutions and only under the supervision of the Ministry of Health.  In response to the question of what effect the sanctions of the enemies have had on the field of plastic and cosmetic surgery and whether you are facing a shortage of drugs in this field, he noted: The field of plastic and cosmetic surgery is not very dependent on the aspect of drugs with shortages, but equipment and devices such as implants, prosthetics and beauty products with changing currency fluctuations have increased prices and sometimes products are scarce and imports are not easy.  He said: "The equipment required by plastic surgeons is provided by different brands, depending on the company's production and distribution and their price varies, but all of these equipment and equipment are of good quality and there is no problem in this regard."  The head of the Iranian Society of Plastic and Aesthetic Surgeons noted that most of the equipment and equipment needed for plastic and cosmetic surgery such as implants and prostheses do not have passenger or luggage entry because the reference of these devices is known and all of them have serial numbers that can be traced on the website of the manufacturer and distributor, so there is no concern in this regard.  Bateni said that patients can use this serial number and specifications to track the prosthesis and device used in their body and make sure of its quality, because the prostheses used in plastic and cosmetic surgeries are different from some other surgeries and the patient has a direct role in its preparation.

Content: Why dental tourism is popular in Moldova, what is the main problem of patients, as well as what unusual requests some of them turn to - this and not only told Dr. Valery Fala. Title: Overseas medical treatment is on the rise, and the medical tourism industry in Asia is booming.
Content: SEOUL, Oct. 4 (Reuters) - This is one of the fastest growing industries in Asia, and it is not showing signs of weakness even as the global economy falters.  Today, medical tourism has become a billion-dollar industry.  From cosmetic surgery to heart bypass, hospitals in India, Singapore and South Korea receive more than 1 million foreign patients a year for no less than the following reasons: cost-effective surgery, no waiting in line for treatment, advanced technology and well-trained doctors.  Industry experts predict that as the number of new affluent people in the region increases, the medical tourism industry in the region will grow at a rate of 15-20% per year.  “As Asia has become richer and more mobile, medical tourism in Asia … seems to be growing, ” said David Vequist, director of the Center for Medical Tourism Research at the University of the Incarnate Word in Texas.  “Consumer choice is now a powerful force in the healthcare industry, with Asia ’ s aging population, growing obesity, sicker populations and more in need all having an impact on the healthcare industry. ”  Medscape News predicts that Asia ’ s medical tourism industry could generate $4.4 billion in value by 2012.  Among them, the largest number of patients came from the United States.  To avoid the high cost of private treatment at home, many Americans seek medical treatment overseas.  In general, this can save Americans 40% -50% of the cost of treatment.  Now, a new patient has been added to the operating table - the Chinese.  Many Chinese people try to solve their problems at any cost.  "No matter how expensive it is, I will do it," said Liu Xiaoyang, a 34-year-old Shanghainese who has just undergone double eyelid surgery, plastic surgery and jaw correction in Seoul, South Korea.  The rise of China's affluent class and the fascination with the "Korean Wave", to the popularity of pop music and Korean dramas, has led to a huge increase in the medical tourism industry in South Korea, especially the plastic surgery industry.  "Every time I watch Korean dramas and TV programs, I think the characters on TV are beautiful, and I hope I can be like them," Liu said.  Kim Byung-gun, a plastic surgeon at BK Dongyang Plastic Surgery Clinic in Seoul, says his patients are as young as six and as old as 70.  On average, their surgery costs about $5,000-10,000.  "The medical tourism industry will become one of the engines of the Korean economy," Kim said, adding that the "Korean Wave" is a key factor in promoting the development of the medical tourism industry in the country.

Title: Chengdu medical beauty market supply and demand two strong driving consumption
Content: The number of medical and aesthetic institutions has reached 381; the scale of the industry is only second to Beijing and Shanghai, and the operating income of the medical and aesthetic industry in Chengdu will reach 100 billion yuan (RMB, the same below) in 2025 and 200 billion yuan in 2030, creating a leading and world-renowned "medical and aesthetic capital" in mainland China.  China News Service reported that Wang Xidan, secretary general of Chengdu Medical and Beauty Industry Association, said that the scale of Chengdu's medical and aesthetic industry in 2018 has reached 48.7 billion yuan.  "The development of the entire industry has formed a relatively healthy cycle, and the market is showing a state of supply and demand." Wang Xidan said that concentrated medical and aesthetic resources and a higher price ratio than first-tier cities have attracted more and more consumers to Chengdu.  In 2018, the number of medical and aesthetic institutions in Chengdu soared to 407, a surge of 131 from the previous year.  The Plastic Surgery Hospital of the Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences also chose to host the first Beijing-outside branch of Chengdu ’ s eight major medical and aesthetic hospitals in Chengdu in 2018.  Tang Yong, director of eight major medical and aesthetic hospitals in Chengdu, said that with nearly 40 days of closure due to the COVID-19 epidemic, the hospital's revenue in 2020 still increased by about 30% compared to 2019.  With the rise of the “face value economy ”, medical beauty has gradually become a pressing need for some contemporary Chinese, among which light medical beauty, which has a short recovery period and low risk, is most popular.  Due to the consideration of safety, reliability and other factors, a large number of consumers have moved to cities where medical and aesthetic resources are concentrated, and "medical and aesthetic tourism" has also quietly emerged.  The total revenue of Sichuan Huamei Zixin Medical Aesthetic Hospital in 2020 is about 600 million yuan.  Xue Hong, general manager of the hospital, said that about 20% of the annual number of patients treated by the hospital are foreign consumers who come to the hospital.  "Especially in recent years, the number of these consumers has grown rapidly, from Gansu, Qinghai, Yunnan, Guizhou and other provinces."  Wang Xidan sees this phenomenon as a new inflection point for the development of Chengdu's medical and aesthetic industry.  She said that medical beauty and tourism, finance, catering and other industries are expected to achieve the continuous development, the next step of the Chengdu Medical and Beauty Industry Association will work from this aspect, strive to create a consumer ecosystem that can maximize meet the diversified needs of consumers, and enhance the competitiveness of Chengdu medical and beauty industry.  Liu Lu, a professor of economics at Southwest University of Finance and Economics, said that the medical and aesthetic industry, as a new economy that can promote regional economic development, should care for its growth, but also need to strengthen supervision, train high-quality personnel, and formulate more stringent industry norms.

Title: 35% of global tourism revenue is Iran ’ s share
Content: The advanced and widespread health services in Iran compared to neighboring countries and the relative superiority of these services in terms of price compared to many advanced countries has made the market of health and medical services in Iran attractive to citizens of other countries and a new branch of tourism called health tourism has emerged in the country.  The presence of many of these health tourists can not be limited to health services; these people can also travel to tourist or pilgrimage areas of Iran during and after treatment, which can also help the tourism development of those areas.  According to the Public Relations Department of the Institute of Cultural Heritage and Tourism, Saeed Amirian, discussed this issue at the specialized meeting of “Risk Management in Health Tourism ” held by the Institute of Tourism.  He described medical tourism as an economic activity that requires trade in services and participation of at least two medical and tourism sectors, adding that medical tourism in most cases includes dental services, cosmetic surgery and other types of surgeries.  Amirian, in the definition of health tourism, said: The use of services that improve or increase health and increase the morale of the person and in a place outside his residence for more than 24 hours is considered to be a health tourism.  Referring to the flow of patients from developed countries to developing countries to receive medical services, he said: “The intensifying factor in the flow of medical tourism in recent years is the third payer, employer or insurance, which encourages patients to find medical services at more affordable and faster prices. ”  In describing the dimensions of medical tourism in Iran, he said: Iran ’ s share of attracting this type of tourism during one year was only 350 million dollars; that is, only 0.35% of global health tourism revenue is Iran ’ s share, and with this amount of income, Iran ranks 10th in terms of attracting health tourists.  Referring to the importance of health tourism in Iran, Amirian stated: "The advanced and widespread health services in Iran compared to neighboring countries and the relative superiority of these services in terms of price compared to many advanced countries has made the market of health and health services of Iran attractive to citizens of other countries and a new branch of tourism called health tourism in the country emerges."  He went on to say something about the risk of tourism, saying: "It is mainly a defect in our knowledge of the future and risk is more in the future; risk and uncertainty start exactly where knowledge ends."  The expert added: "By stating that the risk of uncertainties with probabilities and possible outcomes is known, the risk classification is small and large scale, systematic and unsystematic.  Referring to the theoretical reflections of risk and uncertainty in tourism, Amirian said: "Risk is more as something to be avoided, but risk and uncertainty are considered as tourist attractions, especially adventure tourism."  He went on to describe the risks in tourism including individual risks for tourists, the responsibility of tourism service providers, destination risks and social risks, and by giving examples of risks in individual tourism, he explained the ways to cover risks for individual tourists, destination risks, social and tourism risks and governments and risk management.  Referring to the risk in tourism companies and its types, he said the four main strategies for risk management at the company level are knowledge, diversity, trust, and insurance, and said the risk management principle includes four steps; identification of small and large threats that the company may face in the future, analyzing risks and assessing the amount of costs that each risk may bring to the company, formulating a strategy for each possible risk and designing practical measures to deal with it and monitor damage. It is a risk to the company and a modification of past strategies and approaches.

Title: The main directions of beauty tourism: plastic, weight loss, sleep
Content: Hair transplants in Turkey, sleep recovery in Switzerland, liposuction in Brazil: health tourism is booming and expanding horizons.  "Kommersant Style" tells about popular destinations and beauty programs from around the world.  Medical tourism is not a new phenomenon: there have always been those who want to improve their health abroad.  Many countries have their own medical specialization - they are able to do something better than others.  For example, the United States, Brazil, Japan, Mexico and Italy account for 41.4% of all global plastic surgeries.  Patients Beyond Borders estimates that 14 million people travel abroad every year to seek health care.  The obvious reason for the popularity of such tourism for many is the difference in prices.  For example, rhinoplasty in the United States will cost an average of $4.8 thousand, and in Thailand - $1.6 thousand, in a Moscow clinic - about 200 thousand rubles, depending on the complexity.  According to the WHO, Brazil has the best healthcare system in Latin America thanks to the mass accreditation of hospitals by the Joint International Commission (JCI – the largest and oldest medical accreditation organization in the world).  This led to the phenomenon of such tourism in the country.  Surgeons here are like hairdressers.  The most popular procedures in Brazil are liposuction, abdominoplasty and buttock augmentation, called brazilian butt lift.  Of course, the cult of the body is due to the hot climate.  Interestingly, every year the government subsidizes almost half a million operations, for the locals it is the “right to beauty ”.  The same operations are being carried out in neighboring Colombia.  Almost all patients are from the United States.  About 50,000 medical tourists visit the country every year.  From 2012 to 2018, medical tourism in Colombia grew by 264%.  There are more surgeons in South Korea.  It has one of the highest rates of plastic surgery in the world - about 1 million procedures per year, as well as the largest number of plastic surgeons per capita.  The country boasts a thriving tourism industry in this area.  In Korea, they strive to make facial features more Europeanized, so first of all, they change the shape of the nose, eyes (double eyelid surgery), jaws and cheekbones.  The management of Incheon Airport in Seoul even considered the possibility of creating a plastic surgery clinic in one of the terminals so that travelers did not need to travel around the city.  Photo: Getty Images Turkey, although not one of the most popular places for plastic surgery, but the leader in the market of hair transplantation.  Often on the streets of Istanbul and other major cities of the country you can meet people with bandaged heads.  For comparison, hair transplantation costs about $25 thousand in the United States and Europe, in Turkey - from $600 to $2 thousand, in a Moscow clinic - about 100 thousand rubles. for one graft (a group of one to four follicles).  According to the Hurriyet newspaper, in 2017, among 750 thousand tourists, 60 thousand came for hair transplantation.  Most are from the Middle East.  Popular destinations for dental tourism are Thailand, which is called the "Land of Smiles", Vietnam, Mexico and Costa Rica, in Europe - Hungary and Poland.  The most common procedures are the installation of implants, veneers and crowns, bleaching.  For example, Hungary has become the best place in Europe for this direction, it is visited annually by about 7 thousand patients.  This is due to favorable prices, qualified doctors and modern technologies.  Another two popular areas of tourism are the restoration of sleep and weight loss, but not just on detox programs, but thanks to sports in the camps.  Fitness camps are actually recreational sports camps for adults, where in the circle of like-minded people you can surf in Sri Lanka with the Good Story Surf school, go skating on Lake Baikal with Team Trip or learn how to ski in the vicinity of Gstaad with Pro Trener, World Class or SlimFitClub trainers.  Six Senses Douro Valley The newest wellness trend is slip-retreats, which literally teach you to sleep.  As a rule, resorts for the restoration of sleep are located in picturesque places: in the mountains, overlooking the water.  For example, in Portugal, Germany, Italy and Switzerland.  Services include a menu of pillows: from special anti-snoring to filled with water or memory foam, sleep masks and earplugs to choose from, a music library, meditation on demand, as well as staff who can advise on sleep issues.  For example, the hotel in Manhattan, The Benjamin, designed the Rest & Renew program with Rebecca Robbins, a professor of sleep medicine at Cornell University.  Similar programs have Six Senses Douro Valley in Portugal, Peak Health in Switzerland and Lefay on Lake Garda.  Berlin ’ s Swisstel included in its DeepSleep retreat sessions of aroma- and light therapy, as well as inhalation of mountain air.  Beauty tourism is a thriving niche in the industry.  Clinics and hotels offer complete packages, including transfers, flights, meals and even excursions.  According to a joint study by Visa and Oxford Economics, the global medical tourism industry will grow by 25% per year over the next ten years.  Daria Bogomolova

Title: Dental tourism, looking for a beautiful smile
Content: ISNA / Khorasan Razavi Dental tourism is one of the most important forms of medical tourism and as an emerging industry, it is growing at a high rate.  The criteria for choosing a dentist for medical tourists depend on factors such as cost, location and quality of service.  The researchers noted that today ’ s unhealthy lifestyles, diets and longevity are gradually increasing the demand for quality and professional dental care.  The boom in the worldwide dental tourism market is primarily due to the increase in cases of dental malformation and the second is the increase in the desire for cosmetic dentistry.  The lower cost of treatment and better services in dental treatment in foreign country and the long waiting period for dental treatment in tourist country may boost the growth of this market in the future.  The global dental tourism market can be categorized in the type of treatment and area, and in terms of the type of treatment can be divided into preventive, restorative, prosthetic and other treatments.  Worldwide demand for cosmetic dentistry and therapeutic and restorative dentures has captured a large share of the market.  The pros of dental implant tourism, like medical tourism, are low medical costs, but there are many risks along the way.  Experts predict that the global dental implant market will reach $9 billion by 2027, making dental implants popular for a number of reasons, such as durability and usually success, which can last 20 years or more.  However, they are the best tooth replacement options and, of course, the most expensive, which in turn has led to an increase in dental tourism.  Also, market experts predict that the dental tourism industry will grow to a $5.83 billion sector by 2025, with the most important factors being the cost of treatment in countries and the lack of insurance coverage for many dental treatments.  In dental tourism, people travel abroad to receive dental care.  For example, a U.S. citizen may travel to Mexico to undergo dental implant surgery or an Australian may travel to Thailand to do oral matters.  With the above in mind, most dental tourists are from countries where the cost of treatment is very high, and the destinations in turn are countries known for their cheap services.  The results showed that the success of dental implants depends on the individual ’ s gums, which should be free of disease and infection, and patients who want to have implants but have gum disease should treat the gums first.  Dental tourism makes it difficult to achieve this goal, as it means multiple trips, and sometimes it is very unpleasant.  When the dental tourist encounters the entry of bacteria into the implant at the time of the gum surgery and the infection does not immediately show symptoms and the person returns to the origin, he will face infection after a few days.  Although infections caused by implants are treatable, they are difficult to treat and can be costly, and sometimes a lack of health standards and regulations can lead to these problems.  The researchers noted that regular dental checkups and oral hygiene will be the most important factor for reducing medical tourism trips.  Dentists, in some cases, make medical tourism more charitable, not to reduce costs, but to provide services to low-income people.  Doctors travel to poor countries to put their skills at the mercy of other people and provide the key to good oral health.  Dental tourism in the corona crisis Many patients travel to areas outside their country in search of a perfect smile to fix their oral problems.  According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), travel is likely to increase the incidence of COVID-19, and the farther the trip, the greater the risk.  It should be noted, however, that before COVID-19, travelers were also at risk of developing other diseases.  The financial impact on dental tourism has been dramatic, as this type of tourism will be difficult when patients are unwilling to perform services or unable to travel to the country due to quarantine or travel ban.  References sciencedirect.com romaniandentaltourism.com gordondentalimplantsandcosmetics.com imtj.com transparencymarketresearch.com End of message

passages.title: Pocket park, this year new renovation of 50 - citizens out of the house there is a park, you can walk, chat, fitness, enjoy the green -- News Morning Post official website
passages.passage: Morning Post reporter Yu Wenyan at the corner of Fuxing East Road and Zhonghua Road, there is a small green space of only 500 square meters, which has installed three leisure seats and some small outdoor fitness equipment, which has become a "Cao Jia Street small garden" in the eyes of nearby residents. A number of pocket parks, which are often referred to as street gardens in the past, their presence not only allows nearby residents to walk, chat, fitness, and enjoy the green, but also lights up the environmental face of the block.  It is reported that the city built 47 pocket parks last year, and this year will build or upgrade 50.  Last year, 47 pocket parks were built at the corner of Fuxing East Road and Zhonghua Road, with a small green space of only 500 square meters.  Once, it was a green space, and now, it has become a "small garden in Cao Jia Street" in the eyes of nearby residents.  In Hongkou District, after a number of illegal buildings were demolished, a pocket park was built.  For example, the Huishan Garden at 207 Lintong Road, do not look at it with an area of only 408 square meters, but "five dirty", not only has exquisite and small green products, but also fitness trails.  In order to coordinate with the surrounding architectural style, the entrance to the park has also been designed in the style of Shikumen.  More than 2,300 square meters of public green space has been built in the area of 1501 North Xinshi Road, Jiangwan Town.  If there are no pavilions and seats for rest, it is also a little larger than the green space of Cao Jia Street.  But with activities and rest facilities, it becomes a simple little park.  According to incomplete statistics, 47 pocket parks were built in the city last year.  Pocket Park is not clearly defined Pocket Park, which originated from the proposal of the New York Parks Association in 1963, originally refers to small parks scattered in high-density urban centers and distributed in plaques.  Since the beginning of just over half a century, the United States, Britain, Japan and China and other countries have begun to have their own unique "pocket park plan".  Today's pocket parks refer to small green open spaces scattered in plaques in the city.  At present, there is no clear definition of pocket parks, and various small green spaces, small parks, street gardens, and small community sports venues in the city are common pocket parks.  Liu Yuelai, a scholar at Tongji University's School of Architecture and Urban Planning, said that there is currently no clear definition of the size of the pocket park.  In terms of area, he personally feels that it can be counted as small as tens of square meters and as large as thousands of square meters.  Unlike the comprehensive park, it offers simple and short breaks, such as a walk after a meal, a small sitting or children's play.  The city's greening department said that at present, their definition of the street garden from the area generally refers to the area of 300-3000 square meters of green space.  The municipal greening and cityscape administration bureau recently introduced that this year Shencheng plans to build or upgrade 50 pocket parks.  The actual number may be more than that.  Among the 79 colorful community projects recently released in Pudong, nearly 40 projects are defined as pocket parks. The pocket park in Hongkou District is planning to build the second phase of Yongnian Li, so that the pocket park function is becoming more and more perfect.  This year, Putuo plans to build a new 10,000 li community green space with a total area of 14,930 square meters, consisting of forests, wetlands and pocket parks.  The first part covers an area of about 10,970 square meters, and is designed to be an accessible urban forest and wetland.  The second part is located at the northwest corner of Wanquan Road and Fu Ping Road, covering an area of about 3960 square meters, and is designed to be positioned as a pocket park.  Fang Yan, deputy director of the municipal greening and cityscape administration bureau, said that the greening department is trying to make more parks around the citizens, even some street gardens and pocket parks, so that people can walk in parks not far from their homes.  According to the relevant person in charge of the municipal greening and cityscape administration bureau, the goal of allowing citizens to go out 500 meters to see a 3,000 square meter park green space has been basically achieved.  However, some residents feel that the greening of Shanghai is not enough.  Shanghai is still far behind Beijing, Hangzhou, Guangzhou and other cities, as well as New York, London and Paris.  For example, according to the area of public green space in the city and the base ratio of the resident population of more than 24 million, the per capita public green space is only about 8%, while some cities in China are generally more than 10%.  Therefore, in the case of limited land resources, Shanghai can only build more "pocket parks" and make dojo in snail shells.  It is understood that there are 243 urban parks in Shanghai, and by 2020, the number of urban parks will reach 300, forming a three-level system of "pocket parks - community parks - regional parks", and basically realizing that citizens go out 500 meters to have parks.

passages.title: The gradual introduction of roof gardens to the metropolises of the country / What are the benefits of green roof structures?
passages.passage: Travelers from advanced industrial cities such as Tokyo, Toronto, Berlin, London, and Singapore are frequently confronted with buildings and towers, whether residential or commercial, with green roofs.  These green spaces, although not a new phenomenon in human history, were seen in distant times even in the influential civilizations of Iran, such as Mesopotamia, but after centuries of forgetfulness, they have now come back to the aid of human life and breathing.  According to the Tadbir and Hope Information Network, the cities mentioned are all suffering from high population and density, abundant industrial environments and high traffic and congestion, and therefore breathing space for the city is low.  As a result, the area of green space of the city has been unintentionally reduced and there is not much room for its expansion.  With these conditions, the maximum use of limited spaces to help the environment and life is a priority for urban planners.  It is not surprising that the city management system in all of these cities supports the creation of green spaces on the roof of buildings.  It is called the Garden of Eden.  There are similar examples of cities in our country.  Apart from Tehran, a number of metropolises of the country are also facing high population density and lack of green space and breathing space for the city, and no permanent solution has yet been found.  In recent years, as the problem of air pollution has become more serious, efforts have been made to use the world ’ s new solutions to address it.  Perhaps this is why the roof gardens in the metropolises of the country are slowly opening up.  Although these projects have not yet been comprehensively established among the public, it is foreseeable that in the coming years, they will become not only useful but necessary projects that will require the existence of a certain number of them in metropolitan areas.  Roofing gardens are a necessity in metropolises that grow vertically to horizontally and suffer from the problem of air pollution and lack of green space and even recreational space.  Because the advantage of roof gardens is not limited to helping the environment, it encompasses a large range of technical functions of buildings and even the social sphere of cities.  Reducing heat absorption by the building complex, reducing energy consumption, increasing urban green space per capita, improving air pollution, improving the quality of management and utilization of rainwater, social effects and creating a fun and refreshing environment, reducing travel within the city, beautifying the face and urban environment are some of the most important functions of the roof garden.  Currently, the authorities of some metropolises have officially announced their support for the implementation and expansion of the roof garden.  This is especially seen in the cities of Mashhad, Qom, Tabriz, Isfahan and Kerman and a few other cities.  The municipalities have announced their readiness to support the roof gardens.  Several major projects have been implemented in each of them.  In Isfahan, these projects started a few years ago, in Qom, structures that have a roof garden are discounted in receiving a license.  In Mashhad, this issue has been taken seriously by both the authorities and the executives of the projects, and for example, in the project of the 5-star Arman Hotel of Mashhad, due to its size and technical and structural specifications, a combination of the extensive roof garden system and the centralized roof garden system has been selected.  In Tabriz and Kerman, several projects have been started in this field. passages.title: The most sad playground? The "only panda chair" day in the city, netizens warm heart explained: the universe in the eyes of children
passages.passage: ▲ Netizens found that there is a playground in Tokyo, there is only a panda spring chair.  (Photo / from Twitter / @ m0t00) Reporter Yingzhen Lin / Compilation In Tokyo, Japan, full of high-rise buildings, a playground suddenly burst into red, because the entire playground, there is only a panda spring chair, can only be played by one person, but also have to endure the constant attention of the crowd, making netizens laugh and say, "Half-tone consciousness can not play!" Although most of the netizens think that they may not be able to play, some netizens think that in a busy urban area, it is also good to have a small park to provide personal entertainment. passages.title: Pingtung County Government Purifies Wannian River and Creates Fuxing Park
passages.passage: After creating a waterfront space in Pingtung City, Pingtung County Government purifies the largest stream in the urban area, introduces streams, creates ecological pools, and creates a revitalized park with a waterfront environment. On the 26th, Pingtung City will add new leisure highlights.  Pingtung city of the county park to create a snake Creek waterfront environment combined with the pulp factory industrial site, opened in February this year, hit the national popularity, many foreign tourists came to Pingtung City, has become a well-known scenic spot.  The Pingtung County Government has created a love-living waterfront landscape, striving for a budget under the forward-looking infrastructure water environment plan, and carrying out a plan to improve the environment of Wannian Creek waterfront space. The first phase of Wannian Park was completed last year, and the second phase of the park will be opened on the 26th.  The county government has set up a rubber dam to stop water weir in Wannian Creek, which can adjust and control the water level, effectively block the backflow of poor water quality in the downstream section, and increase the oxygen content of the aeration, overflow the water source of Wannian Creek into the Fuxing Park, and create an ecological pond.  The county government has preserved the old trees and a piece of maple trees in the Fuxing Park. The river and ecological pond that attracted the rivers of thousands of years of river water are created by the space of old trees, suspension bridges, and maple trees.  Pingtung County Mayor Pan Mengan announced the opening of the 26th on Facebook, saying, "This is Pingtung right! Fuxing Park renovation", "taking care of all the details to the best, Pingtung continues to innovate and build, creating more new places in the city."  Pan Mengan said that Pingtung has taken another big step toward an ecologically sustainable livable city, and Fuxing Park has combined water environmental education to become a resilient waterfront park for the new generation.  The total area of Fuxing Park is 6.8 hectares, the water area is 1.7 hectares, and the land area is 5.1 hectares. It has boulevards and waterfront walkways, and retains the original wind and rain courts and small ice skating rinks, creating an integrated children's recreational area, with a total cost of more than NT $180 million.

Referring to the characteristics of desirable cities, Jamalinejad stated: The city should promote the quality of life and connect the basic needs of citizens, change human interactions and relationships, and be flexible with the conditions of the city ’ s atmosphere.  Deputy Minister of Urban and Rural Development of the Interior Minister said that "mayors should also have great aspirations in city management with an inclusive and comprehensive approach", adding that the mayor should have new ideas and words in all areas of economic, social, cultural, architectural and identity, and on the other hand, the citizen should be responsible.  According to the information base of the Islamic City Council of Mashhad, he added: The city is a basket of responsibilities and actions, and the cities of the future have new functions of issues. There is no escape from epidemics, and structural preparedness to deal with these crises is very important, so the management of cities should be such that they have resilience to the crisis and the ability to mobilize resources, and more importantly, they should be citizen-centric. passages.title: Construction and operation of 12 pocket parks in Gorgan
passages.passage: Yahya Sotoudeh Nia, in an interview with Mehr reporter, said: "Pocket parks or small parks are small-scale urban open spaces that large cities and cities go to them to create green space."  Creating very small or pocket parks is a solution to offset part of the lack of green spaces in urban centers, residential complexes and other areas of the city.  Stating that these parks can be a refuge against the city crowds as well as a place for rest and relaxation, Sotoudeh Nia said: In the Fajr decade two pocket parks were exploited in the neighborhoods of Resalat Three and the city of Imam (ra) eight.  He continued: Currently, three pocket parks in the neighborhoods of Buyeh 5, Hafez 2 and Resalat 10 are in the final stages of the construction and operation, and the construction of two other parks in Resalat 48 and Ozeneh are on the agenda of the organization.  Sotoudeh Nia said the work will be carried out in partnership with the Deputy of Infrastructure, Transport and Traffic Affairs, adding: Given Gorgan Municipality ’ s approach to increasing urban green space per capita and the balanced distribution of amenities throughout the city, as well as taking steps towards creating a child-friendly city, Gorgan Municipality will continue its efforts to build and operate 12 pocket parks, with the highest emphasis on creating space for children and installing playgrounds in them until the end of the year. It will take 97 steps.  He expressed hope that by providing enough land and credits, the number of parks will increase to 40 by the end of next year.

passages.title: How to design a "natural play space" in the city, so that outdoor play can become a free place for children?
passages.passage: Christine Lee: Have you ever felt that the upbringing of children, the way of caring for the elderly and children, and the behavioral interactions between people have been profoundly affected by the overall social environment and urban space planning and design?  The initiative of the Alliance for Action on Homecoming Parks has repeatedly stressed that what we should discuss is not the success or failure of different parenting or care work, because urban planning and landscape design for the overall environment lack planning and design to support parents or care workers, and indirectly or directly limit the living needs of children and young people.  The basic life needs of children and young people, let me use a simple diagram (Figure 1) to express, the society's most voiceless users - that is, children and young people - in the end what they need most, in order to be accompanied by a good system in Taiwan's urban environment, and grow up well: A good companion system. Small "pocket parks" in high-density urban settings have numerous benefits for fostering more sustainable and resilient cities.

Pocket parks can provide a refuge against city crowds and a place for rest and relaxation [ee368122-879d-43ed-98ca-293ce65ddf38].
They can also serve as a small-scale urban open space that creates green space in large cities and cities [ee368122-879d-43ed-98ca-293ce65ddf38].
The creation of very small or pocket parks is a solution to offset part of the lack of green spaces in urban centers, residential complexes, and other areas of the city [ee368122-879d-43ed-98ca-293ce65ddf38].
In the context of Shanghai, the goal of allowing citizens to go out 500 meters to see a 3,000 square meter park green space has been basically achieved [93e05d05-4e27-428b-ad4d-dbe50339cb48].
However, some residents feel that the greening of Shanghai is not enough, and the city is still far behind other cities in terms of public green space per capita [93e05d05-4e27-428b-ad4d-dbe50339cb48].

The benefits of pocket parks include reducing heat absorption by the building complex, reducing energy consumption, increasing urban green space per capita, improving air pollution, improving the quality of management and utilization of rainwater, social effects, and creating a fun and refreshing environment [2f31b682-dd36-426c-aee5-509e5172844e].
Reducing travel within the city is also a benefit of pocket parks, as well as beautifying the face and urban environment [2f31b682-dd36-426c-aee5-509e5172844e].
In addition, pocket parks can provide a place for children to play, which is essential for their physical and mental health [19ed0e93-9c89-41e1-9312-86d1ef81346b].
Studies have shown that children who spend more time in nature have better physical and mental health, and are less likely to suffer from obesity, stress, and other health problems [19ed0e93-9c89-41e1-9312-86d1ef81346b].

The features of pocket parks include small green open spaces scattered in plaques in the city [93e05d05-4e27-428b-ad4d-dbe50339cb48].
They can be as small as tens of square meters or as large as thousands of square meters [93e05d05-4e27-428b-ad4d-dbe50339cb48].
Pocket parks can be designed to be accessible and inclusive, with features such as ramps and seating areas [93e05d05-4e27-428b-ad4d-dbe50339cb48].
They can also be designed to be visually appealing, with features such as landscaping and public art [93e05d05-4e27-428b-ad4d-dbe50339cb48].

In terms of the types of features available in pocket parks, some common examples include leisure seats, small outdoor fitness equipment, and children's play areas [93e05d05-4e27-428b-ad4d-dbe50339cb48].
Some pocket parks may also include features such as gardens, green roofs, and rain gardens [2f31b682-dd36-426c-aee5-509e5172844e].
These features can help to reduce the urban heat island effect, manage stormwater runoff, and provide habitat for local wildlife [2f31b682-dd36-426c-aee5-509e5172844e].

Overall, pocket parks are a valuable resource for high-density urban settings, providing numerous benefits for both residents and the environment [ee368122-879d-43ed-98ca-293ce65ddf38].
By incorporating green spaces, accessible design, and visually appealing features, pocket parks can help to create more sustainable and resilient cities [93e05d05-4e27-428b-ad4d-dbe50339cb48].

Pocket parks can be found in various cities around the world, including Shanghai, where the city has built 47 pocket parks last year and plans to build or upgrade 50 this year [93e05d05-4e27-428b-ad4d-dbe50339cb48].
In Gorgan, Iran, the municipality is working to create 12 pocket parks, with a focus on creating space for children and installing playgrounds [ee368122-879d-43ed-98ca-293ce65ddf38].
These pocket parks can serve as a model for other cities to follow, providing a sustainable and accessible way to create green spaces in high-density urban areas [ee368122-879d-43ed-98ca-293ce65ddf38].

In conclusion, pocket parks are a valuable resource for high-density urban settings, providing numerous benefits for both residents and the environment [ee368122-879d-43ed-98ca-293ce65ddf38].
By incorporating green spaces, accessible design, and visually appealing features, pocket parks can help to create more sustainable and resilient cities [93e05d05-4e27-428b-ad4d-dbe50339cb48].

Title: The gradual introduction of roof gardens to the metropolises of the country / What are the benefits of green roof structures?
Content: Travelers from advanced industrial cities such as Tokyo, Toronto, Berlin, London, and Singapore are frequently confronted with buildings and towers, whether residential or commercial, with green roofs.  These green spaces, although not a new phenomenon in human history, were seen in distant times even in the influential civilizations of Iran, such as Mesopotamia, but after centuries of forgetfulness, they have now come back to the aid of human life and breathing.  According to the Tadbir and Hope Information Network, the cities mentioned are all suffering from high population and density, abundant industrial environments and high traffic and congestion, and therefore breathing space for the city is low.  As a result, the area of green space of the city has been unintentionally reduced and there is not much room for its expansion.  With these conditions, the maximum use of limited spaces to help the environment and life is a priority for urban planners.  It is not surprising that the city management system in all of these cities supports the creation of green spaces on the roof of buildings.  It is called the Garden of Eden.  There are similar examples of cities in our country.  Apart from Tehran, a number of metropolises of the country are also facing high population density and lack of green space and breathing space for the city, and no permanent solution has yet been found.  In recent years, as the problem of air pollution has become more serious, efforts have been made to use the world ’ s new solutions to address it.  Perhaps this is why the roof gardens in the metropolises of the country are slowly opening up.  Although these projects have not yet been comprehensively established among the public, it is foreseeable that in the coming years, they will become not only useful but necessary projects that will require the existence of a certain number of them in metropolitan areas.  Roofing gardens are a necessity in metropolises that grow vertically to horizontally and suffer from the problem of air pollution and lack of green space and even recreational space.  Because the advantage of roof gardens is not limited to helping the environment, it encompasses a large range of technical functions of buildings and even the social sphere of cities.  Reducing heat absorption by the building complex, reducing energy consumption, increasing urban green space per capita, improving air pollution, improving the quality of management and utilization of rainwater, social effects and creating a fun and refreshing environment, reducing travel within the city, beautifying the face and urban environment are some of the most important functions of the roof garden.  Currently, the authorities of some metropolises have officially announced their support for the implementation and expansion of the roof garden.  This is especially seen in the cities of Mashhad, Qom, Tabriz, Isfahan and Kerman and a few other cities.  The municipalities have announced their readiness to support the roof gardens.  Several major projects have been implemented in each of them.  In Isfahan, these projects started a few years ago, in Qom, structures that have a roof garden are discounted in receiving a license.  In Mashhad, this issue has been taken seriously by both the authorities and the executives of the projects, and for example, in the project of the 5-star Arman Hotel of Mashhad, due to its size and technical and structural specifications, a combination of the extensive roof garden system and the centralized roof garden system has been selected.  In Tabriz and Kerman, several projects have been started in this field.  With this trend, it can be predicted that with the implementation of this project and similar projects, the roof gardens will open their place in the major cities; an event that is a necessity and hope that this issue will cause other cities of the country to gradually enter this area and even set criteria to support such structures. Pocket Park is not clearly defined Pocket Park, which originated from the proposal of the New York Parks Association in 1963, originally refers to small parks scattered in high-density urban centers and distributed in plaques.  Since the beginning of just over half a century, the United States, Britain, Japan and China and other countries have begun to have their own unique "pocket park plan".  Today's pocket parks refer to small green open spaces scattered in plaques in the city.  At present, there is no clear definition of pocket parks, and various small green spaces, small parks, street gardens, and small community sports venues in the city are common pocket parks.  Liu Yuelai, a scholar at Tongji University's School of Architecture and Urban Planning, said that there is currently no clear definition of the size of the pocket park.  In terms of area, he personally feels that it can be counted as small as tens of square meters and as large as thousands of square meters.  Unlike the comprehensive park, it offers simple and short breaks, such as a walk after a meal, a small sitting or children's play.  The city's greening department said that at present, their definition of the street garden from the area generally refers to the area of 300-3000 square meters of green space. Among the 79 colorful community projects recently released in Pudong, nearly 40 projects are defined as pocket parks. Title: The gradual introduction of roof gardens to the metropolises of the country / What are the benefits of green roof structures?
Content: Travelers from advanced industrial cities such as Tokyo, Toronto, Berlin, London, and Singapore are frequently confronted with buildings and towers, whether residential or commercial, with green roofs.  These green spaces, although not a new phenomenon in human history, were seen in distant times even in the influential civilizations of Iran, such as Mesopotamia, but after centuries of forgetfulness, they have now come back to the aid of human life and breathing.  According to the Tadbir and Hope Information Network, the cities mentioned are all suffering from high population and density, abundant industrial environments and high traffic and congestion, and therefore breathing space for the city is low.  As a result, the area of green space of the city has been unintentionally reduced and there is not much room for its expansion.  With these conditions, the maximum use of limited spaces to help the environment and life is a priority for urban planners.  It is not surprising that the city management system in all of these cities supports the creation of green spaces on the roof of buildings.  It is called the Garden of Eden.  There are similar examples of cities in our country.  Apart from Tehran, a number of metropolises of the country are also facing high population density and lack of green space and breathing space for the city, and no permanent solution has yet been found.  In recent years, as the problem of air pollution has become more serious, efforts have been made to use the world ’ s new solutions to address it.  Perhaps this is why the roof gardens in the metropolises of the country are slowly opening up.  Although these projects have not yet been comprehensively established among the public, it is foreseeable that in the coming years, they will become not only useful but necessary projects that will require the existence of a certain number of them in metropolitan areas.  Roofing gardens are a necessity in metropolises that grow vertically to horizontally and suffer from the problem of air pollution and lack of green space and even recreational space.  Because the advantage of roof gardens is not limited to helping the environment, it encompasses a large range of technical functions of buildings and even the social sphere of cities.  Reducing heat absorption by the building complex, reducing energy consumption, increasing urban green space per capita, improving air pollution, improving the quality of management and utilization of rainwater, social effects and creating a fun and refreshing environment, reducing travel within the city, beautifying the face and urban environment are some of the most important functions of the roof garden.  Currently, the authorities of some metropolises have officially announced their support for the implementation and expansion of the roof garden.  This is especially seen in the cities of Mashhad, Qom, Tabriz, Isfahan and Kerman and a few other cities.  The municipalities have announced their readiness to support the roof gardens.  Several major projects have been implemented in each of them.  In Isfahan, these projects started a few years ago, in Qom, structures that have a roof garden are discounted in receiving a license.  In Mashhad, this issue has been taken seriously by both the authorities and the executives of the projects, and for example, in the project of the 5-star Arman Hotel of Mashhad, due to its size and technical and structural specifications, a combination of the extensive roof garden system and the centralized roof garden system has been selected.  In Tabriz and Kerman, several projects have been started in this field. Title: Construction and operation of 12 pocket parks in Gorgan
Content: Yahya Sotoudeh Nia, in an interview with Mehr reporter, said: "Pocket parks or small parks are small-scale urban open spaces that large cities and cities go to them to create green space."  Creating very small or pocket parks is a solution to offset part of the lack of green spaces in urban centers, residential complexes and other areas of the city.  Stating that these parks can be a refuge against the city crowds as well as a place for rest and relaxation, Sotoudeh Nia said: In the Fajr decade two pocket parks were exploited in the neighborhoods of Resalat Three and the city of Imam (ra) eight.  He continued: Currently, three pocket parks in the neighborhoods of Buyeh 5, Hafez 2 and Resalat 10 are in the final stages of the construction and operation, and the construction of two other parks in Resalat 48 and Ozeneh are on the agenda of the organization.  Sotoudeh Nia said the work will be carried out in partnership with the Deputy of Infrastructure, Transport and Traffic Affairs, adding: Given Gorgan Municipality ’ s approach to increasing urban green space per capita and the balanced distribution of amenities throughout the city, as well as taking steps towards creating a child-friendly city, Gorgan Municipality will continue its efforts to build and operate 12 pocket parks, with the highest emphasis on creating space for children and installing playgrounds in them until the end of the year. It will take 97 steps.  He expressed hope that by providing enough land and credits, the number of parks will increase to 40 by the end of next year.

passages.title: Find out the public face of the theatre from the strategies of the German and English theatres
passages.passage: In the second half of 2019, when the epidemic has not yet occurred, I received funding from the Overseas Art Tour Program of the National Arts Association and went to Europe and the United Kingdom to study theater management and theater ecology.  Towards the end of my journey, I met German director Christopher Rüping in Zurich, who had just left Munich ’ s Münchner Kammerspiele and was preparing to join a new team at Schauspielhaus Zürich. Dog, while answering all the questions I threw around the "theater."  "So, what is the 'Representation' of Taiwan's National Theatre?" Rubin suddenly threw back a question.  I'm stuck.  At the same time as thinking about how to translate the word into Chinese to understand the interpretation, the content shared by the theater and the interviewees who visited in the past two months rushed to their heads unprepared and blocked the mouth that was ready to give the answer … German Theater: A place for people to think and discuss Taiwan ’ s theater creators and audiences are usually impressed by the German-speaking theater (Germany, Austria, Switzerland). Its radical form of expression and subject matter, or the audacious and expensive jaw-dropping stage aesthetics.  On the surface, this enviable creative condition seems to be due to the fact that about 80% of the budget of the German-speaking theater comes from government support, so that creators and the theater can focus on the core of the art rather than box-office pressure; however, in the final analysis, how the German-speaking countries view the existence of the “theater ” in society is the key.  Theatres, in the tradition of German-speaking countries, are regarded as public institutions similar to schools and hospitals; schools teach people's knowledge, hospitals treat people's ailments, and theatres provide a place for people to think and discuss.  Compared with entertainment or economic benefits, the German-language theater, which inherits the spirit of the Enlightenment era to the present day, emphasizes the social function of drama, such as reflecting political reality, criticizing social phenomena, and provoking audience reflection.  In Germany alone, there are more than 180 "public theatres", and the "Stadttheater", which constitutes the most important aspect of contemporary German-speaking theater, runs their own aesthetic routes from the list of co-artists, season presentations, theater positioning, ensemble composition, educational activity design, etc., to compete with each other and operate their own aesthetic routes. The relationship between the audience ’ s region / city / country and them.  Such a blossoming scene of the theater is unimaginable to Taiwanese audiences who have just witnessed the end of the stage of the “Two Houses ” of the Performing Arts Circle.  Shermin Langhoff, who has taken over the Maxim Gorki Theater in Berlin since 2014, is not only the first Turkish female director in the history of German public theater, she and Jens Hillje, the co-artistic director with a background in theater consulting, have positioned the theater as a “Postmigrantisches Theater. ”  Here, all the performances and related activities are closely related to immigration, identity, ethnicity, community, and urban issues. Langhoff has changed the traditional white-owned theater orthodoxy, opened up more diverse ethnic background creators to the theater, even established the “Exile Ensemble ”, and provided English subtitles for every performance in the theater to respond to the needs of the international city of Berlin.  In addition to performances, the “Gorki Forum ” is a regular thematic talk and discussion, planned by the theater ’ s permanent drama production department, inviting experts, sociologists or politicians from various fields to discuss specific issues with the audience, rather than serving as a marketing event for the production of a single performance.  The Zurich Theatre in Switzerland is an interesting example of how German-speaking theatre is facing an ageing audience, liquidating artistic boundaries, acting as a public creative centre and responding immediately to contemporary society. In 2019, two new artistic directors – director Nicolas Stemann and theatre consultant Benjamin von Blomberg – invited eight people, including visual arts and theatre. Contemporary dance background, nationality and cultural background of young creators served as in-house directors (In-house Directors), defining the theater as a place of artistic origin rather than a theater space, re-discussing the relationship between theater and the young generation.  In addition to creating, the directors were given other “tasks ”: Alexander Giesche, who is a visual artist, reinvents the halls of the old theater; Suna Gürler, who is also the director of the theater ’ s education department, plans drama classes and activities for young people; and in the first half of 2020, the theater was forced to suspend live performances and director Rubinsky was quoted as saying. The film" Ten Commandments "is adapted into a nine-episode live online show in response to the human condition under the epidemic.  Whether it is the Galician Theatre ’ s explicit self-positioning in the artistic and operational aspects, or the artists within the Zurich Theatre ’ s system not only respond to society in their works, but must also face the public responsibility within the structure, they all reflect the social function of theater in the German-speaking region.  But (from the creator ’ s point of view) is the utopian German-speaking theater too idealistic for Taiwan, which lacks a deep social context?
