passages.title: New TV Shows Scenes Between Turkey and Saudi Arabia
passages.passage: Turkish TV series, which has been broadcast as the country ’ s soft power in recent years, especially on the television of Arab countries, in addition to laying the groundwork for attracting tourists from these countries, is one of the important tools in advancing the cultural goals of the Ankara government.  Relations between Turkey and Saudi Arabia have deteriorated to the point that even Saudi Arabia ’ s MBC TV group, which broadcasts Turkish series in Saudi Arabia, stopped broadcasting them last year.  In its next step, MBC will be showcasing a series called Kingdoms of Fire from November 17.  The series depicts the end of the Mamlukan country, which was created by the Ottoman Empire from the early 16th century, and in this series, the Ottoman Empire is referred to as a bloodthirsty state.  Although the series has not yet been broadcast, the news of its broadcast in the Turkish media has been evaluated as Saudi Arabia ’ s hostility to Turkey.  The website of the Turkish state broadcaster "TTV".  RT News "In a news with the headline" Saudi Arabia, which has released Turkish TV series, broadcasts a series in which the Ottoman government has been badly introduced ", wrote: The MBC network, which is based in the United Arab Emirates and is founded by a Saudi capitalist, in a series on the overthrow of the Mamluk government, introduces the Ottoman government as an occupying force.  The website of the Turkish state broadcaster "TTV".  RT News "In a news with the headline" Saudi Arabia that has released Turkish TV series, a series in which the Ottoman government is badly presented, "wrote: The MBC network, which is based in the United Arab Emirates and founded by a Saudi capitalist, in a series on the overthrow of the Mamluki government, introduces the Ottoman government as an occupying force.  The series describes the Ottoman Empire as an empire that rules on the basis of human blood.  The base emphasized that MBC ’ s hostility to the Ottoman Empire is not unique to this issue, adding that the series ’ producer Yasser Harb called the occupation of the series in broadcasting scenes from the Ottoman Empire.  MBC was founded in 1991 by Saudi financier Wald bin Ibrahim Al Ibrahim in the United Kingdom; the center of the company was later transferred to the United Arab Emirates and the company began broadcasting television programs in Arabic.  The channel is broadcast in many countries in the Middle East and North Africa, and is said to be broadcast in 24 countries with 18 different channels.  Earlier this year, Saudi Arabia changed its textbooks taught in elementary and high schools, and new books refer to the Ottoman state as an occupying power.  In Saudi textbooks, it is said that the Ottoman government oppressed the Arab people.

passages.title: Home show, competitor or second branch of Turkish networks?
passages.passage: According to the Cinema Zone, the cultural group of the Young Journalists Club, with the increasing influence of satellite networks among Iranian families, one of the most significant damage that was mentioned for these networks was the cultural impact of the works broadcast by these networks, especially the Turkish series dubbed.  The series, based on the family as the central subject, provided sexist, pornographic, aristocratic and corrupt narratives of Turkish families, which due to the visual and sexual attractions, these series were able to tell stories of love triangles, betrayal, class divisions, anti-family, mere pleasure and corruption in the context of melodrama to many audiences with their own.  The increase in the activity of satellite networks and the distribution of Turkish works in Iranian satellite networks coincided with the increase of activities in Iran ’ s home theater network; at that time, some cultural analysts considered the home theater network as a reasonable response to satellite networks and an opportunity to overcome their works, a network that had less audits on its works and could attract the audience of Turkish TV series.  But that ’ s where the mistake started.  Many of the programmers and artists who were born and raised by the IRIB moved from television to the home theater network in order to gain more profit and freedom.  This, more than ever, left the hands of the cultural authorities of the IRIB empty to produce attractive and popular works and caused the TV audience to collapse.  On the other hand, less monitoring of the home screen network caused the creators active in this network, instead of presenting a new form and production of a cultural product, to resort to repetitive and sexual formulas of Turkish series and, with a glance from the rival, produced works that even in some cases, had lower quality and content than their Turkish rivals, and even caused some Iranian families to protest against some of these works.  Works that were only economical and did not spare any effort to sell more, from unnecessarily stretching the story, music-based video clips and creating triangular and square love nodes to the inclusion of erotic sequences.  Content works that, as a cultural commodity, had a countercultural function and only filled the pockets of its creators.  This is something that even the creators of these works are aware of.  From Manouchehr Hadi, the director of the love and romance series, who himself has confessed to modeling the Turkish series, to the writer of the series Dell, who says that the reason for the increase in the series' episodes is more money.  Now, some time after increasing the activity of VOD and attracting the audience through free subscription services and attractive plans to sell the works of the home theater network at a lower price than physical broadcasters and strengthening their position among the families as a multimedia and video broadcaster, in their latest action, they have dubbed and broadcast exclusive Turkish series.  The home theater network and VOD, which were supposed to rival Turkish satellite and TV channels, have now become their second branch.  Their cultural and content performance shows that the lack of proper supervision of the production of cultural works and the transfer of the field to individuals who are concerned only with financial interests, not cultural ones, provides the way for cultural influence and the destruction of the cultural foundations of the country and Iranian families.  Now that we are living in the era of the soft cultural war, the abandonment and lack of supervision in the field of cultural production can cause irreparable damage to our country; therefore, it is recommended that we not leave the field of culture to the enemy, by increasing the controls on the production of cultural works in the home theater network, and by producing great cultural works, such as Mokhtarnameh, the lost innocence, Hazrat Yusuf, English Kiev, Imam Ali, zero degree Hats off and...  We ourselves become the issuer of TV series, not the importer of Turkish serials, which can leave Iranian families with many cultural problems.  Author: The End of the Message

passages.title: The first round of turkeys didn ’ t stop.
passages.passage: While the coronavirus outbreak stopped imaging Turkish series, some of these series continued to work in a new way.  According to ISNA, the Al Jazeera website has reported on how to continue shooting Turkish series that broadcast with a short distance.  The report said that some production groups of Turkish series used a new method to continue shooting their series.  In this way, some parts were filmed in the home of the actors and with the camera of their mobile phones, and without violating the rules of the home quarantine, the desired parts were prepared for broadcast.  The series “Eighties ” and“ Let ’ s Go ” continue to air, reaching audiences both inside and outside Turkey.  In the new episodes, these series also deal with the coronavirus.  In the final episode of the series "Forbidden Apple", before its broadcast temporarily stops, one of the actors of the series, while sitting in a taxi, has used a disinfectant and is worried about the coronavirus.  This is the first scene of the Turkish series that deals with the issue of Corona.  In an episode of the “Miracle Doctor ” series, there is mention of a dangerous virus that has entered Turkey through an East Asian traveler, but the name of the coronavirus is not mentioned.  Turkish actors these days have shared pictures of themselves on social media and in various places have been wearing masks and gloves to warn against the spread of the coronavirus.  The comedy series "Tranquility Neighborhood" has dedicated parts to the coronavirus and the importance of prevention in order to reduce the spread of the virus and how to spend free time during the quarantine.  The series, which explores various social issues with humor, now continues through shooting on mobile phones and in the actors ’ own homes.  Gülce Biersel, author of the series, said: “Shooting on mobile phones and in the actors ’ homes was a new exercise that taught us a lot, but some of the things that are necessary for a comedy show, such as walking, running, and certain body movements, can ’ t be done.  It had to be filmed in a consistent manner.  He added that turning each actor ’ s home into a suitable location for filming was difficult.  We asked them to send us a picture of their house.  The show has 11 actors, all of whom it was difficult to coordinate, but with the effort of the actors, we overcame the technical hurdles and got the job done.  Turkish actor Genghis Buzghorud said on Twitter: “The idea of having mobile phones in our homes was Jali ’ s idea.  I welcomed it as an initiative and set up a tent in my backyard for photography.  Mohammad Oymak, president of the Association for Culture and Literature, also welcomed the idea and expressed hope that the scenes filmed in the actors ’ homes would convey happiness and hope to the viewers.  In particular, this idea has been realized through extensive efforts and cooperation between actors and their technical staff and their Internet communication.  End of message.

passages.title: Turkey's hot markets in South America
passages.passage: Turkish television series now reached South America after capturing the film market of the Indian subcontinent, the Middle East, the Caucasus, Central Asia and the Balkans.  In South America, Chile, Argentina and Mexico are among the biggest customers of Turkish TV series.  The popularity of Turkish series in the Middle East or the Caucasus may be due to cultural and historical commonalities, but what could be the reason for the booming Turkish series market on the other side of the Atlantic in South America?  Tuggs Shaw, a German broadcaster, has been trying to answer this question in a report on the popularity of Turkish shows in South America.  Yamaj Okur, producer of the Çukur story series, which has been translated into Persian as “Gut ”, says that a 140-minute episode will be produced every week, which will be broadcast on Turkish television five days later.  The Trench series is currently one of Turkey ’ s most successful series.  It tells the story of a family who controls one of Istanbul ’ s most dangerous neighborhoods, the Pit.  The neighborhood has long been in the hands of small families, whose most important rule is to be strict about the distribution of drugs in the neighborhood.  If someone spreads drugs, they have to leave the neighborhood.  The first episode of the series premiered on October 23, 2017 on TV and is still ongoing.  Correspondents from Istanbul and Rio de Janeiro say the demand for Turkish TV shows has increased.  Diazis, or series, forms a separate genre on Turkish television that is more comparable to the well-known South American telenovelas.  Araya Kisternas, a Chilean couple who have been married for almost 50 years, has just discovered their love for Turkish TV shows.  They say they show love with respect in this series.  The looks are romantic and traditional families are portrayed as important and valuable.  The Chilean couple have a herd that "in modern South American nostalgia traps shows a lot of bare limbs, men kiss men, and violence is part of the film."  Juan Vicente, director of the Chilean TV channel Mega, brought the first Turkish series to South America seven years ago.  He recalls that when the show “Binbir gece ” was broadcast on the mega network, he enthralled people and saved the mega network from bankruptcy at the time.  Juwan goes on to say that since many South Americans are conservative and dream of an ideal world, Turkish TV shows are in their best interest.  Family structures in Turkey are comparable to those in South America.  The patriarchal structures with a strong grandfather or father who determines and leads everything in the family are similar to the Chilean family structure.  The traditional family structure is also popular in Turkey, thanks to Erdoğan ’ s conservative and Islamist government.  Thousands took to the streets in recent days to protest Turkey ’ s withdrawal from the Convention against Violence against Women, but the protests have not been successful so far.  Yamaj Okor, producer of The Pit, says sex, swearing, alcohol in movies and TV shows are as taboo as they were in the '90s.  Okor added, “We have to tell our stories more gently, otherwise the TV won ’ t play it. ”  The series as Turkey ’ s “soft power ” is different from most Turkish series that depict the glamorous life of the middle and upper classes.  In this series, usually luxury cars, expensive clothes are displayed.  But the hole has a different atmosphere.  The series is filmed in the Balat district of Istanbul.  In the Balat district of Istanbul, which used to be home to Jewish, Armenian and Greek communities, it is now a simple working-class area, but thanks to the series, the neighborhood has now flourished and many cafes have opened in its corners over the past few years.  Tagus Shaw reports that at any given time during filming, about 200 fans of the Pit series gather at the scene.  On the other hand, vendors are trying to sell their goods, and in the future, visitors to South America are likely to be seen in the narrow alleys of Balat.  The series was recently sold to Chile.  The Chilean couple who are fascinated by the film are also planning a trip to Turkey.  Hector said: “A trip to Turkey would be a dream for us. ”  His wife, Patricia, interrupts him: “In the past, we never had any idea of Turkey.  We knew a Turkey full of violence with terrorist attacks.  But now it seems to be getting better. ”  Turkey ’ s $1 billion in revenue has become the world ’ s second-largest TV series exporter after Hollywood.  Recent research by Turkish state television shows that Turkish dramas are a “soft power, ” often trying to convey a specific image in the form of a romantic historical drama from the Ottoman period, which is usually reflected in the politics of the current Turkish government.  Follow Deutsche Welle on Instagram: “We are exporting Turkish culture, language and products.  Many of them just became popular abroad through our series.  Take, for example, Turkish music, which is now popular in South America. ”  According to estimates by the Turkish film industry, the revenue of the series could reach $1 billion by 2023.  At the end of his report on the Turkish series, Tagus Shaw has written that the next goal of the Turkish series is to capture the film market in Spain and Italy.

Title: Find out the public face of the theatre from the strategies of the German and English theatres
Content: In the second half of 2019, when the epidemic has not yet occurred, I received funding from the Overseas Art Tour Program of the National Arts Association and went to Europe and the United Kingdom to study theater management and theater ecology.  Towards the end of my journey, I met German director Christopher Rüping in Zurich, who had just left Munich ’ s Münchner Kammerspiele and was preparing to join a new team at Schauspielhaus Zürich. Dog, while answering all the questions I threw around the "theater."  "So, what is the 'Representation' of Taiwan's National Theatre?" Rubin suddenly threw back a question.  I'm stuck.  At the same time as thinking about how to translate the word into Chinese to understand the interpretation, the content shared by the theater and the interviewees who visited in the past two months rushed to their heads unprepared and blocked the mouth that was ready to give the answer … German Theater: A place for people to think and discuss Taiwan ’ s theater creators and audiences are usually impressed by the German-speaking theater (Germany, Austria, Switzerland). Its radical form of expression and subject matter, or the audacious and expensive jaw-dropping stage aesthetics.  On the surface, this enviable creative condition seems to be due to the fact that about 80% of the budget of the German-speaking theater comes from government support, so that creators and the theater can focus on the core of the art rather than box-office pressure; however, in the final analysis, how the German-speaking countries view the existence of the “theater ” in society is the key.  Theatres, in the tradition of German-speaking countries, are regarded as public institutions similar to schools and hospitals; schools teach people's knowledge, hospitals treat people's ailments, and theatres provide a place for people to think and discuss.  Compared with entertainment or economic benefits, the German-language theater, which inherits the spirit of the Enlightenment era to the present day, emphasizes the social function of drama, such as reflecting political reality, criticizing social phenomena, and provoking audience reflection.  In Germany alone, there are more than 180 "public theatres", and the "Stadttheater", which constitutes the most important aspect of contemporary German-speaking theater, runs their own aesthetic routes from the list of co-artists, season presentations, theater positioning, ensemble composition, educational activity design, etc., to compete with each other and operate their own aesthetic routes. The relationship between the audience ’ s region / city / country and them.  Such a blossoming scene of the theater is unimaginable to Taiwanese audiences who have just witnessed the end of the stage of the “Two Houses ” of the Performing Arts Circle.  Shermin Langhoff, who has taken over the Maxim Gorki Theater in Berlin since 2014, is not only the first Turkish female director in the history of German public theater, she and Jens Hillje, the co-artistic director with a background in theater consulting, have positioned the theater as a “Postmigrantisches Theater. ”  Here, all the performances and related activities are closely related to immigration, identity, ethnicity, community, and urban issues. Langhoff has changed the traditional white-owned theater orthodoxy, opened up more diverse ethnic background creators to the theater, even established the “Exile Ensemble ”, and provided English subtitles for every performance in the theater to respond to the needs of the international city of Berlin.  In addition to performances, the “Gorki Forum ” is a regular thematic talk and discussion, planned by the theater ’ s permanent drama production department, inviting experts, sociologists or politicians from various fields to discuss specific issues with the audience, rather than serving as a marketing event for the production of a single performance.  The Zurich Theatre in Switzerland is an interesting example of how German-speaking theatre is facing an ageing audience, liquidating artistic boundaries, acting as a public creative centre and responding immediately to contemporary society. In 2019, two new artistic directors – director Nicolas Stemann and theatre consultant Benjamin von Blomberg – invited eight people, including visual arts and theatre. Contemporary dance background, nationality and cultural background of young creators served as in-house directors (In-house Directors), defining the theater as a place of artistic origin rather than a theater space, re-discussing the relationship between theater and the young generation.  In addition to creating, the directors were given other “tasks ”: Alexander Giesche, who is a visual artist, reinvents the halls of the old theater; Suna Gürler, who is also the director of the theater ’ s education department, plans drama classes and activities for young people; and in the first half of 2020, the theater was forced to suspend live performances and director Rubinsky was quoted as saying. The film" Ten Commandments "is adapted into a nine-episode live online show in response to the human condition under the epidemic.  Whether it is the Galician Theatre ’ s explicit self-positioning in the artistic and operational aspects, or the artists within the Zurich Theatre ’ s system not only respond to society in their works, but must also face the public responsibility within the structure, they all reflect the social function of theater in the German-speaking region.  But (from the creator ’ s point of view) is the utopian German-speaking theater too idealistic for Taiwan, which lacks a deep social context?

Title: Find out the public face of the theatre from the strategies of the German and English theatres
Content: In the second half of 2019, when the epidemic has not yet occurred, I received funding from the Overseas Art Tour Program of the National Arts Association and went to Europe and the United Kingdom to study theater management and theater ecology.  Towards the end of my journey, I met German director Christopher Rüping in Zurich, who had just left Munich ’ s Münchner Kammerspiele and was preparing to join a new team at Schauspielhaus Zürich. Dog, while answering all the questions I threw around the "theater."  "So, what is the 'Representation' of Taiwan's National Theatre?" Rubin suddenly threw back a question.  I'm stuck.  At the same time as thinking about how to translate the word into Chinese to understand the interpretation, the content shared by the theater and the interviewees who visited in the past two months rushed to their heads unprepared and blocked the mouth that was ready to give the answer … German Theater: A place for people to think and discuss Taiwan ’ s theater creators and audiences are usually impressed by the German-speaking theater (Germany, Austria, Switzerland). Its radical form of expression and subject matter, or the audacious and expensive jaw-dropping stage aesthetics.  On the surface, this enviable creative condition seems to be due to the fact that about 80% of the budget of the German-speaking theater comes from government support, so that creators and the theater can focus on the core of the art rather than box-office pressure; however, in the final analysis, how the German-speaking countries view the existence of the “theater ” in society is the key.  Theatres, in the tradition of German-speaking countries, are regarded as public institutions similar to schools and hospitals; schools teach people's knowledge, hospitals treat people's ailments, and theatres provide a place for people to think and discuss.  Compared with entertainment or economic benefits, the German-language theater, which inherits the spirit of the Enlightenment era to the present day, emphasizes the social function of drama, such as reflecting political reality, criticizing social phenomena, and provoking audience reflection.  In Germany alone, there are more than 180 "public theatres", and the "Stadttheater", which constitutes the most important aspect of contemporary German-speaking theater, runs their own aesthetic routes from the list of co-artists, season presentations, theater positioning, ensemble composition, educational activity design, etc., to compete with each other and operate their own aesthetic routes. The relationship between the audience ’ s region / city / country and them.  Such a blossoming scene of the theater is unimaginable to Taiwanese audiences who have just witnessed the end of the stage of the “Two Houses ” of the Performing Arts Circle.  Shermin Langhoff, who has taken over the Maxim Gorki Theater in Berlin since 2014, is not only the first Turkish female director in the history of German public theater, she and Jens Hillje, the co-artistic director with a background in theater consulting, have positioned the theater as a “Postmigrantisches Theater. ”  Here, all the performances and related activities are closely related to immigration, identity, ethnicity, community, and urban issues. Langhoff has changed the traditional white-owned theater orthodoxy, opened up more diverse ethnic background creators to the theater, even established the “Exile Ensemble ”, and provided English subtitles for every performance in the theater to respond to the needs of the international city of Berlin.  In addition to performances, the “Gorki Forum ” is a regular thematic talk and discussion, planned by the theater ’ s permanent drama production department, inviting experts, sociologists or politicians from various fields to discuss specific issues with the audience, rather than serving as a marketing event for the production of a single performance.  The Zurich Theatre in Switzerland is an interesting example of how German-speaking theatre is facing an ageing audience, liquidating artistic boundaries, acting as a public creative centre and responding immediately to contemporary society. In 2019, two new artistic directors – director Nicolas Stemann and theatre consultant Benjamin von Blomberg – invited eight people, including visual arts and theatre. Contemporary dance background, nationality and cultural background of young creators served as in-house directors (In-house Directors), defining the theater as a place of artistic origin rather than a theater space, re-discussing the relationship between theater and the young generation.  In addition to creating, the directors were given other “tasks ”: Alexander Giesche, who is a visual artist, reinvents the halls of the old theater; Suna Gürler, who is also the director of the theater ’ s education department, plans drama classes and activities for young people; and in the first half of 2020, the theater was forced to suspend live performances and director Rubinsky was quoted as saying. The film" Ten Commandments "is adapted into a nine-episode live online show in response to the human condition under the epidemic.  Whether it is the Galician Theatre ’ s explicit self-positioning in the artistic and operational aspects, or the artists within the Zurich Theatre ’ s system not only respond to society in their works, but must also face the public responsibility within the structure, they all reflect the social function of theater in the German-speaking region.  But (from the creator ’ s point of view) is the utopian German-speaking theater too idealistic for Taiwan, which lacks a deep social context?

Title: New TV Shows Scenes Between Turkey and Saudi Arabia
Content: Turkish TV series, which has been broadcast as the country ’ s soft power in recent years, especially on the television of Arab countries, in addition to laying the groundwork for attracting tourists from these countries, is one of the important tools in advancing the cultural goals of the Ankara government.  Relations between Turkey and Saudi Arabia have deteriorated to the point that even Saudi Arabia ’ s MBC TV group, which broadcasts Turkish series in Saudi Arabia, stopped broadcasting them last year. Title: The first round of turkeys didn ’ t stop.
Content: While the coronavirus outbreak stopped imaging Turkish series, some of these series continued to work in a new way.  According to ISNA, the Al Jazeera website has reported on how to continue shooting Turkish series that broadcast with a short distance.  The report said that some production groups of Turkish series used a new method to continue shooting their series.  In this way, some parts were filmed in the home of the actors and with the camera of their mobile phones, and without violating the rules of the home quarantine, the desired parts were prepared for broadcast.  The series “Eighties ” and“ Let ’ s Go ” continue to air, reaching audiences both inside and outside Turkey.  In the new episodes, these series also deal with the coronavirus.  In the final episode of the series "Forbidden Apple", before its broadcast temporarily stops, one of the actors of the series, while sitting in a taxi, has used a disinfectant and is worried about the coronavirus.  This is the first scene of the Turkish series that deals with the issue of Corona.  In an episode of the “Miracle Doctor ” series, there is mention of a dangerous virus that has entered Turkey through an East Asian traveler, but the name of the coronavirus is not mentioned.  Turkish actors these days have shared pictures of themselves on social media and in various places have been wearing masks and gloves to warn against the spread of the coronavirus.  The comedy series "Tranquility Neighborhood" has dedicated parts to the coronavirus and the importance of prevention in order to reduce the spread of the virus and how to spend free time during the quarantine.  The series, which explores various social issues with humor, now continues through shooting on mobile phones and in the actors ’ own homes.  Gülce Biersel, author of the series, said: “Shooting on mobile phones and in the actors ’ homes was a new exercise that taught us a lot, but some of the things that are necessary for a comedy show, such as walking, running, and certain body movements, can ’ t be done.  It had to be filmed in a consistent manner.  He added that turning each actor ’ s home into a suitable location for filming was difficult.  We asked them to send us a picture of their house.  The show has 11 actors, all of whom it was difficult to coordinate, but with the effort of the actors, we overcame the technical hurdles and got the job done.  Turkish actor Genghis Buzghorud said on Twitter: “The idea of having mobile phones in our homes was Jali ’ s idea.  I welcomed it as an initiative and set up a tent in my backyard for photography.  Mohammad Oymak, president of the Association for Culture and Literature, also welcomed the idea and expressed hope that the scenes filmed in the actors ’ homes would convey happiness and hope to the viewers.  In particular, this idea has been realized through extensive efforts and cooperation between actors and their technical staff and their Internet communication.  End of message.

Title: Turkey's hot markets in South America
Content: Turkish television series now reached South America after capturing the film market of the Indian subcontinent, the Middle East, the Caucasus, Central Asia and the Balkans.  In South America, Chile, Argentina and Mexico are among the biggest customers of Turkish TV series.  The popularity of Turkish series in the Middle East or the Caucasus may be due to cultural and historical commonalities, but what could be the reason for the booming Turkish series market on the other side of the Atlantic in South America?  Tuggs Shaw, a German broadcaster, has been trying to answer this question in a report on the popularity of Turkish shows in South America.  Yamaj Okur, producer of the Çukur story series, which has been translated into Persian as “Gut ”, says that a 140-minute episode will be produced every week, which will be broadcast on Turkish television five days later.  The Trench series is currently one of Turkey ’ s most successful series.  It tells the story of a family who controls one of Istanbul ’ s most dangerous neighborhoods, the Pit.  The neighborhood has long been in the hands of small families, whose most important rule is to be strict about the distribution of drugs in the neighborhood.  If someone spreads drugs, they have to leave the neighborhood.  The first episode of the series premiered on October 23, 2017 on TV and is still ongoing.  Correspondents from Istanbul and Rio de Janeiro say the demand for Turkish TV shows has increased.  Diazis, or series, forms a separate genre on Turkish television that is more comparable to the well-known South American telenovelas.  Araya Kisternas, a Chilean couple who have been married for almost 50 years, has just discovered their love for Turkish TV shows.  They say they show love with respect in this series.  The looks are romantic and traditional families are portrayed as important and valuable.  The Chilean couple have a herd that "in modern South American nostalgia traps shows a lot of bare limbs, men kiss men, and violence is part of the film."  Juan Vicente, director of the Chilean TV channel Mega, brought the first Turkish series to South America seven years ago.  He recalls that when the show “Binbir gece ” was broadcast on the mega network, he enthralled people and saved the mega network from bankruptcy at the time.  Juwan goes on to say that since many South Americans are conservative and dream of an ideal world, Turkish TV shows are in their best interest.  Family structures in Turkey are comparable to those in South America.  The patriarchal structures with a strong grandfather or father who determines and leads everything in the family are similar to the Chilean family structure.  The traditional family structure is also popular in Turkey, thanks to Erdoğan ’ s conservative and Islamist government.  Thousands took to the streets in recent days to protest Turkey ’ s withdrawal from the Convention against Violence against Women, but the protests have not been successful so far.  Yamaj Okor, producer of The Pit, says sex, swearing, alcohol in movies and TV shows are as taboo as they were in the '90s.  Okor added, “We have to tell our stories more gently, otherwise the TV won ’ t play it. ”  The series as Turkey ’ s “soft power ” is different from most Turkish series that depict the glamorous life of the middle and upper classes.  In this series, usually luxury cars, expensive clothes are displayed.  But the hole has a different atmosphere.  The series is filmed in the Balat district of Istanbul.  In the Balat district of Istanbul, which used to be home to Jewish, Armenian and Greek communities, it is now a simple working-class area, but thanks to the series, the neighborhood has now flourished and many cafes have opened in its corners over the past few years.  Tagus Shaw reports that at any given time during filming, about 200 fans of the Pit series gather at the scene.  On the other hand, vendors are trying to sell their goods, and in the future, visitors to South America are likely to be seen in the narrow alleys of Balat.  The series was recently sold to Chile.  The Chilean couple who are fascinated by the film are also planning a trip to Turkey.  Hector said: “A trip to Turkey would be a dream for us. ”  His wife, Patricia, interrupts him: “In the past, we never had any idea of Turkey.  We knew a Turkey full of violence with terrorist attacks.  But now it seems to be getting better. ”  Turkey ’ s $1 billion in revenue has become the world ’ s second-largest TV series exporter after Hollywood.  Recent research by Turkish state television shows that Turkish dramas are a “soft power, ” often trying to convey a specific image in the form of a romantic historical drama from the Ottoman period, which is usually reflected in the politics of the current Turkish government.  Follow Deutsche Welle on Instagram: “We are exporting Turkish culture, language and products.  Many of them just became popular abroad through our series.  Take, for example, Turkish music, which is now popular in South America. ”  According to estimates by the Turkish film industry, the revenue of the series could reach $1 billion by 2023.  At the end of his report on the Turkish series, Tagus Shaw has written that the next goal of the Turkish series is to capture the film market in Spain and Italy.

passages.title: A million people will live on Mars!
passages.passage: Currently, there are almost 50 projects of manned flights to Mars.  The most grandiose of them belongs to the American engineer and entrepreneur Elon Musk, who plans to transport a million people to the Red Planet in the coming decades to create an independent civilization.  This idea seems absolutely fantastic – and meanwhile, the company Srace X, led by Mask, announced that very soon will begin the first flights of its space shuttles.  Go to the Red Planet!  At the International Astronomical Congress held in September 2016 in Mexico, the report of the engineer and entrepreneur made a real sensation.  According to Elon Musk, only the resettlement of a significant part of earthlings to Mars will save humanity from possible extinction.  Life on our planet can be interrupted by many factors: the explosion of a nearby supernova, superflares on the Sun, falling into a black hole, a global epidemic, a collision with a huge asteroid, a man-made disaster.  A large colony of people on another planet will ensure the continued existence of terrestrial civilization.  Why choose Mars?  Compared to other celestial bodies of the solar system, it is better suited for the possible life of earthlings.  The day here lasts 24 hours 37 minutes - that is, suitable for our residents and plants.  Gravity is much smaller than the earth, but is quite suitable for the normal functioning of the human body.  Finally, there is water – albeit in the form of polar ice caps, but it can be easily reached, and pieces of ice melt and use.  The rest of the planets of the solar system are practically unsuitable for such a mission: Mercury has extremely high surface temperatures during the day and very low at night, Venus has a too aggressive atmosphere, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune are mostly composed of liquefied gas.  The closest suitable celestial body to us is the Moon, but it depends entirely on the Earth and in the event of a space disaster may die with it.  Why is the number of one million people chosen?  According to experts, this is the minimum number of people so that their colony can become completely independent and develop.  It will have specialists of all the necessary professions, it will cope with possible diseases and epidemics, as well as ensure a stable natural population growth.  At first, the colonists will face the most difficult task - to turn the Red Planet into their home.  The set of actions to achieve this goal, Maek called the term “terraforming ” – that is, changing the conditions of life on another planet in such a way that they resemble earthly ones.  First of all, you need to melt a sufficient amount of ice at the south pole of the planet, since it will turn to the Sun in the summer, which means that it will be easier to do this than at the north pole.  The water accumulated here is enough to create an ocean several meters deep on the planet.  As the ice cap decreases, a chain reaction will begin - water vapor will begin to compact the atmosphere, which, in turn, will retain more solar heat, due to which the melting process will be more intense.  Technically, it can be launched using nuclear charges or placing laser devices over the south pole of Mars.  After liquid water appears on the planet, you need to start planting plants: initially it will be mosses, but later - vast forests that will saturate the atmosphere of Mars with oxygen (now it is 95% carbon dioxide).  According to Musk, the cultivation of “green lungs ” and the creation of a livable air without spacesuits will take from 300 to 1000 years.  But after that, the Red Planet can be considered terraformed, and people will choose where they live - on Mars or on Earth.  100 thousand flights Elon Maek listed the things and equipment that the first colonists needed.  First of all, these are devices for the production and conversion of energy - nuclear or space.  The most promising direction, the researchers of the company Srace X consider the delivery to Mars of a large number of light folding solar panels.  It will also require a huge amount of plants, both to create oxygen and to supply the settlers with food.  Until the atmosphere of the planet is formed properly, earthlings will need means of protection from solar radiation - after all, until this time, Martian cities will have to be under special domes.  First, the settlers will build small houses, then they will equip complexes, where there will be not only housing, but also schools, hospitals, shops, etc.  Experts Srace X calculated: one flight with the colonists should account for nine flights with payload.  It is based on a ship capable of carrying 100 passengers.  Thus, the total number of flights required to create a million colony on the Red Planet will be about 100 thousand (10 thousand - passenger flights, 90 thousand - cargo).  Elon Maek has already announced that the first expeditions for the delivery of goods should begin at the end of 2022.  By 2035, spacecraft will be built capable of reaching the Red Planet in 80 days, and a million colonists will arrive on Mars within the next few decades.  The main obstacle to the implementation of such a large-scale project, according to Musk and his team, is the high cost of a flight to the Red Planet.  In fact, it is steadily declining.  In 1989, the US national aerospace agency YABA estimated sending astronauts to Mars at $450 billion.  It was assumed that there will be from four to six earthlings — that is, each place was estimated at about $100 billion.  But already in 2004, the same agency reduced the cost of the project nine times — to $50 billion.  Thus, the flight of one person would cost a little more than 10 billion dollars.  This figure is still too high, but the trend towards its decline is clearly visible, and therefore such a task can be solved.  Elon Maek believes that the optimal amount for a flight of one person should be 500 thousand dollars – this is the approximate cost of a middle-class house in a good place.  Moreover, people should understand that they will become real space pioneers, the first permanent residents of another planet – and therefore must pay for their flight themselves.  Opinions of economists and psychologists are unambiguous: only in the United States there are at least a million people who will agree to pay such money for an unprecedented space travel.  But how to reduce the cost of flying each person from 10 billion to 500 thousand dollars, that is, 20 thousand times?  Elon Mayek knows the answer to that question.  Rocket from a private company Team plan Srace X works in two directions.  The first of these is the creation of spacecraft, each of which will be able to carry at least 100 people.  The company Ilona Mask has a successful experience in the construction of devices of a new type.  The engineer and entrepreneur himself says that the huge cost of missiles is primarily a consequence of the lack of competition and the presence of a huge number of subcontractors.  NASA constantly entrusts the execution of its orders only to a few companies.  For example, ULA (United Launch Alliance), a joint venture owned by Boeing and Lockheed Martin, regularly performs missions of the space agency and the US Department of Defense, but at the same time receives more for each launch than anyone else in the world.  Under the pretext of national security, the system of government orders in this area is completely opaque, and the task of many companies is not to reduce the cost of the spacecraft, but to make it more expensive for their own benefit.  In turn, having received the order, large companies transfer it in parts to small subcontractors, who also inflate prices.  But the main thing is that in the absence of competition, there is no need to invent something new!  As a result, the technology of modern spacecraft at best dates back to the 1990s, and the costs of their production and launch are declining extremely slowly.  SpaceX was the first company to start working on a fundamentally different scheme.  Not fulfilling an order, but creating your own device, cheaper and more reliable, which can then be offered to space agencies and organizations.  The company was founded in 2002 with the personal funds of Elon Musk, received from the development and operation of the largest electronic payment system in the United States.  The company created its first rocket, called the Falcon 1 (translated from English “falcon ”).  The two-stage vehicle and its engine were made by Space X workers without the help of intermediaries.  The first three launches ended in accidents.  But the fourth flight, which took place in 2008, was successful.  A cargo detachment simulation was conducted (it remained in the rocket so as not to increase the amount of space debris), and the first stage made a safe landing.  At the same time, Elon Maek, who was in the Mission Control Center at Cape Canaveral, heard the clap, ran out into the street in despair - he thought that this test ended in an explosion.  But it turned out that the sound was caused by the passage of the disconnected first stage of the rocket sound barrier. passages.passage: NASA ’ s mission to search for signs of life on Mars will involve a new generation of rover that explores the delta of the river age of 3.5 billion years.  Susan Carlin of the Fast Company visited the "clean room" (hall for assembling precision instruments, in which air quality is strictly controlled - approx. ed.)  NASA ’ s Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) and found out how the development of a new spacecraft is progressing.  JPL ’ s “Clean Room ” is similar to the television room in Willie Wonka and the Chocolate Factory: it ’ s a flawlessly clean room where people in white jumpsuits and masks engage in technological magic.  But instead of a camera that turns children into miniature figures, the centerpiece here is the new Mars 2020 rover that NASA plans to send to Mars this summer.  Although Mars 2020 does not pose the same challenge to the laws of physics as the Wonka camera, it is no less magical for one good reason: this device may finally answer the question of whether there was life on Mars.  Journalists are interviewing engineers working on the Mars 2020 mission.  The photo was taken in JPL ’ s “clean room ” on December 27, 2019.  Photo: NASA / JPL-Caltech In the last days of 2019, JPL, located in Pasadena, California, provided journalists with a rare opportunity to see High Bay 1, a spacious “clean room ” with a constant online broadcast, where NASA engineers are designing the Mars 2020 rover, as well as systems for descent to the planet and a seven-month journey on it.  Strict control of temperature, humidity and working processes in this room minimizes biological pollution, as well as the amount of dust and particulate matter that can interfere with electronics.  It requires strict rules for guests.  Before entering the “clean room ” we put on“ bunny suits ” – white polyester overalls, boots and hoods, as well as surgical masks and latex gloves glued to the sleeves.  We are also led through the cabin, where strong air currents remove microscopic debris from workwear.  It is not allowed to have cosmetics, perfumes, clothes made of wool and with torn edges, as well as fabric straps on cameras.  At the very door of technology wipe cameras and smartphones with alcohol.  JPL employees can only use unscented shampoos and one type of deodorant, and taking a shower before entering the “clean room ” is prohibited.  Even the High Bay Bob clean room mascot, a mannequin wearing bright green Christmas style sunglasses, wears a white protective suit.  “We don ’ t want to send a spacecraft to Mars and then say, ‘ Hey, there ’ s my hair. ’  All the rules about what you can ’ t do or bring with you are designed to protect the scientific component of this mission, ” said David Gruel, Mars 2020 Assembly, Testing and Launch Manager.  In search of life, Mars 2020, which JPL began building in 2011, will be the first rover to search for evidence that microorganisms lived on Mars in the past.  It will be engaged in drilling, analysis and collection of geological samples from areas that previously could have been inhabited.  It is assumed that future missions will return them to Earth in 2026 for more detailed study.  The launch of Mars 2020 is the first step towards a goal that JPL began discussing back in the 1980s and which eventually became a campaign to obtain geological samples from Mars.  After studying them, some important questions will be answered in the laboratory.  “Could life have formed on Mars, did it happen, and if not, why? ” — quotes the Director of JPL Michael Watkins.  The $2.5 billion project will also test the technologies humans will need for a long-term stay on Mars.  These include tools that improve landing, produce oxygen from Martian air rich in carbon dioxide, determine the composition of soil and groundwater, and record weather conditions.  Among the projects, there is even a small solar-powered helicopter, which is designed for flights taking into account the Martian atmosphere and reduced gravity.  This spring, NASA will announce the official name of Mars 2020, selected from more than 9 million options.  The rover will be launched from Cape Canaveral in Florida during the July-August window, landing on Mars is scheduled for February 8, 2021.  The device will begin its journey around the planet from the crater Jezero, the basin of an ancient lake, where in the past there was a high probability of life.  The mission will last at least one Martian year (approximately 687 Earth days) and cover up to 12 miles (more than 19 km).  One of the most serious problems in the operation of the “clean room ” is the danger of particulate pollution, and the other is the protection of highly sensitive electronics.  Special tape barriers keep reporters a short distance from mechanics to prevent accidental electrostatic discharges.  "The human body is made up of so much water that it is able to conduct electricity.  Electric shock from walking on the carpet and touching the door handle is about 20 thousand volts.  You can damage some of these high-speed electronic devices using just five volts.  We reduce this risk by controlling electrostatic discharge, ” said James Sean Howard, Head of Equipment Inspection at Mars 2020.  To do this, the equipment is surrounded by air ionizers, which neutralize static electricity, filling the air with positively and negatively charged ions.  The “clean room ” also maintains a humidity level above 30%, which makes the air more conductive and allows it to absorb and distribute excess charges.  When engineers work on mechanics, they connect special bracelets to a wire that returns electricity to the ground to prevent sparks.  Protective suits also contain carbon elements to relieve static stress from the fabric.  Faraday cells and electrostatic discharge needles — metal spikes on the outer surface of the rover — will protect electronics on Mars.  Another significant obstacle is the complexity of the instruments and moving parts, many of which the rover displays only after landing.  It uses more than 30 systems that control moving elements.  “Each of these mechanisms, gearboxes and engines is made up of hundreds of small parts, and they all have to be designed, analyzed, assembled and tested.  It ’ s hard to make them super reliable.  And, of course, there is no way to fix them on Mars, ” said Matt Wallace, deputy project manager for Mars 2020.  An engineering model of the Mars 2020 rover is being tested on Mars Yard, an area that mimics Martian conditions.  Photo: NASA / JPL-Caltech Protecting a system from Earth pollution that will place samples of Martian soil in test tubes is especially important.  "The front third of the rover is equipped with a mechanism similar to a Swiss watch, which takes a sample from a robotic arm, evaluates it and seals it tightly in a test tube.  To work on this equipment, a second set of sterile gloves was required, ” says engineer Zach Ousnamer.  The Mars 2020 rover borrowed a lot from Curiosity, while developing new technologies.  It is slightly larger than Curiosity: its length is 10 feet (about 3 m, not including a folding 9-foot robotic arm), width is 9 feet (about 2.7 m), height is 7 feet (about 2.1 m) and weight is 2,314 pounds (more than a ton).  Like Curiosity, Mars 2020 is powered by a combination of nuclear, battery and solar energy.  Its six aluminum wheels have a stronger construction and coating to avoid dents, holes and broken treads that interfered with Curiosity.  The Mars 2020 descent and landing system will repeat the stunning decline of Curiosity, known from the video “Seven Minutes of Horror ”.  Mars 2020 will travel to Mars in a protective airshell consisting of an upper skin and a lower heat-shielding shield.  A circular descent stage with eight brake rockets will be attached to the rover like a jet backpack that will drop it to the surface of the planet.  A few minutes before that, the parachute on the top of the airshell will slow the descent of the device until the need for a heat-shielding screen disappears and it comes off.  At this point, the descent stage will detach from the upper skin, release brake missiles towards the surface of Mars to slow down the descent, and ensure a careful landing of the rover.  Then it will detach, fly away and fall at some distance.  This time, several new onboard technologies will provide more controlled descent maneuvering, accurate landing, and data collection for future missions.  The device will also include a set of cameras and microphones to view what is happening in the first person and listen to the sounds of the landing.  The sensors will measure the temperature of the upper skin and the lower heat shield.  One navigation system will control the descent, focusing on the time of deployment of the parachute and the position of the spacecraft relative to the descent point.  The second will help land, highlighting the dangerous terrain during the descent by comparing fresh images of the approaching surface with a pre-loaded map of Mars.  Once on the surface of Mars, seven instruments — selected from 58 proposals around the world and including the development of the French, Spanish and Norwegian — will conduct a geological assessment of the area in which the rover descended to try to detect signs of ancient Martian life. passages.title: Colonizing other planets? They have to be remade first.
passages.passage: Is it time to colonize other planets?  The population of the Earth is rapidly increasing, and soon humanity will be on the planet closely.  Futurists view the colonization of the solar system as the most likely scenario for the future.  It is possible that people will have to deal with terraforming - engineering change of other worlds.  In September 2015, speaking in one of the humorous television shows, Elon Musk proposed to bomb the poles of Mars with nuclear warheads.  In his opinion, this will allow you to quickly evaporate from the surface of the planet dry ice from carbon dioxide.  Of course, Musk was joking.  There simply aren ’ t enough nuclear weapons on Earth to make the Tesla founder ’ s plan work.  Scientists suggest heating the surface of the red planet in other ways.  For example, to push Mars against an asteroid or use a huge orbital mirror that would concentrate solar energy and direct it to the Martian polar ice caps.  However, at the current level of technology development, it is almost impossible to implement all these scenarios.  In addition, efforts to turn Mars into a planet suitable for life, may be in vain, scientists from the University of Colorado.  After analyzing the data obtained by the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter and Mars Odyssey, they concluded that there is not enough carbon dioxide in the rocks and polar caps on the Red Planet to form a dense atmosphere.  However, Elon Musk, who dreams of building a colony on Mars, believes that a huge amount of carbon dioxide is absorbed in the Martian soil.  When the planet is heated, a powerful release of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere will occur, and this will start the process of terraforming - the transformation of Mars into the likeness of Earth.  To create an atmosphere on Venus, Venus, on the contrary, requires cooling.  The average temperature at its surface is about 452 degrees Celsius, and the pressure is about 90 bar.  Otherwise, in terms of mass, gravity and solar radiation, Venus resembles Earth.  Moreover, according to calculations of scientists from the Goddard Space Research Institute, about two billion years ago, the climate of Venus was similar to that of Earth.  There were liquid oceans on the planet, the temperature was comfortable 15-17 degrees Celsius.  Carl Sagan proposed to sow cyanobacteria in the atmosphere of Venus.  Through photosynthesis, they will convert carbon dioxide into organic matter and release oxygen.  However, whether the bacteria themselves will survive in harsh Venusian conditions is unclear.  In addition, according to physicist Martin Fogg, the process of converting carbon dioxide into organic matter would take about a million years.  A faster way to make Venus habitable is to let a lot of hydrogen into the atmosphere so that all the carbon dioxide it contains turns into graphite and water.  As a catalyst, iron filings can be sprayed over the planet.  It is believed that as a result, the pressure will drop to three bar, the greenhouse effect will disappear, and water will appear on the surface.  In the most favorable scenario, it will cover up to 80 percent of the planet.  However, as noted by the staff of the John Glenn Research Center (NASA), all these methods will not help, if you do not deal with the main problems: sulfuric acid clouds and too long a sunny day, equal to 117 Earth days.  If you figure out how to get rid of these troubles, Venus is quite suitable for terraforming.  It is logical to make a habitable moon much closer to us.  According to American and British scientists, in the past it could have been inhabited.  Now the satellite of the Earth is not the most hospitable place.  The temperature there ranges from minus 180 to plus 120 degrees Celsius.  There is no magnetic field of its own, and therefore cosmic radiation sterilizes the surface.  The atmosphere is so thin that it actually does not exist, which means that the threat of falling meteorites is constantly preserved.  But on the moon there is one of the main conditions of terraforming - water in the form of "icy permafrost" near the poles.  In 2012, the place of its occurrence was studied by the Russian neutron telescope LEND, which is on board the American probe LRO.  The problem with the retention of the atmosphere and the delivery to the moon of volatile elements necessary for life (hydrogen, nitrogen and carbon), most often proposed to solve with the help of comets.  It is believed that these objects, when they collide with the Moon, will dissipate gases and water vapor, thus creating an atmosphere.  The impacts will also release the water contained in the lunar regolith and form natural bodies of water on the surface.  The transmission of the same momentum from comets will accelerate the rotation of the moon, which will contribute to the retention of the atmosphere.  But bombardment of the moon by space objects can touch the Earth tangentially.  A safer option is to make only a small part of the satellite habitable.  Researchers from NASA propose to create in the crater Shackleton, in which a few years ago discovered water ice, a microclimate to grow plants and was suitable for breathing atmosphere.  At first, robots will do this: they will erect a dome and install solar mirrors.

passages.title: A hole under the Chinese rover has been discovered.
passages.passage: China ’ s National Space Administration (CNSA) released new images of the Zhurong rover on Saturday.  The images were interesting in themselves, but an aerospace reporter discovered something interesting about them.  He noticed a large hole beneath the rover.  Jonathan O'Callaghan tweeted: "The crater that the Chinese rover created when it landed on the Red Planet's surface is very interesting.  Phil Metzger, a planetary scientist at the University of Central Florida, responded to the tweet and said it was not a good thing.  He added: “This is a new hole.  Look at its edges and imagine a 40-ton probe on top of it and how big the hole could be.  The crater is likely to collapse, especially in the coming weeks when the soil dries up and falls off the base of the probe.  The researcher explained how falling soil beneath the probe's foundations causes it to tilt, and this is just one of the dangers of landing large probes on the soft soil of Mars.  The second risk is that the material will collide with the probe, because the fuel will come out of the hole before it is cut off, and the third risk is that it will collide with other hardware around it.  China ’ s National Space Administration (CNSA) on Saturday released a selfie taken on the Red Planet by the Mars Rover Jurong.  The rover was launched in July 2020 aboard the Chinese Tianwen-1 spacecraft and entered orbit around Mars in February.  Paul Byrne, a professor of planetary science at NC State University, tweeted: “Chinese rover Zhorong carried a small wireless camera that he placed on the surface of Mars for a group photo.  Another image released by China ’ s National Space Administration (CNSA) shows a clear crystal view of the landing pad amid the rocky red dust of the planet as well as the Martian landscape captured by the Zhorong rover.  China has invested billions of dollars in an intergalactic mission to Mars in an effort to catch up with its rival, the United States, and confirm its status as a major global power.  China ’ s mission to Mars includes several new space projects the country is pursuing, including putting Chinese astronauts on the moon and having a space station by 2022.  China had previously tried to launch a probe to Mars in 2011, but the mission failed and the Chinese spacecraft burned up in the atmosphere after being launched from the Kazakh base.  This time, China not only acted independently on the mission, but also sent a series of orbiters and a rover to Mars to speed up its mission.  The pace of China ’ s space program has been remarkable over the past two decades.  In 2003, Yang Liwei became the first Chinese astronaut to orbit Earth, and last year Chang'e-4 successfully landed on the far side of the moon.

passages.title: Building a futuristic city on Mars with a capacity of one million + images
passages.passage: Plans for the construction of a futuristic city on Mars with a capacity of one million people for the first time have been prepared by Abibo Studio, whose headquarters are in Spain, the United States and India.  A team of academics has also helped the company ’ s designers explore structures related to Mars conditions.  Due to the deadly atmospheric conditions on Mars, the designers have chosen the edge of a rock on Mars to build a vertical city.  The design is based on modular and small components, including recreational areas and food growing sites.  Its vertical buildings protect residents from the conditions and atmosphere of Mars by placing their homes inside radiation-proof rocks.  Alfredo Muons, the founder of Abibo, said: "Sunlight and gamma-rays on Mars have forced us to create spaces that are not directly exposed to the sky and light.  If we were to build buildings like the ground, the buildings would explode with air pressure.  The project, called Neva, consists of five small towns inside a rock with a capacity of 1 million people.  Each city is home to between 200,000 and 250,000 people.  In designing these Martian cities, architects have come up with concrete structures that ensure a suitable habitat for humans and other forms of life.  The designs were submitted earlier this year to a competition organized by the Mars Society.  End of message.

passages.title: Secrets of the Fourth Planet
passages.passage: 2050.  Humanity has finally become an interplanetary species, establishing a colony on Mars that is home to about a million people — more than Amsterdam or Athens.  This is not the beginning of a new science fiction novel or the plot of the film.  This is a vision of the future that Elon Musk recently shared.  The entrepreneur often paints the most fantastic scenarios, but one cannot blame him: it is not only him who is drawn to Mars.  Unfriendly neighbor Mars is not the most hospitable world, if you compare it with the Earth.  The force of gravity here is only 37.5% of the earth ’ s.  The temperature on the surface ranges from freezing -153 ° C to comfortable + 20 ° C.  However, a thin, unsuitable for humans atmosphere, consisting mainly of carbon dioxide, nitrogen and argon, is not able to effectively trap heat from sunlight.  If you were standing on the Martian equator at noon, your feet would have a temperature of + 24 ° C and your head would have a temperature of 0 ° C.  In addition, the pressure on the red planet is much lower – even at the top of Everest on Earth, it is 50 times greater than on the surface of Mars.  However, these worlds have a lot in common.  Beneath our feet is solid land, the area of which is comparable to the land area on our planet, although Mars is about half its size.  The duration of the day, which is called soles, is 24.6 hours, and close to the Earth's angle of inclination of the axis of rotation (23.5 for the Earth and 25.2 for Mars) provides the world with pronounced seasons, which, however, last longer than ours.  For example, spring in the northern hemisphere lasts as much as 194 solas - this is the longest season on the planet.  But the main similarity of the planets remains in the distant past.  Numerous evidence points to the fact that Mars used to be warmer, had a denser atmosphere, and its surface was covered with water - the cradle of intelligent life on our home planet.  That ’ s why researchers are looking so closely at this harsh world.  The chances of life on Mars are slim.  For example, in 2018, a group of European scientists found signs of the existence of a liquid lake hidden 1.5 km below the surface of the southern polar glacier.  Microbes may exist in such a reservoir, but this is only a hypothesis that is difficult to test.  Therefore, scientists rely on the search for signs of the existence of a past life.  It may not sound so exciting, but even such a find will be colossal.  Otherwise, we will face a much larger scientific mystery: why the Earth gave life, and the neighboring world with the right conditions - not.  The race for Martian life began in the 19th century.  In 1877, the Italian astronomer Giovanni Schiaparelli looked through the telescope Mars, which no one imagined, and even made a map.  It depicted seas and continents, as well as an extensive network of lines, which the astronomer called channels.  The word itself prompted the idea of ​ ​ the man-made origin of these objects.  It was later established that the channels were an optical illusion, but the idea of the existence of the Martian civilization that built them was picked up by others.  Astronomers such as American Percival Lowell or Frenchman Camille Flammarion believed in the habitability of the Red Planet, and science fiction writers such as Edgar Burroughs and H.G. Wells.  Of course, this theory was not accepted by everyone, but it was not possible to test it for a long time.  That all changed in the 1950s.  After the launch of the first Soviet satellite in 1957 and the start of the space race, the views of the USSR and the United States quickly rushed beyond the Earth ’ s orbit and even the Moon.  Already in the 1960s, the first automatic interplanetary stations rushed to the Red Planet.  No one thought about landing or orbiters at that time.  AMS sent to other worlds had to fly by, trying to take as many pictures as possible and send them to Earth.  But this task was not easy either.  The first attempt to send a research apparatus to the Red Planet was made by the Soviet Union in 1960, but it, like many others after it, failed.  Soviet devices died, not having time to leave the orbit of the Earth, at best broke down in flight to Mars.  In 1964, NASA entered the game, but its debut was unsuccessful.  The second attempt was successful.  Mariner 4 arrived safely on Mars in 1965.  It flew about 10 thousand km above the surface of the planet and sent 22 photos to Earth.  These were the first images of Mars from such a short distance.  There were no channels on them, but scientists saw the craters decorating the Martian earth, and confirmed that the atmosphere of the planet consists of carbon dioxide.  NASA has been successful ever since.  Until the end of the decade, the agency launched two more AMS, which managed to take two hundred photos, as well as carry out measurements of the surface and temperature of Mars.  The first spacecraft to make a soft landing on Mars was the Soviet Mars-3, but on the surface it worked for a few seconds The Soviet Union caught up with the Americans only in 1971, but by that time the ambitions of local scientists and engineers had grown.  Just flying over the surface wasn ’ t enough.  In 1971, the Soviet Union sent to the Red Planet at once two AMS - "Mars-2" and "Mars-3", which included both orbiters and lander.  These missions have been successful.  Orbiters have been orbiting the planet for months, transmitting data.  As for the landers, one crashed during the landing, and the second successfully inscribed his name in history.  "Mars-3" was the first device to make a soft landing on the red planet, even if it worked in a matter of seconds.  1971 proved to be a fruitful year for the study of the fourth planet.  That year, the American orbiter Mariner 9 arrived, which not only took thousands of photos and made a map of 85% of its surface, but also helped to see the main attractions of Mars.  For example, data from Mariner 9 helped establish the height of Olympus, the tallest volcano in the solar system, which rises 25 km and the diameter of the base is 600 km.  And the NASA research apparatus helped to estimate the scale of the Mariner Valley - the famous system of canyons, which stretches for 4 thousand km along the Martian equator and crashes 7 km deep into the surface of the planet.  The system, named after the probe, is four times deeper and five times longer than the Grand Canyon on Earth.  The next breakthrough in the study of Mars was made only in 1976, when NASA delivered there two AMS - "Viking 1" and "Viking 2".  Like the Soviet Mars, they were equipped with orbiters and landers, but the Vikings were more successful.  They successfully placed in orbit and landed on the surface of the planet, having worked for more than one year.  The Viking 1 lander fell silent only in 1982, and even then after an erroneous command from Earth.  During this time, they replenished the Martian photo archive with tens of thousands of images, but most importantly - they conducted the first field experiments to search for traces of life.  Alas, they did not give a convincing "yes" or a definite "no", but still it was a breakthrough, since previously Mars was studied on the principle of "look, but do not touch".  "Vikings" involuntarily added fuel to the fire of the myth of the Martian civilization, when one of the orbiters sent a curious picture.  It showed a pile of stones, one of which was strikingly reminiscent of a human face.  NASA researchers immediately realized that this is a game of light and shadow, but the impressionable public began to build theories about the remains of an ancient Martian city that rests underground.  The tradition of looking for the usual forms in photos of the Red Planet is still alive today, and those who want to constantly find rodents and insects in the pictures.  But these are just illusions.  Face on Mars.  This image, taken in the AMC "Viking 1" 1976, refreshed the myth of the existence of a developed Martian civilization After the "Vikings" study of the red planet for many years stalled.  For two decades, the US and the USSR, and subsequently Russia, continued to send mechanical researchers, but the attempts were mostly unsuccessful.  A new breakthrough occurred in the second half of the 1990s.  In 1997, NASA delivered the Mars Global Surveyor orbiter to Mars, which helped make a revolutionary discovery: somewhere under the surface of a dead planet, water can still flow, the hunt for which continues to this day.  In the same year, the Pathfinder landed on the surface, which has not happened since the time of the Vikings.  But much more interesting was the cargo that Pathfinder brought with him.  With him on the planet arrived the first mobile research apparatus Sojourner, able to move on

passages.title: Elon Musk said when will finish the rocket for a flight to Mars
passages.passage: The main task of his “Martian ” project, which Musk has been talking about for more than a decade, the entrepreneur considers the creation of an autonomous colony on the Red Planet with a population of up to a million people.  The founder of Tesla and SpaceX, Elon Musk, told when to expect the first flight of the new interplanetary spacecraft being developed by his company.  Fresh details about the planned program for the development of Mars entrepreneur shared at the conference SXSW in Austin, where unexpectedly for all appeared at one of the events, reports vesti.ru.  Recall that in September 2017, Musk announced his project for the development of the red planet and announced that he was going to organize the first delivery of cargo to Mars in 2022.  To perform the flight should not yet ready super-heavy rocket codenamed BFR.  Speaking on Sunday evening at SXSW, the billionaire suggested that the first short test flights of the new missile could take place in the first half of 2019.  “Although sometimes with deadlines I have a little … well, you know, ” Musk joked, hinting that he did not always fulfill his promises to release this or that Tesla product or launch a new SpaceX rocket in the promised time.  The main task of his “Martian ” project, which Musk has been talking about for more than a decade, the entrepreneur considers the creation of an autonomous colony on the Red Planet with a population of up to a million people.  In his opinion, such a settlement is a guarantee of the survival of civilization in the event of a nuclear war or other global cataclysm on Earth.  In the short term, the Martian colony will need glass domes in which it will be possible to maintain an Earth-like composition of air, a propulsion system and a set of other basic things to support life.  Once the infrastructure is ready, “there will really be an explosion of business opportunities, because Mars will need everything from steel mills to pizzerias. ”  But the main threat to humanity, the founder of Tesla and SpacX still considers not weapons of mass destruction or catastrophic climate change, but artificial intelligence.  “Remember my words, ” he told the audience at SXSW,“ AI is far more dangerous than nuclear missiles.  So why isn ’ t it regulated yet? ”  More important news in the Telegram channel “zakon.kz ”.  Sign up!

passages.title: Mars Rover Perseverance for the first time in history was able to get oxygen from the atmosphere of Mars
passages.passage: NASA employees for the first time received oxygen from the atmosphere of Mars, which is 96% carbon dioxide, according to the website of the American space Agency.  On April 20, the Pereverance rover, which has been exploring Mars since February, processed carbon dioxide into oxygen with the help of an experimental MOXIE spacecraft installed aboard the rover.  After two hours of preparation, MOXIE began producing oxygen at a rate of six grams per hour.  During the first experiment, NASA experts received 5.4 grams of oxygen, which would be enough to breathe for 10 minutes.  In general, MOXIE is able to produce up to 10 grams of oxygen per hour.  Jim Reuter, deputy director of NASA's science directorate, called the experiment "an important first step in converting carbon dioxide into oxygen on Mars."  "We are getting closer to our goal: someday see humans on Mars," Reuters said.  According to him, oxygen is important both for breathing people and for obtaining rocket fuel.  “In the future, researchers will need to get fuel on Mars to return home, ” he said.  Minval.az

passages.title: NASA spacecraft will land on Mars today
passages.passage: NASA spacecraft today will land on Mars 18.02.2021 13: 23 Ukrinform Rover Perseverance ("Perseverance") of the US National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) today, February 18, will land on the surface of the Red Planet.  According to Ukrinform, this is reported on the website of the US Department.  The landing itself will take place in the Jezero crater, which is located on the Red Planet.  The active landing phase will begin at 21: 15 in Kiev.  See also: The Chinese probe aligned in the orbit of Mars The current speed of movement is 76 491 km per hour.  The Perseverance rover will look for signs of ancient microbial existence on the Red Planet.  It will also help to characterize the climate and geology of the planet and will be the first planetary mission to collect samples of Martian rock and regolith (broken rock and dust).  NASA plans that the mission of the device on the red planet will last 687 days.  See also: Mars rovers on the red planet to push elbows will not Follow the live broadcast can be here.  It is noted that the rover was launched on the Atlas V launch vehicle on July 30 last year from the spaceport in Florida.  As reported Ukrinform, today, February 18, the American space orbital station Perseverance will deliver to the orbit of Mars a unique in all respects experimental device - "MOXIE" Mars Oxygen ISRU Experiment (Martian oxygen, abbreviation ISRU means "In situ") u ", that is, oxygen produced" in situ "), which for the first time will attempt to obtain O2 from the atmosphere of another planet.  Photo: NASA According to materials: Ukrinform
