Title: Secrets of the Fourth Planet
Content: 2050.  Humanity has finally become an interplanetary species, establishing a colony on Mars that is home to about a million people — more than Amsterdam or Athens.  This is not the beginning of a new science fiction novel or the plot of the film.  This is a vision of the future that Elon Musk recently shared.  The entrepreneur often paints the most fantastic scenarios, but one cannot blame him: it is not only him who is drawn to Mars.  Unfriendly neighbor Mars is not the most hospitable world, if you compare it with the Earth.  The force of gravity here is only 37.5% of the earth ’ s.  The temperature on the surface ranges from freezing -153 ° C to comfortable + 20 ° C.  However, a thin, unsuitable for humans atmosphere, consisting mainly of carbon dioxide, nitrogen and argon, is not able to effectively trap heat from sunlight.  If you were standing on the Martian equator at noon, your feet would have a temperature of + 24 ° C and your head would have a temperature of 0 ° C.  In addition, the pressure on the red planet is much lower – even at the top of Everest on Earth, it is 50 times greater than on the surface of Mars.  However, these worlds have a lot in common.  Beneath our feet is solid land, the area of which is comparable to the land area on our planet, although Mars is about half its size.  The duration of the day, which is called soles, is 24.6 hours, and close to the Earth's angle of inclination of the axis of rotation (23.5 for the Earth and 25.2 for Mars) provides the world with pronounced seasons, which, however, last longer than ours.  For example, spring in the northern hemisphere lasts as much as 194 solas - this is the longest season on the planet.  But the main similarity of the planets remains in the distant past.  Numerous evidence points to the fact that Mars used to be warmer, had a denser atmosphere, and its surface was covered with water - the cradle of intelligent life on our home planet.  That ’ s why researchers are looking so closely at this harsh world.  The chances of life on Mars are slim.  For example, in 2018, a group of European scientists found signs of the existence of a liquid lake hidden 1.5 km below the surface of the southern polar glacier.  Microbes may exist in such a reservoir, but this is only a hypothesis that is difficult to test.  Therefore, scientists rely on the search for signs of the existence of a past life.  It may not sound so exciting, but even such a find will be colossal.  Otherwise, we will face a much larger scientific mystery: why the Earth gave life, and the neighboring world with the right conditions - not.  The race for Martian life began in the 19th century.  In 1877, the Italian astronomer Giovanni Schiaparelli looked through the telescope Mars, which no one imagined, and even made a map.  It depicted seas and continents, as well as an extensive network of lines, which the astronomer called channels.  The word itself prompted the idea of ​ ​ the man-made origin of these objects.  It was later established that the channels were an optical illusion, but the idea of the existence of the Martian civilization that built them was picked up by others.  Astronomers such as American Percival Lowell or Frenchman Camille Flammarion believed in the habitability of the Red Planet, and science fiction writers such as Edgar Burroughs and H.G. Wells.  Of course, this theory was not accepted by everyone, but it was not possible to test it for a long time.  That all changed in the 1950s.  After the launch of the first Soviet satellite in 1957 and the start of the space race, the views of the USSR and the United States quickly rushed beyond the Earth ’ s orbit and even the Moon.  Already in the 1960s, the first automatic interplanetary stations rushed to the Red Planet.  No one thought about landing or orbiters at that time.  AMS sent to other worlds had to fly by, trying to take as many pictures as possible and send them to Earth.  But this task was not easy either.  The first attempt to send a research apparatus to the Red Planet was made by the Soviet Union in 1960, but it, like many others after it, failed.  Soviet devices died, not having time to leave the orbit of the Earth, at best broke down in flight to Mars.  In 1964, NASA entered the game, but its debut was unsuccessful.  The second attempt was successful.  Mariner 4 arrived safely on Mars in 1965.  It flew about 10 thousand km above the surface of the planet and sent 22 photos to Earth.  These were the first images of Mars from such a short distance.  There were no channels on them, but scientists saw the craters decorating the Martian earth, and confirmed that the atmosphere of the planet consists of carbon dioxide.  NASA has been successful ever since.  Until the end of the decade, the agency launched two more AMS, which managed to take two hundred photos, as well as carry out measurements of the surface and temperature of Mars.  The first spacecraft to make a soft landing on Mars was the Soviet Mars-3, but on the surface it worked for a few seconds The Soviet Union caught up with the Americans only in 1971, but by that time the ambitions of local scientists and engineers had grown.  Just flying over the surface wasn ’ t enough.  In 1971, the Soviet Union sent to the Red Planet at once two AMS - "Mars-2" and "Mars-3", which included both orbiters and lander.  These missions have been successful.  Orbiters have been orbiting the planet for months, transmitting data.  As for the landers, one crashed during the landing, and the second successfully inscribed his name in history.  "Mars-3" was the first device to make a soft landing on the red planet, even if it worked in a matter of seconds.  1971 proved to be a fruitful year for the study of the fourth planet.  That year, the American orbiter Mariner 9 arrived, which not only took thousands of photos and made a map of 85% of its surface, but also helped to see the main attractions of Mars.  For example, data from Mariner 9 helped establish the height of Olympus, the tallest volcano in the solar system, which rises 25 km and the diameter of the base is 600 km.  And the NASA research apparatus helped to estimate the scale of the Mariner Valley - the famous system of canyons, which stretches for 4 thousand km along the Martian equator and crashes 7 km deep into the surface of the planet.  The system, named after the probe, is four times deeper and five times longer than the Grand Canyon on Earth.  The next breakthrough in the study of Mars was made only in 1976, when NASA delivered there two AMS - "Viking 1" and "Viking 2".  Like the Soviet Mars, they were equipped with orbiters and landers, but the Vikings were more successful.  They successfully placed in orbit and landed on the surface of the planet, having worked for more than one year.  The Viking 1 lander fell silent only in 1982, and even then after an erroneous command from Earth.  During this time, they replenished the Martian photo archive with tens of thousands of images, but most importantly - they conducted the first field experiments to search for traces of life.  Alas, they did not give a convincing "yes" or a definite "no", but still it was a breakthrough, since previously Mars was studied on the principle of "look, but do not touch".  "Vikings" involuntarily added fuel to the fire of the myth of the Martian civilization, when one of the orbiters sent a curious picture.  It showed a pile of stones, one of which was strikingly reminiscent of a human face.  NASA researchers immediately realized that this is a game of light and shadow, but the impressionable public began to build theories about the remains of an ancient Martian city that rests underground.  The tradition of looking for the usual forms in photos of the Red Planet is still alive today, and those who want to constantly find rodents and insects in the pictures.  But these are just illusions.  Face on Mars.  This image, taken in the AMC "Viking 1" 1976, refreshed the myth of the existence of a developed Martian civilization After the "Vikings" study of the red planet for many years stalled.  For two decades, the US and the USSR, and subsequently Russia, continued to send mechanical researchers, but the attempts were mostly unsuccessful.  A new breakthrough occurred in the second half of the 1990s.  In 1997, NASA delivered the Mars Global Surveyor orbiter to Mars, which helped make a revolutionary discovery: somewhere under the surface of a dead planet, water can still flow, the hunt for which continues to this day.  In the same year, the Pathfinder landed on the surface, which has not happened since the time of the Vikings.  But much more interesting was the cargo that Pathfinder brought with him.  With him on the planet arrived the first mobile research apparatus Sojourner, able to move on

Title: Elon Musk said when will finish the rocket for a flight to Mars
Content: The main task of his “Martian ” project, which Musk has been talking about for more than a decade, the entrepreneur considers the creation of an autonomous colony on the Red Planet with a population of up to a million people.  The founder of Tesla and SpaceX, Elon Musk, told when to expect the first flight of the new interplanetary spacecraft being developed by his company.  Fresh details about the planned program for the development of Mars entrepreneur shared at the conference SXSW in Austin, where unexpectedly for all appeared at one of the events, reports vesti.ru.  Recall that in September 2017, Musk announced his project for the development of the red planet and announced that he was going to organize the first delivery of cargo to Mars in 2022.  To perform the flight should not yet ready super-heavy rocket codenamed BFR. The main task of his “Martian ” project, which Musk has been talking about for more than a decade, the entrepreneur considers the creation of an autonomous colony on the Red Planet with a population of up to a million people. Title: Revealed the mystery of the mysterious Martian “spiders ”
Content: Planetary scientists have successfully recreated the famous Martian "spiders" in the laboratory - these huge figures on the surface of the Red Planet have repeatedly come across scientists in satellite images.  The structure similar to spiders was removed at the south pole of Mars by the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter.  Their size sometimes reaches a kilometer, writes Live Science.  Researchers have long puzzled over the nature of such objects.  As a result, scientists were able to experimentally prove that arachnids on the surface are traces of carbon dioxide vapor escape from cracks in the polar ice.  During the experiments, experts took plates of dry ice and simulated the Martian atmosphere and the soil of the red planet.  After that, they began to raise and lower the plates on the ground - when the cold ice touched the warmer soil, it instantly turned into gas.  This process is called sublimation, it is widespread on Earth.  Patterns in the form of spiders appear during the direct conversion of dry ice from solid to gas.  At the same time, on Mars, this process is especially active in the spring, when the soil is heated by the Sun especially strongly.

Title: Martian organics formed thanks to natural batteries
Content: Scientists seem to have uncovered the secret of the origin of organic matter in meteorites that came from the Red Planet.  The list of participants in the process sounds like this: water, volcanic rocks, electricity.  What is nice is that such processes can take place on many bodies of the solar system.  Scientists seem to have uncovered the secret of the origin of organic matter in meteorites that came from the Red Planet.  The formation of organic matter occurs due to natural “accumulators ” consisting of water, salts and volcanic rocks.  Such conclusions are made in a scientific article published in the journal Science Advanced by a group led by Andrew Steele (Andrew Steele) from the Carnegie Scientific Institute in the USA.Recall that proteins, fats, carbohydrates, DNA, RNA and many other molecules, without which it is impossible to imagine a living organism, belong to organic substances.  Of course, not all organic matter is an integral part of living beings or is formed with their participation, so it is not necessary to equate organic matter with life. However, the presence of such molecules is the most important condition for the appearance of the biosphere.  Apparently, only organic chemistry can provide the variety, flexibility and complexity of chemical processes that are necessary for the existence of even the most primitive microbe.  In 2012, a team led by Steele studied carbon from organic molecules found in ten Martian meteorites.  The researchers came to two conclusions, pleasant and not so.  The good news is that this organics originated on Mars (rather than being brought in by pollution on Earth).  The bad news: it is not a product of the vital activity of living organisms; how was it formed in this case?  This is what the authors of a recent study found out. "Identification of the processes during which organic carbon compounds are formed on Mars is of great interest to determine its habitability potential," says Steel.Scientists used three samples of Martian meteorites.  The first is Tissint, which fell in Morocco in 2011.  The second is Nakhla, discovered in Egypt in 1911.  The third was NWA 1950, found in Morocco in 2001.  In all these celestial stones previously found inclusions of Martian organics.Meteorites were subjected to the most careful analysis.  Among the methods used were both the usual viewing of the sample in an optical microscope, and Raman spectroscopy, translucent electron microscopy, nanoscale mass spectrometry of secondary ions, X-ray absorption near the absorption edge (X-ray absorption near-edge structure) and other methods with names incomprehensible to the average person. Thanks to all these methods, the authors thoroughly studied the chemical composition and fine structure of organic inclusions and the surrounding rocks.  By the way, it turned out that the organics of meteorites are extremely similar to the substances found on the Red Planet by the MSL mission.  The detailed information obtained allowed scientists to draw conclusions about what processes could lead to the formation of these substances. It turned out that one of the necessary ingredients are volcanic minerals such as spinel.  On the Red Planet, rich in ancient volcanoes, there is no shortage of such material.  The second important component is liquid water, in huge concentrations containing various salts (in particular, perchlorates).  Such brines have never been directly detected on Mars, but, according to experts, they can exist there almost everywhere.  Finally, the third element of the “magic potion ” is carbon dioxide.  It is also, to put it mildly, not in deficit: the Martian atmosphere consists of it almost completely.  For a while, there is something like a natural battery.  As a result, organic compounds are formed from carbon CO2 and hydrogen of water. "The discovery that a natural system can essentially form a small battery based on corrosion, which controls electrochemical reactions between minerals and the surrounding liquid, has serious consequences for astrobiology," says Steele. Indeed, it turned out that the synthesis of organic matter does not need exotic conditions or components.  All the necessary ingredients are quite common for Mars, which is either already proven (volcanic minerals and carbon dioxide), or assumed (brines).  Moreover, a similar process can take place on bodies such as Europa or Enceladus.  Recall that earlier "33Live.RuNauka" (nauka.vesti.ru) wrote about how a record amount of organic matter was discovered on Mars, as well as that life in the crust of the planet could be supported by radiation.

Title: Converting Martian salt water into oxygen and fuel with a new technology
Content: New technology allows astronauts to convert Martian saltwater into oxygen and fuel when they land on the Red Planet in 2033.  There is water on Mars, but most of it is frozen, and the rest is mixed with salt, making it useless for future astronauts who plan to land on the planet by 2033.  Now, a team of researchers at Washington University in St. Louis has developed a system that converts unusable water into fuel and oxygen.  The system uses electricity to convert saltwater into oxygen and hydrogen, and has been found to work in the Martian atmosphere at temperatures as low as -33 degrees Fahrenheit.  The saltwater electrolyser produces 25 times more oxygen than NASA ’ s MOXIE, which launched in July 2020 with the Mars 2020 rover and aims to produce a small amount of oxygen on Mars.  Vijay Ramani of the University of Washington said the technology is just as useful on Earth as it is on Mars because it can turn the oceans into a source of oxygen and fuel.  According to Inverse, the device has two parts around it, one of which separates water to form hydroxyl ions and the other separates water again to produce oxygen.  Although the technology is currently being developed on Earth, it is expensive and likely will not be able to withstand the freezing temperatures of Mars.  Ramani and other researchers decided to build a portable version of the technology that could operate on the Red Planet continuously without the need to heat or purify the water source.  Research scientist and first author of the study, Shrihari Sankarasubramanian, said: “Water-soluble perchlorates (so-called impurities) are actually functional in a Mars-like environment because they prevent water from freezing and also improve the performance of the electrolaser system by reducing electrical resistance.  The study is based on data from NASA ’ s Phoenix Mars Lander, which touched Mars in 2008.  Scientists know that in order to live on Mars, even temporarily, astronauts would have to produce some of their needs, especially oxygen for breathing and fuel for travel to Earth or beyond on the Red Planet.  NASA's Mars Endurance rover is currently traveling to Mars by carrying instruments that use electrolysis at high temperatures.  The researchers hope to work with NASA to further develop the system in the future.  End of message.

Title: Oxygen and hydrogen on Mars proposed to get from brine
Content: Scientists have developed a method for producing oxygen and hydrogen from a liquid saline solution in Martian lakes using electrolysis.  A feature of the experiment was the use of lead-ruthenium oxide as an electrocatalyst for oxygen production.  The production of oxygen using such an installation was 25 times more energy efficient than in the case of MOXIE, launched to the Red Planet as part of the Mars 2020 mission, and the size and weight of the device for life support based on the described technology will be less than that of analogues.  The article was published in the journal PNAS.  Conditions on Mars are far from favorable for humans: the atmosphere is rarefied and 95 percent consists of carbon dioxide, and temperature changes exceed 100 degrees Celsius with an average temperature of minus 63 degrees.  Therefore, colonization of the Red Planet is impossible without the creation of a life support system that would be able to provide people with oxygen for breathing and fuel (for example, hydrogen) for energy supply and, ideally, return flight.  To solve the first problem, NASA created MOXIE (Mars Oxygen ISRU Experiment) - an experimental installation for obtaining oxygen from atmospheric carbon dioxide by electrolysis.  To test the effectiveness of such a method in the field, the installation became part of the Mars Rover Perseverance, which was launched on July 30, 2020 as part of the Mars 2020 mission.  An alternative source of not only oxygen, but also hydrogen on Mars can be water, the first direct evidence of the existence of which on the red planet was obtained in 1971.  Particularly attractive for use in applications, however, would be the reserves of salt water, impurities in which would allow it to remain in a liquid state even at low temperature and pressure.  The first traces of such brine (liquid salt solution) with magnesium perchlorate as the main component were found on Mars in 2015, and in 2018, a reservoir with a diameter of about 20 kilometers was found under the polar ice of the planet, which could have been formed due to volcanic activity.  Later, planetary scientists confirmed that such lakes on Mars really exist and can be numerous.  Now Pralay Gayen (Pralay Gayen) from the University of Washington in St. Louis together with colleagues created an installation for obtaining oxygen and hydrogen from a saline solution close in composition and temperature to that in Martian lakes.  As a brine in the experiment, a solution of magnesium perchlorate in water with a concentration of 2.8 mol per liter was used, cooled to minus 36 degrees Celsius and blown by carbon dioxide (the latter played the role of the Martian atmosphere).  As an electrocatalyst for the production of oxygen, the scientists used lead-ruthenium oxide Pb2Ru2O7-δ, the effectiveness of which they previously showed for alkaline solutions.  The electrocatalyst for hydrogen production was platinum on activated carbon - the standard catalyst in this case, and a commercially produced anion-exchange membrane was used as a separator.  Installation diagram.  In the red region, oxygen is produced, in the blue - hydrogen.  Image source: Pralay Gayen et al. / PNAS In the course of the study, scientists showed that lead-ruthenium oxide as an electrocatalyst is indeed several times more effective than the ruthenium oxide commonly used in such installations.  After the behavior of the created installation was studied in a wide range of temperatures from − 36 to 21 degrees Celsius and saw no radical fluctuations in the efficiency and rate of production.  The current output of the experimental installation was 70 percent, and the energy efficiency was in the range between 36 and 70 percent (depending on the voltage applied to the plates).  In addition, the installation was resistant to degradation of the catalyst: scientists were not able to find traces of ruthenium in the solution after 300-minute operation of the device.  The rate of production of oxygen (blue dots) and hydrogen (red dots), depending on the density of the cathode current.  Image source: Pralay Gayen et al. / PNAS Also, the researchers compared the achieved rate of oxygen production with MOXIE values of 10-22 grams per hour: it turned out that with the same energy supply, the created installation produces 25 times more oxygen than the experiment on the Mars Rover “Perseverance ”.  To have the same rate of oxygen production as MOXIE, the device would have to have electrodes with an area of ​ ​ 28-62 square centimeters, and to ensure the vital activity of a sleeping and actively moving person, this parameter would have to be 375 and 1235 square centimeters, respectively.  At the same time, the mass and volume of the installation will be less than if you use the technology inherent in MOXIE.  Moreover, the developed method of obtaining oxygen does not require its subsequent purification, while during electrolysis in MOXIE, carbon monoxide is also produced, which must be filtered.  Dependence on the power consumption of the rate of oxygen production of the installation (blue line), as well as its capes and volume to ensure various modes of human life (black lines).  The blue dot is the power and rate of oxygen production at MOXIE.  Image source: Pralay Gayen et al. / PNAS Previously, we talked about another method of obtaining oxygen from carbon dioxide in the Martian atmosphere (like MOXIE): scientists proposed to do this using low-temperature plasma.  And what is the role of the Mars Rover “Perseverance ” in addition to checking the method of oxygen production, you can read in our material“ Mars, there and back ”.  Nikita Kozyrev

Title: Scientists have found organisms that can give rise to life on Mars
Content: Scientists have found organisms that can give rise to life on Mars 16.02.2021, 14: 58 They are able to grow and multiply in the conditions of the red planet.  New experiments have shown that cyanobacteria, also known as blue-green algae, can successfully grow in Martian atmospheric conditions.  Of course, a few more ingredients will be needed, but when humans get to Mars, they will be able to create life support systems based on cyanobacteria for the human habitat, writes nv.ua.  "Here we show that cyanobacteria can use the gases available in the Martian atmosphere, at low overall pressure, as a source of carbon and nitrogen," said astrobiologist Cyprien Verso from the University of Bremen in Germany.  "Under these conditions, cyanobacteria retained their ability to grow in water containing only Martian dust, and they could be used to feed other microbes.  This can help make long-term missions to Mars sustainable, ” the authors of the study believe.  All types of cyanobacteria produce oxygen as a byproduct of photosynthesis, and even today they are an invaluable source of it.  For several years, scientists have speculated whether we could use the ability of cyanobacteria to produce oxygen to live on Mars.  This will bring additional benefits.  The atmosphere of Mars consists mainly of carbon dioxide (95 percent) and nitrogen (3 percent), which are fixed by cyanobacteria, turning them into organic compounds and nutrients, respectively.  However, atmospheric pressure on Mars is a big problem.  The total pressure there is less than 1% of Earth ’ s — from 6 to 11 GPa: this is too small for the presence of liquid water, while the partial pressure of gaseous nitrogen — from 0.2 to 0.3 GPa — is not enough for their metabolism.  But recreating the atmosphere, like on Earth, would be too expensive: gases would have to be imported.  So the researchers were looking for a middle ground: an atmosphere close to Martian, which allows cyanobacteria to grow well.  The authors have developed a bioreactor called Atmos, which has an atmospheric pressure of about 10 percent of Earth ’ s, but uses only what can be found on Mars, albeit in inverted proportions: 96 percent nitrogen and 4 percent carbon dioxide.  The bioreactor also included water that can be obtained on Mars from melting ice, which in some places is abundant on the surface, and a simulator of Martian regolith, a mixture of minerals created here on Earth using only what can be found on Mars.  The team chose the type of nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria that preliminary trials showed was most likely to thrive under these conditions, Anabaena sp.  PCC 7938, and tested it in a variety of conditions.  The researchers concluded that nitrogen-fixing, oxygen-producing cyanobacteria can be grown on Mars at low pressure under controlled conditions using exclusively local ingredients.  From cyanobacteria, sugar, amino acids and other nutrients can be obtained to feed other crops, which can then be used for other purposes, such as the production of medicines.  Atmos was designed to test whether cyanobacteria can be grown under certain atmospheric conditions rather than for maximum efficiency, and the parameters of the bioreactor will depend on many factors in the mission to Mars, including the payload and mission architecture.  However, now that the concept has been proven, the team can begin work on optimizing the bioreactor system that could one day save us life on Mars. Title: Test satellite. NASA will test on the moon technology for the colonization of Mars
Content: "If God wanted man to become a cosmic species, he would give him the moon."  The famous German rocket engine engineer Kraft Erike uttered these words in 1984, wanting to emphasize the fact that we can use the moon as a springboard to spread human civilization throughout the rest of the solar system, writes Mit Technology Review.  More than a decade has passed since the last Apollo mission to the moon.  Erike watched NASA and the rest of the U.S. space program retreat from hopes of exploring more distant worlds, such as Mars, and instead focus on orbiting the Earth.  However, at the moment, America is again seeking a return to the moon with the mission “Artemis ”, the ambitious goal of which is to send astronauts by 2024.  But for the White House and NASA, this mission is more than just returning humans to the surface of the moon, as it is also an ideal base for developing a follow-up mission to Mars.  For both directions, the goal is not just to fly to the moon and return to Earth, but to create the necessary conditions for permanent residence so that people can work and develop there.  "We are returning to the moon for scientific discoveries, economic benefits and inspiration for a new generation of research.  As we create sustainable conditions for habitation on the moon, we are also striving for the first steps of man on the red planet, ” said NASA Director Jim Bridenstine on September 21.  However, it is not yet clear how this should all work.  The most important projects that Artemis is supposed to launch — the next generation Space Launch System rocket and the Orion crew capsule — have not yet been completed.  Most experts agree that there is insufficient funding for the program.  Moreover, NASA has not even chosen a lunar lander.  But even if we get to the moon in 2024, where is the guarantee that Mars will colonize next?  “The biggest problem we ’ re facing right now is that we don ’ t know how to live and work productively beyond Earth, ” says Clive Neal, an engineer at the University of Notre Dame and an expert on lunar exploration.  The technologies needed for long-term work in space have never been properly tested.  After all, it is necessary to take into account the harsh Martian conditions, with a lower level of temperature and gravity, with a higher level of radiation, as well as a lack of water and oxygen.  "In our backyard, we have our own lab where we can test these conditions," Neal said.  He and his colleagues recently created a new report released by the human rights group Exlore Mars, which promotes sustainable space exploration.  The report identifies dozens of activities and technologies needed to explore Mars that can be developed and tested with the Artemis mission and ongoing lunar exploration.  Almost immediately after the launch of Artemis 3, it will be possible to test some important things for Mars on the Moon.  Life support is at the top of this list, as humans have never built long-term dwellings on another planet before.  And while researchers will apply much of what they ’ ve learned from long missions to the International Space Station, they still need to make sure that a lunar base and a base on Mars can provide such basic needs as food, water, and shelter.  "I think the key will be to immerse more people in the lunar environment," said Joe Cassady, executive director of space operations at Aerojet Rocketdyne and one of the lead editors of the Explore Mars report.  The important point is to collect experience and data from many different astronauts during missions that will last for months.  This experience will help engineers build habitats, spacesuits and ground transportation systems suitable for humans.  But in order for these habitats to last a long time, you need to build something quite sustainable.  Launch windows for missions to Mars (when the planet is closest to Earth) only appear every 26 months, so any return mission to the Red Planet will take some waiting time.  If the journey takes, say, 273 days, then Mars will have to spend at least three to four months before it becomes possible to go back home.  And there are two options: either take enough food with you to last all these months, or look for extraterrestrial resources.  The first option is unlikely to work.  “It is important to use only local resources.  Trying to take with you everything that can help protect astronauts on Mars, simply will not work, ” said Neil.  Water ice will be a vital resource.  It could supply water and oxygen to life support systems, as well as split into hydrogen and oxygen for use as rocket fuel.  It can also be used as a protection against space radiation and micrometeorite bombardment.  There is a lot of ice on Mars.  According to scientists on the moon, too, which makes it an ideal environment for testing the technologies that are needed to explore these reserves, mine them, clean them up and turn them into something that can help preserve the life support of a future settlement.  "The moon is a more extreme habitat.  And that means that if something works on it, it will work on Mars, ” Neal says.  The presence of water ice also somewhat reinforces the argument for launching a spacecraft propulsion system based on hydrogen rather than methane.  The report says that hydrogen can be produced locally on both worlds, while methane is produced from local resources only on Mars, where an atmosphere saturated with carbon dioxide provides a ready source of carbon.  As a result, any methane production on the moon would require importing a carbon source.  The report also recommends the use of power systems that are not entirely dependent on the sun.  On Mars, with its long distance and dusty atmosphere, solar panels will have a harder time converting sunlight into energy.  Nuclear energy seems to be the most obvious approach.  To ensure the functioning of the shelter on the moon, it will not require too much energy, instead it will be needed to perform the mining work necessary to collect and process water ice.  Mining experts told Neal they were likely to look for systems that could deliver power in the megawatt range.  “It was a wake-up call because people in the planetary world don ’ t have that kind of connection to the mining industry, ” Neal says.  Solar energy in this case will be more of a reserve source of energy than the main one.  The moon is also the best place to simulate a mission to Mars, especially when it comes to Gateway, a planned space station designed for lunar orbit.  In fact, it will serve as a springboard for any NASA missions to the surface of the moon (both with a crew and with robots), as well as for further flights to Mars.  The first three elements of the Gateway (power, propulsion and residential module) are scheduled to be launched in 2023.  In their report, Cassady and colleagues suggested that one approach might be for the crew to stay on the lunar space station Gateway for 60-90 days, simulate a mission to Mars on the surface of the moon for more than 30 days, and then, before returning home, complete another stay on the Gateway for 90 days.  It will be a condensed version of the mission to Mars.  It will mimic the changing microgravity conditions that can be encountered on such a journey, and give astronauts an idea of what a Martian mission might be like.  A new NASA Artemis project says the Gateway-to-Surface operating system is similar to how a mission to Mars can work, with the ability of the crew to stay in orbit and deploy on the surface.  In addition, settling on Mars will be a difficult task if scientists do not develop autonomous systems that do not need careful monitoring.  Ground-based service teams are able to manage objects on the moon almost in real time, but the delay in communication from Earth to Mars can reach 22.4 minutes.  “If there is a disaster on Mars like the one that happened with Apollo 13, there will not be a team of engineers who could diagnose and solve the problem in real time, ” said Casey Dreyer, an expert on space policy at the Planetary Society.  The moon is the only good environment in which it is possible to truly test and improve automated systems that can operate reliably without human control.  There are concerns that the U.S. space program could face a dramatic shift in priorities after the November elections, as has happened in previous years.  But so far, the Democratic Party seems to still be in favor of the mission.  “We support NASA ’ s work to bring Americans back to the moon and reach Mars, taking the next step in exploring our solar system. ”  Dreyer notes that the development of the Space Launch System and Orion is almost complete.  In addition, Gateway enjoys a lot of international support: Europe, Japan, Canada and possibly Russia are ready to play their part in its development.  The new Artemis plan explains better than ever how NASA intends to bring humans back to the moon by 2024, but says very little about how it will meet the technological criteria for a sustainable lunar base that will help get to Mars.  Even at a time when Erica ’ s words are closer than ever to life, it will take us a lot of determination to make the leap from the Moon to the Red Planet.

Title: Life in the Caves!
Content: At the initiative of a Spanish company, tourists can live in a cave that simulates the conditions of life on Mars.  The participants are cut off from the outside world and spend three days and nights at a special station called Ares in a cave located in the Cantabrian Mountains.  The cave is 60 meters high and half a kilometer long.  The programme starts earlier with a three-week distance learning course and three days of practical physical and mental training to learn how to cope in the conditions found in this habitat.  Inside the cave, participants experience what human life on Mars would be like.  David Sabalus, CEO of Astroland, who pioneered the experiment, said: “The Martian environment is very hostile to low temperatures, strong winds and high levels of solar radiation.  For this reason, the expeditions to the Red Planet will have no choice but to survive underground and will be the most suitable way to preserve human life below the surface of Mars.  "We have created the right conditions in this cave to conduct a life experiment on Mars."  The Ares station is equipped with research laboratories, spacesuits, special suits for various missions, living chambers, hydroponics laboratory (hydroponics culture, soil-free plant culture), autonomous systems and independent water production, 3D printers, kitchen, recreation area, gym, emergency bio-assistance equipment, food specifically for each member, etc.  Participants will have to pay around 6,000 euros for the three-day trip. Title: People are preparing for the pollution of Mars - our review
Content: The experiment was conducted on Earth, more precisely, in the stratosphere of our planet.  There, scientists from two space agencies sent a probe with various microorganisms to check how they would behave in the atmosphere of the red planet.  "We successfully tested a new method of placing bacteria and fungi in Martian conditions using a probe sent into the stratosphere," says Marta Filipa Cortezao of DLR.  "Some microbes, especially black mold embryos, were able to survive the journey even after exposure to very high levels of ultraviolet radiation."  Understanding how microorganisms react to space travel and the Martian environment is key to future missions.  One of the motives is that in the search for extraterrestrial life, scientists should be sure that there are no microorganisms brought from Earth.  But there are other threats.  “On long missions to Mars, we need to know that the microorganisms associated with humans would survive on the Red Planet, because some of them can threaten the lives of astronauts, ” says Katarina Zins, one of the main authors of the publication, which appeared in the publication Frontiers in Microbiology.  But such resistant to harsh conditions earthly life forms still harbor additional opportunities.  "Some microbes may be underestimated by us in the exploration of Mars.  But they are able to help us in the production of food and other materials, regardless of the Earth.  This is a key opportunity to survive away from home, ” the expert adds.  According to experts, it is very difficult to reproduce Martian conditions on Earth.  However, this was possible outside the ozone layer.  “We sent microorganisms placed inside the MARSBox (Microbes in Atmosphere for Radiation, Survival and Biological Outcomes experiment), in which both the atmosphere of Mars and the pressure were artificially maintained into the stratosphere during the entire scientific mission, ” explains the essence of the experiment Cortezao.

The most grandiose of them belongs to the American engineer and entrepreneur Elon Musk, who plans to transport a million people to the Red Planet in the coming decades to create an independent civilization.  This idea seems absolutely fantastic – and meanwhile, the company Srace X, led by Mask, announced that very soon will begin the first flights of its space shuttles.  Go to the Red Planet!  At the International Astronomical Congress held in September 2016 in Mexico, the report of the engineer and entrepreneur made a real sensation.  According to Elon Musk, only the resettlement of a significant part of earthlings to Mars will save humanity from possible extinction.  Life on our planet can be interrupted by many factors: the explosion of a nearby supernova, superflares on the Sun, falling into a black hole, a global epidemic, a collision with a huge asteroid, a man-made disaster.  A large colony of people on another planet will ensure the continued existence of terrestrial civilization.  Why choose Mars?  Compared to other celestial bodies of the solar system, it is better suited for the possible life of earthlings.  The day here lasts 24 hours 37 minutes - that is, suitable for our residents and plants.  Gravity is much smaller than the earth, but is quite suitable for the normal functioning of the human body.  Finally, there is water – albeit in the form of polar ice caps, but it can be easily reached, and pieces of ice melt and use.  The rest of the planets of the solar system are practically unsuitable for such a mission: Mercury has extremely high surface temperatures during the day and very low at night, Venus has a too aggressive atmosphere, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune are mostly composed of liquefied gas.  The closest suitable celestial body to us is the Moon, but it depends entirely on the Earth and in the event of a space disaster may die with it.  Why is the number of one million people chosen?  According to experts, this is the minimum number of people so that their colony can become completely independent and develop.  It will have specialists of all the necessary professions, it will cope with possible diseases and epidemics, as well as ensure a stable natural population growth.  At first, the colonists will face the most difficult task - to turn the Red Planet into their home.  The set of actions to achieve this goal, Maek called the term “terraforming ” – that is, changing the conditions of life on another planet in such a way that they resemble earthly ones.  First of all, you need to melt a sufficient amount of ice at the south pole of the planet, since it will turn to the Sun in the summer, which means that it will be easier to do this than at the north pole.  The water accumulated here is enough to create an ocean several meters deep on the planet.  As the ice cap decreases, a chain reaction will begin - water vapor will begin to compact the atmosphere, which, in turn, will retain more solar heat, due to which the melting process will be more intense.  Technically, it can be launched using nuclear charges or placing laser devices over the south pole of Mars.  After liquid water appears on the planet, you need to start planting plants: initially it will be mosses, but later - vast forests that will saturate the atmosphere of Mars with oxygen (now it is 95% carbon dioxide).  According to Musk, the cultivation of “green lungs ” and the creation of a livable air without spacesuits will take from 300 to 1000 years.  But after that, the Red Planet can be considered terraformed, and people will choose where they live - on Mars or on Earth.  100 thousand flights Elon Maek listed the things and equipment that the first colonists needed.  First of all, these are devices for the production and conversion of energy - nuclear or space.  The most promising direction, the researchers of the company Srace X consider the delivery to Mars of a large number of light folding solar panels.  It will also require a huge amount of plants, both to create oxygen and to supply the settlers with food.  Until the atmosphere of the planet is formed properly, earthlings will need means of protection from solar radiation - after all, until this time, Martian cities will have to be under special domes.  First, the settlers will build small houses, then they will equip complexes, where there will be not only housing, but also schools, hospitals, shops, etc.  Experts Srace X calculated: one flight with the colonists should account for nine flights with payload.  It is based on a ship capable of carrying 100 passengers.  Thus, the total number of flights required to create a million colony on the Red Planet will be about 100 thousand (10 thousand - passenger flights, 90 thousand - cargo).  Elon Maek has already announced that the first expeditions for the delivery of goods should begin at the end of 2022.  By 2035, spacecraft will be built capable of reaching the Red Planet in 80 days, and a million colonists will arrive on Mars within the next few decades.  The main obstacle to the implementation of such a large-scale project, according to Musk and his team, is the high cost of a flight to the Red Planet.  In fact, it is steadily declining.  In 1989, the US national aerospace agency YABA estimated sending astronauts to Mars at $450 billion.  It was assumed that there will be from four to six earthlings — that is, each place was estimated at about $100 billion.  But already in 2004, the same agency reduced the cost of the project nine times — to $50 billion.  Thus, the flight of one person would cost a little more than 10 billion dollars.  This figure is still too high, but the trend towards its decline is clearly visible, and therefore such a task can be solved.  Elon Maek believes that the optimal amount for a flight of one person should be 500 thousand dollars – this is the approximate cost of a middle-class house in a good place.  Moreover, people should understand that they will become real space pioneers, the first permanent residents of another planet – and therefore must pay for their flight themselves.  Opinions of economists and psychologists are unambiguous: only in the United States there are at least a million people who will agree to pay such money for an unprecedented space travel.  But how to reduce the cost of flying each person from 10 billion to 500 thousand dollars, that is, 20 thousand times?  Elon Mayek knows the answer to that question.  Rocket from a private company Team plan Srace X works in two directions.  The first of these is the creation of spacecraft, each of which will be able to carry at least 100 people.  The company Ilona Mask has a successful experience in the construction of devices of a new type.  The engineer and entrepreneur himself says that the huge cost of missiles is primarily a consequence of the lack of competition and the presence of a huge number of subcontractors.  NASA constantly entrusts the execution of its orders only to a few companies.  For example, ULA (United Launch Alliance), a joint venture owned by Boeing and Lockheed Martin, regularly performs missions of the space agency and the US Department of Defense, but at the same time receives more for each launch than anyone else in the world.  Under the pretext of national security, the system of government orders in this area is completely opaque, and the task of many companies is not to reduce the cost of the spacecraft, but to make it more expensive for their own benefit.  In turn, having received the order, large companies transfer it in parts to small subcontractors, who also inflate prices.  But the main thing is that in the absence of competition, there is no need to invent something new!  As a result, the technology of modern spacecraft at best dates back to the 1990s, and the costs of their production and launch are declining extremely slowly.  SpaceX was the first company to start working on a fundamentally different scheme.  Not fulfilling an order, but creating your own device, cheaper and more reliable, which can then be offered to space agencies and organizations.  The company was founded in 2002 with the personal funds of Elon Musk, received from the development and operation of the largest electronic payment system in the United States.  The company created its first rocket, called the Falcon 1 (translated from English “falcon ”).  The two-stage vehicle and its engine were made by Space X workers without the help of intermediaries.  The first three launches ended in accidents.  But the fourth flight, which took place in 2008, was successful.  A cargo detachment simulation was conducted (it remained in the rocket so as not to increase the amount of space debris), and the first stage made a safe landing. Title: NASA's $2.5 billion mission aims to find signs of life on Mars
Content: NASA ’ s mission to search for signs of life on Mars will involve a new generation of rover that explores the delta of the river age of 3.5 billion years.  Susan Carlin of the Fast Company visited the "clean room" (hall for assembling precision instruments, in which air quality is strictly controlled - approx. ed.)  NASA ’ s Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) and found out how the development of a new spacecraft is progressing.  JPL ’ s “Clean Room ” is similar to the television room in Willie Wonka and the Chocolate Factory: it ’ s a flawlessly clean room where people in white jumpsuits and masks engage in technological magic.  But instead of a camera that turns children into miniature figures, the centerpiece here is the new Mars 2020 rover that NASA plans to send to Mars this summer.  Although Mars 2020 does not pose the same challenge to the laws of physics as the Wonka camera, it is no less magical for one good reason: this device may finally answer the question of whether there was life on Mars.  Journalists are interviewing engineers working on the Mars 2020 mission.  The photo was taken in JPL ’ s “clean room ” on December 27, 2019.  Photo: NASA / JPL-Caltech In the last days of 2019, JPL, located in Pasadena, California, provided journalists with a rare opportunity to see High Bay 1, a spacious “clean room ” with a constant online broadcast, where NASA engineers are designing the Mars 2020 rover, as well as systems for descent to the planet and a seven-month journey on it.  Strict control of temperature, humidity and working processes in this room minimizes biological pollution, as well as the amount of dust and particulate matter that can interfere with electronics.  It requires strict rules for guests.  Before entering the “clean room ” we put on“ bunny suits ” – white polyester overalls, boots and hoods, as well as surgical masks and latex gloves glued to the sleeves.  We are also led through the cabin, where strong air currents remove microscopic debris from workwear.  It is not allowed to have cosmetics, perfumes, clothes made of wool and with torn edges, as well as fabric straps on cameras.  At the very door of technology wipe cameras and smartphones with alcohol.  JPL employees can only use unscented shampoos and one type of deodorant, and taking a shower before entering the “clean room ” is prohibited.  Even the High Bay Bob clean room mascot, a mannequin wearing bright green Christmas style sunglasses, wears a white protective suit.  “We don ’ t want to send a spacecraft to Mars and then say, ‘ Hey, there ’ s my hair. ’  All the rules about what you can ’ t do or bring with you are designed to protect the scientific component of this mission, ” said David Gruel, Mars 2020 Assembly, Testing and Launch Manager.  In search of life, Mars 2020, which JPL began building in 2011, will be the first rover to search for evidence that microorganisms lived on Mars in the past.  It will be engaged in drilling, analysis and collection of geological samples from areas that previously could have been inhabited.  It is assumed that future missions will return them to Earth in 2026 for more detailed study.  The launch of Mars 2020 is the first step towards a goal that JPL began discussing back in the 1980s and which eventually became a campaign to obtain geological samples from Mars.  After studying them, some important questions will be answered in the laboratory.  “Could life have formed on Mars, did it happen, and if not, why? ” — quotes the Director of JPL Michael Watkins.  The $2.5 billion project will also test the technologies humans will need for a long-term stay on Mars.  These include tools that improve landing, produce oxygen from Martian air rich in carbon dioxide, determine the composition of soil and groundwater, and record weather conditions.  Among the projects, there is even a small solar-powered helicopter, which is designed for flights taking into account the Martian atmosphere and reduced gravity.  This spring, NASA will announce the official name of Mars 2020, selected from more than 9 million options.  The rover will be launched from Cape Canaveral in Florida during the July-August window, landing on Mars is scheduled for February 8, 2021.  The device will begin its journey around the planet from the crater Jezero, the basin of an ancient lake, where in the past there was a high probability of life.  The mission will last at least one Martian year (approximately 687 Earth days) and cover up to 12 miles (more than 19 km).  One of the most serious problems in the operation of the “clean room ” is the danger of particulate pollution, and the other is the protection of highly sensitive electronics.  Special tape barriers keep reporters a short distance from mechanics to prevent accidental electrostatic discharges.  "The human body is made up of so much water that it is able to conduct electricity.  Electric shock from walking on the carpet and touching the door handle is about 20 thousand volts.  You can damage some of these high-speed electronic devices using just five volts.  We reduce this risk by controlling electrostatic discharge, ” said James Sean Howard, Head of Equipment Inspection at Mars 2020.  To do this, the equipment is surrounded by air ionizers, which neutralize static electricity, filling the air with positively and negatively charged ions.  The “clean room ” also maintains a humidity level above 30%, which makes the air more conductive and allows it to absorb and distribute excess charges.  When engineers work on mechanics, they connect special bracelets to a wire that returns electricity to the ground to prevent sparks.  Protective suits also contain carbon elements to relieve static stress from the fabric.  Faraday cells and electrostatic discharge needles — metal spikes on the outer surface of the rover — will protect electronics on Mars.  Another significant obstacle is the complexity of the instruments and moving parts, many of which the rover displays only after landing.  It uses more than 30 systems that control moving elements.  “Each of these mechanisms, gearboxes and engines is made up of hundreds of small parts, and they all have to be designed, analyzed, assembled and tested.  It ’ s hard to make them super reliable.  And, of course, there is no way to fix them on Mars, ” said Matt Wallace, deputy project manager for Mars 2020.  An engineering model of the Mars 2020 rover is being tested on Mars Yard, an area that mimics Martian conditions.  Photo: NASA / JPL-Caltech Protecting a system from Earth pollution that will place samples of Martian soil in test tubes is especially important.  "The front third of the rover is equipped with a mechanism similar to a Swiss watch, which takes a sample from a robotic arm, evaluates it and seals it tightly in a test tube.  To work on this equipment, a second set of sterile gloves was required, ” says engineer Zach Ousnamer.  The Mars 2020 rover borrowed a lot from Curiosity, while developing new technologies.  It is slightly larger than Curiosity: its length is 10 feet (about 3 m, not including a folding 9-foot robotic arm), width is 9 feet (about 2.7 m), height is 7 feet (about 2.1 m) and weight is 2,314 pounds (more than a ton).  Like Curiosity, Mars 2020 is powered by a combination of nuclear, battery and solar energy.  Its six aluminum wheels have a stronger construction and coating to avoid dents, holes and broken treads that interfered with Curiosity.  The Mars 2020 descent and landing system will repeat the stunning decline of Curiosity, known from the video “Seven Minutes of Horror ”.  Mars 2020 will travel to Mars in a protective airshell consisting of an upper skin and a lower heat-shielding shield.  A circular descent stage with eight brake rockets will be attached to the rover like a jet backpack that will drop it to the surface of the planet.  A few minutes before that, the parachute on the top of the airshell will slow the descent of the device until the need for a heat-shielding screen disappears and it comes off.  At this point, the descent stage will detach from the upper skin, release brake missiles towards the surface of Mars to slow down the descent, and ensure a careful landing of the rover.  Then it will detach, fly away and fall at some distance.  This time, several new onboard technologies will provide more controlled descent maneuvering, accurate landing, and data collection for future missions.  The device will also include a set of cameras and microphones to view what is happening in the first person and listen to the sounds of the landing.  The sensors will measure the temperature of the upper skin and the lower heat shield.  One navigation system will control the descent, focusing on the time of deployment of the parachute and the position of the spacecraft relative to the descent point.  The second will help land, highlighting the dangerous terrain during the descent by comparing fresh images of the approaching surface with a pre-loaded map of Mars.  Once on the surface of Mars, seven instruments — selected from 58 proposals around the world and including the development of the French, Spanish and Norwegian — will conduct a geological assessment of the area in which the rover descended to try to detect signs of ancient Martian life. Title: Colonizing other planets? They have to be remade first.
Content: Is it time to colonize other planets?  The population of the Earth is rapidly increasing, and soon humanity will be on the planet closely.  Futurists view the colonization of the solar system as the most likely scenario for the future.  It is possible that people will have to deal with terraforming - engineering change of other worlds.  In September 2015, speaking in one of the humorous television shows, Elon Musk proposed to bomb the poles of Mars with nuclear warheads.  In his opinion, this will allow you to quickly evaporate from the surface of the planet dry ice from carbon dioxide.  Of course, Musk was joking.  There simply aren ’ t enough nuclear weapons on Earth to make the Tesla founder ’ s plan work.  Scientists suggest heating the surface of the red planet in other ways.  For example, to push Mars against an asteroid or use a huge orbital mirror that would concentrate solar energy and direct it to the Martian polar ice caps.  However, at the current level of technology development, it is almost impossible to implement all these scenarios.  In addition, efforts to turn Mars into a planet suitable for life, may be in vain, scientists from the University of Colorado.  After analyzing the data obtained by the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter and Mars Odyssey, they concluded that there is not enough carbon dioxide in the rocks and polar caps on the Red Planet to form a dense atmosphere.  However, Elon Musk, who dreams of building a colony on Mars, believes that a huge amount of carbon dioxide is absorbed in the Martian soil.  When the planet is heated, a powerful release of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere will occur, and this will start the process of terraforming - the transformation of Mars into the likeness of Earth.  To create an atmosphere on Venus, Venus, on the contrary, requires cooling.  The average temperature at its surface is about 452 degrees Celsius, and the pressure is about 90 bar.  Otherwise, in terms of mass, gravity and solar radiation, Venus resembles Earth.  Moreover, according to calculations of scientists from the Goddard Space Research Institute, about two billion years ago, the climate of Venus was similar to that of Earth.  There were liquid oceans on the planet, the temperature was comfortable 15-17 degrees Celsius.  Carl Sagan proposed to sow cyanobacteria in the atmosphere of Venus.  Through photosynthesis, they will convert carbon dioxide into organic matter and release oxygen.  However, whether the bacteria themselves will survive in harsh Venusian conditions is unclear.  In addition, according to physicist Martin Fogg, the process of converting carbon dioxide into organic matter would take about a million years.  A faster way to make Venus habitable is to let a lot of hydrogen into the atmosphere so that all the carbon dioxide it contains turns into graphite and water.  As a catalyst, iron filings can be sprayed over the planet.  It is believed that as a result, the pressure will drop to three bar, the greenhouse effect will disappear, and water will appear on the surface.  In the most favorable scenario, it will cover up to 80 percent of the planet.  However, as noted by the staff of the John Glenn Research Center (NASA), all these methods will not help, if you do not deal with the main problems: sulfuric acid clouds and too long a sunny day, equal to 117 Earth days.  If you figure out how to get rid of these troubles, Venus is quite suitable for terraforming.  It is logical to make a habitable moon much closer to us.  According to American and British scientists, in the past it could have been inhabited.  Now the satellite of the Earth is not the most hospitable place.  The temperature there ranges from minus 180 to plus 120 degrees Celsius.  There is no magnetic field of its own, and therefore cosmic radiation sterilizes the surface.  The atmosphere is so thin that it actually does not exist, which means that the threat of falling meteorites is constantly preserved.  But on the moon there is one of the main conditions of terraforming - water in the form of "icy permafrost" near the poles.  In 2012, the place of its occurrence was studied by the Russian neutron telescope LEND, which is on board the American probe LRO.  The problem with the retention of the atmosphere and the delivery to the moon of volatile elements necessary for life (hydrogen, nitrogen and carbon), most often proposed to solve with the help of comets.  It is believed that these objects, when they collide with the Moon, will dissipate gases and water vapor, thus creating an atmosphere.  The impacts will also release the water contained in the lunar regolith and form natural bodies of water on the surface.  The transmission of the same momentum from comets will accelerate the rotation of the moon, which will contribute to the retention of the atmosphere.  But bombardment of the moon by space objects can touch the Earth tangentially.  A safer option is to make only a small part of the satellite habitable.  Researchers from NASA propose to create in the crater Shackleton, in which a few years ago discovered water ice, a microclimate to grow plants and was suitable for breathing atmosphere.  At first, robots will do this: they will erect a dome and install solar mirrors.

Title: A hole under the Chinese rover has been discovered.
Content: China ’ s National Space Administration (CNSA) released new images of the Zhurong rover on Saturday.  The images were interesting in themselves, but an aerospace reporter discovered something interesting about them.  He noticed a large hole beneath the rover.  Jonathan O'Callaghan tweeted: "The crater that the Chinese rover created when it landed on the Red Planet's surface is very interesting.  Phil Metzger, a planetary scientist at the University of Central Florida, responded to the tweet and said it was not a good thing.  He added: “This is a new hole.  Look at its edges and imagine a 40-ton probe on top of it and how big the hole could be.  The crater is likely to collapse, especially in the coming weeks when the soil dries up and falls off the base of the probe.  The researcher explained how falling soil beneath the probe's foundations causes it to tilt, and this is just one of the dangers of landing large probes on the soft soil of Mars.  The second risk is that the material will collide with the probe, because the fuel will come out of the hole before it is cut off, and the third risk is that it will collide with other hardware around it.  China ’ s National Space Administration (CNSA) on Saturday released a selfie taken on the Red Planet by the Mars Rover Jurong. Title: Secrets of the Fourth Planet
Content: 2050.  Humanity has finally become an interplanetary species, establishing a colony on Mars that is home to about a million people — more than Amsterdam or Athens.  This is not the beginning of a new science fiction novel or the plot of the film.  This is a vision of the future that Elon Musk recently shared.  The entrepreneur often paints the most fantastic scenarios, but one cannot blame him: it is not only him who is drawn to Mars.  Unfriendly neighbor Mars is not the most hospitable world, if you compare it with the Earth.  The force of gravity here is only 37.5% of the earth ’ s.  The temperature on the surface ranges from freezing -153 ° C to comfortable + 20 ° C.  However, a thin, unsuitable for humans atmosphere, consisting mainly of carbon dioxide, nitrogen and argon, is not able to effectively trap heat from sunlight.  If you were standing on the Martian equator at noon, your feet would have a temperature of + 24 ° C and your head would have a temperature of 0 ° C.  In addition, the pressure on the red planet is much lower – even at the top of Everest on Earth, it is 50 times greater than on the surface of Mars.  However, these worlds have a lot in common.  Beneath our feet is solid land, the area of which is comparable to the land area on our planet, although Mars is about half its size.  The duration of the day, which is called soles, is 24.6 hours, and close to the Earth's angle of inclination of the axis of rotation (23.5 for the Earth and 25.2 for Mars) provides the world with pronounced seasons, which, however, last longer than ours.  For example, spring in the northern hemisphere lasts as much as 194 solas - this is the longest season on the planet.  But the main similarity of the planets remains in the distant past.  Numerous evidence points to the fact that Mars used to be warmer, had a denser atmosphere, and its surface was covered with water - the cradle of intelligent life on our home planet.  That ’ s why researchers are looking so closely at this harsh world.  The chances of life on Mars are slim.  For example, in 2018, a group of European scientists found signs of the existence of a liquid lake hidden 1.5 km below the surface of the southern polar glacier.  Microbes may exist in such a reservoir, but this is only a hypothesis that is difficult to test.  Therefore, scientists rely on the search for signs of the existence of a past life.  It may not sound so exciting, but even such a find will be colossal.  Otherwise, we will face a much larger scientific mystery: why the Earth gave life, and the neighboring world with the right conditions - not.  The race for Martian life began in the 19th century.  In 1877, the Italian astronomer Giovanni Schiaparelli looked through the telescope Mars, which no one imagined, and even made a map.  It depicted seas and continents, as well as an extensive network of lines, which the astronomer called channels.  The word itself prompted the idea of ​ ​ the man-made origin of these objects.  It was later established that the channels were an optical illusion, but the idea of the existence of the Martian civilization that built them was picked up by others.  Astronomers such as American Percival Lowell or Frenchman Camille Flammarion believed in the habitability of the Red Planet, and science fiction writers such as Edgar Burroughs and H.G. Wells.  Of course, this theory was not accepted by everyone, but it was not possible to test it for a long time.  That all changed in the 1950s.  After the launch of the first Soviet satellite in 1957 and the start of the space race, the views of the USSR and the United States quickly rushed beyond the Earth ’ s orbit and even the Moon.  Already in the 1960s, the first automatic interplanetary stations rushed to the Red Planet.  No one thought about landing or orbiters at that time.  AMS sent to other worlds had to fly by, trying to take as many pictures as possible and send them to Earth.  But this task was not easy either.  The first attempt to send a research apparatus to the Red Planet was made by the Soviet Union in 1960, but it, like many others after it, failed.  Soviet devices died, not having time to leave the orbit of the Earth, at best broke down in flight to Mars.  In 1964, NASA entered the game, but its debut was unsuccessful.  The second attempt was successful.  Mariner 4 arrived safely on Mars in 1965.  It flew about 10 thousand km above the surface of the planet and sent 22 photos to Earth.  These were the first images of Mars from such a short distance.  There were no channels on them, but scientists saw the craters decorating the Martian earth, and confirmed that the atmosphere of the planet consists of carbon dioxide.  NASA has been successful ever since.  Until the end of the decade, the agency launched two more AMS, which managed to take two hundred photos, as well as carry out measurements of the surface and temperature of Mars.  The first spacecraft to make a soft landing on Mars was the Soviet Mars-3, but on the surface it worked for a few seconds The Soviet Union caught up with the Americans only in 1971, but by that time the ambitions of local scientists and engineers had grown.  Just flying over the surface wasn ’ t enough.  In 1971, the Soviet Union sent to the Red Planet at once two AMS - "Mars-2" and "Mars-3", which included both orbiters and lander.  These missions have been successful.  Orbiters have been orbiting the planet for months, transmitting data.  As for the landers, one crashed during the landing, and the second successfully inscribed his name in history.  "Mars-3" was the first device to make a soft landing on the red planet, even if it worked in a matter of seconds.  1971 proved to be a fruitful year for the study of the fourth planet.  That year, the American orbiter Mariner 9 arrived, which not only took thousands of photos and made a map of 85% of its surface, but also helped to see the main attractions of Mars.  For example, data from Mariner 9 helped establish the height of Olympus, the tallest volcano in the solar system, which rises 25 km and the diameter of the base is 600 km.  And the NASA research apparatus helped to estimate the scale of the Mariner Valley - the famous system of canyons, which stretches for 4 thousand km along the Martian equator and crashes 7 km deep into the surface of the planet.  The system, named after the probe, is four times deeper and five times longer than the Grand Canyon on Earth.  The next breakthrough in the study of Mars was made only in 1976, when NASA delivered there two AMS - "Viking 1" and "Viking 2".  Like the Soviet Mars, they were equipped with orbiters and landers, but the Vikings were more successful.  They successfully placed in orbit and landed on the surface of the planet, having worked for more than one year.  The Viking 1 lander fell silent only in 1982, and even then after an erroneous command from Earth.  During this time, they replenished the Martian photo archive with tens of thousands of images, but most importantly - they conducted the first field experiments to search for traces of life.  Alas, they did not give a convincing "yes" or a definite "no", but still it was a breakthrough, since previously Mars was studied on the principle of "look, but do not touch".  "Vikings" involuntarily added fuel to the fire of the myth of the Martian civilization, when one of the orbiters sent a curious picture.  It showed a pile of stones, one of which was strikingly reminiscent of a human face.  NASA researchers immediately realized that this is a game of light and shadow, but the impressionable public began to build theories about the remains of an ancient Martian city that rests underground.  The tradition of looking for the usual forms in photos of the Red Planet is still alive today, and those who want to constantly find rodents and insects in the pictures.  But these are just illusions.  Face on Mars.  This image, taken in the AMC "Viking 1" 1976, refreshed the myth of the existence of a developed Martian civilization After the "Vikings" study of the red planet for many years stalled.  For two decades, the US and the USSR, and subsequently Russia, continued to send mechanical researchers, but the attempts were mostly unsuccessful.  A new breakthrough occurred in the second half of the 1990s.  In 1997, NASA delivered the Mars Global Surveyor orbiter to Mars, which helped make a revolutionary discovery: somewhere under the surface of a dead planet, water can still flow, the hunt for which continues to this day.  In the same year, the Pathfinder landed on the surface, which has not happened since the time of the Vikings.  But much more interesting was the cargo that Pathfinder brought with him.  With him on the planet arrived the first mobile research apparatus Sojourner, able to move on

As the government and business sectors recently asked the government to pardon Li, he appeared in court again on Thursday (22) on charges of fraud and stock price manipulation, the first appearance of the company after about three months. Russia plans to withdraw from the International Space Station from 2025, space agency chief Dmitry Rogozin said on Wednesday, with President Vladimir Putin's approval, Russia will build its own space station and hopes to put it into orbit by 2030, a plan that reportedly costs $6 billion (about HK $46.6 billion).  If successful, it will open a new chapter in Russia ’ s space exploration and end more than two decades of U.S.-Russian cooperation on the International Space Station.  Russian Deputy Prime Minister Yuri Borisov told Russian television last weekend that Moscow would notify its partners to leave the International Space Station from 2025.  Russia ’ s Interfax news agency reported that Rogozin said it plans to put the space station into orbit by 2030, and unlike the International Space Station, it is likely that there will not be permanent members of the Russian space station, because the space station ’ s orbit will expose the astronauts to high radiation, but Russian astronauts can go, and the space station will also use artificial intelligence and robots.  He added that Russia is ready to consider allowing foreign space visitors, “but the space station must be national … If you want to do things well, you have to do it yourself. ”  Since 1998, Russian cosmonauts have cooperated with astronauts from the United States and 16 other countries on missions to the International Space Station, one of the areas in which Moscow has worked closely with Washington.  However, the US-Russian relationship is in crisis due to issues such as human rights and hacking.  NASA ’ s Perseverance successfully extracted oxygen from the Martian atmosphere The recent mission of the Mars rover Perseverance successfully converted carbon dioxide from the Martian atmosphere into breathable pure oxygen, NASA said on Wednesday.  NASA said that the device, called MOXIE (Mars Oxygen In-Situ Resource Utilization Experiment), is the size of a toaster, and uses extreme heat to separate oxygen atoms from carbon dioxide molecules through electrolysis work. MOXIE successfully generated about 5 grams of oxygen, which can allow an astronaut to breathe for 10 minutes.  This feat marks the first time humans have extracted natural resources available for human use from the environment of another planet.  Oxygen content in the Martian atmosphere is extremely low, carbon dioxide accounts for 95% of the Martian atmosphere, and the rest is mainly composed of molecular nitrogen and argon.  Adequate oxygen supply is key to human exploration of Mars, experts believe that astronauts living and working on Mars may need 1 ton of oxygen to maintain their needs for a year, and believe that it is more practical to convert oxygen on Mars than to transport 25 tons of oxygen from Earth.  MOXIE ’ s operating concept is to produce 10 grams of oxygen per hour.  NASA says scientists plan to run the MOXIE device at least nine more times over the next two years, under different conditions and at different speeds. Title: Revealed the mystery of the mysterious Martian “spiders ”
Content: Planetary scientists have successfully recreated the famous Martian "spiders" in the laboratory - these huge figures on the surface of the Red Planet have repeatedly come across scientists in satellite images.  The structure similar to spiders was removed at the south pole of Mars by the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter.  Their size sometimes reaches a kilometer, writes Live Science.  Researchers have long puzzled over the nature of such objects.  As a result, scientists were able to experimentally prove that arachnids on the surface are traces of carbon dioxide vapor escape from cracks in the polar ice.  During the experiments, experts took plates of dry ice and simulated the Martian atmosphere and the soil of the red planet.  After that, they began to raise and lower the plates on the ground - when the cold ice touched the warmer soil, it instantly turned into gas.  This process is called sublimation, it is widespread on Earth.  Patterns in the form of spiders appear during the direct conversion of dry ice from solid to gas.  At the same time, on Mars, this process is especially active in the spring, when the soil is heated by the Sun especially strongly.
