Title: Martian organics formed thanks to natural batteries
Content: Scientists seem to have uncovered the secret of the origin of organic matter in meteorites that came from the Red Planet.  The list of participants in the process sounds like this: water, volcanic rocks, electricity.  What is nice is that such processes can take place on many bodies of the solar system.  Scientists seem to have uncovered the secret of the origin of organic matter in meteorites that came from the Red Planet.  The formation of organic matter occurs due to natural “accumulators ” consisting of water, salts and volcanic rocks.  Such conclusions are made in a scientific article published in the journal Science Advanced by a group led by Andrew Steele (Andrew Steele) from the Carnegie Scientific Institute in the USA.Recall that proteins, fats, carbohydrates, DNA, RNA and many other molecules, without which it is impossible to imagine a living organism, belong to organic substances.  Of course, not all organic matter is an integral part of living beings or is formed with their participation, so it is not necessary to equate organic matter with life. However, the presence of such molecules is the most important condition for the appearance of the biosphere.  Apparently, only organic chemistry can provide the variety, flexibility and complexity of chemical processes that are necessary for the existence of even the most primitive microbe.  In 2012, a team led by Steele studied carbon from organic molecules found in ten Martian meteorites.  The researchers came to two conclusions, pleasant and not so.  The good news is that this organics originated on Mars (rather than being brought in by pollution on Earth).  The bad news: it is not a product of the vital activity of living organisms; how was it formed in this case?  This is what the authors of a recent study found out. "Identification of the processes during which organic carbon compounds are formed on Mars is of great interest to determine its habitability potential," says Steel.Scientists used three samples of Martian meteorites.  The first is Tissint, which fell in Morocco in 2011.  The second is Nakhla, discovered in Egypt in 1911.  The third was NWA 1950, found in Morocco in 2001.  In all these celestial stones previously found inclusions of Martian organics.Meteorites were subjected to the most careful analysis.  Among the methods used were both the usual viewing of the sample in an optical microscope, and Raman spectroscopy, translucent electron microscopy, nanoscale mass spectrometry of secondary ions, X-ray absorption near the absorption edge (X-ray absorption near-edge structure) and other methods with names incomprehensible to the average person. Thanks to all these methods, the authors thoroughly studied the chemical composition and fine structure of organic inclusions and the surrounding rocks.  By the way, it turned out that the organics of meteorites are extremely similar to the substances found on the Red Planet by the MSL mission.  The detailed information obtained allowed scientists to draw conclusions about what processes could lead to the formation of these substances. It turned out that one of the necessary ingredients are volcanic minerals such as spinel.  On the Red Planet, rich in ancient volcanoes, there is no shortage of such material.  The second important component is liquid water, in huge concentrations containing various salts (in particular, perchlorates).  Such brines have never been directly detected on Mars, but, according to experts, they can exist there almost everywhere.  Finally, the third element of the “magic potion ” is carbon dioxide.  It is also, to put it mildly, not in deficit: the Martian atmosphere consists of it almost completely.  For a while, there is something like a natural battery.  As a result, organic compounds are formed from carbon CO2 and hydrogen of water. "The discovery that a natural system can essentially form a small battery based on corrosion, which controls electrochemical reactions between minerals and the surrounding liquid, has serious consequences for astrobiology," says Steele. Indeed, it turned out that the synthesis of organic matter does not need exotic conditions or components.  All the necessary ingredients are quite common for Mars, which is either already proven (volcanic minerals and carbon dioxide), or assumed (brines).  Moreover, a similar process can take place on bodies such as Europa or Enceladus.  Recall that earlier "33Live.RuNauka" (nauka.vesti.ru) wrote about how a record amount of organic matter was discovered on Mars, as well as that life in the crust of the planet could be supported by radiation.

Title: Found organisms that can survive on Mars
Content: Scientists at the University of Bremen in Germany have found microorganisms that can grow and develop in the Martian atmosphere.  According to the researchers, based on cyanobacteria or blue-green algae, it is possible to create life support systems for people who will live on the surface of Mars.  This is reported in an article published in the journal Frontiers in Microbiology.  Scientists have shown that cyanobacteria can support life by using the gases of the Martian atmosphere as a source of carbon and oxygen, despite the low pressure.  Blue-green algae multiplied in water with a suspension of Martian dust, which makes it possible to use them to feed other living organisms.  In addition, cyanobacteria produce oxygen as a byproduct of photosynthesis.  Researchers have developed an Atmos bioreactor that maintains atmospheric pressure at 10 percent of Earth ’ s and nitrogen and carbon dioxide concentrations of 96 percent and 4 percent, respectively.  These conditions are close to Martian, but differ from them: atmospheric pressure is a percentage of Earth's, and the proportion of carbon dioxide is 95 percent.  Water and a mixture of minerals mimicking Martian regolith were also added to the bioreactor.  For the experiment, the team chose a species of nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria Anabaena sp.  PCC 7938, which preliminary tests have shown is most likely to thrive in these conditions.  Although the bacteria grew better on a nutrient medium, the researchers also observed growth on Martian regolith.  Then the scientists dried the culture of microorganisms and used it as a substrate for growing E. coli.  This proves that cyanobacteria on Mars can be used to feed crops that, in turn, are suitable for the synthesis of nutrients, including drugs.  Leonid Nemov

Title: Converting Martian salt water into oxygen and fuel with a new technology
Content: New technology allows astronauts to convert Martian saltwater into oxygen and fuel when they land on the Red Planet in 2033.  There is water on Mars, but most of it is frozen, and the rest is mixed with salt, making it useless for future astronauts who plan to land on the planet by 2033.  Now, a team of researchers at Washington University in St. Louis has developed a system that converts unusable water into fuel and oxygen.  The system uses electricity to convert saltwater into oxygen and hydrogen, and has been found to work in the Martian atmosphere at temperatures as low as -33 degrees Fahrenheit.  The saltwater electrolyser produces 25 times more oxygen than NASA ’ s MOXIE, which launched in July 2020 with the Mars 2020 rover and aims to produce a small amount of oxygen on Mars.  Vijay Ramani of the University of Washington said the technology is just as useful on Earth as it is on Mars because it can turn the oceans into a source of oxygen and fuel.  According to Inverse, the device has two parts around it, one of which separates water to form hydroxyl ions and the other separates water again to produce oxygen.  Although the technology is currently being developed on Earth, it is expensive and likely will not be able to withstand the freezing temperatures of Mars.  Ramani and other researchers decided to build a portable version of the technology that could operate on the Red Planet continuously without the need to heat or purify the water source.  Research scientist and first author of the study, Shrihari Sankarasubramanian, said: “Water-soluble perchlorates (so-called impurities) are actually functional in a Mars-like environment because they prevent water from freezing and also improve the performance of the electrolaser system by reducing electrical resistance.  The study is based on data from NASA ’ s Phoenix Mars Lander, which touched Mars in 2008.  Scientists know that in order to live on Mars, even temporarily, astronauts would have to produce some of their needs, especially oxygen for breathing and fuel for travel to Earth or beyond on the Red Planet.  NASA's Mars Endurance rover is currently traveling to Mars by carrying instruments that use electrolysis at high temperatures.  The researchers hope to work with NASA to further develop the system in the future.  End of message.

Title: New technology turns Martian salt water into usable fuel and oxygen
Content: According to past research, there is water on Mars, but most of it is frozen and the rest is combined with salt and cannot be used as a supply for astronauts who will visit Mars in 2033.  However, Ars Technica recently reported that a team at Washington University in St. Louis has developed a new technology that uses electricity to break down salt water into oxygen and hydrogen, convert it into usable fuel and oxygen, and can operate in the minus 36 degrees Celsius Martian atmosphere.  The device also produces 25 times more oxygen than NASA ’ s Mars Oxygen ISRU Experiment in July.  Scientists earlier discovered that astronauts need to breathe oxygen and fuel to return to Earth, even if they are only living on Mars for a short time.  At present, the US National Aeronautics and Space Administration's Mars 2020 mission to Mars is equipped with high-temperature electrolysis instruments, which can only produce oxygen from carbon dioxide in the air, but not hydrogen.  Vijay Ramani, a professor at the University of Washington, said that the latest technology could break down salt water into oxygen and hydrogen, changing the Mars program and even “turning the oceans into usable sources of oxygen and fuel on Earth. ”  The University of Washington research team looks forward to working with NASA to develop the technology, which it hopes will be used in the development of deep sea resources on Earth.

Title: Oxygen and hydrogen on Mars proposed to get from brine
Content: Scientists have developed a method for producing oxygen and hydrogen from a liquid saline solution in Martian lakes using electrolysis.  A feature of the experiment was the use of lead-ruthenium oxide as an electrocatalyst for oxygen production.  The production of oxygen using such an installation was 25 times more energy efficient than in the case of MOXIE, launched to the Red Planet as part of the Mars 2020 mission, and the size and weight of the device for life support based on the described technology will be less than that of analogues.  The article was published in the journal PNAS.  Conditions on Mars are far from favorable for humans: the atmosphere is rarefied and 95 percent consists of carbon dioxide, and temperature changes exceed 100 degrees Celsius with an average temperature of minus 63 degrees.  Therefore, colonization of the Red Planet is impossible without the creation of a life support system that would be able to provide people with oxygen for breathing and fuel (for example, hydrogen) for energy supply and, ideally, return flight.  To solve the first problem, NASA created MOXIE (Mars Oxygen ISRU Experiment) - an experimental installation for obtaining oxygen from atmospheric carbon dioxide by electrolysis.  To test the effectiveness of such a method in the field, the installation became part of the Mars Rover Perseverance, which was launched on July 30, 2020 as part of the Mars 2020 mission.  An alternative source of not only oxygen, but also hydrogen on Mars can be water, the first direct evidence of the existence of which on the red planet was obtained in 1971.  Particularly attractive for use in applications, however, would be the reserves of salt water, impurities in which would allow it to remain in a liquid state even at low temperature and pressure.  The first traces of such brine (liquid salt solution) with magnesium perchlorate as the main component were found on Mars in 2015, and in 2018, a reservoir with a diameter of about 20 kilometers was found under the polar ice of the planet, which could have been formed due to volcanic activity.  Later, planetary scientists confirmed that such lakes on Mars really exist and can be numerous.  Now Pralay Gayen (Pralay Gayen) from the University of Washington in St. Louis together with colleagues created an installation for obtaining oxygen and hydrogen from a saline solution close in composition and temperature to that in Martian lakes.  As a brine in the experiment, a solution of magnesium perchlorate in water with a concentration of 2.8 mol per liter was used, cooled to minus 36 degrees Celsius and blown by carbon dioxide (the latter played the role of the Martian atmosphere).  As an electrocatalyst for the production of oxygen, the scientists used lead-ruthenium oxide Pb2Ru2O7-δ, the effectiveness of which they previously showed for alkaline solutions.  The electrocatalyst for hydrogen production was platinum on activated carbon - the standard catalyst in this case, and a commercially produced anion-exchange membrane was used as a separator.  Installation diagram.  In the red region, oxygen is produced, in the blue - hydrogen.  Image source: Pralay Gayen et al. / PNAS In the course of the study, scientists showed that lead-ruthenium oxide as an electrocatalyst is indeed several times more effective than the ruthenium oxide commonly used in such installations.  After the behavior of the created installation was studied in a wide range of temperatures from − 36 to 21 degrees Celsius and saw no radical fluctuations in the efficiency and rate of production.  The current output of the experimental installation was 70 percent, and the energy efficiency was in the range between 36 and 70 percent (depending on the voltage applied to the plates).  In addition, the installation was resistant to degradation of the catalyst: scientists were not able to find traces of ruthenium in the solution after 300-minute operation of the device.  The rate of production of oxygen (blue dots) and hydrogen (red dots), depending on the density of the cathode current.  Image source: Pralay Gayen et al. / PNAS Also, the researchers compared the achieved rate of oxygen production with MOXIE values of 10-22 grams per hour: it turned out that with the same energy supply, the created installation produces 25 times more oxygen than the experiment on the Mars Rover “Perseverance ”.  To have the same rate of oxygen production as MOXIE, the device would have to have electrodes with an area of ​ ​ 28-62 square centimeters, and to ensure the vital activity of a sleeping and actively moving person, this parameter would have to be 375 and 1235 square centimeters, respectively.  At the same time, the mass and volume of the installation will be less than if you use the technology inherent in MOXIE.  Moreover, the developed method of obtaining oxygen does not require its subsequent purification, while during electrolysis in MOXIE, carbon monoxide is also produced, which must be filtered.  Dependence on the power consumption of the rate of oxygen production of the installation (blue line), as well as its capes and volume to ensure various modes of human life (black lines).  The blue dot is the power and rate of oxygen production at MOXIE.  Image source: Pralay Gayen et al. / PNAS Previously, we talked about another method of obtaining oxygen from carbon dioxide in the Martian atmosphere (like MOXIE): scientists proposed to do this using low-temperature plasma.  And what is the role of the Mars Rover “Perseverance ” in addition to checking the method of oxygen production, you can read in our material“ Mars, there and back ”.  Nikita Kozyrev

Title: Scientists have found organisms that can give rise to life on Mars
Content: Scientists have found organisms that can give rise to life on Mars 16.02.2021, 14: 58 They are able to grow and multiply in the conditions of the red planet.  New experiments have shown that cyanobacteria, also known as blue-green algae, can successfully grow in Martian atmospheric conditions.  Of course, a few more ingredients will be needed, but when humans get to Mars, they will be able to create life support systems based on cyanobacteria for the human habitat, writes nv.ua.  "Here we show that cyanobacteria can use the gases available in the Martian atmosphere, at low overall pressure, as a source of carbon and nitrogen," said astrobiologist Cyprien Verso from the University of Bremen in Germany.  "Under these conditions, cyanobacteria retained their ability to grow in water containing only Martian dust, and they could be used to feed other microbes.  This can help make long-term missions to Mars sustainable, ” the authors of the study believe.  All types of cyanobacteria produce oxygen as a byproduct of photosynthesis, and even today they are an invaluable source of it.  For several years, scientists have speculated whether we could use the ability of cyanobacteria to produce oxygen to live on Mars.  This will bring additional benefits.  The atmosphere of Mars consists mainly of carbon dioxide (95 percent) and nitrogen (3 percent), which are fixed by cyanobacteria, turning them into organic compounds and nutrients, respectively.  However, atmospheric pressure on Mars is a big problem.  The total pressure there is less than 1% of Earth ’ s — from 6 to 11 GPa: this is too small for the presence of liquid water, while the partial pressure of gaseous nitrogen — from 0.2 to 0.3 GPa — is not enough for their metabolism.  But recreating the atmosphere, like on Earth, would be too expensive: gases would have to be imported.  So the researchers were looking for a middle ground: an atmosphere close to Martian, which allows cyanobacteria to grow well.  The authors have developed a bioreactor called Atmos, which has an atmospheric pressure of about 10 percent of Earth ’ s, but uses only what can be found on Mars, albeit in inverted proportions: 96 percent nitrogen and 4 percent carbon dioxide.  The bioreactor also included water that can be obtained on Mars from melting ice, which in some places is abundant on the surface, and a simulator of Martian regolith, a mixture of minerals created here on Earth using only what can be found on Mars.  The team chose the type of nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria that preliminary trials showed was most likely to thrive under these conditions, Anabaena sp.  PCC 7938, and tested it in a variety of conditions.  The researchers concluded that nitrogen-fixing, oxygen-producing cyanobacteria can be grown on Mars at low pressure under controlled conditions using exclusively local ingredients.  From cyanobacteria, sugar, amino acids and other nutrients can be obtained to feed other crops, which can then be used for other purposes, such as the production of medicines.  Atmos was designed to test whether cyanobacteria can be grown under certain atmospheric conditions rather than for maximum efficiency, and the parameters of the bioreactor will depend on many factors in the mission to Mars, including the payload and mission architecture.  However, now that the concept has been proven, the team can begin work on optimizing the bioreactor system that could one day save us life on Mars. Title: Test satellite. NASA will test on the moon technology for the colonization of Mars
Content: "If God wanted man to become a cosmic species, he would give him the moon."  The famous German rocket engine engineer Kraft Erike uttered these words in 1984, wanting to emphasize the fact that we can use the moon as a springboard to spread human civilization throughout the rest of the solar system, writes Mit Technology Review.  More than a decade has passed since the last Apollo mission to the moon.  Erike watched NASA and the rest of the U.S. space program retreat from hopes of exploring more distant worlds, such as Mars, and instead focus on orbiting the Earth.  However, at the moment, America is again seeking a return to the moon with the mission “Artemis ”, the ambitious goal of which is to send astronauts by 2024.  But for the White House and NASA, this mission is more than just returning humans to the surface of the moon, as it is also an ideal base for developing a follow-up mission to Mars.  For both directions, the goal is not just to fly to the moon and return to Earth, but to create the necessary conditions for permanent residence so that people can work and develop there.  "We are returning to the moon for scientific discoveries, economic benefits and inspiration for a new generation of research.  As we create sustainable conditions for habitation on the moon, we are also striving for the first steps of man on the red planet, ” said NASA Director Jim Bridenstine on September 21.  However, it is not yet clear how this should all work.  The most important projects that Artemis is supposed to launch — the next generation Space Launch System rocket and the Orion crew capsule — have not yet been completed.  Most experts agree that there is insufficient funding for the program.  Moreover, NASA has not even chosen a lunar lander.  But even if we get to the moon in 2024, where is the guarantee that Mars will colonize next?  “The biggest problem we ’ re facing right now is that we don ’ t know how to live and work productively beyond Earth, ” says Clive Neal, an engineer at the University of Notre Dame and an expert on lunar exploration.  The technologies needed for long-term work in space have never been properly tested.  After all, it is necessary to take into account the harsh Martian conditions, with a lower level of temperature and gravity, with a higher level of radiation, as well as a lack of water and oxygen.  "In our backyard, we have our own lab where we can test these conditions," Neal said.  He and his colleagues recently created a new report released by the human rights group Exlore Mars, which promotes sustainable space exploration.  The report identifies dozens of activities and technologies needed to explore Mars that can be developed and tested with the Artemis mission and ongoing lunar exploration.  Almost immediately after the launch of Artemis 3, it will be possible to test some important things for Mars on the Moon.  Life support is at the top of this list, as humans have never built long-term dwellings on another planet before.  And while researchers will apply much of what they ’ ve learned from long missions to the International Space Station, they still need to make sure that a lunar base and a base on Mars can provide such basic needs as food, water, and shelter.  "I think the key will be to immerse more people in the lunar environment," said Joe Cassady, executive director of space operations at Aerojet Rocketdyne and one of the lead editors of the Explore Mars report.  The important point is to collect experience and data from many different astronauts during missions that will last for months.  This experience will help engineers build habitats, spacesuits and ground transportation systems suitable for humans.  But in order for these habitats to last a long time, you need to build something quite sustainable.  Launch windows for missions to Mars (when the planet is closest to Earth) only appear every 26 months, so any return mission to the Red Planet will take some waiting time.  If the journey takes, say, 273 days, then Mars will have to spend at least three to four months before it becomes possible to go back home.  And there are two options: either take enough food with you to last all these months, or look for extraterrestrial resources.  The first option is unlikely to work.  “It is important to use only local resources.  Trying to take with you everything that can help protect astronauts on Mars, simply will not work, ” said Neil.  Water ice will be a vital resource.  It could supply water and oxygen to life support systems, as well as split into hydrogen and oxygen for use as rocket fuel.  It can also be used as a protection against space radiation and micrometeorite bombardment.  There is a lot of ice on Mars.  According to scientists on the moon, too, which makes it an ideal environment for testing the technologies that are needed to explore these reserves, mine them, clean them up and turn them into something that can help preserve the life support of a future settlement.  "The moon is a more extreme habitat.  And that means that if something works on it, it will work on Mars, ” Neal says.  The presence of water ice also somewhat reinforces the argument for launching a spacecraft propulsion system based on hydrogen rather than methane.  The report says that hydrogen can be produced locally on both worlds, while methane is produced from local resources only on Mars, where an atmosphere saturated with carbon dioxide provides a ready source of carbon.  As a result, any methane production on the moon would require importing a carbon source.  The report also recommends the use of power systems that are not entirely dependent on the sun.  On Mars, with its long distance and dusty atmosphere, solar panels will have a harder time converting sunlight into energy.  Nuclear energy seems to be the most obvious approach.  To ensure the functioning of the shelter on the moon, it will not require too much energy, instead it will be needed to perform the mining work necessary to collect and process water ice.  Mining experts told Neal they were likely to look for systems that could deliver power in the megawatt range.  “It was a wake-up call because people in the planetary world don ’ t have that kind of connection to the mining industry, ” Neal says.  Solar energy in this case will be more of a reserve source of energy than the main one.  The moon is also the best place to simulate a mission to Mars, especially when it comes to Gateway, a planned space station designed for lunar orbit.  In fact, it will serve as a springboard for any NASA missions to the surface of the moon (both with a crew and with robots), as well as for further flights to Mars.  The first three elements of the Gateway (power, propulsion and residential module) are scheduled to be launched in 2023.  In their report, Cassady and colleagues suggested that one approach might be for the crew to stay on the lunar space station Gateway for 60-90 days, simulate a mission to Mars on the surface of the moon for more than 30 days, and then, before returning home, complete another stay on the Gateway for 90 days.  It will be a condensed version of the mission to Mars.  It will mimic the changing microgravity conditions that can be encountered on such a journey, and give astronauts an idea of what a Martian mission might be like.  A new NASA Artemis project says the Gateway-to-Surface operating system is similar to how a mission to Mars can work, with the ability of the crew to stay in orbit and deploy on the surface.  In addition, settling on Mars will be a difficult task if scientists do not develop autonomous systems that do not need careful monitoring.  Ground-based service teams are able to manage objects on the moon almost in real time, but the delay in communication from Earth to Mars can reach 22.4 minutes.  “If there is a disaster on Mars like the one that happened with Apollo 13, there will not be a team of engineers who could diagnose and solve the problem in real time, ” said Casey Dreyer, an expert on space policy at the Planetary Society.  The moon is the only good environment in which it is possible to truly test and improve automated systems that can operate reliably without human control.  There are concerns that the U.S. space program could face a dramatic shift in priorities after the November elections, as has happened in previous years.  But so far, the Democratic Party seems to still be in favor of the mission.  “We support NASA ’ s work to bring Americans back to the moon and reach Mars, taking the next step in exploring our solar system. ”  Dreyer notes that the development of the Space Launch System and Orion is almost complete.  In addition, Gateway enjoys a lot of international support: Europe, Japan, Canada and possibly Russia are ready to play their part in its development.  The new Artemis plan explains better than ever how NASA intends to bring humans back to the moon by 2024, but says very little about how it will meet the technological criteria for a sustainable lunar base that will help get to Mars.  Even at a time when Erica ’ s words are closer than ever to life, it will take us a lot of determination to make the leap from the Moon to the Red Planet.

Title: Life in the Caves!
Content: At the initiative of a Spanish company, tourists can live in a cave that simulates the conditions of life on Mars.  The participants are cut off from the outside world and spend three days and nights at a special station called Ares in a cave located in the Cantabrian Mountains.  The cave is 60 meters high and half a kilometer long.  The programme starts earlier with a three-week distance learning course and three days of practical physical and mental training to learn how to cope in the conditions found in this habitat.  Inside the cave, participants experience what human life on Mars would be like.  David Sabalus, CEO of Astroland, who pioneered the experiment, said: “The Martian environment is very hostile to low temperatures, strong winds and high levels of solar radiation.  For this reason, the expeditions to the Red Planet will have no choice but to survive underground and will be the most suitable way to preserve human life below the surface of Mars.  "We have created the right conditions in this cave to conduct a life experiment on Mars."  The Ares station is equipped with research laboratories, spacesuits, special suits for various missions, living chambers, hydroponics laboratory (hydroponics culture, soil-free plant culture), autonomous systems and independent water production, 3D printers, kitchen, recreation area, gym, emergency bio-assistance equipment, food specifically for each member, etc.  Participants will have to pay around 6,000 euros for the three-day trip.  End of message.

Title: On the "Martian" and "lunar" soil grew plants: photo
Content: In the Netherlands, scientists from Wageningen University sowed samples of model soil of Mars and the Moon, developed by NASA, with ten different crops.  This is reported by Open Agriculture.  Researchers planted watercress, arugula, tomatoes, radish, rye, quinoa, chives, spinach, peas and leeks.  The same cultures for control were planted on the ground.  All plants, except spinach, grew well on model soils and gave edible parts.  The amount of biomass on the simulated Martian soil was comparable to the biomass given by the earth ’ s soil.  Indicators on simulations of lunar regolith refused to be smaller, but scientists recognized them as good.  Model soils were previously enriched with organic additives to reproduce the soil on which some crops were already grown.  See also: In space managed to “grow ” meat: video

Title: People are preparing for the pollution of Mars - our review
Content: The experiment was conducted on Earth, more precisely, in the stratosphere of our planet.  There, scientists from two space agencies sent a probe with various microorganisms to check how they would behave in the atmosphere of the red planet.  "We successfully tested a new method of placing bacteria and fungi in Martian conditions using a probe sent into the stratosphere," says Marta Filipa Cortezao of DLR.  "Some microbes, especially black mold embryos, were able to survive the journey even after exposure to very high levels of ultraviolet radiation."  Understanding how microorganisms react to space travel and the Martian environment is key to future missions.  One of the motives is that in the search for extraterrestrial life, scientists should be sure that there are no microorganisms brought from Earth.  But there are other threats.  “On long missions to Mars, we need to know that the microorganisms associated with humans would survive on the Red Planet, because some of them can threaten the lives of astronauts, ” says Katarina Zins, one of the main authors of the publication, which appeared in the publication Frontiers in Microbiology.  But such resistant to harsh conditions earthly life forms still harbor additional opportunities.  "Some microbes may be underestimated by us in the exploration of Mars.  But they are able to help us in the production of food and other materials, regardless of the Earth.  This is a key opportunity to survive away from home, ” the expert adds.  According to experts, it is very difficult to reproduce Martian conditions on Earth.  However, this was possible outside the ozone layer.  “We sent microorganisms placed inside the MARSBox (Microbes in Atmosphere for Radiation, Survival and Biological Outcomes experiment), in which both the atmosphere of Mars and the pressure were artificially maintained into the stratosphere during the entire scientific mission, ” explains the essence of the experiment Cortezao.

It was a milestone for the German company in the legal battle that has dragged down Bayer ’ s share price for nearly two years. passages.title: Bayer Roundup Lawsuit Settlement Talks Hit New Frustration
passages.passage: Lawyers for the plaintiffs said in court Thursday that a $10.9 billion settlement that Bayer AG (BAYRY) paid to settle concerns about the safety of its herbicide Roundup has stalled.  The German chemical and pharmaceutical giant said in June that it had reached a settlement to settle 75 percent of the 125,000 lawsuits alleging cancer caused by its top-selling herbicide, and was working to settle the remaining lawsuits.  Shareholders welcomed the news that three California juries had rejected the company ’ s massive damages award in the Roundup lawsuit.  Bayer said Roundup is safe and does not cause non-Hodgkin lymphoma.  Lawyers told the judge at Thursday's hearing that Bayer has yet to sign an agreement with lead plaintiffs' attorneys Aimee Wagstaff and Jennifer Moore.  Brent Wisner, a lawyer for the plaintiffs, said another agreement to settle a large number of lawsuits was terminated earlier this month.  According to Wagstaff, the three firms collectively represent about 20,000 plaintiffs.  It's...

passages.title: "International Industry" Herbicide Law Dispute Bayer $2 Billion Settlement - Finance
passages.passage: Bayer, the German chemical company, said on Wednesday that a legal dispute over cancer caused by its Roundup brand herbicide has reached a $2 billion settlement with regulators.  Bayer acquired Monsanto for $63 billion in 2018, taking over the company ’ s business and litigation.  Bayer says decades of research have shown that Roundup herbicides and glyphosate are safe for human use.  Wednesday ’ s settlement also includes claims for individuals exposed to Roundup herbicides and diagnosed with non-Hodgkin ’ s lymphoma in the future.  Under the agreement, Bayer will provide $2 billion for four years and for diagnostic assistance; each individual requesting a claim will receive up to $200,000.  The settlement is subject to approval by the San Francisco Court.  Under the amended agreement, any individual who has not filed a claim within a four-year period can appeal to the court for a better outcome.  Bayer has faced more than 100,000 lawsuits in the United States for its herbicide.  (Times Information)

passages.title: Bayer reported a bad quarter due to the pandemic and lawsuits « Russian Pharmaceuticals
passages.passage: Bayer reported an unsuccessful quarter due to the pandemic and lawsuits Bayer published a report for the third quarter, according to which revenue and sales of the company decreased.  The pharmaceutical industry of the corporation tried as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic and legal proceedings.  German chemical-pharmaceutical transnational corporation Bayer published a report for the third quarter of 2020 fiscal year, which states that the manufacturer of medicines suffered due to the coronavirus pandemic, resulting in net losses of the company amounted to $3.2 billion, and revenue decreased by 4.2% to $36.8 billion.  In general, Bayer sales in the third quarter fell by 13.5% compared to the same period of 2019 - to $9.9 billion.  Sales in the pharmaceutical sector decreased by 6.1%, reaching $4.9 billion.  Among the positive aspects, we can note the increase in sales of oral anticoagulant "Xarelto" by 13.8%, which has a special demand in Germany and Russia; ophthalmic drug "Eilea", actively sold in China; anti-cancer drug "Stivarga" by 17.5%, especially in the United States.  COVID-19 is said to have exacerbated the problems Bayer faced after its acquisition of agricultural company Monsanto two years ago.  This summer, the pharmaceutical company pledged to pay $10.9 billion in court compensation for cancer patients from the herbicide Roundup, which went to Bayer from Monsanto.  More than 125,000 people filed their claims.  However, it has not yet been established whether this herbicide causes cancer.  Bayer said it would need an additional $750 million to pay off the debt.  Against the background of litigation, the shares of the drug manufacturer fell to record low values (by 43% since the beginning of the year).  In the second quarter, net losses amounted to $11 billion due to the need to pay compensation.  The company has already paid off its debt in 80,000 lawsuits.  Bayer CFO Wolfgang Nickle stressed that the third quarter was difficult mainly due to problems in the agricultural sector of the corporation.  The company is gradually restoring its position in the field of production of medicines.  Photo: Bayer AG Vladimir Zabolotskikh pharmvestnik

passages.title: Most of Europe ’ s stock markets are rising, Italy is in the red due to budget disputes with the EU
passages.passage: Most of Europe's stock markets are rising, Italy is in the red due to disputes with the EU over the budget Western European stock indexes are mainly rising during trading on Tuesday amid company reporting and statistics.  In addition, market participants hope for progress in resolving trade disputes between the United States and China.  The only significant exception is Italy, with investors worried about its disputes with Brussels over next year ’ s budget.  The composite index of the largest enterprises in the region Stoxx Europe 600 is growing for the first time in three sessions, by 11: 45 QoQ it rose by 0.6%, to 364.06 points.  According to media reports, Vice Premier Liu He will visit the United States to prepare for a meeting of the leaders of the two countries at the G20 summit in Argentina in late November.  During telephone conversations on Friday, Liu He and U.S. Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin did not agree on options for a rapprochement.  The British FTSE 100 grew by 0.5%, the French CAC 40 - by 0.4%, the German DAX added 0.7%.  The Italian FTSE MIB declined by 0.1%.  The Italian government has until the end of the day on Tuesday to send the European Commission a revised draft budget.  According to La Stampa and Il Sole 24 Ore, Rome is not going to make concessions on public spending and budget deficits, but probably admits that the measures taken will not have such a strong positive impact on the economy, as previously claimed.  The Ministry of Finance of Italy can reduce the estimate of growth for next year from 1.5% to 1.3% or even 1.2%, the latter option will correspond to the forecast of the European Commission itself.  Despite the lack of changes in terms of the budget deficit, Italian Prime Minister Giuseppe Conte hopes that the new version of the document will at least partially satisfy Brussels, writes Il Messagero.  According to the Italian newspaper, Deputy Prime Minister Luigi Di Maio and Matteo Salvini insist on maintaining the original version of the budget.  On Tuesday, data on the UK labour market were released.  The unemployment rate in July-September unexpectedly rose to 4.1%, while it was expected to remain at around 4%.  At the same time, the rate of increase in the average wage in this period accelerated to the maximum since 2008 - 3.2% in annual terms.  In Germany, inflation in October accelerated to a maximum in 10 years - 2.5% in annual terms, according to the final data.  The capitalization of the German chemical company Bayer increased by 2.6%.  Adjusted EBITDA in the third quarter amounted to 2.2 billion euros and was higher than market expectations.  At the same time, the management of Bayer assured investors that the acquisition of American Monsanto for $63 billion will improve financial performance.  Top managers also promised to continue fighting lawsuits against Monsanto in connection with the herbicide Roundup, which, according to the plaintiffs, contributed to the development of cancer and other diseases.  Quarterly reporting supported a jump in the price of Vodafone shares by 6.5%.  The British telecommunications group recorded an operating loss of 2.07 billion euros in April-September due to losses on the sale of Vodafone India.  At the same time, the organic growth of adjusted EBITDA was 2.9%, reaching EUR 7.08 billion.  Vodafone narrowed its forecast for annual profit growth to 3% from previously expected 1-5%, set new cost reduction targets and froze the payment of interim dividends.  Telecom Italia ’ s stock price fell 1.7% in Milan, while the phone company ’ s bonds are also falling in price.  Telecom Italia CEO Amos Genis was stripped of his powers by a majority decision of the board of directors.  His powers are temporarily transferred to the chairman of the board of directors Fulvio Conti.  Shares of the pharmaceutical company AstraZeneca rose by 0.9% after the sale of the Swedish Orphan Biovitrum rights to the drug for the treatment of respiratory diseases Synagis in the US market.

passages.title: Bayer raises Roundup herbicide-related future litigation costs to $2 billion
passages.passage: Bayer AG (BAYRY, BAYN.XE) on Tuesday raised its cost estimate for future litigation related to its controversial herbicide product Roundup to $2 billion from $1.25 billion.  The German chemical and pharmaceutical group said it made additional provisions in the third quarter to cover the increased costs associated with the case.  Bayer announced that as of the end of June, there were about 125,000 filed and unfiled Roundad-related claims, and the company is continuing to work with plaintiffs ’ lawyers to develop a joint program to resolve future Roundad-related claims.  (This article is from the Dow Jones News Agency)

passages.title: Herbicide cancer-causing controversy again: whether China's manufacturing and agriculture will be affected
passages.passage: Image copyright AFP Image caption A large amount of pesticides are sprayed in Argentina's soybean fields.  A jury in the United States has ruled that the ingredients of one of the world's most commonly used herbicides are a "key factor" in causing cancer in a man.  What impact does this have on mainland China and Taiwan?  But German chemical and pharmaceutical giant Bayer has strongly denied claims that its Monsanto unit, Roundup, which makes glyphosate ingredients, causes cancer.  But a jury in San Francisco ruled unanimously that the product caused California resident Edwin Hardman to develop non-Hodgkin's lymphoma.  The next phase of the court trial will consider the issue of damages and liability for Bayer products.  At this stage of the trial, Hardman ’ s lawyers are expected to provide evidence of Bayer ’ s efforts to influence scientists, regulators and the public ’ s perception of the safety implications of its products.  After the news came to light, Bayer's share price plunged about 12 percent.  1,200 related cases In 2018, Germany's Bayer company bought US rival Monsanto for $66 billion, and Monsanto's product Roundup was also part of the acquisition.  Bayer said it was disappointed by the ruling.  The company will present evidence of the safety of Monsanto ’ s products, as well as a strong belief in scientific proof that glyphosate-based herbicides do not cause cancer.  The case is only the second of about 1,200 lawsuits against Roundup in the United States.  In August 2018, a California court jury found another California man was awarded $289 million in damages because Roundup caused his cancer.  The ruling in the case at the time also caused Bayer's share price to plummet.  The case was later reduced to 78 million dollars, and Bayer is still appealing the case.  As an agricultural power, China, GM and Roundup have become the largest producer and exporter of glyphosate in the world, and are also one of the largest users of glyphosate.  More than half of glyphosate produced in China is exported, including the Roundup herbicide that Monsanto manufactures and distributes globally.  At the same time, China also imports a lot of processed glyphosate.  According to statistics, Roundup products account for 80% of herbicide products in China.  Glyphosate use and consumption are mainly concentrated in some agricultural countries, especially large countries that produce genetically modified crops.  There are thousands of glyphosate pesticide products in mainland China.  In Taiwan and Hong Kong, there are also Roundup sales, which in Taiwan is translated as “Spring of the Year ”.  Image copyright Getty Images Image caption Monsanto's popular glyphosate product Roundup sells worldwide.  In Taiwan, its translation is Spring of the Year.  What is glyphosate and is it dangerous?  Glyphosate is a herbicide invented by Monsanto in 1974, but its patent expired in 2000.  It is currently the highest selling pesticide in the world.  In 2015, the World Health Organization's International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) concluded that glyphosate "may be carcinogenic."  However, the EPA insists that careful use of glyphosate is safe.  The European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) also said glyphosate is unlikely to cause cancer.  However, due to the excessive use of glyphosate, improper spraying of glyphosate has a lot of incidents that directly lead to human poisoning.  In addition, glyphosate has been found in rain, rivers, agricultural products, food (including beer, bread, etc.), meat products and human bodies, leading to an international campaign against the use of glyphosate.  In November 2017, the European Union decided to extend the license for glyphosate use for five years.  California lists glyphosate as a chemical known to cause cancer.  But the agricultural industry is opposed to putting such a label on glyphosate.

passages.passage: The French government approved the decision of the American jury, which sentenced the biotechnology corporation Monsanto to pay $289 million to American Dwayne Johnson.  This was reported on August 12 by AFP.  http: / / ru.rfi.fr / v-mire / 20180812-frantsuzskoe-pravitelstvo-odobrilo-isk-k-proizvoditelyu-pesticidov? ref = tw “Johnson, who worked as a gardener, claims that due to the use of anti-weeds Roundup and RangerPro containing glycol Fosat, he got cancer.  State Secretary of the French Ministry of Ecology, Brune Poiarson, commented on the decision: “We did not wait for the historic decision of the American court to take action.  France voted against the extension of the permit for the use of glyphosate in Europe, and we are trying to mobilize other European states to share our position. ”  French Environment Minister Nicolas Hulot called on Europeans and Americans to take part in the “war against pesticides ”.  The decision of the California court was also welcomed by the Confederation of French Peasants.  “This decision once again confirms that pesticides are dangerous to health, especially for those who use them, that is, for peasants, ” said Laurent Pinatel, a representative of the Confederation, recalling Emmanuel Macron ’ s promise to ban the use of pesticides by 2021.  Despite France ’ s efforts, the European Commission recently extended the license for glyphosate for another five years.  Glyphosate due to its cheapness and ease of use is very widespread and is often used to control weeds.  In 2015, the International Agency for Research on Cancer and the WHO Cancer Agency concluded that the substance is “probably carcinogenic to humans. ”  The lawsuit of Dewayne Johnson, who was diagnosed with non-Hodgkin ’ s lymphoma in 2014, is the first glyphosate case to go to trial.  In the United States, Monsanto has already filed about five thousand similar lawsuits.  German pharmaceutical group Bayer, which recently acquired the Monsanto group, continues to argue that the herbicide Roundup is “reliable and not carcinogenic ” and is going to appeal the court ’ s decision.  In the light of subsequent events, the court ’ s decision does not seem final.  As previously reported, in June of this year, Bayer closed the acquisition of Monsanto http: / / www.monsantoglobal.com / global / en / newsviews / Pages / bayer-closes-monsanto-acquisition.aspx “LEVERCOUSEN (June 7, 2018) – On Thursday, Bayer successfully completed the acquisition of Monsanto to.  Shares of the American company will no longer be traded on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE), as Bayer became the sole owner of Monsanto.  Monsanto shareholders will receive a payment of $128 per share of the company.  Investment bank J.P. Morgan assisted Bayer in securing payment for the largest transaction in the company ’ s history.  According to the preliminary approval of the US Department of Justice, Monsanto ’ s integration into Bayer will occur after the completion of the sale of part of the assets to BASF.  Integration is expected to begin in about two months.  “Today is a great day: for our customers, farmers around the world, whom we can help to increase the quality and volume of the crop; our shareholders, as this transaction will increase the value of the company; consumers and society as a whole, as we will have more opportunities to help farmers increase the production of quality food, adhering to the principles of sustainable development.  As a leader in innovation for agriculture, we are a promising employer and offer employees opportunities for professional development, ” said Werner Baumann, Chairman of the Board of Management of Bayer.  “Our goals for sustainable agriculture are no less important than financial growth.  We understand that leadership entails responsibility in the field of doing business and establishing an open dialogue with society. ”  And here is the latest news: it is officially announced that the conditions for the start of Monsanto integration have been met.  .https: / / monsanto.com / news-releases / bayer-conditions-beginning-monsanto-integration-filled / ” Leverkusen, August 16, 2018 – Monsanto ’ s integration into the Bayer Group may begin after Bayer ’ s handover to BASF of some Crop Science businesses with total sales of around 2.2 billion euros.  One of the requirements of the US Department of Justice was that Bayer and Monsanto remain separate companies and continue to operate independently until the completion of these divestments at BASF, and it finally happened.  As previously reported, Bayer expects the acquisition to make a positive contribution to core earnings per share starting in 2019, with a double-digit percentage from 2021.  Since 2022, annual contributions of $1.2 billion have been made.  In addition, it is estimated that US $1 million will be invested in EBITDA before special items are planned on a synergistic basis.  Moreover, Bayer will continue to strengthen its commitment to sustainability.  As for the verdict on glyphosate in California on August 10, 2018, Bayer believes that the jury ’ s decision contradicts the weight of scientific evidence, decades of real world experience and the conclusions of regulators around the world, which confirm that glyphosate is safe and its use does not cause non-Hodgkin ’ s lymphoma.  Recently, the National Institutes of Health (NIH) confirmed that glyphosate does not cause cancer.  The US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA), the European Chemicals Agency (ECHA) and other regulatory bodies around the world have also concluded that glyphosate can be used safely.  The jury ’ s verdict is only the first step in this case, and it remains the subject of post-trial motions in the court of first instance and appeal, as Monsanto announced.  The continuation of the story, according to Bayer, will be that the courts will eventually find that Monsanto and glyphosate are not responsible for Mr. Johnson ’ s disease.  Due to the above-mentioned requirements established by the US Department of Justice, Bayer did not have access to detailed internal information at Monsanto.  Under these circumstances, Bayer was not allowed to influence Monsanto ’ s business affairs, and its ability to actively comment on them in detail was extremely limited.  Today, however, Bayer has been able to actively engage in advocacy efforts in glyphosate trials and any other legal disputes, such as potential damage claims in connection with the Dicamba product. ”  The Germans are now involved in the dispute.  They probably don ’ t want to pay anything.  Is it possible that they will drag the courts to Germany under local jurisdiction?  But they will definitely try.  http: / / procomp.info / news / 730-kolichestvo-sudebnyh-iskov-protiv-monsanto-vyroslo-s-5200-do-8000.html “A surge of lawsuits followed after a California court ordered Monsanto to pay $289 million in compensation to the gardener.  Since then, Bayer shares have lost more than 10 percent.  Asked whether Bayer would consider settling cases out of court, CEO Werner Baumann said: “We will actively defend this case and all pending cases. ”  He also said on Thursday that “as of the end of July, the number of plaintiffs in both state and federal lawsuits is approximately 8,000.  These numbers may increase or decrease over time. ”  According to Baumann, when Bayer bought Monsanto, he “could not have foreseen the scale of the current lawsuits. ”  The $63 billion acquisition was completed in June.  The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) says glyphosate is unlikely to be carcinogenic.  Glyphosate is an active ingredient in Monsanto ’ s Roundup, which is the most popular weed killer in the US. ”  So, it's still ahead.

passages.passage: Bayer AG (BAYRY) said it will evaluate whether to continue to use the active ingredient in its popular Roundup herbicide in the U.S. residential supplies market.  On Wednesday, Bayer's attempts to limit future liability for whether the product could cause cancer suffered a setback in court.  Bayer said it would pay up to $9.6 billion in damages to settle an existing Roundup case related to non-Hodgkin lymphoma and another $2 billion for future claims.  The German company lost three lawsuits filed between 2018 and 2019 by Roundup users who said the product caused them to develop cancer, and the company is working to resolve about 125,000 similar claims.  Bayer is seeking to resolve future cases in a novel form of class-action settlement that seeks to involve Roundup users who have used Roundup but are not yet sick, and those who have cancer but are yet to be prosecuted. passages.title: Turkey will not leave the observation post surrounded by the Syrian army in Idlib
passages.passage: Turkish soldiers stand on a hill overlooking the Syrian city of Kobani, near Suruk, on the border between Turkey and Syria © AP Photo / Vadim Ghirda Turkish soldiers stand on a hill overlooking the Syrian city of Kobani, near Suruk, on the border between Turkey and Syria ANTAKYA (Turkey), Aug 22 – RIA Novosti.  Turkey does not intend to leave its observation post for the de-escalation zone in the Syrian village of Murek, which was surrounded by the Syrian army, Turkish Foreign Ministry spokesman Hami Aksoy told RIA Novosti.  The Syrian government army occupied the city of Khan Sheikhoun in the south of the province of Idlib, now the city is being stripped and demined, a Syrian field source told RIA Novosti earlier on Thursday.  On Wednesday evening, the Syrian army closed a siege around the cities of Latmane, Kafr Zeita, Latmin and Murik in the north of Hama province south of the city of Khan Shaykhun, a local military source told RIA Novosti.  The cities are under the fire control of the army.  “The ninth observation post of Turkey in the village of Murek will remain in its place, despite the establishment of the control of the Syrian army over the city of Khan Shaykhun, ” said Aksoy.  The diplomat did not answer the question of how the observation post will continue to exist when the Syrian army takes control of Murek.  After the talks on Syria in Nur-Sultan on August 2, the "ceasefire" came into force in Idlib.  The command of the armed forces of the Syrian Arab Republic said that it would stop the fighting if Turkey fulfilled its obligations under the Russian-Turkish agreement reached in September 2018 in Sochi.  The main point was the withdrawal of heavy and medium weapons militants 20 kilometers from the demilitarized zone in Idlib.  Three days later, on August 5, the army resumed the operation due to the failure of the gangs to fulfill the conditions, which, taking advantage of the lull, made attempts to attack the positions of the Syrian army in the north of Hama province and repeatedly opened fire on residential settlements in the area.

passages.title: Грызы: one of the most original nationalities of Azerbaijan - INTERESTING FACTS - PHOTOS
passages.passage: Herzy is one of the small indigenous peoples of Azerbaijan.  In the 1980s, the study of the etymology of the toponym "Gryz" was deeply engaged in a prominent Azerbaijani ethnographer G.A.Heybullayev, who came to the conclusion that the ancestors of this people were the ancient Albanian tribes of the Er.  In the course of ethnographic research close to the hernias by origin and language, it turned out that the latter called themselves "har" ("her"), while the inhabitants of the village of Elik who spoke the same language called them "horud", and the inhabitants of the village of Jack - "cherud".  In this case, the components "chorus" - "cher" - "har" - to the self-name of the hopyts, and "ud" ("ut") - the affix of belonging in the Gryz language.  At the same time, the rodents called their main village in the form of "Gerez".  According to experts, here the component "ger" - this again means the self-name of the rodents.  Interestingly, the hoofs called the rodents "shered", and the budugs - "hered".  As you can see, in all the above toponyms, the particle "hair", "ger" appears in minor variations.  This makes it possible to conclude that the "heri" - "hari" - "geri", from which modern hernias originated, are associated with Albanian tribes, which in ancient sources are referred to as "er".  And from here comes the connection with the homeland of these tribes - the historical region of Hereti (Hereti), which was located between the rivers Alazani (Ganich) and Iori (Gabyrra).  Apparently, when, as a result of the fall of Caucasian Albania, Iberia began to expand its borders to the east, after which part of the indigenous Albanian population of Hereti became Georgian, and another part, including the ancestors of modern rodents and Khinalygs, did not submit to the Georgian princes and migrated to Shahdag.  As Day.Az reports with reference to Azerhistory, the ancestors of modern rodents and Khinalygs, as well as other related Albanian ethnic groups, adopted Sunni Islam and for a long time were part of the state of the Shirvanshahs, from the XVI century - the state of the Safavids, and from the middle of the XVIII century - the Khanate of Guba.  NUMBER * * * * * In the first half of the nineteenth century, residents of the villages nearby to the village of Gryz - Hapitly, Elikli, Yerkudzhlu, Dzhekli villages began to move to the flat part of the Guba district in connection with the intensive development of marina plantations and formed a number of settlements here.  In addition, the khapits founded 4 villages in the Guba district, 5 in Goychay and Shamakhi districts, and 2 in Nukha district. * * * * * In the 1980s, there were 1,433 khapits in the Khapit villages of the Mushkur Plain within the Guba district, according to the census, in 6 khapit villages of Goychay and Shamakhi districts. Shamakhi uyezds - 71,013.  In the 30-40s of the XIX century, as a result of the transformation of winter pastures and pastures into sowing marens in these places, a total of 58 Gryz settlements arose, of which 35 were created by immigrants from the village of Gryz, and 23 - from the village of Jack.  * * * * * In the 80s of the same century, the total population of the Gryz on the Mushkur Plain reached 5,100 people.  The vast majority of the descendants of these settlers to the plain later settled in several villages of the Khachmaz district. * * * * * In the 80s of the XIX century, there were 61 Gryz villages in the Guba district, where 6137 residents were noted.  If we add here more than 2140 khapits who settled in other Azerbaijani counties, it turns out that the total number of the population of Gryz by the end of the XIX century approached 8.5 thousand.  However, even then, the rodents who migrated to the plains were subjected to significant assimilation.  * * * * * Due to strong assimilation, in the course of the census of 1886, rodents were indicated either by Azerbaijanis or Lezgins.  This census recorded a total of 178 people in the villages of Jack, Yerkudzh and Khapit, while 558 residents of the village of Gryz and 454 residents of the village of Elik were listed as Lezgins. * * * * In the first general census of the population of the Russian Empire in 1897, the Rodents, like other Shahdag nationalities, were not marked as separate peoples, but indicated in the column "mountain peoples of the Caucasus" ". * * * * In the course of the first All-Union census of the USSR in 1926, 2600 rodents were noted.  The social life of the hernias, like that of other mountain peoples, bore strong imprints of the patriarchal communal order.  At the same time, the social system and socio-economic development of rodents were significantly influenced by the feudal relations of the states in which they were part. * * * * * Due to the prevailing patriarchal-feudal relations, sown lands and livestock were considered private property, and pastures and hayfields were considered communal.  In the management of the free community, the main role was played by the council of tribal elders, without which no important issue was resolved.  * * * * * The elders of the tribes resolved disputes and conflicts between tribes on the basis of customary law, discussed everyday issues of the community.  Along with the Council of Elders, village headmen participated in the management of the free Hryz community on behalf of the Shirvanshahs, and later the Guba khan. * * * * * In the mountain hernias, patriarchal communal relations prevailed, and among the settlers to the lowland territories - feudal relations.  Among mountain hernias, remnants of traditional tribal and patriarchal relations persisted until recently.  This was manifested in the quarterly division of the Gryz villages and in the folding of the settlements on the Mushkur Plain by separate genera.  * * * * * Traditionally, there was a custom of blood feuds between individual herring families.  To reconcile the bloodlines resorted to such measures as replacing the murder with the payment of a sum of money, the kinship of warring clans.  If reconciliation efforts failed, elders intervened.  Occasionally, if the loss was particularly severe, even the efforts of the elders were unsuccessful, and the bloodshed on both sides continued.  One of the ancient customs of rodents, as with other mountain peoples of the Caucasus, has always been hospitality.  From time immemorial, the guest was revered on an equal footing with family members, considered as an inviolable person; the expression “God ’ s guest ” has long been used.  Wealthy people built special houses for guests, and those who were poorer, allocated a special room in their house; these rooms were cleaned with carpets, stored new bedding and utensils, and kept locked in anticipation of the guest.  It does not matter whether a relative is a guest, an acquaintance or a stranger, it was not customary to ask him who he was, where he was coming from and when he intended to leave the house.  In case of any danger to the guest, the owner was obliged to protect him with his weapon, in case of a robbery of the guest - to compensate for the damage, and in case of his murder - to take revenge on the relatives of the killer.  The * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *  Most of the necessities of life were produced within the economy, and only a small part of the products and household items were purchased or exchanged.  The main occupation of the herds was cattle breeding, primarily sheep breeding.  This is due to the natural conditions of the highland territory of the traditional settlement of rodents, where the scarcity of suitable land for cultivation and an unfavorable climate did not allow to satisfy even minimal needs at the expense of agriculture.  * * * * The slopes of Shahdag were excellent pastures, replete with nutritious fodder.  Winter pastures were rented on the Caspian plain territories.  Sheep breeding gave wool, leather, from which clothes, bedding, nightmares and some other household items, meat and milk, as well as fat for lighting and manure (kizyak) for heating the dwelling were made. * * * * Along with animal husbandry, domestic crafts were traditionally developed in rodents, especially the manufacture of shawls and carpets.  Women in their free time weaved shawls, stockings, onuchi and wraps, gloves, and on the letovki - carpet products.  Gryzskie carpets with their unique ornament due to the beauty of the patterns and the perfection of the composition enjoyed fame throughout

passages.title: The most unusual settlements in the world, where people manage to live
passages.passage: The population of the independent state of Sealand is one person / Photo: scrolltoday.com 1.  Cappadocia in Turkey In Turkish Cappadocia apartment buildings hollowed out directly in the rocks / Photo: funart.pro Owners of unusual houses are happy to demonstrate them to tourists / Photo: muz4in.net 2.  Chinese monastery Xuankun-si almost hangs on the slope / Photo: fregataero.ru In Greece on the tops of the so-called pillars of Meteors there are several monasteries / Photo: 123ru.net In the Spanish monastery of Montserrat to get quite difficult / Photo: teg.com.ua Opposite San Pedro on the very edge of the cliff are almost hanging houses / Photo: Twitter 3.  Villages in places with extremely low temperatures In northern Oymyakon, a record low temperature was recorded at around -70 degrees / Photo: mapme.club In Matmata, because of the unbearable heat, people live in semi-underground buildings of round shape, in which there is always coolness / Photo: travel-dom.ru In Al-Hajar, houses were built specifically on the rocks for safety and rescue from the heat / Photo: straitstimes.com Our world is ambiguous and constantly surprising.  In particular, this applies to places where people live on a permanent basis.  And there are no obvious reasons for the formation of such settlements.  Overpopulation is not observed here, since they were formed long ago, when on the planet you could choose absolutely any corner for settlement.  Most likely, those who settled here, pursued the goal of protecting themselves or to get the opportunity to seclude.The most strange of all the settlements, which is at the same time a country, can be called the Principality of Sealand.  The rather loud name hides only a platform located in the North Sea.  It was Bates, a major from Great Britain, who elevated it to the rank of an independent state.  Of the population only one citizen, but the history of the country is quite rich.  In other countries, in places that are not understood by ordinary people, a much larger number of people.In this area, people settled directly in the rocks.  The terrain is almost mystical. Housing hollowed out right in the mountains.  In the end, they changed their shape.  These are not just caves, but full-fledged apartments and even multi-apartment houses.  In some settlements there are already brick extensions, which absolutely does not spoil the overall picture.  The owners of these houses are happy to show them to tourists.  True, there are abandoned, dilapidated dwellings in the rocks in Turkey, which people left due to a number of natural phenomena, collapses.  Housing built on the very top of a mountain or rock is also not uncommon.  In the world of such villages there are several, and often they have a relationship with monasteries. In China, on Mount Heng, almost on a steep slope, there is a monastery Xuankun-si.  The place is not for the faint of heart and not everyone would have decided to live there.  A similar situation is observed in Greece.  Here, on the very tops of the so-called Meteor pillars, there is not one monastery, but several.  In Spain, in the mountains, where it is extremely difficult to get, built the monastery of Montserrat, and in Cuenca – the monastery of San Pedro.  At the very edge of the cliff, opposite San Pedro, there are practically hanging houses.  Apparently, their residents are not afraid of heights. There are two such settlements on the planet - Oymyakon and Verkhoyansk.  The strangeness is that in winter the air temperature here drops to minus fifty to sixty degrees.  But the record was also recorded – about minus seventy.  Why people continue to live here remains a mystery to many.  In Tunisia, there is a city called Matmata, where the summer is too hot.  The population here lives in semi-underground buildings of round shape, in which there is always cool.In Yemen, in the city-fortress, which is called Al-Hajar, the inhabitants themselves built up the rocks in which they built their homes. passages.title: Monsanto's second defeat
passages.passage: The second defeat in the US court suffered in the last 8 months Monsanto Company.  On Wednesday, the Federal District of San Francisco ordered the world leader of plant biotechnology to pay more than $80 million to Edwin Hardman.  The 70-year-old farmer, who for 25 years sprayed the most famous herbicide Monsanto Roundup on his site, was diagnosed with cancer of the lymphatic system.  During the trial, which lasted a month, the jury ruled that the plaintiff developed cancer as a result of the use of Roundup (the main active ingredient of which is glyphosate) and that Monsanto did not properly inform consumers about the dangers of its products.  German chemical company Bayer, which owns Monsanto Company today, said it was "disappointed by the jury's decision" and would appeal the verdict.  In the United States, another 11,000 Roundup lawsuits are on the way; six hearings are scheduled this year alone.  Since its purchase of Monsanto last June, Bayer has lost more than 45% of its market value.  The news of the second verdict further plunged into the "red" actions of the chemical giant.  The first person to win the case against Monsanto was school gardener Diwayne Johnson, who used the herbicide extensively.  In August last year, a California court ordered to pay him more than $289 million, later the amount of compensation was reduced to $78 million.

passages.title: Bayer lost the first stage of the court in the United States in the case of a potentially carcinogenic herbicide Roundup
passages.passage: This content was published on March 20, 2019.  9: 26 in San Francisco.  March 20.  German chemical company Bayer AG lost the first stage of the trial in the United States in the case of a potentially carcinogenic herbicide Roundup, developed by the American company Monsanto, which since June last year came under the control of Bayer.  According to The Wall Street Journal, a jury in San Francisco ruled that plaintiff Edwin Hardeman contracted cancer as a result of the use of the herbicide Roundup.  During the first stage, only evidence of the potential harm of Roundup and its active substance, glyphosate, was considered.  In the second phase of the trial, which begins on March 20, six jurors must determine whether Monsanto should be held accountable.  Their decision could mean significant financial losses for Monsanto and Bayer, as their turn is waiting for about 11.2 thousand related to Roundup claims.  According to Bloomberg Intelligence analyst Holly Froome, the aggregate payments for all claims could exceed $5 billion.  Another six hearings are already scheduled for 2019.  Shares of Bayer fell more than 10% at the opening of trading in Frankfurt on Wednesday, then the fall slowed to 9.9%.  In August last year, a court in the United States ruled that Bayer should pay $289.2 million to school gardener Diwayne Johnson, who contracted cancer as a result of the use of the herbicide Roundup.  A few months later, the amount was reduced to $78.5 million as a result of Bayer ’ s appeal.  During the second stage, as in the case of D. Johnson, the jury will have to consider the role of Monsanto in concealing data on the dangers of glyphosate.  According to the plaintiffs, the company did not warn buyers of its products that herbicides can lead to cancer.  There is no consensus on the effects of glyphosate, the most common element in herbicides.  The International Agency for Research on Cancer considers this substance "probably carcinogenic", while the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) of the United States claims that glyphosate is safe when used cautiously. passages.title: Bayer recalled from the market one of the best-selling drugs: what happened
passages.passage: The well-known German pharmaceutical company Bayer announced the withdrawal from the market of a thousandth batch of one of the best-selling drugs - drugs against hemophilia - due to erroneous labeling.  This was reported on the portal Pharma.net.ua.  It is noted that the vials were labeled as containing the drug for the treatment of hemophilia Kogenate FS, but in fact they were filled with Jivi – blood clotting factor VIII.  Although both Kogenate FS and Jivi belong to the replacement therapy of hemophilia A, there is one significant difference - Kogenate FS is approved for the treatment of adults and children with hemophilia A, while Jivi is intended only for adults and adolescents aged at least 12 years who have previously been treated.  The company said that the error was discovered in mid-July and most of the bottles came out with the correct marking.  The amount of the drug with the error was 990 bottles and they appeared on sale only in the United States.  Jivi and Kogenate FS are among Bayer ’ s most sought-after drugs.  In the first quarter of 2019, their total sales reached $213 million.  As reported by OBOZREVATEL, earlier a court in the United States recognized that the herbicide Roundup based on glyphosate of the German company Bayer led to cancer.  Don't miss the lightning!
