passages.title: Death in the garden: an American corporation found guilty of selling a carcinogenic herbicide
passages.passage: When the elderly Pilliod of California heard the fatal diagnosis of non-Hodgkin lymphoma, they did not know that a few years later they would win a lawsuit against Monsanto, the world ’ s largest producer of chemicals for the agro-industrial complex.  However, this trial was only the tip of the iceberg, because thousands of Americans with cancer caused by Monsanto products are ready to file similar lawsuits.  Izvestia found out what transnational corporations are ready to do for billions of dollars in profits.  The manufacturer does not warn Alberta and Alva Pilliod began using Monsanto's Roundup herbicide to kill weeds in 1975.  Roundup was a novelty: Monsanto employee John Franz synthesized the active ingredient of the herbicide, glyphosate, only in 1970.  The couple bought Roundup for four decades, until in 2011 Alva heard a diagnosis of non-Hodgkin lymphoma, a cancer of the lymphatic system with lesions of the bones, including the spine.  Four years later, non-Hodgkin lymphoma was found in his wife Alberta, but with brain damage.  In 2017, the couple filed a lawsuit against Monsanto, based on the fact that two years earlier, the International Agency for Research on Cancer at the WHO announced the probable carcinogenicity of glyphosate.  In addition, their claim was not the first: at that time, the courts had already considered several similar complaints.  The case was accelerated due to the poor health of the plaintiffs, who at that time were already in their 70s, and on May 14, 2019, the jury decided after five weeks of consideration that Monsanto violated the law by not warning buyers about the likely risks, in connection with which it must pay a fine of $2 billion and $55 million in damages in favor of the plaintiffs.  This is the eighth highest fine in the history of the United States.  Monsanto Roundup sprayers in a garden shop Photo: REUTERS / Yves Herman Representatives of the owner of Monsanto - the German concern Bayer - said that they do not agree with the decision and will appeal because "all the world's leading health organizations agree on the safety of glyphosate and its non-carcinogenicity" It seems that justice has been served, greedy industries the nics got what they deserved, and the ordinary people who suffered from their actions left as winners.  If not for a few “but ”: first, victory in court will not save the lives of cancer patients.  And, secondly, the compensation awarded to them to the Pilliod spouses will not receive soon and in the wrong volumes.  The fact is that, according to a 2016 ruling of the US Supreme Court, the amount of the fine cannot exceed the amount of compensation for damage by more than nine times.  Thus, even if the appellate court reduces the amount of punitive payments to the maximum possible, the Pilliod spouses will receive, in addition to their compensatory $55 million, only $495 million.  This is the most favorable outcome for the plaintiffs.  Throughout the process, Monsanto ’ s lawyers argued that their products were harmless, as confirmed by research from the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), a federal agency that develops and monitors compliance with environmental and human health standards.  Moreover, in April, the EPA confirmed its initial findings, saying that while glyphosate use does entail some environmental risks, the agency ’ s findings on its impact on human health are consistent with those of other federal agencies.  “If we are going to feed 10 billion people by 2050, we will need all the tools at our disposal, including glyphosate, ” U.S. Secretary of Agriculture Sonny Purdue said in a statement.  Monsanto ’ s defense was largely based on the findings of an EPA study, and Bayer said after the verdict that the decision would not have been so harsh if the scientists ’ findings had been taken into account.  According to the defendant, Alva and Alberta Pilliod suffered from various diseases for a long time, which became the main factor in the development of cancer.  The concern also noted that if it were not for glyphosate, which is poured into fields to destroy weeds, the soil would have to be plowed regularly, which is expensive and harmful to the environment, since a large amount of carbon dioxide is emitted due to the overturning of the earth.  During the judicial investigation, it turned out that those conclusions of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), which the company refers to more than once as a justification for the safety of Roundup, can be questioned.  Demonstrators protest against Bayer Monsanto on the Place de la République in Paris Photo: REUTERS / Philippe Wojazer At the disposal of CNN was the correspondence of a Monsanto employee with one of the Agency officials Jess Rowland.  In it, a federal employee notes that if he can “kill ” glyphosate research at the Agency for the Registration of Toxic Substances and Diseases, he will“ deserve a medal. ”  Monsanto employees in internal correspondence note a low probability that Rowland and the EPA will be able to stop the study of another agency, but note that there is hope.  Judging by the fact that the Agency for the Registration of Toxic Substances never released a study on glyphosate, Rowland, already happily retired, coped with the task.  The Pilliod case is the third trial Bayer has faced over Monsanto products, particularly glyphosate-containing Roundup.  In all three cases, the jury ruled in favor of the plaintiffs with oncology, which developed due to prolonged contact with herbicides.  The first lawsuit against Monsanto was considered by the court last year.  In August, a San Francisco jury awarded $289 million to a former school gardener who was diagnosed with late-stage cancer.  However, a few months later, the judge reduced this amount to $78 million.  The case did not end there, as Bayer filed an appeal.  As a result, after almost a year, the cancer claimant still did not receive the compensation awarded to him.  In March this year, a California resident was awarded $80 million after he sued Monsanto for developing non-Hodgkin lymphoma.  The result is predictable: Bayer appealed, far from the outcome.  Thus, the concern is currently awaiting a decision on three appeals due to Monsanto products.  In addition, there are about 130,000 such claims under consideration in the United States.  And even for a giant like Bayer, it ’ s a pretty sensitive punch.  Bayer acquired 100% of Monsanto in 2018 for $63.5 billion, becoming the largest agricultural concern.  Since the first Roundup carcinogenicity conviction, the conglomerate has lost nearly 46% of its market value and its share price has fallen to 2012 levels.  According to The Fortune, Bayer shareholders told the company ’ s CEO Werner Baumann, who made the merger deal with Monsanto, of no confidence.  He was given nine months to prove that he deserved his place.  Glyphosate is currently the most popular herbicide in the world, despite the fact that after the report of the Agency for Research on Cancer, first France and then other European countries raised the issue of using this substance to combat weeds, and then began to remove it from store shelves.  Despite this, in 2017, EU countries extended the license for the use of glyphosate in agriculture for five years.  Photo: Global Look Press / Christian Charisius / dpa In Russia, Monsanto is present as a supplier of seeds of traditional breeding of corn, vegetable crops, offers farmers various plant protection products, while some of the products are produced in Russia since 2015.  Also in the country you can freely buy the herbicide Roundup, both wholesale and retail.  In addition, Russian companies produce about a hundred drugs based on glyphosate (the Monsanto patent for the molecule of the substance expired in 2000).  The volume of sales of the substance offered under the trademarks "Hurricane", "Typhoon", "Tornado" and others, is estimated at 15-20 thousand tons per year.  Monsanto is no stranger to scandals with seven-mile-long steps: since the 1980s, the company has been a defendant in cases involving harm to health with dioxin, polychlorinated biphenyls, the EU-banned Alachlor herbicide and Agent Orange defoliant used during the Vietnam War.  In addition, several senior employees of the corporation were found guilty of corruption in 2005; the company admitted that it paid bribes to Indonesian officials between 1997 and 2002.  So why are the US, EU and other countries stubbornly renewing the license to use glyphosate-containing herbicides?  Thanks to the more than $4 million that, according to OpenSecrets, Monsanto spends annually on lobbying?  Or because otherwise you will have to use more expensive ways to control weeds, which will reduce the effectiveness of soil use? bed Red-brown grass after treatment with a herbicide Photo: Depositphotos Probably, each of the reasons can be called correct.  World agriculture is dependent on chemical fertilizers, the former methods of tillage already seem ineffective.  Governments and world leaders are thinking about how to feed millions of people, forgetting that they may be losing their health.  In addition, the harm of glyphosate has not been proven, and this makes it possible to sleep peacefully.

passages.title: Europe ’ s stock markets rise after a sharp drop a day earlier
passages.passage: MOSCOW, May 14 — PRIME.  Europe ’ s main stock indexes are rising on Tuesday after a decline of 1.5% a day earlier, while growth is constrained by weak statistics from Germany, according to trading data.  As of 13.00 MSK, the British FTSE 100 index grew by 0.79%, to 7221.08 points, the French CAC 40 - by 1.01%, to 5315.88 points, the German DAX - by 0.45%, to 11930.15 points.  European markets on Tuesday recouped the fall of the previous day, which reached 1.5% amid the escalation of the trade conflict between the United States and China in the form of a new round of mutual duties.  Investors also paid attention to corporate news.  German automaker Volkswagen has announced that it has decided to resume preparations for the initial public offering (IPO) of the company ’ s truck production unit Traton, which was suspended in March.  The company's shares are rising in price by 1.2%.  At the same time, shares of the German corporation Bayer are falling by more than 2% amid news that a court in the United States awarded a fine of $2 billion to the company in a cancer case.  The jury found it proven that the elderly couple contracted lymphoma due to the fact that for 30 years used a sprayer for weeds Roundup - this brand belongs to Bayer.  The growth of European stock markets is constrained by statistics from Germany from the Center for European Economic Research (Zentrum fuer Europaische Wirtschaftsforschung, ZEW), according to which the index of investor confidence in the German economy in May fell to minus 2.1 points from 3.1 points in April.  Analysts expected the indicator to grow to 5.1 points.

passages.title: Working with comfort: how the leading companies of Ukraine care about their employees | Comments Ukraine
passages.passage: An effective management system is one of the main tasks of a modern company, in which the management of personnel plays a huge role.  In the modern world, working with people is one of the main functions of management and it is on the employees that the success of the company depends.  In order to effectively use the human resources at the disposal of the organization, it is necessary to create conditions for people in which they would like to work for the benefit of themselves and the organization.  Therefore, the social policy of the company, which plays a special role in the formation of motivation of employees, increasing their self-expression in work, is becoming increasingly important.  The publication "Comments" appealed to the leading Ukrainian companies working in various fields to find out what conditions of work they provide so that their employees feel comfortable and safe, how to encourage diligent workers and punish unscrupulous ones, how to motivate the team and stimulate its members to personal development.  The largest retail and retail enterprise in the country, which has 66 hypermarkets with a total area of ​ ​ more than 1 million m2.  This is an omnichannel ecosystem that unites the trade networks "Epicenter" and "New Line", a network of multi-brand sports stores "Intersport-Ukraine", agroholding "Epicenter Agro", factories for the production of ceramic tiles Epicenter Ceramic Corporation, woodworking production - CBM "Osmoloda", logistics facilities, and recently also pharmacies with products. Vymi shops.  The group of companies has 34,000 employees.  Search for candidates for positions in Epicenter The company “Epicenter K ” uses different methods to search for candidates.  First of all, the image of the employer works.  The presence of positive feedback from employees, a comfortable modern office, all these are auxiliary components that help in attracting employees.  Secondly, ads on different kinds of job-sites.  In the case of the IT sphere, these are DOU and Djinni sites.  And if we are talking about the search for managers, accountants, sales employees, lawyers, etc., it is WorkUA and RabotaUA.  In addition, there is a paid resource AmazingHiring.  This is, in fact, a generator of different audience of professionals: "If a person is in social networks, instant messengers, file storages and somewhere you can see what he is doing, this aggregator finds his contact.  Thus, it is possible to get contacts of a huge number of required candidates, - commented in the press service of "Epicenter K".  The range of candidates and positions is very wide.  Depending on what position a person needs, the company also pays attention to personal qualities - soft skills, which sometimes even prevail on professionalism.  "Epicenter" pays attention to what a person has already achieved at his age.  The system of bonuses and penalties in the company Epicenter K The system of bonuses and penalties is available to employees of shopping centers.  In the central office, there is no incentive system as such.  But for good work, they assure the company, they can bonus on an individual basis.  Epicenter K social packages / compensations The company does not have insurance, but the central office has its own medical center, in which employees can be treated free of charge and arrange sick leave.  In addition, the office has a large modern and absolutely free fitness center for employees.  Here you can practice with professional coaches and take part in group classes – pilates, dancing, and much more.  On the territory of the office there are also four modern sports grounds, which, by the way, are allowed to play during working hours.  As for the employees of shopping centers, the company provides them with free meals.  In addition, the company has a system of discounts for employees, which allows you to purchase online goods at special prices.  Given that today the range of "Epicenter" covers almost all product groups - from nails to food, medicines and clothing - for people this is a very significant savings.  In "Epicenter" believe that the most motivates an employee when his salary is above average and does not lag behind the market.  Interesting tasks, a good team, a comfortable place of work and an atmosphere in the team are also important.  All this motivates you to come to work and benefit the company on a daily basis.  Training and development of employees in Epicenter The company has a training center that trains sales staff.  There is also a mandatory internship in shopping centers.  It concerns not only "hall workers", but also employees of the central office.  The main goal of this approach is that a person understands how the company works, due to what he earns, who should be contacted when a particular issue arises, and so on.  Bayer is an international company operating in the fields of health and agriculture.  "Bayer" in Ukraine is part of the global concern "Bayer AG" (Bayer AG).  About 700 professional employees work to create innovative products and knowledge about them for Ukrainian consumers.  The company in Ukraine is represented by the following areas: pharmaceutical division, OTC division and agricultural division.  Search for candidates for positions in Bayer The company uses various options for recruiting personnel - it can be the recommendation of employees, posting vacancies on internal and external specialized sites and, if necessary, attracting external professional recruitment agencies.  In any case, the experience of candidates is studied and analyzed by professional HR business partners, conduct interviews with the involvement of direct managers.  Depending on the level of the position, the management of the relevant unit or function may also participate in the interviews.  During the selection of employees, professional skills and experience are of great importance.  However, it is equally important for the company to choose people who correspond to the values and culture of the company, namely - Leadership, Honesty, Efficiency and Flexibility.  The system of bonuses and penalties in Bayer "Bayer" has a system of bonuses for employees.  The amount of remuneration and the frequency of its payment depends on the category of employee.  Those that directly affect the level of sales – they have a premium for the implementation of plans.  Office workers and company management receive bonuses depending on the results of business activities or the company as a whole, and certain qualitative indicators recorded as global strategies of the corporation.  In addition to the main bonus, employees can receive a bonus for special projects or performing additional tasks that have positively affected the company ’ s results.  The company has a wide package of additional benefits and compensations - this is health insurance, accident insurance, maternity leave benefits, and there are lunches in the office.  Bayer partially compensates for the cost of a gym subscription and there are many other compensations in support of employees.  The company believes that without a common culture and team spirit, the company cannot achieve great goals and results, so one of the tasks of each manager is to promote and support this spirit.  Depending on the needs, it can be a team building, and celebration of achievements, and constant dialogues with employees to understand their motivation and needs, and various types of training.  Depending on the needs of a particular position, the company can pay for language courses and additional training to develop certain skills, also the company has a large base of online training programs for self-development of employees.  During the quarantine period, most meetings take place online, so the company practices stress management sessions for all employees, trainings on how to avoid burnout and maintain work-life balance.  The company also has a development program "School of Manager", which is aimed at supporting novice managers to create an effective team.  Huawei is a high-tech enterprise engaged in the research, development, production and sale of telecommunications equipment, is one of the largest suppliers of network solutions worldwide.  The company has more than 194,000 employees in more than 170 countries and regions, serving more than 3 billion people worldwide.  Search for employees for vacant positions is carried out by various methods: "First of all - among the internal resource, that is, among those of our employees who have shown good results.  We are looking for candidates on LinkedIn, profile sites Work and Work i grc.ua.  Also, the company actively cooperates with many universities, distributes news about the vacancy among students ", - said the portal" Comments "Deputy head of the Department of personnel of the company" Huawei Ukraine "Vladimir Bilavka.  In addition, Huawei has a referral system, that is, employees can recommend their friend, girlfriend, acquaintance or just a colleague with whom they previously studied or worked.  If the recommended person is hired, the employee who made the recommendations will receive a bonus.  The company is looking for candidates on a daily basis.  Since the activity is mainly related to telecommunications, people with significant technical experience are often sought.  You have to look for them on your own.  At the same time, Huawei is the world's leading provider of information and communication technology infrastructure, so they really get a lot of resumes.  If there are no current open positions for such resumes, candidates are asked for permission to enter them into our database and are contacted in case of a relevant vacancy.  The system of bonuses and penalties in Huawei The company offers a variety of bonuses and incentives: both tangible and intangible.  This is an annual bonus, and a bonus for the project or for the best achieved result in a team or company.  In addition, the company gives its employees the opportunity to purchase products with additional discounts.  As already mentioned, the company can encourage recommendations for open vacancies.  There are no material fines

passages.title: "The Transport Issue"
passages.passage: Deputies of the regional parliament indexed payments to adoptive parents, discussed the results of audits for 2019 and the “transport issue ” .It became one of the central topics of discussion at the February meeting of the Legislative Assembly.  It was about the problems in the passenger transportation market.  He is again "feverish" due to the change of players.  Deputies have prepared a request addressed to the Governor. “Complaints have not been received? ” The situation in the passenger transportation market is concerned by both carriers and passengers.  Especially acute problems began to appear on intercity routes, where they have already reduced the number of flights, reduced the number of cars on the route and their capacity, canceled some stops.Deputy request for a whole range of problems was formulated by Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly Dmitry Rozhkov.  He assured: the document was written on the basis, first of all, of numerous appeals of residents.  The Department of Transport changed the characteristics of the rolling stock on route 115, without warning either the administration of ZATO or the local motor transport company.  Seven large buses and one medium were replaced by eight medium buses.  These cars (with a capacity of less than 90 people) can not cope with the large passenger traffic of the morning hours, when about 3.5 thousand residents of Raduzhny go to Vladimir for work or study.  And this, of course, causes people ’ s dissatisfaction.  A critical situation has developed in the Sudogodsky district, in other territories of the region.  Routes there also began to serve a new carrier, whose work does not suit local residents.  They are outraged by the new procedure for holding competitions: “The criteria for trouble-free and long-term work in the field of passenger transportation have depreciated, while secondary requirements related to the technical characteristics of transport (electronic display, sound informer, class of video recorder and others) have become decisive, ” the document states the position of the heads of transport enterprises.  The new mechanism of payment for the services of this GUP threatens carriers with an increase in costs in the amount of 100 to 3000%.  Transport companies complain about the fact that SUE "Vladimir bus station", in their opinion, deliberately creates them financial problems, delaying the transfer of money for tickets sold through the ticket offices.  Entrepreneurs have an opinion that "the leadership of the Department of Transport and Road Facilities (represented by Levin P.V., former head of the State Unitary Enterprise" Vladimir Bus Terminal ", now - Deputy Director of the Department of Transport and Road Facilities) acts in their own interests" .In the hall were the heads of several transport companies and representatives from the territories.  They added very eloquent details and examples to the theses formulated in the request.  Members of Parliament were also aware of many specific issues and concerns.  Perhaps even more so than the director of the profile department Alexei Kosilov.  All his answers were of a very general nature and were reduced to the fact that “everything happens according to the law ” and“ no complaints were received ”.  By an overwhelming majority of votes, the deputies supported the request and sent it to the governor.  The head of the region is obliged to respond and officially clarify his position on all these problems.Hurried? Before the deputies began to consider the main agenda and discuss bills, the chairman of the regional Accounting Chamber Irina Tulyakova made a report to them. She spoke about the main results of the work of auditors for 2019.  It turns out that the inspectors have serious questions about the effectiveness of support for small and medium-sized businesses, investments in state media and in some other directions.But before discussing and analyzing the content of the report, the deputies had to understand why the information contained in it “leaked ” to the media ahead of time.  According to the Law “On the Accounts Chamber of the Vladimir Region ”, the report can be published in the media or posted on the Internet only after it is considered in the Legislative Assembly.  However, some online publications have already published articles with the text of the report of the Accounts Chamber.  According to the chief auditor, the leak occurred from the assistant head of the Communist party faction Maxim Shevchenko.  The assistant published the document in his telegram channel.  The fact is that he received access to the report precisely as an assistant to the deputy - the text for consideration by the people's deputies is sent in advance.  Irina Tulyakova asked to conduct an inspection on the fact of violation of the law.Orphans and educators In the social block of the agenda of the meeting, the deputies considered and adopted changes to the current law on payments to foster parents and foster caregivers.  They were indexed by 3.8%.  In the region, more than 1,200 children are growing up in non-native families.  For each such child, the state pays a certain amount.  From January 1, 2020 (that is, the law adopted in February will apply to the previous month), the following standards were established: one adoptive parent - 6069 rubles per month (now 5847 rubles), the second - 3034 rubles (now 2923 rubles), the only - 9103 rubles (now 8770 rubles). left without parental care.  In addition, an additional allowance was provided for those who took care of a disabled child or brings up 6 or more foster children.Till approvedAlexander Bayer, the acting first deputy governor who oversees issues on the development of infrastructure, housing and utilities and energy, did not get rid of the “console ”.  According to the regional law, the approval of vice-governors is the prerogative of the Legislative Assembly.  Governor Vladimir Sipyagin for a long time did not submit the candidacies of his deputies to the regional parliament, so they considered and discussed them in detail only in December last year.  In the road and housing and communal services - the sphere of competence of the first vice-governor - a lot of problems have accumulated.  At the February meeting, the deputies voted against the approval of Alexander Bayer for the post of first deputy governor.  During the "postponement" of problems in the areas of responsibility of Bayer, according to the deputies, only increased.  The governor has the right to submit Bayer's candidacy to the regional parliament again.

passages.title: Russia: Environmental issues turn into political issues
passages.passage: For the second month in Russia, the scandal continues around the Yadrovo test site near Moscow in the city of Volokolamsk, where mass poisoning of children occurred due to emissions from the test site, after which rallies began.  Protests continue in mid-April, and the city authorities, meanwhile, intend to introduce a state of emergency and solve the problem with the landfill.  The situation in Volokolamsk is a sign of a deeper problem, which is associated with the annual growth of industrial and consumer waste in the country, which has nowhere to go.  The state to solve the problem announced garbage reform, which for various reasons has stalled.  The environmental crisis, meanwhile, has begun a transition into a political channel, which does not bode well for the authorities, experts say.  According to Rosstat, from 2006 to 2016, the formation of production and consumption waste in the country increased by 55% to 5.4 billion tons per year, and in comparison with 2003 - by 108%.  Data for 2017 are not available.  The special representative of the President of the Russian Federation on environmental protection, ecology and transport Sergey Ivanov at the end of 2016 estimated at 100 billion tons the volume of accumulated in the country for all time undisposed waste.  The accumulation of waste appears to be related to the underdeveloped recycling market.  Secondary use, according to the Ministry of Natural Resources, is limited to the processing of 50% of industrial waste and 10% of municipal waste.  Everything else is sent to landfills and buried in landfills.  In turn, representatives of Rosprirodnadzor said in 2016 that the existing capacities of the landfills will be enough to receive new waste for another 3-4 years.  The most acute situation with the loading of landfills is in the Central, North-Western, Volga, Siberian and North Caucasian districts.  The lack of space not only at landfills, but also at landfills, is stated in the “Final report of the ONF for the Year of Ecology 2017 ”.  “There are almost no free and suitable places for waste disposal, ” the authors write.  The situation is aggravated by the spread of illegal garbage dumps, which usually appear in forests.  At the end of 2017, Sergei Ivanov estimated the number of illegal dumps in the country at 60 thousand (it is assumed that the number of legal dumps is 4 thousand).  The cost of eliminating environmental damage from their work, he estimated at “trillions of rubles. ”  Political scientist Georgy Bovt is convinced that the work of illegal dumps is carried out with the tacit permission of the regional authorities.  “There are very specific people here.  Municipal authorities simply cannot fail to be a part of it.  For the sake of curiosity, ask in the search engine “garbage collection ”.  You will receive dozens of proposals, most of which will be related to illegal business, ” he writes in his column.  “The profitability of the shadow business associated with waste, only slightly lost [until 2016] revenues from drug trafficking, ” said Deputy Minister of Natural Resources Artem Sidorov.  Hazards to nature and health Landfills and landfills contain a considerable amount of waste that is hazardous to nature and health.  According to the latest report of Rosprirodnadzor, published in February 2018, at the beginning of 2016 in Russia there were 743 objects with a particularly harmful impact on the environment.  And these are only those that were at that time on the account of the department.  Due to the lack of separate garbage collection, extremely toxic materials fall into the garbage dumps, including mercury (from lamps and thermometer), nickel, cadmium and lead (from batteries and accumulators), etc.  The country has no capacity to accommodate or dispose of such waste, follows from the data of the meeting of the board of the Ministry of Natural Resources on plans for 2018.  Every year, the volume of waste of the second and first hazard classes (highly hazardous and extremely hazardous) increases by 300 thousand and 30 thousand tons, respectively.  In addition to waste officially recognized as dangerous, landfills, according to the ONF report, get cheap types of packaging, which “can have a strong negative impact on nature and health. ”  “For example, foamed polystyrene, which is almost not processed and when heated emits carcinogens.  In addition, manufacturers of goods often use multicomponent packaging, that is, consisting of and assembled from various materials, which, due to the need for additional separation into components, are usually ignored by processors as unprofitable and as a result they are sent to landfill, ” the report says.  According to the analytical department of the Federation Council, the contribution of environmental problems to public health is estimated by different specialists in the range of 10-50%, and in the near future “due to the progressive environmental crisis and the low level of material provision of medical institutions ” this contribution will grow to 60% or more.  However, according to the requirements of the World Health Organization, this contribution should not exceed 25%.  To solve the problem in 2015, Russia launched a reform in the field of waste management, which involves the gradual abandonment of burial in favor of recycling.  According to the idea of the government, manufacturers and importers of certain goods must either process the waste themselves or pay an environmental fee to the budget, with the money of which the state is going to build processing plants and organize a system of separate reception of garbage.  However, on the one hand, the collection rate was below the expectations of the state, and, on the other hand, state bodies for more than two years of reform, according to the ONF, could not combine their efforts and distribute powers among themselves.  In this regard, according to the authors of the report, the situation in this area has practically not changed.  Against this background, the authorities continue to develop plans for the construction of incinerators, which contradicts the ideas of reform.  In particular, four such enterprises are planned to be built in the Moscow region, another in Tatarstan.  However, according to ONF, the new plants in the Moscow region will not cope with the influx of garbage from the capital.  Their total capacity is 2.8 million tons per year, while the actual formation of only municipal waste in Moscow, subject to export to other subjects, is 6 million tons, the report says.  Moreover, three of the four plots allocated for the plants are located in a densely populated recreational area, which causes discontent among the local population, according to the report of the Council for the Development of Civil Society and Human Rights under the President of the Russian Federation.  “To date, neither Rosprirodnadzor nor the population has the necessary information about the detailed characteristics of the incinerators planned for construction and convincing evidence of their safety for the environment and the health of citizens, ” the report says.  As a result of the operation of these plants, ash and slag will be formed in the amount of 30% of the initial volume of waste, which have a higher hazard class and require placement on special landfills.  According to Nikolai Kichigin, associate professor at the Higher School of Urban Studies, there is nothing wrong with burning garbage (in some European countries, according to him, up to 50% of garbage is burned), but provided that the garbage is carefully sorted before this.  But in Russia, this condition has not yet been met.  In addition to the environmental crisis, problems with garbage, according to some experts, caused political difficulties.  According to political scientist Lilia Shevtsova, the events in Volokolamsk, caused by the mass poisoning of children, became one of the reasons for the “blow to the new presidency [of Vladimir Putin]. ”  Rallies in Volokolamsk are a sign of “changes in public consciousness and a serious challenge to the authorities, ” said Maxim Artemyev, an associate professor at the Russian State Humanitarian Institute.  “Environmental issues are at the forefront of the agenda of political and public life.  A few years ago in Italy, the garbage collection crisis in Naples was one of the reasons for the fall of the government of Roman Prodi, ” he said.

passages.title: Detecting plastic particles in water bottles
passages.passage: Tests on large company water bottles show that almost all of them contain tiny plastic particles.  In the largest study of its kind, 250 bottles purchased in nine different countries were tested.  The study, led by the press organization Orb Media, found that on average, there are 10 plastic particles per liter of water, each wider than a human hair (more than 100 microns) in diameter.  Manufacturers whose products were tested told the BBC that their factories operate to the highest standard.  The experiments were conducted at New York State University in Fredonia.  Sherry Mason, a chemistry professor at the university who conducted the analysis, told the BBC: “Bottle after bottle, Mark after Mark had plastic particles. ”  “The goal is not to make certain brands conspicuous; this experiment shows that the problem is universal, and plastic has become such a pervasive material in our society that it has found its way into all of the products we consume. ”  There is currently no evidence that microplastics are harmful, but understanding the potential consequences is a matter of scientific investigation.  Commenting on the results, Professor Mason said: “The numbers we see are not catastrophic, but they are a cause for concern.  Experts told the BBC that people in countries where tap water is likely to be contaminated should continue to use bottled water.  Playback of this file on your device is not supported.  Thousands of plastic particles in drinking water bottles from manufacturers have responded to the BBC by insisting that their products meet the highest standards of safety and quality.  They also noted the lack of regulations regulating microplastics and their standard testing practices.  Professor Mason found plastic particles in samples of tap water last year, and other researchers have found them in seafood, beer, sea salt and even air.  The new study comes amid further attention to the increasing penetration of plastic materials into nature following the BBC's second series "Blue Planet", in which Sir David Attenborough highlighted the threat of plastic waste in the oceans.  Aquaphina, Dasani, Evian, Nesli Pure Life and San Pellegrino as internationally recognized products, and Aqua (Indonesia), Bisleri (India), Opura (Mexico), Gerolsteiner (Germany), Minalba (Brazil) and Vahaha (China) as national products were reviewed in this study.  The number of particles smaller than 100 microns (one thousandth of a millimeter per micron) was much higher than the number of particles larger than 100 microns, which averaged 314 particles per liter.  The chemical composition of this group of smaller particles was not confirmed, but Professor Mason said they could also be expected to be plastic.  One obvious question was how the plastic got into the water.  One theory is that due to the amount of polypropylin used in production in the bottle, the process of opening the bottle may cause it to leak into the water.

**Report:**

A total of 130,000 Roundup cases are under consideration in the United States against Bayer [2e190a2b-468a-400a-a1b7-7c137ccfeed9]. 


Bayer acquired 100% of Monsanto in 2018 for $63.5 billion, becoming the largest agricultural concern [2e190a2b-468a-400a-a1b7-7c137ccfeed9]. 


Since the first Roundup carcinogenicity conviction, the conglomerate has lost nearly 46% of its market value and its share price has fallen to 2012 levels [2e190a2b-468a-400a-a1b7-7c137ccfeed9]. 


Bayer shareholders told the company's CEO Werner Baumann, who made the merger deal with Monsanto, of no confidence [2e190a2b-468a-400a-a1b7-7c137ccfeed9]. 


He was given nine months to prove that he deserved his place [2e190a2b-468a-400a-a1b7-7c137ccfeed9]. 


Glyphosate is currently the most popular herbicide in the world, despite the fact that after the report of the Agency for Research on Cancer, first France and then other European countries raised the issue of using this substance to combat weeds, and then began to remove it from store shelves [2e190a2b-468a-400a-a1b7-7c137ccfeed9]. 


In 2017, EU countries extended the license for the use of glyphosate in agriculture for five years [e7e49238-e932-4dde-a2e6-0280531a2e6e]. 


In Russia, Monsanto is present as a supplier of seeds of traditional breeding of corn, vegetable crops, offers farmers various plant protection products, while some of the products are produced in Russia since 2015 [2e190a2b-468a-400a-a1b7-7c137ccfeed9]. 


Russian companies produce about a hundred drugs based on glyphosate (the Monsanto patent for the molecule of the substance expired in 2000) [2e190a2b-468a-400a-a1b7-7c137ccfeed9]. 


The volume of sales of the substance offered under the trademarks "Hurricane", "Typhoon", "Tornado" and others, is estimated at 15-20 thousand tons per year [2e190a2b-468a-400a-a1b7-7c137ccfeed9]. 


Monsanto has been a defendant in cases involving harm to health with dioxin, polychlorinated biphenyls, the EU-banned Alachlor herbicide and Agent Orange defoliant used during the Vietnam War [2e190a2b-468a-400a-a1b7-7c137ccfeed9]. 


Several senior employees of the corporation were found guilty of corruption in 2005; the company admitted that it paid bribes to Indonesian officials between 1997 and 2002 [2e190a2b-468a-400a-a1b7-7c137ccfeed9]. 


The company is currently awaiting a decision on three appeals due to Monsanto products [2e190a2b-468a-400a-a1b7-7c137ccfeed9]. 


In addition to the Roundup cases, Bayer has faced other lawsuits, including one related to its Xarelto blood thinner, which was withdrawn from the market due to erroneous labeling [b433c7fb-bed1-4b2c-a4bc-5b65cb9aa348]. 


The company announced the withdrawal from the market of a thousandth batch of one of the best-selling drugs - drugs against hemophilia - due to erroneous labeling [b433c7fb-bed1-4b2c-a4bc-5b65cb9aa348]. 


The vials were labeled as containing the drug for the treatment of hemophilia Kogenate FS, but in fact they were filled with Jivi – blood clotting factor VIII [b433c7fb-bed1-4b2c-a4bc-5b65cb9aa348]. 


The company said that the error was discovered in mid-July and most of the bottles came out with the correct marking [b433c7fb-bed1-4b2c-a4bc-5b65cb9aa348]. 


The amount of the drug with the error was 990 bottles and they appeared on sale only in the United States [b433c7fb-bed1-4b2c-a4bc-5b65cb9aa348]. 


Jivi and Kogenate FS are among Bayer’s most sought-after drugs [b433c7fb-bed1-4b2c-a4bc-5b65cb9aa348]. 


In the first quarter of 2019, their total sales reached $213 million [b433c7fb-bed1-4b2c-a4bc-5b65cb9aa348]. 


The company has a system of bonuses for employees [01f4529c-bb7b-4742-8e59-071f1464d1c1]. 


The amount of remuneration and the frequency of its payment depends on the category of employee [01f4529c-bb7b-4742-8e59-071f1464d1c1]. 


Those that directly affect the level of sales – they have a premium for the implementation of plans [01f4529c-bb7b-4742-8e59-071f1464d1c1]. 


Office workers and company management receive bonuses depending on the results of business activities or the company as a whole, and certain qualitative indicators recorded as global strategies of the corporation [01f4529c-bb7b-4742-8e59-071f1464d1c1]. 


In addition to the main bonus, employees can receive a bonus for special projects or performing additional tasks that have positively affected the company’s results [01f4529c-bb7b-4742-8e59-071f1464d1c1]. 


The company has a wide package of additional benefits and compensations - this is health insurance, accident insurance, maternity leave benefits, and there are lunches in the office [01f4529c-bb7b-4742-8e59-071f1464d1c1]. 


Bayer partially compensates for the cost of a gym subscription and there are many other compensations in support of employees [01f4529c-bb7b-4742-8e59-071f1464d1c1]. 


The company believes that without a common culture and team spirit, the company cannot achieve great goals and results, so one of the tasks of each manager is to promote and support this spirit [01f4529c-bb7b-4742-8e59-071f1464d1c1]. 


The company has a development program "School of Manager", which is aimed at supporting novice managers to create an effective team [01f4529c-bb7b-4742-8e59-071f1464d1c1]. 


During the quarantine period, most meetings take place online, so the company practices stress management sessions for all employees, trainings on how to avoid burnout and maintain work-life balance [01f4529c-bb7b-4742-8e59-071f1464d1c1]. 


The company also has a large base of online training programs for self-development of employees [01f4529c-bb7b-4742-8e59-071f1464d1c1]. 


In the case of Bayer, the company has faced several lawsuits related to its Roundup herbicide, including one in which a California court ordered the company to pay $2 billion in damages to a couple who claimed that their use of the product caused their cancer [2e190a2b-468a-400a-a1b7-7c137ccfeed9]. 


The couple, Alva and Alberta Pilliod, were awarded $55 million in compensatory damages and $2 billion in punitive damages [2e190a2b-468a-400a-a1b7-7c137ccfeed9]. 


Bayer has also faced other lawsuits related to its Roundup herbicide, including one in which a jury in San Francisco ruled that the company must pay more than $80 million to a man who claimed that his use of the product caused his cancer [fbeefdd0-f410-4630-82fc-bb061c00eed6]. 


The man, Edwin Hardeman, was diagnosed with non-Hodgkin's lymphoma after using Roundup for 25 years [fbeefdd0-f410-4630-82fc-bb061c00eed6]. 


The jury found that Monsanto, which is now owned by Bayer, did not properly inform consumers about the dangers of its products [fbeefdd0-f410-4630-82fc-bb061c00eed6]. 


Bayer has appealed the verdict and the case is ongoing [fbeefdd0-f410-4630-82fc-bb061c00eed6]. 


In addition to the lawsuits, Bayer has also faced criticism for its handling of the Roundup herbicide, including allegations that the company knew about the potential health risks of the product but failed to disclose them to consumers [2e190a2b-468a-400a-a1b7-7c137ccfeed9]. 


The company has also faced criticism for its lobbying efforts, including allegations that it has spent millions of dollars to influence policy makers and regulators [2e190a2b-468a-400a-a1b7-7c137ccfeed9]. 


Bayer has also faced criticism for its environmental record, including allegations that its production of Roundup has contributed to the decline of bee populations and the contamination of waterways [2e190a2b-468a-400a-a1b7-7c137ccfeed9].

Title: "International Industry" Herbicide Law Dispute Bayer $2 Billion Settlement - Finance
Content: Bayer, the German chemical company, said on Wednesday that a legal dispute over cancer caused by its Roundup brand herbicide has reached a $2 billion settlement with regulators.  Bayer acquired Monsanto for $63 billion in 2018, taking over the company ’ s business and litigation.  Bayer says decades of research have shown that Roundup herbicides and glyphosate are safe for human use.  Wednesday ’ s settlement also includes claims for individuals exposed to Roundup herbicides and diagnosed with non-Hodgkin ’ s lymphoma in the future.  Under the agreement, Bayer will provide $2 billion for four years and for diagnostic assistance; each individual requesting a claim will receive up to $200,000.  The settlement is subject to approval by the San Francisco Court.  Under the amended agreement, any individual who has not filed a claim within a four-year period can appeal to the court for a better outcome.  Bayer has faced more than 100,000 lawsuits in the United States for its herbicide.  (Times Information)

Title: Bayer reported a bad quarter due to the pandemic and lawsuits « Russian Pharmaceuticals
Content: Bayer reported an unsuccessful quarter due to the pandemic and lawsuits Bayer published a report for the third quarter, according to which revenue and sales of the company decreased.  The pharmaceutical industry of the corporation tried as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic and legal proceedings.  German chemical-pharmaceutical transnational corporation Bayer published a report for the third quarter of 2020 fiscal year, which states that the manufacturer of medicines suffered due to the coronavirus pandemic, resulting in net losses of the company amounted to $3.2 billion, and revenue decreased by 4.2% to $36.8 billion.  In general, Bayer sales in the third quarter fell by 13.5% compared to the same period of 2019 - to $9.9 billion.  Sales in the pharmaceutical sector decreased by 6.1%, reaching $4.9 billion.  Among the positive aspects, we can note the increase in sales of oral anticoagulant "Xarelto" by 13.8%, which has a special demand in Germany and Russia; ophthalmic drug "Eilea", actively sold in China; anti-cancer drug "Stivarga" by 17.5%, especially in the United States.  COVID-19 is said to have exacerbated the problems Bayer faced after its acquisition of agricultural company Monsanto two years ago.  This summer, the pharmaceutical company pledged to pay $10.9 billion in court compensation for cancer patients from the herbicide Roundup, which went to Bayer from Monsanto.  More than 125,000 people filed their claims.  However, it has not yet been established whether this herbicide causes cancer.  Bayer said it would need an additional $750 million to pay off the debt.  Against the background of litigation, the shares of the drug manufacturer fell to record low values (by 43% since the beginning of the year).  In the second quarter, net losses amounted to $11 billion due to the need to pay compensation.  The company has already paid off its debt in 80,000 lawsuits.  Bayer CFO Wolfgang Nickle stressed that the third quarter was difficult mainly due to problems in the agricultural sector of the corporation.  The company is gradually restoring its position in the field of production of medicines.  Photo: Bayer AG Vladimir Zabolotskikh pharmvestnik

Title: Most of Europe ’ s stock markets are rising, Italy is in the red due to budget disputes with the EU
Content: Most of Europe's stock markets are rising, Italy is in the red due to disputes with the EU over the budget Western European stock indexes are mainly rising during trading on Tuesday amid company reporting and statistics.  In addition, market participants hope for progress in resolving trade disputes between the United States and China.  The only significant exception is Italy, with investors worried about its disputes with Brussels over next year ’ s budget.  The composite index of the largest enterprises in the region Stoxx Europe 600 is growing for the first time in three sessions, by 11: 45 QoQ it rose by 0.6%, to 364.06 points.  According to media reports, Vice Premier Liu He will visit the United States to prepare for a meeting of the leaders of the two countries at the G20 summit in Argentina in late November.  During telephone conversations on Friday, Liu He and U.S. Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin did not agree on options for a rapprochement.  The British FTSE 100 grew by 0.5%, the French CAC 40 - by 0.4%, the German DAX added 0.7%.  The Italian FTSE MIB declined by 0.1%.  The Italian government has until the end of the day on Tuesday to send the European Commission a revised draft budget.  According to La Stampa and Il Sole 24 Ore, Rome is not going to make concessions on public spending and budget deficits, but probably admits that the measures taken will not have such a strong positive impact on the economy, as previously claimed.  The Ministry of Finance of Italy can reduce the estimate of growth for next year from 1.5% to 1.3% or even 1.2%, the latter option will correspond to the forecast of the European Commission itself.  Despite the lack of changes in terms of the budget deficit, Italian Prime Minister Giuseppe Conte hopes that the new version of the document will at least partially satisfy Brussels, writes Il Messagero.  According to the Italian newspaper, Deputy Prime Minister Luigi Di Maio and Matteo Salvini insist on maintaining the original version of the budget.  On Tuesday, data on the UK labour market were released.  The unemployment rate in July-September unexpectedly rose to 4.1%, while it was expected to remain at around 4%.  At the same time, the rate of increase in the average wage in this period accelerated to the maximum since 2008 - 3.2% in annual terms.  In Germany, inflation in October accelerated to a maximum in 10 years - 2.5% in annual terms, according to the final data.  The capitalization of the German chemical company Bayer increased by 2.6%.  Adjusted EBITDA in the third quarter amounted to 2.2 billion euros and was higher than market expectations.  At the same time, the management of Bayer assured investors that the acquisition of American Monsanto for $63 billion will improve financial performance.  Top managers also promised to continue fighting lawsuits against Monsanto in connection with the herbicide Roundup, which, according to the plaintiffs, contributed to the development of cancer and other diseases.  Quarterly reporting supported a jump in the price of Vodafone shares by 6.5%.  The British telecommunications group recorded an operating loss of 2.07 billion euros in April-September due to losses on the sale of Vodafone India. Title: Herbicide cancer-causing controversy again: whether China's manufacturing and agriculture will be affected
Content: Image copyright AFP Image caption A large amount of pesticides are sprayed in Argentina's soybean fields.  A jury in the United States has ruled that the ingredients of one of the world's most commonly used herbicides are a "key factor" in causing cancer in a man.  What impact does this have on mainland China and Taiwan?  But German chemical and pharmaceutical giant Bayer has strongly denied claims that its Monsanto unit, Roundup, which makes glyphosate ingredients, causes cancer.  But a jury in San Francisco ruled unanimously that the product caused California resident Edwin Hardman to develop non-Hodgkin's lymphoma.  The next phase of the court trial will consider the issue of damages and liability for Bayer products.  At this stage of the trial, Hardman ’ s lawyers are expected to provide evidence of Bayer ’ s efforts to influence scientists, regulators and the public ’ s perception of the safety implications of its products.  After the news came to light, Bayer's share price plunged about 12 percent.  1,200 related cases In 2018, Germany's Bayer company bought US rival Monsanto for $66 billion, and Monsanto's product Roundup was also part of the acquisition.  Bayer said it was disappointed by the ruling.  The company will present evidence of the safety of Monsanto ’ s products, as well as a strong belief in scientific proof that glyphosate-based herbicides do not cause cancer.  The case is only the second of about 1,200 lawsuits against Roundup in the United States.  In August 2018, a California court jury found another California man was awarded $289 million in damages because Roundup caused his cancer.  The ruling in the case at the time also caused Bayer's share price to plummet.  The case was later reduced to 78 million dollars, and Bayer is still appealing the case.  As an agricultural power, China, GM and Roundup have become the largest producer and exporter of glyphosate in the world, and are also one of the largest users of glyphosate.  More than half of glyphosate produced in China is exported, including the Roundup herbicide that Monsanto manufactures and distributes globally.  At the same time, China also imports a lot of processed glyphosate.  According to statistics, Roundup products account for 80% of herbicide products in China.  Glyphosate use and consumption are mainly concentrated in some agricultural countries, especially large countries that produce genetically modified crops.  There are thousands of glyphosate pesticide products in mainland China.  In Taiwan and Hong Kong, there are also Roundup sales, which in Taiwan is translated as “Spring of the Year ”.  Image copyright Getty Images Image caption Monsanto's popular glyphosate product Roundup sells worldwide.  In Taiwan, its translation is Spring of the Year.  What is glyphosate and is it dangerous?  Glyphosate is a herbicide invented by Monsanto in 1974, but its patent expired in 2000.  It is currently the highest selling pesticide in the world.  In 2015, the World Health Organization's International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) concluded that glyphosate "may be carcinogenic."  However, the EPA insists that careful use of glyphosate is safe.  The European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) also said glyphosate is unlikely to cause cancer.  However, due to the excessive use of glyphosate, improper spraying of glyphosate has a lot of incidents that directly lead to human poisoning.  In addition, glyphosate has been found in rain, rivers, agricultural products, food (including beer, bread, etc.), meat products and human bodies, leading to an international campaign against the use of glyphosate.  In November 2017, the European Union decided to extend the license for glyphosate use for five years.  California lists glyphosate as a chemical known to cause cancer.  But the agricultural industry is opposed to putting such a label on glyphosate.

Content: The French government approved the decision of the American jury, which sentenced the biotechnology corporation Monsanto to pay $289 million to American Dwayne Johnson. State Secretary of the French Ministry of Ecology, Brune Poiarson, commented on the decision: “We did not wait for the historic decision of the American court to take action.  France voted against the extension of the permit for the use of glyphosate in Europe, and we are trying to mobilize other European states to share our position. ”  French Environment Minister Nicolas Hulot called on Europeans and Americans to take part in the “war against pesticides ”.  The decision of the California court was also welcomed by the Confederation of French Peasants.  “This decision once again confirms that pesticides are dangerous to health, especially for those who use them, that is, for peasants, ” said Laurent Pinatel, a representative of the Confederation, recalling Emmanuel Macron ’ s promise to ban the use of pesticides by 2021.  Despite France ’ s efforts, the European Commission recently extended the license for glyphosate for another five years.  Glyphosate due to its cheapness and ease of use is very widespread and is often used to control weeds.  In 2015, the International Agency for Research on Cancer and the WHO Cancer Agency concluded that the substance is “probably carcinogenic to humans. ”  The lawsuit of Dewayne Johnson, who was diagnosed with non-Hodgkin ’ s lymphoma in 2014, is the first glyphosate case to go to trial.  In the United States, Monsanto has already filed about five thousand similar lawsuits.  German pharmaceutical group Bayer, which recently acquired the Monsanto group, continues to argue that the herbicide Roundup is “reliable and not carcinogenic ” and is going to appeal the court ’ s decision.  In the light of subsequent events, the court ’ s decision does not seem final.  As previously reported, in June of this year, Bayer closed the acquisition of Monsanto http: / / www.monsantoglobal.com / global / en / newsviews / Pages / bayer-closes-monsanto-acquisition.aspx “LEVERCOUSEN (June 7, 2018) – On Thursday, Bayer successfully completed the acquisition of Monsanto to.  Shares of the American company will no longer be traded on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE), as Bayer became the sole owner of Monsanto.  Monsanto shareholders will receive a payment of $128 per share of the company.  Investment bank J.P. Morgan assisted Bayer in securing payment for the largest transaction in the company ’ s history.  According to the preliminary approval of the US Department of Justice, Monsanto ’ s integration into Bayer will occur after the completion of the sale of part of the assets to BASF. As a leader in innovation for agriculture, we are a promising employer and offer employees opportunities for professional development, ” said Werner Baumann, Chairman of the Board of Management of Bayer.  “Our goals for sustainable agriculture are no less important than financial growth.  We understand that leadership entails responsibility in the field of doing business and establishing an open dialogue with society. ”  And here is the latest news: it is officially announced that the conditions for the start of Monsanto integration have been met.  .https: / / monsanto.com / news-releases / bayer-conditions-beginning-monsanto-integration-filled / ” Leverkusen, August 16, 2018 – Monsanto ’ s integration into the Bayer Group may begin after Bayer ’ s handover to BASF of some Crop Science businesses with total sales of around 2.2 billion euros.  One of the requirements of the US Department of Justice was that Bayer and Monsanto remain separate companies and continue to operate independently until the completion of these divestments at BASF, and it finally happened.  As previously reported, Bayer expects the acquisition to make a positive contribution to core earnings per share starting in 2019, with a double-digit percentage from 2021.  Since 2022, annual contributions of $1.2 billion have been made.  In addition, it is estimated that US $1 million will be invested in EBITDA before special items are planned on a synergistic basis.  Moreover, Bayer will continue to strengthen its commitment to sustainability.  As for the verdict on glyphosate in California on August 10, 2018, Bayer believes that the jury ’ s decision contradicts the weight of scientific evidence, decades of real world experience and the conclusions of regulators around the world, which confirm that glyphosate is safe and its use does not cause non-Hodgkin ’ s lymphoma.  Recently, the National Institutes of Health (NIH) confirmed that glyphosate does not cause cancer.  The US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA), the European Chemicals Agency (ECHA) and other regulatory bodies around the world have also concluded that glyphosate can be used safely.  The jury ’ s verdict is only the first step in this case, and it remains the subject of post-trial motions in the court of first instance and appeal, as Monsanto announced.  The continuation of the story, according to Bayer, will be that the courts will eventually find that Monsanto and glyphosate are not responsible for Mr. Johnson ’ s disease.  Due to the above-mentioned requirements established by the US Department of Justice, Bayer did not have access to detailed internal information at Monsanto.  Under these circumstances, Bayer was not allowed to influence Monsanto ’ s business affairs, and its ability to actively comment on them in detail was extremely limited.  Today, however, Bayer has been able to actively engage in advocacy efforts in glyphosate trials and any other legal disputes, such as potential damage claims in connection with the Dicamba product. ”  The Germans are now involved in the dispute.  They probably don ’ t want to pay anything.  Is it possible that they will drag the courts to Germany under local jurisdiction? Since then, Bayer shares have lost more than 10 percent.  Asked whether Bayer would consider settling cases out of court, CEO Werner Baumann said: “We will actively defend this case and all pending cases. ”  He also said on Thursday that “as of the end of July, the number of plaintiffs in both state and federal lawsuits is approximately 8,000.  These numbers may increase or decrease over time. ”  According to Baumann, when Bayer bought Monsanto, he “could not have foreseen the scale of the current lawsuits. ”  The $63 billion acquisition was completed in June.  The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) says glyphosate is unlikely to be carcinogenic.  Glyphosate is an active ingredient in Monsanto ’ s Roundup, which is the most popular weed killer in the US. ”  So, it's still ahead.

Title: Turkey will not leave the observation post surrounded by the Syrian army in Idlib
Content: Turkish soldiers stand on a hill overlooking the Syrian city of Kobani, near Suruk, on the border between Turkey and Syria © AP Photo / Vadim Ghirda Turkish soldiers stand on a hill overlooking the Syrian city of Kobani, near Suruk, on the border between Turkey and Syria ANTAKYA (Turkey), Aug 22 – RIA Novosti.  Turkey does not intend to leave its observation post for the de-escalation zone in the Syrian village of Murek, which was surrounded by the Syrian army, Turkish Foreign Ministry spokesman Hami Aksoy told RIA Novosti.  The Syrian government army occupied the city of Khan Sheikhoun in the south of the province of Idlib, now the city is being stripped and demined, a Syrian field source told RIA Novosti earlier on Thursday.  On Wednesday evening, the Syrian army closed a siege around the cities of Latmane, Kafr Zeita, Latmin and Murik in the north of Hama province south of the city of Khan Shaykhun, a local military source told RIA Novosti.  The cities are under the fire control of the army.  “The ninth observation post of Turkey in the village of Murek will remain in its place, despite the establishment of the control of the Syrian army over the city of Khan Shaykhun, ” said Aksoy.  The diplomat did not answer the question of how the observation post will continue to exist when the Syrian army takes control of Murek.  After the talks on Syria in Nur-Sultan on August 2, the "ceasefire" came into force in Idlib.  The command of the armed forces of the Syrian Arab Republic said that it would stop the fighting if Turkey fulfilled its obligations under the Russian-Turkish agreement reached in September 2018 in Sochi.  The main point was the withdrawal of heavy and medium weapons militants 20 kilometers from the demilitarized zone in Idlib.  Three days later, on August 5, the army resumed the operation due to the failure of the gangs to fulfill the conditions, which, taking advantage of the lull, made attempts to attack the positions of the Syrian army in the north of Hama province and repeatedly opened fire on residential settlements in the area.

Title: Грызы: one of the most original nationalities of Azerbaijan - INTERESTING FACTS - PHOTOS
Content: Herzy is one of the small indigenous peoples of Azerbaijan.  In the 1980s, the study of the etymology of the toponym "Gryz" was deeply engaged in a prominent Azerbaijani ethnographer G.A.Heybullayev, who came to the conclusion that the ancestors of this people were the ancient Albanian tribes of the Er.  In the course of ethnographic research close to the hernias by origin and language, it turned out that the latter called themselves "har" ("her"), while the inhabitants of the village of Elik who spoke the same language called them "horud", and the inhabitants of the village of Jack - "cherud".  In this case, the components "chorus" - "cher" - "har" - to the self-name of the hopyts, and "ud" ("ut") - the affix of belonging in the Gryz language.  At the same time, the rodents called their main village in the form of "Gerez".  According to experts, here the component "ger" - this again means the self-name of the rodents.  Interestingly, the hoofs called the rodents "shered", and the budugs - "hered".  As you can see, in all the above toponyms, the particle "hair", "ger" appears in minor variations.  This makes it possible to conclude that the "heri" - "hari" - "geri", from which modern hernias originated, are associated with Albanian tribes, which in ancient sources are referred to as "er".  And from here comes the connection with the homeland of these tribes - the historical region of Hereti (Hereti), which was located between the rivers Alazani (Ganich) and Iori (Gabyrra).  Apparently, when, as a result of the fall of Caucasian Albania, Iberia began to expand its borders to the east, after which part of the indigenous Albanian population of Hereti became Georgian, and another part, including the ancestors of modern rodents and Khinalygs, did not submit to the Georgian princes and migrated to Shahdag.  As Day.Az reports with reference to Azerhistory, the ancestors of modern rodents and Khinalygs, as well as other related Albanian ethnic groups, adopted Sunni Islam and for a long time were part of the state of the Shirvanshahs, from the XVI century - the state of the Safavids, and from the middle of the XVIII century - the Khanate of Guba.  NUMBER * * * * * In the first half of the nineteenth century, residents of the villages nearby to the village of Gryz - Hapitly, Elikli, Yerkudzhlu, Dzhekli villages began to move to the flat part of the Guba district in connection with the intensive development of marina plantations and formed a number of settlements here.  In addition, the khapits founded 4 villages in the Guba district, 5 in Goychay and Shamakhi districts, and 2 in Nukha district. * * * * * In the 1980s, there were 1,433 khapits in the Khapit villages of the Mushkur Plain within the Guba district, according to the census, in 6 khapit villages of Goychay and Shamakhi districts. Shamakhi uyezds - 71,013.  In the 30-40s of the XIX century, as a result of the transformation of winter pastures and pastures into sowing marens in these places, a total of 58 Gryz settlements arose, of which 35 were created by immigrants from the village of Gryz, and 23 - from the village of Jack.  * * * * * In the 80s of the same century, the total population of the Gryz on the Mushkur Plain reached 5,100 people.  The vast majority of the descendants of these settlers to the plain later settled in several villages of the Khachmaz district. * * * * * In the 80s of the XIX century, there were 61 Gryz villages in the Guba district, where 6137 residents were noted.  If we add here more than 2140 khapits who settled in other Azerbaijani counties, it turns out that the total number of the population of Gryz by the end of the XIX century approached 8.5 thousand.  However, even then, the rodents who migrated to the plains were subjected to significant assimilation.  * * * * * Due to strong assimilation, in the course of the census of 1886, rodents were indicated either by Azerbaijanis or Lezgins.  This census recorded a total of 178 people in the villages of Jack, Yerkudzh and Khapit, while 558 residents of the village of Gryz and 454 residents of the village of Elik were listed as Lezgins. * * * * In the first general census of the population of the Russian Empire in 1897, the Rodents, like other Shahdag nationalities, were not marked as separate peoples, but indicated in the column "mountain peoples of the Caucasus" ". * * * * In the course of the first All-Union census of the USSR in 1926, 2600 rodents were noted.  The social life of the hernias, like that of other mountain peoples, bore strong imprints of the patriarchal communal order.  At the same time, the social system and socio-economic development of rodents were significantly influenced by the feudal relations of the states in which they were part. * * * * * Due to the prevailing patriarchal-feudal relations, sown lands and livestock were considered private property, and pastures and hayfields were considered communal.  In the management of the free community, the main role was played by the council of tribal elders, without which no important issue was resolved.  * * * * * The elders of the tribes resolved disputes and conflicts between tribes on the basis of customary law, discussed everyday issues of the community.  Along with the Council of Elders, village headmen participated in the management of the free Hryz community on behalf of the Shirvanshahs, and later the Guba khan. * * * * * In the mountain hernias, patriarchal communal relations prevailed, and among the settlers to the lowland territories - feudal relations.  Among mountain hernias, remnants of traditional tribal and patriarchal relations persisted until recently.  This was manifested in the quarterly division of the Gryz villages and in the folding of the settlements on the Mushkur Plain by separate genera.  * * * * * Traditionally, there was a custom of blood feuds between individual herring families.  To reconcile the bloodlines resorted to such measures as replacing the murder with the payment of a sum of money, the kinship of warring clans.  If reconciliation efforts failed, elders intervened.  Occasionally, if the loss was particularly severe, even the efforts of the elders were unsuccessful, and the bloodshed on both sides continued.  One of the ancient customs of rodents, as with other mountain peoples of the Caucasus, has always been hospitality.  From time immemorial, the guest was revered on an equal footing with family members, considered as an inviolable person; the expression “God ’ s guest ” has long been used.  Wealthy people built special houses for guests, and those who were poorer, allocated a special room in their house; these rooms were cleaned with carpets, stored new bedding and utensils, and kept locked in anticipation of the guest.  It does not matter whether a relative is a guest, an acquaintance or a stranger, it was not customary to ask him who he was, where he was coming from and when he intended to leave the house.  In case of any danger to the guest, the owner was obliged to protect him with his weapon, in case of a robbery of the guest - to compensate for the damage, and in case of his murder - to take revenge on the relatives of the killer.  The * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *  Most of the necessities of life were produced within the economy, and only a small part of the products and household items were purchased or exchanged.  The main occupation of the herds was cattle breeding, primarily sheep breeding.  This is due to the natural conditions of the highland territory of the traditional settlement of rodents, where the scarcity of suitable land for cultivation and an unfavorable climate did not allow to satisfy even minimal needs at the expense of agriculture.  * * * * The slopes of Shahdag were excellent pastures, replete with nutritious fodder.  Winter pastures were rented on the Caspian plain territories.  Sheep breeding gave wool, leather, from which clothes, bedding, nightmares and some other household items, meat and milk, as well as fat for lighting and manure (kizyak) for heating the dwelling were made. * * * * Along with animal husbandry, domestic crafts were traditionally developed in rodents, especially the manufacture of shawls and carpets.  Women in their free time weaved shawls, stockings, onuchi and wraps, gloves, and on the letovki - carpet products.  Gryzskie carpets with their unique ornament due to the beauty of the patterns and the perfection of the composition enjoyed fame throughout

Title: The most unusual settlements in the world, where people manage to live
Content: The population of the independent state of Sealand is one person / Photo: scrolltoday.com 1.  Cappadocia in Turkey In Turkish Cappadocia apartment buildings hollowed out directly in the rocks / Photo: funart.pro Owners of unusual houses are happy to demonstrate them to tourists / Photo: muz4in.net 2.  Chinese monastery Xuankun-si almost hangs on the slope / Photo: fregataero.ru In Greece on the tops of the so-called pillars of Meteors there are several monasteries / Photo: 123ru.net In the Spanish monastery of Montserrat to get quite difficult / Photo: teg.com.ua Opposite San Pedro on the very edge of the cliff are almost hanging houses / Photo: Twitter 3.  Villages in places with extremely low temperatures In northern Oymyakon, a record low temperature was recorded at around -70 degrees / Photo: mapme.club In Matmata, because of the unbearable heat, people live in semi-underground buildings of round shape, in which there is always coolness / Photo: travel-dom.ru In Al-Hajar, houses were built specifically on the rocks for safety and rescue from the heat / Photo: straitstimes.com Our world is ambiguous and constantly surprising.  In particular, this applies to places where people live on a permanent basis.  And there are no obvious reasons for the formation of such settlements.  Overpopulation is not observed here, since they were formed long ago, when on the planet you could choose absolutely any corner for settlement.  Most likely, those who settled here, pursued the goal of protecting themselves or to get the opportunity to seclude.The most strange of all the settlements, which is at the same time a country, can be called the Principality of Sealand.  The rather loud name hides only a platform located in the North Sea.  It was Bates, a major from Great Britain, who elevated it to the rank of an independent state.  Of the population only one citizen, but the history of the country is quite rich.  In other countries, in places that are not understood by ordinary people, a much larger number of people.In this area, people settled directly in the rocks.  The terrain is almost mystical. Housing hollowed out right in the mountains.  In the end, they changed their shape.  These are not just caves, but full-fledged apartments and even multi-apartment houses.  In some settlements there are already brick extensions, which absolutely does not spoil the overall picture.  The owners of these houses are happy to show them to tourists.  True, there are abandoned, dilapidated dwellings in the rocks in Turkey, which people left due to a number of natural phenomena, collapses.  Housing built on the very top of a mountain or rock is also not uncommon.  In the world of such villages there are several, and often they have a relationship with monasteries. In China, on Mount Heng, almost on a steep slope, there is a monastery Xuankun-si.  The place is not for the faint of heart and not everyone would have decided to live there.  A similar situation is observed in Greece.  Here, on the very tops of the so-called Meteor pillars, there is not one monastery, but several.  In Spain, in the mountains, where it is extremely difficult to get, built the monastery of Montserrat, and in Cuenca – the monastery of San Pedro.  At the very edge of the cliff, opposite San Pedro, there are practically hanging houses.  Apparently, their residents are not afraid of heights. There are two such settlements on the planet - Oymyakon and Verkhoyansk.  The strangeness is that in winter the air temperature here drops to minus fifty to sixty degrees.  But the record was also recorded – about minus seventy.  Why people continue to live here remains a mystery to many.  In Tunisia, there is a city called Matmata, where the summer is too hot.
