Title: Russia: Environmental issues turn into political issues
Content: For the second month in Russia, the scandal continues around the Yadrovo test site near Moscow in the city of Volokolamsk, where mass poisoning of children occurred due to emissions from the test site, after which rallies began.  Protests continue in mid-April, and the city authorities, meanwhile, intend to introduce a state of emergency and solve the problem with the landfill.  The situation in Volokolamsk is a sign of a deeper problem, which is associated with the annual growth of industrial and consumer waste in the country, which has nowhere to go.  The state to solve the problem announced garbage reform, which for various reasons has stalled.  The environmental crisis, meanwhile, has begun a transition into a political channel, which does not bode well for the authorities, experts say.  According to Rosstat, from 2006 to 2016, the formation of production and consumption waste in the country increased by 55% to 5.4 billion tons per year, and in comparison with 2003 - by 108%.  Data for 2017 are not available.  The special representative of the President of the Russian Federation on environmental protection, ecology and transport Sergey Ivanov at the end of 2016 estimated at 100 billion tons the volume of accumulated in the country for all time undisposed waste.  The accumulation of waste appears to be related to the underdeveloped recycling market.  Secondary use, according to the Ministry of Natural Resources, is limited to the processing of 50% of industrial waste and 10% of municipal waste.  Everything else is sent to landfills and buried in landfills.  In turn, representatives of Rosprirodnadzor said in 2016 that the existing capacities of the landfills will be enough to receive new waste for another 3-4 years.  The most acute situation with the loading of landfills is in the Central, North-Western, Volga, Siberian and North Caucasian districts.  The lack of space not only at landfills, but also at landfills, is stated in the “Final report of the ONF for the Year of Ecology 2017 ”.  “There are almost no free and suitable places for waste disposal, ” the authors write.  The situation is aggravated by the spread of illegal garbage dumps, which usually appear in forests.  At the end of 2017, Sergei Ivanov estimated the number of illegal dumps in the country at 60 thousand (it is assumed that the number of legal dumps is 4 thousand).  The cost of eliminating environmental damage from their work, he estimated at “trillions of rubles. ”  Political scientist Georgy Bovt is convinced that the work of illegal dumps is carried out with the tacit permission of the regional authorities.  “There are very specific people here.  Municipal authorities simply cannot fail to be a part of it.  For the sake of curiosity, ask in the search engine “garbage collection ”.  You will receive dozens of proposals, most of which will be related to illegal business, ” he writes in his column.  “The profitability of the shadow business associated with waste, only slightly lost [until 2016] revenues from drug trafficking, ” said Deputy Minister of Natural Resources Artem Sidorov.  Hazards to nature and health Landfills and landfills contain a considerable amount of waste that is hazardous to nature and health.  According to the latest report of Rosprirodnadzor, published in February 2018, at the beginning of 2016 in Russia there were 743 objects with a particularly harmful impact on the environment.  And these are only those that were at that time on the account of the department.  Due to the lack of separate garbage collection, extremely toxic materials fall into the garbage dumps, including mercury (from lamps and thermometer), nickel, cadmium and lead (from batteries and accumulators), etc.  The country has no capacity to accommodate or dispose of such waste, follows from the data of the meeting of the board of the Ministry of Natural Resources on plans for 2018.  Every year, the volume of waste of the second and first hazard classes (highly hazardous and extremely hazardous) increases by 300 thousand and 30 thousand tons, respectively.  In addition to waste officially recognized as dangerous, landfills, according to the ONF report, get cheap types of packaging, which “can have a strong negative impact on nature and health. ”  “For example, foamed polystyrene, which is almost not processed and when heated emits carcinogens.  In addition, manufacturers of goods often use multicomponent packaging, that is, consisting of and assembled from various materials, which, due to the need for additional separation into components, are usually ignored by processors as unprofitable and as a result they are sent to landfill, ” the report says.  According to the analytical department of the Federation Council, the contribution of environmental problems to public health is estimated by different specialists in the range of 10-50%, and in the near future “due to the progressive environmental crisis and the low level of material provision of medical institutions ” this contribution will grow to 60% or more.  However, according to the requirements of the World Health Organization, this contribution should not exceed 25%.  To solve the problem in 2015, Russia launched a reform in the field of waste management, which involves the gradual abandonment of burial in favor of recycling.  According to the idea of the government, manufacturers and importers of certain goods must either process the waste themselves or pay an environmental fee to the budget, with the money of which the state is going to build processing plants and organize a system of separate reception of garbage.  However, on the one hand, the collection rate was below the expectations of the state, and, on the other hand, state bodies for more than two years of reform, according to the ONF, could not combine their efforts and distribute powers among themselves.  In this regard, according to the authors of the report, the situation in this area has practically not changed.  Against this background, the authorities continue to develop plans for the construction of incinerators, which contradicts the ideas of reform.  In particular, four such enterprises are planned to be built in the Moscow region, another in Tatarstan.  However, according to ONF, the new plants in the Moscow region will not cope with the influx of garbage from the capital.  Their total capacity is 2.8 million tons per year, while the actual formation of only municipal waste in Moscow, subject to export to other subjects, is 6 million tons, the report says.  Moreover, three of the four plots allocated for the plants are located in a densely populated recreational area, which causes discontent among the local population, according to the report of the Council for the Development of Civil Society and Human Rights under the President of the Russian Federation.  “To date, neither Rosprirodnadzor nor the population has the necessary information about the detailed characteristics of the incinerators planned for construction and convincing evidence of their safety for the environment and the health of citizens, ” the report says.  As a result of the operation of these plants, ash and slag will be formed in the amount of 30% of the initial volume of waste, which have a higher hazard class and require placement on special landfills.  According to Nikolai Kichigin, associate professor at the Higher School of Urban Studies, there is nothing wrong with burning garbage (in some European countries, according to him, up to 50% of garbage is burned), but provided that the garbage is carefully sorted before this.  But in Russia, this condition has not yet been met.  In addition to the environmental crisis, problems with garbage, according to some experts, caused political difficulties.  According to political scientist Lilia Shevtsova, the events in Volokolamsk, caused by the mass poisoning of children, became one of the reasons for the “blow to the new presidency [of Vladimir Putin]. ”  Rallies in Volokolamsk are a sign of “changes in public consciousness and a serious challenge to the authorities, ” said Maxim Artemyev, an associate professor at the Russian State Humanitarian Institute.  “Environmental issues are at the forefront of the agenda of political and public life.  A few years ago in Italy, the garbage collection crisis in Naples was one of the reasons for the fall of the government of Roman Prodi, ” he said.

Title: Detecting plastic particles in water bottles
Content: Tests on large company water bottles show that almost all of them contain tiny plastic particles.  In the largest study of its kind, 250 bottles purchased in nine different countries were tested.  The study, led by the press organization Orb Media, found that on average, there are 10 plastic particles per liter of water, each wider than a human hair (more than 100 microns) in diameter.  Manufacturers whose products were tested told the BBC that their factories operate to the highest standard.  The experiments were conducted at New York State University in Fredonia.  Sherry Mason, a chemistry professor at the university who conducted the analysis, told the BBC: “Bottle after bottle, Mark after Mark had plastic particles. ”  “The goal is not to make certain brands conspicuous; this experiment shows that the problem is universal, and plastic has become such a pervasive material in our society that it has found its way into all of the products we consume. ”  There is currently no evidence that microplastics are harmful, but understanding the potential consequences is a matter of scientific investigation.  Commenting on the results, Professor Mason said: “The numbers we see are not catastrophic, but they are a cause for concern.  Experts told the BBC that people in countries where tap water is likely to be contaminated should continue to use bottled water.  Playback of this file on your device is not supported.  Thousands of plastic particles in drinking water bottles from manufacturers have responded to the BBC by insisting that their products meet the highest standards of safety and quality.  They also noted the lack of regulations regulating microplastics and their standard testing practices.  Professor Mason found plastic particles in samples of tap water last year, and other researchers have found them in seafood, beer, sea salt and even air.  The new study comes amid further attention to the increasing penetration of plastic materials into nature following the BBC's second series "Blue Planet", in which Sir David Attenborough highlighted the threat of plastic waste in the oceans.  Aquaphina, Dasani, Evian, Nesli Pure Life and San Pellegrino as internationally recognized products, and Aqua (Indonesia), Bisleri (India), Opura (Mexico), Gerolsteiner (Germany), Minalba (Brazil) and Vahaha (China) as national products were reviewed in this study.  The number of particles smaller than 100 microns (one thousandth of a millimeter per micron) was much higher than the number of particles larger than 100 microns, which averaged 314 particles per liter.  The chemical composition of this group of smaller particles was not confirmed, but Professor Mason said they could also be expected to be plastic.  One obvious question was how the plastic got into the water.  One theory is that due to the amount of polypropylin used in production in the bottle, the process of opening the bottle may cause it to leak into the water.

passages.title: Klimt's stolen masterpiece found 23 years ago, but still questionable - International
passages.passage: Twenty-three years ago, Gustav Klimt ’ s Portrait of a Lady was stolen from the Ricci Oddi Gallery of Modern Art in Piacenza, Italy.  On February 22, 1997, the gallery was being renovated for a special exhibition.  The painting mysteriously disappeared, only the outer frame of the painting was found by the roof skylight. When the police determined that the thief removed the frame, the entire painting was rolled up and carried out of the skylight, but no suspects were found. In 2014, the Italian police reopened the investigation and found the suspected painting, but it was later confirmed to be a fake or a copy.  In December last year, a gardener at the Ricci Oddi Gallery found a plastic bag inside the sandwich of the wall, which turned out to be the famous painting.  At that time, everyone suspected that this was the original painting.  After careful examination by experts, it was announced to the outside on Friday that it was confirmed to be the original painting.  In the future, the police still have to clarify the suspicion of the theft, such as: Is the painting hidden in the gallery from the beginning to the end?  Or was it returned after being stolen?  Who did it again?  (Photo / Associated Press) The Ricci Oddi Gallery sent police officers to guard the painting, which was protected by a specially made frame, when it announced the news.  Prosecutor Ornella Chicca said excitedly: "After infrared radiation and other non-invasive detection methods, we are excited to determine that this is the real Klimt."  Klimt completed this masterpiece in 1917, the last year of his life, and the Ricci Oddi Gallery acquired it in 1925 until it was stolen in 1997.  The expert said that the painting is in good condition, only the edge of the canvas is slightly damaged, and it is suspected that the suspect left traces when he hurriedly removed the frame.  (China Times Newsletter)

passages.passage: A painting by Gustav Klimt, a famous Austrian artist, discovered after decades at the site of the robbery, is on display again in its former location.  In February 1997, a painting by Gustav Klimt was stolen from the Ricci Odi art gallery in Piacenza.  The painting, known as “Portrait of a Young Woman, ” was the gallery ’ s most valuable work.  The painting was discovered at the scene of the robbery.  Workers at the Ricci Odi Gallery in Piacenza, after cleaning the outer wall of the gallery, came upon a secret door containing a portrait of a young woman.  Workers discovered the artwork while it was placed in a plastic bag.  Upon the discovery of the painting, the thieves admitted that they had returned the artwork to the scene of the theft.  After one of Caravaggio ’ s paintings stolen from a church in Sicily in 1969, it is considered the second most valuable art stolen in Italy.  The portrait of a young woman doubled in value when, shortly before it disappeared, an art student noticed that the portrait of the young woman had been painted on the portrait of another young woman.  It became the only painting by Gustav Klimt in the art world that has been painted twice.  Due to the closure of galleries and museums in Italy due to the spread of the coronavirus, it has not been possible for the public to visit the work in person, and officials of the Ricci Odi Gallery have provided the opportunity to visit the painting in its former exhibition.  Upon the return of the painting, the gallery ’ s director, Massimo Ferrari, referred to it as part of his gallery identity. passages.title: 23 year old Klimt painting accidentally found in stolen museum
passages.passage: A painting by Austrian painter Klimt was stolen from an Italian art museum nearly 23 years ago, but it was accidentally recovered when a gardener cleaned the ivy on the exterior of the museum.  But exactly why this painting is hidden in the alcove of the outer wall of the museum is still a mystery.  Italian authorities have confirmed that the painting found last December at the Ricci Oddi Gallery of Modern Art in the northern Italian city of Piacenza is indeed the “Portrait of a Lady ” by Gustav Klimt, which was stolen from the gallery in 1997.  The painting was painted by Klimt in 1916-1917, bought by Italian collector Giuseppe Ricci Oddi in 1925, and kept in his own museum of the same name until it was stolen in preparation for a special exhibition on February 22, 1997.  The painting is valued at at least 60 million euros.  Just when everyone thought that the "lady portrait" will always evaporate, in December last year, the gardener cleaned the ivy of the outer wall of the Richie Odie Museum of Modern Art, but accidentally found a metal door panel, opened to find an alcove, there is a black bag in the wall, which is suspected of the painting.  In order to determine whether the paintings found were genuine, the experts irradiated them with infrared and ultraviolet light and compared them with the images taken during the examination of the original paintings in 1996.  "I can tell you with emotion that this work is genuine," said Italian prosecutor Ornella Chicca.  As for whether the painting has been placed in this niche after it has been stolen, or only after it has been placed, more tests are still needed to clarify.  According to the museum ’ s official statement, the exterior wall of the painting has not been trimmed for nearly 10 years. passages.passage: The Belverede.Wien Museum Image caption A critic of the Kiss has called the "Image of Humanity" all great artists have a handwriting that is more or less recognizable, but if there is one whose works can be truly considered unique and imitable, Gustav Klimt is an Austrian artist of the early 20th century.  Klimt is hard to imitate in the days of “mechanical reproduction, ” as Walter Benjamin put it, but no one has ever been able to replicate the artist ’ s work with that stunning focus, balance, and harmonic balance.  Klimt ’ s art has a twofold and sometimes contradictory aspect: he was on the one hand a pioneer and avant-garde artist of his time who influenced a generation of modernist artists with impressive innovations and bold experiences, but on the other hand he based his art on simple and familiar themes that are beautiful and caressing to every eye.  Klimt ’ s paintings are easily adapted to any look and “eat ” the wall of any bedroom, living room or office.  It should not be forgotten that this perfection has been achieved with a lifetime of effort and struggle.  The revolution in the decorative art of Vienna at the beginning of the 20th century and the period known as the "end of the century" or "degeneration" stage was one of the main bases of modern art.  Gustav Klimt, with his revolt against academic painting, is one of the main representatives of the Art Nouveau style, which together with a group of modernist artists affiliated with the Céción exhibition created the Yogendale Steele (Young Style).  Classical and “scholastic ” painters considered Klimt ’ s work to be more of an arrangement and decor that moves away from“ the higher purposes of art. ”  In contrast to Klimt and his friends, they believed that the artist should have complete freedom in creativity and taste testing, and that no authority had the right to set a course for him.  Unlike many of his fellow artists, Klimt studied not at the Vienna School of Art, but at the Academy of Industrial and Applied Arts.  In the first phase of Klimt ’ s career, which he co-operated with his younger brother in a workshop, the combination of artistic creation and craftsmanship forms an intense combination that is both beautiful and “beneficial. ”  In the "Gesst" school, these compositional works, which could be a mixture of painting, sculpture and architecture, were called "art collections".  The aim of these "artisan artists" was to create harmonic forms and eye-catching compositions that can be used both in functional industries such as consumer appliances and furniture, as well as in the decoration of halls, interior decoration and architectural style of facades.  It was a poem of fine writing and color.  He has more than three thousand designs left, revealing his precise look and powerful hand. Klimt came up with a string of sketches as “metaphors, ” many of which are“ black-haired ” for his larger works and color paintings.  These works usually have a dramatic background or reference, in ancient mythology or tragic heroes, such as Salome, Judith, Danae and Athena.  He was very close to the stage of his career.  In many of these works he has a tendency to symbolism, which was one of the main trends in the art of the day.  As a passionate poet, he tries to embody general and abstract concepts such as life, death, philosophy, music, lust and jealousy with subtle and symbolic lines and forms.  In a series of colorful designs and paintings, "Hope" is a pregnant woman who is staring at her bulging stomach.  Despite Klimt ’ s mastery of design, he shuns accurate representations of the real world in colorful paintings.  His human figures change shape, along with the wave of lines and the dance of forms.  Klimt always fills the place of the "natural" motif with small and compact designs, so that the main texture of the figures and their surroundings is full of spirit and movement.  The Klimt gives the viewer the freedom to see the work in his own way and to evaluate and interpret it with his own mood.  In his art, he finds something hidden with a profound meaning that cannot be expressed; or he simply looks and moves the eye around the angles of lines, designs, and colors, and enjoys their harmony.  Klimt has something for every view and taste, and approaching his art does not require an expert.  Klimt's paintings are best known for their works known as the "Golden Age" and were created more or less during his artistic maturity, around the age of 40.  His father was an avid engraver and worked with gold.  It can be said that he inherited his love of gold from his father, but his familiarity with Byzantine tiles and paintings undoubtedly contributed to his interest in gold motifs. You have made your beanstalk with earthworms.  In his works, there are usually beautiful, naked and charming women in place of saints.  He may follow the Father ’ s tradition, showing each figure as a “piece of jewelry. ”  Perhaps the most famous of these is "The Kiss".  It all revolves around a love kiss.  Men and women kneel before each other in an ethereal space.  The man is strong, and the woman is strong, and he is strong.  The man ’ s coat is of angular and “hard ” roles, while the woman ’ s coat is covered with round and“ soft ” roles.  He is naked and alone, and does not reveal anything about the position of man or woman.  They are just two ordinary people who are intertwined with two different organs and can belong to any age and culture.  A critic has dubbed this position “the image of humanity. ”  By the end of Klimt ’ s life, the cold and grim charm of Expressionism had filled the air, but Klimt was more inclined to praise the joy of life, the joy of love, and the drink.  Her lively and beautiful nature is best seen in her natural landscapes and female portraits, which she brought to the canvas in the last decade of her life, from 1908 to 1918, with stunning perfection.  In these works, Klimt has achieved a calm and harmonious style that can be felt like a musical drum.  But sometimes in this tender and caressing song, the mood of the tumultuous times is felt, even in lyrical paintings such as Kiss or "Affection", there is a hidden anxiety that tells the lovers to never end this infinite moment. Title: Klimt's stolen masterpiece found 23 years ago, but still questionable - International
Content: Twenty-three years ago, Gustav Klimt ’ s Portrait of a Lady was stolen from the Ricci Oddi Gallery of Modern Art in Piacenza, Italy.  On February 22, 1997, the gallery was being renovated for a special exhibition.  The painting mysteriously disappeared, only the outer frame of the painting was found by the roof skylight. When the police determined that the thief removed the frame, the entire painting was rolled up and carried out of the skylight, but no suspects were found. In 2014, the Italian police reopened the investigation and found the suspected painting, but it was later confirmed to be a fake or a copy.  In December last year, a gardener at the Ricci Oddi Gallery found a plastic bag inside the sandwich of the wall, which turned out to be the famous painting.  At that time, everyone suspected that this was the original painting.  After careful examination by experts, it was announced to the outside on Friday that it was confirmed to be the original painting.  In the future, the police still have to clarify the suspicion of the theft, such as: Is the painting hidden in the gallery from the beginning to the end?  Or was it returned after being stolen? Prosecutor Ornella Chicca said excitedly: "After infrared radiation and other non-invasive detection methods, we are excited to determine that this is the real Klimt."  Klimt completed this masterpiece in 1917, the last year of his life, and the Ricci Oddi Gallery acquired it in 1925 until it was stolen in 1997. Content: The Belverede.Wien Museum Image caption A critic of the Kiss has called the "Image of Humanity" all great artists have a handwriting that is more or less recognizable, but if there is one whose works can be truly considered unique and imitable, Gustav Klimt is an Austrian artist of the early 20th century.  Klimt is hard to imitate in the days of “mechanical reproduction, ” as Walter Benjamin put it, but no one has ever been able to replicate the artist ’ s work with that stunning focus, balance, and harmonic balance.  Klimt ’ s art has a twofold and sometimes contradictory aspect: he was on the one hand a pioneer and avant-garde artist of his time who influenced a generation of modernist artists with impressive innovations and bold experiences, but on the other hand he based his art on simple and familiar themes that are beautiful and caressing to every eye.  Klimt ’ s paintings are easily adapted to any look and “eat ” the wall of any bedroom, living room or office.  It should not be forgotten that this perfection has been achieved with a lifetime of effort and struggle.  The revolution in the decorative art of Vienna at the beginning of the 20th century and the period known as the "end of the century" or "degeneration" stage was one of the main bases of modern art.  Gustav Klimt, with his revolt against academic painting, is one of the main representatives of the Art Nouveau style, which together with a group of modernist artists affiliated with the Céción exhibition created the Yogendale Steele (Young Style).  Classical and “scholastic ” painters considered Klimt ’ s work to be more of an arrangement and decor that moves away from“ the higher purposes of art. ”  In contrast to Klimt and his friends, they believed that the artist should have complete freedom in creativity and taste testing, and that no authority had the right to set a course for him.  Unlike many of his fellow artists, Klimt studied not at the Vienna School of Art, but at the Academy of Industrial and Applied Arts.  In the first phase of Klimt ’ s career, which he co-operated with his younger brother in a workshop, the combination of artistic creation and craftsmanship forms an intense combination that is both beautiful and “beneficial. ”  In the "Gesst" school, these compositional works, which could be a mixture of painting, sculpture and architecture, were called "art collections".  The aim of these "artisan artists" was to create harmonic forms and eye-catching compositions that can be used both in functional industries such as consumer appliances and furniture, as well as in the decoration of halls, interior decoration and architectural style of facades.  It was a poem of fine writing and color.  He has more than three thousand designs left, revealing his precise look and powerful hand. In many of these works he has a tendency to symbolism, which was one of the main trends in the art of the day.  As a passionate poet, he tries to embody general and abstract concepts such as life, death, philosophy, music, lust and jealousy with subtle and symbolic lines and forms.  In a series of colorful designs and paintings, "Hope" is a pregnant woman who is staring at her bulging stomach.  Despite Klimt ’ s mastery of design, he shuns accurate representations of the real world in colorful paintings.  His human figures change shape, along with the wave of lines and the dance of forms.  Klimt always fills the place of the "natural" motif with small and compact designs, so that the main texture of the figures and their surroundings is full of spirit and movement.  The Klimt gives the viewer the freedom to see the work in his own way and to evaluate and interpret it with his own mood.  In his art, he finds something hidden with a profound meaning that cannot be expressed; or he simply looks and moves the eye around the angles of lines, designs, and colors, and enjoys their harmony.  Klimt has something for every view and taste, and approaching his art does not require an expert.  Klimt's paintings are best known for their works known as the "Golden Age" and were created more or less during his artistic maturity, around the age of 40. passages.title: Climate change and 21% reduction in agricultural productivity
passages.passage: In a new study led by Cornell University in the US, experts have found that farms have averaged 21 percent less yields over the past six decades as a result of climate change.  According to the researchers, this equates to a total loss of seven years of agricultural productivity growth.  Global agriculture is increasingly exposed to the effects of climate change, with warmer places such as Africa and Latin America suffering the most, and agricultural productivity growth is currently down by 34%.  To quantify the impact of human-induced climate change on what economists call “total factor productivity or a measure of overall agricultural sector productivity, ” experts developed a comprehensive econometric model.  Professor Robert Chambers, from the University of Maryland, said the results show that climate-related factors have already had a major impact on agricultural productivity.  In this paper, we used a model to estimate how the total factor productivity patterns would be if climate change were not present.  Professor Ariel Ortiz Boba, principal investigator of the study and assistant professor at Cornell University ’ s School of Applied Economics and Management, said: “We found that climate change has wiped out about seven years of progress in agricultural productivity over the past 60 years, equating to pressing the stop button for productivity growth in 2013, after which no progress has been made, and now human climate change is slowing down.  According to Professor Ortiz Boba, the group considered more than 200 systematic changes from the econometric model, and the results were largely consistent.  When we focus on different regions of the world, we find that the historical impacts of climate change have been greatest in areas that have become warmer, including areas of Africa, Latin America and Asia. passages.passage: According to the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) website, the Latin American and Caribbean region produces enough food to meet the needs of all its inhabitants. FAO Deputy General and Representative of the Organization for Latin America Julio Bardege told DW on the occasion of World Food Day that hunger in Latin America is due to insufficient income and significant economic inequality, which afflicts millions of people in the region. According to the FAO, the rise in food prices was due to higher demand and weaker dollar values.  According to experts, although there is no pressure on food shortages, the impact of the epidemic on the supply chain and the restriction of traffic has caused damage to farms. However, the COVID-19 epidemic has caused an unprecedented setback in the region ’ s struggle against hunger, adding more than 20 million people to the ranks of poverty.  The unprecedented health crisis that has plagued the world for nearly two years has also hit Latin America.  Latin America, which was among the most vulnerable regions in the world due to the epidemic, has seen the spread of poverty and food shortages in recent decades, not only due to the spread of the coronavirus and the increase in deaths caused by it, but also due to numerous other factors such as climate change, mismanagement and the increasing deterioration of the labor market and sanctions. A situation that has sounded warnings and alarms about the lack of social security networks to reduce the consequences of the epidemic in Latin America.  The NGO Action Against Hunger reported a three-fold increase in the number of people suffering from food insecurity in Latin America in 2020 due to the outbreak of COVID-19.  In Peru, 80 percent of people lost their jobs or their incomes dropped by an average of 33 percent, according to the Humanitarian Institute ’ s survey.  The 20% drop in global food production due to climate change is another crisis that experts have warned of.  Studies show that climate change has reduced global food production by more than 20 percent in the past 60 years.  Farmers have one-fifth less food than they had in 1961; in warmer regions such as Latin America and Africa, the decline is up to 34 percent.  According to available data, the United States only sees growth of 5 to 15 percent, while the world's population is projected to reach 10 billion by 2050.  Climate change has changed the favorable conditions for growing crops and is hurting the food chain in the future.  Experts believe that temperature in plant growth and development is one of the important factors.  Temperature, along with the surface of light; carbon dioxide, temperature humidity, water and nutrients, affect the growth and ultimately the production of crops.  All of these factors need to be balanced.  While the global population continues to rise, a new study suggests that agricultural productivity has fallen sharply due to the effects of climate change.  On the other hand, some coercive measures by the hegemonic powers against the countries of the Latin American resistance, such as Venezuela, have exacerbated the food crisis in the region.  Along with mismanagement of the country ’ s food security, the impact of sanctions has affected 96 percent of Venezuelans, according to a new study.  The region ’ s response to the epidemic of the Director General of the Latin American Regional Agricultural Organization has increased despite the region ’ s worsening agricultural export unemployment during the epidemic.  In response to COVID-19 pandemic, the director of the Food and Agriculture Organization has sought to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of food production with a strategic approach, and has made a huge change in the agricultural sector with new regional initiatives.  The senior official of the agricultural organization of the region also emphasized the need for large-scale investments, especially in supply chain infrastructure and agricultural innovations, expressed hope about the region ’ s significant capacities, such as the enormous natural resources of the region, abundance of fresh water and fertile lands, as well as diverse ecosystems.  Despite this, the devastating effects of the epidemic will continue to plague the Latin American region.  Predictably, in most of these countries, rising debt due to the injection of emergency funds into the health sector and the provision of direct assistance to affected families and industrial sectors affected by the recession reduced economic activity by 7.7% in 2020.  The unemployment rate, which is the main cause of poverty, increased by 2.6 percent and with a significant portion of the workforce leaving, it reached 10.7 percent from its previous year in 2019.  In the same vein, because it was not possible for many jobs to work remotely, only 21.3 percent of those employed in the Latin American region were able to continue working this way.  According to the study, the highest unemployment rate was found in Peru (39.5%), Argentina (20.9%), Colombia (21.8%), Costa Rica (20.1%), and in the poorest households, informal work dominated.  According to the website Wordo Mitters, more than 33,581 million people in Latin America and the Caribbean have been infected with the coronavirus, and more than 1.2 million people have died from the disease.

passages.title: Infographic Understanding Climate Change: Warmer weather not only harms human health, but agriculture and the economy have also paid the price
passages.passage: David Nelles and Christian Serrer: Climate change has now directly or indirectly affected the lives of 7.5 billion people on the planet.  However, the impact of global warming varies from place to place, which means that people and people living together in different regions will also be affected to varying degrees.  In any case, one thing is certain: the continued warming of the climate will continue to bring all kinds of adverse effects to mankind.  Climate change can have many effects on human health, such as heat stress caused by high temperature, operating environment factors (including air temperature, humidity, wind speed and radiation heat) and clothing, and high temperature events, which can worsen heart, blood circulation and respiratory related diseases. Increase the mortality rate of these diseases.  On the other hand, high temperatures are conducive to the formation of ozone close to the ground, which has adverse effects on human health, such as may lead to decreased lung function.  Extreme weather events such as floods or storms are more frequent and can also bring more hidden risks to human health, such as injuries and even death in serious cases.  In addition, already polluted waters may increase the risk of infectious disease outbreaks due to heavy rainfall and flooding.  Another effect of climate change in Germany is the lengthening of the pollen season, which exacerbates the symptoms of respiratory diseases such as asthma or allergic rhinitis.  And such climatic conditions are more conducive to the growth and reproduction of allergenic plants, such as Ambrosia is a good example.  Photo Credit: Businessweek / Lisa Schwegler, Stefan Kraiss, and Janna Geisse Produced The 2010 increase in global deaths due to climate change A spreading vector of disease caused by climate change refers to organisms that can transmit pathogens from infected animals or humans to other animals or humans, such as ticks commonly known as ticks, or mosquitoes.  Climate change is changing the current environmental conditions in which pathogens are spread by vectors.  In recent decades, due to globalization and favorable climatic conditions, the Asian-native Aedes albopictus (also known as the Asian tiger mosquito) has reached parts of southern Europe.  In the near future, other areas of higher latitudes in Europe should also become suitable for mosquito activity due to climate change.  It is important to note that the white line mosquito spreads dengue fever and Chikungunya virus.  On the other hand, the high temperature must be maintained for a period of time before the virus can be spread through the infected mosquitoes, because the warm temperature allows the virus to successfully reproduce in the mosquitoes and then transmit the virus to humans when the mosquitoes bite.  Rising temperatures create favorable conditions for the spread of Aedes albopictus and shorten the propagation time of the virus in Aedes albopictus.  Combining globalization with the risks that come with it, such as the importation of foreign goods that could trap Aedes albopictus, or returning travelers infected with the virus, increases the risk of disease transmission.  Photo Credit: Businessweek / Lisa Schwegler, Stefan Kraiss, and Janna Geisse produce Climate change impacts on agriculture High temperatures, high levels of carbon dioxide in the air, changes in rainfall patterns, and associated changing weather parameters can affect plant growth.  When the temperature rises to the most appropriate growth temperature, the yield of a particular crop can be increased, but once the temperature exceeds this optimum value, the crop yield begins to decrease.  In the case of corn and soybeans, as long as the growth period is more than 30 ° C, it is not conducive to the development of these crops.  In addition, extreme weather, especially drought and high temperatures, as well as heavy rain, can negatively affect yields. Between 2000 and 2007 alone, droughts and high temperatures have reduced global cereal crops by about 6.2%.  When the concentration of carbon dioxide in the air increases, many plants respond quickly by reducing the amount of water released from the leaves and increasing photosynthesis.  In this way, there is enough water and nutrients to promote plant growth, which is known as the "CO2 fertilization effect" (CO2-Düngungseffekt).  There is debate as to how much this fertilization effect can offset the reduction in production in some areas due to changes in temperature and rainfall patterns.  In addition, increased carbon dioxide concentration in the air can promote plant growth, but it also means that the nutrient concentration in the plant will be relatively reduced.  If higher average temperatures lead to longer tillage periods, less cold damage and higher crop yields, then climate change has positive implications for higher latitudes, such as northern Europe.  In contrast, climate change is not necessarily a good thing for crop yields in tropical and subtropical regions.  Climate change comes with three different types of costs: First, the cost of damage, such as direct damage to real estate or public infrastructure caused by extreme weather events.  This is followed by adaptation costs, such as levees or ponds for flood control.  The third is the so-called avoidance costs, such as the costs of switching from fossil to renewable energy to limit future global warming.  Because it is not possible to have a clear and comprehensive picture of all the costs incurred, it is actually very difficult to calculate precise figures for the economic costs of climate change.  Therefore, the calculated cost can only depend on the assumptions made, and it is very difficult to accurately grasp the costs of such things, such as melted permafrost, so it is extremely difficult to analyze the chart below.  Photo Credit: Business Week Publishing / Produced by Lisa Schwegler, Stefan Kraiss, and Janna Geisse Because of these high levels of uncertainty, it is very difficult to know exactly what climate protection measures should be taken and how much it should be interfered with from a purely economic point of view.  If people want to limit warming to 1.5 ° C, they will have to pay a very high investment cost.  Compared to setting the temperature rise range at a maximum of 3.5 ° C, the investment cost, although significantly reduced, will result in higher damage costs.  Overall, the cost of limiting global warming should be much less than the cost of damage caused by an unrestricted rise in global temperatures.  It is worth noting that as the temperature rises, the risk of irreversible damage is also increased.  Photo Credit: Businessweek / Lisa Schwegler, Stefan Kraiss, and Janna Geisse conclude that climate change is not a distant vision of the future, and that it represents more than just melting icebergs and rising sea levels, which are already threatening many people and their livelihoods.  In addition, it also shows that the temperature rise observed since the beginning of the industrial era is mainly due to man-made greenhouse gas emissions.  Fortunately, there ’ s also some ironic good news: we have the opportunity to influence the future of the climate, and we ’ re not completely powerless against climate change!  Climate model simulations show that as long as humans reduce greenhouse gas emissions, it is expected to limit the development of global warming.  Photo Credit: Businessweek / Lisa Schwegler, Stefan Kraiss, and Janna Geisse produced a global average temperature forecast for greenhouse gas emissions, but since the United Nations Climate Conference (UN-Klimakonferenz) was first held in Berlin in 1995, global greenhouse gas emissions have risen by 50%, reaching a record high.  If human beings continue to produce large quantities of greenhouse gases, it is not impossible to imagine that global temperatures will rise by another 5 ° C by the end of the century.  Therefore, we must all be aware of our responsibility: how the future of the climate, and the extent to which the impact of global warming will worsen, is entirely in our hands! The forest that disappears every minute is the size of 35 football pitches; animals and plants have to move 11 meters high every 10 years to survive; Aedes albopictus brings dengue fever from Asia to Europe...  Climate change is not a distant issue, but a real crisis that affects all aspects of your life!  This book provides a brief overview of the specific causes and possible consequences of climate change, including impacts on the permafrost, oceans, extreme weather, ecosystems, and humans.  With the support of more than 100 scientists, the results of the latest scientific knowledge are displayed in front of readers.  At the same time, the text is simple, so that readers can grasp the climate change issue in the shortest time.  Today ’ s global warming is mainly caused by human behavior, but as long as we and the people around us are willing to take positive action to protect the environment and the climate, we can make a huge contribution to the environment and ourselves! passages.title: Tyumen scientists conduct observations at the biological station "Lake Kuchak"
passages.passage: Tyumen scientists conduct observations at the biological station "Lake Kuchak" | Photo: Tyumen State University | Photo: Tyumen State University Regular observations of the growth and development of various field crops, taking into account the impact on plants of meteorological factors on the experimental site of the biological station of Tyumen State University "Lake Kuchak" are carried out by scientists of the Institute of Biology of Tyumen State University since May 2020, according to the Department of Strategic Communications of the university.  The territory is a natural testing ground for the study of ecological plasticity of plants and the selection of forms with high adaptive potential.  As explained by the head of the Department of Botany, Biotechnology and Landscape Architecture of Tyumen State University, Professor Nina Bome, the growing season of 2020 is characterized by an extremely uneven distribution in time of precipitation and air temperature.  Drought-resistant forms of cultivated plants that have the ability to adapt to the temperature stresses of the environment acquire practical value.  The success of the introduction of cultivated species can be achieved only with the right selection of varieties and the development of elements of regional cultivation technology.  In this regard, plant forms created by scientists of the Institute of Biology with the help of modern genetic and biotechnological methods are of particular value: chemical mutagenesis, hybridization, selection.  In total, about 800 experimental variants of the genetic diversity of cultivated plants were included in the research.  Some research projects are carried out in partnership with scientific and educational Russian and foreign centers.

passages.title: Climate Change Impact Assessment on Taiwan ’ s Human Resources (Part I)
passages.passage: Rising temperatures, intense heat, drought, orchard burning and heavy rain are expected to increasingly undermine agricultural productivity.  Challenges to livestock health, expected increases, declining crop yields and quality, and changes in extreme weather threaten rural livelihoods, food security, and price stability.  Pixabay economic growth is engulfed if we do not make substantial and sustained global mitigation of climate change, and regional adaptation efforts, it is expected to cost us infrastructure and property, increasingly, and hinder economic growth.  In the absence of major global mitigation actions and regional adaptation efforts, rising temperatures, rising sea levels and changes in extreme weather will continue to destroy infrastructure and property, labor productivity, and community vitality, especially as regional economies and industries that rely on natural resources and climate-friendly conditions, such as agriculture, tourism, and fisheries, are increasingly vulnerable to climate change.  Rising temperatures are expected to reduce the efficiency of power generation and increase energy demand, which in turn increases the cost of electricity.  Climate change is also expected to increasingly affect trade and the economy, including import and export prices, as well as businesses with overseas operations and supply chains.  In a moderately warm world, some aspects of the economy may improve slightly in the short term.  However, if the world does not reduce greenhouse gas emissions significantly and continuously, the planet is expected to continue to warm, causing significant net damage to the economy this century, especially as adaptation efforts are thwarted.  It is expected that the annual losses in some sectors of the economy will reach hundreds of billions of dollars by the end of the century, continuing to grow at the rate of past emissions.  Agriculture is highly challenged and threatened by rising temperatures, heat, drought, orchard burning and heavy rains, which are expected to increasingly undermine agricultural productivity.  Challenges to livestock health, expected increases, declining crop yields and quality, and changes in extreme weather threaten rural livelihoods, food security, and price stability.  Climate change poses many challenges to maintaining and improving crop productivity, livestock health and the economic viability of rural communities.  While some regions may see gains in productivity favoring expanded or alternative crops in the coming decades, overall, production of major crops is expected to decline due to higher temperatures, potentially altering water availability, soil erosion, and outbreaks of disease and pests.  Rising temperatures during the growing season are expected to be the biggest factor in the decline in agricultural productivity.  If the temperature at night exceeds 35 ° C, it will cause rice to be unable to pollinate; it will also aggravate the impact of diseases and pests, affecting the harvest of crops; high temperature and rain will make the soil unable to maintain nutrients, reduce crop yields and increase production costs.  The expected increase in extreme hot weather is expected to result in further heat stress for livestock, resulting in significant economic losses for producers.  Climate change is also likely to cause large-scale changes in the supply and prices of many agricultural products around the world, and the global supply and prices of agricultural products will also change dramatically.  These changes threaten future gains in commodity crop production and endanger rural livelihoods.  Agricultural production is an industry that is highly dependent on natural resources such as water, soil and biodiversity.  Climate change causes global temperature increases and uneven rainfall, disrupting crop growth, affecting the original habitats of ecosystems, and affecting the yield and quality of agricultural products, endangering food security and productivity, and causing loss of biodiversity.  There are many adaptation strategies to cope with climate variability, while reversing the adverse effects of change on agricultural production.  These include changes in production content, production inputs, the adoption of new technologies, and changes in management principles.  However, these strategies have limitations under severe climate change impacts and require both long-term and short-term investments.  High risk to health Climate change Air quality and health risks from extreme weather, air quality, and insects and pests, diseases transmitted through food and water supplies, are increasingly threatening the health and well-being of already vulnerable people; changes in temperature and precipitation increase air quality and health risks from wildfires (or incineration) and ground ozone pollution; rising air and water temperatures and more intense extreme weather are expected to increase exposure to waterborne diseases and foodborne diseases (food Sexual diseases), affecting the safety of food and water supplies.  Due to climate change, the frequency and severity of allergic diseases, including asthma and pollen fever, are expected to increase.  It also changes and expands the geographical distribution of disease-carrying insects and pests, exposing more people to the lice that bring Lyme disease and the mosquitoes that transmit Zika virus (such as dengue, yellow fever, Japanese encephalitis and Nile virus), which affect different transregions.  For example, communities in southwestern Taiwan are particularly vulnerable to the combined health effects of vector-borne diseases and high temperatures and floods.  Extreme and climate-related weather can have lasting mental health effects on communities, with adverse consequences, in particular resulting in degradation of livelihoods or relocation of communities.  Including the elderly, children, people in low-income communities and some indigenous and new communities, they tend to be disproportionately affected by the health impacts of climate change and are less resilient.  This helps individuals, communities, and counties to prepare for climate change risks with policies and programs to adapt and mitigate to reduce the number of injuries, illnesses, and deaths from adverse health outcomes.  According to the study, if the average temperature in Taiwan increases by 1 ° C in the future, the high risk of dengue fever will increase to 86, affecting more than 7 million people. In addition, the number of medium-risk areas has also increased to 203, and the future warming status will significantly increase the prevalence of dengue fever in Taiwan.  In addition, the increase in temperature in Taiwan will also increase the risk of related infectious diseases, and the impact of rainfall changes on infectious diseases will be more significant when the "daily extreme rainfall" is greater than 200mm.  In the face of the impact of climate change on public health, the adaptation that must be considered and prepared can be classified as at least three major aspects of infectious diseases, chronic non-communicable diseases and emergency medical care.  The main adjustment policies can basically be considered from the angle of strengthening and prevention.

passages.title: Eric Firvald, Syngenta. “Climate change will be a major global factor ”
passages.passage: — More than two years ago, we met at SPIEF — shortly after the closing of the deal with ChemChina.  You said then that this is the optimal shareholder, which will preserve the independence of the company, including the operating one.  It's been a while.  Can you say the same now?  I would like to draw your attention to the fact that outside of China the influence of our shareholders is quite limited.  The only thing they can do is support us, including investment.  Support is coming!  We have made five acquisitions, including our largest acquisition of Nidera, the digital platform Cropio, two deals in the vegetable segment and one in the digital tools segment.  There is also support from shareholders.  Let ’ s say in China, they help us to better understand the local market in order to improve the service of Chinese customers.  Historically, there have been problems in China with the use of low-quality pesticides, overuse of pesticides, low-quality fertilizers...  As a result, this has led to soil degradation and environmental problems.  Accordingly, with the new Chinese shareholder, we have the opportunity to increase our share in the Chinese market, while bringing our high-quality modern products to it and thereby help the country overcome the difficulties that it has. - How has your share in the Chinese market increased since the transaction? - We have significantly increased it.  We had less than 1% of the market in China and 6% in the crop.  By the end of last year, we already had 4% for seeds and 10% of the crop protection market.  If we talk about the implementation, then by the end of 2019, our sales in China amounted to $336 million.  By the end of 2020, our sales in China will exceed $4 billion, and the market share will increase significantly.  Eric Firvald.  CEO Syngenta was born on July 29, 1959 in the United States.  1981 – Graduated from the University of Delaware (Chemical Engineering).  1998 — studied in the program of training of top managers of Harvard Business School.  2003 - Vice President, Agriculture and Nutrition, DuPont Group.  2008 — Chairman of the Board of Directors, President and CEO at Nalco (water treatment technologies, services for energy companies).  2011 — President of EcoLab (water, hygiene and energy technologies and services).  2012 — Executive Director of Univar (world distributor of chemical products, including agricultural products).  Since 2016 — CEO of Syngenta. — Tell us the details of the transactions. — Nidera is a company that deals with corn and soybean seeds, one of the largest players of this level in Brazil and Argentina.  And, of course, integration with the Syngenta business turns the now merged company Syngenta-Nidera into one of the leading market makers in the markets of these countries.  With the acquisition of Nidera, we also gained access to advanced technologies in the field of sunflower and, by the way, these technologies will soon be available in Russia.  The second two important acquisitions are the digital platforms Cropio and Strider.  Digital platforms help to keep a record of the use of all those crop protection products and fertilizers used by the agricultural producer, and give him certain advice.  In this way, they help us to improve our customer service.  Among our deals are two more seed companies in the vegetable segment: Abbott & Cobb and Floranova.  These companies are mainly represented in the markets of the United States and the United Kingdom, but their hermoplasm is used far beyond these countries. – Name, if possible, the amount of each of the transactions. – This I can not do.  I will only say that all five acquisitions cost the company and its shareholders $2 billion. — Can an M & A deal similar to one of these five be concluded in Russia? — I will say at once that Chinese investors fully support our course to increase investment in Russian business.  But here we have a few other plans.  When I talk about Russia, I mean, first of all, not M & A, but the construction of a plant for the production of plant protection products near Lipetsk and the creation of the Institute for Seed Protection in the Voronezh region, which will support our business in this segment.  We also intend to significantly increase the number of full-time employees in Russia. - And how much does Russia occupy in your sales? - 4%, but at the same time we maintain a constant increase in sales here.  Of course, its pace is not as fast as in China, but our starting positions in the two countries are different. – Another question about the new digital assets of Syngenta.  The Cropio platform is relatively known in Russia, and almost nothing is known about Strider.  What is this platform where it works, what is its uniqueness for the company and synergy for the general business contour of Syngenta? - In the US market, we have historically had a fairly strong presence in the digital technology segment.  There we have a platform called AgriEdge.  And, of course, we would like to have the same strong presence in Brazil as in the United States.  Accordingly, Strider is a Brazilian company, a digital platform with an already very strong presence there.  Just like Cropio we bought to strengthen its position in Russia and, in general, in Eastern Europe. - But Cropio in Russia is almost not represented.  I think there is a small office, and that ’ s it. – Yes, maybe it is, but the platform has a huge potential and scope for scaling.  It is very important to keep in mind that Cropio has a professional team, and when integrating their platform and their team with our growth opportunities opens up very large ones.  And another strong point of Cropio is that the application in the form in which it is already available can be widely used in Russia.  You were right to say that Cropio has a limited team here.  So if you combine the Cropio software with the large team of sales managers that are in the Russian Syngenta, if you even slightly modify the platform, then there will be very great opportunities. - Are there any calculated figures on the timing, volume of space that you plan to take Cropio services in Russia? - Of course.  At the time of purchase of the service in 2019, Cropio ’ s coverage in Russia was already about 2 million hectares.  In the near future, our goal is to increase this figure to 5 million hectares.  Cropio is a tool that creates additional value for agricultural producers, and it will successfully integrate with the model of creating demand that Syngenta has in Russia.  These are people, a lot of people who will be able to use Cropio and continue to distribute this system. – I understand correctly that your future plant of the SZR near Lipetsk is a tolling model, and there will be no full-fledged localization? – We use the tolling scheme for a very long time, and we will continue to use it in the same place as now – at the Kirovo-Chepetsk Chemical Plant.  But at the same time in Lipetsk we will have our own form, our own packaging of products.  That is, there will be the same process as in Kirovo-Chepetsk.  - Then what is the fundamental difference between what is and what will be? - We see a great prospect of market growth in Russia, we see the opportunity to produce products closer to the client in the Central Black Earth region.  Therefore, we have a lot of flexibility in responding to customer requests.  At the same time, we see great opportunities for exporting our products from this new plant to the EurAsEC countries.  Syngenta.  The producer of seeds and agrochemicals was founded in 2000 on the basis of the agricultural divisions of Novartis and AstraZeneca.  In 2016, it was 100% acquired by the Chinese chemical state corporation ChemChina.  Headquartered in Basel, Switzerland.  It has offices in 90 + countries of the world.  The staff is 28,000 people.  Revenue in 2019 is $13.6 billion (unchanged from 2018), EBITDA is $2.9 billion ($2.7 billion in 2018), net income is $1.45 billion against $1.44 billion a year earlier.  Two-thirds of the company's sales in monetary terms (more than $10 billion) accounted for agrochemicals, a third ($3 billion with a little) - for seeds.  Data on Russia is not disclosed.  Based on Eric Firvald ’ s estimate of Syngenta ’ s 3% share of Russian sales made in this interview, in terms of money they could be at $520 million per year.  Question to you as CEO of the company.  How can you articulate the essence of the new strategy of the company in Russia, which was publicly announced in 2019? - Our strategy in Russia is to be the leader in the segment of crop protection, strengthen our leadership position in sunflower seeds and reach the first place in sales of corn seeds and vegetable crops.  And we want to achieve this by bringing the best world technologies to the Russian market, having high-quality production of the best quality and at the same time providing comprehensive agronomic support with the help of our sales managers and our distribution partners

passages.title: In the North Caucasus and southern Russia will increase snowfall and droughts
passages.passage: Climatologists predict that in the 21st century, the amount and intensity of snowfall will increase throughout Russia, and in some regions, arid conditions are expected to worsen.  This is reported by RIA Novosti with reference to the national report “Global climate and soil cover of Russia: assessment of risks and environmental and economic consequences of land degradation ”.  The study was conducted with the aim of developing measures for adapting agricultural and forest management systems and technologies to climate change.  Discussion of the report, analyzing the forecast scenarios of climate change and their impact on agriculture and forestry, was held at the Vasily Dokuchaev Soil Institute.  According to scientists, if at the beginning of the XXI century in Russia there was a small increase in precipitation, then by the middle of the century it will increase, especially in the eastern and northern regions of the country.  “The increase in summer precipitation is most significant, mainly in the north and east of Russia.  In the south of the European part of Russia - in the Southern and North Caucasus Federal Districts - the worsening of arid (on average per year) conditions is expected, "the study says.  At the same time, more "sharp" precipitation will probably occur in the form of separate showers or snowfalls.  There will also be more floods and floods.  Note that recently, scientists said that in 30 years the climate of the Rostov region in 30 years may change to subtropical, and the weather on the coast of the Sea of Azov will be close to the climate of Abkhazia and Sochi.  So far, we are lagging behind in temperatures: in the subtropics, the annual is + 11, we have + 9.95, - said Lyudmila Bespalova, Doctor of Geographical Sciences.  In her opinion, the summer shallowing of the Don in 2017, when the water left the coast by ten meters, is one of the brightest examples of climate change.  Changes in climatic conditions can lead not only to a change in flora and fauna, but also to a change in the economy of the region.  For example, Don farmers will have to breed new varieties of wheat and shift the timing of crops.

passages.title: Land abuse contributes to climate change
passages.passage: The land is often abused and contributes to the harm of climate change 2019-08-06 16: 42 Taiwan Awakening News reporter Zhuang Ruimeng / Taipei reported that the land has been used by humans to cultivate and lose its original function of absorbing carbon.  (Photo by M. Prinke on Flicker under Creative Commons license) Share Facebook Treating land better helps humanity fight climate change.  The UN Intergovernmental Panel of Experts on Climate Change, which is currently meeting, will present an updated report on the current state of human land use.  Experts pointed out that due to human behavior, land has changed from carbon capture to carbon release, threatening to exacerbate the power of climate change, and highlighting the importance of land use.  According to The Independent, global soils can currently absorb 1% of carbon, down from 7% in the past.  If the land is cultivated in a more sustainable way, carbon will be absorbed by the soil to become a carbon reservoir.  Currently, 1 / 3 of all pollution emissions come from land.  “If we take the severity of the climate problem seriously now, it will be worse if we don ’ t have land as a carbon reservoir, ” said Li Wen, a representative of the World Resources Institute. The scientists also pointed out that continued pressure on land, including the provision of food, wood and plant raw materials to meet increasing population needs, will make carbon reduction targets more difficult to achieve.  In addition, 33% of arable land has been used to grow crops that provide animal feed.  Professor Lixon of the University of Clanfield in the UK also believes that the latest IPCC report will provide more evidence that land degradation will also exacerbate climate change and lead to an increase in the crisis.  Addressing land abuse can focus on intensive agriculture, which involves farming on as small a land as possible, allowing more natural land to absorb carbon dioxide, according to the BBC.  Another option is to farm in a less dense and friendly climate.  Either way, however, the IPCC report will point out that poor farmers will be the group most affected by global warming.  Professor Berman, of the University of Oxford ’ s Institute of Environmental Change, said climate change had led to soil erosion in the south of the UK through more intense rainfall.  “Warmer temperatures and heavier rainfall will worsen soil erosion, soil compaction, loss of organic matter and biodiversity, and soil and rock flows, ” said Li Huicheng, chairman of the IPCC.“ I hope this report will serve to remind the world more about the threat that climate change poses to land. ”  [More details, see here]

passages.title: Climate change and water scarcity are top priorities.
passages.passage: Assistant Professor of Water Engineering at the Faculty of Agriculture of Shahrekord University said: “The main priority of the authorities should be water shortage and climate change, so that water factories are moved to the seaside and agriculture in areas that are facing water shortage is limited. ”  He said: “It ’ s been a long time, it ’ s been a long time, it ’ s been a long time, it ’ s been a long time.  “When we talk about climate change, we mean meteorological parameters that have been measured over long periods of time, and these changes manifest themselves in either natural or artificial forms, which are caused by humans.  Nasr Esfahani said: “Various factors such as sunspots, changes in the earth ’ s crust, changes in vegetation or the movement of continents, or changes in ocean temperature naturally cause climate change.  “What has happened in the past year is that humans have caused an imbalance in meteorological parameters due to excessive consumption of natural resources, including oil, gas and fossil fuels, and by destroying natural resources such as forests and expanding factories and cities.  The university professor pointed out that the country is climatally located in a dry region, saying: "We should not expect the climate to change from dry to wet, because this is a very wrong expectation that some in the society suggest this."  He said: "Climate change has become very clear in the last 40 years, so we have to adapt to this situation that has been fluctuating and know that drought or drought fluctuations are part of the nature of the region's climate."  Nasr Isfahani said: "In this situation, climate change is occurring and extreme phenomena such as severe droughts, drought, heat and cold are increasing, there is no alternative but to adapt to them, for example, agricultural products can be used to prevent frostbite, to use resistant products.  Regarding water resources, he said: “At the same time as the climate change, the consumption of water resources has greatly expanded, especially in the last 50 years, when agriculture has been the center of development in the country. ”  The university professor said: "If we examine the rainfall parameter in more detail, we see that the average rainfall has not changed, but the extremes have changed a lot and these changes are significant, on the other hand, the effective rainfall has not changed and the ineffective rainfall has increased, which means that there is a shortage of water resources."  He said: "What has been observed is that, contrary to the rainfall parameter, changes in the temperature parameter, especially the minimum temperature, are highly effective and the trend of increasing the minimum temperature is observed in many stations in the country."  Nasr Esfahani pointed out that in mountainous areas the precipitation has changed from solid to liquid state, adding: "When there is snow in the region, because the snow is slowly melting and sinking into underground sources, it feeds them, on the other hand, the occurrence of rain brings water runoff, which feeds surface water instead of feeding groundwater resources."  He added that excessive consumption of water resources, expansion of the area under cultivation, non-observance of the cultivation pattern and the use of traditional methods for irrigation have led to the reduction of groundwater.  Assistant Professor of Water Engineering at Shahrekord University emphasized: "The authorities were aware of the current situation, but they did not think that the effects of climate change would be egregious and misrepresented, and today we face a fundamental problem, for example, if there was a shortage of water, it was solved by harvesting from underground water resources and we assigned this problem to the future." Nasr Esfahani said that for short-term purposes, water resources have not been considered because steel and water mills have been built in the country, which if this decision process continues, despite the lack of water resources, will still be built in the future.  “We should not expect that one day our country will be as abundant as Europe, because the lack of rainfall in our region has been caused by the rotation of the earth and the circulation of the atmosphere, so in addition to adapting to climate change, if there is to be a cost to this, it should be done today and we should not postpone those costs to the future, because we may face more limitations in the future. ”  The university professor noted that the main priority of the authorities should be water scarcity and climate change, so that water factories are moved to the seaside and agriculture is limited in areas with water scarcity. Title: Climate change and 21% reduction in agricultural productivity
Content: In a new study led by Cornell University in the US, experts have found that farms have averaged 21 percent less yields over the past six decades as a result of climate change.  According to the researchers, this equates to a total loss of seven years of agricultural productivity growth.  Global agriculture is increasingly exposed to the effects of climate change, with warmer places such as Africa and Latin America suffering the most, and agricultural productivity growth is currently down by 34%.  To quantify the impact of human-induced climate change on what economists call “total factor productivity or a measure of overall agricultural sector productivity, ” experts developed a comprehensive econometric model.  Professor Robert Chambers, from the University of Maryland, said the results show that climate-related factors have already had a major impact on agricultural productivity.  In this paper, we used a model to estimate how the total factor productivity patterns would be if climate change were not present.  Professor Ariel Ortiz Boba, principal investigator of the study and assistant professor at Cornell University ’ s School of Applied Economics and Management, said: “We found that climate change has wiped out about seven years of progress in agricultural productivity over the past 60 years, equating to pressing the stop button for productivity growth in 2013, after which no progress has been made, and now human climate change is slowing down.  According to Professor Ortiz Boba, the group considered more than 200 systematic changes from the econometric model, and the results were largely consistent.  When we focus on different regions of the world, we find that the historical impacts of climate change have been greatest in areas that have become warmer, including areas of Africa, Latin America and Asia.  Most people see climate change as a distant problem, but it ’ s one that ’ s already having an impact.  We need to address climate change now so that we can prevent future generations from being harmed.  The study was published in the journal Nature Climate Change.  End of message.
