Title: Land abuse contributes to climate change
Content: The land is often abused and contributes to the harm of climate change 2019-08-06 16: 42 Taiwan Awakening News reporter Zhuang Ruimeng / Taipei reported that the land has been used by humans to cultivate and lose its original function of absorbing carbon.  (Photo by M. Prinke on Flicker under Creative Commons license) Share Facebook Treating land better helps humanity fight climate change.  The UN Intergovernmental Panel of Experts on Climate Change, which is currently meeting, will present an updated report on the current state of human land use.  Experts pointed out that due to human behavior, land has changed from carbon capture to carbon release, threatening to exacerbate the power of climate change, and highlighting the importance of land use.  According to The Independent, global soils can currently absorb 1% of carbon, down from 7% in the past.  If the land is cultivated in a more sustainable way, carbon will be absorbed by the soil to become a carbon reservoir.  Currently, 1 / 3 of all pollution emissions come from land.  “If we take the severity of the climate problem seriously now, it will be worse if we don ’ t have land as a carbon reservoir, ” said Li Wen, a representative of the World Resources Institute. The scientists also pointed out that continued pressure on land, including the provision of food, wood and plant raw materials to meet increasing population needs, will make carbon reduction targets more difficult to achieve.  In addition, 33% of arable land has been used to grow crops that provide animal feed.  Professor Lixon of the University of Clanfield in the UK also believes that the latest IPCC report will provide more evidence that land degradation will also exacerbate climate change and lead to an increase in the crisis.  Addressing land abuse can focus on intensive agriculture, which involves farming on as small a land as possible, allowing more natural land to absorb carbon dioxide, according to the BBC.  Another option is to farm in a less dense and friendly climate.  Either way, however, the IPCC report will point out that poor farmers will be the group most affected by global warming.  Professor Berman, of the University of Oxford ’ s Institute of Environmental Change, said climate change had led to soil erosion in the south of the UK through more intense rainfall.  “Warmer temperatures and heavier rainfall will worsen soil erosion, soil compaction, loss of organic matter and biodiversity, and soil and rock flows, ” said Li Huicheng, chairman of the IPCC.“ I hope this report will serve to remind the world more about the threat that climate change poses to land. ”  [More details, see here]

Title: Climate change and water scarcity are top priorities.
Content: Assistant Professor of Water Engineering at the Faculty of Agriculture of Shahrekord University said: “The main priority of the authorities should be water shortage and climate change, so that water factories are moved to the seaside and agriculture in areas that are facing water shortage is limited. ”  He said: “It ’ s been a long time, it ’ s been a long time, it ’ s been a long time, it ’ s been a long time.  “When we talk about climate change, we mean meteorological parameters that have been measured over long periods of time, and these changes manifest themselves in either natural or artificial forms, which are caused by humans.  Nasr Esfahani said: “Various factors such as sunspots, changes in the earth ’ s crust, changes in vegetation or the movement of continents, or changes in ocean temperature naturally cause climate change.  “What has happened in the past year is that humans have caused an imbalance in meteorological parameters due to excessive consumption of natural resources, including oil, gas and fossil fuels, and by destroying natural resources such as forests and expanding factories and cities.  The university professor pointed out that the country is climatally located in a dry region, saying: "We should not expect the climate to change from dry to wet, because this is a very wrong expectation that some in the society suggest this."  He said: "Climate change has become very clear in the last 40 years, so we have to adapt to this situation that has been fluctuating and know that drought or drought fluctuations are part of the nature of the region's climate."  Nasr Isfahani said: "In this situation, climate change is occurring and extreme phenomena such as severe droughts, drought, heat and cold are increasing, there is no alternative but to adapt to them, for example, agricultural products can be used to prevent frostbite, to use resistant products.  Regarding water resources, he said: “At the same time as the climate change, the consumption of water resources has greatly expanded, especially in the last 50 years, when agriculture has been the center of development in the country. ”  The university professor said: "If we examine the rainfall parameter in more detail, we see that the average rainfall has not changed, but the extremes have changed a lot and these changes are significant, on the other hand, the effective rainfall has not changed and the ineffective rainfall has increased, which means that there is a shortage of water resources." passages.title: The End of Berlinale: Women ’ s Full Hands and Iranians ’ Empty Hands
passages.passage: The Berlin International Film Festival ended on Saturday, February 24 with a special ceremony.  The ceremony was attended by more than 1,600 guests at Berlin ’ s Berlinale Palace.  The Best Golden Bear Award went to the Romanian film “Don ’ t Touch Me ” by Adina Pintielli.  Iranian filmmakers returned home empty-handed this time.  In the main section of this year ’ s festival, 24 films were screened, of which 19 were competing for the Golden Bear and the Silver Bears of Berlinale.  This year ’ s jury consisted of German director and producer Tom Tikor, American critic Stephanie Zachark, Spanish film expert Chema Prado, American producer Adele Romanski, Japanese actress and musician Ryuichi Sakamoto, and Belgian actor Cecil de France.  “Don ’ t Touch Me ” co-directed by Germany, France, Romania, Bulgaria and the Czech Republic won the Berlinale Golden Bear.  The film also won the festival ’ s 50,000 Euro prize as the first film.  The Grand Jury Prize went to Polish film Mogue, and the Silver Bear went to American director Wes Anderson for his film Island of Dogs.  Other awards in this year ’ s main section were awarded in the following order: Silver Bear for Best Actor: Anthony Bajon for his performance in Praying from France.  Silver Bear for Best Actress: Anna Brown for her role in the film Heir Women from Paraguay.  (The film, directed by Marcelo Martisi, also received the Silver Bear Award for Best Film with a New Vision.)  Silver Bear for Best Screenplay: Alonso Virilassius and Manuel Alcala from Mexico for Museum Film.  Silver Bear for Outstanding Art Work: Elena Okinaya from Russia for the costume design of the Dolatov film.  The best short and documentary films in the Golden Bear category were given to the Rwandan and Swiss short film The Men Behind the Wall, directed by Samuel Eichmore, from Israel and the Silver Bear, and to the Rwandan and Swiss short film Imfura.  In the documentary category, Ruth Beckermann ’ s “Waltz Waldheim ” from Austria was selected as the best film of the year for the Berlinale.  The other Berlinale Awards are held annually in Berlinale, another section entitled Panorama.  In this section, awards are given to the best films by audience selection.  This year, the film "Profile", directed by Timur Bekmantov, and the documentary "Silence of Others", directed by Almodeena Karasedo, were awarded in the Panorama category.  The profile is a joint creation of the United States, Russia, Britain and Cyprus and the silence of others is a joint product of the United States and Spain.  The Crystal Bear received the adolescents section over the age of 14 from the Swiss feature film "Fortona" by Germinal Rao.  The film also won the 7,500 Euro International Jury Prize.  In this section, the film "Kim Hollikhanda" by Sara Voltmaier from the Netherlands was also awarded the Crystal Bear and the film Dressage by Pouya Badkoobeh was honored.  In the “Generation ” category for children ’ s films, this year the feature film“ Hand on Heart ” by Luke Picard from Canada and the short film “Guide to a 12-year-old Girl ” by Tilda Cobham Hervey from Australia received the Crystal Bears.  The empty hands of Iranians and the audacity of Leila Hatami all the Iranian artists present at the Berlin International Film Festival returned home empty-handed this year, and only the film “Dresaj ” directed by Pooya Badkoobeh was appreciated for the clever narrative of the story.  But the press conference of Mani Haghighi and Leila Hatami, the director and lead actress of the film "Pig", created controversy.  At the press conference, Leila Hatami lamented that peaceful protests in Iran are being violently suppressed, saying she suffered greatly from the issue.  In contrast, Mani Haghighi, while acknowledging that there is censorship in Iran and that artists are trying to circumvent this censorship in their own way, protested to journalists why they always ask political questions at press conferences when they reach Iranian artists instead of doing their work.  After the conference, Leila Hatami was severely criticized by the Fajr Film Festival officials and some regime figures on social media.  But Mani Haghighi supported Hatami in a video posted on YouTube and social media, saying: “Peaceful demonstrations are people ’ s natural right and they should not be repressed for it.  Laila Hatami ’ s discomfort was justified, and I understand that. ”

Reports vary as to the number of people on board; some sources say the sinking boat had 19 people on board, and some say there were 28 people on board, Iranian and Iraqi.  After the accident, a number of helicopters, military boats and fishing boats approached to help people who were drowning.  The coast of Dunkirk, north of France and the country ’ s closest coast to Britain, is known as one of the main illegal crossings from France to Britain.  In addition to the French police and navy, NGOs are patrolling these not-too-deep but extremely turbulent waters on a daily basis to rescue refugees who are desperate for water.  Rescue teams were not close enough to do anything faster on Wednesday after a boat accident.  A French rescue helicopter in the port of Dunkirk, Rasoul Irannejad, 35, the father of a Kurdish family from Sardasht, West Azerbaijan, died before being pulled out of the water, his wife Shiva Mohammad Panahi, 35, and two children, Anita, 9, and Armin, 6, died after being pulled out of the water, and their 15-month-old baby Artin has not yet been found.  French officials say John is unlikely to be a slave.  Mr. Irannejad ’ s brother, the uncle of the drowned children, says the family left Iran in the summer.  They criticized his father ’ s simple labor income and everything he had and didn ’ t have, and they went illegally to Turkey, from there to Italy.  After a 20-day stay in Italy, they arrived in France.  Their destination was the UK, and twice before the final attempt by sea, they tried to cross the border illegally and enter the UK, where they thought they would earn £100 a day and pay back the loans they had taken and be happy.  A friend of the Irannejad family, who was with them in France, said about their decision to cross the Channel: “About a month ago, we talked about it with Shiva.  "I told him it was very dangerous and if something happened, the kids..."  The family friend, who asked the Guardian to be called Ali, said Shiva replied, “Everyone goes the same way, God willing, nothing happens. ”  Immigration laws have been tightened in recent months in the UK.  Under the impact of the coronavirus epidemic, safe routes to enter and declare asylum in the country have been closed, but small boats and the English Channel are still open.  So far this year, at the end of the 10th month of 2020, 7,400 people have made their way to the UK via the English Channel, four times the number of people who entered the UK illegally last year.  At least seven people have drowned in these waters this year, including four members of Mr. Irannejad ’ s family, as well as their missing baby.  The cost of crossing the Channel for refugees is between 5,000 and 6,000 euros per person.  Getting out of Iran, especially if you live in border areas, doesn ’ t cost much.  The main cost is to pass through Turkey and get to one of the Western European countries.  In the case of the Irannejad family, crossing the Turkish waters to Italy and arriving from Italy to France amounted to almost 8,000 euros per person.  At least €13,000 for every person from Turkey until they reach the UK.  This number needs to be multiplied by five to find out what the Iranian family, apart from their lives, has paid for taking refuge in another country.  The tent on the right: the last residence of the “Irannejad ” family in the past three days after the last incident of the sinking of the refugee boat in the English Channel, in addition to Boris Johnson, other British officials have also expressed regret about the incident and promised to cooperate with the French authorities to clarify the dimensions of the incident, but at the same time they have not opened the legal route of refugees to their country.  Following Wednesday ’ s incident, UNHCR has expressed hope that Britain will open legal pathways for refugees to prevent a repeat of the tragedy, although even if such a decision is made in the coming days, the Irannejad family will no longer be returned to us.  Those who leave the country to seek asylum, in the first step, burn their ID documents such as passports, national ID cards and identity cards and prefer to live without the country for a while, rather than find shelter elsewhere through a path that was very dangerous even in ordinary days and became more difficult during the coronavirus epidemic.  Refugees often escape war, chaos, political conflicts and socio-economic crises.  Some of them clash with the central governments of their country and flee because of political charges, some flee because of threats of murder and assault from the chaos and conflict of armed groups and civil war, and some seek a place where they can feed themselves and their families more safely.  The fear of conflict with the police due to participation in ordinary crimes, fraud, return checks, interference in smuggling and theft, and the like sometimes causes people to cross the borders of countries illegally and apply for asylum.  There are those who, in the hope of heaven, go elsewhere, without knowing what the hell it is to live in a camp, to be detained in a temporary detention center before receiving a residence permit in the host country, and how dangerous and even deadly the road can be.  Anita Irannejad Mohammad Hossein Mahdavian – director of Iranian cinema and creator of works such as “Standing in the Dust ” and“ Nimroz Adventure ” – posted a few videos and photos of Anita Irannejad on her Instagram page on Friday while showing the girl performing an acting test, writing: “Look at these photos and videos.  Each has a story.  Last year, we did a detailed local search for actors for the children ’ s roles in the movie Walnut Tree.  The children should have spoken the Kurdish language of Sorani, which is the language and accent of Sardasht people.  Only a few Iranian cities in the north of Kurdistan and the south of West Azerbaijan speak this particular dialect, which made it difficult.  One of the roles we were looking for was the role of a six-year-old girl in the film.  Look at the girl in the second photo, her eyes.  It is a combination of pain and at the same time beauty and hope.  This girl was one of our final few options, along with a few other beautiful and innocent girls, each of whom came to us with the hope that they might find a future for themselves by flaunting their talents for a few who came from Tehran.  He was not chosen and the role went to Gina.  If the image of the girl is familiar to you, you are right.  The next images are short videos of Anita trying to get the part. Yes.  Her name is Anita, Anita of Iran.  If the name is familiar to you, you are right.  The last two pictures are a piece of news that the media has been talking about for a couple of days.  Anita and her entire family are stranded in foreign territorial waters on a risky migration from Iran.  Since yesterday, Ibrahim, and especially Amir Hossein, who had done the last tests and exercises with Anita, have been constantly reviewing the image of Anita ’ s tears and grieving, and I think about the family of this family.  What a strange name!  The Iranian family, whose Iran was not a warm and hopeful home for them. ”  But Mehdi Issa Zadeh, a member of the parliament ’ s social commission, in an interview with the site “The Choice ” and in response to the question, are you aware of the details of the drowning of the Iranian family on the path to immigration to the UK?  He said: “Well, I haven ’ t received any information or explanation about the incident yet.  One reason for this is that if it had happened on the border of neighboring countries like Turkey, there would have been better information, but because it has happened in a country like the United Kingdom, we have not received enough information.  He has also stated that foreigners are advertising Utopia to Iranian citizens abroad.  During the short time that I am a member of the Social Commission, I have received many referrals and many of those who have emigrated have expressed regret and asked to return to Iran.  Over the past few days, a family from the United States, an Australian and a Dutch have asked me to help them get back to Iran.  These people thought that if they went abroad, this would happen, but now they see that all countries have the same problem as us.  Last week, a person called me and told me that he had a home and a job in Iran and the conditions were not bad in Iran, but now he has emigrated and lives in a camp and shared a hall with several Arab families and his wife is pregnant.  Unfortunately, some people still think that the chicken next door is a goose.  Mehdi Issa Zadeh, the parliament

passages.title: Four refugees, including two children, drowned in the English Channel.
passages.passage: Four asylum-seekers, including two children, drowned in the English Channel (Reuters) Photo source: A rescue operation has been going on for hours by French boats since French authorities announced the deaths of two children and a man and woman who were trying to cross the English Channel to reach Britain.  A boat carrying refugees has sunk across the English Channel between France and Britain.  The prosecutor of the French city of Dunkirk has opened an investigation into the cause of the sinking of the ship.  These people are said to be Iranian.  A massive rescue operation has been under way for hours, which crashed near the northern French city of Dunkirk.  According to French authorities, two children aged 5 and 8 and a man and woman died.  The other 14 were taken to hospitals in the port of Calais and the French city of Dunkirk.  The English Channel, between France and Britain, is one of the world ’ s busiest waterways, and it can be dangerous to cross by small vessels, especially in winter when the sea is stormy.  Another disaster came after the British Meteorological Office warned of bad weather and strong winds in the Channel region.  Natalie Alpeik, MP for the Dover region in the British Parliament, said: “It ’ s terrible that there ’ s been another disaster on the canal.  Human traffickers have no respect for human life: "A sailboat accidentally encountered a ship and alerted French authorities of the incident.  Four French ships, a Belgian helicopter and a French fishing vessel were involved in the rescue.  Since the beginning of the year, more than 7,400 asylum seekers have arrived in Britain by sea in small boats.  While there are still two months left until the end of 2020, that number is 1,825 more than in 2019.  The survivors were taken by helicopter to hospitals in the port of Calais and the northern French city of Dunkirk on Thursday, August 6, and a total of 235 migrants, including several pregnant women, crossed the English Channel from Europe to the southern coast of Britain.  This is the highest recorded number of illegal immigrants arriving in the region in a single day.  About ten days ago, Home Secretary Priti Patel announced the “most significant revision ” of the country ’ s asylum system in a decade.

passages.title: Refugee crisis: France and Britain strengthen border surveillance to stop migrants crossing the Channel
passages.passage: France and the United Kingdom have signed a new agreement to end illegal immigration through the English Channel.  In recent months, with an increasing number of migrants trying to reach the British coast illegally, the English Channel has become one of the most dangerous crossings for asylum seekers.  Since the beginning of the year, seven people, including a family of five, have drowned while crossing the English Channel.  Britain ’ s interior minister, Priti Patel, announced on Saturday that the French and British governments had reached an agreement to combat migrant smuggling and stop illegal immigration through the Channel.  Britain ’ s interior minister and his French counterpart, Gerald Darmann, have signed the agreement, stressing that they intend to make it impossible for asylum seekers to cross the English Channel, which has reached more than 8,000 this year.  Priti Patel said that as part of the agreement, the French government has committed to doubling the number of its coast guard patrols in the area by December 1 to stop migrant boats in the Channel, and to use new equipment such as drones and radar to identify people trying to cross the Channel to reach the British coast.  Britain ’ s interior minister expressed his satisfaction with the signing of the agreement, saying: “This agreement will make it possible for both France and Britain to make it impossible for migrants to cross the Channel. ”  Signing a new 😍 😍 😍 😍 covenant to tackle small boat crossings.  There will be an increase in surveillance with cuttingedge tech introduce greater security at ports Ensure accommodation for migrants in France https: / / t.co / vjG1KiTkep pic.twitter.com / COJ1jncjcjitC — i Patel (@ pritipatel) November 28, 2020 According to AFP, the two countries have agreed to spend 31.4 million euros on the joint project.  In recent months, the number of migrants attempting to cross the English Channel illegally has increased dramatically.  News of the sinking of boats carrying refugees, which killed four people last year and killed seven this year, including a family of five, has made the Channel a dangerous crossroads for migrants and has severely affected public opinion.  Following the incident, the British government accused France of not doing enough to stop refugees from crossing the Channel.  In September, French authorities said they had blocked 1,300 migrants trying to cross the English Channel.  Between January 1 and August 31, some 6,200 asylum seekers, wearing life jackets and using a variety of inflatable boats, paddles and kayaks provided by smugglers, tried to reach the British coast by illegally crossing the English Channel.  On October 27, following the capsizing of the boat carrying refugees, the majority of whom were Iranian nationals, the 35-year-old Rasoul Irannejad, his wife Shiva Mohammad Panahi, two children aged 6 and 9, and their 15-month-old baby, who were from Sardasht and were trying to cross the Channel from France to Britain, drowned and died.  One of the first asylum seekers to drown in the English Channel in 2019 was Mitra, a 31-year-old Iranian girl with a master ’ s degree in psychology who, along with 19 Iranian and Iraqi refugees, including seven children, boarded a boat for the UK on August 9.  Every year, thousands of people from the Middle East and African countries try to reach Britain through the English Channel.  The Channel, which lies between France and Britain, has seen a dramatic increase in small boats carrying refugees to Britain since 1918, in which a number of refugees have been involved in accidents and some have died. passages.title: Britain calls on social media to remove videos of crossing the Channel
passages.passage: Britain has asked social media to remove videos of people crossing the English Channel (16 June 1400 – 6 June 2021) Image source, UK Home Secretary PA Media has called for social media to remove videos showing refugees crossing the Channel as "attractive" and encouraging them to cross.  Britain ’ s Interior Minister Priti Patel said in a letter to social media executives on Saturday that “videos ” of refugees crossing the English Channel from Europe to Britain were“ unacceptable ”.  Over the past week, hundreds of asylum seekers have crossed the Channel; five days ago, the Home Office confirmed that more than 568 people had crossed the Channel in four days.  Last Saturday alone, 336 people were taken off 19 boats and on Friday 144 on 7 boats.  The Home Office also said it was investigating reports that a British border patrol vessel had requested entry into French waters and that asylum seekers had been taken from a boat en route to Britain.  The British Home Secretary ’ s letter came after a widely circulated video on social media, including TikTok, showing a group of men crossing the English Channel.  The Interior Ministry says smugglers are using the video, which has been shared on Twitter, Instagram and Facebook, to advise desperate refugees to cross the Channel.  Ms Patel says the messages posted on social media that “promote this deadly crossing, and even make it look attractive, are unacceptable. ”  "These images encourage those in a safe European country to leave, putting their lives and their families at risk."  The UK Home Secretary says human traffickers are using the videos to promote their deadly trade.  The letter said: "What is not mentioned in the videos are those who lost their lives and that refugees must be stranded for at least 13 hours in an unfit boat in cold water."  The source, PA Media, said the British border boat had taken the refugees from the water, saying social media had made "great progress" in removing the videos, but that it needed to be done faster and more effectively so that more men, women and children did not die as they crossed the channel.  Less than a year ago, a family of five Iranians died crossing the Channel when the boat capsized: Rasoul Irannejad, 35, his wife, Shiva Mohammad Panahi, 35, Anita Irannejad, 9, and Armin Irannejad, 6, died in the accident, and the body of their 15-month-old son was never found.  Britain ’ s Border Patrol says 83 people came to Britain on four boats last Friday alone.  The Home Office says it is fighting human trafficking gangs and has managed to stop some 4,000 asylum seekers from travelling to the UK last year.  The head of the refugee council says the government's measures are "not effective" and should instead "increase safe routes so people don't risk their lives".

passages.title: Drowned refugees in the Channel are Iranians.
passages.passage: A woman and a man who died with their three children while trying to reach Britain are from the village of Glynne.  The website also published the names and photos of the deceased.  French authorities on Tuesday confirmed the capsizing of a small boat carrying asylum seekers and the death of four people on board in the English Channel.  The third child of the Kurdish family is missing.  A total of 27 people were on the way.  A number of survivors are being treated in the hospital.  The rescue operation involved several coast guard boats and a Belgian army helicopter.  British Prime Minister Boris Johnson offered his condolences to the survivors.  British Home Secretary Priti Patel expressed sympathy for the victims and said she was very sorry to hear the news.  Patel said the incident once again highlighted the dangers of crossing the canal.  He promised to do everything in his power to stop traffickers from exploiting refugees in need.  The English Channel (English Channel) is a canal in northern France and southern Britain that connects the Atlantic Ocean to the North Sea.  According to data from PA Media, more than 7,400 people reached the UK via the English Channel in small boats this year, nearly four times more than in 2019.  This year ’ s “record ” was set with the arrival of 416 refugees on September 2.  Official statistics show that from June 2019 to June 2020, more than 3,400 people who applied for asylum are under the age of 17.  Of these, nearly 2,800 were unaccompanied children.  The British government can return refugees arriving from France under the Dublin Accords.  According to the treaty, asylum seekers who have entered Europe are only allowed to apply for asylum at their place of entry on European soil.

passages.title: 40 refugees, including several Iranians, rescued from the English Channel
passages.passage: British and French officials said they had rescued a total of 40 asylum-seekers, including several children, in separate operations in the English Channel on Tuesday morning.  The migrants were on five boats and, according to British officials, came from three countries: Iraq, Iran and Afghanistan.  Eight of them, including two children, were rescued by the French navy after their boat ’ s engine failed 20 kilometers from Calais.  France has extradited these refugees to Britain.  All of the rescued refugees were handed over to immigration authorities after initial medical treatment.  Children have also been handed over to youth support institutions.  Join Deutsche Welle ’ s Telegram channel. Thousands of refugees have been trying to reach Britain through France in recent years.  Two years ago, French authorities closed a refugee camp in the port of Calais, known as the Jungle.  There were 6,000 refugees in the camp.  Since then, France has been trying to prevent the formation of small refugee camps.  In the past few months, several asylum seekers believed to be Iranian nationals have been rescued by British forces in the English Channel.  In November, about 100 asylum-seekers, most of them Iranian nationals, made their way to Britain ’ s shores via the English Channel.  The English Channel is located in the north of France and the south of England and is one of the busiest British shipping routes.

passages.title: About 50 Iranian and Iraqi refugees arrested near British coast
passages.passage: Photo copyright PA Media Image caption HMC Reicher is one of four UK Border Guard patrol boats patrolling the Port of Dover in Kent province, and about 50 refugees who were boat bound for the UK were stopped and arrested by the British Coast Guard at separate events near the coast of Kent and Sussex in the south of the UK.  They said they have Iranian and Iraqi nationality.  Twenty of these illegal immigrants were arrested on the beach of the village of Dungenes in Kent, England.  In the second case, British Coast Guard forces intercepted a small boat with 11 men on board as it crossed the English Channel and transported the passengers to Dover Harbor.  Sussex police have arrested six illegal immigrants, including three children, on the coast of the province.  In another incident, the Home Office reported that at noon yesterday, 10 asylum-seekers, including eight men and two women, were taken ashore by border guards from another boat crossing the Channel.  All 47 illegal immigrants said they had Iranian and Iraqi nationality.  Since 3 November 2018, at least 976 people, including 89 children, have crossed the English Channel, the shortest water route between France and Britain, to reach the UK.  In November last year there was a significant increase in the number of asylum seekers trying to cross the English Channel to Britain, with the Home Secretary calling the issue a "serious incident" and calling for the French government to work together to resolve the issue.  A significant number of the refugees were Iranian, Afghan and Syrian.  A Home Office spokesman told the BBC: "People crossing the Channel in these small boats are putting their lives and their children at risk."  He added that since December, two British patrol ships have been patrolling the area from their overseas missions to protect the waterfront.  It has also been agreed with the French authorities that the border authorities of the two countries will increase their activities at the Information and Cooperation Centre in the French port of Calais.  “Under current practice, people in need of protection and seeking asylum must apply for asylum in the first safe country they arrive in, and more than 50 asylum seekers who arrived in the UK illegally have been returned to Europe since January, ” the Home Office said.  Calais, France ’ s closest port to Britain, has been the main route for illegal immigration for more than three decades.  Nearly three years after the destruction of the Jungle camp in the port of Calais, nearly 1,000 refugees are still in the city to make their way to Britain.

passages.title: Deportation of thousands of illegal asylum seekers in the UK with the easing of Croatian restrictions
passages.passage: The Guardian has gained access to the contents of a document in which a Home Office official wrote to city council chiefs in a letter that the process began with a view to cutting off government support for people whose asylum claims have been rejected.  Detainees will only have 21 days to evacuate the accommodation provided to them by the government and then leave the country.  Deputy Home Secretary Chris Phillip wrote in the letter that he would provide details of the cases of people under investigation by the Home Office to city councils for evacuation plans.  Meanwhile, a Home Office spokesman said the government has spent the past year using taxpayer money to resettle migrants whose asylum claims were rejected in the coronavirus outbreak, but with the reduction of Croatian restrictions and when rejected refugees can return to their homes, “it makes sense that this support should be stopped. ”  Charities and human rights activists have condemned the government ’ s decision as inhumane.  They have warned that the move will increase the number of homeless people in the city and lead to an increase in the number of people infected with coronavirus, and the UK's public health agency has also expressed concern about the government's decision.  According to the Guardian, around 60,000 migrants whose asylum cases have been rejected have been resettled by the Home Office.  Andy Hewitt, a senior fellow at the UK Refugee Council, said: “This is deeply troubling news for people in vulnerable situations, putting them at risk of homelessness.  We should not forget that the coronavirus epidemic has not yet ended and people are still denied access to humanitarian agencies and services.  The move comes as the UK government has recently made changes to the country ’ s immigration system, making it harder to grant asylum to people who enter the country illegally.  Home Secretary Priti Patel last month detailed the government ’ s plan, explaining that under the new rules, people who enter the UK illegally will not have the same rights as people who enter the UK legally.  He said many refugees, including women and children, had died en route to the UK, saying the new asylum system would work faster, more fairly and better to protect vulnerable people.  Stating that the way to prevent the death of refugees is to prevent human trafficking, he said the new measures by the London government have created a safe and legal route for immigration to the country.  “So if you enter the UK illegally through a safe country where you could apply for asylum, you ’ re not actually seeking asylum to escape an immediate danger, you ’ re choosing the UK as your destination. ”  He is referring to the refugees who took the perilous route of the English Channel by boat from France to reach England.  Activists and human rights activists described the immigration crackdown of the British interior minister as similar to the policies of the former US president and warned against repeating the fate of Donald Trump.  During his four years in office, Trump has implemented the most stringent immigration policies against Muslim-majority countries.

passages.title: Britain is changing the rules for accepting refugees. Those who import people illegally face life sentences.
passages.passage: Britain is changing the rules for accepting refugees.  A group of migrants on the banks of the English Channel in the English county of Kent The British government is preparing to present a "new immigration plan" that will change the rules of asylum in the country.  It provides for restrictions on obtaining legal status for those who illegally cross the border, as well as life imprisonment for those who help to enter the country illegally.  Interior Minister Priti Patel believes that the new system will be fairer and will help fight crime.  But human rights activists and the opposition criticize the government ’ s plans, seeing them as discrimination against refugees on the basis of how they got into the country.  Over the past year, 35,000 people have applied for asylum in the UK.  Among them, most were citizens of Iran, Albania and Iraq.  How does the system work and what do the authorities want to change?  Britain ’ s Conservative Party has consistently fought against illegal immigration.  Now the government is going to deprive migrants who entered the country illegally, the opportunity to receive asylum on an equal basis with those who entered on official documents.  In an interview with BBC Radio 4, Interior Minister Preeti Patel criticized the existing system of filing and processing asylum applications.  According to her, officials are littered with fictitious statements, and the number of illegal migrants threatens the lives of ordinary people and causes an increase in crime.  Photo caption: Patel believes the current refugee reception system is dangerous to society.  “We want a comprehensive reform to make our system work, ” the minister said.  She assured that the new system would accept people who are really fleeing persecution – for example, women, children and families stuck in “squalid camps in scary parts of the world. ”  According to the minister, it is inhumane to allow illegal migration and smuggling of people, which leads to migrants being found dead in the back of a truck or drowning in the English Channel.  In 2019, a truck was found in England with the bodies of 39 people who were migrants from Vietnam.  Patel insists that migrants should seek asylum in the EU country where they first arrived, rather than trying to get from there to Britain.  It looked forward to the cooperation of European countries in preventing that practice.  Photo caption: Border guards are taking migrants to the English Channel near Dover "These are not hot spots.  These are safe countries.  It is important to emphasize this, ” the minister added.  In addition, the government wants to significantly speed up the process of deporting those whose petitions have been rejected.  This will require reform of the appeals system.  But refugees who arrived in Britain through legal resettlement schemes from countries such as Syria and Iran, under the new rules, will immediately have the right to remain in the country.  Those migrants who paid smugglers to enter the country will be able to get only temporary status, which will be constantly reviewed.  In addition, it is proposed to strictly check the age of migrants to prevent the entry of adults under the guise of minors.  Patel also announced that migrants who returned to Britain after a failed asylum application and deportation would face up to five years in prison.  Under current rules, the maximum penalty is six months in prison.  Smugglers will face a lifetime sentence.  Over the past year, 8,500 people have crossed the English Channel illegally, and many of them have resorted to the services of criminals.  More than 8,000 migrants have crossed the English Channel illegally over the past year.  The head of the British NGO "Refugee Union" Enver Solomon accused the government of plans to discriminate refugees on the basis of how they got into the country.  The head of the British Red Cross, Mike Adamson, agreed.  He believes that the proposed amendments essentially create an unfair two-tier system in which each case and the degree of support will be determined by how the person got into the country, not how much they need to be protected.  He said it was inhuman.  Shadow Home Secretary Nick Thomas-Symonds, a spokesman for the opposition Labour Party, told BBC Radio 4 that the government ’ s plans will not speed up the processing of applications and will not stop criminals and those who turn to them, but may deprive those who really need it.  “The validity of the asylum application does not depend on how the person entered the country, ” said Thomas-Symonds.  He promised, however, to study the Government's plans in detail when they were presented.  Sangita Iyengar, an immigration law expert at London-based law firm Goldsmith Chambers, criticized the government ’ s plans in an interview with the BBC.  She considered that they could be contrary to international law and could be challenged in court, since international refugee provisions did not contain the concept of illegal immigration.  The author of the photo, Getty Images caption to the photo, Refugees from Syria on the Scottish island of Bute "It's just illegal," Iyengar said.  "We have an international obligation under the Refugee Convention to protect anyone who is persecuted and to consider applications based on the need for such protection.  How a person got to Britain doesn ’ t matter. ”  Dominique Cassiani, the BBC ’ s domestic policy correspondent, last year nearly 30,000 people applied for asylum in Britain.  Of these, more than 8,000 crossed the English Channel in small boats with the help of smugglers.  The Interior Ministry claims that the system is collapsing under the pressure of illegal migration.  However, the number of people entering Britain today is a third of the record, and this figure is significantly lower than in a number of neighboring countries of the European Union.  But at the same time, the number of people waiting for a decision on their application is eight times higher than a decade ago, and this is not counting the effect of the pandemic.  Critics cite these figures and say the real problem is years of mismanagement.  Now the UK can send asylum seekers back to the countries from which they came, only with the consent of the authorities of these countries.  Although flights regularly return migrants from some regions, the government no longer has such an arrangement with the EU.  As part of Brexit, it decided to leave the European scheme, which allowed the return of migrants to France and other countries.  About the plans and timing of the new agreement with Brussels is not yet known.  Now the procedure for applying for asylum in the UK consists of several stages.  Firstly, the applicant must leave his or her country or be unable to return because of the threat of persecution.  Photo caption by PA Media, Border Patrol in the English Channel To start the process, he must file a petition and be interviewed by an immigration official.  For providing knowingly false information, the migrant faces deportation or imprisonment for up to two years.  If the application is rejected at the initial stage, the person must return to their country or "safe country" - the one through which they got to Britain, or the state with which they are somehow connected.  If it is rejected after a detailed examination, the applicant can appeal the decision.  If the application is granted and the person (or family) receives asylum, he can stay in the UK for five years, and then apply for a residence permit and even citizenship.  With the withdrawal from the European Union, Britain also left the Dublin Convention on Refugees, which regulates the responsibility of EU countries with regard to refugees.  Thus, the old arrangements for the return of migrants from Britain to the EU are no longer valid.

passages.title: Times – cruelty and waste of money – imprisonment of illegal migrants will cost Britons more than their maintenance
passages.passage: The House of Commons of the British Parliament will consider a bill providing for criminal liability for migrants crossing the border “without a valid entry permit ”, writes The Times.  According to a study by the Refugee Board, the cost of imprisoning refugees would be five times higher than the cost of maintaining them in the asylum support system.  A proposal by the UK Home Office led by Priti Patel to tighten immigration laws will cost taxpayers up to £412 million a year, The Times reported, citing a study by the Refugee Council.  On Monday evening, Patel will inform members of the House of Commons that refugees arriving in the country legally will be granted an indefinite residence permit from October, and, on the contrary, those who cross the border “without a valid entry permit ” face criminal liability.  After the speech of the Minister, parliamentarians will vote for the bill, according to which the punishment for this crime will be up to four years in prison.  According to the newspaper, last year 8,420 people illegally crossed the English Channel.  Under the old rules, only a few dozen of them could be prosecuted, since the crime of “entering the country without permission ” technically does not apply to migrants intercepted in territorial waters and brought ashore by border forces.  The new rules would make it possible to condemn most of these illegal migrants, as criminal liability would extend to those who were intercepted and escorted to a safe place by border forces.  However, according to a study by the Refugee Council, jailing illegal migrants could cost the UK £412 million annually, or £1.65 billion in four years in prison.  According to the charity, the cost of imprisonment of refugees will be five times higher than the cost of their maintenance in the system of support for asylum seekers.  Moreover, according to a survey conducted by the organization in conjunction with the analytical center British Future, the majority of Britons do not support the bill.  For example, three out of five residents of Albion agree that the asylum system needs improvement, but they believe that any reforms should preserve the basic principle of providing protection to those who need it.  More than half of the respondents agreed that every migrant should expect a fair consideration of an asylum application.  “Treating vulnerable men, women and children who have put their lives at risk to be safe in the UK as criminals is not only a waste of taxpayer money, but also a cruel, ruthless and heartless response from the government, ” said Executive Director of the Council, Enver Solomon.  Resettlement is the main way to obtain asylum in the UK.  Currently, the rules imply that refugees can stay in the country for five years, after which they can apply for permission to stay indefinitely.  However, from October, the scheme will allow you to obtain an indefinite residence permit.  Those who arrive in the UK illegally will only be able to apply for temporary settlement, which will be repeatedly reviewed until migrants can return to a safe country.  Patel is expected to speak in the House of Commons in defense of changing the rules, pointing to the "generosity" of the British people to refugees.  In particular, according to the head of the Ministry of Internal Affairs, since 2015 more than 25 thousand people have moved to the country from regions torn by conflicts.

passages.title: Iranian migrant boat sinking in English Channel; UK and France
passages.passage: The sinking of boats of Iranian migrants in the English Channel; the support of refugees from Britain and France has been criticized by several refugee organizations, Reuters, who have said that the deaths of two children and two adults in the sinking of a boat carrying migrants in the English Channel should be a "wake-up call" for those in power.  Save the Children said the English Channel should not be a graveyard for children.  On Monday, a boat carrying refugees sank across the English Channel in waters between France and Britain, killing at least four people.  The victims may have been Iranian.  A man drowned, and a woman and two children aged five and eight died of cardiac arrest, but their resuscitation was not successful.  Another 15 people believed to be Iranian were taken to the hospital, and two others are believed to be missing at sea.  Arsalan Yarahmadi, editor-in-chief of the website of the Hengaw Human Rights Organization, told BBC Persian that our sources have confirmed that "the drowned were five members of a cold-blooded family".  The Hengaw human rights organization said: "The bodies of four members of the family have been discovered by search teams.  “There is no news of the 15-month-old baby. ”  The search for the missing passengers is expected to resume today, after a nighttime stop.  The BBC's Simon Jones said: "If someone is still on the channel, it's probably not a 'rescue operation' anymore and it's a search operation."  The prosecutor of the French city of Dunkirk has opened an investigation into the cause of the sinking of the ship.  Image source, Reuters explaining the image, the survivors were taken to hospital by the group "Calais Care", calling on the British government to find a legal way for refugees to arrive in the country.  “The loss of life should be a wake-up call for those in power in France and Britain. ”  The organisation said the creation of a new system that would allow asylum seekers to enter the UK from outside its borders would "put an end to the dreaded and dangerous sea crossing and prevent such catastrophes".  British Prime Minister Boris Johnson expressed his condolences to the families of the victims, saying: “We have told France that we will not spare any support to investigate this terrible incident and at the same time we will do all we can to crack down on ruthless criminal groups who are sending vulnerable people on such dangerous journeys. ”  At the same time, Save the Children called for a “joint action plan ” between France and Britain to ensure the safety of families affected.  The English Channel should not be turned into a children ’ s cemetery.  The boat, about two kilometres off the coast of France, was accidentally spotted by a passing sailboat at 9: 30 am local time and the matter was immediately reported to French authorities.  Four French vessels, a Belgian helicopter and a French fishing boat were involved in the search, but when rescue teams arrived, the boat had sunk.

passages.title: France to implement action plan to prevent migrants crossing the English Channel
passages.passage: Paris, January 5, 2019 (AFP) The French government announced today that it will use a "plan of action" to counter migrants attempting to cross the English Channel to the UK, pledging to end the phenomenon, which the British Conservative government fears.  The increase in asylum seekers across the sea, mostly Iranians, has put pressure on the British government to respond, with Home Secretary Sajid Javid declaring it a “major event ”.  French Interior Minister Christophe Castaner said in a statement today: "This project should allow us to put an end to the sea crossing," adding that these actions are not only illegal but also extremely dangerous.  "It is in our interest and that of the United Kingdom to do everything possible to prevent the development of new networks that would again attract irregular migrants to our shores," the statement added.  The plan will increase police patrols near ports where some migrants try to steal boats and monitor beaches where rubber boats have been deployed.  In addition to four British coastal patrol vessels, a British naval vessel was also patrolling the English Channel today.  A spokesman for French maritime operations in the region told AFP this week that France had doubled the number of coast guard vessels in the Channel depending on the weather. passages.title: France and Britain strengthen security measures to prevent illegal crossings of asylum seekers from the Channel Sea
passages.passage: France ’ s Interior Minister Christophe Castaner and his British counterpart Sajid Javid met on Sunday to discuss the expansion of cooperation between the two countries to deal with the illegal passage of asylum seekers across the Channel Sea, and several measures will be implemented soon.  Measures taken by both France and the United Kingdom to prevent asylum seekers from moving from northern France to the United Kingdom will include an increase in the number of surveillance patrols, serious measures to combat trafficking groups, as well as alerting refugees to the dangers of unsafe passage through the Channel Sea.  Interior Minister Sajid Javid said more border protection would also protect refugees and prevent humanitarian disasters.  According to the House of Commons MP Kent, more than 200 illegal asylum seekers have arrived in the UK from France in the past two months using unsafe boats and equipment.  On Sunday, December 30, an Iranian asylum seeker who had crossed the Channel using a motorboat to reach the UK were arrested.

passages.title: 25 migrants found in Dutch ship morgue in UK
passages.passage: Dutch authorities said on Wednesday that all of the migrants were alive and that a number of them, who were likely to develop hypothermia, had been taken to the clinic for medical examinations.  Hypothermia, or frostbite, is a general condition that follows a decrease in body temperature, causing damage to all organs and dysfunction.  This condition can cause death if advanced and untreated.  According to the report, the migrants were hiding on the British ship Sewis, which was supposed to be heading from the Dutch port of Flurdingen to the port of Suffolk.  When the ship ’ s officials detect the presence of migrants, the ship returns halfway to its origin.  At the same time, police forces are ready to interrogate migrants to take them to detention centers after medical examinations.  The identity of the migrants is not known, but reports suggest that most of them are men.  A spokesman for the ship told the Guardian that refrigerated containers were routinely checked and sealed, but smugglers appeared to have pierced them to accommodate the migrants.  It is not yet clear how the migrants managed to get onto the ship due to security considerations, he added, but one has to accept the fact that, despite all security considerations, some operations are being carried out successfully, "after the bodies of 39 people were found inside a refrigerated truck in Essex, England, last month.  It was later discovered that the bodies belonged to illegal immigrants.  British police began their investigation after the bodies were found, which included eight women and 31 men.  With the discovery of a truck carrying the bodies in Essex, police in the early stages of their investigation suspected that the victims were Chinese.  A spokesman for China's foreign ministry said police had said the nationalities of the victims were indistinguishable, but the Chinese embassy in London remained in close contact with the British government and urged the UK to provide more information.  On Saturday, China ’ s official Xinhua news agency quoted British police as saying all 39 people on board were Vietnamese.  In 2000, 58 Chinese citizens were found dead in a truck in the British port of Dover, and in 2015 71 bodies were found on a highway in Austria.  Belgian police also found 12 illegal migrants in a refrigerated truck in the north of the country.  Belgian police found the illegal migrants from Syria and Sudan in an area near the port city of Antwerp.  The undocumented migrants were taken to an immigration office in the city of Antwerp.  The number of migrants arriving in the UK has been increasing since the end of last year.  They are trying to get to the UK before the EU tightens its immigration rules, but there are no figures on the number, but last Sunday 39 migrants arrived in the UK via four inflatable boats through the English Channel and were arrested by police.  Last September, 86 migrants illegally entered the south coast of England in one day and were taken to detention centres.

passages.title: Hundreds of refugees arrested in the Channel
passages.passage: According to a statement released by the Home Office on Friday, 102 migrants were arrested on this day alone as they crossed the English Channel from France to enter the UK.  The number of those arrested in the last two days has risen to about 200.  British border police arrested at least 90 migrants on Thursday, including 15 minors.  Many of those arrested said they were Iranian citizens.  A number have also come from Afghanistan, Pakistan, Syria and Iraq.  They are expected to be returned to France under the Dublin agreement.  According to the agreement, asylum seekers who have entered Europe are only allowed to apply for asylum at their place of entry.  If they go to another European country, they will be returned to their country of origin in Europe.  The number of migrants crossing the Channel has fallen, according to security minister Brandon Lewis, as the number of migrants and asylum seekers entering the UK via the English Channel has fallen.  He said on Friday that a large number of migrants crossing the English Channel illegally into the UK had been "stopped".  Lewis said only close to 25 percent of migrants who attempted to cross the waterway this year were successful, a significant decrease compared to the same period last year (48 percent).  French police have warned migrants not to use small boats to cross the blue border.  Some reports suggest that the reason why migrants are safe in unsafe boats has been the calm of the sea in recent days.  The English Channel (English Channel) is a canal in northern France and southern England that connects the Atlantic Ocean to the North Sea.

passages.title: The UK government ’ s anti-immigration policies.
passages.passage: Britain ’ s Interior Minister Priti Patel, who has proposed the plan, plans to send migrants to countries such as Turkey, the Isle of Man or Gibraltar.  Islands outside Scotland are also being explored as options.  Patel claimed that he had spoken with the authorities of the aforementioned countries and obtained their initial approval.  The Gibraltar government reacted to the British interior minister's claim hours after the news was published, calling it unfounded speculation by the London government.  At the same time, charities have called the UK ’ s proposal “inhumane ” and experts have warned of legal problems.  An unnamed immigration expert told The Times of London that there is no legal barrier to deportations to third countries.  But the measure is debatable and can be taken to court.  Patel will soon propose a plan to transform the UK ’ s immigration system, which he says is “fair but solid. ”  He said he would provide legal pathways for migrants from war-torn countries to enter.  People from safe countries will not be granted asylum in the UK.  They are then transferred to third countries to be assigned.  That said, the process could take months or even years.  Last year, more than 8,420 migrants illegally crossed the English Channel from France to the south west coast.  Since the beginning of the year, 800 people have immigrated to the UK illegally.  Britain has shunned the EU ’ s plan to accept refugees among its member states by leaving the EU, but the continued illegal entry and the Paris government ’ s failure to work together to stop the flow of migrants through the English Channel have become the Achilles heel of Britain ’ s immigration policies.  Activists and human rights activists described the immigration crackdown of the British interior minister as similar to the policies of the former US president and warned against repeating the fate of Donald Trump.  During his four years in office, Trump has implemented the most stringent immigration policies against Muslim-majority countries.

passages.title: The flow of refugees and immigrants to Europe has decreased – UN
passages.passage: The flow of refugees and immigrants to Europe decreased in the first half of 2017, but many of them are still subjected to violence and die in attempts to cross the Mediterranean.  This is stated in a new report published by the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees.  Despite the decline in arrivals, the number of deaths remains high due to the fact that those wishing to reach the shores of Europe often use the services of smugglers, the document says.  READ ALSO: Rioting migrants in Rome were pacified by water cannons “It is morally unacceptable to take measures to reduce the number of refugees and immigrants arriving in Europe without working for peace and development, ” said UN High Commissioner for Refugees Filippo Grandi.  “We can ’ t afford to ignore crimes that are certain to be happening simply because they are happening out of our sight, ” he added.  Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF), an international organization known by its French acronym, has suspended its humanitarian mission to rescue migrants in the Mediterranean because of threats from the Libyan coast guard, as well as obstacles that the Italian government creates for the activists of the organization.

passages.title: 39 bodies hidden in a container truck in the United Kingdom reveal the sad song of illegal immigrants to go to a free country ｜ Hong Kong 01 ｜ Real-time International
passages.passage: In Essex, England, 39 people were found dead in a container truck.  Authorities are investigating the identities of the dead and where they came from, but the incident raises the question of why illegal immigrants continue to risk their lives to the UK.  Thousands of people have died on their way to Europe, the BBC said, and many have been found dead in long-distance container trucks like this incident, and countless others have drowned.  According to the United Nations, since the outbreak of the refugee crisis in 2014, nearly 17,500 people have died in the Angry Sea.  Debbie Busler, head of the Refugee Support Unit of the British Red Cross, believes that these refugees are carrying different kinds of pain and insecurity that make them determined to leave their homes, such as fleeing war or political, religious or gender-related persecution, so they are betting on their lives to escape to safe areas.  The streets of the French port city of Ouistreham are often filled with thrilling scenes of people chasing cars, mainly refugees from Africa, who want to board ferries to the UK on a “windmill ”. (Getty Images) Basler said that even if they“ arrive ”, there may be a lack of basic services such as translation, which will make it difficult for them to integrate into the new world for years.  Therefore, she believes that people should not label them simply as "refugees", but rather respect their dignity and regard them as people in desperate need of help.  However, there is a downward trend in the official number of asylum seekers, but it is very difficult for illegal immigrants to be granted refugee status.  In the first nine months of 2019, 1,742 people applied for asylum in Bulgaria, of which only 132 were granted asylum, 212 were granted humanitarian assistance and 932 were denied.  The numbers of applications in 2018, 17 and 16 were 2536, 3700 and 19480 respectively.  The authorities said the largest influx of illegal immigrants into the UK was in the African country of Eritrea, Iraq, Afghanistan and Iran in the Middle East.  In fact, to sneak to the UK, you first need to reach Europe. The BBC points out that illegal immigrants have four main routes to Europe, including from West and North Africa to Spain, via the Mediterranean to Italy, from the east to Poland, and the busiest route: via Turkey to the Balkans.  At the end of the day, across the English Channel, illegal immigrants have mostly turned to Europe to enter the UK, such as from Cherbourg in France to Rosslare or Dublin in Ireland, and then to Holyhead in the north of Wales, due to the closure of the Calais refugee camp in 2016 and increased security. head).  Even as French authorities cleared refugee camps and tightened security in 2016, Calais still lures many illegal immigrants to the country in the hope of finding a new life in the UK. (Getty Images) Expensive and adventurous trip The National Crime Agency (NCA) acknowledges that illegal immigrants may use all ports to enter the country, along with vast coastlines and the huge annual cargo throughput that law enforcement must eliminate. Immigrants are very difficult.  Figures from the Department for Transport show that around 3.6 million lorries and containers entered the UK through 40 ports across the country in 2018, making them the main vehicle for illegal immigration.  They paid at least £10,000 in exchange for a small space to hide in the vehicles.  The NCA is currently sharing intelligence with a number of countries in the UK and Europe to combat human trafficking syndicates, and Europol has set up a special intelligence centre to collect information on human trafficking.  British police have targeted large gangs such as Bulgaria, Serbia, Bosnia and Montenegro for smuggling from the Balkan Peninsula, and have joined forces with the Home Office to ensure that the country will continue to work with Europe to combat illegal immigration in the post-Brexit era.

passages.title: UN reports record number of refugee deaths in Mediterranean
passages.passage: A record number of deaths of migrants and refugees in the Mediterranean Sea occurred in 2018.  The number of people killed or missing has already exceeded 1,600, according to a report by the UN Refugee Agency (UNHCR).  According to the document, in 2018, the number of refugees arriving in Europe decreased by 42%, but the mortality rate among them increased sharply.  In particular, in the Mediterranean last year for every 43rd refugee accounted for one dead, now every 18th migrant dies in this area.  “This report confirms once again that the Mediterranean route is the most deadly, ” said Pascal Moreau, head of UNHCR ’ s European Office.  The number of refugees seeking to move to Europe via the Mediterranean coast increased in 2015 due to the sharp escalation of conflicts in several countries in the Middle East and North Africa.  In July, 63 people went missing off the coast of Libya as a result of a shipwreck.

passages.title: In a refugee camp in Greece, there was a fire, there is a dead man
passages.passage: In connection with the wars in Africa and the Middle East, which involved the countries of Europe and the United States, since 2015 the world has been overwhelmed by a wave of refugees and other African, Middle Eastern and South Asian migrants.  If in 2014 280 thousand migrants arrived in the European Union, in 2015 their number was up to 2 million people.  The main source of refugees was Syria.  Most migrants applied for asylum in Germany: almost 500,000 in 2015.  Hungary and Sweden have also become “popular ” countries.  The refugees reached their destination countries mainly by overloaded and fragile inflatable and wooden boats, which were repeatedly wrecked.  Mass migration has led to a crisis in the European Union and a sharp increase in social tensions.  Particularly resonant was the news of crimes committed by migrants, some of whom entered Europe under the guise of refugees.  Britain ’ s exit from the European Union, in particular, was associated with the demand for stricter regulation of the flow of migrants.  However, according to the decision of the court of the European Union, until Brexit is fully completed, Britain is obliged to accept refugees from the EU.  Many experts in 2019 believe that a new migration crisis for Europe is only a matter of time, as instability in the world continues to increase.  Since 2013, Australia has adopted very strict rules on refugees.  As early as 2001, the Australian authorities reached an agreement with neighboring poor countries, Nauru and Papua New Guinea, to establish refugee reception centers on their territory, where all asylum seekers in Australia were redirected.  Since 2008, the program was stopped, but in 2013 it was resumed again, further fencing off the territory of Australia itself from migrants.  Human rights defenders have reported numerous human rights violations in the centres and intolerable living conditions, with repeated riots and riots.  In 2015, there were only 35,600 refugees in Australia.

passages.title: Forecast for 2021: what should we prepare for?
passages.passage: Behind us is an epochal, difficult year that forced society to adapt to new realities.  We face many common challenges at the economic, geopolitical, social and climate levels.  The UN has declared 2021 the International Year of Peace and Trust, as well as the Year of the Creative Economy for Sustainable Development.  What can we expect from the coming year?  COVID-19 Vaccination in Puerto Rico Carlos Giusti / Copyright 2019 The Associated Press.  All rights reserved.  The future of the coronavirus pandemic will largely depend on two things, experts say: the strength of immunity developed after an infection, and the effectiveness of vaccines.  In Europe, vaccines are promised to provide everyone, as well as implement a plan for economic recovery.  Joe Biden Patrick Semansky / Copyright 2020 The Associated Press.  All rights reserved.  In the United States, the era of Donald Trump ends and the era of Joe Biden begins. The agreement sets a framework for limiting global warming to up to 1.5 ° C.  Migration Residents of a migrant camp near Athens Yorgos Karahalis / Copyright 2020 The Associated Press. To fully recover from the shock caused by the coronavirus pandemic, it will take much longer than originally expected.  This was stated by the head of the European Central Bank. This means that new rules will come into force for business, trade and Britons, including those living abroad.  Key dates for 2021 January 1: Brexit will take effect on the first day of the year.  January 20: Biden is scheduled to be inaugurated in Washington as the 46th President of the United States.
