May 18-21: A pandemic forced the World Economic Forum to move from Davos to Singapore in 2021.  May 18-22: Eurovision Song Contest will be held, cancelled in 2020 due to coronavirus.  June 18: Presidential elections in Iran.  September 11 will mark the 20th anniversary of the largest terrorist attacks in history.  September 19: elections to the State Duma of the Russian Federation.  September 26: 20th Bundestag election.  October 15-16: Parliamentary elections in the Czech Republic.

passages.title: A repeat of the nightmare of 2015. Europe is facing a new migration crisis
passages.passage: https: / / ria.ru / 20210525 / migratsiya-1733716124.html A repeat of the nightmare of 2015.  Europe is facing a new migration crisis, a repeat of the nightmare of 2015.  Europe is waiting for a new migration crisis - RIA Novosti, 25.05.2021 A repeat of the nightmare of 2015.  Europe is once again on the brink of a migration crisis.  And this is not yet the summer, which traditionally accounts for the peak of the wave of illegal migration from countries...  RIA Novosti, 25.05.2021 2021-05-25T08: 00 2021-05-25T08: 00 2021-05-25T08: 02 migrants refugees europe authors / html / head / meta [@ name = 'og: title'] / @ content / html / head / meta [@ name = 'og: description'] / @ content https: / / cdn.com 24.img.ria.ru / images / 07e5 / 05 / 18 / 1733713287 _ 0: 153: 1920: 1233 _ 1920x0 _ 80 _ 0 _ 85ca65dc729db44d8073637ad5013c74.jpg Europe is again on the verge of a migration crisis.  And this is not yet the summer, which traditionally accounts for the peak of the wave of illegal migration from Asia and Africa.Now in the center of attention is Ceuta, a Spanish enclave in North Africa, where thousands of illegal refugees from Morocco rushed.  The refugee crisis in Ceuta and Melilla (another Spanish port in Africa) is largely the result of the artificial escalation of relations between Spain and Morocco.  According to many observers, Rabat decided to take revenge on Madrid for the assistance recently provided to the Polisario Front (which for many years has been fighting for the independence of Western Sahara from Morocco).  The revenge was the actual inaction of the border guards of this country, who turned a blind eye to the crowds of migrants breaking into Ceuta.  According to The Economist magazine, in this way King Mohammed VI of Morocco “made migration a weapon ” .But in fact, the sharp influx of refugees from Africa began not only in the Spanish enclaves.  Again, a series of flimsy ships illegally transporting Africans (mainly Libyans) from Tunisia to the Italian island of Lampedusa.  Last week, 1,200 people were transferred there during 12 hours of good weather alone.  And even despite the weather, accidents were recorded: 73 refugees from Bangladesh almost drowned trying to reach the cherished island.  How long it took, no one can say.  According to the Italian Interior Ministry, 4,290 migrants reached the country ’ s shores in the first three weeks of May.  While for the whole of May last year, their number was 1654 people.  The flow of illegal refugees is also increasing between the EU and Britain.  Since January, more than three thousand people have crossed the English Channel.  And over the same period last year, this figure was 1,400 refugees – more than double the growth.  Just the other day, the Belgian coast guard rescued a sinking ship on which 49 migrants, mostly Vietnamese, tried to cross the strait.  Based on the above facts and statistics, we can safely assume that the migration crisis will return to the European agenda in the foreseeable future.  However, the numbers are not as catastrophic as they were in 2015, when Europe was literally drowned by a flood of refugees.  And the increase compared to last year is easily explained by the fact that in 2020, many people in Asia and Africa gave up their intentions to go to pandemics in Europe.  In addition, the result of the shift of public attention from the problem of migration to the fight against the covid was a noticeable decrease in the ratings of a number of parties advocating strict measures to limit the influx of immigrants (in the Western media, these political organizations are usually indiscriminately called ultra-right, even despite the rather liberal economic program of many of them).  It is quite logical that now, with the rapid return of migration problems to the agenda, many publications have sounded the alarm in connection with the imminent growth of the popularity of these political forces.  Almost all analysts agree that the crisis around Ceuta, which has not descended from the front pages of the Spanish press for several days, will significantly strengthen the anti-Islamic party Vox (Voice).  Even before the current crisis, it actively dispersed the fears of the enclave residents in connection with the influx of poor Africans.  And in the end, it won the first place in the parliamentary elections of 2019, receiving more than 35 percent of the vote – and this is in a city where 40 percent of the population is Muslim.  It would be strange if the Vox party did not now take advantage of the crisis to increase its popularity in Ceuta.  For example, a local cell of the party is publicizing protests against the fact that African migrants entering the Spanish enclave receive coronavirus vaccinations, while Spanish citizens living there wait months for their turn.  This is confirmed by events in the regional parliament of Andalusia, where after the 2018 elections, for the first time in history, the People ’ s Party took the first place and was able to form a minority government.  Until last week, it relied solely on the informal support of Vox MPs.  However, on Thursday, they announced the termination of cooperation with the senior partner in connection with the fact that the authorities of the region agreed to accept 13 minor refugees who infiltrated Ceuta.  This could lead to the fall of the regional government and early elections.  That is why the People ’ s Party is forced to show more and more rigidity in the migration issue, causing panic in the European liberal media.Even more worrying in the mainstream is the electoral situation in Italy.  After the 2015 crisis, the League party, led by Matteo Salvini, has been the consistent leader of the polls there.  Having proved himself a tough fighter against illegal migration as the Minister of Internal Affairs, he increased the leadership of his party to record levels.  At the peak of popularity in the summer of 2019, the League ’ s figures were approaching 40 percent, which gave it hope even for the formation of its government.  Based on these calculations, Salvini provoked a government crisis in order to hold early elections, but was outplayed by opponents.  Since last year, there has been a drop in the ratings of this political force, whose supporters cannot forgive the support it expressed for the technocratic government of Mario Draghi.  Liberals can breathe freely.  But the fact is that the ratings of the League, which is still in the first place in the polls, are moving on opposite courses with the rapidly growing indicators of the even more right-wing and even more anti-migrant party “Brothers of Italy ”.  According to some polls, she already came in second place after the League, behind that couple of percent.  Three years ago, its ratings fluctuated around three to four percent, and now confidently approaching 20.  If elections were held now, these two forces, with the support of Silvio Berlusconi ’ s Forward Italy party, could well form a majority government.  They do not hide their ideological continuity from the far-right Italian social movement, which was created in 1946 by former supporters of Benito Mussolini.  This legacy is clearly indicated by the logo of the party, which includes the former symbol of ISD.The growth of the popularity of the "Brothers" will contribute to the charisma of the head of the party Georgia Meloni ("Sisters of Italy", as it was nicknamed by the press) - she last year surpassed in the approval ratings of the leader of the "League", becoming the second most popular politician in the country after the current prime minister.  There is no doubt that in the event of an aggravation of the migration crisis, the League and Brothers will be able to get additional votes to their already serious ratings.  Trends in the first months of the year show that the threat of the covid is no longer deterring refugees seeking to Europe.  And this means that the nightmare of 2015 may repeat itself — and the popularity of far-right, anti-migrant, anti-Islamic, Eurosceptic parties will again sharply rise.  The readiness of Brussels to these challenges looks very doubtful.  https: / / ria.ru / 20201030 / proval-1582373436.html https: / / radiosputnik.  ria.ru / 20200303 / 1568118823.html https: / / ria.ru / 20200306 / 1568246603.html https: / / radiosputnik.  ria.ru / 20210125 / parizh-1594449907.html https: / / ria.ru / 20201030 / migratsiya-1582276677.html https: / / ria.ru / 20200522 / 1571842607.html Europe RIA Novosti 1 5 4.7 96 internet-group @ rian.ru 7 495 645-6401 FSUE P MIA "Russia Today" https: / / xn-c1acbl2abdlkab1og.xn-p1ai / awards / 353 60 2021 Vladimir Kornilov https: / / cdn23.img

passages.title: UN: EU to Blame for Deaths of Migrants in Mediterranean Sea
passages.passage: The United Nations has been implicated in the deaths of migrants in the Mediterranean because of its refusal to respond to calls for emergency relief, its refusal to meet humanitarian rescue efforts and its push to return them to Libya.  In its 37-page report, the UN said the number of migrant deaths this year on the sea route had so far reached 632.  The United Nations has described the incident as a “large-scale humanitarian tragedy. ”  Thousands of migrants and refugees, including from African countries, make long and risky voyages through Libya each year in hopes of getting to Europe and living a better life.  They often use small, inflatable boats to cross this dangerous path.  The report concluded that the lack of protection for migrants “is not a sad anomaly, but rather a consequence of the policies, decisions and actions of Libyan authorities, EU members, institutions and other actors.  The European Union has not only reduced the search and rescue operations of migrants in Mediterranean waters, but its governments have each hindered the rescue operations of humanitarian organizations with their own administrative and criminal proceedings.  Migrants told the UN Human Rights Office there were also efforts to "repatriate migrants at sea", which would return ships carrying migrants from international waters to Libya with the help of European helicopters.  The report is based on interviews with 80 migrants between January 2019 and December 2020.  According to them, some have faced interception operations by Libyan officials and their lives are in danger.  Some boats have been shot down, causing boats to capsize or forcing migrants to jump into the sea.  Most of the migrants returned to Libya face exploitation and ill-treatment.  Commenting on the report, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Michelle Bachelet called for urgent reforms in the search and rescue policies and actions taken by Libya, the European Union and its member states to ensure that such policies and measures are complied with international law.  The real tragedy is that it is preventable to prevent the suffering and deaths of migrants on the current Mediterranean route.  The United Nations has called on European countries to use more effective and efficient mechanisms to address the wave of migrants and refugees.  The Guardian previously revealed that European countries used brutal methods to stop the passage of almost 40,000 refugees during the coronavirus epidemic, resulting in 2,000 deaths.

passages.title: 39 'Iranian' refugees detained on Britain's southeast coast
passages.passage: Sean Gallup / Getty Images Image caption One of the boats normally used by asylum seekers to cross the Channel to the UK, four boats carrying 39 Iranian refugees were taken off Sunday, November 17, at separate events off Britain's southeast coast.  The British Interior Ministry confirmed that all of the asylum seekers identified themselves as “Iranian ”.  The first boat, which had nine people on board, took off at 4: 40 a.m. yesterday, while the second, with five people on board, reached the British coast at around 6 a.m.  According to the Coast Guard and Kent County Police, a boat with 11 people on board was seized at around 7 a.m. and a half hour later another boat with 14 people was taken off the coast of the UK.  As soon as they received a message of help from the boats, rescue helicopters, as well as rescue boats from the ports of Dover, Dunness and Hastings, as well as two coast guard vessels, took action to rescue the passengers.  A Home Office spokesman said: "Crossing the canal by these small boats is extremely dangerous.  For those who have gone through such a journey, their lives and their loved ones are at risk. ”  According to the British Home Office, over the past two years Iranian citizens have applied for asylum more than any other country in the UK.  In 2017, about 9% of all 26,350 asylum applications were submitted by Iranians.  In November last year there was a significant increase in the number of asylum seekers trying to cross the English Channel to Britain, with the Home Secretary calling the issue a "serious incident" and calling for the French government to work together to resolve the issue.  Due to the increasing number of migrants and asylum seekers arriving on the east coast of the UK via the sea and the English Channel, the British Coast Guard has announced an increase in staff.

A large number of these refugees are Iranian.  Sajid Javid, the British Home Secretary, returned to London in the middle of a family holiday and planned a joint Blue Patrol force with his French counterpart.  It was reported that on Sunday, at the same time as the minister ’ s efforts, six other Iranian men reached the beach near Dover.  The French say they stopped the influx of more refugees on Saturday.  Mr Javid has been accused by his rival party and even his own party of failing to act properly and should have dealt with the matter more harshly.  Javid eventually reached an agreement with French Interior Minister Christophe Castaner to become more active in the coming weeks.  LEWIS MORRIS Image caption Six Iranian men were taken from the water on Sunday The group was found in a boat where the two ministers agreed to deal with human traffickers, and another part involved informing refugees about the dangers of crossing the Channel in small boats.  The British Interior Ministry has given no further explanation in this regard.  More than 220 people have tried to reach the UK by boat in the past two months.  In addition to the Iranians, citizens of Afghanistan and Syria are also among the refugees.  Britain has five lifeboats, only one currently operating.  The other four are in the Mediterranean Sea and are helping with rescue operations there.  It is not known whether the other four boats will return to Britain.  Since 2017, about 2,200 people have taken refuge in the UK every month.  The increase in the number of Iranian refugees, according to the Financial Times, is the result of the worsening economic situation in the country.

Title: Refugee crisis: France and Britain strengthen border surveillance to stop migrants crossing the Channel
Content: France and the United Kingdom have signed a new agreement to end illegal immigration through the English Channel.  In recent months, with an increasing number of migrants trying to reach the British coast illegally, the English Channel has become one of the most dangerous crossings for asylum seekers.  Since the beginning of the year, seven people, including a family of five, have drowned while crossing the English Channel.  Britain ’ s interior minister, Priti Patel, announced on Saturday that the French and British governments had reached an agreement to combat migrant smuggling and stop illegal immigration through the Channel.  Britain ’ s interior minister and his French counterpart, Gerald Darmann, have signed the agreement, stressing that they intend to make it impossible for asylum seekers to cross the English Channel, which has reached more than 8,000 this year.  Priti Patel said that as part of the agreement, the French government has committed to doubling the number of its coast guard patrols in the area by December 1 to stop migrant boats in the Channel, and to use new equipment such as drones and radar to identify people trying to cross the Channel to reach the British coast.  Britain ’ s interior minister expressed his satisfaction with the signing of the agreement, saying: “This agreement will make it possible for both France and Britain to make it impossible for migrants to cross the Channel. ”  Signing a new 😍 😍 😍 😍 covenant to tackle small boat crossings.  There will be an increase in surveillance with cuttingedge tech introduce greater security at ports Ensure accommodation for migrants in France https: / / t.co / vjG1KiTkep pic.twitter.com / COJ1jncjcjitC — i Patel (@ pritipatel) November 28, 2020 According to AFP, the two countries have agreed to spend 31.4 million euros on the joint project.  In recent months, the number of migrants attempting to cross the English Channel illegally has increased dramatically.  News of the sinking of boats carrying refugees, which killed four people last year and killed seven this year, including a family of five, has made the Channel a dangerous crossroads for migrants and has severely affected public opinion.  Following the incident, the British government accused France of not doing enough to stop refugees from crossing the Channel.  In September, French authorities said they had blocked 1,300 migrants trying to cross the English Channel.  Between January 1 and August 31, some 6,200 asylum seekers, wearing life jackets and using a variety of inflatable boats, paddles and kayaks provided by smugglers, tried to reach the British coast by illegally crossing the English Channel.  On October 27, following the capsizing of the boat carrying refugees, the majority of whom were Iranian nationals, the 35-year-old Rasoul Irannejad, his wife Shiva Mohammad Panahi, two children aged 6 and 9, and their 15-month-old baby, who were from Sardasht and were trying to cross the Channel from France to Britain, drowned and died.  One of the first asylum seekers to drown in the English Channel in 2019 was Mitra, a 31-year-old Iranian girl with a master ’ s degree in psychology who, along with 19 Iranian and Iraqi refugees, including seven children, boarded a boat for the UK on August 9.  Every year, thousands of people from the Middle East and African countries try to reach Britain through the English Channel.  The Channel, which lies between France and Britain, has seen a dramatic increase in small boats carrying refugees to Britain since 1918, in which a number of refugees have been involved in accidents and some have died. Title: Britain calls on social media to remove videos of crossing the Channel
Content: Britain has asked social media to remove videos of people crossing the English Channel (16 June 1400 – 6 June 2021) Image source, UK Home Secretary PA Media has called for social media to remove videos showing refugees crossing the Channel as "attractive" and encouraging them to cross.  Britain ’ s Interior Minister Priti Patel said in a letter to social media executives on Saturday that “videos ” of refugees crossing the English Channel from Europe to Britain were“ unacceptable ”. The Home Office also said it was investigating reports that a British border patrol vessel had requested entry into French waters and that asylum seekers had been taken from a boat en route to Britain.  The British Home Secretary ’ s letter came after a widely circulated video on social media, including TikTok, showing a group of men crossing the English Channel.  The Interior Ministry says smugglers are using the video, which has been shared on Twitter, Instagram and Facebook, to advise desperate refugees to cross the Channel.  Ms Patel says the messages posted on social media that “promote this deadly crossing, and even make it look attractive, are unacceptable. ”  "These images encourage those in a safe European country to leave, putting their lives and their families at risk."  The UK Home Secretary says human traffickers are using the videos to promote their deadly trade.  The letter said: "What is not mentioned in the videos are those who lost their lives and that refugees must be stranded for at least 13 hours in an unfit boat in cold water."  The source, PA Media, said the British border boat had taken the refugees from the water, saying social media had made "great progress" in removing the videos, but that it needed to be done faster and more effectively so that more men, women and children did not die as they crossed the channel.  Less than a year ago, a family of five Iranians died crossing the Channel when the boat capsized: Rasoul Irannejad, 35, his wife, Shiva Mohammad Panahi, 35, Anita Irannejad, 9, and Armin Irannejad, 6, died in the accident, and the body of their 15-month-old son was never found. Title: Deportation of thousands of illegal asylum seekers in the UK with the easing of Croatian restrictions
Content: The Guardian has gained access to the contents of a document in which a Home Office official wrote to city council chiefs in a letter that the process began with a view to cutting off government support for people whose asylum claims have been rejected.  Detainees will only have 21 days to evacuate the accommodation provided to them by the government and then leave the country.  Deputy Home Secretary Chris Phillip wrote in the letter that he would provide details of the cases of people under investigation by the Home Office to city councils for evacuation plans.  Meanwhile, a Home Office spokesman said the government has spent the past year using taxpayer money to resettle migrants whose asylum claims were rejected in the coronavirus outbreak, but with the reduction of Croatian restrictions and when rejected refugees can return to their homes, “it makes sense that this support should be stopped. ”  Charities and human rights activists have condemned the government ’ s decision as inhumane.  They have warned that the move will increase the number of homeless people in the city and lead to an increase in the number of people infected with coronavirus, and the UK's public health agency has also expressed concern about the government's decision.  According to the Guardian, around 60,000 migrants whose asylum cases have been rejected have been resettled by the Home Office.  Andy Hewitt, a senior fellow at the UK Refugee Council, said: “This is deeply troubling news for people in vulnerable situations, putting them at risk of homelessness.  We should not forget that the coronavirus epidemic has not yet ended and people are still denied access to humanitarian agencies and services.  The move comes as the UK government has recently made changes to the country ’ s immigration system, making it harder to grant asylum to people who enter the country illegally.  Home Secretary Priti Patel last month detailed the government ’ s plan, explaining that under the new rules, people who enter the UK illegally will not have the same rights as people who enter the UK legally.  He said many refugees, including women and children, had died en route to the UK, saying the new asylum system would work faster, more fairly and better to protect vulnerable people.  Stating that the way to prevent the death of refugees is to prevent human trafficking, he said the new measures by the London government have created a safe and legal route for immigration to the country.  “So if you enter the UK illegally through a safe country where you could apply for asylum, you ’ re not actually seeking asylum to escape an immediate danger, you ’ re choosing the UK as your destination. ”  He is referring to the refugees who took the perilous route of the English Channel by boat from France to reach England.  Activists and human rights activists described the immigration crackdown of the British interior minister as similar to the policies of the former US president and warned against repeating the fate of Donald Trump.  During his four years in office, Trump has implemented the most stringent immigration policies against Muslim-majority countries.

Title: Britain is changing the rules for accepting refugees. Those who import people illegally face life sentences.
Content: Britain is changing the rules for accepting refugees.  A group of migrants on the banks of the English Channel in the English county of Kent The British government is preparing to present a "new immigration plan" that will change the rules of asylum in the country.  It provides for restrictions on obtaining legal status for those who illegally cross the border, as well as life imprisonment for those who help to enter the country illegally.  Interior Minister Priti Patel believes that the new system will be fairer and will help fight crime.  But human rights activists and the opposition criticize the government ’ s plans, seeing them as discrimination against refugees on the basis of how they got into the country.  Over the past year, 35,000 people have applied for asylum in the UK.  Among them, most were citizens of Iran, Albania and Iraq.  How does the system work and what do the authorities want to change?  Britain ’ s Conservative Party has consistently fought against illegal immigration.  Now the government is going to deprive migrants who entered the country illegally, the opportunity to receive asylum on an equal basis with those who entered on official documents.  In an interview with BBC Radio 4, Interior Minister Preeti Patel criticized the existing system of filing and processing asylum applications.  According to her, officials are littered with fictitious statements, and the number of illegal migrants threatens the lives of ordinary people and causes an increase in crime.  Photo caption: Patel believes the current refugee reception system is dangerous to society.  “We want a comprehensive reform to make our system work, ” the minister said.  She assured that the new system would accept people who are really fleeing persecution – for example, women, children and families stuck in “squalid camps in scary parts of the world. ”  According to the minister, it is inhumane to allow illegal migration and smuggling of people, which leads to migrants being found dead in the back of a truck or drowning in the English Channel.  In 2019, a truck was found in England with the bodies of 39 people who were migrants from Vietnam.  Patel insists that migrants should seek asylum in the EU country where they first arrived, rather than trying to get from there to Britain.  It looked forward to the cooperation of European countries in preventing that practice.  Photo caption: Border guards are taking migrants to the English Channel near Dover "These are not hot spots.  These are safe countries.  It is important to emphasize this, ” the minister added.  In addition, the government wants to significantly speed up the process of deporting those whose petitions have been rejected.  This will require reform of the appeals system.  But refugees who arrived in Britain through legal resettlement schemes from countries such as Syria and Iran, under the new rules, will immediately have the right to remain in the country.  Those migrants who paid smugglers to enter the country will be able to get only temporary status, which will be constantly reviewed.  In addition, it is proposed to strictly check the age of migrants to prevent the entry of adults under the guise of minors.  Patel also announced that migrants who returned to Britain after a failed asylum application and deportation would face up to five years in prison.  Under current rules, the maximum penalty is six months in prison.  Smugglers will face a lifetime sentence.  Over the past year, 8,500 people have crossed the English Channel illegally, and many of them have resorted to the services of criminals.  More than 8,000 migrants have crossed the English Channel illegally over the past year.  The head of the British NGO "Refugee Union" Enver Solomon accused the government of plans to discriminate refugees on the basis of how they got into the country.  The head of the British Red Cross, Mike Adamson, agreed.  He believes that the proposed amendments essentially create an unfair two-tier system in which each case and the degree of support will be determined by how the person got into the country, not how much they need to be protected.  He said it was inhuman.  Shadow Home Secretary Nick Thomas-Symonds, a spokesman for the opposition Labour Party, told BBC Radio 4 that the government ’ s plans will not speed up the processing of applications and will not stop criminals and those who turn to them, but may deprive those who really need it.  “The validity of the asylum application does not depend on how the person entered the country, ” said Thomas-Symonds.  He promised, however, to study the Government's plans in detail when they were presented.  Sangita Iyengar, an immigration law expert at London-based law firm Goldsmith Chambers, criticized the government ’ s plans in an interview with the BBC.  She considered that they could be contrary to international law and could be challenged in court, since international refugee provisions did not contain the concept of illegal immigration.  The author of the photo, Getty Images caption to the photo, Refugees from Syria on the Scottish island of Bute "It's just illegal," Iyengar said.  "We have an international obligation under the Refugee Convention to protect anyone who is persecuted and to consider applications based on the need for such protection.  How a person got to Britain doesn ’ t matter. ”  Dominique Cassiani, the BBC ’ s domestic policy correspondent, last year nearly 30,000 people applied for asylum in Britain.  Of these, more than 8,000 crossed the English Channel in small boats with the help of smugglers.  The Interior Ministry claims that the system is collapsing under the pressure of illegal migration.  However, the number of people entering Britain today is a third of the record, and this figure is significantly lower than in a number of neighboring countries of the European Union.  But at the same time, the number of people waiting for a decision on their application is eight times higher than a decade ago, and this is not counting the effect of the pandemic.  Critics cite these figures and say the real problem is years of mismanagement.  Now the UK can send asylum seekers back to the countries from which they came, only with the consent of the authorities of these countries.  Although flights regularly return migrants from some regions, the government no longer has such an arrangement with the EU.  As part of Brexit, it decided to leave the European scheme, which allowed the return of migrants to France and other countries.  About the plans and timing of the new agreement with Brussels is not yet known.  Now the procedure for applying for asylum in the UK consists of several stages.  Firstly, the applicant must leave his or her country or be unable to return because of the threat of persecution.  Photo caption by PA Media, Border Patrol in the English Channel To start the process, he must file a petition and be interviewed by an immigration official.  For providing knowingly false information, the migrant faces deportation or imprisonment for up to two years.  If the application is rejected at the initial stage, the person must return to their country or "safe country" - the one through which they got to Britain, or the state with which they are somehow connected.  If it is rejected after a detailed examination, the applicant can appeal the decision.  If the application is granted and the person (or family) receives asylum, he can stay in the UK for five years, and then apply for a residence permit and even citizenship.  With the withdrawal from the European Union, Britain also left the Dublin Convention on Refugees, which regulates the responsibility of EU countries with regard to refugees.  Thus, the old arrangements for the return of migrants from Britain to the EU are no longer valid.

Title: Times – cruelty and waste of money – imprisonment of illegal migrants will cost Britons more than their maintenance
Content: The House of Commons of the British Parliament will consider a bill providing for criminal liability for migrants crossing the border “without a valid entry permit ”, writes The Times.  According to a study by the Refugee Board, the cost of imprisoning refugees would be five times higher than the cost of maintaining them in the asylum support system.  A proposal by the UK Home Office led by Priti Patel to tighten immigration laws will cost taxpayers up to £412 million a year, The Times reported, citing a study by the Refugee Council.  On Monday evening, Patel will inform members of the House of Commons that refugees arriving in the country legally will be granted an indefinite residence permit from October, and, on the contrary, those who cross the border “without a valid entry permit ” face criminal liability.  After the speech of the Minister, parliamentarians will vote for the bill, according to which the punishment for this crime will be up to four years in prison.  According to the newspaper, last year 8,420 people illegally crossed the English Channel.  Under the old rules, only a few dozen of them could be prosecuted, since the crime of “entering the country without permission ” technically does not apply to migrants intercepted in territorial waters and brought ashore by border forces.  The new rules would make it possible to condemn most of these illegal migrants, as criminal liability would extend to those who were intercepted and escorted to a safe place by border forces.  However, according to a study by the Refugee Council, jailing illegal migrants could cost the UK £412 million annually, or £1.65 billion in four years in prison.  According to the charity, the cost of imprisonment of refugees will be five times higher than the cost of their maintenance in the system of support for asylum seekers.  Moreover, according to a survey conducted by the organization in conjunction with the analytical center British Future, the majority of Britons do not support the bill.  For example, three out of five residents of Albion agree that the asylum system needs improvement, but they believe that any reforms should preserve the basic principle of providing protection to those who need it.  More than half of the respondents agreed that every migrant should expect a fair consideration of an asylum application.  “Treating vulnerable men, women and children who have put their lives at risk to be safe in the UK as criminals is not only a waste of taxpayer money, but also a cruel, ruthless and heartless response from the government, ” said Executive Director of the Council, Enver Solomon.  Resettlement is the main way to obtain asylum in the UK.  Currently, the rules imply that refugees can stay in the country for five years, after which they can apply for permission to stay indefinitely.  However, from October, the scheme will allow you to obtain an indefinite residence permit.  Those who arrive in the UK illegally will only be able to apply for temporary settlement, which will be repeatedly reviewed until migrants can return to a safe country.  Patel is expected to speak in the House of Commons in defense of changing the rules, pointing to the "generosity" of the British people to refugees.  In particular, according to the head of the Ministry of Internal Affairs, since 2015 more than 25 thousand people have moved to the country from regions torn by conflicts.

Europe is waiting for a new migration crisis - RIA Novosti, 25.05.2021 A repeat of the nightmare of 2015.  Europe is once again on the brink of a migration crisis. RIA Novosti, 25.05.2021 2021-05-25T08: 00 2021-05-25T08: 00 2021-05-25T08: 02 migrants refugees europe authors / html / head / meta [@ name = 'og: title'] / @ content / html / head / meta [@ name = 'og: description'] / @ content https: / / cdn.com 24.img.ria.ru / images / 07e5 / 05 / 18 / 1733713287 _ 0: 153: 1920: 1233 _ 1920x0 _ 80 _ 0 _ 85ca65dc729db44d8073637ad5013c74.jpg Europe is again on the verge of a migration crisis.  And this is not yet the summer, which traditionally accounts for the peak of the wave of illegal migration from Asia and Africa.Now in the center of attention is Ceuta, a Spanish enclave in North Africa, where thousands of illegal refugees from Morocco rushed.  The refugee crisis in Ceuta and Melilla (another Spanish port in Africa) is largely the result of the artificial escalation of relations between Spain and Morocco.  According to many observers, Rabat decided to take revenge on Madrid for the assistance recently provided to the Polisario Front (which for many years has been fighting for the independence of Western Sahara from Morocco).  The revenge was the actual inaction of the border guards of this country, who turned a blind eye to the crowds of migrants breaking into Ceuta.  According to The Economist magazine, in this way King Mohammed VI of Morocco “made migration a weapon ” .But in fact, the sharp influx of refugees from Africa began not only in the Spanish enclaves.  Again, a series of flimsy ships illegally transporting Africans (mainly Libyans) from Tunisia to the Italian island of Lampedusa.  Last week, 1,200 people were transferred there during 12 hours of good weather alone.  And even despite the weather, accidents were recorded: 73 refugees from Bangladesh almost drowned trying to reach the cherished island.  How long it took, no one can say.  According to the Italian Interior Ministry, 4,290 migrants reached the country ’ s shores in the first three weeks of May.  While for the whole of May last year, their number was 1654 people.  The flow of illegal refugees is also increasing between the EU and Britain.  Since January, more than three thousand people have crossed the English Channel.  And over the same period last year, this figure was 1,400 refugees – more than double the growth.  Just the other day, the Belgian coast guard rescued a sinking ship on which 49 migrants, mostly Vietnamese, tried to cross the strait.  Based on the above facts and statistics, we can safely assume that the migration crisis will return to the European agenda in the foreseeable future.  However, the numbers are not as catastrophic as they were in 2015, when Europe was literally drowned by a flood of refugees.  And the increase compared to last year is easily explained by the fact that in 2020, many people in Asia and Africa gave up their intentions to go to pandemics in Europe.  In addition, the result of the shift of public attention from the problem of migration to the fight against the covid was a noticeable decrease in the ratings of a number of parties advocating strict measures to limit the influx of immigrants (in the Western media, these political organizations are usually indiscriminately called ultra-right, even despite the rather liberal economic program of many of them).  It is quite logical that now, with the rapid return of migration problems to the agenda, many publications have sounded the alarm in connection with the imminent growth of the popularity of these political forces.  Almost all analysts agree that the crisis around Ceuta, which has not descended from the front pages of the Spanish press for several days, will significantly strengthen the anti-Islamic party Vox (Voice).  Even before the current crisis, it actively dispersed the fears of the enclave residents in connection with the influx of poor Africans.  And in the end, it won the first place in the parliamentary elections of 2019, receiving more than 35 percent of the vote – and this is in a city where 40 percent of the population is Muslim.  It would be strange if the Vox party did not now take advantage of the crisis to increase its popularity in Ceuta.  For example, a local cell of the party is publicizing protests against the fact that African migrants entering the Spanish enclave receive coronavirus vaccinations, while Spanish citizens living there wait months for their turn.  This is confirmed by events in the regional parliament of Andalusia, where after the 2018 elections, for the first time in history, the People ’ s Party took the first place and was able to form a minority government.  Until last week, it relied solely on the informal support of Vox MPs.  However, on Thursday, they announced the termination of cooperation with the senior partner in connection with the fact that the authorities of the region agreed to accept 13 minor refugees who infiltrated Ceuta.  This could lead to the fall of the regional government and early elections.  That is why the People ’ s Party is forced to show more and more rigidity in the migration issue, causing panic in the European liberal media.Even more worrying in the mainstream is the electoral situation in Italy.  After the 2015 crisis, the League party, led by Matteo Salvini, has been the consistent leader of the polls there.  Having proved himself a tough fighter against illegal migration as the Minister of Internal Affairs, he increased the leadership of his party to record levels.  At the peak of popularity in the summer of 2019, the League ’ s figures were approaching 40 percent, which gave it hope even for the formation of its government.  Based on these calculations, Salvini provoked a government crisis in order to hold early elections, but was outplayed by opponents.  Since last year, there has been a drop in the ratings of this political force, whose supporters cannot forgive the support it expressed for the technocratic government of Mario Draghi.  Liberals can breathe freely.  But the fact is that the ratings of the League, which is still in the first place in the polls, are moving on opposite courses with the rapidly growing indicators of the even more right-wing and even more anti-migrant party “Brothers of Italy ”.  According to some polls, she already came in second place after the League, behind that couple of percent.  Three years ago, its ratings fluctuated around three to four percent, and now confidently approaching 20.  If elections were held now, these two forces, with the support of Silvio Berlusconi ’ s Forward Italy party, could well form a majority government.  They do not hide their ideological continuity from the far-right Italian social movement, which was created in 1946 by former supporters of Benito Mussolini.  This legacy is clearly indicated by the logo of the party, which includes the former symbol of ISD.The growth of the popularity of the "Brothers" will contribute to the charisma of the head of the party Georgia Meloni ("Sisters of Italy", as it was nicknamed by the press) - she last year surpassed in the approval ratings of the leader of the "League", becoming the second most popular politician in the country after the current prime minister.  There is no doubt that in the event of an aggravation of the migration crisis, the League and Brothers will be able to get additional votes to their already serious ratings.  Trends in the first months of the year show that the threat of the covid is no longer deterring refugees seeking to Europe.  And this means that the nightmare of 2015 may repeat itself — and the popularity of far-right, anti-migrant, anti-Islamic, Eurosceptic parties will again sharply rise. Title: Four refugees, including two children, drowned in the English Channel.
Content: Four asylum-seekers, including two children, drowned in the English Channel (Reuters) Photo source: A rescue operation has been going on for hours by French boats since French authorities announced the deaths of two children and a man and woman who were trying to cross the English Channel to reach Britain.  A boat carrying refugees has sunk across the English Channel between France and Britain.  The prosecutor of the French city of Dunkirk has opened an investigation into the cause of the sinking of the ship.  These people are said to be Iranian.  A massive rescue operation has been under way for hours, which crashed near the northern French city of Dunkirk.  According to French authorities, two children aged 5 and 8 and a man and woman died.  The other 14 were taken to hospitals in the port of Calais and the French city of Dunkirk.  The English Channel, between France and Britain, is one of the world ’ s busiest waterways, and it can be dangerous to cross by small vessels, especially in winter when the sea is stormy.  Another disaster came after the British Meteorological Office warned of bad weather and strong winds in the Channel region.  Natalie Alpeik, MP for the Dover region in the British Parliament, said: “It ’ s terrible that there ’ s been another disaster on the canal.  Human traffickers have no respect for human life: "A sailboat accidentally encountered a ship and alerted French authorities of the incident.  Four French ships, a Belgian helicopter and a French fishing vessel were involved in the rescue.  Since the beginning of the year, more than 7,400 asylum seekers have arrived in Britain by sea in small boats.  While there are still two months left until the end of 2020, that number is 1,825 more than in 2019.  The survivors were taken by helicopter to hospitals in the port of Calais and the northern French city of Dunkirk on Thursday, August 6, and a total of 235 migrants, including several pregnant women, crossed the English Channel from Europe to the southern coast of Britain.  This is the highest recorded number of illegal immigrants arriving in the region in a single day.  About ten days ago, Home Secretary Priti Patel announced the “most significant revision ” of the country ’ s asylum system in a decade.

Title: Refugee crisis: France and Britain strengthen border surveillance to stop migrants crossing the Channel
Content: France and the United Kingdom have signed a new agreement to end illegal immigration through the English Channel.  In recent months, with an increasing number of migrants trying to reach the British coast illegally, the English Channel has become one of the most dangerous crossings for asylum seekers.  Since the beginning of the year, seven people, including a family of five, have drowned while crossing the English Channel.  Britain ’ s interior minister, Priti Patel, announced on Saturday that the French and British governments had reached an agreement to combat migrant smuggling and stop illegal immigration through the Channel.  Britain ’ s interior minister and his French counterpart, Gerald Darmann, have signed the agreement, stressing that they intend to make it impossible for asylum seekers to cross the English Channel, which has reached more than 8,000 this year.  Priti Patel said that as part of the agreement, the French government has committed to doubling the number of its coast guard patrols in the area by December 1 to stop migrant boats in the Channel, and to use new equipment such as drones and radar to identify people trying to cross the Channel to reach the British coast.  Britain ’ s interior minister expressed his satisfaction with the signing of the agreement, saying: “This agreement will make it possible for both France and Britain to make it impossible for migrants to cross the Channel. ”  Signing a new 😍 😍 😍 😍 covenant to tackle small boat crossings.  There will be an increase in surveillance with cuttingedge tech introduce greater security at ports Ensure accommodation for migrants in France https: / / t.co / vjG1KiTkep pic.twitter.com / COJ1jncjcjitC — i Patel (@ pritipatel) November 28, 2020 According to AFP, the two countries have agreed to spend 31.4 million euros on the joint project.  In recent months, the number of migrants attempting to cross the English Channel illegally has increased dramatically.  News of the sinking of boats carrying refugees, which killed four people last year and killed seven this year, including a family of five, has made the Channel a dangerous crossroads for migrants and has severely affected public opinion.  Following the incident, the British government accused France of not doing enough to stop refugees from crossing the Channel.  In September, French authorities said they had blocked 1,300 migrants trying to cross the English Channel.  Between January 1 and August 31, some 6,200 asylum seekers, wearing life jackets and using a variety of inflatable boats, paddles and kayaks provided by smugglers, tried to reach the British coast by illegally crossing the English Channel.  On October 27, following the capsizing of the boat carrying refugees, the majority of whom were Iranian nationals, the 35-year-old Rasoul Irannejad, his wife Shiva Mohammad Panahi, two children aged 6 and 9, and their 15-month-old baby, who were from Sardasht and were trying to cross the Channel from France to Britain, drowned and died.  One of the first asylum seekers to drown in the English Channel in 2019 was Mitra, a 31-year-old Iranian girl with a master ’ s degree in psychology who, along with 19 Iranian and Iraqi refugees, including seven children, boarded a boat for the UK on August 9.  Every year, thousands of people from the Middle East and African countries try to reach Britain through the English Channel.  The Channel, which lies between France and Britain, has seen a dramatic increase in small boats carrying refugees to Britain since 1918, in which a number of refugees have been involved in accidents and some have died. Title: Britain calls on social media to remove videos of crossing the Channel
Content: Britain has asked social media to remove videos of people crossing the English Channel (16 June 1400 – 6 June 2021) Image source, UK Home Secretary PA Media has called for social media to remove videos showing refugees crossing the Channel as "attractive" and encouraging them to cross.  Britain ’ s Interior Minister Priti Patel said in a letter to social media executives on Saturday that “videos ” of refugees crossing the English Channel from Europe to Britain were“ unacceptable ”.  Over the past week, hundreds of asylum seekers have crossed the Channel; five days ago, the Home Office confirmed that more than 568 people had crossed the Channel in four days.  Last Saturday alone, 336 people were taken off 19 boats and on Friday 144 on 7 boats.  The Home Office also said it was investigating reports that a British border patrol vessel had requested entry into French waters and that asylum seekers had been taken from a boat en route to Britain.  The British Home Secretary ’ s letter came after a widely circulated video on social media, including TikTok, showing a group of men crossing the English Channel.  The Interior Ministry says smugglers are using the video, which has been shared on Twitter, Instagram and Facebook, to advise desperate refugees to cross the Channel.  Ms Patel says the messages posted on social media that “promote this deadly crossing, and even make it look attractive, are unacceptable. ”  "These images encourage those in a safe European country to leave, putting their lives and their families at risk."  The UK Home Secretary says human traffickers are using the videos to promote their deadly trade.  The letter said: "What is not mentioned in the videos are those who lost their lives and that refugees must be stranded for at least 13 hours in an unfit boat in cold water."  The source, PA Media, said the British border boat had taken the refugees from the water, saying social media had made "great progress" in removing the videos, but that it needed to be done faster and more effectively so that more men, women and children did not die as they crossed the channel.  Less than a year ago, a family of five Iranians died crossing the Channel when the boat capsized: Rasoul Irannejad, 35, his wife, Shiva Mohammad Panahi, 35, Anita Irannejad, 9, and Armin Irannejad, 6, died in the accident, and the body of their 15-month-old son was never found.  Britain ’ s Border Patrol says 83 people came to Britain on four boats last Friday alone.  The Home Office says it is fighting human trafficking gangs and has managed to stop some 4,000 asylum seekers from travelling to the UK last year.  The head of the refugee council says the government's measures are "not effective" and should instead "increase safe routes so people don't risk their lives".

Title: 40 refugees, including several Iranians, rescued from the English Channel
Content: British and French officials said they had rescued a total of 40 asylum-seekers, including several children, in separate operations in the English Channel on Tuesday morning.  The migrants were on five boats and, according to British officials, came from three countries: Iraq, Iran and Afghanistan.  Eight of them, including two children, were rescued by the French navy after their boat ’ s engine failed 20 kilometers from Calais.  France has extradited these refugees to Britain.  All of the rescued refugees were handed over to immigration authorities after initial medical treatment.  Children have also been handed over to youth support institutions.  Join Deutsche Welle ’ s Telegram channel. Thousands of refugees have been trying to reach Britain through France in recent years.  Two years ago, French authorities closed a refugee camp in the port of Calais, known as the Jungle.  There were 6,000 refugees in the camp.  Since then, France has been trying to prevent the formation of small refugee camps.  In the past few months, several asylum seekers believed to be Iranian nationals have been rescued by British forces in the English Channel.  In November, about 100 asylum-seekers, most of them Iranian nationals, made their way to Britain ’ s shores via the English Channel.  The English Channel is located in the north of France and the south of England and is one of the busiest British shipping routes.

Title: About 50 Iranian and Iraqi refugees arrested near British coast
Content: Photo copyright PA Media Image caption HMC Reicher is one of four UK Border Guard patrol boats patrolling the Port of Dover in Kent province, and about 50 refugees who were boat bound for the UK were stopped and arrested by the British Coast Guard at separate events near the coast of Kent and Sussex in the south of the UK. In the second case, British Coast Guard forces intercepted a small boat with 11 men on board as it crossed the English Channel and transported the passengers to Dover Harbor.  Sussex police have arrested six illegal immigrants, including three children, on the coast of the province.  In another incident, the Home Office reported that at noon yesterday, 10 asylum-seekers, including eight men and two women, were taken ashore by border guards from another boat crossing the Channel. He added that since December, two British patrol ships have been patrolling the area from their overseas missions to protect the waterfront.  It has also been agreed with the French authorities that the border authorities of the two countries will increase their activities at the Information and Cooperation Centre in the French port of Calais.  “Under current practice, people in need of protection and seeking asylum must apply for asylum in the first safe country they arrive in, and more than 50 asylum seekers who arrived in the UK illegally have been returned to Europe since January, ” the Home Office said.  Calais, France ’ s closest port to Britain, has been the main route for illegal immigration for more than three decades.  Nearly three years after the destruction of the Jungle camp in the port of Calais, nearly 1,000 refugees are still in the city to make their way to Britain.

Title: Deportation of thousands of illegal asylum seekers in the UK with the easing of Croatian restrictions
Content: The Guardian has gained access to the contents of a document in which a Home Office official wrote to city council chiefs in a letter that the process began with a view to cutting off government support for people whose asylum claims have been rejected.  Detainees will only have 21 days to evacuate the accommodation provided to them by the government and then leave the country.  Deputy Home Secretary Chris Phillip wrote in the letter that he would provide details of the cases of people under investigation by the Home Office to city councils for evacuation plans.  Meanwhile, a Home Office spokesman said the government has spent the past year using taxpayer money to resettle migrants whose asylum claims were rejected in the coronavirus outbreak, but with the reduction of Croatian restrictions and when rejected refugees can return to their homes, “it makes sense that this support should be stopped. ”  Charities and human rights activists have condemned the government ’ s decision as inhumane.  They have warned that the move will increase the number of homeless people in the city and lead to an increase in the number of people infected with coronavirus, and the UK's public health agency has also expressed concern about the government's decision.  According to the Guardian, around 60,000 migrants whose asylum cases have been rejected have been resettled by the Home Office.  Andy Hewitt, a senior fellow at the UK Refugee Council, said: “This is deeply troubling news for people in vulnerable situations, putting them at risk of homelessness.  We should not forget that the coronavirus epidemic has not yet ended and people are still denied access to humanitarian agencies and services.  The move comes as the UK government has recently made changes to the country ’ s immigration system, making it harder to grant asylum to people who enter the country illegally.  Home Secretary Priti Patel last month detailed the government ’ s plan, explaining that under the new rules, people who enter the UK illegally will not have the same rights as people who enter the UK legally.  He said many refugees, including women and children, had died en route to the UK, saying the new asylum system would work faster, more fairly and better to protect vulnerable people.  Stating that the way to prevent the death of refugees is to prevent human trafficking, he said the new measures by the London government have created a safe and legal route for immigration to the country.  “So if you enter the UK illegally through a safe country where you could apply for asylum, you ’ re not actually seeking asylum to escape an immediate danger, you ’ re choosing the UK as your destination. ”  He is referring to the refugees who took the perilous route of the English Channel by boat from France to reach England.  Activists and human rights activists described the immigration crackdown of the British interior minister as similar to the policies of the former US president and warned against repeating the fate of Donald Trump.  During his four years in office, Trump has implemented the most stringent immigration policies against Muslim-majority countries.

Title: Britain is changing the rules for accepting refugees. Those who import people illegally face life sentences.
Content: Britain is changing the rules for accepting refugees.  A group of migrants on the banks of the English Channel in the English county of Kent The British government is preparing to present a "new immigration plan" that will change the rules of asylum in the country.  It provides for restrictions on obtaining legal status for those who illegally cross the border, as well as life imprisonment for those who help to enter the country illegally.  Interior Minister Priti Patel believes that the new system will be fairer and will help fight crime.  But human rights activists and the opposition criticize the government ’ s plans, seeing them as discrimination against refugees on the basis of how they got into the country.  Over the past year, 35,000 people have applied for asylum in the UK.  Among them, most were citizens of Iran, Albania and Iraq.  How does the system work and what do the authorities want to change?  Britain ’ s Conservative Party has consistently fought against illegal immigration.  Now the government is going to deprive migrants who entered the country illegally, the opportunity to receive asylum on an equal basis with those who entered on official documents.  In an interview with BBC Radio 4, Interior Minister Preeti Patel criticized the existing system of filing and processing asylum applications.  According to her, officials are littered with fictitious statements, and the number of illegal migrants threatens the lives of ordinary people and causes an increase in crime.  Photo caption: Patel believes the current refugee reception system is dangerous to society.  “We want a comprehensive reform to make our system work, ” the minister said.  She assured that the new system would accept people who are really fleeing persecution – for example, women, children and families stuck in “squalid camps in scary parts of the world. ”  According to the minister, it is inhumane to allow illegal migration and smuggling of people, which leads to migrants being found dead in the back of a truck or drowning in the English Channel.  In 2019, a truck was found in England with the bodies of 39 people who were migrants from Vietnam.  Patel insists that migrants should seek asylum in the EU country where they first arrived, rather than trying to get from there to Britain.  It looked forward to the cooperation of European countries in preventing that practice.  Photo caption: Border guards are taking migrants to the English Channel near Dover "These are not hot spots.  These are safe countries.  It is important to emphasize this, ” the minister added.  In addition, the government wants to significantly speed up the process of deporting those whose petitions have been rejected.  This will require reform of the appeals system.  But refugees who arrived in Britain through legal resettlement schemes from countries such as Syria and Iran, under the new rules, will immediately have the right to remain in the country.  Those migrants who paid smugglers to enter the country will be able to get only temporary status, which will be constantly reviewed.  In addition, it is proposed to strictly check the age of migrants to prevent the entry of adults under the guise of minors.  Patel also announced that migrants who returned to Britain after a failed asylum application and deportation would face up to five years in prison.  Under current rules, the maximum penalty is six months in prison.  Smugglers will face a lifetime sentence.  Over the past year, 8,500 people have crossed the English Channel illegally, and many of them have resorted to the services of criminals.  More than 8,000 migrants have crossed the English Channel illegally over the past year.  The head of the British NGO "Refugee Union" Enver Solomon accused the government of plans to discriminate refugees on the basis of how they got into the country.  The head of the British Red Cross, Mike Adamson, agreed.  He believes that the proposed amendments essentially create an unfair two-tier system in which each case and the degree of support will be determined by how the person got into the country, not how much they need to be protected.  He said it was inhuman.  Shadow Home Secretary Nick Thomas-Symonds, a spokesman for the opposition Labour Party, told BBC Radio 4 that the government ’ s plans will not speed up the processing of applications and will not stop criminals and those who turn to them, but may deprive those who really need it.  “The validity of the asylum application does not depend on how the person entered the country, ” said Thomas-Symonds.  He promised, however, to study the Government's plans in detail when they were presented.  Sangita Iyengar, an immigration law expert at London-based law firm Goldsmith Chambers, criticized the government ’ s plans in an interview with the BBC.  She considered that they could be contrary to international law and could be challenged in court, since international refugee provisions did not contain the concept of illegal immigration.  The author of the photo, Getty Images caption to the photo, Refugees from Syria on the Scottish island of Bute "It's just illegal," Iyengar said.  "We have an international obligation under the Refugee Convention to protect anyone who is persecuted and to consider applications based on the need for such protection.  How a person got to Britain doesn ’ t matter. ”  Dominique Cassiani, the BBC ’ s domestic policy correspondent, last year nearly 30,000 people applied for asylum in Britain.  Of these, more than 8,000 crossed the English Channel in small boats with the help of smugglers.  The Interior Ministry claims that the system is collapsing under the pressure of illegal migration.  However, the number of people entering Britain today is a third of the record, and this figure is significantly lower than in a number of neighboring countries of the European Union.  But at the same time, the number of people waiting for a decision on their application is eight times higher than a decade ago, and this is not counting the effect of the pandemic.  Critics cite these figures and say the real problem is years of mismanagement.  Now the UK can send asylum seekers back to the countries from which they came, only with the consent of the authorities of these countries.  Although flights regularly return migrants from some regions, the government no longer has such an arrangement with the EU.  As part of Brexit, it decided to leave the European scheme, which allowed the return of migrants to France and other countries.  About the plans and timing of the new agreement with Brussels is not yet known.  Now the procedure for applying for asylum in the UK consists of several stages.  Firstly, the applicant must leave his or her country or be unable to return because of the threat of persecution.  Photo caption by PA Media, Border Patrol in the English Channel To start the process, he must file a petition and be interviewed by an immigration official.  For providing knowingly false information, the migrant faces deportation or imprisonment for up to two years.  If the application is rejected at the initial stage, the person must return to their country or "safe country" - the one through which they got to Britain, or the state with which they are somehow connected.  If it is rejected after a detailed examination, the applicant can appeal the decision.  If the application is granted and the person (or family) receives asylum, he can stay in the UK for five years, and then apply for a residence permit and even citizenship.  With the withdrawal from the European Union, Britain also left the Dublin Convention on Refugees, which regulates the responsibility of EU countries with regard to refugees.  Thus, the old arrangements for the return of migrants from Britain to the EU are no longer valid.

Title: Times – cruelty and waste of money – imprisonment of illegal migrants will cost Britons more than their maintenance
Content: The House of Commons of the British Parliament will consider a bill providing for criminal liability for migrants crossing the border “without a valid entry permit ”, writes The Times.  According to a study by the Refugee Board, the cost of imprisoning refugees would be five times higher than the cost of maintaining them in the asylum support system.  A proposal by the UK Home Office led by Priti Patel to tighten immigration laws will cost taxpayers up to £412 million a year, The Times reported, citing a study by the Refugee Council.  On Monday evening, Patel will inform members of the House of Commons that refugees arriving in the country legally will be granted an indefinite residence permit from October, and, on the contrary, those who cross the border “without a valid entry permit ” face criminal liability.  After the speech of the Minister, parliamentarians will vote for the bill, according to which the punishment for this crime will be up to four years in prison.  According to the newspaper, last year 8,420 people illegally crossed the English Channel.  Under the old rules, only a few dozen of them could be prosecuted, since the crime of “entering the country without permission ” technically does not apply to migrants intercepted in territorial waters and brought ashore by border forces.  The new rules would make it possible to condemn most of these illegal migrants, as criminal liability would extend to those who were intercepted and escorted to a safe place by border forces.  However, according to a study by the Refugee Council, jailing illegal migrants could cost the UK £412 million annually, or £1.65 billion in four years in prison.  According to the charity, the cost of imprisonment of refugees will be five times higher than the cost of their maintenance in the system of support for asylum seekers.  Moreover, according to a survey conducted by the organization in conjunction with the analytical center British Future, the majority of Britons do not support the bill.  For example, three out of five residents of Albion agree that the asylum system needs improvement, but they believe that any reforms should preserve the basic principle of providing protection to those who need it.  More than half of the respondents agreed that every migrant should expect a fair consideration of an asylum application.  “Treating vulnerable men, women and children who have put their lives at risk to be safe in the UK as criminals is not only a waste of taxpayer money, but also a cruel, ruthless and heartless response from the government, ” said Executive Director of the Council, Enver Solomon.  Resettlement is the main way to obtain asylum in the UK.  Currently, the rules imply that refugees can stay in the country for five years, after which they can apply for permission to stay indefinitely.  However, from October, the scheme will allow you to obtain an indefinite residence permit.  Those who arrive in the UK illegally will only be able to apply for temporary settlement, which will be repeatedly reviewed until migrants can return to a safe country.  Patel is expected to speak in the House of Commons in defense of changing the rules, pointing to the "generosity" of the British people to refugees.  In particular, according to the head of the Ministry of Internal Affairs, since 2015 more than 25 thousand people have moved to the country from regions torn by conflicts.

Title: Iranian migrant boat sinking in English Channel; UK and France
Content: The sinking of boats of Iranian migrants in the English Channel; the support of refugees from Britain and France has been criticized by several refugee organizations, Reuters, who have said that the deaths of two children and two adults in the sinking of a boat carrying migrants in the English Channel should be a "wake-up call" for those in power.  Save the Children said the English Channel should not be a graveyard for children.  On Monday, a boat carrying refugees sank across the English Channel in waters between France and Britain, killing at least four people.  The victims may have been Iranian.  A man drowned, and a woman and two children aged five and eight died of cardiac arrest, but their resuscitation was not successful.  Another 15 people believed to be Iranian were taken to the hospital, and two others are believed to be missing at sea.  Arsalan Yarahmadi, editor-in-chief of the website of the Hengaw Human Rights Organization, told BBC Persian that our sources have confirmed that "the drowned were five members of a cold-blooded family".  The Hengaw human rights organization said: "The bodies of four members of the family have been discovered by search teams.  “There is no news of the 15-month-old baby. ”  The search for the missing passengers is expected to resume today, after a nighttime stop.  The BBC's Simon Jones said: "If someone is still on the channel, it's probably not a 'rescue operation' anymore and it's a search operation."  The prosecutor of the French city of Dunkirk has opened an investigation into the cause of the sinking of the ship.  Image source, Reuters explaining the image, the survivors were taken to hospital by the group "Calais Care", calling on the British government to find a legal way for refugees to arrive in the country.  “The loss of life should be a wake-up call for those in power in France and Britain. ”  The organisation said the creation of a new system that would allow asylum seekers to enter the UK from outside its borders would "put an end to the dreaded and dangerous sea crossing and prevent such catastrophes".  British Prime Minister Boris Johnson expressed his condolences to the families of the victims, saying: “We have told France that we will not spare any support to investigate this terrible incident and at the same time we will do all we can to crack down on ruthless criminal groups who are sending vulnerable people on such dangerous journeys. ”  At the same time, Save the Children called for a “joint action plan ” between France and Britain to ensure the safety of families affected.  The English Channel should not be turned into a children ’ s cemetery.  The boat, about two kilometres off the coast of France, was accidentally spotted by a passing sailboat at 9: 30 am local time and the matter was immediately reported to French authorities.  Four French vessels, a Belgian helicopter and a French fishing boat were involved in the search, but when rescue teams arrived, the boat had sunk.

Title: France to implement action plan to prevent migrants crossing the English Channel
Content: Paris, January 5, 2019 (AFP) The French government announced today that it will use a "plan of action" to counter migrants attempting to cross the English Channel to the UK, pledging to end the phenomenon, which the British Conservative government fears.  The increase in asylum seekers across the sea, mostly Iranians, has put pressure on the British government to respond, with Home Secretary Sajid Javid declaring it a “major event ”.  French Interior Minister Christophe Castaner said in a statement today: "This project should allow us to put an end to the sea crossing," adding that these actions are not only illegal but also extremely dangerous.  "It is in our interest and that of the United Kingdom to do everything possible to prevent the development of new networks that would again attract irregular migrants to our shores," the statement added.  The plan will increase police patrols near ports where some migrants try to steal boats and monitor beaches where rubber boats have been deployed.  In addition to four British coastal patrol vessels, a British naval vessel was also patrolling the English Channel today.  A spokesman for French maritime operations in the region told AFP this week that France had doubled the number of coast guard vessels in the Channel depending on the weather.
