Title: The launch of the spacecraft Crew Dragon (Crew-2) with astronauts to the ISS due to the weather was postponed to April 23
Content: NASA and SpaceX announced the postponement of the launch of the mission to change the crew of the ISS Crew-2, also known as USCV-2 (US Crew Vehicle 2): it was shifted by only one day — on April 23.  The reason for the transfer is adverse weather conditions.  Launch Update @ NASA and @ SpaceX now are targeting Friday, April 23 at 5: 49 a.m.  ET for the launch of the Crew-2 mission to the @ Space _ Station due to unfavorable weather conditions along the flight path on Thursday.  Learn more: https: / / t.co / GSBum6JjfN pic.twitter.com / ylfQx0u2qT — NASA Commercial Crew (@ Commercial _ Crew) April 21, 2021 Estimated launch time of Crew-2 — 12: 49 Kyiv time.  First of all, the Crew-2 mission is distinguished by the fact that SpaceX uses the restored first stage of the Falcon 9 and the Crew Dragon spacecraft - the stage with the inventory number B1061.2, which launched the Crew-1 mission, and the C206 Endeavour spacecraft, which flew to the ISS as part of the first demo mission Demo-2.  And this will be the first manned flight on a rocket and a ship that has already flown into space.  In June 2020, NASA allowed SpaceX to reuse the Crew Dragon capsule and the first stage of the Falcon 9 rocket to deliver astronauts to the ISS.  The Crew-2 rocket and spacecraft have already passed all checks, they are installed vertically on the LC-39A launch pad at the Kennedy Space Center in Florida.  Recall, the company of Elon Musk has long used already flying ships and the first stages of the Falcon 9 rocket to deliver cargo under the Commercial Resupply Services contract (in December 2017, the first launch took place as part of the CRS-13 mission, in which the launch vehicle and the ship were reused simultaneously - SpaceX maximum launched the same ship three times).  The current record for reusable Falcon 9 is nine restarts of the same first stage.  Crew-2 is SpaceX ’ s second full-time mission to send people to the ISS as part of its ongoing contact with NASA and its Commercial Crew Program, aimed at supporting commercial companies engaged in the development of space vehicles.  At least four more are planned.  The Crew-2 crew was announced back in July 2020 — two NASA astronauts (Robert Shane Kimbro and Catherine Megan MacArthur) and one each from ESA (Tom Pesquet) and JAXA (Akihiko Hoshide) will go to the ISS.  They will be part of the ISS-65 / 66 expedition.  The duration of this mission will be 180 days.  On April 5, 2020, NASA and SpaceX successfully redocked the Crew Dragon spacecraft of the Crew-1 mission for the first time from the IDA-1 docking node to IDA-3 to make room for the Crew-2 mission spacecraft.  After sending the Crew-1 crew to the IDA-3 node, Cargo Dragon 2 will dock.  When Crew-2 arrives on the ISS, the crew of the station until May 9 will consist of 11 people.  The current record is 13.  It has been holding since July 2009, when the space shuttle Endeavour (STS-127) arrived on the ISS.

Title: SpaceX successfully sent two astronauts into space as part of the Demo-2 mission » DailyTechInfo
Content: On May 30, 2020, at 19: 22 GMT, the famous American space company SpaceX successfully launched a manned mission Demo-2.  The Crew Dragon spacecraft, which now holds two astronauts, Robert Behnken and Douglas Hurley, was launched into space by a Falcon 9 rocket launched from Launch Complex 39A at NASA ’ s Kennedy Space Center in Florida.  The spacecraft is currently in space, performing maneuvers that will lead it to the International Space Station (ISS), docking with which will be made during today, May 31, 2020.Yesterday's launch was made after the first attempt, scheduled for Wednesday last week, was postponed due to the approach of the storm front, carrying strong wind, rain and an increased risk of lightning strike.  By the time of the delayed launch, the weather had improved significantly, but NASA weather forecasters still gave a 50 percent chance of re-carrying the launch.  The Crew Dragon spacecraft successfully entered orbit, which was a mark of two significant events at once.  The Demo-2 mission was the first manned mission launched from the United States since 2011, when NASA retired its fleet of space shuttles.  And the second event was that the Demo-2 mission is the world ’ s first commercial mission, in which a spacecraft with astronauts on board was put into orbit. If the Demo-2 mission is successfully carried out until the very end, then SpaceX will begin to carry out regular flights to the ISS, delivering astronauts and various cargoes back to Earth.  And in conclusion, it should be noted that in the case of a successful docking of the Crew Dragon spacecraft with the space station, astronauts Robert Benken and Douglas Hurley will spend on board it from one to three months, after which they will return to Earth.

Title: The launch of the ship Crew Dragon – NASA flight: date, all that is known
Content: Already this week, SpaceX ’ s Crew Dragon spacecraft will go to the ISS as part of the Demo-2 test mission.  The launch will mark the return of the United States to manned flights, which ended with the closure of the Space Shuttle program in 2011.  How the mission will take place and why it is important, we tell in our material.  Channel 24 closely followed the process of preparation for the manned launch of the manned spacecraft Crew Dragon.  We decided to collect all the details and interesting points in one article so that you could get acquainted with the key stages of the mission.  Do not miss the US returning to the ISS: SpaceX and NASA have revealed the details of the historic mission What is happening The United States of America is returning to manned flights to the ISS using its own ships.  Already this week, on May 27, the first ever manned launch of a spacecraft to the ISS, carried out by a private company SpaceX, will take place.  Crew Dragon will have two American astronauts on board.  After launch, the ship docks with the International Space Station at an altitude of 400 kilometers above the surface of the planet.  The astronauts will get to the station, where they will continue their mission, the duration of which is not yet known and will depend on a number of factors, both during the launch and during the flight of the ship until the moment of docking with the ISS.  Despite the fact that the flight is manned, and the mission of astronauts will take a lot of time on the ISS, it is still a test, so it is called Demo-2.  Previously, SpaceX has already tested the ship Crew Dragon, but this time the company will do it for the first time as part of a crewed mission.  The broadcast of the flight will take place on Techno 24.  So visit our website on May 27 at 23: 15.  The start is scheduled for 23: 30 in Kiev.  In addition, the broadcast will be available here: NASA TV: YouTube; SpaceX: YouTube link to the broadcast will be available before launch.  The fact is that the manned launch of Demo-2 will be the first such launch from American soil in almost a decade.  The last manned spacecraft to perform such a mission was the Space Shuttle Atlantis, which landed on July 21, 2011 as part of the STS-135 mission.  After that, the shuttles to the ISS no longer flew, and NASA was forced to buy seats for its astronauts on the Russian Soyuz, which cost the United States a considerable amount.  It is worth paying attention to the fact that after the American shuttles stopped flying, Russia constantly raised the price of seats for American astronauts and other partners on board the Soyuz spacecraft.  As of today, one seat on the Soyuz costs NASA $90 million (in 2010 it cost about $30 million).  The Alpha Centauri portal notes that given the approximate prices of Russian state launch contracts, it turns out that NASA pays the entire ship and the full cost of launching as part of the mission, paying only for one of its astronauts.  According to the report of NASA OIG on the audit of the manned flight program / The Alpha Centauri Here are more interesting facts about the ISS: how to create a research bastion of humanity in space Commercial Crew Program A year before the last flight of the shuttle, NASA initiated the launch of the manned flight program.  Even then, the search for a replacement for space shuttles began, the launches of which were quite expensive for the state.  Then came the idea, which at that time was revolutionary and even strange: the delivery of astronauts to the ISS should be engaged in private space companies.  NASA in this scenario took over the control of the design and preparation for the launch and the payment of seats for astronauts.  Space Shuttle Atlantis 30 minutes after landing in the last flight of the program Finally, in 2014, two companies were selected that will continue to prepare and present manned ships that will be able to carry out the mission.  These companies are Boeing and SpaceX.  As for the first company, the launch of the Boeing Starliner was unsuccessful, despite the fact that the ship landed successfully.  The company was unable to ensure the docking of the ship with the ISS due to a number of errors.  Now Boeing is engaged in fixing all the problems and preparing for a new test launch, but for their money.  Boeing Starliner, after landing SpaceX in March 2020, successfully launched Crew Dragon, which has passed a number of tests and landed proving its ability to ensure the delivery of astronauts to the ISS.  After additional tests and final preparations, the ship was prepared for an important event - a manned launch, which will take place on May 27, 2020.  Crew Crew Dragon To the ISS will go two NASA astronauts: Robert "Bob" Benken and Douglas "Doug" Gurley.  Both of them were test pilots and together in 2000 got to NASA as part of the 18th selection of astronauts.  Robert "Bob" Benken and Douglas "Dag" Gurley / NASA As for Robert Benken, during his time at NASA, he took part in two missions of the shuttle Endeavour: STS-123 (2008) and STS-130 (2010).  As part of these missions, Benken had three spacewalks.  Astronaut Robert Benken During the Demo-2 flight, Robert Benken will take command of the flight stages that will be coordinated by the mission control center.  Douglas Gurley also participated in two missions of the shuttle Endevour on missions STS-127 (2009) and STS-135 (2011).  In both missions, Gurley was a shuttle pilot, and STS-135 was the last mission to complete the space shuttle program.  During the Demo-2 flight, Douglas Hurley will be the commander of the ship and responsible for all procedures related to the launch and landing of the Crew Dragon spacecraft.  As already noted, the launch of the Crew Dragon is scheduled for May 27.  It is worth noting that the mission can still be postponed.  The reasons for this may be, as detected at the last moment technical problems or the weather, which should be favorable not only at the launch site, but also throughout the flight path of the Falcon 9 rocket.  Because in these places must pass the splashdown of the crew, if something went wrong at the time of launch or flight.  The ship Crew Dragon / SpaceX Now it is known that if the launch does not take place on May 27, then it can be postponed both on May 30 and on May 31.  If everything goes according to plan and the ship successfully enters orbit, it will spend about 19 hours there.  This is necessary for additional tests and maneuvers as part of the test – Crew Dragon can get to the ISS much faster.  In orbit, the astronauts will check the operation of all systems, switch to manual control, perform several maneuvers and eventually experience how comfortable Crew Dragon is for sleeping.  Docking with the IDA-2 node of the Harmony module on the ISS is scheduled for May 28 at about 15: 39 UTC (18: 39 Kyiv time).  Before that, the astronauts will approach the ISS and conduct several maneuvers near the station.  It is worth noting that the entire docking process with the ISS will take place automatically.  Astronauts will observe the process and will be able to intercept control in case of an emergency.  After the crew of Crew Dragon will get to the station, he will meet with members of the 63rd expedition - Chris Cassidy, Anatoly Ivanishin and Ivan Wagner.  As noted at the beginning of the material, the duration of stay of astronauts on the ISS is still unknown.  It will finally be determined during the flight, taking into account the state of the Crew Dragon ship and the readiness of the next Crew Dragon capsule, which is already designed for flight as part of the first full-fledged mission.  Let me remind you that despite the manned flight, this is still a test flight.  In addition, NASA expects to keep Demo-2 in orbit for as long as possible.  It is necessary for that.  after returning to finish the certification of the ship and begin preparations for the next mission.  In general, Demo-2 has every chance to stay in orbit for up to 120 days.  Rehearsal of the launch of Demo-2 / SpaceX Here it is worth noting that this limitation is due to the peculiarity of the design of the Crew Dragon.  In particular, it is said about solar panels, which gradually deteriorate during their stay in orbit due to the concentration of atomic oxygen.  The next Crew Dragon ships already have a protective coating of silicon dioxide, which will allow them to stay in orbit for all 210 days.  Whatever it was, and after the expiration of their stay on the ISS, the astronauts will return to the ship, undock and land in the waters of the Atlantic Ocean near the coast of Florida. Title: Tomorrow SpaceX will test the emergency rescue system of the Crew Dragon spacecraft in flight. This is the last major test before the first operational flight with astronauts on board
Content: Tomorrow, January 18, SpaceX intends to make the final major test of Crew Dragon ahead of the long-awaited Demo-2 mission with the first operational flight of a crewed spacecraft to the ISS.  We are talking about those additional tests of the emergency rescue system (SAS) with the shooting of the capsule during the flight.  Of course, the launch will be broadcast online, and those who want to watch the broadcast will find it below in this note.  The carrier rocket itself with the ship is already installed at the site of the SLC-40 complex at Cape Canaveral and is waiting for the countdown; a suitable launch window for the launch of the rocket opens on January 18 at 15: 00 Kyiv time.  SpaceX will have four hours to conduct the launch; assess the weather conditions as favorable and state that the probability of a successful launch is 90%.  Falcon 9 and Crew Dragon went vertical and the crew access arm was extended last night ahead of tomorrow's in-flight demonstration of the spacecraft's launch escape system.  The four-hour launch window opens at 8: 00 a.m.  EST, 13: 00 UTC → https: / / t.co / gtC39uBC7z pic.twitter.com / dS6R3hCgZi — SpaceX (@ SpaceX) January 17, 2020 These tests are not a mandatory part of NASA ’ s Crew Dragon certification program, but SpaceX on its own initiative intends to conduct them to demonstrate the reliability of the SAS and even donate one Falcon 9 rockets - for the purity of the experiment with simulated accident, it is likely to be destroyed during the flight, and the capsule soon after firing parachutes and splashdown in the ocean.  The animation for tomorrow ’ s launch can be seen below.  @ SpaceX's uncrewed in-flight abort test is targeted for 8am ET on Jan. 18.  This test will show that the # CrewDragon can protect astronauts even in the unlikely event of an emergency during launch.  Currently, weather is 90% GO for the demonstration.  https: / / t.co / PgHZol6PQA pic.twitter.com / kWCq7IHiq1 — NASA Commercial Crew (@ Commercial _ Crew) January 15, 2020 Recall that the Crew Dragon ship is equipped with two types of propulsion systems (low and high pressure).  The first with sixteen Draco engines is designed for orbital maneuvers and orientation of the ship in space, and the second with eight SuperDraco engines is responsible for shooting and controlled landing of the rescue capsule in case of an emergency. passages.title: Iran rejects claims to pay $1.1 billion in compensation for Canadians killed in UIA plane
passages.passage: 12.02.2020, 16: 42, News of the day Iran does not intend to pay to representatives of Canada $1.1 billion in compensation for those killed in the plane of Ukraine International Airlines.  Iranian Foreign Minister Javad Zarif told reporters on February 11, ISNA reports.  According to the diplomat, there are “no grounds ” for such a demand.  Zarif claims that the Iranian authorities acted in accordance with international law.  On February 7, it became known that a Canadian lawyer filed a lawsuit against the Iranian authorities in the High Court of Ontario in Toronto on behalf of his client John Doe.  Behind this name is a relative of one of the dead passengers.  The statement of claim says that the crash of the UIA plane was a “deliberate terrorist act. ”  A passenger plane Boeing 737-800 of Ukraine International Airlines, following flight PS752 Tehran – Kiev, crashed on January 8 near the capital of Iran.  There were 167 passengers and nine crew members on board.  No one survived.  Among the dead were 57 Canadians.  Initially, the Iranian authorities insisted on a technical malfunction or accident as the main reason for the crash, but on January 11, the General Staff of the Iranian Armed Forces admitted that the UIA plane was shot down by the Iranian military.  The ministry claimed that the disaster occurred shortly after Iran shelled US military bases in Iraq.  The aircraft, as stated in the message, approached one of the important objects of the Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and “the shape and height of the flight resembled an enemy object. ”  On January 20, in an official report, Iran admitted that two Tor-M1 surface-to-air missiles were fired at the aircraft three minutes after its departure from Imam Khomeini airport.

passages.title: Kiev welcomes Iran ’ s readiness to pay compensation for downing Ukrainian plane
passages.passage: Kiev welcomed Tehran ’ s readiness to pay compensation for the downing of the Ukrainian plane and reiterated that the amount of compensation would be examined after the details of the incident were determined.  Shargh newspaper reported in Tuesday ’ s issue that the Iranian government is planning to allocate 200 million euros in next year ’ s budget to pay compensation for flight 752.  The amount that is to be paid from the National Development Fund is not yet final and must be approved by the Islamic Consultative Assembly and approved by the Guardian Council.  According to Radio Farda sources, Ukraine International Airlines expects to receive $200 million from Iran alone.  The head of the Ukrainian delegation of negotiators on the issues of Flight 752 welcomed the Iranian government ’ s intention to allocate funds to compensate for the crash of Flight 752.  Ukraine ’ s Deputy Foreign Minister Yevgeny Yinin told Radio Farda on Tuesday that it was “too early to talk about the compensation. ”  “I recall that during the last round of negotiations, the Iranian side reiterated its readiness to pay equal compensation to the relatives of all the victims of this flight regardless of their nationality, but so far we have not started to investigate the compensation amount.  We believe that, first of all, we need to know the causes of the accident, to be sure of the quality of the technical and criminal investigation of the accident, to see who will be identified as responsible and, depending on the level and type of cooperation of the Iranian side, we will review the amount of compensation during the next rounds of negotiations. ”  While diplomats have not begun to review the compensation for flight 752, Ukraine International Airlines asked Iran for $200 million in non-material compensation during talks held in Tehran a month ago.  Radio Farda ’ s sources say, “This amount includes expenses that are not covered by insurance. ”  The company has not responded to repeated requests by Radio Farda to explain the issue.  Last week, Ukraine International Airlines CEO Yevgeny Dichne told the Ukrainian media in Babol: “The renter has received the cost of losing a Boeing 737 from the insurance company, and we expect the airline to be compensated for the loss. ”  One month ago, at the conclusion of the second round of negotiations on Flight 752, Mohsen Baharvand, Iran ’ s deputy foreign minister and the head of Iranian negotiators, told IRNA news agency: “The international procedure does not support the demands of the Ukrainian side, but we have not closed the negotiations. ”  It is not clear whether the €200 million budget, which the Iranian government plans to pay for the 752 flight, according to a report in the newspaper Shargh, covers the costs that MAV has demanded from Iran.  A source from Radio Farda, who declined to be identified, suggested that Iran and Maw could reach an agreement on $100 million or less.  Ukrainian Airlines recently estimated that it will lose $60 million by the end of the year for a variety of reasons.  International aviation lawyer Andrei Kozlov says the airline ’ s negotiations with Iran are not to the detriment of the relatives of the victims.  He continued, “Requesting compensation for the incidental costs, including the unearned profits resulting from a plane crash, is customary in international law.  "By paying this price, Iran will prove that it has accepted its responsibility for the downing of the Ukrainian plane."  According to the lawyers, airlines and relatives of the victims are on the same front to receive the most compensation from Iran.  Kozlov added: “The report does not specify how much is being allocated to the airlines and how much is being allocated to the families of the victims, nor does it cover the cost of the aircraft owned by the insurance company. ”  He also emphasized, “In ideal circumstances, compensation for the families of the victims and airlines should be paid at the same time so that no party feels dissatisfied, but it is unlikely that the complaints of the families of the victims against the airlines will be successful, and if an intergovernmental agreement on compensation is reached, it is customary for the parties to promise not to pursue this case in court. ”  The Ukrainian plane, with the flight number PS752, was shot down by the IRGC air defense last year and all 176 people on board died.  Hamed Ismailion, a spokesman for the Association of the Families of the Victims of the Flight, in response to the Shargh newspaper ’ s report about the payment of compensation for the Ukrainian aircraft from the National Development Fund, wrote on his Facebook page: “They take the cost of shooting children out of people ’ s pockets. ”  A group of families affected by the crash have filed a lawsuit in Ottawa in Canada against the Islamic Republic of Iran, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and Ukraine International Airlines.  Iran has repeatedly criticized Canada ’ s approach in recent days, accusing it of “politicizing ” the Ukrainian plane crash to prevent Iran from trying to explain the reality.  The governments of Canada and Ukraine, however, say Iran has not fulfilled its promises of full accountability and is not cooperating to clarify the "truth."

passages.title: Canadian court: Iran ’ s downing of Ukraine Flight 752 was an act of terror – Radio France Internationale
passages.passage: OTTAWA (AFP) - A Canadian court today ruled that the shooting down of Ukrainian International Airlines flight PS752 by Iranian forces early last year was a deliberate "terrorist act" and that the decision will pave the way for possible compensation for the families of the victims.  On January 8, Ukraine International Airlines Flight PS752 crashed near Tehran, killing all 176 people on board, including 85 Canadian citizens and permanent residents.  Iran initially denied the Western accusations, but three days later admitted that the Iranian military shot down the other side "unintentionally".  The Ontario Superior Court of Justice in Canada said it had determined, after "weighing the odds," that the plane was hit by two missiles shortly after take-off in Tehran, as a result of a "deliberate" act.  Judge Edward Belobaba also ruled that “the plaintiff ’ s claim that the shooting down of Flight 752 was an act of terrorism. ”  The plaintiffs ’ lawyers called the ruling “unprecedented in Canadian law. ”  "This will have a significant impact on the immediate families of the victims seeking justice," they said in a statement.  The lawsuit, filed by the families of the four victims, seeks 1.5 billion Canadian dollars (about NT $35.3 billion).  They claim that Iran launched the missile attack in retaliation for the US killing of Qasem Soleimani, the commander of the Quds Force of the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps, near Baghdad airport in Iraq, days before the crash. passages.title: Ontario court: Iran shooting down Ukrainian plane was' intentional and terrorism'
passages.passage: Ontario Court: The shooting of Ukrainian aircraft by Iran was' intentional and terrorist 'May 30, 1400 - May 20, 2021, 20: 18 GMT Updated 4 minutes ago Picture description, memorial to the victims - 176 Sereneges were killed Flight 752 The Ontario Supreme Court in Canada has concluded that the shooting of Ukrainian flight PS752 by Iran was a deliberate act and based on criminal law of terrorist act.  Ukraine International Airlines Flight 752 was hit by two Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps missiles in January 2020, killing 176 people.  Judge Edward Blubaba wrote in a decision issued Thursday: "By weighing the possibilities, I found that the missile attacks on Flight 752 were deliberate and directly responsible for the deaths of all those on board."  "I also realized, weighing the possibilities, that there was no armed conflict in the region at the time."  The judge said the plaintiffs had proven that the downing of the plane was based on state immunity laws, justice for victims of terrorist acts and criminal law as "terrorist activity."  Former Canadian Foreign Minister Francois Philippe Champagne said in December that he did not believe the flight was caused by human error.  The plaintiffs' lawyer said in a statement that another hearing would be held in the court to determine compensation.  Mark Arnold has previously said that the best way to get compensation for the families of the victims is to accuse the Iranian government of “committing a terrorist act. ”  He is the legal representative of the plaintiffs who lost their relatives on that flight.  Despite being informed of the charge, the Iranian government has refused to defend itself in this court.  Mark and Jonah Arnold, lawyers for the case, wrote: “The decision of the Supreme Court of Justice in Canada is unprecedented.  "This is a significant ruling in terms of the immediate impact on the families of victims seeking justice."  Habib Haghjoo, whose daughter Shahnaz Haghjoo and eight-year-old grandson Elsa lost a new one on flight 752, said it was a success for the families making the complaint.  He said: “I ’ m very happy and I think it ’ s a big step.  Canadian Foreign Minister Mark Garneau told parliament last week that Canada would soon negotiate compensation for the families of the victims.  The association representing the families of the victims has repeatedly said it wants answers and justice for the overthrow before any talks about reparations.  More than a year after the shooting down of the plane, there are still serious uncertainties about the causes of the shooting down and those involved in the “unconscionable, ” Mr. Garno told a parliamentary committee on Thursday:“ I must honestly say that the behavior of the Iranian government over the past 15 months has been unconscionable and we will not let them go to ensure accountability. ”  After months of pressure, Tehran has just agreed to hand over flight data recorders for independent analysis, he said, adding that Iran has not yet explained why it did not close its skies on the night of the incident.  Flight 752 was hit by two IRGC missiles on January 8, 2020.  Ukraine and four other countries where citizens or residents were killed - including Canada, Britain, Afghanistan and Sweden - have called on Iran to provide a full and comprehensive explanation of the downing of the plane.  The Iranian armed forces denied any responsibility within three days of the overthrow.  Authorities also allowed the occupants ’ assets scattered at the crash site to be looted and then bulldozed.  But accumulating evidence from the IRGC Aerospace Force, he said that an anti-aircraft unit mistook the Boeing 737-800 for a missile.  On that day, Iran ’ s air defenses were on high alert because of the IRGC ’ s action in firing missiles at two Iraqi bases where U.S. forces were stationed.  Iran was targeting these bases in retaliation for the killing of Qods Force commander Qassem Soleimani.  The Civil Aviation Organization recently reported in March 2021 that an anti-aircraft defense operator of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) had “mistakenly ” identified the aircraft as hostile and fired the missiles without the permission of the commanders.  According to Iran ’ s Civil Aviation Organization, the downing of the plane was due to a “chain of human errors ” that occurred on the day of the disaster.  Ukraine and Canada rejected the report.  In a video post on Facebook, Ukraine ’ s Foreign Minister Dmitry Kolba called the Iran investigation “unilateral, ” calling the evidence“ selective, ” and the result “deceptive. ”  Canada ’ s foreign and transport ministers, Mark Garneau and Omar Alghbra, said in a statement that the Iran report “makes no attempt to answer fundamental questions about what really happened, appears incomplete, and contains no facts or tangible evidence. ”

passages.title: The crash of the MAU plane. Ukraine, Canada, Sweden and the UK put forward demands on Iran
passages.passage: The crash of the MAU plane.  Ukraine, Canada, Sweden and the United Kingdom put forward demands to Iran “The actions and inaction of the Islamic Republic of Iran are a violation of international law.  Our statement notes that our states, their citizens and residents on board flight PS752 suffered substantial and irreparable damage as a result of the tragedy, and Iran must fulfill its obligations to ensure full reparation to the group of states.  The signatories demand that Iran acknowledge the wrongdoing and provide a full account of the circumstances that led to the downing of the plane.  Also, the foreign ministers of Ukraine, Canada, Sweden and the United Kingdom demand a public apology, the return of the missing and stolen personal belongings of the victims, assurances of the prevention of such actions in the future, ensuring the transparency of the criminal investigation, as well as fair compensation to the families of those killed in the accident, regardless of nationality.  “We call on Iran to cooperate in order to determine the date of the official start of negotiations on reparations, which we will conduct in good faith, ” the authors of the appeal added.  Context: A Boeing 737-800 passenger plane of Ukraine International Airlines flight PS752, which was en route from Tehran to Kiev, crashed on January 8, 2020 near the capital of Iran.  There were 167 passengers and nine crew members on board.  No one survived.  Among the dead were 11 citizens of Ukraine.  Most of the passengers were citizens of Iran and Canada.  Iranian authorities, initially claiming that the plane crashed due to a technical malfunction, on January 11, under pressure from Western leaders, admitted that flight PS752 was shot down by an Iranian missile by mistake.  Deputy Foreign Minister of Ukraine Yevgeny Yenin July 23 said that the decryption of the black boxes, which was completed in France, confirmed the illegal interference in the work of the passenger liner.  On August 23, the Civil Aviation Organization of Iran released a series of data obtained from the onboard voice recorder and flight data recorder of the UIA aircraft.  According to the records, the crew knew about the emergency situation and tried to control the plane to the last.  The New York Times reported that Iranian Foreign Minister Javad Zarif gave an interview to Iranian economist Said Leilaz in March 2020.  In it, he admitted that the Iranian military immediately learned that the plane “International airlines of Ukraine ” was shot down.  Iran on February 20, 2021 announced the completion of the investigation of the disaster.  The Iranian prosecutor ’ s office accuses 10 people of involvement in the crash, among them the top military commanders of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.  The Minister of foreign Affairs of Ukraine Dmitry Kuleba called the report of Iran biased and promised to continue to seek punishment of Iran for this crime.  Yenin said that Ukraine will demand from Iran to continue the investigation.  The court of the Canadian province of Ontario on May 20 recognized the crash of the UIA airline as a deliberate terrorist act.  Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Saeed Khatibzadeh said the court had no jurisdiction to decide on a claim for damages in the plane crash because it occurred outside of Canada.  The National Security and Defense Council of Ukraine is inclined to believe that the crash of the UIA plane in Iran was a terrorist attack.  Tehran insists on the version of the unintentional shooting down of the plane.

passages.title: Ukraine Threatens Iran with International Court of Justice
passages.passage: Ukraine may file a lawsuit with the International Court of Justice if negotiations with Iran over the downed Boeing 737-800 of Ukraine International Airlines (UIA) near Tehran are unsuccessful.  This was stated by Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine Yevgeny Yenin in an interview with Radio Liberty.  “If negotiations reach a deadlock, we will be forced to resort to international arbitration, in particular the International Court of Justice.  We are talking not only about Ukraine, but about a united front of the states of Canada, Great Britain, Sweden, Afghanistan and Ukraine, ” Yenin threatened.  He expressed hope that Iran will fulfill its international obligations and hand over the black boxes for their decoding.  Yenin stressed that there are not so many states in the world today that have the necessary software.  The diplomat said that the issue of conducting an examination in France has already been worked out.  In mid-February, Iranian Foreign Minister Mohammad Javad Zarif said that the country does not have the technical capabilities to decipher the black boxes.  Minval.az

Title: Iran rejects claims to pay $1.1 billion in compensation for Canadians killed in UIA plane
Content: 12.02.2020, 16: 42, News of the day Iran does not intend to pay to representatives of Canada $1.1 billion in compensation for those killed in the plane of Ukraine International Airlines.  Iranian Foreign Minister Javad Zarif told reporters on February 11, ISNA reports.  According to the diplomat, there are “no grounds ” for such a demand.  Zarif claims that the Iranian authorities acted in accordance with international law.  On February 7, it became known that a Canadian lawyer filed a lawsuit against the Iranian authorities in the High Court of Ontario in Toronto on behalf of his client John Doe.  Behind this name is a relative of one of the dead passengers.  The statement of claim says that the crash of the UIA plane was a “deliberate terrorist act. ”  A passenger plane Boeing 737-800 of Ukraine International Airlines, following flight PS752 Tehran – Kiev, crashed on January 8 near the capital of Iran.  There were 167 passengers and nine crew members on board.  No one survived.  Among the dead were 57 Canadians.  Initially, the Iranian authorities insisted on a technical malfunction or accident as the main reason for the crash, but on January 11, the General Staff of the Iranian Armed Forces admitted that the UIA plane was shot down by the Iranian military.  The ministry claimed that the disaster occurred shortly after Iran shelled US military bases in Iraq.  The aircraft, as stated in the message, approached one of the important objects of the Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and “the shape and height of the flight resembled an enemy object. ”  On January 20, in an official report, Iran admitted that two Tor-M1 surface-to-air missiles were fired at the aircraft three minutes after its departure from Imam Khomeini airport.

Title: Kiev welcomes Iran ’ s readiness to pay compensation for downing Ukrainian plane
Content: Kiev welcomed Tehran ’ s readiness to pay compensation for the downing of the Ukrainian plane and reiterated that the amount of compensation would be examined after the details of the incident were determined.  Shargh newspaper reported in Tuesday ’ s issue that the Iranian government is planning to allocate 200 million euros in next year ’ s budget to pay compensation for flight 752.  The amount that is to be paid from the National Development Fund is not yet final and must be approved by the Islamic Consultative Assembly and approved by the Guardian Council.  According to Radio Farda sources, Ukraine International Airlines expects to receive $200 million from Iran alone.  The head of the Ukrainian delegation of negotiators on the issues of Flight 752 welcomed the Iranian government ’ s intention to allocate funds to compensate for the crash of Flight 752.  Ukraine ’ s Deputy Foreign Minister Yevgeny Yinin told Radio Farda on Tuesday that it was “too early to talk about the compensation. ”  “I recall that during the last round of negotiations, the Iranian side reiterated its readiness to pay equal compensation to the relatives of all the victims of this flight regardless of their nationality, but so far we have not started to investigate the compensation amount.  We believe that, first of all, we need to know the causes of the accident, to be sure of the quality of the technical and criminal investigation of the accident, to see who will be identified as responsible and, depending on the level and type of cooperation of the Iranian side, we will review the amount of compensation during the next rounds of negotiations. ”  While diplomats have not begun to review the compensation for flight 752, Ukraine International Airlines asked Iran for $200 million in non-material compensation during talks held in Tehran a month ago.  Radio Farda ’ s sources say, “This amount includes expenses that are not covered by insurance. ”  The company has not responded to repeated requests by Radio Farda to explain the issue.  Last week, Ukraine International Airlines CEO Yevgeny Dichne told the Ukrainian media in Babol: “The renter has received the cost of losing a Boeing 737 from the insurance company, and we expect the airline to be compensated for the loss. ”  One month ago, at the conclusion of the second round of negotiations on Flight 752, Mohsen Baharvand, Iran ’ s deputy foreign minister and the head of Iranian negotiators, told IRNA news agency: “The international procedure does not support the demands of the Ukrainian side, but we have not closed the negotiations. ”  It is not clear whether the €200 million budget, which the Iranian government plans to pay for the 752 flight, according to a report in the newspaper Shargh, covers the costs that MAV has demanded from Iran.  A source from Radio Farda, who declined to be identified, suggested that Iran and Maw could reach an agreement on $100 million or less.  Ukrainian Airlines recently estimated that it will lose $60 million by the end of the year for a variety of reasons.  International aviation lawyer Andrei Kozlov says the airline ’ s negotiations with Iran are not to the detriment of the relatives of the victims.  He continued, “Requesting compensation for the incidental costs, including the unearned profits resulting from a plane crash, is customary in international law.  "By paying this price, Iran will prove that it has accepted its responsibility for the downing of the Ukrainian plane."  According to the lawyers, airlines and relatives of the victims are on the same front to receive the most compensation from Iran.  Kozlov added: “The report does not specify how much is being allocated to the airlines and how much is being allocated to the families of the victims, nor does it cover the cost of the aircraft owned by the insurance company. ”  He also emphasized, “In ideal circumstances, compensation for the families of the victims and airlines should be paid at the same time so that no party feels dissatisfied, but it is unlikely that the complaints of the families of the victims against the airlines will be successful, and if an intergovernmental agreement on compensation is reached, it is customary for the parties to promise not to pursue this case in court. ”  The Ukrainian plane, with the flight number PS752, was shot down by the IRGC air defense last year and all 176 people on board died.  Hamed Ismailion, a spokesman for the Association of the Families of the Victims of the Flight, in response to the Shargh newspaper ’ s report about the payment of compensation for the Ukrainian aircraft from the National Development Fund, wrote on his Facebook page: “They take the cost of shooting children out of people ’ s pockets. ”  A group of families affected by the crash have filed a lawsuit in Ottawa in Canada against the Islamic Republic of Iran, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and Ukraine International Airlines.  Iran has repeatedly criticized Canada ’ s approach in recent days, accusing it of “politicizing ” the Ukrainian plane crash to prevent Iran from trying to explain the reality.  The governments of Canada and Ukraine, however, say Iran has not fulfilled its promises of full accountability and is not cooperating to clarify the "truth."

Title: Canadian court: Iran ’ s downing of Ukraine Flight 752 was an act of terror – Radio France Internationale
Content: OTTAWA (AFP) - A Canadian court today ruled that the shooting down of Ukrainian International Airlines flight PS752 by Iranian forces early last year was a deliberate "terrorist act" and that the decision will pave the way for possible compensation for the families of the victims.  On January 8, Ukraine International Airlines Flight PS752 crashed near Tehran, killing all 176 people on board, including 85 Canadian citizens and permanent residents.  Iran initially denied the Western accusations, but three days later admitted that the Iranian military shot down the other side "unintentionally".  The Ontario Superior Court of Justice in Canada said it had determined, after "weighing the odds," that the plane was hit by two missiles shortly after take-off in Tehran, as a result of a "deliberate" act.  Judge Edward Belobaba also ruled that “the plaintiff ’ s claim that the shooting down of Flight 752 was an act of terrorism. ”  The plaintiffs ’ lawyers called the ruling “unprecedented in Canadian law. ”  "This will have a significant impact on the immediate families of the victims seeking justice," they said in a statement.  The lawsuit, filed by the families of the four victims, seeks 1.5 billion Canadian dollars (about NT $35.3 billion).  They claim that Iran launched the missile attack in retaliation for the US killing of Qasem Soleimani, the commander of the Quds Force of the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps, near Baghdad airport in Iraq, days before the crash.  A final report released in March by the Iran Civil Aviation Organisation said the missile attack and the "vigilant" response of ground forces were the result of high tensions between Iran and the United States at the time.  Eleven Ukrainian citizens were killed in the crash.  The Ukrainian side pointed out that behind the report there was a "ridiculous attempt to cover up the real cause", while Canada said the report contained "no strong facts or evidence" and promised to publish its findings soon.  Iran did not defend itself in court, but three days after the crash admitted that Iranian forces shot down the Boeing 737-800 bound for Kiev.  The court will then decide on the amount of compensation. © 2021 AFP

Title: The crash of the MAU plane. Ukraine, Canada, Sweden and the UK put forward demands on Iran
Content: The crash of the MAU plane.  Ukraine, Canada, Sweden and the United Kingdom put forward demands to Iran “The actions and inaction of the Islamic Republic of Iran are a violation of international law.  Our statement notes that our states, their citizens and residents on board flight PS752 suffered substantial and irreparable damage as a result of the tragedy, and Iran must fulfill its obligations to ensure full reparation to the group of states.  The signatories demand that Iran acknowledge the wrongdoing and provide a full account of the circumstances that led to the downing of the plane.  Also, the foreign ministers of Ukraine, Canada, Sweden and the United Kingdom demand a public apology, the return of the missing and stolen personal belongings of the victims, assurances of the prevention of such actions in the future, ensuring the transparency of the criminal investigation, as well as fair compensation to the families of those killed in the accident, regardless of nationality.  “We call on Iran to cooperate in order to determine the date of the official start of negotiations on reparations, which we will conduct in good faith, ” the authors of the appeal added.  Context: A Boeing 737-800 passenger plane of Ukraine International Airlines flight PS752, which was en route from Tehran to Kiev, crashed on January 8, 2020 near the capital of Iran.  There were 167 passengers and nine crew members on board.  No one survived.  Among the dead were 11 citizens of Ukraine.  Most of the passengers were citizens of Iran and Canada.  Iranian authorities, initially claiming that the plane crashed due to a technical malfunction, on January 11, under pressure from Western leaders, admitted that flight PS752 was shot down by an Iranian missile by mistake.  Deputy Foreign Minister of Ukraine Yevgeny Yenin July 23 said that the decryption of the black boxes, which was completed in France, confirmed the illegal interference in the work of the passenger liner.  On August 23, the Civil Aviation Organization of Iran released a series of data obtained from the onboard voice recorder and flight data recorder of the UIA aircraft.  According to the records, the crew knew about the emergency situation and tried to control the plane to the last.  The New York Times reported that Iranian Foreign Minister Javad Zarif gave an interview to Iranian economist Said Leilaz in March 2020.  In it, he admitted that the Iranian military immediately learned that the plane “International airlines of Ukraine ” was shot down.  Iran on February 20, 2021 announced the completion of the investigation of the disaster.  The Iranian prosecutor ’ s office accuses 10 people of involvement in the crash, among them the top military commanders of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.  The Minister of foreign Affairs of Ukraine Dmitry Kuleba called the report of Iran biased and promised to continue to seek punishment of Iran for this crime.  Yenin said that Ukraine will demand from Iran to continue the investigation.  The court of the Canadian province of Ontario on May 20 recognized the crash of the UIA airline as a deliberate terrorist act.  Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Saeed Khatibzadeh said the court had no jurisdiction to decide on a claim for damages in the plane crash because it occurred outside of Canada.  The National Security and Defense Council of Ukraine is inclined to believe that the crash of the UIA plane in Iran was a terrorist attack.  Tehran insists on the version of the unintentional shooting down of the plane.

Title: Ukraine Threatens Iran with International Court of Justice
Content: Ukraine may file a lawsuit with the International Court of Justice if negotiations with Iran over the downed Boeing 737-800 of Ukraine International Airlines (UIA) near Tehran are unsuccessful.  This was stated by Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine Yevgeny Yenin in an interview with Radio Liberty.  “If negotiations reach a deadlock, we will be forced to resort to international arbitration, in particular the International Court of Justice.  We are talking not only about Ukraine, but about a united front of the states of Canada, Great Britain, Sweden, Afghanistan and Ukraine, ” Yenin threatened.  He expressed hope that Iran will fulfill its international obligations and hand over the black boxes for their decoding.  Yenin stressed that there are not so many states in the world today that have the necessary software.  The diplomat said that the issue of conducting an examination in France has already been worked out.  In mid-February, Iranian Foreign Minister Mohammad Javad Zarif said that the country does not have the technical capabilities to decipher the black boxes.  Minval.az

passages.title: Seafarers helped with water
passages.passage: The crew on the ship detained in the DPRK runs out of food and fuel On the tenth day from the moment of detention by the border guards of the DPRK seiner "Xianhailin-8" Russia managed to ensure that 17 sailors of the ship, 15 of whom are citizens of Russia, and two - South Korea, delivered water on board.  This was announced by the deputy director of the company - the owner of the vessel Sergey Sedler.  As he specified, “Xianghailin-8 ” runs out of products and fuel.  The Russian Foreign Ministry said that it is doing everything possible to “resolve the situation ”.  The representative of the diplomatic mission of the DPRK in Moscow noted that the ship was flying the South Korean flag and the captain has already recognized the fact of violation of territorial waters.  The Russian ship “Xianghailin-8 ” brought water, said the Deputy Director of the North-Eastern fishing company Sergey Sedler.  “We brought water to the ship today.  The delivery was organized by the Koreans at the request of our embassy, ” he said.  He said the ship was running out of food and fuel.  “Now all efforts have been directed to speed up the inspection so that the ship will return home as soon as possible, because everything ends with them, ” he added.  Following the results of yesterday ’ s visit to the ship by employees of the Russian Consulate in the DPRK, the Russian Foreign Ministry issued a statement, according to which it has already “put before the North Korean side the issue of ensuring proper conditions for the detained sailors. ”  A Kommersant source in the Russian Foreign Ministry confirmed that work on the release of the sailors is already underway, and assured that there is no doubt about the positive outcome of the case.  According to the Russian Foreign Ministry, the crew is “in satisfactory condition ”.  The representative of the Embassy of the DPRK yesterday said that the ship was flying the South Korean flag, and that the captain recognized the violation of territorial waters, reports TASS.  He said that now in respect of the seafarers check.  “Given the good relations between Russia and the DPRK, we expect that after the inspection, the sailors and the ship will be sent to the Russian Federation, ” the embassy added.  According to the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, territorial waters end 12 nautical miles from shore, while the ship was detained about 50 miles away.  The All-Russian Association of Fishery Producers sent an appeal to the Russian Foreign Ministry with its interpretation of the actions of the North Korean side.  According to the association, the incident is related to the tightening of control over the activities of Korean ships: in 2018, the Russian border service “stopped the illegal activities of 68 fishing vessels of the DPRK off the coast of Primorsky Krai. ”  The chairman of the Far Eastern regional organization of the Russian Seafarers ’ Union said that the organization is ready to do everything possible to release the ship ’ s crew, even to contact North Korean trade unions if the relatives of the detainees so request.  Recall, on Tuesday it became known about the detention of the North Korean authorities of a fishing vessel with 17 sailors — 15 Russians and two South Korean citizens.  On July 16, the seiner left the port of the South Korean city of Sokcho for crab fishing and, according to Rosrybolovstvo, went to the control point “Vostok-1 ”.  The next morning, the North Korean border service detained the ship 55 miles from its shores for violating the so-called protection zone, which is not recognized by either Russia or the world community.  Seiner was escorted to the North Korean port of Wonsan.  The crew is charged with violating the rules of entry and stay in the country.  The Ministry of Unification of the Republic of Korea tried to find out the details of the incident and the situation of the fishermen through the inter-Korean liaison office in Kaesong, but received no response.  On July 19, Seoul sent a similar request through the Red Cross, but this attempt did not end.  This was reported yesterday by the Korean edition of The Kyunghyang Shinmun.  Rosrybolovstvo also made a statement.  The ministry condemned the actions of North Korean border guards and called the detention illegal.  Referring to the information of the Russian Consulate in the DPRK, Rosrybolovstvo reported that “on the ship the means of technical control and satellite telephone communication were disabled, mobile phones from the crew members were seized ”, and the captain and his assistant are in the hotel separately from the rest and do not have contact with them.  The deputy director of the company also indicated that the Xianhailin-8 was heading to the Sea of Japan for crab fishing.  One of Kommersant ’ s sources in the Russian Foreign Ministry suggested a possible plot of the incident: the crew was transporting contraband goods.  Seiner could try to escape from the Russian border guards and thus be in the security zone of the DPRK.  According to Sergei Sedler, the ship at the time of detention was without cargo.  "Kommersant" could not quickly get a comment from the Far Eastern Customs Administration.  Alexandra Fokina, Mikhail Korostikov

passages.title: North Korea Seizes Russian Ship
passages.passage: North Korea seized a Russian fishing boat with 17 sailors on board.  This was reported to Kommersant by the deputy director of the North-Eastern fishing company that owns the ship, Sergei Sedler.  The incident occurred on the night of July 17.  According to him, on the ship "Xianghailin-8" were 15 Russians and 2 South Koreans - they were heading from the South Korean port of Sokcho to the Sea of Japan for crab mining.  North Korea seized the ship 55 miles from the country ’ s border.  At the time of the arrest, the ship was unloaded.  “At 4 a.m. on July 17, border guards landed on the ship and cut off all communications.  We did not even immediately understand what happened, at first we thought that they were drifting, but then we realized that they were captured, ” Sedler explained.  He added that the reason for the arrest was the illegal crossing of the border of the “military protection zone ”, which the DPRK arbitrarily established 50 nautical miles from the shore.  The sailors were escorted to the North Korean port of Wonsan, the Russian consul visited them only on Tuesday, July 23.  He said that the Russians are kept in closed cabins, where they are regularly searched and interrogated.  North Korea has not explained when the trial will begin.

passages.title: The crew of the ship “Patriot ” can not return from China to Russia due to the situation with the coronavirus
passages.passage: Repatriation of the crew of the vessel “Patriot ”, which is located in the Chinese port of Ningde, is delayed due to the forced extended holidays with the authorities in China, which are engaged in the registration of documents for sailors.  As told TASS Deputy Director of the ship-owner "Hudson" Oleg Anikin, now "Patriot" is in the port of Ningde, where he came for repair, sailors are provided with everything necessary.  “We managed to agree on work with the shipyard, but due to the outbreak of pneumonia from the coronavirus, representatives of the plant are not yet able to start repairing, they do not even say when it will be possible.  As for the return of the crew to their homeland, there are obstacles.  The fact is that all official authorities in China, which are engaged in the registration of documents necessary for repatriation, are now on forced holidays at least until the 10th, and maybe longer, ” Anikin said.  According to him, the company has a prospect in terms of providing contracts for the work of its ships, which will allow in February to start paying seafarers debts.  In this, Hudson is assisted by a special commission of the Russian government, which was created to solve the problems of entrepreneurs who fell under American sanctions.  Earlier, the chairman of the Far Eastern regional organization of the Russian Seamen ’ s Trade Union Nikolai Sukhanov said that the crew of the Patriot appealed to the trade union with a request to assist in returning to their homeland.  During the stoppage at the port, the sailors complained of irregular supplies and non-payment of wages.  According to the Far Eastern Transport Prosecutor ’ s Office, the amount of debt on the salary of 19 crew members is 1.6 million rubles for November, December 2019 and January 2020.  Recall that in 2018, the United States Department of the Treasury announced the expansion of sanctions lists on the DPRK, which included the Russian-based shipping company Hudson.  In particular, the list includes six ships under the Russian flag: “Patriot ”,“ Neptune ”, “Bogatyr ”,“ Bella ”, “Partizan ” and“ Sevastopol ”.  According to the US authorities, they are involved “in the transfer of oil products to ships flying the flag of the DPRK, as well as activities prohibited by the UN Security Council. ”  The report of the UN expert group on the situation with the DPRK, which was published on the organization ’ s website on March 12, 2019, said that the experts did not receive from the United States evidence of pumping oil products from the company ’ s ship “Patriot ” to two North Korean tankers in January 2018, but so far the company is not excluded from the sanctions list.  After multiple detentions of ships and refusals of the company ’ s partners from contracts (in Hudson, this is associated with sanctions), employees of the shipping company wrote an open letter to the leadership of Russia in May last year, in which they asked to provide the company with monetary assistance and give access to government contracts in order to prevent bankruptcy.

Title: Seafarers helped with water
Content: The crew on the ship detained in the DPRK runs out of food and fuel On the tenth day from the moment of detention by the border guards of the DPRK seiner "Xianhailin-8" Russia managed to ensure that 17 sailors of the ship, 15 of whom are citizens of Russia, and two - South Korea, delivered water on board.  This was announced by the deputy director of the company - the owner of the vessel Sergey Sedler.  As he specified, “Xianghailin-8 ” runs out of products and fuel.  The Russian Foreign Ministry said that it is doing everything possible to “resolve the situation ”.  The representative of the diplomatic mission of the DPRK in Moscow noted that the ship was flying the South Korean flag and the captain has already recognized the fact of violation of territorial waters.  The Russian ship “Xianghailin-8 ” brought water, said the Deputy Director of the North-Eastern fishing company Sergey Sedler.  “We brought water to the ship today.  The delivery was organized by the Koreans at the request of our embassy, ” he said.  He said the ship was running out of food and fuel.  “Now all efforts have been directed to speed up the inspection so that the ship will return home as soon as possible, because everything ends with them, ” he added.  Following the results of yesterday ’ s visit to the ship by employees of the Russian Consulate in the DPRK, the Russian Foreign Ministry issued a statement, according to which it has already “put before the North Korean side the issue of ensuring proper conditions for the detained sailors. ”  A Kommersant source in the Russian Foreign Ministry confirmed that work on the release of the sailors is already underway, and assured that there is no doubt about the positive outcome of the case.  According to the Russian Foreign Ministry, the crew is “in satisfactory condition ”.  The representative of the Embassy of the DPRK yesterday said that the ship was flying the South Korean flag, and that the captain recognized the violation of territorial waters, reports TASS.  He said that now in respect of the seafarers check.  “Given the good relations between Russia and the DPRK, we expect that after the inspection, the sailors and the ship will be sent to the Russian Federation, ” the embassy added.  According to the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, territorial waters end 12 nautical miles from shore, while the ship was detained about 50 miles away.  The All-Russian Association of Fishery Producers sent an appeal to the Russian Foreign Ministry with its interpretation of the actions of the North Korean side.  According to the association, the incident is related to the tightening of control over the activities of Korean ships: in 2018, the Russian border service “stopped the illegal activities of 68 fishing vessels of the DPRK off the coast of Primorsky Krai. ”  The chairman of the Far Eastern regional organization of the Russian Seafarers ’ Union said that the organization is ready to do everything possible to release the ship ’ s crew, even to contact North Korean trade unions if the relatives of the detainees so request.  Recall, on Tuesday it became known about the detention of the North Korean authorities of a fishing vessel with 17 sailors — 15 Russians and two South Korean citizens.  On July 16, the seiner left the port of the South Korean city of Sokcho for crab fishing and, according to Rosrybolovstvo, went to the control point “Vostok-1 ”.  The next morning, the North Korean border service detained the ship 55 miles from its shores for violating the so-called protection zone, which is not recognized by either Russia or the world community.  Seiner was escorted to the North Korean port of Wonsan.  The crew is charged with violating the rules of entry and stay in the country.  The Ministry of Unification of the Republic of Korea tried to find out the details of the incident and the situation of the fishermen through the inter-Korean liaison office in Kaesong, but received no response.  On July 19, Seoul sent a similar request through the Red Cross, but this attempt did not end.  This was reported yesterday by the Korean edition of The Kyunghyang Shinmun.  Rosrybolovstvo also made a statement.  The ministry condemned the actions of North Korean border guards and called the detention illegal.  Referring to the information of the Russian Consulate in the DPRK, Rosrybolovstvo reported that “on the ship the means of technical control and satellite telephone communication were disabled, mobile phones from the crew members were seized ”, and the captain and his assistant are in the hotel separately from the rest and do not have contact with them.  The deputy director of the company also indicated that the Xianhailin-8 was heading to the Sea of Japan for crab fishing.  One of Kommersant ’ s sources in the Russian Foreign Ministry suggested a possible plot of the incident: the crew was transporting contraband goods.  Seiner could try to escape from the Russian border guards and thus be in the security zone of the DPRK.  According to Sergei Sedler, the ship at the time of detention was without cargo.  "Kommersant" could not quickly get a comment from the Far Eastern Customs Administration.  Alexandra Fokina, Mikhail Korostikov

Title: The crew of the ship “Patriot ” can not return from China to Russia due to the situation with the coronavirus
Content: Repatriation of the crew of the vessel “Patriot ”, which is located in the Chinese port of Ningde, is delayed due to the forced extended holidays with the authorities in China, which are engaged in the registration of documents for sailors.  As told TASS Deputy Director of the ship-owner "Hudson" Oleg Anikin, now "Patriot" is in the port of Ningde, where he came for repair, sailors are provided with everything necessary.  “We managed to agree on work with the shipyard, but due to the outbreak of pneumonia from the coronavirus, representatives of the plant are not yet able to start repairing, they do not even say when it will be possible.  As for the return of the crew to their homeland, there are obstacles.  The fact is that all official authorities in China, which are engaged in the registration of documents necessary for repatriation, are now on forced holidays at least until the 10th, and maybe longer, ” Anikin said.  According to him, the company has a prospect in terms of providing contracts for the work of its ships, which will allow in February to start paying seafarers debts.  In this, Hudson is assisted by a special commission of the Russian government, which was created to solve the problems of entrepreneurs who fell under American sanctions.  Earlier, the chairman of the Far Eastern regional organization of the Russian Seamen ’ s Trade Union Nikolai Sukhanov said that the crew of the Patriot appealed to the trade union with a request to assist in returning to their homeland.  During the stoppage at the port, the sailors complained of irregular supplies and non-payment of wages.  According to the Far Eastern Transport Prosecutor ’ s Office, the amount of debt on the salary of 19 crew members is 1.6 million rubles for November, December 2019 and January 2020.  Recall that in 2018, the United States Department of the Treasury announced the expansion of sanctions lists on the DPRK, which included the Russian-based shipping company Hudson.  In particular, the list includes six ships under the Russian flag: “Patriot ”,“ Neptune ”, “Bogatyr ”,“ Bella ”, “Partizan ” and“ Sevastopol ”.  According to the US authorities, they are involved “in the transfer of oil products to ships flying the flag of the DPRK, as well as activities prohibited by the UN Security Council. ”  The report of the UN expert group on the situation with the DPRK, which was published on the organization ’ s website on March 12, 2019, said that the experts did not receive from the United States evidence of pumping oil products from the company ’ s ship “Patriot ” to two North Korean tankers in January 2018, but so far the company is not excluded from the sanctions list.  After multiple detentions of ships and refusals of the company ’ s partners from contracts (in Hudson, this is associated with sanctions), employees of the shipping company wrote an open letter to the leadership of Russia in May last year, in which they asked to provide the company with monetary assistance and give access to government contracts in order to prevent bankruptcy.

Title: The crew of the ship “Patriot ” can not return from China to Russia due to the situation with the coronavirus
Content: Repatriation of the crew of the vessel “Patriot ”, which is located in the Chinese port of Ningde, is delayed due to the forced extended holidays with the authorities in China, which are engaged in the registration of documents for sailors.  As told TASS Deputy Director of the ship-owner "Hudson" Oleg Anikin, now "Patriot" is in the port of Ningde, where he came for repair, sailors are provided with everything necessary.  “We managed to agree on work with the shipyard, but due to the outbreak of pneumonia from the coronavirus, representatives of the plant are not yet able to start repairing, they do not even say when it will be possible.  As for the return of the crew to their homeland, there are obstacles.  The fact is that all official authorities in China, which are engaged in the registration of documents necessary for repatriation, are now on forced holidays at least until the 10th, and maybe longer, ” Anikin said.  According to him, the company has a prospect in terms of providing contracts for the work of its ships, which will allow in February to start paying seafarers debts.  In this, Hudson is assisted by a special commission of the Russian government, which was created to solve the problems of entrepreneurs who fell under American sanctions.  Earlier, the chairman of the Far Eastern regional organization of the Russian Seamen ’ s Trade Union Nikolai Sukhanov said that the crew of the Patriot appealed to the trade union with a request to assist in returning to their homeland.  During the stoppage at the port, the sailors complained of irregular supplies and non-payment of wages.  According to the Far Eastern Transport Prosecutor ’ s Office, the amount of debt on the salary of 19 crew members is 1.6 million rubles for November, December 2019 and January 2020.  Recall that in 2018, the United States Department of the Treasury announced the expansion of sanctions lists on the DPRK, which included the Russian-based shipping company Hudson.  In particular, the list includes six ships under the Russian flag: “Patriot ”,“ Neptune ”, “Bogatyr ”,“ Bella ”, “Partizan ” and“ Sevastopol ”.  According to the US authorities, they are involved “in the transfer of oil products to ships flying the flag of the DPRK, as well as activities prohibited by the UN Security Council. ”  The report of the UN expert group on the situation with the DPRK, which was published on the organization ’ s website on March 12, 2019, said that the experts did not receive from the United States evidence of pumping oil products from the company ’ s ship “Patriot ” to two North Korean tankers in January 2018, but so far the company is not excluded from the sanctions list.  After multiple detentions of ships and refusals of the company ’ s partners from contracts (in Hudson, this is associated with sanctions), employees of the shipping company wrote an open letter to the leadership of Russia in May last year, in which they asked to provide the company with monetary assistance and give access to government contracts in order to prevent bankruptcy.

passages.title: Japan to resume whaling for first time in 30 years
passages.passage: Japan will cease membership in the International Whaling Commission from 2019.  This was reported by the representative of the government of the country, reports AFP.  The government of Japan made this decision because the country ’ s attempts to convince the commission to restore commercial whaling failed, due to resistance from countries struggling with whaling.  Government spokesman Yoshihihido Suga said Japan is withdrawing from the commission to restore commercial whale hunting on its own in July 2019.  “Commercial whaling will be restored in July next year and will be limited to Japan ’ s territorial waters and the country ’ s exclusive economic zones.  We will not hunt in Antarctic waters or in the southern hemisphere, ” Suga said.  Australia and New Zealand have always opposed attempts to restore commercial whaling.  Both countries are calling for a complete end to whaling.  Iceland and Norway have traditionally opposed the moratorium on whaling in addition to Japan.  Both Scandinavian countries have limited whaling.  Japan has officially stopped commercial whaling under a moratorium imposed in 1986.  But in two years, Japan resumed whaling in Antarctic waters “for scientific purposes. ”

passages.title: Iceland halts whaling for first time in 17 years
passages.passage: Icelandic whaling companies have announced the suspension of whaling for the first time in 17 years.  On Friday, June 28, one of Iceland ’ s two whaling companies, IP-Utgerd, announced that its workers will not hunt ocean mammals during the current summer season.  This decision is dictated by the fact that the authorities are increasingly expanding the coastal zone in which whaling is prohibited.  Therefore, the ships of the company have to go as far as possible to the sea, reports the Correspondent.  The fact is that the company IP-Utgerd specializes in catching minke whales.  These mammals are not very large, so going out for them far into the open sea is not worth it.  But the company ’ s employees intend to focus on catching holothuria.  The second Icelandic whaling company, Hvalur, announced in early June that its vessels would not go to sea this summer.  The management of the company specializing in minke fin, explained his move lack of time for full preparation, because this year the authorities issued permits for whaling too late.  In addition, there are now significant problems with the sale of whaling products in the Japanese market.  Iceland ’ s current suspension of whaling occurred for the first time in 17 years.  In 2018, Icelandic whaling companies caught 145 fin whales and six minke whales.  The annual quotas set by the local authorities for whaling companies are 209 fin whales and 217 minke whales.  These rules are valid until 2023.  In 1986, the International Whaling Commission banned the hunting of whales of any kind.  The decision was not supported by Iceland and Norway.  Japan also hunts whales.  The Japanese explain their actions by saying that the ban contains an exception for whaling for scientific purposes.
