passages.title: Exclusive: Japan launches first coastal cetacean ecological survey in winter and spring
passages.passage: News from Japan (Kyodo News Agency, June 28) On the 26th, the Japan Cetacean Research Institute launched a "winter to spring" whale ecology visual survey on the coast of Japan for the first time this year.  The previous survey focused on the "spring to autumn" of the fishing season.  With the reactivation of commercial whaling, proper management of whale resources is the goal.  The survey also found that as a whaling object of the minke whale, some relevant people put forward "if the resources are confirmed to be sufficient, hope to expand the fishing limit".  The survey, using subsidies provided by the Department of Aquaculture, was carried out in the coastal waters of the Northeast region from March 15 to 29, and selected the most suitable weather to go to sea in winter and spring.  The four small whalers sailed about 50 kilometers from the fishing ports of Tabata and Hachinohe in Aomori Prefecture, Yamada fishing port in Iwate Prefecture, and Catagawa fishing port in Miyagi Prefecture. The crew conducted visual investigations through binoculars.  A total of 25 humpback whales, 11 minke whales, 6 sperm whales, and 2 fin whales were found, totaling 44.  The head of the institute said: "Because this is the first attempt, whether the number of heads is more or less needs to be discussed later than future surveys." Next year's plan will be decided later.  According to the Fisheries Agency, in addition to the coast of Japan, where the implementation period was expanded this year, the visual survey continues to be carried out in the Antarctic and offshore North Pacific.  In addition, a new research project on stranded whales has been launched since the current year.  Prior to Japan ’ s withdrawal from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) in 2019, it conducted scientific whaling in the Antarctic Sea and the Northwest Pacific Ocean. After resuming commercial whaling, it operated in the territorial sea and the Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ).  The 2021 catch limit decided by the Department of Aquaculture is 295 minke whales, Bryde whales and Sei whales.  Including the number of mixed fishing in fixed nets, the fishing limit is 383, which is only about 60% of the 2018 catch of scientific whaling. (Finish)

passages.title: Common ships will spend 6 billion yen to build new whaling mother ship
passages.passage: News from Japan (Kyodo News Agency, May 11) In the context of the commercial whaling that has resumed in Japan after 31 years in 2019, President Hideki So, the only company to carry out offshore operations, held a press conference in Tokyo on the 10th, announcing plans to spend about 6 billion yen (about 350 million yuan) to build a new whaling ship.  The company is optimistic that the Japanese government will expand the fishing quota and target sea areas in the future, and renovate the old mother ship.  Originally, it was "always said that it would cost more than 10 billion yen" (in the words of the president), but the cost was reduced by reducing the speed of the current mother ship "Nisin Maru".  It is expected to be completed in March 2024.  The government currently restricts commercial whaling to the exclusive economic zone (EEZ) of Japan, which covers only three species of minke whales, Bryde whales and Sei whales.  The new mother ship was also designed to operate outside the EEZ in the future. It can also catch large fin whales and ensure that it has the ability to reach the Antarctic waters.  The construction fee will not rely on subsidies, but will be obtained through crowdfunding through loans and online fundraising.  The president said that in order to guarantee the repayment of funds, "we hope to increase the amount of fishing in 2024."  He also stressed that the expansion of the whale meat market will be driven by higher wholesale prices and increased imports.  Japan withdrew from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) at the end of June 2019 and stopped its previous investigation of whaling activities.

passages.title: Animal Husbandry in the World + Pictures
passages.passage: They send a boat to find whales and dolphins in front of them.  After finding a flock of animals, other boats make terrible noises and sound walls as they move.  Frightened whales and dolphins swim to the bay, after the animals are exhausted, spears are thrust into their bodies, and the entire sea turns red.  Images of the sea of blood and the slaughter of animals have been repeatedly published in the media.  Japan is one of the countries that, as a tradition, kill large numbers of whales and dolphins.  Although environmental groups have repeatedly protested the move, the country withdrew from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) last year and resumed whaling.  Japan has been whaling for centuries, and its meat has been used as a key source of protein in the post-World War II years when the country was in extreme poverty.  Japanese fishermen also killed more than 300 large finned whales in the Antarctic Ocean last year, including 122 pregnant whales.  The country says it hunts for scientific research, while critics argue that killing whales is for commercial use and Japan sells and uses them for food.  In 2014, the International Court of Justice ruled that Japan ’ s Antarctic whaling program was not for scientific and research purposes and therefore had to be stopped.  However, Japanese authorities claim that the scale of whaling off beaches for commercial purposes is very small compared to whaling in the northern ocean for scientific purposes.  Apart from Japan, many other countries offer different animal sacrifices each year.  The killing of cows after bullfights in Spain, animal sacrifices in Haiti, the killing of whales in Denmark, and the killing of cows and sheep in Nepal and Africa are still held around the world, and in some cases, people are injured or killed.  Photographs published by Alistair Ward, a 22-year-old student at the University of Cambridge, of whaling in Sandavago Bay have received a lot of media attention.  People from the Faroe Islands in Denmark kill whales every year, and this tradition has been going on for centuries.  The Faroe Islands lie in northern Europe between the Norwegian Sea and the North Atlantic Ocean and are made up of 18 small islands.  Whale meat and tallow are a source of food for the nearly 59,000 islanders who are said to be spending the winter there.  The hunters at this ceremony guide the whales to the bay with their oars, and when they get close enough, the killing begins.  Even children participate in the ceremony.  Residents of the area consider whaling a collective activity that everyone can participate in.  They say this is done under national regulations and laws, so that the whales suffer the least amount of pain and suffering.  Many Faroe Islanders believe whaling is not incompatible with the ecosystem, and they hunt 800 pilot whales each year out of the 100,000 whales that surround the island.  Images of this massacre on social media caused a lot of reactions, and some of them, in response to the reaction of European animal rights defenders to the slaughter of animals in East Asia and Africa, wrote sarcastically: “Because Europeans are blond and white, the name of this work is not barbarism and the supply of meat, but the religious slaughter of Muslims is barbaric! ”  The Gadhimai Festival is another event in which thousands of cows and sheep are sacrificed.  The ceremony takes place every five years over two days in Nepal and is inspired by a Hindu religion in the village of Baryapur, which believes that sacrificing to the goddess Gadhimai will capture the devil and bring them happiness.  What animal rights advocates have been protesting at the festival is an unusual form of victimization.  In this place, the cattle are gathered in a field, and they are slashed from the back of the neck.  Animal rights advocates call it the largest animal slaughterhouse in the world because of its remarkable violence.  In addition to the whaling, the Gadhimai festival in Japan has another 3,500-year-old ceremony that takes place in Taiji.  This event is known for the hunt of dolphins by the people of the world.  The people of this city have long been engaged in fishing and whale or dolphin hunting.  Despite opposition, Taijis continue to do so for their food, claiming it has long been a source of livelihood and a part of their cultural identity.  Taiji ’ s history shows the existence of 400-year-old whaling weapons.  The World Health Organization (WHO) studied dolphin meat and declared the amount of toxins and mercury in the meat to be very high, warning people that high levels of mercury in dolphin meat cause diseases such as cancer, infertility and suppression of the immune system.  However, traditional Taiji fishermen continue to slaughter the animal, and its products can be seen in the city ’ s stores.  The people of Taiji send a boat out to hunt for the dolphins in the first place.  After finding a flock of dolphins, the other boats are arranged in the shape of an English letter V, making terrifying sounds and sound walls as they move.  Scared dolphins swim to the bay.  Then other boats chase them to throw their frightened dolphins ashore and crash into the rocks.  After the dolphins are exhausted, the spears are thrust into the bodies of these animals and the entire sea turns red.  Among the wounded dolphins, the more beautiful ones are hunted for aquariums and circuses.  In Taiji, Haiti, there is also a ceremony in which animals are killed.  Voodoo believers gather in the country in April and declare their obedience to their gods by sacrificing animals, dancing and playing music.  After the sacrifice, they pour the warm blood of the animal into a container and drink it.  Those present in the ceremony, dressed in white, shed some of this blood on themselves, and while believing that they are under the control of the spirits, they jump into the water and continue to worship.  Wearing white clothes with blood symbolizes adherence to voodoo.  Followers of the cult have combined drum dancing as an African tradition with traditional elements of the Catholic religion.  Millions of Haitians believe in voodoo, and the government adopted it as an official religion in 1960.  But in 2012, the Haitian Senate and House of Representatives decried Voodoo as the official religion with a constitutional amendment approved by their president, a move that caused widespread discontent among Haitian followers.  In Spain, bullfighting is also one of the most popular entertainment in the world.  San Fermin in Spain attracts many tourists every year.  The celebration of the release and running of angry cows among the crowd through the narrow alleys lasts a few minutes, but the celebration lasts for hours.  Cows enter the stadium after passing through the city center to witness the matador battle with the bulls.  In the past, due to the narrow streets and the lack of possibility of passing the cart, ranchers had to drive the cows on a short path to the stadium.  Over time, young people started running in front of the cows to show their courage.  Those who run in front of cows traditionally wear white shirts and trousers and a red necktie around their necks.  Every year, the ceremony leaves a number of injured and even killed.  At the end of the festivities in Spain, bullfighters circle the animals and kill them with decorated spears and knives.  Due to opposition to the ceremony, bullfighting festivals were banned in some Spanish cities, including the Canary Islands.  It is not only in rituals that animals are abused and slaughtered, but also in pictures and videos of the slaughter of pregnant cows in France, sheep in Australian slaughterhouses, the killing of goats in Thailand, the slaughter of camels in Mauritania, and the cooking of live pigs in Europe. Title: Japan to resume whaling for first time in 30 years
Content: Japan will cease membership in the International Whaling Commission from 2019.  This was reported by the representative of the government of the country, reports AFP. We will not hunt in Antarctic waters or in the southern hemisphere, ” Suga said.  Australia and New Zealand have always opposed attempts to restore commercial whaling.  Both countries are calling for a complete end to whaling.  Iceland and Norway have traditionally opposed the moratorium on whaling in addition to Japan.  Both Scandinavian countries have limited whaling.  Japan has officially stopped commercial whaling under a moratorium imposed in 1986. Title: Iceland halts whaling for first time in 17 years
Content: Icelandic whaling companies have announced the suspension of whaling for the first time in 17 years.  On Friday, June 28, one of Iceland ’ s two whaling companies, IP-Utgerd, announced that its workers will not hunt ocean mammals during the current summer season.  This decision is dictated by the fact that the authorities are increasingly expanding the coastal zone in which whaling is prohibited.  Therefore, the ships of the company have to go as far as possible to the sea, reports the Correspondent.  The fact is that the company IP-Utgerd specializes in catching minke whales.  These mammals are not very large, so going out for them far into the open sea is not worth it.  But the company ’ s employees intend to focus on catching holothuria.  The second Icelandic whaling company, Hvalur, announced in early June that its vessels would not go to sea this summer.  The management of the company specializing in minke fin, explained his move lack of time for full preparation, because this year the authorities issued permits for whaling too late.  In addition, there are now significant problems with the sale of whaling products in the Japanese market.  Iceland ’ s current suspension of whaling occurred for the first time in 17 years.  In 2018, Icelandic whaling companies caught 145 fin whales and six minke whales.  The annual quotas set by the local authorities for whaling companies are 209 fin whales and 217 minke whales.  These rules are valid until 2023.  In 1986, the International Whaling Commission banned the hunting of whales of any kind.  The decision was not supported by Iceland and Norway.  Japan also hunts whales.  The Japanese explain their actions by saying that the ban contains an exception for whaling for scientific purposes.

Title: Exclusive: Japan launches first coastal cetacean ecological survey in winter and spring
Content: News from Japan (Kyodo News Agency, June 28) On the 26th, the Japan Cetacean Research Institute launched a "winter to spring" whale ecology visual survey on the coast of Japan for the first time this year.  The previous survey focused on the "spring to autumn" of the fishing season.  With the reactivation of commercial whaling, proper management of whale resources is the goal.  The survey also found that as a whaling object of the minke whale, some relevant people put forward "if the resources are confirmed to be sufficient, hope to expand the fishing limit".  The survey, using subsidies provided by the Department of Aquaculture, was carried out in the coastal waters of the Northeast region from March 15 to 29, and selected the most suitable weather to go to sea in winter and spring.  The four small whalers sailed about 50 kilometers from the fishing ports of Tabata and Hachinohe in Aomori Prefecture, Yamada fishing port in Iwate Prefecture, and Catagawa fishing port in Miyagi Prefecture. The crew conducted visual investigations through binoculars.  A total of 25 humpback whales, 11 minke whales, 6 sperm whales, and 2 fin whales were found, totaling 44.  The head of the institute said: "Because this is the first attempt, whether the number of heads is more or less needs to be discussed later than future surveys." Next year's plan will be decided later.  According to the Fisheries Agency, in addition to the coast of Japan, where the implementation period was expanded this year, the visual survey continues to be carried out in the Antarctic and offshore North Pacific.  In addition, a new research project on stranded whales has been launched since the current year. The 2021 catch limit decided by the Department of Aquaculture is 295 minke whales, Bryde whales and Sei whales. Title: Common ships will spend 6 billion yen to build new whaling mother ship
Content: News from Japan (Kyodo News Agency, May 11) In the context of the commercial whaling that has resumed in Japan after 31 years in 2019, President Hideki So, the only company to carry out offshore operations, held a press conference in Tokyo on the 10th, announcing plans to spend about 6 billion yen (about 350 million yuan) to build a new whaling ship. Title: Animal Husbandry in the World + Pictures
Content: They send a boat to find whales and dolphins in front of them.  After finding a flock of animals, other boats make terrible noises and sound walls as they move.  Frightened whales and dolphins swim to the bay, after the animals are exhausted, spears are thrust into their bodies, and the entire sea turns red.  Images of the sea of blood and the slaughter of animals have been repeatedly published in the media.  Japan is one of the countries that, as a tradition, kill large numbers of whales and dolphins.  Although environmental groups have repeatedly protested the move, the country withdrew from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) last year and resumed whaling.  Japan has been whaling for centuries, and its meat has been used as a key source of protein in the post-World War II years when the country was in extreme poverty.  Japanese fishermen also killed more than 300 large finned whales in the Antarctic Ocean last year, including 122 pregnant whales.  The country says it hunts for scientific research, while critics argue that killing whales is for commercial use and Japan sells and uses them for food.  In 2014, the International Court of Justice ruled that Japan ’ s Antarctic whaling program was not for scientific and research purposes and therefore had to be stopped.  However, Japanese authorities claim that the scale of whaling off beaches for commercial purposes is very small compared to whaling in the northern ocean for scientific purposes.  Apart from Japan, many other countries offer different animal sacrifices each year.  The killing of cows after bullfights in Spain, animal sacrifices in Haiti, the killing of whales in Denmark, and the killing of cows and sheep in Nepal and Africa are still held around the world, and in some cases, people are injured or killed.  Photographs published by Alistair Ward, a 22-year-old student at the University of Cambridge, of whaling in Sandavago Bay have received a lot of media attention.  People from the Faroe Islands in Denmark kill whales every year, and this tradition has been going on for centuries.  The Faroe Islands lie in northern Europe between the Norwegian Sea and the North Atlantic Ocean and are made up of 18 small islands.  Whale meat and tallow are a source of food for the nearly 59,000 islanders who are said to be spending the winter there.  The hunters at this ceremony guide the whales to the bay with their oars, and when they get close enough, the killing begins.  Even children participate in the ceremony.  Residents of the area consider whaling a collective activity that everyone can participate in.  They say this is done under national regulations and laws, so that the whales suffer the least amount of pain and suffering.  Many Faroe Islanders believe whaling is not incompatible with the ecosystem, and they hunt 800 pilot whales each year out of the 100,000 whales that surround the island.  Images of this massacre on social media caused a lot of reactions, and some of them, in response to the reaction of European animal rights defenders to the slaughter of animals in East Asia and Africa, wrote sarcastically: “Because Europeans are blond and white, the name of this work is not barbarism and the supply of meat, but the religious slaughter of Muslims is barbaric! ”  The Gadhimai Festival is another event in which thousands of cows and sheep are sacrificed.  The ceremony takes place every five years over two days in Nepal and is inspired by a Hindu religion in the village of Baryapur, which believes that sacrificing to the goddess Gadhimai will capture the devil and bring them happiness.  What animal rights advocates have been protesting at the festival is an unusual form of victimization.  In this place, the cattle are gathered in a field, and they are slashed from the back of the neck.  Animal rights advocates call it the largest animal slaughterhouse in the world because of its remarkable violence.  In addition to the whaling, the Gadhimai festival in Japan has another 3,500-year-old ceremony that takes place in Taiji.  This event is known for the hunt of dolphins by the people of the world.  The people of this city have long been engaged in fishing and whale or dolphin hunting.  Despite opposition, Taijis continue to do so for their food, claiming it has long been a source of livelihood and a part of their cultural identity.  Taiji ’ s history shows the existence of 400-year-old whaling weapons.  The World Health Organization (WHO) studied dolphin meat and declared the amount of toxins and mercury in the meat to be very high, warning people that high levels of mercury in dolphin meat cause diseases such as cancer, infertility and suppression of the immune system.  However, traditional Taiji fishermen continue to slaughter the animal, and its products can be seen in the city ’ s stores.  The people of Taiji send a boat out to hunt for the dolphins in the first place.  After finding a flock of dolphins, the other boats are arranged in the shape of an English letter V, making terrifying sounds and sound walls as they move.  Scared dolphins swim to the bay.  Then other boats chase them to throw their frightened dolphins ashore and crash into the rocks.  After the dolphins are exhausted, the spears are thrust into the bodies of these animals and the entire sea turns red.  Among the wounded dolphins, the more beautiful ones are hunted for aquariums and circuses.  In Taiji, Haiti, there is also a ceremony in which animals are killed.  Voodoo believers gather in the country in April and declare their obedience to their gods by sacrificing animals, dancing and playing music.  After the sacrifice, they pour the warm blood of the animal into a container and drink it.  Those present in the ceremony, dressed in white, shed some of this blood on themselves, and while believing that they are under the control of the spirits, they jump into the water and continue to worship.  Wearing white clothes with blood symbolizes adherence to voodoo.  Followers of the cult have combined drum dancing as an African tradition with traditional elements of the Catholic religion.  Millions of Haitians believe in voodoo, and the government adopted it as an official religion in 1960.  But in 2012, the Haitian Senate and House of Representatives decried Voodoo as the official religion with a constitutional amendment approved by their president, a move that caused widespread discontent among Haitian followers.  In Spain, bullfighting is also one of the most popular entertainment in the world.  San Fermin in Spain attracts many tourists every year.  The celebration of the release and running of angry cows among the crowd through the narrow alleys lasts a few minutes, but the celebration lasts for hours.  Cows enter the stadium after passing through the city center to witness the matador battle with the bulls.  In the past, due to the narrow streets and the lack of possibility of passing the cart, ranchers had to drive the cows on a short path to the stadium.  Over time, young people started running in front of the cows to show their courage.  Those who run in front of cows traditionally wear white shirts and trousers and a red necktie around their necks.  Every year, the ceremony leaves a number of injured and even killed.  At the end of the festivities in Spain, bullfighters circle the animals and kill them with decorated spears and knives.  Due to opposition to the ceremony, bullfighting festivals were banned in some Spanish cities, including the Canary Islands.  It is not only in rituals that animals are abused and slaughtered, but also in pictures and videos of the slaughter of pregnant cows in France, sheep in Australian slaughterhouses, the killing of goats in Thailand, the slaughter of camels in Mauritania, and the cooking of live pigs in Europe. Wearing white clothes with blood symbolizes adherence to voodoo.  Followers of the cult have combined drum dancing as an African tradition with traditional elements of the Catholic religion. passages.passage: The novel is like an iceberg, only one eighth of which is on the surface of the water, and the rest is underwater.  Deleting more sentences and leaving more sentences underwater is enough to strengthen your novel.  This is Ernest Hemingway ’ s “theory of the iceberg ”, which he implemented in his novels. Today, 1940, For Whom the Bell Tolls is published.  Before publication, Hemingway revised the manuscript every day after finishing it, and did not leave the room for 96 consecutive hours.  He used iceberg theory to remove unnecessary sentences, and used symbols, pictures and ideas to navigate the story, resulting in this monumental work that was later adapted into a film and used by the college to teach literature.  Ernest Hemingway (Getty Images) The bell-ringing story in the field focuses on an attack by a guerrilla group during the Spanish Civil War in the summer of 1937.  The story is only four days long, focusing on the tension of the war and the appearance of human nature.  The protagonist, Robert Jordan, is an American professor who teaches Spanish. At the outbreak of the war, he joined the volunteer army and was ordered to go deep into the mountains to break through enemy lines, and the story begins when the protagonist enters the mountains, he tries to contact the guerrillas and cooperate with them to blow up the bridge.  For Whom the Bell Tolls: The Hemingway Library Edition (Scribner) Guerrilla Captain Pablo opposes the bridge, losing his fighting spirit and even stealing the detonator.  Robert manages to gain support from the rest of the team, isolating the captain and planning to blow up the bridge.  Robert takes in Maria, a girl who has been abused and enslaved by the enemy, and falls in love with her.  After stealing the horses from the enemy line, the two walked hand in hand, and he imagined that after the war was over, he would return to the United States to teach, and the two would end up together.  But after a while, he shot and killed one of the other soldiers, and while he did not get any information from the enemy, he read a home letter, which made him feel the cruelty of the war.  In the early hours of the last day, the few remaining teams set out for the bridge, and due to the small number of people and the behavior of the captain, several people had to risk their lives.  In the final scene, Robert and his companions blow the bridge in mid-air with explosives, but when he runs away on horseback in the direction of Maria, he is unfortunately shot and fell, his left leg is broken, and he can no longer escape from the enemy's attack.  At the end of his life, he said to Mary, “As long as one of us lives, the other will live in his heart forever. ”  In 1943, Battlefield Bell was transformed into a film (file picture) The tragic color of "tough man" Hemingway's novels often appear as "tough man", meaning that he has a very strong will and a strong and unyielding spirit.  When the Nobel Prize for Literature was awarded to him, he said that he "has a kind of man who likes to take risks" and vowed not to bow down and fight to the end when faced with the pressure of fate.  The old fisherman in The Old Man and the Sea said, “Man can be destroyed, but he cannot be defeated. ”  But when we talk about fate and rebellion, we often talk about tragedy, and the end of Battlefield Bell is clearly tragic.  [The Old Man and the Sea] Hemingway's many novels have been exposed hundreds of wrong scholars: The fault is not in the spirit of his ancient Greek tragedy, it is that when people face the choice of fate, they know that they have to bear a heavy price and still struggle to insist on their own choices, and finally they really want to meet the tragic consequences.  It may be against fate, it may be against power, and it ends tragically.  In The Birth of Tragedy, Nietzsche pointed out that the ancient Greek tragedy was the manifestation of the god of wine, freed from the "self", disordered and led to a carnival, chanting that people "believe in eternal life". passages.title: How to read Hemingway?
passages.passage: Ernest Hemingway, a Nobel laureate and one of the most important of the 20th century, was born on July 21, 1899 in Illinois and wrote seven novels, six collections of short stories and two nonfiction books during his lifetime.  On the occasion of the birth of this author, which coincided with the thirteenth of July, we have suggestions for better reading of the works of this author.  Hemingway ’ s work is fluid, simple, and clear, but for many readers of literature, it may be difficult to begin reading Hemingway ’ s books.  Why read Hemingway?  Ernest Hemingway is an influential writer in the history of literature and fiction, his works have repeatedly won the most prestigious international literary awards such as Nobel and Pulitzer, this author employed a different kind of narrative description and caused many writers after him to borrow his own literary style.  Hemingway has named his literary style the Iceberg Theory, in this way of writing, fictional events are narrated like an iceberg floating in water, only one-eighth of which is visible, and the author includes only the information that is essential in the process and omits the rest of the information.  This technique created a tremendous change in storytelling, especially the writing of short stories, and it was a development that freed the stories from conventional chatter.  Hemingway ’ s works are included in the list of books of the century, books to read before death, and the best fiction books in history, highlighting the importance of this author.  What do we need to know?  One of the topics that helps to better understand Ernest Hemingway ’ s work is getting to know his personal life.  Much of what we read in his books is what he has turned from his personal life into a story.  At the age of 19, he volunteered for the First World War but was not allowed to fight because of poor eyesight, but Hemingway insisted on serving as an ambulance driver for the Red Cross.  He was wounded several times during the Chang, but his most significant injury is when he was wounded by mortar shell fragments and spent a long time in the hospital, a novel about this part of Hemingway ’ s life and the war.  Even the character of Catherine Barkley in this book is based on the nurse Hemingway fell in love with.  Hemingway also participated in World War II as a war correspondent, and several short stories are the result of this era.  The sun continues to blow, the Great River or along the river to the trees, each of which is somehow tied to the World War, and their heroes are survivors of the war and have many memories of these days.  But Hemingway ’ s most important masterpiece is a relic of his childhood, Hemingway ’ s father had a great interest in fishing, and this hobby was passed on to Ernest, a point that can be clearly seen in the famous and widely read story of The Old Man and the Sea.  But before the Old Man and the Sea, Hemingway had written about having and not having a fishing boat captain.  Another important point to know before reading Hemingway ’ s works is his political approach, he has written a lot in opposition to fascism and against dictatorship, both as a journalist and as a writer, sometimes even changing from a journalist to a social-political activist, who is this point in The Bell for, or who is this death knell?  It is a story of an American soldier in the Spanish Civil War fighting alongside groups against General Franco, which Hemingway did.  Perhaps the other thing that matters is that during the World War, Hemingway led a French group against the Nazis that was tried after the war for armed acts but was never proven guilty.  The political and social history of the world in the years of Hemingway's life, his personal life, as well as the knowledge of his contemporaries, such as Scott Fitzgerald, with whom he has written, are points that contribute to the understanding of his works.  Getting to know Hemingway ’ s contemporary writers helps to better understand the difference between him and his contemporaries.  Is it a classic?  To read Hemingway ’ s work, we must note that he is not a classic writer in his different style, he did not deal with the long margins and descriptions of classical literature, and his long novels are not immune.  He was interested in shorthand and engaging the audience with fiction, which is a feature of modern literature.  In general, Hemingway ’ s works are innovative and even among modern works have their own creativity, but the value of this author ’ s work has always been compared to classical works, and even classical enthusiasts have not been able to be indifferent to it.  In these works we have a happy and well-spoken writer, a writer who was in middle age with young people and was even close friends with a group of hippies.  Hemingway is a realistic writer, but he has always tried to maintain his sense of humor.  Where do we start?  To read Hemingway ’ s works, the first and most important suggestion is The Old Man and the Sea.  The book, translated by Najaf Daryabandari, was published in 222 pages by Kharazmi Publications.  The next book, Farewell to Arms, is again translated by Najaf Daryabendari, published by Amir Kabir Publications in 343 pages.  These two books are always on the list of works to be read or masterpieces of the 20th century.  If you are interested in short stories, you can also read Men Without Women, a collection of stories that have been published in various magazines by the author.  This book has been translated by Asadollah Amraei for publication of Horizon in 222 pages.  Even if you are interested in writing, Hemingway can be a good teacher and read his series of talks and learn very precise points.  The book The Last Interview and Other Conversations of Ernest Hemingway with a translation by Houshang Jirani has been published in 88 pages by Cheshmeh Publishing.  The final chapter of many critics considered Ernest Hemingway to be the greatest writer of the 20th century.  His stories are an exploration of real human life, suffering and the meaning of life.  The portrayal of human inner feelings is the most important characteristic of this author, which makes his works a read for every reader.  Who was Ernest Hemingway?  Ernest Hemingway was born on July 21, 1899 in Oak Park, Illinois.  His father, Clarence, was a doctor and his mother, Grace, was a piano and singing teacher.  Ernest spent the summers with his family in northern Michigan, where he discovered his passion for fishing.  After finishing high school, he worked for a while in Kansas City as a reporter for the Star Chronicle in 1917.  During World War I, he volunteered to serve in the army, but poor eyesight prevented him from doing so, instead serving as an ambulance driver for the Red Cross near the Italian front.  On July 8, 1918, he was injured and spent months in the hospital.  In 1925, his first collection of short stories, in our time, was published, which spoke well of his particular style.  His memoirs from that period were published after his death in 1964 as The Variable Eid.  Ernest Hemingway was an adventurer for most of his life.  From being wounded in Italy by 200 pieces of Austrian shrapnel during World War I, to taking part in the frontlines of the Spanish Civil War or touring the African wilderness, to fishing and hunting wildlife and living in Cuba.  He finally said goodbye to life with his hunting rifle.

Although some believe that Hemingway did not participate in the Spanish Civil War and was sent there only as a journalist, this did not prevent Hemingway from taking an impartial view of one of the great events of the country and the people of Spain and presenting the Spanish nation as it was and as it is by taking a small part in the many years of war and slaughter.  The heroic records of the peoples of this region, since they ended the tyrannical rule and tyrannical occupation of the Greyhounds, and were the only nation to bring Napoleon to his knees with all his successes in various battles, have provided a lesson in the history of humanity that can serve as a good example for all the enslaved nations of the world.  Hemingway defines the revolution and the aftermath of the Spanish fratricide war impartially, why not impartially, because while advocating their libertarian uprising, it does not mention the excesses and follies seen in all revolutions, among all nations.  What follows is the full text of Parviz Shahdi ’ s preface to the translation of Ernest Hemingway ’ s “The Grief Bell Strikes ”.  This introduction, which was signed by the translator in the summer of 2009 and testifies to the 10-year wait for its publication, provides a detailed description of Hemingway ’ s works and opinions, especially this book: “Perhaps the reader will be asked the question that Hemingway is better known in Iran than anyone would like to introduce him.  True, but for my generation and my generation after me, who are familiar with his life and his work, what about this third generation today, who knows, or has even heard of Hemingway?  Maybe yes, maybe no, but the probability of knowing him is very low, because his works, which have been translated into Persian, are no longer reprinted (with the exception of “A Farewell to Arms ”).  But does he have to give up on oblivion?  No, he was one of the giants of American and world literature of the last century.  Hemingway was not a coward, but the thought of death did not stop for a moment.  If all, or most, of his stories end with the death of the hero or the main protagonists, it is no coincidence.  According to Gertrude Stein, an American female writer and critic based in Paris, Hemingway is part of the “bewildered generation ” after World War I.  He has in common with writers of his time who are part of this generation, such as Dos Passos, Joyce, Sherwood Andersen, and so on.  But only the title of “Lost Generation ” is what he has in common with his contemporaries, or else his way is separate from all the others, each of which has its own way, style, and place in world literature.  On the surface, especially when he settled in Paris, Hemingway was a happy, healthy, playful young man who loved adventure and risk.  His tall, broad shoulders, and keen interest in boxing, hunting, fishing, and bullfighting confirm this.  He drove an ambulance in World War I, fought Franco ’ s supporters in the Spanish Civil War, worked as a reporter in World War II.  He traversed the pristine forests of Africa for a long time, even on one of these trips his plane crashed and almost died.  He liked to watch cowboy matches and was very friendly with matrons.  Many parts of the sun are still blowing for these competitions and traffic with bullfighters.  Most of his stories are set in Spain, the Caribbean, Africa and Central America.  There are few stories of him that took place in his own country, in contrast to Faulkner and Steinbeck, where not only America, but a particular region, is the scene of the events of their stories.  There are two sides to the coin of life and death.  He who loved her, loved her, loved her, loved her, loved her, and loved her.  But inside he was a different person, one who saw nothing in the mirror of life but death, and unlike his strong and dangerous body, the thought of death never left him, which is perhaps why he always went to risk to overcome this fear, like cowards who risk to hide their fear in order to appear bold and reckless.  Hemingway was not a coward, but the thought of death did not stop for a moment.  If all, or most, of his stories end with the death of the hero or the main protagonists, it is no coincidence. They will enjoy life, and they will enjoy it, and they will enjoy it forever.  Their love for women is deep, but they don ’ t seem to show anything.  From the short stories with which he began to write, this attitude is clear, even though he was still young at the time and looking for a name.  In a continuous celebration of autobiography, he describes the beginning of his career in Paris, his acquaintance with the companions of the bewildered generation, especially his compatriot Edward Fitzgerald.  The Sun Still Rises is his first serious novel, followed by A Farewell to Arms.  In The Sun Still Blowing, we find promiscuous people who, regardless of the doomed world, have nothing to do but drink and make love and watch a bull fight, plus Jake Barnes, the main hero, is deprived of the pleasure of making love because of a wound in the war.  In A Farewell to Arms, the hero ’ s violent attitude and indifference to life are diminished, although in this story, the main hero, Frederick Henry, still ridicules life, love, war, and in short, everything, following the slogan “The tail is the booty ”, after wounding in the war (which is again taken from Hemingway ’ s own life), in the hospital and during his convalescence, only pauses. Love, of course, cannot end happily in a world in which everything is falling apart.  Even in Hemingway ’ s short stories, we see death behind the seemingly happy face of life.  It ’ s as if it ’ s actually death who ’ s been born and lives for a while under the mask of life to finally show his true face.  In the short, happy life of Francis Macomber, the snows of Kilimanjaro, death in the afternoon, assassins, and many other short stories, there is more death talk than life.  The hero of having and not having, Henry Morgan, is apparently different from the other heroes of Hemingway, tries to live a simple and uncontroversial life, to provide for himself and his family by fishing, but still faces the harsh face of death, behind the political and mafia organization of American life, and his end is destroyed. Title: 【 Green Bird Residence 】 Event Feature ： Chen Jung-bin / Impression of Paris in Hemingway 's Text
Content: In the 1920s, the Treaty of Versailles proclaimed the end of World War I, Hitler in Europe joined the Nazi Party, and the Communist Party of China rose in the East.  And the United States introduced a national prohibition of alcohol, so a group of American "expats" came to Paris, free and exile in various cafes and bars. Hemingway also moved to the old city as a reporter in 1921, beginning his penniless, but indulgent days.  A hundred years later, Chen Jung-bin and the audience of the Blue Bird House look back at the impression of Paris that was reflected in Hemingway ’ s words.  The Old Man and the Sea was born on an alcohol-soaked beach in Cuba; The War Bell is an interview from the Spanish Civil War; The Dawn of Truth records the memories of a trip to Africa with his fourth wife, Mary, and Hemingway, born in Oak Park, Illinois, USA.  At the age of 21, he worked as a reporter for the Toronto Star in Canada, became a special correspondent in Europe the next year, and moved to Paris to spend his 20 generations, nearly a decade of his golden years.  Ernest Hemingway in World War I. When he first arrived in Paris, he stayed in a small hotel and wrote in the Toronto Star: “PARIS — Paris in the winter is rainy, cold, beautiful and cheap. ”  It is also noisy, jostling, crowded and cheap.  It is anything you want — and cheap. ” — Living on $1,000 a Year in Paris Describes the bankruptcy of Europe at the end of World War I, the relative advantage of the dollar, and the ability to spend a thousand dollars in Paris for a year.  Although this article is published in the newspaper, the writing and rhyme are poetic.  “We ate well and cheaply and drank well and cheaply and slept well and warm together and love each other. ”  After graduating from high school, Hemingway worked as a reporter for the Kansas City Star, and his entire writing career was inextricably linked to journalistic writing.  “From Hemingway ’ s early writings, the Kansas Star newspaper ’ s“ style sheet ” for the rookie reporter shaped his unique style of writing, and the rules in the guide were as many as 110, and the first paragraph was indeed Hemingway ’ s rule: write short sentences.  The first paragraph is shorter.  Write articles in vivid English.  The influence of the rookie reporter period on his career also corresponds to the iceberg theory he proposed in 1932: "Prose is like architecture, not interior decoration, and the Baroque era is over... If you have enough understanding of what you are describing and write well enough, even if you write only one-eighth of the text, you can let the reader fully grasp the scene, plot and character description that he wants to express." Hemingway often uses a concise style to bury clues in the details or background, so that it is connected with emotional intimacy.  Paris was not only the place where Hemingway worked as a journalist, but also the beginning of his literary career.  The first two books, Three Stories & Ten Poems, and a collection of short stories, in our time, were published here.  Ernest Hemingway wrote many notes about his life and literary work in the 1920s. Two boxes were left in the basement of the Ritz Hotel in Paris, and when he returned to Paris in 1957, he opened these dusty old memories, namely, "The Feast on the Move".  This prose memoir of Paris also later became a guide for people on their pilgrimage journey, following Hemingway for a drink, order a cup of coffee at the Lilac Café, borrow a book at Shakespeare ’ s Bookstore on the Rue d ’ Odeon, and then take a walk in Luxembourg Park.  “If you are lucky enough to have lived in Paris as a young man, then wherever you go for the rest of your life it stays with you, for Paris is a movable feast. ” — Ernest Hemingway A moving feast.  Shakespeare Bookstore (Photo / Courtesy of Blue Bird) Mr. Chen then pointed out on the map several places where Hemingway often stopped in Paris. First came to the Shakespeare Bookstore, which is also like a library, which can rent books at affordable prices, and also provides mail collection services, which is suitable for young and poor boy Hemingway.  The owner of the bookstore, Shelville Beach, is also an American, and in her autobiography, Shakespeare's Bookstore, there is a chapter entitled "The Best Customer Hemingway".  In his translation of the book, Mr. Chen found hundreds of references to Hemingway, and the description of his affinity showed their deep and warm friendship at the time.  At the end of World War II, Hemingway returns to Paris with the Americans and meets Chevelle again.  There are still a lot of gun battles in the theater street, and we ’ ve had enough.  One day a jeep pulled into the street and stopped at the door of my bookstore.  I heard a low voice shouting, “Chevy! ” and it spread all over the street.  Edhiena cried, "It's Hemingway! It's Hemingway!" I rushed downstairs and hit the oncoming Hemingway.  He picked me up in circles and kissed me, and the people at the window of the street cheered … He asked if there was anything else I could do, and I said if I could get rid of the Nazi snipers on the roof of the street, especially those on Edsieena ’ s roof.  He called his buddies out of their jeeps, took them all to the roof, and then came the last gunfight on Theater Street.  Hemingway got down with his men and drove off in the jeep — next, Hemingway said, to the wine cellar at the Ritz.  The Lilac Garden Cafe (Photo / Courtesy of the Blue Bird House) The Lilac Garden on the Boulevard Montparnasse is the place where the artistic and cultural trends of Paris in the 1920s met and collided, and where Fitzgerald, Zola, Cezanne and Picasso all stopped.  “I sat in the corner writing with my notebook, and the afternoon sun was on my shoulders.  The waiter took me a cup of hot cream coffee (café crème), and I drank half of it after cooling, and the other half was on the table while I was writing.  When I stopped writing, I really didn ’ t want to leave the river where the trout could be seen in the pool. ” — Chen Jung-bin, author of “Feast on the Move, ” mentioned this text, poetically describing the process of creating the novel“ Our Time ” in Lilac Garden, and the river where the trout can be seen is the title of the book, “The Big Twin Heart River. ”  A Good Café on the Place St.-Michel "A girl walks into a cafe and sits alone at a table by the window.  She was beautiful, and her face was as fresh as a new coin — if only coins could be minted with silky muscles and rain-washed skin.  Her hair was as dark as the wings of a raven, cut into a blade, and covered her face obliquely.  I stared at her, and she disturbed my thoughts and made me very excited.  I wanted to put her in my novel or something, but she was sitting where she could see the street and the entrance to the cafe, so I knew she was waiting for someone.  So I continued to write.  The story seemed to unfold automatically, and my pen managed to keep up with it.  I ordered another glass of St. James ’ s brandy.  Whenever I raised my head or sharpened the pencil with a sharpener, I would look at the girl and let the curly scraps fall into the saucer under the glass. "  "I see you, my beauty, now you belong to me, no matter who you are waiting for, and no matter whether I can see you again in the future," I thought.  You belong to me, and all Paris belongs to me, and I belong to this notebook and this pencil.  From this Paris memoir, Teacher Chen Jung-bin led us to read this famous article. Reading this text, we followed Hemingway ’ s eyes, met the girl who distracted him in a cafe next to the square, took control between the mind and the pen, and then sat in the whole Paris.  Hemingway and Fitzgerald Fitzgerald (Photo / Courtesy of Blue Bird) Hemingway and artists from all walks of life in Paris, and Fitzgerald also met here, they first met at Dingo American Bar, and each other's affirmation is extremely sincere.  Hemingway left such a comment on Fitzgerald in "The Moving Feast": After reading "The Tycoon", he felt that no matter what outrageous things Fitzgerald did, he had to treat it as if Fitzgerald was sick, and he had to try to help him from the standpoint of a friend, "because, if he could write such a book, he could write a better book." This is probably the biggest compliment Hemingway has ever given to any of his peers.  Fitzgerald also gave Hemingway "He's the real thing." Title: Ernest Hemingway: As long as one of us lives, the other lives forever in his heart.
Content: The novel is like an iceberg, only one eighth of which is on the surface of the water, and the rest is underwater.  Deleting more sentences and leaving more sentences underwater is enough to strengthen your novel.  This is Ernest Hemingway ’ s “theory of the iceberg ”, which he implemented in his novels. Today, 1940, For Whom the Bell Tolls is published.  Before publication, Hemingway revised the manuscript every day after finishing it, and did not leave the room for 96 consecutive hours.  He used iceberg theory to remove unnecessary sentences, and used symbols, pictures and ideas to navigate the story, resulting in this monumental work that was later adapted into a film and used by the college to teach literature.  Ernest Hemingway (Getty Images) The bell-ringing story in the field focuses on an attack by a guerrilla group during the Spanish Civil War in the summer of 1937.  The story is only four days long, focusing on the tension of the war and the appearance of human nature.  The protagonist, Robert Jordan, is an American professor who teaches Spanish. At the outbreak of the war, he joined the volunteer army and was ordered to go deep into the mountains to break through enemy lines, and the story begins when the protagonist enters the mountains, he tries to contact the guerrillas and cooperate with them to blow up the bridge.  For Whom the Bell Tolls: The Hemingway Library Edition (Scribner) Guerrilla Captain Pablo opposes the bridge, losing his fighting spirit and even stealing the detonator.  Robert manages to gain support from the rest of the team, isolating the captain and planning to blow up the bridge.  Robert takes in Maria, a girl who has been abused and enslaved by the enemy, and falls in love with her.  After stealing the horses from the enemy line, the two walked hand in hand, and he imagined that after the war was over, he would return to the United States to teach, and the two would end up together.  But after a while, he shot and killed one of the other soldiers, and while he did not get any information from the enemy, he read a home letter, which made him feel the cruelty of the war.  In the early hours of the last day, the few remaining teams set out for the bridge, and due to the small number of people and the behavior of the captain, several people had to risk their lives.  In the final scene, Robert and his companions blow the bridge in mid-air with explosives, but when he runs away on horseback in the direction of Maria, he is unfortunately shot and fell, his left leg is broken, and he can no longer escape from the enemy's attack.  At the end of his life, he said to Mary, “As long as one of us lives, the other will live in his heart forever. ”  In 1943, Battlefield Bell was transformed into a film (file picture) The tragic color of "tough man" Hemingway's novels often appear as "tough man", meaning that he has a very strong will and a strong and unyielding spirit.  When the Nobel Prize for Literature was awarded to him, he said that he "has a kind of man who likes to take risks" and vowed not to bow down and fight to the end when faced with the pressure of fate.  The old fisherman in The Old Man and the Sea said, “Man can be destroyed, but he cannot be defeated. ”  But when we talk about fate and rebellion, we often talk about tragedy, and the end of Battlefield Bell is clearly tragic.  [The Old Man and the Sea] Hemingway's many novels have been exposed hundreds of wrong scholars: The fault is not in the spirit of his ancient Greek tragedy, it is that when people face the choice of fate, they know that they have to bear a heavy price and still struggle to insist on their own choices, and finally they really want to meet the tragic consequences.  It may be against fate, it may be against power, and it ends tragically.  In The Birth of Tragedy, Nietzsche pointed out that the ancient Greek tragedy was the manifestation of the god of wine, freed from the "self", disordered and led to a carnival, chanting that people "believe in eternal life". Content: Hemingway ’ s old sea man Santiago came ashore when he saw a crowd gathered to hear the story of his heroic resistance and his fight for the greatest catch of his life.  Many of the children and relatives of Caspian hunters were the same builders of the Anzali city.  Those who sail in one of the most ferocious and wild seas in the world. He asked the audience to link this story to their memories of the suffering and struggle of the city fishermen.  A book that has perhaps been read more than many other stories on the planet and won its creator the Nobel Prize in Literature.  A short novel that Anzali people may feel closer and familiar with than many other places.  But then, in the end, the Lord will reveal Himself to those who are on the other side of the earth.  He told me this short story about the nature of the effects of the effects of Hemingway.  That his stories were the closest thing to reality, but he put pure reality into artistic form and made it a pure story.  That Hemingway ’ s work is easy to read while it is easy to read, but understanding its deep layers may not be as easy as it seems.  He said that many writers tried to write like him, but could not do it.  Maryam Saheli, author and lecturer of the Anzali Thousand and One Nights Story Society and the host of the program, said: Ernest Miller Hemingway was a writer with many biological experiences.  His presence in the war, his numerous trips and his proximity to nature made him a collection of information and memories that are well evident in his works.  Simple prose, objectivism summarization, powerful illustration of outstanding dialogue writing is one of the features of this influential author. Title: How to read Hemingway?
Content: Ernest Hemingway, a Nobel laureate and one of the most important of the 20th century, was born on July 21, 1899 in Illinois and wrote seven novels, six collections of short stories and two nonfiction books during his lifetime.  On the occasion of the birth of this author, which coincided with the thirteenth of July, we have suggestions for better reading of the works of this author.  Hemingway ’ s work is fluid, simple, and clear, but for many readers of literature, it may be difficult to begin reading Hemingway ’ s books.  Why read Hemingway?  Ernest Hemingway is an influential writer in the history of literature and fiction, his works have repeatedly won the most prestigious international literary awards such as Nobel and Pulitzer, this author employed a different kind of narrative description and caused many writers after him to borrow his own literary style.  Hemingway has named his literary style the Iceberg Theory, in this way of writing, fictional events are narrated like an iceberg floating in water, only one-eighth of which is visible, and the author includes only the information that is essential in the process and omits the rest of the information.  This technique created a tremendous change in storytelling, especially the writing of short stories, and it was a development that freed the stories from conventional chatter.  Hemingway ’ s works are included in the list of books of the century, books to read before death, and the best fiction books in history, highlighting the importance of this author.  What do we need to know?  One of the topics that helps to better understand Ernest Hemingway ’ s work is getting to know his personal life.  Much of what we read in his books is what he has turned from his personal life into a story.  At the age of 19, he volunteered for the First World War but was not allowed to fight because of poor eyesight, but Hemingway insisted on serving as an ambulance driver for the Red Cross.  He was wounded several times during the Chang, but his most significant injury is when he was wounded by mortar shell fragments and spent a long time in the hospital, a novel about this part of Hemingway ’ s life and the war.  Even the character of Catherine Barkley in this book is based on the nurse Hemingway fell in love with.  Hemingway also participated in World War II as a war correspondent, and several short stories are the result of this era.  The sun continues to blow, the Great River or along the river to the trees, each of which is somehow tied to the World War, and their heroes are survivors of the war and have many memories of these days.  But Hemingway ’ s most important masterpiece is a relic of his childhood, Hemingway ’ s father had a great interest in fishing, and this hobby was passed on to Ernest, a point that can be clearly seen in the famous and widely read story of The Old Man and the Sea.  But before the Old Man and the Sea, Hemingway had written about having and not having a fishing boat captain.  Another important point to know before reading Hemingway ’ s works is his political approach, he has written a lot in opposition to fascism and against dictatorship, both as a journalist and as a writer, sometimes even changing from a journalist to a social-political activist, who is this point in The Bell for, or who is this death knell?  It is a story of an American soldier in the Spanish Civil War fighting alongside groups against General Franco, which Hemingway did.  Perhaps the other thing that matters is that during the World War, Hemingway led a French group against the Nazis that was tried after the war for armed acts but was never proven guilty.  The political and social history of the world in the years of Hemingway's life, his personal life, as well as the knowledge of his contemporaries, such as Scott Fitzgerald, with whom he has written, are points that contribute to the understanding of his works.  Getting to know Hemingway ’ s contemporary writers helps to better understand the difference between him and his contemporaries.  Is it a classic?  To read Hemingway ’ s work, we must note that he is not a classic writer in his different style, he did not deal with the long margins and descriptions of classical literature, and his long novels are not immune.  He was interested in shorthand and engaging the audience with fiction, which is a feature of modern literature.  In general, Hemingway ’ s works are innovative and even among modern works have their own creativity, but the value of this author ’ s work has always been compared to classical works, and even classical enthusiasts have not been able to be indifferent to it.  In these works we have a happy and well-spoken writer, a writer who was in middle age with young people and was even close friends with a group of hippies.  Hemingway is a realistic writer, but he has always tried to maintain his sense of humor.  Where do we start?  To read Hemingway ’ s works, the first and most important suggestion is The Old Man and the Sea.  The book, translated by Najaf Daryabandari, was published in 222 pages by Kharazmi Publications.  The next book, Farewell to Arms, is again translated by Najaf Daryabendari, published by Amir Kabir Publications in 343 pages.  These two books are always on the list of works to be read or masterpieces of the 20th century.  If you are interested in short stories, you can also read Men Without Women, a collection of stories that have been published in various magazines by the author.  This book has been translated by Asadollah Amraei for publication of Horizon in 222 pages.  Even if you are interested in writing, Hemingway can be a good teacher and read his series of talks and learn very precise points.  The book The Last Interview and Other Conversations of Ernest Hemingway with a translation by Houshang Jirani has been published in 88 pages by Cheshmeh Publishing.  The final chapter of many critics considered Ernest Hemingway to be the greatest writer of the 20th century.  His stories are an exploration of real human life, suffering and the meaning of life.  The portrayal of human inner feelings is the most important characteristic of this author, which makes his works a read for every reader.  Who was Ernest Hemingway?  Ernest Hemingway was born on July 21, 1899 in Oak Park, Illinois.  His father, Clarence, was a doctor and his mother, Grace, was a piano and singing teacher.  Ernest spent the summers with his family in northern Michigan, where he discovered his passion for fishing.  After finishing high school, he worked for a while in Kansas City as a reporter for the Star Chronicle in 1917.  During World War I, he volunteered to serve in the army, but poor eyesight prevented him from doing so, instead serving as an ambulance driver for the Red Cross near the Italian front.  On July 8, 1918, he was injured and spent months in the hospital.  In 1925, his first collection of short stories, in our time, was published, which spoke well of his particular style.  His memoirs from that period were published after his death in 1964 as The Variable Eid.  Ernest Hemingway was an adventurer for most of his life.  From being wounded in Italy by 200 pieces of Austrian shrapnel during World War I, to taking part in the frontlines of the Spanish Civil War or touring the African wilderness, to fishing and hunting wildlife and living in Cuba.  He finally said goodbye to life with his hunting rifle.

The Old Man and the Sea was born on an alcohol-soaked beach in Cuba; The War Bell is an interview from the Spanish Civil War; The Dawn of Truth records the memories of a trip to Africa with his fourth wife, Mary, and Hemingway, born in Oak Park, Illinois, USA. Ernest Hemingway in World War I. When he first arrived in Paris, he stayed in a small hotel and wrote in the Toronto Star: “PARIS — Paris in the winter is rainy, cold, beautiful and cheap. ”  It is also noisy, jostling, crowded and cheap.  It is anything you want — and cheap. ” — Living on $1,000 a Year in Paris Describes the bankruptcy of Europe at the end of World War I, the relative advantage of the dollar, and the ability to spend a thousand dollars in Paris for a year.  Although this article is published in the newspaper, the writing and rhyme are poetic.  “We ate well and cheaply and drank well and cheaply and slept well and warm together and love each other. ”  After graduating from high school, Hemingway worked as a reporter for the Kansas City Star, and his entire writing career was inextricably linked to journalistic writing.  “From Hemingway ’ s early writings, the Kansas Star newspaper ’ s“ style sheet ” for the rookie reporter shaped his unique style of writing, and the rules in the guide were as many as 110, and the first paragraph was indeed Hemingway ’ s rule: write short sentences.  The first paragraph is shorter.  Write articles in vivid English.  The influence of the rookie reporter period on his career also corresponds to the iceberg theory he proposed in 1932: "Prose is like architecture, not interior decoration, and the Baroque era is over... If you have enough understanding of what you are describing and write well enough, even if you write only one-eighth of the text, you can let the reader fully grasp the scene, plot and character description that he wants to express." Hemingway often uses a concise style to bury clues in the details or background, so that it is connected with emotional intimacy.  Paris was not only the place where Hemingway worked as a journalist, but also the beginning of his literary career.  The first two books, Three Stories & Ten Poems, and a collection of short stories, in our time, were published here.  Ernest Hemingway wrote many notes about his life and literary work in the 1920s. Two boxes were left in the basement of the Ritz Hotel in Paris, and when he returned to Paris in 1957, he opened these dusty old memories, namely, "The Feast on the Move".  This prose memoir of Paris also later became a guide for people on their pilgrimage journey, following Hemingway for a drink, order a cup of coffee at the Lilac Café, borrow a book at Shakespeare ’ s Bookstore on the Rue d ’ Odeon, and then take a walk in Luxembourg Park.  “If you are lucky enough to have lived in Paris as a young man, then wherever you go for the rest of your life it stays with you, for Paris is a movable feast. ” — Ernest Hemingway A moving feast. Hemingway got down with his men and drove off in the jeep — next, Hemingway said, to the wine cellar at the Ritz.  The Lilac Garden Cafe (Photo / Courtesy of the Blue Bird House) The Lilac Garden on the Boulevard Montparnasse is the place where the artistic and cultural trends of Paris in the 1920s met and collided, and where Fitzgerald, Zola, Cezanne and Picasso all stopped.  “I sat in the corner writing with my notebook, and the afternoon sun was on my shoulders. Her hair was as dark as the wings of a raven, cut into a blade, and covered her face obliquely.  I stared at her, and she disturbed my thoughts and made me very excited.  I wanted to put her in my novel or something, but she was sitting where she could see the street and the entrance to the cafe, so I knew she was waiting for someone.  So I continued to write.  The story seemed to unfold automatically, and my pen managed to keep up with it.  I ordered another glass of St. James ’ s brandy. Title: Ernest Hemingway: As long as one of us lives, the other lives forever in his heart.
Content: The novel is like an iceberg, only one eighth of which is on the surface of the water, and the rest is underwater.  Deleting more sentences and leaving more sentences underwater is enough to strengthen your novel.  This is Ernest Hemingway ’ s “theory of the iceberg ”, which he implemented in his novels. Today, 1940, For Whom the Bell Tolls is published.  Before publication, Hemingway revised the manuscript every day after finishing it, and did not leave the room for 96 consecutive hours.  He used iceberg theory to remove unnecessary sentences, and used symbols, pictures and ideas to navigate the story, resulting in this monumental work that was later adapted into a film and used by the college to teach literature.  Ernest Hemingway (Getty Images) The bell-ringing story in the field focuses on an attack by a guerrilla group during the Spanish Civil War in the summer of 1937.  The story is only four days long, focusing on the tension of the war and the appearance of human nature.  The protagonist, Robert Jordan, is an American professor who teaches Spanish. At the outbreak of the war, he joined the volunteer army and was ordered to go deep into the mountains to break through enemy lines, and the story begins when the protagonist enters the mountains, he tries to contact the guerrillas and cooperate with them to blow up the bridge.  For Whom the Bell Tolls: The Hemingway Library Edition (Scribner) Guerrilla Captain Pablo opposes the bridge, losing his fighting spirit and even stealing the detonator.  Robert manages to gain support from the rest of the team, isolating the captain and planning to blow up the bridge.  Robert takes in Maria, a girl who has been abused and enslaved by the enemy, and falls in love with her.  After stealing the horses from the enemy line, the two walked hand in hand, and he imagined that after the war was over, he would return to the United States to teach, and the two would end up together.  But after a while, he shot and killed one of the other soldiers, and while he did not get any information from the enemy, he read a home letter, which made him feel the cruelty of the war.  In the early hours of the last day, the few remaining teams set out for the bridge, and due to the small number of people and the behavior of the captain, several people had to risk their lives.  In the final scene, Robert and his companions blow the bridge in mid-air with explosives, but when he runs away on horseback in the direction of Maria, he is unfortunately shot and fell, his left leg is broken, and he can no longer escape from the enemy's attack.  At the end of his life, he said to Mary, “As long as one of us lives, the other will live in his heart forever. ”  In 1943, Battlefield Bell was transformed into a film (file picture) The tragic color of "tough man" Hemingway's novels often appear as "tough man", meaning that he has a very strong will and a strong and unyielding spirit.  When the Nobel Prize for Literature was awarded to him, he said that he "has a kind of man who likes to take risks" and vowed not to bow down and fight to the end when faced with the pressure of fate.  The old fisherman in The Old Man and the Sea said, “Man can be destroyed, but he cannot be defeated. ”  But when we talk about fate and rebellion, we often talk about tragedy, and the end of Battlefield Bell is clearly tragic.  [The Old Man and the Sea] Hemingway's many novels have been exposed hundreds of wrong scholars: The fault is not in the spirit of his ancient Greek tragedy, it is that when people face the choice of fate, they know that they have to bear a heavy price and still struggle to insist on their own choices, and finally they really want to meet the tragic consequences.  It may be against fate, it may be against power, and it ends tragically.  In The Birth of Tragedy, Nietzsche pointed out that the ancient Greek tragedy was the manifestation of the god of wine, freed from the "self", disordered and led to a carnival, chanting that people "believe in eternal life".
